ARC-005.confidence_rationale: exp=5 entry(s), lit=7 entry(s), exp_conf=0.889, lit_conf=0.859

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: mixed direction

Placebo-controlled crossover pharmacological manipulation (atomoxetine, a noradrenergic reuptake blocker = a direct precision/gain-channel intervention) with clean, reported effect sizes on a downstream perceptual-sensitivity readout. This is the single most directly quotable effect-size anchor for the commissioning question. It is 'mixed' for ARC-005 because it cuts both ways: it confirms a catecholaminergic gain channel DOES route a detectable downstream effect (supports routing), while showing that effect is small-to-moderate and channel/readout-specific (null on metacognition) -- which is exactly the yardstick against which REE's ~180x-below-noise effect looks anomalously tiny. Small N (27, male-only) holds confidence at 0.7.
failure_signatures: Atomoxetine improved perceptual sensitivity d' with Cohen's d = 0.39 (t(26)=2.06, p=0.02) -- i.e. the downstream effect of a noradrenergic gain manipulation is ~0.39 SD. REE channel 1's raw effect is ~1/180 SD (d~0.006), roughly 65x smaller than this biological benchmark, which the biology does NOT predict for a functioning precision channel.

The effect was readout-specific: metacognitive sensitivity meta-d' was unaffected (d=0.16, BF01=3.55 favouring the null). Precision manipulations produce localized, not diffuse, downstream footprints -- consistent with REE channel 2 being architecturally null, but NOT with channel 1's footprint being ~2 orders of magnitude below any detectable biological effect.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Large-N (102) placebo-controlled human pharmacology establishing a CAUSAL link between catecholamine enhancement (methylphenidate) and the adjustment of a meta-learning parameter -- learning rate as a function of environmental volatility -- which is the closest empirical analogue to REE's precision-routing readout (the precision channel should modulate how strongly evidence updates internal state as a function of context). Direction is supports for ARC-005's routing premise; confidence 0.73 reflects strong design but a specific/partial effect (experiential learning only, no effect on inferred-value learning) and the usual pharmacology-to-engineered-substrate transfer gap.
failure_signatures: The catecholamine effect on learning-rate adaptation was significant only for direct/experiential learning and NOT for inferred-value learning -- precision-routing effects are real but conditional on the pathway being the one the neuromodulator actually gates. A REE channel wired to a degenerate or off-scale upstream signal is the analogue of the inferred-value pathway: the manipulation lands on nothing.

The effect is a detectable shift in a volatility-driven learning-rate parameter, i.e. a routing effect of measurable magnitude in a 102-person sample -- categorically unlike REE channel 1's ~180x-below-noise footprint, which no comparable sample would detect.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled acute tryptophan depletion in healthy humans (N=97) directly manipulating the serotonergic channel -- the biological analogue of REE's channel-1 '5-HT rigidity' -- with a DOSE-DEPENDENT downstream behavioral effect (reversal deficit magnitude correlated with extent of depletion). Dose-dependence is the strongest possible evidence that the channel routes: the readout tracks the manipulation monotonically, which is exactly the C_precision_monotonicity property REE is trying to demonstrate. Supports ARC-005's routing premise. Confidence 0.74: strong design and the most on-target channel (5-HT rigidity), tempered by reversal-learning being a flexibility readout rather than a direct precision readout.
failure_signatures: The serotonergic manipulation produced a DOSE-DEPENDENT reversal deficit: the downstream readout scaled monotonically with the size of the manipulation. This is precisely the monotonicity ARC-005's C_precision_monotonicity criterion demands, achieved biologically -- a REE channel that produces only 4/10 units with |rho|>=0.6 and an effect ~180x below noise is failing to reproduce a property the biology shows cleanly at N=97.

The 5-HT channel here has a real, replicable, behaviorally consequential footprint on a flexibility readout; REE's homologous channel-1 (5-HT rigidity / dACC precision) footprint is ~2 orders of magnitude below noise -- the gap points to an implementation deficit (untrained dACC adapter) rather than a biologically tiny effect.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily-cited theoretical/computational formalization of exactly the mechanism ARC-005 imports: neuromodulatory precision-weighting of top-down expectation vs bottom-up evidence (ACh = expected uncertainty, NE = unexpected uncertainty). High mapping fidelity to the ARC-005 premise that a control plane can route precision. But it is a MODEL paper, not an effect-size measurement, so it establishes that the routing mechanism is real and functionally consequential without itself bounding the magnitude an intervention should produce -- hence 0.72, not higher.
failure_signatures: The model predicts precision-weighting is FUNCTIONALLY LOAD-BEARING -- it changes how much sensory evidence updates belief -- not a negligible perturbation. A precision channel whose downstream effect is ~180x below cross-seed noise is not routing in the sense this model requires; it is decorative at the readout.

The model treats NE/ACh gain as multiplicative on the inference, so a channel that is architecturally invariant under normal committed operation (REE channel 2, ~97% committed) or reads a collapsed/degenerate upstream signal (REE channel 1's dACC adapter, response 4-7 orders of magnitude off scale) fails to implement the mechanism this paper describes.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The foundational theoretical argument (correlation theory of brain function) for WHY binding needs a dynamic temporal tag at all: static feature-cell coding suffers a 'superposition catastrophe' when multiple objects are present, so a separate binding variable is required. Strong, canonical grounding for ARC-006's premise that entities are dynamically BINDABLE structures rather than fixed conjunction cells. Held at 0.68 because it is a theoretical/modeler's argument (not empirical) and the temporal-binding solution it argues for is contested.
failure_signatures: The superposition-catastrophe argument shows static conjunction coding is INSUFFICIENT, but it does not by itself prove temporal correlation is THE solution -- competing solutions (e.g. competitive slot allocation, attention) also avoid the catastrophe. So it motivates a binding variable without uniquely selecting synchrony.

A modeler's-perspective theoretical paper: it argues for what a binding mechanism must accomplish, not what the brain demonstrably does -- empirical adjudication is elsewhere (and contested, per Shadlen & Movshon 1999).

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Object-trace cells are the closest neural correlate of the PERSISTENCE half of MECH-045: LEC neurons that fire at the location where an object USED TO BE after it is removed. That firing-in-the-object's-absence is the single-unit signature of an entity buffer that outlives perceptual contact -- precisely 'minimal entity persistence across time'. Combined with LEC's role as the 'what/content' stream (vs MEC 'where'), it grounds the identity-content side that object-vector cells (MEC) do not. Confidence 0.72: a clean, on-point persistence signature, discounted because trace cells code a remembered object-PLACE (still partly location-bound) rather than a label-free token followed through motion, and because it is rodent single-unit data.
failure_signatures: Object-trace cells encode where an object WAS (object-place memory), so persistence here is still partly anchored to a remembered LOCATION; a REE buffer that only remembers last-seen position would reproduce trace-cell firing without re-identifying the object once it has MOVED -- the exact cross-motion gap that separates persistence-through-absence from token tracking.

Only a small subset of LEC cells show the trace property; the signal is sparse and the mechanism by which experience-history is written is not resolved -- so the paper licenses 'a persistence buffer exists' but not its update rule.

LEC object firing reflects higher-order experience history, not pure stimulus drive; disentangling genuine identity persistence from slow sensory adaptation requires the kind of ablation/shuffle control the REE experiment must build in.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Object-vector cells are the strongest single-unit evidence that the mammalian brain has a dedicated, object-anchored coding scheme that GENERALISES across distinct objects irrespective of their location -- a real neural substrate for object-relative representation, supporting the premise that entities are a first-class representational primitive (ARC-006). But the mapping to MECH-045's TOKEN-INSTANCE buffer is only partial and partly adverse: object-vector cells code a vectorial RELATION (distance + direction) to objects and are tuned 'equally to a spectrum of discrete objects', i.e. they are object-GENERIC and allocentric, NOT a per-token identity store that re-identifies THIS object across motion. Mixed, 0.66: confirms the brain reserves machinery for objects, but the specific cell type is closer to the ANCHOR/where axis (SD-039 lineage) than to the token KEY MECH-045 needs.
failure_signatures: Object-vector cells are tuned EQUALLY across discrete objects irrespective of identity -- they encode 'an object is HERE relative to me', not 'this is object #7 again'. Modelling MECH-045's token KEY on object-vector coding would yield a where-signal with no instance identity, reproducing the ANCHOR-keyed gap (SD-039) rather than closing the token gap.

The code is vectorial/allocentric (egocentric distance + allocentric direction to a confined object); REE's z_world is not an explicit spatial-vector code, so the substrate analogy is structural, not mechanistic -- the same 'structural-analogy-no-mechanism' failure mode flagged for the 641a coherence diagnostic.
Rodent foraging in open fields with discrete physical objects; no demonstration that a single object's IDENTITY is tracked through occlusion or relabelled after it moves.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Pylyshyn's FINST / visual-index theory supplies the part of MECH-045's specification that the object-file literature leaves implicit: the KEY. A visual index individuates and tracks ~4-5 objects 'preconceptually' -- without encoding their identities or any conceptual label -- which is the cleanest available statement of MECH-045's 'WITHOUT symbolic/type labels'. The multiple-object-tracking paradigm it spawned is the direct behavioural test of tracking-through-motion. Confidence 0.78: high theoretical mapping fidelity, discounted because it is a framework + paradigm rather than a single decisive experiment, and because the index is a pure pointer (no feature buffer) -- it grounds the KEY but not the per-token feature store.
failure_signatures: Visual indexes carry NO feature content -- they are bare pointers. A REE buffer modelled too literally on FINSTs would track identity but store nothing to bind, defeating the 'per-token feature buffer' half of MECH-045; the design must add the feature store the index theory deliberately omits.

The ~4-5 index capacity limit is a hard cap; MOT studies show tracking collapses when objects coincide/occlude or move too fast. A REE buffer with unbounded tokens would not reproduce the human capacity signature and would have no principled token-eviction policy.

Pylyshyn argues indexing is bottom-up and stimulus-driven, partly DIVORCED from attention; this is in mild tension with ARC-006/MECH-045's 'attention-gated' commitment, so the attention coupling REE proposes is an addition, not a borrowing.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Bratman 1987 is the foundational philosophical account of commitment as a distinct mental state category. His central argument is that intentions cannot be reduced to beliefs and desires -- they are 'prior intentions' that stabilise future-directed planning by generating conduct-controlling pro-attitudes that resist reconsideration. This directly grounds ARC-014's commitment architecture: the pre-commit/post-commit boundary exists because committed intentions must be treated as stable rather than continuously re-evaluated, otherwise planning becomes computationally incoherent. Bratman's 'Commitment Revisited' chapter makes explicit that once an intention is formed it functions as a constraint on further deliberation, not a re-evaluated option -- this is the philosophical basis for the categorical (not graded) character of ARC-014's commitment boundary. Confidence is moderate-high: mapping fidelity to ARC-014's architectural necessity claim is good; transfer risk is moderate because Bratman is analysing human practical reasoning, not neural architecture, and the commitment-channel separation (pre-commit simulation vs. post-commit realised outcome) is an REE implementation that Bratman's framework supports but does not directly specify.
failure_signatures: Bratman's framework is normative philosophy of action -- it does not make predictions about neural implementation or information-flow architecture.
Bratman treats commitment stability as a matter of rational norms, not architectural necessity -- the move from 'rationally appropriate' to 'architecturally necessary' is an REE inference.

The pre-commit/post-commit channel separation (distinct error signals, residue write-gating) is not addressed in Bratman's framework, which operates at the level of intentional states, not computational channels.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Elster's Ulysses Unbound (and its predecessor Ulysses and the Sirens, 1979) develops the theoretical account of precommitment as a rational strategy: an agent binds themselves in advance to prevent future irrational reconsideration. This maps onto ARC-014's pre/post-commit boundary: the commitment architecture creates an asymmetry where actions, once committed, are not available for re-simulation -- they have crossed from the domain of options into the domain of enacted consequences. Elster's account of why precommitment is sometimes necessary (weakness of will, time-inconsistency, strategic self-binding) provides the functional motivation for why a sharp pre/post-commit boundary is architecturally superior to continuous re-evaluation. The Ulysses metaphor is precise: committed actions cannot be 'unsimulated' just as Ulysses cannot un-hear the Sirens once the ship has passed -- consequence attribution must happen offline precisely because the action is no longer a hypothesis. Confidence is moderate: Elster's framework is descriptive of human precommitment strategies, not a neural or computational architecture, and ARC-014's offline attribution necessity is an engineering inference from the philosophical structure.
failure_signatures: Elster addresses voluntary self-binding strategies; ARC-014 concerns an architectural necessity imposed by the structure of action execution, not a voluntary strategic choice.
Elster's analysis focuses on inter-temporal consistency and weakness of will -- the relevance to ethical residue attribution (phi(z) write access) requires a non-obvious translation.
The commitment boundary in Elster is permeable and voluntary (one can choose to un-commit); ARC-014's boundary is architectural and categorical -- this is a structural disanalogy.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Rangel, Camerer and Montague 2008 propose a five-process framework for value-based decision making: (1) represent the decision problem, (2) assign values to options, (3) select an action, (4) evaluate the outcome after implementation, (5) update processes for future decisions. This framework explicitly posits a structural discontinuity between the selection phase (process 3) and the outcome evaluation phase (process 4): outcome evaluation occurs after action implementation and measures the 'desirability of outcomes that have been received'. This sequential, post-hoc structure provides neuroscientific support for ARC-014's pre/post-commit boundary. The evaluation-after-implementation structure is architecturally identical to REE's post-commit offline attribution: consequences are evaluated in a phase that is structurally distinct from and sequential to selection. The paper directly implies that a system that evaluated outcomes before action completion would be confusing prospective planning with retrospective attribution -- the separation is necessary for coherent learning. Confidence is moderate: the mapping to the specific ARC-014 claims about commitment architecture and phi(z) write access requires interpretation; the paper provides supporting structure rather than direct evidence for the categorical boundary.
failure_signatures: Rangel et al. frame the five-process model descriptively; they do not argue for architectural necessity of the pre/post boundary in the sense ARC-014 requires.
Outcome evaluation (process 4) in Rangel et al. is about learning signal computation, not about ethical residue accumulation -- the phi(z) attribution function is an REE extension.
The framework is agnostic about whether the selection-to-evaluation boundary is categorical or graded; ARC-014 claims a categorical route switch.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the equation-level synthesis that makes WS-5's core point precise. It shows verbatim that (a) the approximate posterior FACTORISES under a mean-field approximation over hidden-state factors, and (b) expected free energy is a SUM of separable epistemic (salience + novelty) and extrinsic (risk) terms -- i.e. active inference optimises a factorized functional, not an undifferentiated scalar. That directly WEAKENS REE's 'active inference is just one scalar' objection (a strawman as stated). Simultaneously it pins the GENUINE departure: every term of G(pi) is measured in nats and summed, so risk + ambiguity is one commensurable number -- the exact common-currency assumption MECH-069/ARC-021 reject. Confidence moderate: it is a normative-mathematical paper (no empirical test of incommensurability), and the mapping onto REE's three specific channels is interpretive.
failure_signatures: Expected free energy is explicitly assembled as risk + ambiguity (state pathway) or, dually, negative extrinsic value + negative epistemic value -- all in nats and additively combined. This is the concrete existence proof that reward-seeking and information-seeking are COMMENSURABLE and summable, which is the assumption REE's incommensurability claim denies. If a single summed functional over factorized states can reproduce REE's mode/credit behaviour, MECH-069's strong form is unsupported.

The mean-field factorisation Q(s_1:T | pi) = product over tau of Q(s_tau | pi), and the factorisation over distinct hidden-state factors, show active inference already SEPARATES representational dimensions. So REE cannot claim novelty for 'separate channels' -- only for the stronger claim that the separated channels' errors cannot be re-combined into any shared scalar, which this paper does not test and its formalism does not require.

Precision here (including policy precision gamma with its Gamma prior) is a scalar/low-dimensional gain on a common surprise currency. It provides no distinct, non-exchangeable precision axes, so ARC-016's multi-axis precision is an addition NOT licensed by this formalism and must be independently justified.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical, comprehensive statement of active inference. Strongly SUPPORTS ARC-016: precision as inverse variance weighting prediction errors, and precision over policies (gamma) as the control variable that sets the behavioural regime, is exactly the precision-to-commitment vocabulary REE re-derived without the calculus. WEAKENS-leaning on the strong form of MECH-069/ARC-021: the textbook shows a single expected-free-energy functional G(pi) can absorb reward-seeking and information-seeking as decomposed terms, so REE's blanket 'active inference is one scalar' objection is partly a strawman -- but the same fact makes the unified functional a live alternative hypothesis to strict incommensurability, which is why the direction is 'mixed' not 'supports'. Confidence is moderate because a textbook is a synthesis, not new empirical evidence, and the mapping onto REE's specific three-channel architecture requires interpretation.
failure_signatures: Active inference derives everything -- perception, learning, action, precision, exploration -- from a SINGLE scalar (variational / expected free energy). This is a standing existence proof that REE's three functionally-distinct control objectives COULD in principle be unified into one functional over a factorized state space, which is precisely the alternative MECH-069 must rule out rather than assume away.

The textbook's precision is a scalar (or low-dimensional) gain on a common prediction-error currency (surprise, measured in nats). REE's ARC-016 asserts multi-axis / heterogeneous precision; active inference does not obviously supply distinct, non-exchangeable precision axes, so the departure REE claims is not free -- it must be shown that a single-currency precision cannot reproduce REE's mode transitions.

Epistemic value in active inference is information gain measured in the same nats as pragmatic value; the two are commensurable and summable by construction. REE's claim that its three error channels are INcommensurable (no common currency at all) is a stronger and different claim than 'distinct terms in one functional', and the textbook offers no support for non-commensurability -- if anything it is the null this claim contradicts.

Key findings: (1) multiple thalamic nuclei relay vestibular signals (ventroposterior complex, ventroanterior-ventrolateral complex, intralaminar, posterior nuclear group) — these contain multisensory neurons integrating vestibular, proprioceptive, and visual signals; (2) the parieto-insular vestibular cortex (PIVC) is the core vestibular cortical region, with additional projections to somatosensory cortex (areas 2v, 3av), intraparietal sulcus, posterior parietal cortex (area 7), MST, frontal cortex, and hippocampus; (3) vestibular signals influence self-motion perception, spatial navigation, internal models of gravity, and bodily self-consciousness. This directly grounds the VESTIBULAR stream as distinct from both SELF_SENSORY/proprioception (joint/muscle state) and WORLD (exteroceptive content), with its own thalamo-cortical relay to parietal and MST areas that inform z_self's spatial frame.

ARC-018.confidence_rationale: exp=4 entry(s), lit=19 entry(s), exp_conf=0.608, lit_conf=0.846

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative review dissociating the functional roles of different frontal regions (OFC, vmPFC, ACC, lateral PFC) in reward-guided action selection. Core claim relevant here: OFC and vmPFC compute expected value of options before action (evaluator role), distinct from ACC's role in action-outcome learning (comparator / credit assignment role). This is the clearest statement of the evaluator-comparator dissociation at the frontal level, and it directly supports the architectural separation between pre-action value estimation and post-action attribution that the SD-003 successor needs. Confidence 0.72 because the dissociation is cleaner in some contexts than others, and the review does not adjudicate whether both circuits share the same forward model or maintain separate forward models.
failure_signatures: If the vmPFC value signal depends on state representations computed by the same forward model that ACC uses for credit assignment, the circuits are not as separated as the functional dissociation suggests, and the SD-003-successor 'same substrate, different modes' reading becomes stronger.
Lesion data is sometimes ambiguous between 'region computes X' and 'region provides inputs to region that computes X'; the review is cautious about this but the transfer risk to REE is real.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical dissociation of model-based (forward-model rollout-based) and model-free (cached-value) contributions to human action selection, with fMRI evidence that both signals coexist in ventral striatum. Critical for the SD-003 successor question: it demonstrates that pre-action value estimation uses both rollout-based and model-free pathways in the same brain, and that behavior reflects a weighted mixture. This establishes the evaluator mode as a real, measurable computation and constrains where forward-model rollouts feed value signals. Confidence 0.78 because it is high-quality primary data in Neuron, central to a decade of computational neuroscience, and directly addresses forward-model-based value computation.
failure_signatures: If the two-step task's model-based/model-free dissociation conflates forward-model rollout depth with other properties (planning horizon, effortful computation), then the mapping to REE's evaluator mode is partial.
The paper shows model-based signals in striatum but cannot directly address hippocampal rollout generation — the forward-model substrate is inferred, not recorded.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Direct electrophysiological evidence that the same hippocampal cellular assembly expresses temporally structured sequences both before an experience (preplay) and after it (replay), using overlapping but not identical sequences. This is the cleanest biological case of a single predictive-sequence substrate read in two different modes -- prospective anticipation and retrospective consolidation -- within the same neural population. Maps directly onto the E2 dual-function question: preplay corresponds roughly to prospective rollout / evaluation mode, replay corresponds roughly to retrospective attribution / consolidation mode. The paper supports single-substrate-plus-mode-dependent-readout. Direction marked mixed because the paper also emphasises that preplay sequences are a pre-configured subset, which opens the door to sub-population specialisation (partial dual-substrate interpretation). Confidence 0.70 because the evidence is direct, from a canonical electrophysiology paper, with tight experimental controls.
failure_signatures: If preplay sequences involve a distinct subset of cells from replay sequences in a systematic, non-overlapping way, the single-substrate interpretation weakens -- preplay and replay would use distinct sub-populations even within the same anatomical region.

The transfer to E2 assumes the hippocampal sequence precedent generalises to forward-model dynamics prediction. Hippocampus does spatial/episodic sequencing; E2 does action-consequence dynamics. The principle of sequence reuse may not be equivalent to forward-model reuse.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: FAIL with weakening direction

Strong formal analogue for ARC-018: a learned cognitive map plus a state-difference-to-action inverse model plus stochastic virtual action selection generates goal-directed imagined trajectories, including spatial rerouting, abstract graph paths, and compositional silhouette decomposition. Marked mixed rather than supports because it is a simulation/model paper, not direct biological evidence, and because it leaves ARC-018's REE-specific gaps untouched: E2 action-object indexing, live E2 fidelity, and harm/goal error updating.
failure_signatures: If REE's cognitive-map substrate lacks any reliable state-difference-to-action inverse readout, it will miss the core GCML mechanism that turns a map into goal-directed imagined action sequences.

If stochastic proposal generation is unconstrained by map geometry, it is not the GCML/Pfeiffer-style mechanism; useful randomness should remain goal-directed and self-correcting rather than pure trajectory noise.
If a future ARC-018 validation treats this paper as direct biological support, it overclaims; the source only supports formal plausibility and benchmark behavior.

ARC-019.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=5 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.688

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Strong, well-sourced review of head-camera and eye-tracker corpora showing that infant first-person visual input is not a stationary sample but a systematically ordered sequence of highly selective datasets that changes as sensorimotor capability changes. This is good evidence that biological development *is* curriculum-structured, which is the premise REE's brain-like-construction principle leans on. It is weak evidence for ARC-019 as stated, for two reasons that dominate the aggregate: the ordering is descriptive and correlational (no arm without it), and the curriculum is *emergent from the body* rather than imposed by explicit gates -- which is arguably an argument for letting REE's staging fall out of embodiment rather than for the InfantCurriculumScheduler's criterion gates.
failure_signatures: The infant curriculum is generated by changing sensorimotor capability, not by an external gate; if REE's staging is load-bearing only because it proxies an embodiment constraint the substrate does not otherwise have, then implementing the constraint directly would make the explicit gates redundant -- a distinct architecture from ARC-019.

No causal manipulation is available: nothing in this literature shows an infant given adult-like input from birth learns worse, so the observation that development is ordered cannot by itself discriminate ARC-019's CONFIRMING from its FALSIFYING branch.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The closest existing analogue to ARC-019's own falsifier design, and the reason this entry carries the highest confidence in the directory. Wu et al. run thousands of orderings under a matched budget with a random-ordering control that isolates the confound ARC-019's non-degeneracy precondition is groping toward: any apparent curriculum benefit on standard benchmarks is attributable to the *dynamic training-set size*, not to the ordering, because random-curriculum matches or beats curriculum. That is a direct weakening. But the same paper finds curricula do help under a limited training-time budget or with noisy data -- and REE's regime is exactly limited-budget and noisy -- so the honest direction is mixed, not weakens. Held below 0.8 by domain distance: supervised image classification with example-level difficulty ordering, not embodied phase-advance gating.
failure_signatures: Any REE staged-vs-flat advantage may be an artefact of the staged arm's smaller effective early training set rather than of the gate ordering; without a random-ordering (or shuffled-phase) control at matched budget, a positive V3 result cannot distinguish these and would not license ARC-019.

Wu et al. report curricula are beneficial only under limited budget or label noise, so a staged-arm advantage observed at a small episode budget may vanish at a larger one -- a REE experiment that measures one budget cannot claim staging is architecturally load-bearing, only that it is budget-efficient at that point.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The closest mechanistic analogue in this pull to what ARC-019 actually commits to: advancement driven by a measured competence signal rather than a fixed schedule. TSCL selects sub-tasks by the slope of the student's learning curve and additionally revisits tasks whose performance is degrading, and matches or surpasses hand-crafted curricula on decimal addition and Minecraft navigation, solving tasks that were otherwise unsolvable. Mapping fidelity is the highest here because the gate is a competence criterion in a sequential RL setting. Confidence is capped by the same non-degeneracy problem ARC-019 itself flags: where the flat baseline cannot solve the task at all, the comparison shows the curriculum is *necessary for traversal*, not that it produces better outcomes at matched budget.
failure_signatures: TSCL's advantage is largest exactly where the ungated baseline fails outright, which is the V3-EXQ-591 degenerate-comparison shape in mirror image -- a REE result of this form would confirm the substrate needs a curriculum to traverse the task, not that ARC-019's outcome-quality claim holds.

The teacher gates on learning-progress slope, not on the fixed 7-criterion developmental gate REE uses; if progress-gating is what does the work, REE's fixed DEV-NEED-008 criteria could be the wrong gate and a staged-arm null would then be evidence against the *criteria*, not against staged development.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical origin of the 'staged development is necessary' position and the closest historical analogue to ARC-019's architectural commitment: a recurrent network trained on the full-complexity corpus from the start failed, while the same network succeeded when either the input or its own working memory was staged. Source quality is held down by its being a single 1993 simulation study on one artificial grammar with no replication reported in-paper, and by the fact that the central result was later directly contradicted (see the Rohde & Plaut 1999 entry in this directory). Mapping fidelity is moderate: Elman staged input complexity and memory span, not phase-advance on explicit competence criteria as ARC-019 specifies, and his comparison was staged-vs-full-from-the-start rather than matched-total-budget staged-vs-ungated. Aggregate weighted toward mapping_fidelity, as ARC-019 is an architectural commitment.
failure_signatures: The staged advantage in Elman (1993) was obtained under a comparison where the ungated control never traversed the task at all; an equivalent REE result would be indistinguishable from the V3-EXQ-591 substrate-ceiling non-result unless the non-degeneracy precondition is independently verified first.

Elman's gating variable was capacity/complexity of the input, not a competence criterion; a REE staged arm gated on DEV-NEED-008 criteria could reproduce his benefit purely by limiting effective input dimensionality early, with the explicit gate doing no work.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A direct, systematic attempt to reproduce Elman (1993) that found the opposite: none of their simulations showed an advantage to starting small, and in most cases the staged regime actively hurt, with the harm growing as the artificial language was made more English-like. Source quality is high for this class -- a broader parameter sweep than the original, in the same journal, by authors with no stake in the negative result. Mapping fidelity is the limiting factor: like Elman, they manipulate input/memory complexity rather than a criterion-gated phase advance, and the domain is again language modelling rather than embodied developmental competence. Confidence is set above the Elman entry because a well-executed failure-to-replicate is stronger evidence about a general architectural commitment than the original positive finding it targets.
failure_signatures: Staged input presentation produced worse asymptotic performance than full-complexity training in the majority of Rohde & Plaut's simulations, and the deficit increased with task realism -- so a REE staged arm could plausibly underperform its flat control precisely on the harder, more naturalistic tasks REE cares about.

The original starting-small advantage appears to have been contingent on specific network capacity and training-schedule choices rather than on staging per se; a REE result favouring ARM_2 over ARM_0 therefore requires a hyperparameter-robustness check before it counts as evidence for ARC-019.

ARC-021.confidence_rationale: exp=2 entry(s), lit=9 entry(s), exp_conf=0.613, lit_conf=0.862

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Neuron review by two of the field's leading figures, surveying four generations of empirical work on goal-directed vs habit dichotomy. Argues that the dichotomy is better understood as a SPECTRUM with intermediate levels, and that the strict two-system framing of Daw 2005 has been complicated by subsequent evidence (e.g., model-based and model-free systems share circuitry, Pavlovian-to-instrumental transfer reveals additional levels, the dichotomy may be parametric rather than discrete). Confidence 0.82: high source quality, definitive review of the field's state, directly informs whether REE should commit to two-system or richer architecture.
failure_signatures: Dolan & Dayan argue the dichotomy is more like a spectrum or a continuum than two discrete systems. An REE architectural commitment to 'two and only two systems' (habit cache + goal-directed planner) would over-simplify. The paper licenses a richer architecture but does not specify exactly how many levels or what the intermediate substrates are.

The 'fifth generation' work the paper points to (model-based / model-free interactions, Pavlovian-to-instrumental transfer, mixed strategies) is recent enough that the architectural picture is still evolving. Any REE substrate decision based on Dolan-Dayan's reading should remain provisional pending further empirical resolution.

The paper does not address hierarchical / option-level action representation directly. The decomposition Dolan & Dayan discuss is goal-directed vs habit, not goal-directed vs option-level vs habit -- these are orthogonal dimensions that REE's architectural mapping has to resolve.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Annu Rev Neurosci review by the leading authority on basal ganglia and habit formation. Synthesises decades of single-unit, lesion, and behavioural evidence for action chunking in striatum: action sequences are 'chunked' into unitary representations whose start/stop is bracketed by phasic firing in striatal task-bracketing cells. Direct neural-substrate evidence for the action-chunk level of the decomposition. Confidence 0.84: high source quality, direct mapping to REE's missing habit / chunked-action substrate, modest transfer risk.
failure_signatures: The chunked action sequences described are typically motor sequences in well-trained animals (rats running fixed mazes, monkeys executing learned saccade chains). Whether this generalises to abstract / cognitive action chunks (e.g., 'forage at this location' as a chunk) is plausible but less directly evidenced.

The substrate is described as 'basal ganglia broadly' with emphasis on dorsolateral striatum and on cortico-striatal loops. Within REE's ARC-021 three-loop framework, the habit-chunk role would land in the dorsolateral-loop slot. The paper does not pin chunking to a specific BG subdivision in the kind of microscope-level detail REE's substrate map prefers.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Cognition paper integrating the hierarchical-RL options framework (Sutton-Precup-Singh 1999) with neuroscience evidence. Argues that the divisibility of behaviour into tasks-subtasks-actions corresponds to options at multiple temporal scales, and maps options onto dorsolateral / orbital PFC. Strongest framework paper for the option / hierarchical-RL level of the action decomposition. Confidence 0.83: high source quality, the framework is widely adopted, but the substrate-level neural evidence is partly inferential (mapping computational primitives onto known PFC functions rather than direct empirical dissociation).
failure_signatures: The neural mapping is partly inferential rather than directly demonstrated. The paper argues that hierarchical-RL components 'might map onto neural structures' in PFC, with the strongest empirical support coming from later fMRI work (Ribas-Fernandes 2011 etc.) rather than from the original framework paper.

The framework leaves open the key question of how the agent IDENTIFIES new option subroutines from experience. Botvinick et al. flag this as an important open question -- how learning carves the action space into useful chunks. For an REE option library, this is the same question: how would the substrate populate its option dictionary from experience?

Options as temporally extended actions can recurse (options containing sub-options). The paper allows this in principle but does not specify how deep the recursion goes biologically. An REE option library would need to commit to a finite hierarchy depth or accept open-ended recursion.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the equation-level synthesis that makes WS-5's core point precise. It shows verbatim that (a) the approximate posterior FACTORISES under a mean-field approximation over hidden-state factors, and (b) expected free energy is a SUM of separable epistemic (salience + novelty) and extrinsic (risk) terms -- i.e. active inference optimises a factorized functional, not an undifferentiated scalar. That directly WEAKENS REE's 'active inference is just one scalar' objection (a strawman as stated). Simultaneously it pins the GENUINE departure: every term of G(pi) is measured in nats and summed, so risk + ambiguity is one commensurable number -- the exact common-currency assumption MECH-069/ARC-021 reject. Confidence moderate: it is a normative-mathematical paper (no empirical test of incommensurability), and the mapping onto REE's three specific channels is interpretive.
failure_signatures: Expected free energy is explicitly assembled as risk + ambiguity (state pathway) or, dually, negative extrinsic value + negative epistemic value -- all in nats and additively combined. This is the concrete existence proof that reward-seeking and information-seeking are COMMENSURABLE and summable, which is the assumption REE's incommensurability claim denies. If a single summed functional over factorized states can reproduce REE's mode/credit behaviour, MECH-069's strong form is unsupported.

The mean-field factorisation Q(s_1:T | pi) = product over tau of Q(s_tau | pi), and the factorisation over distinct hidden-state factors, show active inference already SEPARATES representational dimensions. So REE cannot claim novelty for 'separate channels' -- only for the stronger claim that the separated channels' errors cannot be re-combined into any shared scalar, which this paper does not test and its formalism does not require.

Precision here (including policy precision gamma with its Gamma prior) is a scalar/low-dimensional gain on a common surprise currency. It provides no distinct, non-exchangeable precision axes, so ARC-016's multi-axis precision is an addition NOT licensed by this formalism and must be independently justified.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical, comprehensive statement of active inference. Strongly SUPPORTS ARC-016: precision as inverse variance weighting prediction errors, and precision over policies (gamma) as the control variable that sets the behavioural regime, is exactly the precision-to-commitment vocabulary REE re-derived without the calculus. WEAKENS-leaning on the strong form of MECH-069/ARC-021: the textbook shows a single expected-free-energy functional G(pi) can absorb reward-seeking and information-seeking as decomposed terms, so REE's blanket 'active inference is one scalar' objection is partly a strawman -- but the same fact makes the unified functional a live alternative hypothesis to strict incommensurability, which is why the direction is 'mixed' not 'supports'. Confidence is moderate because a textbook is a synthesis, not new empirical evidence, and the mapping onto REE's specific three-channel architecture requires interpretation.
failure_signatures: Active inference derives everything -- perception, learning, action, precision, exploration -- from a SINGLE scalar (variational / expected free energy). This is a standing existence proof that REE's three functionally-distinct control objectives COULD in principle be unified into one functional over a factorized state space, which is precisely the alternative MECH-069 must rule out rather than assume away.

The textbook's precision is a scalar (or low-dimensional) gain on a common prediction-error currency (surprise, measured in nats). REE's ARC-016 asserts multi-axis / heterogeneous precision; active inference does not obviously supply distinct, non-exchangeable precision axes, so the departure REE claims is not free -- it must be shown that a single-currency precision cannot reproduce REE's mode transitions.

Epistemic value in active inference is information gain measured in the same nats as pragmatic value; the two are commensurable and summable by construction. REE's claim that its three error channels are INcommensurable (no common currency at all) is a stronger and different claim than 'distinct terms in one functional', and the textbook offers no support for non-commensurability -- if anything it is the null this claim contradicts.

ARC-022.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=7 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.819

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Strong mapping to ARC-022's core typed-object abstraction claim: the dynamic predictive coding model demonstrates that each cortical level encodes outputs of the level below at greater temporal abstraction, with lower levels handling brief sequences and higher levels operating on longer timescale objects. The three-level extension directly instantiates the E1->E2->higher layer logic of ARC-022. The hippocampal-augmented variant supports the terminus-level (hippocampus) receiving chained sequence representations rather than raw sensory input. Transfer risk: this is a computational/theoretical model, not a direct anatomical connectivity study, so it supports the abstract pipeline logic rather than providing direct neuroanatomical grounding for the specific E1->E2->DMN->Goal/Avoid->Hippocampus sequence. Confidence penalised accordingly.
failure_signatures: The model is a computational proposal, not a direct empirical study of hierarchical typed-object passing between identifiable anatomical regions.
The three-level hierarchy is sensory (V1-like -> motion -> higher dynamics); the mapping to E1 (motor/sensory prediction), E2 (transition model), DMN-regime, E3, hippocampus requires inference.

The hippocampal augmentation in the model is an associative memory for episodic retrieval, not a valenced cognitive map or trajectory-proposal system -- only partially overlapping with ARC-022's hippocampus role.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Provides direct empirical evidence that lower cortical areas receive typed prediction signals from higher areas that carry view-invariant, identity-specific properties -- a signature of typed-object passing across hierarchy levels rather than raw sensory signal passing. This is the physiological correlate of ARC-022's typed-object abstraction principle. However, mapping fidelity is moderate: the face-processing hierarchy (ML -> AL areas) is a specialised visual object domain, and the inference to E1->E2 typed-object passing requires treating low-level prediction-error responses as the functional equivalent of E1 consuming E2-derived objects. The finding that statistical learning enables lower areas to test predictions at higher abstraction levels supports ARC-022's claim that each layer 'operates on the output type of the layer below without re-instantiating lower-level computations'.
failure_signatures: The study is restricted to face processing in macaque inferotemporal cortex -- a highly specialised domain with a well-characterised object hierarchy. Generalisation to action/planning hierarchies requires substantial inference.

The effect depends on prior statistical learning of face sequences; whether analogous typed-object prediction signals exist in motor/planning hierarchies without extensive sequence training is not shown.
The study supports feedback prediction signals carrying higher-level object properties but does not directly test the pipeline topology (E1->E2->DMN->Goal->Hippocampus) that ARC-022 specifies.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Provides empirical grounding for the Goal/Avoid layer of ARC-022's pipeline: orbitofrontal cortex encodes abstract task-state objects -- a cognitive map of state space that is not directly observable from sensory input. This supports ARC-022's claim that the Goal/Avoid systems (E3 + control-plane valence channels) operate on abstracted state objects rather than raw sensory or low-level transition outputs. The OFC's state-map is a typed object: it encodes which state-in-task-space the agent occupies, providing the valenced possibility-space that ARC-022 assigns to the Goal/Avoid layer. Behavioural error correlates with decoding accuracy, confirming the functional role of this abstract representation. Confidence penalised because the study concerns OFC as Goal/Avoid analogue, not the full E1->E2->DMN->Goal/Avoid->Hippocampus chain; the pipeline structure above and below OFC is not examined.
failure_signatures: The study focuses on OFC as a state-map encoder during a 16-state decision task; it does not establish that OFC receives typed trajectory-bundle inputs from a DMN-regime layer, or that it sends typed possibility-space outputs to a hippocampal map layer.

The OFC state map here is a cognitive/task-state map, not a valenced goal/avoid space per se -- the valence structure is implicit in task design rather than explicitly tested as a Goal/Avoid pipeline layer.
The study supports OFC's role in abstract state representation but cannot adjudicate whether this is a pipeline stage (ARC-022) or an independent computation that interfaces with other regions.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: THICK (Temporal Hierarchies from Invariant Context Kernels) is the strongest computational existence proof for ARC-022's typed-object pipeline principle: the lower level generates invariant contexts (typed state objects) sparsely in time, and the higher level exclusively predicts situations involving changes in these context objects. This is structurally identical to ARC-022's claim that each layer operates on the output type of the layer below without re-instantiating lower-level computation. The model learns categorical, interpretable temporal abstractions at the higher level while preserving precise low-level predictions -- directly supporting ARC-022's claim that abstraction hierarchy explains why E2 operates on z_gamma rather than raw sensory streams. Confidence penalised for being a purely computational model (no biological substrate testing) and for framing the hierarchy as two levels rather than the five-stage pipeline ARC-022 specifies.
failure_signatures: THICK demonstrates a two-level hierarchy (low-level prediction + high-level context); ARC-022 specifies a five-stage pipeline. Whether the THICK principle generalises to five levels with heterogeneous computation at each stage is not shown.
THICK's higher level predicts context changes -- it does not generate goal/avoid valuations or trajectory proposals. The Goal/Avoid and Hippocampus stages of ARC-022's pipeline are not instantiated.
The model is a reinforcement learning planning tool, not a model of biological neural circuitry. Its correspondence to E1->E2->DMN->Goal/Avoid->Hippocampus anatomy requires biological transfer.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This paper establishes the typed-prediction-descent principle as a theoretical proposition about neocortical architecture — the direct conceptual ancestor of the Schwiedrzik & Freiwald (2017) result and the framework that Rao & Ballard (1999) formalised computationally. Mumford explicitly proposes that top-down (feedback) cortico-cortical connections carry predictions/interpretations generated by the higher area, while bottom-up (feedforward) connections carry residuals — the part of lower-level activity not explained by the higher-level prediction. Because predictions are generated by the higher-level model, they inherit the representational format of that level by construction: typed prediction descent is a theorem of this architecture, not an empirical observation. This is the foundational theoretical prior art for the inference Schwiedrzik & Freiwald's result is used to license. Confidence is high because the mapping to ARC-022's E1->E2 typed-object interface is direct and the argument is domain-independent by construction. Penalised modestly because the paper is theoretical/mathematical rather than empirically supported at the time of writing (no electrophysiological confirmation existed in 1992), and because Mumford's formulation is for a two-level exchange rather than the five-level pipeline ARC-022 specifies.
failure_signatures: Mumford's framework is a general-purpose prediction/residual architecture and does not specify the representational content of predictions at each level. ARC-022's specific claim that z_gamma transitions (rather than sensory predictions) are the typed objects at the E1->E2 interface is not derivable from Mumford alone.

The original paper discusses cortico-cortical loops in a two-area framework. The extension to a five-stage pipeline (E1->E2->DMN->Goal/Avoid->Hippocampus) requires iterating the framework across heterogeneous computation types, which Mumford does not explicitly address.

The 1992 paper pre-dates the experimental validation tradition. The claim that this specific framework characterises neocortex was not empirically confirmed until Rao & Ballard (1999) and Bastos et al. (2012).

ARC-023.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=5 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.801

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Direct evidence that MD thalamus gates prefrontal processing via two distinct projection types (signal amplification vs noise suppression); supports ARC-023's claim that MD thalamus is the gate for the E3 planning-gates loop. Supports TRN-as-inter-loop-router via established inhibitory TRN architecture. Main caveat: the paper addresses signal/noise control in a single loop, not multi-rate coordination across three loops.

Comprehensive review of BG oscillatory dynamics across frequency bands, drawing on human DBS recordings, MEG, and ECoG. Provides convergent evidence that different functional territories of the BG-thalamocortical network exhibit characteristic frequency signatures: beta (13-35 Hz) dominates motor territories, gamma (40-90 Hz) associates with active movement processing, theta/alpha (4-12 Hz) associates with cognitive/executive functions in ventral STN and limbic territories. This frequency segregation across functional domains supports ARC-023's claim of characteristic loop rates. However, as a review it does not provide novel primary data, and the frequency-territory mapping is correlational rather than causal. The thalamic rate-setting role specifically claimed by ARC-023 is not directly addressed.
failure_signatures: Review, not primary data; frequency-territory associations are correlational
Thalamic nuclei as rate-setters not directly addressed; focus is on cortical-STN-GPi dynamics
Motor territory beta dominance is well-established but cognitive/limbic frequency signatures are less firmly characterized

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Human intracranial + MEG data showing MD thalamus at 7-8 Hz coupling with PFC at ~10-11 Hz is strong direct evidence for a characteristic thalamic frequency in the cognitive/deliberative loop. The frequency hierarchy (MD slower than PFC) aligns with ARC-023's prediction. However, only one thalamic nucleus-cortical target pair is tested, so extrapolation to a full three-loop frequency hierarchy requires inference.
failure_signatures: Cortical activity leads thalamic oscillations in this study, suggesting PFC drives MD rather than MD setting the pace -- this inverts ARC-023's framing of thalamic nuclei as rate-setters.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Human intraoperative recordings from motor thalamus (VIM) showing characteristic beta (13-30 Hz) oscillations that are task-modulated. Directly demonstrates that the motor thalamic relay operates at beta frequency -- distinct from the MD thalamic theta (~7-8 Hz) shown by Griffiths 2022. The two papers together support ARC-023's claim of frequency-specific thalamic nuclei. Confidence limited by patient population (essential tremor) and single nucleus studied.
failure_signatures: Patient population has essential tremor -- thalamic oscillatory dynamics may be pathologically altered rather than representative of healthy motor thalamus.
Motor thalamic beta may originate from cerebellum rather than BG, complicating the mapping to a BG-thalamocortical loop.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Nature paper with causal optogenetic evidence showing TRN subnetworks mediate modality-specific gating of thalamocortical pathways under PFC control. Directly supports ARC-023's TRN-as-routing-switch claim. Confidence limited by mouse-to-human transfer and the fact that modality-specific gating (sensory selection) is not identical to frequency-specific loop gating.
failure_signatures: The study demonstrates modality-specific TRN gating (visual vs auditory), not frequency-specific gating between processing levels (sensory vs motor vs cognitive). The mapping from modality-routing to loop-routing is an inference step.

Strong mapping fidelity: predatory imminence continuum theory is the ethological formalisation of ARC-024's gradient structure claim, providing both the theoretical grounding and neural circuit detail. Pre-encounter, post-encounter, and circa-strike modes directly instantiate the gradient: behaviour form and vigour both change continuously as a function of perceived threat distance, before contact occurs. Source quality is solid (Fanselow is the originator of PIC theory, open-access PMC journal). Transfer risk is moderate (primarily animal literature; human data exists but is secondary).

Primarily rodent literature; human PIC research (including Mobbs 2007) is referenced but not the primary evidence base of this review.

This is the most direct evidence on developmental timeline of play signal competence in a non-canid species, directly relevant to REE's DEV-NEED-009 (play-dominant childhood builds the play frame substrate). Confidence reflects good behavioral data from zoo geladas with systematic age comparisons, published in J Comparative Psychology.
failure_signatures: If immatures and adults showed identical play face variant usage and response sensitivity, this would undermine the developmental trajectory claim and weaken DEV-NEED-009's prediction that childhood play builds adult social signal competence.
If PF and FPF had identical social consequences (same response rates from partners), there would be no evidence that signal variant encodes contextually important information.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the first study documenting open-mouth play signals and rapid facial mimicry (RFM) in a marine mammal species (bottlenose dolphins, Tursiops truncatus). Dolphins are phylogenetically distant from primates and terrestrial carnivores, separated by approximately 95 million years. The finding that dolphins use open-mouth displays almost exclusively during social (conspecific) play (not solitary play, not interspecific play), emit the display within the receiver's visual field at significantly higher rates than non-visual-context events, and replicate a partner's OM display 13x more often when they can see it (vs. control condition), provides strong cross-taxon convergent evidence for the background signal mechanism. The 33% replication rate falls within the range reported for terrestrial carnivores (meerkats 27%, sun bears 39%). PMC full-text available. Published October 2024 in iScience (Cell Press). High methodological quality with multiple observation sessions across two facilities.
failure_signatures: If open-mouth displays in dolphins were not context-specific (occurring equally in solitary and social play), this would argue against the signal interpretation and for a non-communicative motor pattern.

If the 13x RFM odds ratio were an artifact of behavioral synchrony (both dolphins opening mouths for the same reason simultaneously), the mimicry interpretation would be confounded -- the study addresses this by showing the ratio drops dramatically when the partner cannot see the signal.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This study tests the metacommunicative repair hypothesis (bows bracket ambiguous actions) vs. the reinitiation hypothesis (bows restart play after pauses) in dog and wolf puppies. The primary finding is that play bows in young dogs occur most often after brief pauses in play, not after ambiguous actions -- supporting the reinitiation hypothesis over the repair hypothesis for dogs. Wolf puppies show bows in similar temporal positions but bows are less effective at eliciting continued play from wolf partners. This refines rather than contradicts REE's architecture: reinitiation after pause is itself a form of ambiguity management (silence/pause can be misread as disengagement or pending aggression). Confidence reflects good methodology and PMC availability, but the sample is limited to captive puppies and the wolf n is small. [2026-08-14: evidence_direction was recorded as the non-enum token 'refines', which build_experiment_indexes._normalize_direction silently coerced to 'unknown'. Set to 'mixed' to match this rationale -- the study supports the reinitiation reading and disconfirms the repair reading.]
failure_signatures: If play bows in wolves were as effective as in dogs at reinitiation, this would suggest domestication does not modulate the repair signal architecture -- which would simplify the cross-species story for REE but reduce the developmental modulation finding.
If bows were completely random in timing, both repair and reinitiation hypotheses would fail, undermining the level-3 signal concept entirely.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This study documents two morphologically distinct play face variants in Western Lowland gorillas: the standard play face (ROM, relaxed open mouth, lower teeth only) and the full play face (upper teeth exposed), and shows they have different functions. The full play face was more common in intense play and was associated with longer intense play bouts and higher post-play affiliative behavior relative to standard play face. This provides evidence that within the background signal level (level-2), signal modulation encodes intensity information -- the background signal is not binary but graded. This is important for REE's architecture: the level-2 background signal may carry a continuous intensity channel rather than being a binary 'play on/play off' marker. Confidence reflects solid behavioral data from captive gorillas with good focal animal sampling, but the captive setting and single-species scope limit generalizability.
failure_signatures: If the full play face and standard play face had identical behavioral consequences (same bout length, same post-play affiliation), there would be no evidence for within-level signal modulation and REE's level-2 could be treated as binary.
If the full play face occurred randomly with respect to play intensity, the hypothesis that signals encode intensity would be unsupported.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This study documents emotional play contagion in juvenile common ravens (Corvus corax) as young as 3 months post-hatching -- evidence for generalized playful mood transfer in a corvid (non-mammalian) species. Ravens are among the most cognitively sophisticated non-mammalian species, but they are separated from mammals by approximately 320 million years. The finding that observer ravens show increased locomotion and social play (but not the same motor patterns as demonstrators) after observing demonstrators playing argues for mood-state transfer rather than behavioral mimicry -- a general playful-mood-contagion mechanism. This extends the play signal architecture argument to birds. However, the study does not address discrete play signals (play bows, play faces) -- corvids have very limited facial mobility. Confidence reflects good experimental design with two test ages (3 and 6 months), solid sample size (N=10), and PMC availability, but the absence of specific visual signal documentation limits direct mapping to ARC-049's signal levels.
failure_signatures: If observer ravens showed increased object play (same category as demonstrators) rather than locomotion/social play, this would be behavioral contagion (imitation) rather than emotional contagion (mood spread) -- weakening the mood-transfer interpretation.

If emotional contagion was absent at 3 months but present at 6 months, this would place the onset of play frame sensitivity outside the earliest developmental period -- but both ages showed the effect, supporting early onset.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: ICLR-published computational framework demonstrating that diverse skills can be acquired without reward by maximizing mutual information I(S;Z) between states and skill identifiers. The discriminability metric operationalizes rollout diversity measurement: skills are diverse to the extent that a discriminator can reliably identify which skill generated a given state sequence. This provides a concrete diversity metric for the DEV-NEED gate. However, DIAYN does not model play frames -- all skill learning is real-signal (states are real environment states) -- and the mutual information metric measures discriminability rather than strategy-calibration separation. Mapping fidelity to MECH-195 is moderate: DIAYN separates what-skill from how-well-skilled (the two entropy components) but does not separate strategy structure from magnitude calibration in the REE sense.
failure_signatures: DIAYN skills are learned without reward -- this is not analogous to play (which uses synthetic rewards). The absence of reward in DIAYN is a methodological choice; play's synthetic reward is a frame-maintenance mechanism. The analogy is structural, not mechanistic.
Mutual information I(S;Z) measures discriminability of state distributions, not strategy quality or calibration accuracy. A skill can be highly discriminable but poorly calibrated.
State coverage (skill state distributions being spread across the state space) is used as a proxy for diversity but may conflate geometric coverage with behavioral strategy diversity.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Empirically demonstrated computational system (real humanoid robot) achieving automatic curriculum via competence-progress measurement. The competence-progress metric -- rate of change in success rate within sliding windows over goal regions -- is operationally defined and non-Goodharted: it selects for regions where learning is active, not for regions where performance is already high or already near chance. Direct relevance to INV-060 (play dominates childhood; type progresses by subsystem competence) and MECH-197 (stage progression tracks competence dependencies). Source quality high (JMLR). Mapping fidelity moderate because IMGEP uses goal-region competence rather than play-mode competence specifically.
failure_signatures: IMGEP does not distinguish play mode from non-play mode -- all exploration is treated as intrinsically motivated, without a separate frame signal architecture.
Competence progress metric is continuous; stage transitions are not formally gated -- the curriculum is self-organizing but does not produce discrete stage certificates.
Diversity of the learned repertoire is measured implicitly by goal coverage, not by an explicit behavioral characterization metric -- this conflates exploration coverage with behavioral diversity.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Well-specified review synthesizing infant and robot developmental data. Stage metrics (retention interval, reactivation window, generalization tolerance, means-end revaluation) are operationally concrete and cross-validated across species. Moderate transfer risk because the robot blueprint is architecturally schematic rather than implemented end-to-end. Mapping fidelity to INV-060 (play dominates child phase, progression by subsystem competence) is indirect -- the paper does not explicitly discuss play as the mechanism, only sensorimotor contingency sensitivity. Strong alignment with MECH-197 stage ordering via the 3-month, 6-month, 9-month, 24-month developmental pivots.
failure_signatures: The paper does not define discrete gated stages with formal threshold criteria -- progression is described as continuous accumulation of matching events, not as a pass/fail stage gate.

Competence-calibration separation is implicit, not formally defined: the finding that 7-month-olds have bidirectional contingency knowledge but cannot use it in action selection shows dissociation, but no metric distinguishes the two channels.
Blueprint architecture is schematic (Mannella 2018 instantiation) rather than a validated metric framework usable as a developmental readiness gate.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational support for treating wanting as a preserved motivational variable distinct from local reward contact. This directly strengthens the need for a goal-linked payload in unresolved-goal traces. The remaining gap is hippocampal specificity.
failure_signatures: If wanting collapsed to contact pleasure, preserving goal-linked payloads on inactive anchors would be unnecessary.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Strong clinical support that sustained goal representations are necessary for purposive behavior and cannot be replaced by local liking or simple harm avoidance. This supports the need for preserved goal traces when local routes fail.
failure_signatures: If intact local liking were sufficient for sustained goal pursuit, explicit unresolved-goal traces would add little architectural value.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Classic controlled experiment isolating goal GRANULARITY: identical material, only the goal framing varied (proximal subgoals vs single distal goal vs no goals). Proximal subgoals produced the strongest gains on every measure; distal goals 'had no demonstrable effects'. Directly supports Strand G (proximal subgoals sustain distal motivation) and the maintenance thesis (a bare superordinate goal does not by itself drive sustained effort -- it must be decomposed). Confidence 0.60: small-N developmental study (40 children, ~10/cell), single domain, and the mechanism ('self-efficacy') has no clean computational analog.
failure_signatures: Distal goal alone was statistically indistinguishable from no goals -- a cautionary datum for any REE design that expects a bare superordinate goal representation to sustain long-horizon effort without intermediate structure.

The mechanism is human self-efficacy self-appraisal; the study conflates subgoals-as-frequent-success-signals with subgoals-as-capability-information, which a computational model would need to separate.
Small N (~10/cell), single domain (arithmetic), four sessions -- noisy effect-size estimates.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Field-defining review with neuroimaging + anatomical + electrophysiological + developmental convergence for a rostro-caudal abstraction gradient (rostral=abstract/superordinate, caudal=concrete/proximate), including the asymmetric top-down control signature (anterior predicts caudal activation, not vice versa). Supports a granularity-matched goal hierarchy. Capped at 0.62 because 'abstraction' conflates several axes and the 2018 follow-up (Badre & Nee) argues the organization is discrete (3 zones) rather than a continuous unidimensional gradient -- a material qualification for any continuous-granularity model.
failure_signatures: The 2018 synthesis (Badre & Nee, TICS) revises the picture: evidence 'consistently supports three major functional subdivisions' that are 'functionally discontinuous, violating a linear, progressive rostro-caudal gradient' -- a continuous granularity axis is a modeling simplification, not the current consensus.

'Abstraction has been defined somewhat differently across these experiments' (domain-generality, relational integration, temporal abstraction, policy abstraction are conflated), so the mapping of a single goal-granularity axis onto the anatomical axis is not clean.
The review itself cautions that the gradient features 'do not, by themselves, require that the organization be hierarchical.'
