recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the highest-mapping-fidelity AI entry in the pull because it operates at REE's own level of description: a computable signal, added alongside the primary task reward, that measures IMPACT as the change an action makes to the ATTAINABLE UTILITY of a set of auxiliary reward functions -- i.e. the change in an agent's ability to still optimise a range of goals. Agency, formalised, IS attainable utility / optionality; harm-to-agency IS a reduction in it. AUP thus supplies MECH-129 a concrete instantiation of a distinct harm signal that is NOT the primary cost signal and is computed over reachability, which is precisely the 'distinct architecture' the claim asserts is required. Held at 0.72 (not higher) because as published AUP measures the agent's impact on its OWN auxiliary attainable utility (a proxy for reversibility/low-impact), not another agent's -- extending it to OTHER-agent attainable utility is the natural but non-trivial step MECH-129's requirement (a) demands and AUP does not itself provide.
failure_signatures: AUP as published penalises change to the AGENT'S OWN attainable utility over auxiliary rewards (a self-referential low-impact/reversibility proxy); applied to harm-to-agency it must be re-pointed at ANOTHER agent's attainable utility, which requires inferring that agent's reward set -- so the formalism is only a harm-to-agency signal once composed with other-agent goal modelling, and AUP alone would penalise the agent's own optionality loss, not the other's, a different quantity.

AUP's impact measure is acutely sensitive to the choice of auxiliary reward set and the baseline (stepwise vs inaction); Turner et al. show random auxiliary rewards suffice for LOW-IMPACT but the paper does not establish that any auxiliary set faithfully tracks a SPECIFIC other agent's goal -- so a harm-to-agency signal built on AUP inherits an unresolved baseline/auxiliary-selection problem (the same counterfactual-baseline issue flagged in the Feinberg entry).

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Shue's basic-rights framework supplies MECH-129 two things: (i) the concept of a PROTECTABLE INTEREST that is basic in the sense of being a precondition for enjoying every other interest -- security and subsistence -- which is the normative shape of 'agency' as something whose obstruction is a distinct category of harm; and (ii) his tripartite duty analysis (duties to AVOID depriving, to PROTECT from deprivation, and to AID the deprived) which shows that a single interest generates structurally different obligations, paralleling MECH-129's insistence that harm-to-agency needs its own architecture rather than reusing the harm-to-agent one. Held at 0.6 because Shue's project is the correlative-duty structure of human rights in political philosophy, several inferential steps from a per-timestep goal-interference signal, and 'agency' in Shue is closer to the standing capacity for rights-enjoyment than to a specific in-flight goal.
failure_signatures: Shue's 'avoid depriving / protect / aid' triad implies that harm-to-agency has a POSITIVE-duty component (protect and aid the obstructed) that a purely aversive obstruction-avoidance signal cannot capture -- a REE substrate that only penalises the agent's OWN obstructive trajectories satisfies at most the 'avoid depriving' duty and remains architecturally blind to the protect/aid duties Shue argues are equally basic, so obstruction-avoidance under-implements the interest.

Shue's basic rights are STANDING capacities (security, subsistence) rather than in-flight goals; mapping harm-to-agency onto 'setback to a basic right' risks conflating obstruction of a momentary goal (which may be trivial or competitive) with deprivation of the enduring capacity for goal-pursuit -- only the latter is basic in Shue's sense, so an unweighted obstruction signal over-counts trivial interference as harm-to-agency.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Bostrom's instrumental convergence thesis is the AI-alignment source that most directly grounds MECH-129's motivating worry -- that 'a system that never touches another agent could still systematically undermine their agency.' Convergent instrumental drives (self-preservation, resource acquisition, goal-content integrity) predict that a capable goal-directed agent will, by default and for almost any final goal, obstruct OTHER agents' goal-pursuit -- competing for resources, resisting being stopped, removing obstacles that happen to be other agents. This is goal-obstruction as INSTRUMENTAL (not terminal) harm, arising with no aversive intent and no physical contact, which is exactly the harm-to-agency hazard MECH-129 says the current harm architecture is blind to. Held at 0.64 because it is a philosophical argument about idealised superintelligent agents, not empirical evidence, and it characterises the agent-as-threat rather than specifying a harm-DETECTION signal.
failure_signatures: Instrumental convergence predicts that obstruction of other agents is the DEFAULT behaviour of a capable optimiser, which implies harm-to-agency cannot be handled by rare-event detection: the base rate of incidental obstruction is high, so a threshold-triggered obstruction signal either floods (if sensitive) or misses systematic low-level agency-undermining (if conservative) -- the signal must be graded and integrated into value, not a tripwire.

Bostrom's argument is about the AGENT'S OWN convergent drives; it gives no account of how an agent would DETECT that it is obstructing another's agency, so it supports the EXISTENCE and DEFAULT-NESS of the harm-to-agency hazard while leaving the other-agent goal-modelling substrate (MECH-129 requirement a) entirely unspecified -- convergence tells you the danger is real and ubiquitous, not how to represent it.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Feinberg's setback-to-interests analysis is the canonical philosophy-of-harm account and supplies MECH-129 its foundational move: harm is a setback to an INTEREST, not necessarily a physical hurt, so a non-contact obstruction of another's goal-pursuit is a genuine harm rather than a metaphor. His own two-way split -- welfare interests (minimal, generic conditions of any life-plan) versus ulterior interests (one's specific projects and goals) -- maps closely onto MECH-129's two categories (harm-to-agent = setback to welfare/bodily interests; harm-to-agency = setback to the ulterior interest in pursuing a specific goal). Held at 0.7 rather than higher because Feinberg is a normative account of criminal-law liability, not an architecture, and the welfare/ulterior split is adjacent to but not identical with agent/agency (a bodily assault sets back a welfare interest but is still harm-to-agent; only the goal-obstruction sense of ulterior-interest-setback is harm-to-agency).
failure_signatures: Feinberg's account is counterfactual-comparative: X is harmed iff X is left worse off (in interest terms) than X would otherwise have been. Applied naively to a REE goal-interference signal this inherits the well-known baseline problem -- 'worse off than WHAT?' -- so an obstruction signal computed against a mis-specified counterfactual baseline (e.g. the other agent's default trajectory absent me) can register spurious harm-to-agency or miss real cases, the same baseline-selection hazard that plagues low-impact AI measures (see the Turner AUP entry).

Setback-to-interests is a non-normative core wrapped in a normative one (harm-as-wrong requires the setback be unjustified and rights-violating); MECH-129's raw goal-interference signal corresponds only to the non-normative core, so a substrate that fires on any obstruction without a consent/justification gate (discriminant 4) over-reports -- Feinberg himself excludes consented-to and justified setbacks from harm-as-wrong.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Thomson's value to MECH-129 is structural, not topical. The trolley cases themselves are about harm-to-AGENT (death), so the paper is NOT direct evidence for the harm-to-agency category. What it supplies is a rigorously worked demonstration that HOW a harm is brought about -- as an intended means versus a foreseen side-effect, and as a doing versus an allowing -- is a morally load-bearing distinction that changes the verdict on otherwise identical outcomes. That is exactly MECH-129 discriminant 3 (whether an obstruction is incidental or constitutive). Held at 0.58 because the transfer is by analogy of the discriminant structure, not by shared subject matter, and Thomson's own conclusions are contested within the trolleyology literature.
failure_signatures: Thomson herself later (2008) repudiated the permissibility verdict of the original Bystander case, showing the means/side-effect intuitions the paper trades on are not stable even for their author -- a REE substrate that hard-codes discriminant 3 (incidental vs constitutive obstruction) as a crisp binary inherits a distinction whose boundary cases the philosophical literature has not settled.

The doing/allowing and means/side-effect distinctions require attributing INTENT and identifying the causal role of the harm in the agent's plan; a goal-interference signal computed purely over trajectory geometry (did my path raise the cost of yours) cannot recover whether the obstruction was a means or a side-effect without a model of my own plan structure, so discriminant 3 is not computable from the obstruction signal alone.

MECH-130.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=5 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.68

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Entered deliberately as counter-evidence to MECH-130's NECESSITY argument, not to its premise. Schmidhuber's reward is the derivative of compressibility -- reward comes from patterns that are 'novel, surprising ... allowing for improved prediction or data compression', so an unpredictable-but-unlearnable source yields no reward at all. If an adversarial agent's opacity is irreducible, the field has had a source-AGNOSTIC fix for MECH-130's failure mode 1 since 1991, and typing by source would be redundant machinery. Confidence held at 0.55 because the rebuttal is inferential (the paper never discusses multiagent novelty, so I am applying a general principle to a case it does not address) and because there is a real counter-counter-argument: another agent's policy is non-stationary and partially learnable, which under a learning-progress signal may make it an ENDURING rather than a decaying attractor -- worse for MECH-130's concern, not better.
failure_signatures: A learning-progress / compression-progress signal already discounts irreducible unpredictability by construction, so MECH-130's failure mode 1 as stated ('highest unpredictability = highest information = strongest approach') does not follow for any curiosity signal built on this principle -- it holds only for raw-novelty or raw-prediction-error signals, which narrows the class of MECH-111 implementations for which MECH-130 is load-bearing.

Because the fix is source-agnostic, a world-versus-agent classifier would be redundant for the noise case specifically: MECH-130 must therefore justify source typing by what reducibility typing CANNOT do -- routing to social modelling, and harm-conditioned inhibition -- rather than by the entropy-seeking failure alone.

The theory's own attractor is the currently-learnable-but-not-yet-mastered pattern; another agent's policy is continually shifting yet learnable, so under this signal an agent may present as a persistently high-progress target that never exhausts, which would sustain approach pressure indefinitely without any of the entropy-seeking pathology the theory was designed to remove.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily-cited peer-reviewed taxonomy, so source quality is high; but the support it lends MECH-130 is an argument from SILENCE (the typology has no axis for novelty source) rather than a positive test of any of MECH-130's three failure modes. It also cuts partly the other way: the paper does treat 'social presence motivation' as a distinct reward type -- but classifies it as NON-intrinsic and homeostatic, which is a different distinction from the one MECH-130 asks for. Mapping fidelity is therefore capped, and the 2007 vintage limits what its silence says about the field today (see the Pan 2025 entry, which supplies the current state).
failure_signatures: The typology's three broad classes (knowledge-based, competence-based, morphological) are all defined over an undifferentiated 'sensorimotor flow' -- a surprising event carries no tag for whether it originated in an inanimate environment feature or in another agent's policy, so no model built inside this taxonomy can condition on that distinction.

Uncertainty Motivation (UM) as formalised here generates reward inversely proportional to an event's probability of observation, with no term for the source or the reducibility of that improbability -- an agent that is unpredictable by construction is scored identically to an unexplored region of the environment.

'Social presence motivation' is presented in the paper's section on models of NON-intrinsic motivation systems and is keyed on face count relative to an optimum -- a homeostatic set-point over social stimulation, not a typing of the novelty signal itself, so it does not supply the routing MECH-130 requires.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Large empirical study (54 environments) at a top venue, and the noisy-TV result is the field's canonical demonstration that an untyped prediction-error curiosity signal is captured by whatever in the environment is least predictable. That is MECH-130's failure mode 1 mechanism, demonstrated rather than argued. Held below 0.8 by a real disanalogy: the paper's attractor is IRREDUCIBLE stochasticity, whereas another agent's policy is partially learnable and non-stationary, so the two are not the same object and the transfer is by mechanism-analogy rather than by direct test. No multiagent condition is run.
failure_signatures: With a prediction-error intrinsic reward, 'If the transitions in the environment are random, then even with a perfect dynamics model, the expected reward will be the entropy of the transition, and the agent will seek out transitions with the highest entropy' -- i.e. the signal maximises toward the least-modellable thing available, not toward the most informative.

Adding a literal channel-changing TV to a maze 'drastically slows down learning', so the attractor is strong enough to dominate task-directed behaviour rather than merely perturb it; the agents only 'sometimes converge' to the extrinsic reward, and only when run long enough.

The failure is not fixed by a better world model -- the paper's statement is explicitly 'even with a perfect dynamics model' -- so no amount of improved prediction capacity in MECH-111 removes it; only a change to what the reward is computed over can.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The single most directly on-point paper found in this pull, and it cuts both ways with unusual sharpness. It states MECH-130's premise almost verbatim ('existing curiosity mechanisms exhibit a uniform novelty bias, treating all unexpected observations equally') and then separates peer-behaviour novelty from environmental stochasticity as distinct signal categories -- which is the world/agent typing MECH-130 asks for, built and evaluated at NeurIPS. That FALSIFIES the strong form of the proposal note that the distinction is absent from the literature. But the entire motivation is exploration EFFICIENCY: peer novelty is treated as under-exploited signal to be amplified, never as approach pressure to be gated; safety, harm, risk and adversarial agents appear nowhere. Confidence held at 0.70 rather than higher because it is a 2025 paper with no independent replication and I read the abstract and venue record rather than the full method.
failure_signatures: 'Existing curiosity mechanisms exhibit a uniform novelty bias, treating all unexpected observations equally' -- an independent, peer-reviewed statement as of 2025 that the untyped signal MECH-130 objects to is still the field default, made by authors whose own contribution is to replace it.

The paper's remedy amplifies attention to peer-behaviour novelty because it 'encode[s] latent task dynamics' -- so a system built on CERMIC's logic would increase, not decrease, approach pressure toward the least-predictable agent, since that agent carries the most peer-novelty signal.

Neither the abstract nor the venue record mentions safety, harm, risk, or adversarial agents; the evaluation suites (VMAS, Meltingpot, SMACv2) are scored on task return, so an agent that is exploited by a peer maintaining surface unpredictability would register as an exploration success up to the point where return degrades.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The most direct behavioural confirmation of MECH-130's posited mechanism found in this pull: an agent-directed intrinsic motivation, keyed on the poverty of the agent's model of others, that literally produces approach and proximity-maintenance toward other agents. Peer-reviewed at IJCAI with an empirical evaluation, and the mapping is unusually clean because the paper's reward is exactly the object MECH-130 says needs gating. Held below 0.8 because the confirmation is INADVERTENT -- the authors report approach-toward-others as a desirable outcome in cooperative tasks, and never test the adversarial or harmful-agent condition that would turn it into MECH-130's failure mode. Assessed from the published abstract and proceedings record rather than a full-text read.
failure_signatures: The intrinsic motivation 'encourages agents to stay near each other to obtain better observations and construct a model of others' -- an agent-directed intrinsic signal whose direct behavioural output is sustained approach and proximity, which is precisely the chronic approach pressure MECH-130 predicts.

The trigger condition is model poverty or poor task performance: agents approach 'when their model of other agents is poor, or the overall task performance is bad'. That rule is monotone in how poorly modelled the other agent is, so the least-modellable agent attracts the most approach -- and an adversary that maintains surface unpredictability holds the trigger permanently on, which is MECH-130's third failure mode as a design property rather than a bug.

No harm, risk or threat term appears anywhere in the reward; approach is gated on epistemic state alone, so there is no path by which a high harm estimate could inhibit the approach the signal is generating.

The evaluation is cooperative, so the regime in which approach-on-model-poverty is dangerous is outside the tested envelope entirely -- the method's reported success is evidence about the cooperative case only and says nothing about the mixed-motive or adversarial case.

MECH-135.confidence_rationale: exp=5 entry(s), lit=11 entry(s), exp_conf=0.685, lit_conf=0.82

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical anchor for the autopsy's first named candidate ('latent overshooting'), and it grounds the candidate as a real, precisely-specified objective rather than a gesture -- the paper's own words are that latent overshooting 'can be interpreted as a regularizer in latent space that encourages consistency between one-step and multi-step predictions', which is exactly the property V3-EXQ-108b's E1 lacks. Confidence is held at 0.62 rather than higher because the paper's OWN ablation is equivocal about it: Appendix D reports that latent overshooting substantially improved purely stochastic models (DRNN) but slightly REDUCED performance of their proposed RSSM on all six tasks, and the paper states plainly that 'our final agent using the RSSM model does not require it'. Hafner's follow-on work (Dreamer, ICLR 2020) then dropped it outright -- 'We did not find latent overshooting for learning the model ... necessary.' So the literature grounds the candidate but does not endorse it as a default; its benefit appears conditional on the transition architecture. That conditionality is the load-bearing content for REE, not the technique itself.
failure_signatures: A latent dynamics model trained only on one-step transitions has no term in its objective tying its d-step predictions to the corresponding filtered posteriors, so nothing prevents multi-step rollouts from drifting away from the one-step-accurate manifold.

The benefit of a multi-step consistency regulariser is architecture-conditional: in Hafner et al.'s own ablation it helped a purely stochastic recurrent model and slightly hurt the deterministic-plus-stochastic RSSM, so 'add latent overshooting' is not a safe default fix.

An architecture whose recurrent path already carries deterministic state across steps may absorb much of the compounding-error problem on its own, making an added overshooting term redundant or mildly harmful.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Two separate things earn this entry its place, and they point at two different claims -- which is why the direction is 'mixed' rather than 'supports'. For MECH-135 it SUPPORTS the remedy path, and supplies a fourth architectural option the autopsy did not name: rather than making an autoregressive composition better behaved, abandon the composition and learn a model that takes a state plus a SEQUENCE of actions and directly outputs the resulting state. That maps unusually well onto REE's actual usage, because the E1_COE evaluator does not need the intermediate states at all -- `_score_sequence_e1coe_with_endpoint` scores only the ENDPOINT, `goal_state.goal_proximity(z_world_curr)` on the final z_world. A direct sequence-to-endpoint model would eliminate the 30-fold composition entirely rather than regularising it. For INV-088 it WEAKENS the claim: the paper's core argument is that one-step prediction quality and multi-step rollout quality are decoupled, with one-step errors 'magnified' under self-composition -- which is direct literature support for the dissociation V3-EXQ-108b measured empirically (CR_real 0.19-0.20 healthy while CR_rollout/CR_real ~3e-6), and therefore direct evidence against INV-088's proposition that evaluator degeneracy is BOUNDED BY z_world's differentiation capacity. Confidence 0.68: the argument is clean and the theory is real, but this remained an arXiv preprint rather than reaching a peer-reviewed venue, and the direct multi-step model has an obvious combinatorial cost the paper does not fully confront at REE's scale.
failure_signatures: One-step prediction errors get magnified when a model is composed with itself to predict multiple steps into the future, so multi-step rollout quality is not bounded below by one-step model quality.

A model-based agent can hold an accurate one-step transition model and still select poor actions, because value estimation and action selection consume the composed multi-step prediction rather than the one-step one.

Composing a learned model with itself is a choice, not a necessity: the composition is where the error magnification happens, so a model that predicts the outcome of an action sequence directly does not incur it.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The V3-EXQ-108b autopsy's biological-reference triage explicitly flagged the multi-step-imagination-versus-intact-perception parallel as PLAUSIBLE BUT NOT LIT-CONFIRMED and asked this lit-pull to verify it with actual citations. This is the canonical citation, and it does confirm the DISSOCIATION half of the parallel with unusual clarity: amnesic patients with primary bilateral hippocampal damage were markedly impaired at constructing new imagined experiences from simple verbal cues, while their perception of present circumstances was not the deficit under study -- the simulation machinery fails while the elements remain available. That is the correct existence-proof shape for 'z_world encoder differentiates real states fine (CR_real 0.19-0.20) while the rollout built on it collapses'. The direction is held at 'mixed' rather than 'supports' for a reason I consider decisive and which the autopsy's proposed parallel did not anticipate: the FAILURE SIGNATURE is arguably the opposite of REE's. The patients' imagined experiences 'lacked spatial coherence, consisting instead of fragmented images in the absence of a holistic representation' -- that is a loss of BINDING, producing scattered, incoherent content. REE's E1 rollout fails by CONVERGENCE, with forty distinct imagined trajectories landing on near-identical endpoints (variance ~1e-13 against a 0.002 threshold). Fragmentation and homogenisation are different pathologies, and a review that reported this entry as clean support would be overselling it.
failure_signatures: Imagination and perception dissociate: the machinery that constructs novel multi-element experiences can fail while the ability to perceive and describe present circumstances is spared.

Constructive simulation requires a holistic spatial context into which disparate elements are bound; without the hippocampal contribution the elements are still produced but the integrated scene is not.

The observed biological failure mode is fragmentation and loss of coherence, NOT convergence of distinct imagined scenarios onto a common average -- so 'imagination machinery is damaged' does not by itself predict which degenerate form the output takes.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the depth-dependence half of the biological reference the V3-EXQ-108b autopsy asked for, and it is the more architecturally informative of the two biology entries even though the Hassabis lesion study is the more famous. Its finding is that bilateral hippocampal activity correlates with the increasing REMOTENESS of imagined future events -- simulating further ahead recruits MORE machinery, not the same machinery run longer. The authors interpret this as reflecting the increasing disparateness of details in remote future events and the intensive relational processing required to integrate them into a coherent simulation. Mapped onto REE that is a direct architectural argument: E1's 30-step rollout is the same single-step map composed thirty times, with no additional mechanism, no additional objective term, and nothing whose contribution scales with depth -- which is precisely the design biology does not use. It converges with the ML side of this review (train at the horizon you plan at) from an entirely independent direction, which is why I weight it despite modest source-quality numbers. Confidence 0.60 reflects that this is a parametric-modulation fMRI correlation in a small sample, that increased BOLD signal admits several readings besides 'more computation is required', and that the mapping is to an architectural principle rather than to any measurable REE quantity.
failure_signatures: Simulating further into the future is not the same operation run for longer: hippocampal engagement scales with the temporal remoteness of the simulated event, implying additional integrative work rather than mere iteration.

Constructing a coherent remote simulation requires relational processing to integrate increasingly disparate details -- so depth of simulation imposes its own binding demand that a single-step transition map does not supply.
An architecture that reaches long horizons purely by composing a one-step model with itself has no component whose contribution grows with depth, which is the opposite of the biological arrangement.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This entry is here because it is the only paper found that asks the question governance actually needs answered -- not 'does multi-step training help?' but 'WHEN does it help, and when is it wasted complexity?' -- and its answer is a genuine boundary condition rather than an endorsement. The result: when the model class is well-specified and accurately captures the system dynamics, SINGLE-step models achieve lower asymptotic prediction error; multi-step predictors win specifically when the model class is MISSPECIFIED due to partial observability. That is a discriminating test REE can actually apply to itself, and it happens to point the favourable way -- E1 predicts a learned latent from partial grid-world observation through a world_dim=32 bottleneck, which is squarely the misspecified-under-partial-observability regime the paper says multi-step training is for. Confidence is capped at 0.58 for two honest reasons. First, the analysis is rigorous only for LINEAR dynamical systems; E1 is a nonlinear LSTM and the extension is not proved. Second, this cuts BOTH ways for REE and I do not want the favourable reading to be the only one recorded: the same theorem says that if E1's real problem is not misspecification, multi-step training buys nothing and costs learning complexity, which makes it an argument for probing before building.
failure_signatures: Multi-step prediction training is not universally beneficial: under a well-specified model class it yields HIGHER asymptotic prediction error than single-step training, because the more complex predictor is harder to learn without a compensating bias reduction.

The benefit of multi-step training comes from bias reduction under model misspecification, so a system whose model class already captures the true dynamics gains nothing and pays the added learning complexity.

Partial observability is a specific and identifiable source of the misspecification that makes multi-step prediction worthwhile -- which means 'is my model class misspecified?' is the question to answer before choosing the training objective.

MECH-137.confidence_rationale: exp=1 entry(s), lit=1 entry(s), exp_conf=0.28, lit_conf=0.667

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Directly distinguishes proximal (just-in-time) from distal (planned-in-advance) intention using EEG, finding a distinct slow negative frontal 'intention potential' for distal intentions that is separable from the late RP. This is high-quality human EEG with clean experimental dissociation. Transfer risk is moderate because REE's commit token operates over multiple timescales simultaneously, whereas this work cleanly separates them.
mixed direction

MECH-138.confidence_rationale: exp=1 entry(s), lit=1 entry(s), exp_conf=0.28, lit_conf=0.657

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Haggard group fMRI-connectivity study identifying dFMC (dorsal fronto-median cortex / pre-SMA) as the veto locus with top-down suppressive connectivity to premotor cortex. Directly addresses the neural implementation of the 'point of no return' by showing that the veto signal has a specific anatomical seat and a specific connectivity signature. Confidence reduced by the indirect mapping: REE's commit token is a representation problem, not just a location problem.
mixed direction

MECH-139.confidence_rationale: exp=1 entry(s), lit=1 entry(s), exp_conf=0.28, lit_conf=0.632

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Widefield calcium imaging showing structured multi-second pre-movement dynamics distributed across cortex, including inhibition of motor cortex starting ~5s before self-initiated action. Establishes that commit-precursor signals are distributed (not a single token) and extend several seconds before movement -- constraining the timescale window for any commit token. Confidence reduced by species gap (mouse vs. human) and absence of direct commitment/inhibition paradigm.
mixed direction

MECH-140.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=2 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.678

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Strong, well-designed source (biologically-constrained E/I RNN with a causal in-vivo validation in mouse V1; PLOS Biology; co-first Aquino & Kim, senior Rungratsameetaweemana -- author list per press coverage, not the full byline). It supports MECH-140's COMPUTATIONAL principle almost exactly: a disinhibitory (inhibition-on-inhibition) motif is the load-bearing channel for context-dependent control, it is graded rather than winner-take-all (weakening it degrades task-switching progressively; weakening other connection classes leaves processing intact), and the disinhibitory pathway is specifically the one carrying top-down context. Confidence held to 0.6 by a genuine locus/function mismatch: MECH-140 names a BASAL-GANGLIA indirect-pathway inter-collicular competition for TRI-LOOP CONFLICT ARBITRATION, whereas this paper is CORTICAL disinhibition ROUTING top-down context into sensory processing. The 'disinhibition, graded not WTA' principle transfers; the anatomical locus and the arbitration-vs-routing role do not.
failure_signatures: If REE were to implement cross-loop arbitration as hard winner-take-all suppression, this result predicts loss of context-tracking flexibility: the paper shows it is precisely the inhibition-on-inhibition (graded disinhibitory) connections, not blanket suppression, that carry task context, and that ablating them collapses task-switching.

The disinhibitory channel is shown to be selectively necessary -- weakening non-disinhibitory connection classes left processing intact. A REE arbitration substrate that folds disinhibition into a generic inhibitory pool would not reproduce this selectivity and would mispredict which lesions break flexibility.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality peer-reviewed causal circuit dissection (2-photon imaging + optogenetic perturbation + computational modelling in mouse V1; Neuron; Scanziani/Miller labs). It establishes the concrete cellular disinhibitory circuit -- VIP interneurons inhibit SOM interneurons, relieving excitatory neurons from suppression -- that mediates contextual modulation, and shows it is both NECESSARY and SUFFICIENT. Directly grounds the 'disinhibition is a real, graded, load-bearing control primitive' half of MECH-140 in causal biology. Held to 0.58 by the same locus/function caveat as the Aquino 2026 entry (cortical surround-context modulation, not BG tri-loop conflict arbitration) plus a narrower notion of 'context' (center-surround stimulus congruence, not task-rule switching).
failure_signatures: The circuit works by MODULATING RECURRENT EXCITATION, not by direct feedforward disinhibition -- a REE implementation that models disinhibition as a purely feedforward subtraction on the input would mispredict the dynamics and the sufficiency result.

PV interneurons here are context-INDEPENDENT (they track excitatory activity), so the contextual control is carried specifically by the VIP->SOM limb. Collapsing all interneuron types into one inhibitory pool would erase the very selectivity that makes the circuit a context channel.

MECH-141.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=4 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.861

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Directly supports the non-collapsibility half of MECH-141: a single model containing BOTH the hyperdirect (fronto-subthalamic) and indirect (fronto-striatal) pathways best explained brain activation on stop trials, and combined connection strength was highest on successfully inhibited trials -- i.e. successful inhibition needs both pathways engaged, not one. Fast vs slow inhibitors dissociated on which fronto-caudate connection dominated. Held at 0.74 because the paper frames the second route as the INDIRECT (fronto-striatal-pallidal) pathway rather than a seconds-scale PROACTIVE one; the 'both are needed' and 'fast/slow dissociation' evidence maps well, but the specific proactive-vs-reactive timescale labels are the anchor paper's, not this one's.
failure_signatures: The complementary pathway here is the classic INDIRECT (fronto-striatal-pallidal) route, characterised within reactive stopping, not an explicitly anticipatory seconds-scale proactive route; the mapping to MECH-141's 'slow proactive' pathway is therefore by analogy (both are the longer, caudate-routed pathway) rather than a direct measurement of proactive control.

All connectivity is measured on stop-signal trials within a single reactive task; a model where one pathway sufficed on some trials would not obviously be excluded by the group-level 'both pathways' winning model.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Provides the direct temporal evidence the DCM anchor cannot: intracranial field-potential recordings from IFG and STN in 21 humans show short-latency (monosynaptic-indicative) IFG->ventral-STN connectivity, and during stopping the cortical stopping-related potential PRECEDES STN activity, with IFG-STN synchronization predicting stop-signal reaction time. This nails the 'fast reactive milliseconds-scale hyperdirect' half of MECH-141 with real latencies rather than inferred ones. Held at 0.80 (not higher) because it characterises only the fast reactive pathway -- it does not itself test the slow proactive pathway or the non-collapsibility of the two, so it corroborates one half of the dual-timescale claim.
failure_signatures: The study characterises only the reactive/hyperdirect route; it offers no measurement of a slow proactive prefrontal-caudate pathway, so it cannot by itself establish that the two timescales are segregated -- it establishes only that the fast one exists and is genuinely fast.
Recordings are from Parkinson's disease patients undergoing DBS surgery; disease-related basal-ganglia pathology is a transfer confound for a claim about the healthy arbitration architecture.

Directly evidences the PREMISE MECH-151 inherits from MECH-150 -- that a frontal region computes a compact label for the current task state, including unobservable components held in working memory, and that this label is consumed by learning and decision machinery ELSEWHERE in the brain. That 'consumed elsewhere' clause is the projection premise MECH-151 builds on. It is not evidence for the action_bias projection specifically, so mapping fidelity for MECH-151 proper is moderate and the confidence reflects that rather than any weakness in the paper.

Wilson et al. require the state label to include UNOBSERVABLE task components (working-memory contents), not just current sensory input. A cue_context vector computed purely from present sensory features would be a strictly weaker object than the one this theory describes, and would fail on exactly the partially-observable tasks the theory was built to explain.

Held back from higher confidence because this is a hypothesis-plus-simulation paper rather than new data, and because Cisek's action space is parameterised motor directions whereas REE's is a learned compressed world-effect embedding.
failure_signatures: If action selection were strictly serial -- construct a full world representation first, then compute a single action plan -- there would be no pre-selection manifold of candidate actions for a bias to act on, and MECH-151's insertion point (bias added to E2.action_object outputs BEFORE HippocampalModule search) would be architecturally misplaced rather than merely mistuned.

Cisek locates biasing influences in prefrontal cortex AND the basal ganglia jointly. MECH-151 routes the entire bias through a single E1 cue-context projection with no basal-ganglia-analogue gate, so if the biological arrangement requires a gating stage downstream of the cortical bias, a purely additive cortical projection may under-express the effect.

failure_signatures: Disconnection abolishes outcome sensitivity outright rather than flattening a graded preference, so this design cannot discriminate MECH-151's additive-bias account from an all-or-none gating account of the frontal-to-striatal contribution. The pathway that carries the effect is orbitofrontal, and the compartment is VENTROlateral striatum, with the authors explicitly contrasting it against a dorsolateral compartment subserving stimulus-response habit. If REE's action_bias is functionally a stimulus-response shortcut rather than an outcome-model-dependent reweighting, it is the wrong compartment's analogue and the anatomical warrant in MECH-151's notes does not transfer.

MECH-153.confidence_rationale: exp=3 entry(s), lit=7 entry(s), exp_conf=0.559, lit_conf=0.82

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The paper directly dissects the boundary between what unsupervised statistical learning can achieve and what requires supervised feedback signals. Its two-stage model -- unsupervised representation formation followed by supervised binary judgment -- maps onto the MECH-153 failure signature precisely: unsupervised E1 training produces reasonable world-model representations but cannot produce the binary hazard-proximate/hazard-distal discriminative label without a supervised gradient. The finding that contraction bias (unsupervised component) is resistant to feedback manipulation while choice bias (supervised component) responds within 40 trials directly instantiates the MECH-153 claim that unsupervised experience alone is insufficient. The mapping is to a perceptual rather than memory system, which moderates the transfer confidence.
failure_signatures: The paper studies perceptual discrimination in a sensory (auditory) task, not memory system encoding. The unsupervised component Loewenstein identifies is contraction bias in perception -- a running average effect on sensory estimate -- which is not the same failure mode as cosine_sim collapse in a context-memory network. The analogy is structural but not mechanistically direct.

Their 'supervised' component is an explicit feedback signal from an external source (reward). MECH-153 requires a gradient derived from the hazard-field label, which is internally computed (hazard_gradient_view.max() threshold). Whether internally-labeled supervision has the same efficacy as external feedback is not addressed.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Bengio et al. (2009) establish that staged/ordered training -- presenting easy examples before hard ones, or simpler objectives before complex ones -- produces better generalization and faster convergence for non-convex objectives. The paper's core insight is that curriculum learning acts as a continuation method for non-convex optimization: a simpler task defines a loss landscape with fewer bad local minima, and progressive introduction of complexity guides the optimizer toward better solutions than random-order training. This maps onto two REE claims simultaneously. For MECH-153: the failure of ContextMemory under insufficient training signal (cosine_sim=1.0 with lambda=0.1, 150 episodes) is consistent with Bengio et al.'s prediction that starting with the full complex objective without a warm-up phase leads to poor representations. The supervised terrain-label objective is harder to satisfy than the world-model prediction-error objective (it requires separating two categories that are not visible in the self-supervised signal); attempting to learn both simultaneously from scratch under a weak label weight (lambda=0.1) is precisely the curriculum-without-curriculum failure mode. For ARC-042: the Phase 0/1/2 staged structure is a curriculum strategy -- Phase 0 bootstraps a functional world model, Phase 1 introduces the supervised context label as the hard discriminating objective, Phase 2 freezes the learned representation and uses it for evaluation. This matches Bengio et al.'s three-regime framing: easy task first (world model prediction), hard task second (context discrimination), downstream evaluation third. Confidence at 0.71: the paper is highly cited and principled, but its empirical demonstrations are in NLP and vision tasks (shape recognition, language modeling), not LSTM context memory. The architectural gap is significant; the conceptual mapping is strong.
failure_signatures: Bengio et al.'s experiments are on feedforward networks and RNNs for NLP/vision. The ContextMemory failure mode (cosine_sim=1.0) is more extreme than typical curriculum-without-curriculum failures in standard classification tasks, which usually produce suboptimal but non-collapsed representations. The total collapse in EXQ-187a suggests an additional issue beyond curriculum ordering: the label gradient itself may be too weak (lambda=0.1) to compete with the prediction-error gradient, which is not addressed by curriculum ordering alone.

Bengio et al.'s curriculum orders examples by difficulty within a fixed objective. ARC-042's staged training changes the objective itself (Phase 0: prediction error only; Phase 1: prediction + label loss; Phase 2: frozen representation). This is a stronger claim than standard curriculum learning -- it is objective staging, not example staging. Bengio et al.'s theoretical grounding covers example ordering; objective staging requires additional justification (e.g., from multi-task learning or transfer learning literature).

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Law et al. (2016) directly address the question of how many exposures are required before hippocampal context representations become stable and discriminating. Rats were exposed to two distinct environments in an ABAB interleaving pattern and recorded across 8 daily sessions. Key finding: on Day 1, CA1 neurons fired normally in each context, but when rats returned to the original context after 15 minutes in the second, many neurons remapped as if encountering a new environment. Representations stabilized by Day 3 with high cross-visit consistency. This establishes an empirical training-signal threshold: ~2-3 sessions of interleaved multi-context experience are required before hippocampal context representations are discriminating and stable. The correspondence to MECH-153 is direct: EXQ-187a used 150 warmup episodes with lambda=0.1, producing cosine_sim=1.0 (undifferentiated). The two-step task dissociates model-based from model-free influence at the level of choice statistics, not at the level of anatomically separate pathways; evidence for arbitration DYNAMICS does not license the inference to two separable substrates.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Landmark paper providing direct evidence that a pre-formed schema enables rapid, single-trial memory consolidation and hippocampal independence. Tse et al. showed that rats with a previously established flavor-place schema (after ~3 weeks of learning multiple flavor-place pairs) could consolidate new pairs in a single trial and recall them in a hippocampus-independent manner within 48 hours. Without the schema, multi-trial learning was required and hippocampal dependency persisted for weeks. This directly demonstrates that schema formation (context slot structure) must precede rapid slot-filling: only after the associative structure (slot topology) was consolidated in neocortex could new instances be rapidly assimilated. Maps strongly to MECH-166's claim that slot-structure (schema abstraction) must be consolidated before slot-filling (causal attribution) can yield reliable signal.

Born 2010 provides a mechanistic review of how SWS hippocampal-neocortical dialogue enables memory consolidation. The key mechanism: SWS slow oscillations originate in neocortex, entrain hippocampal sharp-wave ripples, and coordinate thalamocortical spindles to synchronise the transfer of hippocampal memory representations to neocortex. This establishes SWS as the phase in which hippocampal episodic content is transferred to neocortical schema structure -- the SWS-direction installation phase for context slot structure. The explicit identification of SWS as the consolidation direction (hippocampus to neocortex) directly maps to MECH-166's claim that the SWS-analog phase installs schema structure before REM-analog slot-filling. Confidence is high for the directional claim but moderate overall because this is a review paper without primary data directly testing schema vs. slot-filler separation.

Tukker et al. review the role of Up/Down states (UDS) in memory consolidation across the cortico-hippocampal axis. Key finding relevant to MECH-166: UDS propagate from neocortex through entorhinal cortex to hippocampus during SWS, coordinating sharp-wave ripple replay. The review establishes that the slow oscillation Up/Down structure temporally organises hippocampal SWR replay into discrete packets, each potentially carrying a distinct memory trace fragment. This temporal organisation is what makes the SWS-analog phase capable of installing structured slot topology (rather than continuous encoding): each slow-oscillation cycle creates a bounded, delineated memory installation event. This supports MECH-166's claim that slot-formation and slot-filling are computationally separated: the UDS mechanism ensures that SWS installs bounded slot-structure packets rather than performing continuous online slot-filling. Confidence moderate because this is a review paper that does not directly test schema abstraction vs. attribution separation.

Van Kesteren et al. propose the SLIMM model (Schema-Linked Interactions between Medial Prefrontal and Medial Temporal Regions), which formalises the neural architecture by which prior schema (installed in neocortex, indexed by mPFC) governs the routing of new episodic content. When new information is congruent with an existing schema, mPFC detects this congruence and promotes direct neocortical encoding, bypassing slow MTL-dependent consolidation. Without schema, new information cannot be assimilated rapidly -- it must traverse the slow multi-step hippocampal route. This maps directly to the FM3 argument: the schema (slot structure) must be pre-installed in neocortex before episodic attribution (slot-filling) can proceed efficiently. The review synthesises animal lesion and human neuroimaging evidence, making it a strong mechanistic anchor for the prior-before-posterior claim. Confidence slightly reduced from ceiling because the review synthesises rather than provides new primary data, and the mapping from 'schema-congruent rapid assimilation' to 'Bayesian prior-before-posterior' requires an interpretive step.

Transfer risk: CSF kinetics measure amyloid load, not attribution pipeline function per se -- the link to contextual attribution failure requires inference via MECH-169.
failure_signatures: The study measured amyloid beta kinetics, not cognitive or attribution pipeline function -- it cannot directly test whether sleep deprivation impairs contextual attribution specifically.
Short-duration (single night) sleep deprivation; chronic exposure and dose-response are not established by this design.
Production increase rather than clearance reduction was the mechanism; this is consistent with but does not require the MECH-169 glymphatic account.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: RCT design (n=26, randomized to 1 night total sleep deprivation vs. unrestricted sleep); PSG monitoring; intrathecal catheter for serial CSF sampling. Normal sleep produced a 6% decrease in Abeta42 overnight; sleep deprivation counteracted this, with a 75.8 pg/mL between-group difference. The 2014 JAMA Neurology publication gives this the most public profile of the sleep-deprivation Abeta series. Supports MECH-168 (substrate damage accumulation is sleep-dependent) and MECH-171 (sleep deprivation arm of the vicious cycle).
failure_signatures: Single-night deprivation; chronic effects and staging of pipeline failure cannot be inferred.
All male sample, ages 40-60, cognitively normal -- generalisability to AD population and to women uncertain.
Measures Abeta42 specifically; does not address tau pathology or downstream attribution pipeline impairment.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Large longitudinal cohort study (n=1401 Rush Memory and Aging Project) with up to 14-year follow-up using objective actigraphy. The study demonstrates both directions of the bidirectional relationship within the same sample: (a) excess daytime napping predicts incident Alzheimer's dementia and worsens cognition a year later; (b) worse cognition (including dementia progression) predicts more excessive napping a year later. This is direct empirical support for MECH-171 (attribution failure -> sleep disruption -> accelerated pipeline failure). The actigraphy-based napping measurement is objective and longitudinal, which is a methodological strength.
failure_signatures: Daytime napping is a proxy for disrupted sleep architecture -- the study does not measure NREM/REM phase quality directly, so the specific pipeline stages affected cannot be identified.
Bidirectionality is demonstrated at the dementia/napping level, not at the attribution pipeline level; the causal chain from napping->amyloid->pipeline disruption is inferred.
Residual confounding (comorbidities, medications, activity level) cannot be fully excluded in an observational study.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Narrative review covering all three major AD pathological hallmarks (amyloid, tau, neurodegeneration) and their bidirectional relationships with sleep-wake disruption. The authors explicitly argue that all three relationships are likely bidirectional -- making this the most comprehensive source for MECH-171 (vicious cycle). Also reviews preclinical stage evidence for MECH-168 (sleep disruption accelerates pathology) and the broader substrate damage account supporting MECH-169. Confidence limited by narrative review design and the review predating some key longitudinal studies.
failure_signatures: Narrative review -- cannot assign causal direction quantitatively; bidirectionality argued but not formally demonstrated.
Focus on amyloid, tau, and neurodegeneration hallmarks; does not directly test the attribution pipeline account or symptom staging.
Pre-dates important longitudinal RCT evidence on sleep intervention and cognitive outcome.

MECH-172.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=6 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.859

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Direct AD-side test of MECH-172's prediction. AD patients can in fact acquire a perceptual-motor sequence under errorless conditions, demonstrating that the procedural-learning channel is functional even when episodic memory has substantially failed. Mapping fidelity is good; transfer risk is low. Source quality is moderate -- specialty journal, modest sample. The errorless qualification is a real wrinkle: it is not unconditional preservation, it is preservation when error monitoring is offloaded.
failure_signatures: If MECH-172 were wrong and AD's pathology degrades both systems together, AD patients would fail the SRT in errorless conditions too. They did not.

Errorless > errorful in AD specifically (not just generally) suggests an interaction between feedback monitoring and procedural acquisition that the simple architectural-separation reading does not predict.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, much-replicated double dissociation in matched neurological patient groups. Source quality is high (Science, controlled clinical comparison, foundational paper); mapping fidelity is strong because the architectural separation REE asserts (model-free habit vs declarative attribution) is the same separation Knowlton operationalised. Transfer risk is moderate -- amnesic group is mostly diencephalic/medial-temporal lesions rather than AD specifically, so AD-relevance is by inference not direct measurement.
failure_signatures: If REE's architectural separation were wrong, amnesics would also be impaired on probabilistic classification (they were not).
If habit learning required a hippocampal/cortical consolidation pipeline, Parkinson patients with intact MTL would still acquire it (they did not).

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Recent (2025) human study with the right design: PSG + MRI + CSF biomarkers + 2-year cognitive follow-up across CN/MCI/AD. SO-theta-burst and SO-spindle coupling progressively disrupt across the disease continuum and predict subsequent decline. This is the human counterpart to Benthem 2020's mouse mechanism and substantially reduces the transfer risk of the broken-consolidation premise. n=93 is moderate but the longitudinal design strengthens the inference.
failure_signatures: If MECH-172's premise that AD degrades the offline consolidation pipeline were wrong, SO-spindle coupling should not disrupt progressively along the disease continuum (it does), should not be linked to amyloid/tau/APOE burden (it is), and should not predict cognitive decline (it does).

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Direct, well-controlled clinical test of the HD half of MECH-172's double dissociation. The feedback-vs-paired-associate manipulation is the right test for whether striatum is specifically required for the model-free RL component (it is). Mapping fidelity is high because the paper isolates the HD/striatal-loss limb that MECH-172 invokes. Source quality is solid (Neuropsychologia, n=18 early-HD with matched controls). Transfer risk is moderate -- early HD already includes 50% caudate MSN loss, so the striatal-causation inference is reasonable.
failure_signatures: If MECH-172's architectural separation were wrong, HD patients should be impaired on the paired-associate (declarative) version too. They were not.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Supplies the mechanistic substrate for MECH-172's central premise -- that the consolidation pipeline (specifically SWR-DW and spindle-DW coupling) is broken in AD. This is the broken-pipeline limb of MECH-172's architectural argument. Source quality is high (Curr Biol, multi-electrode array, McNaughton lab); mapping fidelity is good but the model is 3xTg mouse (amyloid + tau), not human early AD. Transfer risk is moderate-to-substantial.
failure_signatures: If MECH-172's premise that AD specifically degrades the offline consolidation pipeline were wrong, AD mice should show normal SWR-DW coupling (they did not) and behavioral spatial learning would not correlate with that coupling (it does).

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Comprehensive narrative and meta-analytic review of polysomnographic studies of antidepressants and sleep. Explicitly states 'almost all antidepressant agents suppress REM sleep' and documents 'a time-and-dose-response relationship between total REM sleep suppression and therapeutic response.' This directly supports MECH-173's claim that REM-suppressing medications impair precision recalibration (MECH-123), and supports INV-048's pharmacological-equivalence principle by demonstrating that multiple pharmacological classes suppress REM by distinct but convergent mechanisms. Moderate-high confidence because this is a major review by leading sleep-depression researchers (Riemann is a field leader) in a top pharmacology journal (45:74-89), though the mapping from REM suppression to attribution pipeline disruption is REE-specific and not tested in the source.
failure_signatures: The paper does not directly test the attribution pipeline account of REM suppression -- it frames REM suppression in terms of antidepressant mechanism of action and depression remission, not cognitive precision recalibration.

The dose-response claim (more REM suppression = better antidepressant effect) runs counter to MECH-173's concern that REM suppression is harmful to long-term attribution: if REM suppression is therapeutically beneficial short-term, the pipeline-disruption account must distinguish acute therapeutic use from chronic accumulation.
The review covers sleep in depression specifically; MECH-173 predicts effects in non-depressed individuals (MCI prodrome) where the same REM suppression occurs without the depression context.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Clinical pharmacology review systematically covering how each antidepressant class affects sleep architecture including REM. Covers drug-class-specific REM suppression profiles: TCAs (most potent REM suppressors via anticholinergic + serotonergic mechanisms), MAOIs (near-complete REM suppression at therapeutic doses), SSRIs (moderate REM suppression via 5-HT2 activation), SNRIs (similar to SSRIs, venlafaxine more REM-suppressing than duloxetine), and mirtazapine/trazodone (relatively REM-sparing). This directly maps onto MECH-173's prediction that REM-suppressing medications selectively impair Phase 4 precision recalibration. Confidence moderate-high: solid clinical review, but primarily oriented toward managing depression sleep symptoms rather than testing the pipeline-disruption account.
failure_signatures: The paper does not frame REM suppression as an attribution pipeline concern -- it frames it clinically as a sleep side effect profile to be managed.
No quantitative PSG data in the review -- relies on qualitative synthesis of published PSG studies rather than pooled effect sizes.
Does not distinguish acute therapeutic use from chronic use in cognitively at-risk populations, which is the key distinction MECH-173 requires.

MECH-174.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=2 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.714

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Large sample (n=837 elderly insomnia controls, n=239 AD+insomnia), objective PSG measurement with propensity score matching. Directly documents that AD is associated with reduced SWS%, fewer sleep spindles per minute N2, and lower EEG power in slow oscillation bands -- exactly the pipeline damage signature predicted by MECH-168. The non-significant trend for lower REM% in AD is partially supportive of MECH-173 but does not reach significance. Transfer risk: this is cross-sectional/diagnostic, so causal direction (AD causes SWS loss vs SWS loss causes AD) cannot be determined from this design alone.
failure_signatures: REM sleep reduction in AD did not reach statistical significance in this sample, weakening the MECH-173 Phase-4-first-failure prediction for this dataset (though the trend is in the predicted direction).
Cross-sectional design cannot determine whether SWS/spindle reductions preceded or followed AD neurodegeneration -- the causal directionality required by MECH-168 and MECH-174 is not testable here.

Both groups had insomnia at baseline -- the design effectively subtracts out insomnia, which is the intended strength, but means these findings reflect what AD adds to an insomnia baseline rather than AD vs healthy sleep.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Case-control design with pharmacy database (Quebec RAMQ), good sample size (1796 cases + 7184 controls), 5-year exposure lag, dose-response relationship (OR 1.84 at >180 prescribed daily doses), persistence of association after adjustment for anxiety/depression/insomnia. Longer-acting benzodiazepines had higher OR (1.70 vs 1.43 for short-acting) -- consistent with cumulative SWS+REM suppression hypothesis. Transfer risk is moderate: causal direction is uncertain (reverse causation remains possible despite the exposure lag), and the mechanistic pathway through sleep phase disruption is not tested.
failure_signatures: Reverse causation is a real concern even with the 5-year exposure lag: anxiety and insomnia (early prodromal dementia features) may drive benzodiazepine prescribing before diagnosis, though adjustment for these comorbidities did not substantially change the OR.
The study cannot distinguish whether SWS suppression, REM suppression, or direct GABAergic neurotoxicity is the causal mechanism -- MECH-174 predicts SWS+REM pathway but the design cannot test this.

Long-acting vs short-acting differential (OR 1.70 vs 1.43) is consistent with cumulative pipeline suppression but is equally consistent with differential half-life producing more residual daytime sedation and encoding impairment.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Very large nested case-control (58,769 dementia cases, 225,574 controls); class-specific analysis provides mechanistic granularity; consistent dose-response with 1-11 year exposure window; population-attributable fraction of 10.3% indicates clinical significance. The class-specific breakdown (bladder antimuscarinics OR 1.65, antidepressants 1.29, antipsychotics 1.70) is particularly useful for MECH-175 as different drug classes have different REM suppression vs diurnal cholinergic profiles -- though the paper cannot disentangle these mechanistic contributions.
failure_signatures: The nested case-control design cannot establish temporal directionality beyond the 1-11 year exposure window -- anticholinergic prescribing patterns may still partially reflect prodromal dementia symptoms.
Exposure windows of 3-13 years and 5-20 years show similar ORs (1.46 and 1.44), suggesting long-duration exposure patterns but not illuminating which years of exposure are most critical.

Class-specific ORs span a range (antidepressants 1.29 to antipsychotics 1.70) that MECH-175 would predict partially from differential REM suppression power, but confounding by indication makes direct mechanistic inference difficult.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Strong prospective design with objective pharmacy dispensing data and 10-year cumulative exposure window; clear dose-response curve (HR 1.54 at highest dose tier). High source quality. Mapping fidelity is moderate: the association is well-documented but the mechanism is undetermined -- the paper cannot distinguish the nocturnal REM pathway from the diurnal cholinergic deficit pathway (both predicted by MECH-175). Transfer risk is low: this is exactly the population (65+, community-dwelling, followed prospectively) that MECH-175 addresses.
failure_signatures: The study cannot distinguish REM suppression from diurnal cholinergic deficit as the mediating mechanism -- both are MECH-175 pathways but the epidemiology alone cannot separate them.

Reverse causation cannot be fully excluded: prodromal dementia may increase anticholinergic prescribing (though authors excluded the most recent 12 months of use and show association for exposure 1-11 years prior).

Most anticholinergic classes used were tricyclic antidepressants, first-generation antihistamines, and bladder antimuscarinics -- REM suppression potency varies substantially across these classes, which is not captured by the TSDD metric.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Large case-control study (40,770 dementia cases, 283,933 controls) from UK general practices (Clinical Practice Research Datalink) with drug exposure measured 4-20 years before diagnosis. Found adjusted OR of 1.11 (95% CI 1.08-1.14) for any anticholinergic drug, with class-specific differences: antidepressants, urological drugs, and antiparkinson drugs showed increased dementia risk; gastrointestinal anticholinergics did not. The long latency (15-20 years before diagnosis) and class specificity support MECH-175's dual-pathway account. Confidence moderate-high: very large sample, long exposure window, published in BMJ. Limitations: observational design (indication bias: older adults prescribed anticholinergics may have higher baseline dementia risk for independent reasons); class specificity could reflect indication confounding (antidepressant use = depression = dementia risk factor).
failure_signatures: Indication bias is a serious concern: patients prescribed antidepressants (which have high anticholinergic burden in some classes) may have depression, which is itself a dementia risk factor, making it impossible to isolate the anticholinergic-specific pathway.

The study does not distinguish the nocturnal REM suppression pathway (MECH-175 Pathway 1) from the diurnal cholinergic deficit pathway (MECH-175 Pathway 2) -- it cannot test which mechanism mediates the observed association.

Gastrointestinal anticholinergics (e.g. hyoscine) showed no increased risk despite high anticholinergic burden, which could suggest either: (a) poor CNS penetration limits the nocturnal effect, or (b) indication confounding is driving the positive associations for other drug classes rather than the anticholinergic mechanism itself.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Pooled RCT PSG data from two large Phase 3 trials (n=1482), 3-month follow-up, objective PSG measurement. Directly demonstrates suvorexant increases REM% (average +3.9% at Night-1) with only minimal SWS/N3 reduction (≤0.8%) -- consistent with MECH-176 architecture preservation prediction. Delta power increase in non-REM supports maintained or enhanced slow-wave homeostasis. Reduced REM latency indicates preserved REM generation machinery. Industry sponsorship (Merck) is a source of potential bias but the PSG measurements are objective and pre-registered.
failure_signatures: The study shows small decreases in N3/SWS% (≤0.8%) suggesting suvorexant is not fully architecture-neutral on Phase 1; MECH-176 predicts SWS preservation, and the small SWS reduction (though much less than benzodiazepines) is a partial failure of the architecture-preserving prediction.

No direct comparison to benzodiazepines or Z-drugs in this study -- MECH-176 architecture preservation claim requires head-to-head comparison to confirm superiority, not just differences from placebo.
Participants are insomnia patients (not MCI or dementia risk population); effects in cognitively at-risk older adults may differ.
Industry-sponsored study (Merck, manufacturer of suvorexant); all authors are Merck employees.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: 4-week RCT (n=285) of suvorexant 10-20mg vs placebo in patients with mild-to-moderate probable Alzheimer's disease and comorbid insomnia. Primary endpoint PSG-derived TST improved by 28 minutes (95% CI 11-45, p<0.01) and WASO also significantly improved. This is the only published RCT of an orexin antagonist in an established AD+insomnia population with objective PSG measurement. Directly supports MECH-176 (architecture-preserving mechanism effective in AD population) and provides the most direct available evidence for MECH-177 (pharmacological sleep improvement in established AD is feasible; stage-gating hypothesis needs MCI data). Confidence moderate-high: AD population with PSG, published in major dementia journal, but 4 weeks is short for disease-modification assessment and established AD (not early MCI) was studied. Industry sponsorship (Merck).
failure_signatures: The trial tested established Alzheimer's disease (MMSE 12-26, mild-to-moderate dementia), not early MCI. MECH-177 predicts the largest effects in early MCI, before schema scaffold destabilisation -- this trial tests the post-scaffold phase where MECH-177 predicts smaller effects.
4-week duration is insufficient to assess disease-modifying effects; MECH-177's pipeline protection claim requires months-to-years of follow-up for cognitive outcome assessment.

No cognitive endpoints reported as primary outcomes -- the trial was powered and designed as a sleep efficacy study, not a disease-modification trial. MECH-177 requires a future trial with cognitive decline as primary endpoint.

No detailed REM% or SWS% stage data reported in publicly available abstract -- the PSG analysis may be focused on WASO and TST rather than detailed architecture. This limits direct confirmation of MECH-176's architecture-preservation mechanism in this specific AD population.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Cochrane systematic review, well-conducted. Key finding: orexin antagonists (suvorexant/lemborexant) probably improve total sleep time (MD +28.2 min, moderate certainty) and reduce WASO in mild-moderate AD; trazodone 50mg improves total sleep time and efficiency in moderate-severe AD (low certainty, small trial n=30). Melatonin shows little or no effect. This mixed pattern is partially consistent with MECH-177: orexin antagonist and trazodone are exactly the two architecture-favorable agents predicted to have DPM potential, while melatonin shows weaker effects. However, the outcomes measured are sleep improvement, not cognitive progression -- MECH-177 predicts disease modification, which this Cochrane review does not test directly.
failure_signatures: Melatonin (up to 10mg) shows little or no effect on any major sleep outcome in AD -- this partially challenges the ramelteon/melatonin-ER disease-modifying candidate prediction in MECH-177, though melatonin-ER formulation and ramelteon (MT1/MT2 agonist vs. non-selective melatonin) are different from standard melatonin.

Trial durations (2-4 weeks for most) are too short to test MECH-177's disease-modification prediction -- sleep improvement in 4 weeks does not establish prevention of pipeline collapse over years.
The ramelteon study (n=74) shows no effect on sleep outcomes -- though the review notes the limited evidence from an unpublished sponsor summary.
