Reality filtering is fast (200-300 ms) and source monitoring slow (>400 ms) and less accurate; a retention read-out that relies on the slow, error-prone content check to gate actionability inherits its error rate.

MECH-489.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=5 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.825

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Human psychophysiology with two convergent and mechanistically distinct indices (startle potentiation for defensive activation, fear bradycardia for attentive orienting), which were positively correlated with one another -- that convergence is what makes the 'immobility is an ATTENTIVE state' reading solid rather than inferential. Supports MECH-489's claim structure directly: the claim asserts freeze-arrest coupled to an orient/identify step, and this is evidence that biological defensive immobility is exactly such a coupled state rather than pure motor arrest. Mapping fidelity is good because the claim-level assertion (freeze co-occurs with active monitoring) is what was measured. Held at 0.72 rather than higher because the paradigm is conditioned distal threat in a laboratory, and because the study indexes attention physiologically rather than demonstrating that information is actually acquired and used.
failure_signatures: An implementation in which the arrest state performs no sensory-sampling change, no active localisation and no belief update is not modelling attentive immobility -- it is modelling the motor-arrest half of a state whose defining property in the biology is that motor arrest and heightened sensory intake occur TOGETHER.

If the arrest is genuinely attentive, the organism's defensive sensitivity should be ELEVATED during immobility rather than merely held constant; a substrate whose arrest is a pure no-op predicts no such elevation.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative synthesis in a top venue proposing that the central amygdala uses mutually inhibitory, winner-takes-all circuits to switch between discrete defensive modes organised along threat imminence. Supports two structural commitments MECH-489 makes: that post-arrest action selection is a selection among mutually exclusive defensive modes (approach / withdraw / resume) rather than a continuous adjustment, and that phasic and chronic defensive states are architecturally distinct (the MECH-489 vs MECH-279 boundary). Confidence is 0.70 rather than higher because this is a review/perspective rather than a single decisive experiment, and because the organising variable it proposes -- threat imminence, learned through association -- is not the variable MECH-489 gates on.
failure_signatures: If defensive modes are selected by mutually inhibitory winner-takes-all competition, a decision layer that resolves to the same mode on every single override event is not exhibiting selection at all -- a winner-takes-all circuit with a structurally biased input produces exactly that degenerate signature.

Defensive mode is organised by threat imminence and prior association; a mechanism that gates only on instantaneous onset magnitude has no representation of imminence and so cannot reproduce the mode ordering the biology shows.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Very strong source (Neuron, circuit dissection with identified parallel superior colliculus to basolateral amygdala routes, plus a behavioural-phenotype split). Direction is mixed and the reasoning matters: it SUPPORTS MECH-489's assertion that defensive-response termination is a governed process rather than a fixed schedule -- habituation here is an active, circuit-mediated, arousal-modulated computation with stable individual differences, not stimulus-response fatigue -- while simultaneously indicating that the governing variable is AROUSAL STATE rather than epistemic resolution, which is not what MECH-489's 'epistemic-sufficiency override' asserts. Confidence held to 0.58 by the binding mapping problem: this is habituation ACROSS repeated stimulus presentations, whereas MECH-489's release is WITHIN a single arrest episode. Those are different timescales and the paper does not bridge them.
failure_signatures: Response decrement that is governed by arousal state and shows stable individual differences cannot be reproduced by a fixed decay constant applied uniformly -- a substrate whose release is a pure signal-decay timer predicts no between-individual variation in habituation rate and no arousal dependence, both of which are observed.
Two animals receiving identical stimulus sequences diverge into persistent-escape and rapid-habituation phenotypes, so the decrement cannot be a function of the stimulus history alone.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Review of human motor defensive reactions to violence-related threat using stabilometry, distinguishing three distinct immobility types within a defensive cascade, of which attentive immobility is one and peritraumatic tonic immobility -- strongly associated with PTSD severity -- is another. Supports MECH-489's registered boundary against MECH-279 with human data, which is a different and complementary line of support from the rodent circuit work in this directory. Confidence 0.68: the taxonomic distinction is well established and the human-clinical grounding is genuinely valuable for a claim about a PAG-subject mechanism, but the paper is a review, the stabilometry evidence base is comparatively small, and the immobility types are distinguished largely descriptively rather than by dissociating mechanism.
failure_signatures: Collapsing distinct immobility types into a single freeze mechanism loses the clinically load-bearing distinction between an attentive, reversible, orienting immobility and a tonic, unresponsive peritraumatic immobility that predicts PTSD severity -- these have different triggers, different durations and different outcomes.
A phasic arrest whose duration is governed only by decay of the eliciting signal has no way to represent the transition into tonic immobility, which is not a longer version of the same state.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: High source quality -- Current Biology, cell-type-specific (Kcnip2+) ablation AND selective optogenetic activation, i.e. both necessity and sufficiency for the behaviour, with recordings showing the cells encode looming size. The direction is genuinely mixed rather than a clean weakens because MECH-489's trigger is stated as a DISJUNCTION: unsigned prediction-error surprise OR sensory-discriminative harm. This paper weakens the first disjunct and supports the second. Confidence is held at 0.62 rather than higher because mapping fidelity is the binding constraint: REE has no retina and no visual looming feature, so the transfer is at the level of channel ARCHITECTURE (dedicated feature-specific line vs generic magnitude signal), not of the specific detector.
failure_signatures: A defensive-orienting trigger built on a generic, modality-agnostic surprise magnitude will under-fire on ethologically specific threat events, because the biological system does not route those events through a generic salience channel at all -- it routes them through a dedicated feature-tuned line that is separable from novelty.

Ablating the dedicated channel abolishes the defensive response even though generic visual novelty and stimulus change remain intact, showing the two signals are dissociable and that novelty alone is not sufficient to elicit the response.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the strongest available direct precedent for MECH-490's specific mechanistic distinction (execution FLUENCY of an already-formed sequence, not chunk formation itself) and for its REM-vs-SWS question. failure_signatures: The paper measures movement-transition SPEED (relative Element Movement Time) at chunk boundaries, not an explicit per-tick re-decision or re-planning rate -- mapping this onto E3Selector's commit-variance/re-scoring frequency is an inference, not a direct read-out of the same variable.

Older adults showing 'no significant sleep-dependent improvement' in concatenation is explained post hoc as reduced nREM2 sigma power with age -- an association, not a manipulation, so the sigma-power-drives-concatenation causal claim rests on correlation within a small sample stratified by age.

This is a human finger/arm-sequence paradigm with a fixed, externally-imposed action sequence (a keypress or pegboard order) learned via massed practice -- structurally different from Fishtank's continuously re-planned, environment-conditioned action sequence, where 'the sequence' is generated online by CEM/softmax rather than rote-learned once.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Independent corroboration (different sequence type -- gross arm movements on a 15-element pegboard, not finger keypresses) of the same formation-vs-fluency dissociation as the Bottary companion entry, with sleep specifically implicated (gains present after a night of sleep, absent after equivalent waking retention) -- but this paper does not report sleep-stage EEG data at all, so it cannot independently speak to the REM-vs-SWS question. Confidence set lower than the Bottary entry for that reason and for a smaller, non-age-stratified sample.
failure_signatures: No polysomnography or sleep-stage breakdown is reported in this paper -- the sleep-vs-wake comparison establishes that sleep (of unspecified composition) matters, but says nothing about which stage, so it cannot independently discriminate the REM-vs-SWS question MECH-490's depends_on (MECH-204) raises.

The reanalysis is of Malangre et al. (2014)'s original dataset restricted to element-level movement times -- a secondary, exploratory analysis on an already-collected small sample (n=24, two groups of 12), not a study purpose-designed to test the concatenation hypothesis with adequate power.

As with the Bottary entry, this is a rote, once-learned, externally-specified motor sequence (a fixed pegboard order practiced to criterion), not an online-replanned action sequence in a changing task environment -- the same structural transfer risk to Fishtank applies.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Included as evidence for a PRECONDITION of MECH-490, not for the sleep-link claim itself: it establishes that a variance/threshold-gated commitment architecture -- evidence accumulates, is smoothed, and only releases motor execution once a gate threshold is crossed, after which the motor system commits and stops re-accumulating fresh evidence for that action -- is an empirically supported human decision-motor mechanism, closely analogous in structure to E3Selector's commit_variance/threshold gate. Marked evidence_direction 'unknown' rather than 'supports' because the paper contains no sleep, consolidation, or offline-processing content whatsoever and therefore cannot speak to whether sleep modulates gate persistence -- it only speaks to whether the gate architecture itself is neurally real.
failure_signatures: Zero sleep, consolidation, or time-of-day content in this paper -- it is a same-session, single-timepoint decision-making study (motion perception, numerical cognition, recognition memory, lexical knowledge tasks with EMG), so it provides NO evidence, direction, or otherwise, about whether sleep changes the gate threshold or the persistence of a committed state. Citing it as support for the sleep-link half of MECH-490 would overstate what it shows.

The four tasks tested are single discrete perceptual/cognitive decisions with one motor response each, not a multi-step action SEQUENCE with an open-loop execution period -- the paper's 'gate' releases one motor act, not a run of several ticks executed without re-scoring, so the analogy to E3Selector's sequence-level commitment is structural, not a direct empirical match.

The paper does not identify what determines gate-threshold PERSISTENCE or how it might change over time (practice, fatigue, or otherwise) -- it characterises the gate's existence and its role in RT/EMG dynamics within a session, not what modulates its stability across sessions, which is exactly the open question MECH-490 poses for sleep specifically.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The foundational, most-cited paper establishing that sleep -- specifically the amount of stage-2 NREM late in the night -- drives overnight motor sequence gains that equivalent wake time does not. Included as the canonical anchor the later chunk-concatenation work refines, and as independent, large-effect, well-replicated confirmation of the NREM2-not-REM stage attribution. Held at moderate rather than high confidence because it measures whole-sequence speed and accuracy (a coarser index than the later chunk-transition-specific work) and does not itself distinguish chunk formation from execution fluency -- that refinement came from the later papers, not this one.
failure_signatures: The outcome measure is overall sequence typing speed and accuracy, not a transition-level or chunk-level breakdown -- this paper alone cannot distinguish 'sleep formed better chunks' from 'sleep made execution of the same chunks more fluent,' the exact distinction MECH-490 needs; that separation is only available from the later Bottary/Blischke work.

A finger-keypress sequence task, learned to criterion via massed practice in a single session, then retested after one night -- a much shorter and simpler learning/consolidation window than a Fishtank agent's ongoing, environment-conditioned replanning.

Some later studies (e.g. Rickard et al. 2008, cited widely as a partial non-replication for probabilistic sequence learning) found sleep benefits were smaller or absent for less deterministic sequence structures -- this paper's finding is robust for a fixed, deterministic sequence but should not be over-generalised to all motor-sequence learning without qualification.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: PASS with supporting direction

It is scored MIXED rather than supports because the same review is the clearest literature statement of MECH-492's ALSO-FALSIFYING branch: when arbitration is competitive across several inputs, one weak or uninformative input need not change the decision if another is reliably binding. Confidence is the lowest of the three MECH-492 entries because a review cuts both ways here and supplies no measurement.

Because arbitration is competitive rather than conjunctive, the review supports MECH-492's own weaker ALSO-FALSIFYING outcome -- the term may be near-constant while the gate's behaviour is unaffected because another conjunct is always binding -- so this entry does not license reading the claim as fully supported.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality field study using accelerometry on wild baboons, and the single most direct literature evidence available that PLACE -- specifically the unfamiliarity of the sleep site -- is an independent input to sleep expression that can override homeostatic pressure. That is the exact functional role MECH-286's threat conjunct is named for. Held below 0.75 because the paper is behavioural rather than mechanistic: it demonstrates that place modulates sleep without identifying the signal that carries place safety, so it establishes the FUNCTION MECH-492 says is unserved without speaking to the sourcing defect itself.
failure_signatures: Sleep expression varied with location novelty in the ABSENCE of any injury, so a place-safety gate sourced from tissue damage would be blind to the entire effect this study measures.

The reduced sleep near unfamiliar locations was NOT followed by compensatory recovery sleep, indicating the place term dominates rather than merely biasing the homeostatic drive -- consistent with MECH-492's framing of the threat conjunct as a hard AND term whose miscalibration is consequential rather than cosmetic.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality circuit-dissection paper in Neuron combining in vivo recording with cell-type-specific gain- and loss-of-function manipulation, establishing a DEDICATED, multimodally-driven exteroceptive threat channel (mSTN CRH -> LGP) that gates sleep-state transitions. Source quality is high. It supports MECH-492 structurally rather than directly: it establishes that the biological analogue of the gate's threat conjunct is a purpose-built predator-sensing pathway, not a readout of tissue damage -- which is the architectural premise MECH-492 asserts REE's implementation violates. Confidence is held below 0.8 because the paper never addresses signal SOURCING as a design question and cannot speak to REE's specific z_harm_a wiring or its 0.4 threshold.
failure_signatures: A sleep-permission threat term whose source is nociceptive/damage-derived cannot reproduce the demonstrated function of the mSTN CRH pathway, which responds to predator stimuli received through multiple sensory modalities in the ABSENCE of any tissue damage -- i.e. exactly the regime where an animal must refuse sleep.

The mSTN CRH population is shown to serve normal REM regulation AND acute threat response through the same cells; a threat term that is near-constant across the hazard gradient collapses both roles at once, so the defect is not confined to the safety function.

MECH-499.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=3 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.739

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Strong, canonical, high-citation theory paper directly about the functional consequence of oscillatory phase relationships between neural populations -- but the mechanism it describes (selective gating/routing of an ALREADY-EXISTING representation via gamma-band entrainment, arbitrated by top-down alpha-beta) is functionally distinct from MECH-499's specific claim that the field-level aggregate itself CONSTITUTES a composite content state. Necessary supporting context, not a direct test of the aggregation-for-content function.
failure_signatures: CTC's own framing is a filter, not a constructor: 'If a stimulus is selected by attention, its neuronal representation shows stronger and higher-frequency gamma-band synchronization... thereby the attended stimulus representation selectively entrains postsynaptic neurons' -- the content being routed pre-exists the synchronization event; synchronization determines whether it gets through, not what it is.

The theory is explicitly about SELECTION among multiple already-formed competing representations converging on a postsynaptic population, not about FUSING distributed streams into one new temporally-structured composite -- the opposite direction of information flow from what MECH-499 needs.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Direct human EEG evidence that cross-frequency (theta-gamma) phase synchronization functionally instantiates a content-level comparison operation -- whether current sensory input matches a held working-memory template -- rather than merely gating attention or arousal. This is the best evidence found in this pull that oscillatory cross-frequency relationships can carry/implement content-relevant computations, though the substrate (scalp EEG, cortical, synaptic network) and species differ substantially from MECH-499's proposed hippocampal ephaptic mechanism.
failure_signatures: Synchronization was WEAKER, not stronger, when multiple templates had to be matched simultaneously -- i.e. the mechanism appears to have a low aggregation capacity/bandwidth, in tension with MECH-499's requirement that the field-level aggregate compose information from many concurrent streams at once.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Direct primate electrophysiology showing that the RELATIVE PHASE relationship between two synchronized oscillatory populations (not just synchrony magnitude) has a measurable downstream behavioral consequence (reaction time). This is the closest empirical anchor found for MECH-499's specific emphasis on relative phase as an information-bearing dimension, though the task/circuit (inter-areal visual attention routing) is not hippocampal proposal-generation-state construction.
failure_signatures: The effect is a modest RT modulation (13-31 ms) tied to deviation from an OPTIMAL phase relationship, i.e. the finding is about transmission EFFICIENCY at a preferred phase offset, not about the phase relationship encoding distinct CONTENT -- a structurally different claim from MECH-499's 'phase relationships constitute a composite state.'

MECH-500.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=2 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.68

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Review arguing that slow oscillatory/subthreshold potential dynamics -- not classic accumulate-to-bound evidence accumulation alone -- may set the timing of voluntary movement initiation, which is at least compatible with MECH-500's premise that readiness timing need not reduce entirely to evidence accumulation. But the review's own proposed mechanism (single-region slow-wave threshold-crossing, in the same RP/CNV family Schurger's accumulator model already re-explains) is not the CROSS-SYSTEM FIELD COHERENCE mechanism MECH-500 specifically proposes, so it supports the general axis-distinction more than the specific mechanism.
failure_signatures: The review's own proposed causal mechanism -- 'slow changes in neuroelectric potentials may play a role in the timing of movement onset by pushing brain activity above a threshold to trigger the initiation of action' -- is a single-region threshold-crossing account structurally identical in form to the accumulator model in the companion Schurger 2012 entry, not a cross-population coherence/synchrony account; it does not test or propose field coherence BETWEEN systems as the readiness variable.

The authors explicitly flag correlation-vs-causation as unresolved ('propose using non-invasive brain stimulation... to determine whether these neural patterns actually cause movement initiation or merely correlate with it'), i.e. even the single-region oscillatory-threshold account this review favors is not yet established as causal.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Highly cited, well-validated model showing that the readiness potential -- the canonical single-region neural signature of impending voluntary-movement commitment -- is well explained by a leaky stochastic accumulator crossing a fixed threshold, i.e. the SAME evidence-accumulation-class mechanism family MECH-434 already covers, rather than requiring a distinct coherence-based mechanism. Direct parsimony challenge to MECH-500's premise that a mechanism DISTINCT from evidence accumulation is needed for commitment-readiness timing.
failure_signatures: The model requires no field-coherence or cross-population-synchrony term at all: 'a leaky stochastic accumulator' operating on ordinary (largely uncorrelated, spontaneously fluctuating) neural noise reproduces both the RP shape and the timing distribution of self-initiated movement -- an existence proof that the phenomenon MECH-500 targets (locating the moment a candidate becomes 'ready' for commitment) does not by itself require positing field coherence as the mechanism.

Confirmed prediction: rapid responses to unexpected interruptions were preceded by a slow negative voltage deflection beginning well before the interruption, even absent any prior intention to move -- i.e. what looks like a 'readiness' signal can arise from generic accumulating noise crossing threshold, not from a dedicated commitment-readiness-detection mechanism.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Pellegrini et al. give direct, empirical continual-learning evidence for the failure mode MECH-513 is designed to prevent: when a network's intermediate representation keeps changing (as lower layers keep training), previously stored activations of that representation drift out of alignment with what the current network would produce, degrading recognition performance across non-uniform, real-time data streams (CORe50 NICv2, OpenLORIS). This directly corroborates the raw thought's framing that a change in representational primitives can silently invalidate previously stored, indexed content unless something explicit is done about it -- exactly the failure MECH-513 names for episodic memory. The paper's own fix, however, is a different strategy from MECH-513's: rather than reindexing/versioning stored content after the representation changes, it prevents most of the drift from occurring in the first place by slowing (near-freezing) learning in the layers below the replay point while letting only the layers above it train freely. MECH-513 explicitly declines to freeze representational structure and instead proposes an additive, versioned reindexing layer that lets episodes remain interpretable under both the old and new scheme -- so this paper evidences the problem MECH-513 responds to and the empirical cost of not solving it, without evidencing MECH-513's specific proposed solution.
failure_signatures: Pellegrini et al.'s primary mitigation is architectural rate-limiting (freeze/slow lower layers), not the additive versioned reindexing MECH-513 proposes -- the paper does not test or validate an explicit multi-version indexing scheme against a frozen-lower-layers baseline.

The paper's representation is a CNN's intermediate feature layer under supervised image/video classification; MECH-513's target is episodic memory indexed by structures like ContextMemory slots or an E1 associative manifold (MECH-154), which are not evaluated here.

MECH-513's change drivers include bucket split/merge and dimensionality crystallisation (MECH-496) as discrete structural events; the paper's drift is continuous and gradual (ongoing SGD on lower layers), a different temporal profile than a discrete re-indexing event.

MECH-514.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=2 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.635

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Jardri & Deneve build a hierarchical Bayesian message-passing model in which subtle excitatory/inhibitory imbalance lets bottom-up sensory evidence and top-down predictions reverberate rather than being correctly discounted for their shared history -- a pathological loop they name 'circular belief propagation'. This is a structural analogue of the self-reinforcing loop ARC-132/MECH-514's notes describe (attractor -> biased perception/retrieval -> attractor-consistent derived material -> selective replay -> apparent confirmation -> stronger attractor): in both cases, failing to keep evidence and its own downstream reinterpretation separately tagged lets non-independent signal be double-counted as fresh confirmation, producing pathological over-confidence, spurious causal learning, and (in the model) resistance to perceptual illusions that lower-confidence percepts would normally show. That structural parallel is real corroboration for why ARC-132 requires an attractor's carried quantities to stay separable rather than collapsing into one strength scalar, and for why MECH-514's anti-circularity requirement (repeated replay of one episode must not be miscounted as independent samples) is a load-bearing design constraint rather than an optional nicety. Confidence is kept low and the direction is read narrowly: the raw thought's own evidential-boundary section and both claims' notes are explicit that this paper is cited as failure-mode inspiration only, not as demonstrated evidence that REE's attractor architecture works this way or that axis-conflation is schizophrenia's actual mechanism -- Jardri & Deneve's model is a specific message-passing algorithm error in a clinical human population, not an architectural commitment about carried-quantity separability in an artificial cognitive system. This entry should not be read as hardening either claim past 'candidate' / substrate_conditional.
failure_signatures: The paper's mechanism is a computational-psychiatry model of excitatory/inhibitory imbalance in cortical hierarchical inference, not a claim about multi-axis attractor properties (reliability, confidence, familiarity, valence, salience, urgency, self-relevance, source) -- ARC-132's axis list has no counterpart in the model.

Jardri & Deneve's circular belief propagation is a failure of discounting shared history between bottom-up and top-down signal in one inference pass; REE's self-reinforcing loop (per the raw thought) operates across perception, retrieval, and replay over time -- same qualitative shape (double-counting non-independent evidence), different granularity and timescale.

The model is validated against schizophrenia symptom clusters (hallucinations, delusions, illusion resistance) in a clinical population; there is no direct test of an artificial multi-axis attractor representation or of an offline counterfactual-replay protocol.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Shumailov et al. give a rigorous, general demonstration -- theoretical plus empirical across LLMs, VAEs, and Gaussian mixture models -- that indiscriminately training a generative model on its own (or a related model's) generated output causes 'model collapse': tails of the true distribution disappear and errors compound across generations, an effect they show is close to inevitable without deliberate countermeasures. This directly corroborates the load-bearing anti-circularity requirement MECH-514 registers: 'repeated simulations derived from one episode must not become multiple independent samples,' and the raw thought's own framing that 'the central danger is that material generated or interpreted through the attractor is counted as independent evidence for it.' Model collapse is the demonstrated failure mode when that discipline is absent at the scale of generative-model training; MECH-514 proposes the analogous discipline (provenance-tagging every replay-derived item, requiring some independence in what gets selected for replay) at the scale of one system's offline counterfactual replay. The paper does not test MECH-514's specific protocol (bounded alternative-model construction, held-out validation before granting reindexing authority) -- it establishes the generic hazard MECH-514's anti-pseudo-replication requirement exists to prevent, at one remove.
failure_signatures: Model collapse is demonstrated for generative models trained across successive generations/iterations on self-generated data at population/corpus scale (LLMs, VAEs, GMMs); MECH-514's anti-circularity concern is about a single system's own online-vs-replay bookkeeping within one memory/inference cycle, a different granularity than multi-generation training collapse.

The paper's countermeasure discussion centres on preserving access to genuine, human-generated data as generated content proliferates online; it does not propose or test a provenance-tagging / replay-selector-independence mechanism of the specific kind MECH-514 requires.

No neuroscience or hippocampal-replay content: this is a pure ML/statistics paper about training-data composition over generations, with no claim about biological memory consolidation or offline replay.

MECH-520.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=4 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.802

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Contrastive losses on the next-state prediction explicitly pull together (s_t, a_t) -> s_{t+1} pairs and push apart distractors. This is structurally the right inductive bias for preserving per-action divergence -- you cannot solve the contrastive task if K different actions all map to the same predicted z. Direct ML evidence for the kind of training objective option (ii) would use. Workshop venue and lack of explicit per-action-distinguishability metrics knock confidence down somewhat.
failure_signatures: Reconstruction-based latent dynamics losses (the standard RSSM objective) are agnostic to whether actions are distinguishable in the predicted latent -- they only require pixel reconstruction; the contrastive alternative directly penalises action-conditional indistinguishability.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational formal-methods paper defining a bisimulation pseudometric between MDP states as a fixed point combining immediate-reward difference and a Wasserstein (earth-mover) distance between next-state transition distributions, with the guarantee that the optimal value function varies continuously (Lipschitz) with respect to this metric. This is a REWARD/VALUE-relevant state-similarity metric, structurally in the same family as value equivalence (Grimm et al. 2020, companion entry in this directory) -- it collapses states that differ in ways that do not affect reward or future value-relevant transition structure, which is again closer to the compression MECH-520 warns about than to the anti-collapse constraint MECH-520 proposes. Confidence capped and direction marked mixed for the same reason as the VE entry, plus reduced source-quality certainty because full-text verification of the exact metric definition was blocked by an unreadable PDF in this pull.
failure_signatures: Bisimulation metrics are explicitly REWARD-relevant: two states with identical reward and reward-relevant transition structure but different underlying features (e.g. different textures, different irrelevant background objects) are metrically CLOSE or IDENTICAL under bisimulation, by design. This is precisely the kind of compression MECH-520 warns a pure value-carving objective will produce -- discarding structure that is not currently reward/value-relevant -- rather than a demonstrated anti-collapse mechanism.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The most mechanistically direct paper found in this pull: it studies self-predictive representation learning in RL (an online network predicting its own future latent, BYOL/SimSiam-style, structurally close to a predictive-obligation objective) and shows explicitly that such objectives ADMIT trivial collapsed solutions (constant representations) that minimize the loss, yet typically do not collapse in practice -- and identifies the SPECIFIC optimization-dynamics ingredients (asymmetric predictor/representation learning speed, semi-gradient rather than full-gradient updates on the representation) responsible for avoiding collapse. This directly speaks to MECH-520's central mechanism claim, but complicates rather than simply confirms it: a predictive objective's FUNCTIONAL FORM does not by itself guarantee anti-collapse (contra a naive reading of MECH-520); specific training dynamics are doing the load-bearing work.
failure_signatures: The paper explicitly identifies that trivial, fully-collapsed representations (e.g. mapping every state to a constant vector) achieve zero self-prediction loss and are therefore globally optimal for a naively-specified predictive objective -- meaning 'require the representation to be predictive across horizons' is NOT, by itself, a sufficient anti-collapse constraint in the way a literal reading of MECH-520 might suggest. Collapse is avoided only when specific optimization dynamics (a predictor network updated faster than the representation, and semi-gradient rather than full-gradient flow into the representation from the predictor) are present; absent these, the same objective's collapsed global optimum is reachable.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Formalizes value equivalence (VE): two models are VE with respect to a set of policies and value functions if they yield identical Bellman updates for that set. The paper's own central theorem is the precise formal anchor for MECH-520's collapse worry: as the policy/function set considered SHRINKS, the class of models satisfying VE GROWS, admitting increasingly degenerate/under-constrained models, and only as the set is augmented does the VE-model class shrink toward a single point (a perfect, non-degenerate model). This is exactly MECH-520's claim that value-carving ALONE (a narrow, near-scalar target) under-constrains representation, formalized in the RL theory the claim itself cites. Marked mixed rather than supports because the paper's own stated purpose and empirical framing is celebratory of this property (it enables SIMPLER, more efficient models, and grounds MuZero's success) rather than diagnostic of a hazard -- the paper does not itself argue value-only compression is dangerous; MECH-520 reads the same formal fact in the opposite light.
failure_signatures: The paper's own abstract states the class of value-equivalent models shrinks toward a single (perfect) model only as the policy and function set is augmented -- meaning a SMALL policy/function set (the degenerate case closest to 'value alone') leaves a large, under-constrained space of models satisfying the VE criterion, many of which need not preserve state structure irrelevant to that narrow set. This is a precise formal statement of MECH-520's exact worry: a pure value-carving objective, formalized as VE over a minimal policy/function set, provably admits a wide space of solutions that discard everything not currently useful to that set.

MECH-521.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=4 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.808

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The foundational theoretical argument (correlation theory of brain function) for WHY binding needs a dynamic temporal tag at all: static feature-cell coding suffers a 'superposition catastrophe' when multiple objects are present, so a separate binding variable is required. Strong, canonical grounding for ARC-006's premise that entities are dynamically BINDABLE structures rather than fixed conjunction cells. Held at 0.68 because it is a theoretical/modeler's argument (not empirical) and the temporal-binding solution it argues for is contested.
failure_signatures: The superposition-catastrophe argument shows static conjunction coding is INSUFFICIENT, but it does not by itself prove temporal correlation is THE solution -- competing solutions (e.g. competitive slot allocation, attention) also avoid the catastrophe. So it motivates a binding variable without uniquely selecting synchrony.

A modeler's-perspective theoretical paper: it argues for what a binding mechanism must accomplish, not what the brain demonstrably does -- empirical adjudication is elsewhere (and contested, per Shadlen & Movshon 1999).

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Uses exploratory factor analysis across multiple number-limited and resolution-limited visual working memory tasks and finds a two-factor model with FULLY ORTHOGONAL factors: how many items are held (number) and how precisely each is held (resolution) empirically dissociate, with only the number factor predicting fluid intelligence. This is a clean, direct empirical demonstration that two working-memory parameters that could in principle be a single underlying quantity are instead statistically independent -- structurally the kind of dissociation MECH-521 asserts between capacity and occupancy, though the specific dissociated pair (item count vs. per-item precision) is not identical to MECH-521's pair (capacity ceiling vs. realized domain count).
failure_signatures: If number and resolution were the same underlying working-memory quantity expressed two ways (e.g. a single resource that could be spent on either more items or more precision per item, producing a forced trade-off), the two factors should load together or trade off against each other and both should predict fluid intelligence similarly. Instead the factor analysis found orthogonal loadings and the fluid-intelligence relationship was carried entirely by the number factor, not the resolution factor -- inconsistent with a single-quantity account and consistent with genuinely separable regulators of working memory performance.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Shows that the number of objects successfully tracked in multiple-object-tracking (MOT) is not a fixed slot count but trades off logarithmically against target speed -- up to ~8 at slow speeds, as few as 1 at high speeds -- attributed to a flexibly-divisible attentional resource. This is structurally close to MECH-521's capacity/occupancy split: a bounded resource (capacity) from which a task-dependent, dynamically realized tracking count (occupancy) emerges. Marked mixed rather than supports because a later, direct challenge (Franconeri and colleagues' object-spacing account) argues the same data are better explained by a spatial-interference limit than by a divisible resource pool, which is a live complication for reading this as clean capacity/occupancy evidence.
failure_signatures: A fixed-slot model (a hard N-item ceiling, period) predicts a flat tracking-count-vs-speed function up to the slot limit and then a cliff; the observed smooth, logarithmic trade-off between target speed and the number of objects that can be tracked is inconsistent with a pure fixed-slot account and is the paper's central argument for a divisible resource instead.

A published follow-up line of work (object-spacing accounts, e.g. Franconeri, Jonathan & Scimeca and related studies) argues the same speed-count trade-off is largely explained by inter-object spacing/crowding rather than by a divisible attentional resource per se -- meaning the 'resource pool bounded above by capacity' interpretation this entry leans on is contested, not settled, in the tracking literature itself.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A causal (not merely correlational) manipulation: transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) at 4 Hz vs. 7 Hz over parietal cortex CHANGES visuospatial working-memory capacity (K-values) in opposite directions, lateralized to the stimulated hemisphere's contralateral visual field. This is the strongest available direct evidence in this pull that a rhythm/frequency parameter can SET item capacity rather than merely correlating with a separately-determined count -- the exact causal direction MECH-522 needs (coupling constant as setter, not readout). Confidence is capped because the manipulated frequency band and mechanism (theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling via cortical rhythms) is a single GLOBAL parietal rhythm setting ONE capacity number, not a heterogeneous field acting differently per stream -- MECH-522's more specific and more distinctive claim.
failure_signatures: If working-memory item capacity were fixed by a slot-count mechanism independent of oscillatory dynamics, externally imposing a different theta frequency via tACS should not change K-values at all -- but 4-Hz tACS significantly enhanced K-values (and accuracy) relative to sham while 7-Hz tACS significantly reduced them (Cohen's d 0.44-0.57), which is inconsistent with a fixed, rhythm-independent capacity and consistent with the rhythm ITSELF acting as (or directly setting) the capacity-determining parameter.

MECH-522.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=2 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.728

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This entry verifies a citation MECH-522's own registration text already relies on ('the single ordered abstraction axis that Badre and Nee 2018 reports the evidence does not support'). The review's systematic synthesis of rostrocaudal prefrontal hierarchy evidence concludes against BOTH a unitary model of lateral frontal function AND a single unidimensional abstraction gradient, instead favoring separate interacting frontal networks -- confirming the citation is accurate and directly relevant to MECH-522's heterogeneity claim. Confidence is capped because this is prefrontal hierarchical CONTROL abstraction (levels of policy abstraction), not perceptual GRAIN (domain count in a settling competition), so the domain match is at the level of a shared architectural principle (heterogeneity over unidimensionality) rather than the same mechanism.
failure_signatures: If cognitive control abstraction in prefrontal cortex were organized along a single ordered rostrocaudal gradient (as some earlier unidimensional models proposed), a systematic review of the evidence should converge on that gradient as the best-supported account. Instead Badre & Nee's synthesis concludes the evidence supports neither a unitary model nor a single unidimensional gradient, but rather separate, interacting frontal networks operating at local and global hierarchical levels simultaneously -- the same qualitative shape (heterogeneous, multi-network organization rather than one ordered axis) MECH-522 claims should hold for perceptual grain regulation.

MECH-524.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=10 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.826

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Recent, open-access, pre-registered-style meta-analysis directly on point, and it forces a correction to the naive framing of the anchor task. It WEAKENS the Zeigarnik 1927 claim itself (no reliable recall advantage for interrupted tasks once the original 1927 data is excluded) but SUPPORTS the distinct, more behaviorally relevant Ovsiankina effect (a general, more reliably replicating tendency to resume interrupted tasks). MECH-524 is a resumption-behavior mechanism, not a recall-strength mechanism, so the paper's net effect on MECH-524 specifically is supportive once the correct effect is cited.
failure_signatures: Grounding an REE resumption trigger in 'interrupted goals are simply remembered better' (naive Zeigarnik) reproduces an effect that does not reliably replicate once experimenter-authority / ego-involvement / voluntary-participation moderators are absent, as they are in most modern lab settings.

Historical moderators (ego-involvement, expectation of resuming, experimenter authority, emotional stakes) that inflated the original 1927 effect have no stated REE analogue yet -- a naive port risks smuggling in an unmodeled confound rather than an architectural principle.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Master anchor for the dissociative pole: puts Janet's clinical account of dissociation as disrupted integration into a modern frame, and its own taxonomy (compartmentalization vs. detachment vs. structural dissociation) maps directly onto two structurally distinct ways MECH-524's restrictive trigger could fail, rather than the single undifferentiated 'stuck too restrictive' pole the claim's notes currently name. Confidence held at moderate because the paper's own three-level neuronal integration proposal is explicitly offered as hypothesis, not established mechanism.
failure_signatures: A dissociative agent failure mode may not be a single unitary 'trigger too restrictive' phenomenon: Janet/Scalabrini's own clinical taxonomy separates compartmentalization (content never captured or made accessible -- amnesia-like) from detachment (content present but subjectively estranged and not engaged -- depersonalization-like). If the analogy holds, MECH-524's restrictive pole should itself split into a snapshot-never-captured failure and a snapshot-captured-but-never-reseeded failure, with potentially different falsifiers for each.

The paper explicitly states the exact neuronal mechanisms leading from disrupted integration to the different dissociative symptom clusters 'remain unclear.' Grounding MECH-524's dissociative pole in this literature borrows a clinical taxonomy and a hypothesis about levels of integration, not a validated neural mechanism -- premature to treat the three-level (regional/network/global) proposal as anything more than a structural analogy.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative field-wide critical review that plays the same corrective role for MECH-524's dissociative pole that Ghibellini & Meier 2025 plays for its Zeigarnik framing (see that companion entry): it weakens a naive single-mechanism (trauma-fixation-only) reading of the restrictive pole and supports a broader, multi-factor reading. Confidence held at moderate because its contribution to MECH-524 is corrective/contextual rather than direct positive evidence for the mechanism's own design.
failure_signatures: Treating dissociative loss-of-thread as evidence the restrictive-trigger pole is a single identifiable failure mode risks the same error the field spent decades making about trauma-vs-sociocognitive causation generally: multiple distinct mechanisms can converge on the same behavioral phenotype (no resumption), and a falsifier that only tests one candidate mechanism could pass despite the pole being real for a different, unmodeled reason.

This review explicitly argues dissociation is transdiagnostic and multifactorial (sleep disturbance, impaired self-regulation/inhibition, hyperassociation and attentional set-shifting, deficits in reality testing/source monitoring/metacognition). MECH-524's notes currently ground the restrictive pole with none of these factors named -- the gap this lit-pull closes is narrower than 'is there clinical grounding' and closer to 'which of several plausible clinical mechanisms, if any, does MECH-524's own trigger design actually resemble.'

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Closest available clinical existence-proof of MECH-524's restrictive pole read literally: a person whose stress-response capacity is intact or hyperactive, yet whose engagement with self/world content does not resume. Held at moderate-low confidence because depersonalization/derealization disorder is a tonic, global, trait-like detachment state, not the episodic per-goal reseeding failure MECH-524's trigger is specified as, and a narrative single-author review is weaker source quality than a meta-analysis.
failure_signatures: DPDR's detachment is typically tonic and trait-like across the entire self-world relationship, not an episodic per-goal reseeding failure. If MECH-524's dissociative pole in REE were similarly tonic -- a general dampening of the spare-compute trigger across ALL parked entries rather than a per-entry mis-trigger -- that would be a different, and arguably more concerning, failure mode, and the falsifier design in MECH-524's own notes does not yet distinguish 'this one entry never got reseeded' from 'the trigger itself is globally suppressed.'

The review explicitly notes DPDR's precise neurocircuit-to-symptom mapping remains incompletely resolved even for the human clinical case. Citing it grounds the EXISTENCE and clinical plausibility of a capacity-present/engagement-absent phenotype, not a specific implementable trigger-failure mechanism.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational structural-dissociation-theory article grounding the clinical phenotype of chronically un-resumed goal-directed functioning under trauma. Held at moderate confidence because the proposed mechanism (capacity chronically captured by a rival fixated part) is a structurally different failure shape than the uniform under-triggering MECH-524's own notes currently describe, and because the theory itself is contested (see the Lynn et al. 2022 entry in this directory for the counter-perspective).
failure_signatures: If the dissociative-loss-of-thread pole is produced by a rival capacity-capturing entry rather than uniform under-triggering, MECH-524's own falsifier design (b) -- 'snapshot exists but no active trigger... recently-interrupted entries resume no faster than merely stale entries' -- would not detect it, since it assumes the trigger simply fails to fire for the entry in question, not that the trigger fires abundantly for a different entry while starving all others.

Structural dissociation theory's chronically fixated 'emotional part' has no MECH-292/MECH-524 substrate correlate. Importing the clinical phenotype without importing (or explicitly declining to import) a capacity-monopolization mechanism risks a mismatch between what this literature actually predicts and what MECH-524's falsifier is designed to test.

MECH-527.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=4 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.891

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The single most decision-relevant paper in this pull, and the only one that directly adjudicates the question MECH-440 was commissioned on. Source quality is very high: millions of trials in a well-controlled rodent forelimb task, with a model comparison that separates the two processes quantitatively rather than asserting them. Mapping fidelity is good but not perfect -- motor variability in a ballistic forelimb movement is not categorical action selection in E3, and the correspondence is functional (what regulates injected variability) rather than structural. Confidence is held below 0.9 by that mapping gap alone, not by any weakness in the source. It is high for a literature entry because the paper's decomposition is exactly the dissociation MECH-440 assumes away, measured directly.
failure_signatures: Motor variability is regulated by TWO distinct processes with different timescales and different inputs, not one. A mechanism that packages state-conditioning and self-annealing as a single learned quantity is asserting a coupling this paper measures apart.

The FAST process is keyed to recent trial OUTCOMES -- variability increases when performance is poor. It is failure-driven, not uncertainty-driven. A design that expects a single noise parameter to both track state and anneal with confidence is asking one quantity to carry two signals that biology delivers separately.

The SLOW process does not itself inject variability -- it tunes the GAIN of the fast process, and it is keyed to uncertainty in the reward landscape. So uncertainty enters at the gain-setting layer, one level above the variability injection, rather than scaling the noise directly.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Filed mixed, and the mixture is the point: this paper supports MECH-527's TRIGGER cleanly while supplying the sharpest available evidence against its ATTRACTOR-ESCAPE framing. Source quality is good -- three reinforcement schedules including a yoked control, which rules out the obvious confound that the animals had simply been trained to vary. Confidence 0.74 rather than higher because it is a 2001 operant study in rats with response-sequence topography as the DV, and because the negative half of its message rests on a qualitative statement about rank ordering rather than a quantitative test of basin escape. DOI: none is listed in the PubMed record, so only the PMID is recorded.
failure_signatures: Variability rose during extinction but 'the ordering of sequence probabilities was generally unchanged, the most common sequences during reinforcement continuing to be most frequent in extinction'. Persistent failure increased the TAIL of the behavioural distribution without dislodging the dominant response. That is added variation around a preserved attractor, not escape from it.

The effect appeared under all three schedules including the yoked, non-contingent one, so it is not explained by the animals having previously been reinforced for varying -- which strengthens the trigger finding and, correspondingly, makes the failure to reorder the distribution harder to dismiss.
The design contrasts acquisition with extinction phases, so it does not test escalation of variability as stuckness persists within an episode, nor decay after a resolution.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The closest biological match in the literature to what MECH-527 describes, and the reason this pull can say the mechanism is attested rather than merely plausible. Source quality is high -- population recording in rat mPFC with a task designed to dissociate internal-state coding from behavioural coding, published in Science and well cited. Mapping fidelity is the best of any entry in this pull because the paper's own description (a network-wide destabilisation of the dominant belief representation, which decays as a new stable representation forms) is almost a restatement of MECH-527's above-action-level perturbation with post-resolution decay. Held below 0.9 because the paper frames its trigger as the onset of behavioural UNCERTAINTY, which is the one word MECH-527 is at pains to exclude -- see the caveat.
failure_signatures: The paper's own framing is 'the onset of behavioral uncertainty', not 'confidence without resolution'. MECH-527 wants failure and uncertainty separated as triggers; this paper does not manipulate them independently, so it cannot by itself establish that the trigger is unresolvedness rather than uncertainty.

Escalating breadth under CONTINUED stuckness is not demonstrated. The paper reports a switch into instability and its subsequent decay, not a graded escalation of perturbation as failure persists. The escalation half of MECH-527 is unsupported by this entry.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Filed supports at moderate confidence, and the moderation is deliberate: this is a formal precedent, not empirical evidence. VNS specifies exactly the escalate-on-stagnation, reset-on-improvement dynamic that MECH-527 asserts, which matters because that half of the claim has no biological support in this pull -- Karlsson gives the decay but not the escalation. Source quality is high for what it is (the canonical statement of a widely used metaheuristic). Confidence is capped at 0.70 because an optimization metaheuristic being effective on combinatorial problems is weak evidence that a brain does anything similar, and REE's biology-before-formal-definitions invariant means a formal match should inform naming and design rather than count as grounding.
failure_signatures: VNS supplies the escalation rule that the biological literature in this pull does not: on failure to improve, the search moves to a broader neighborhood (k <- k+1); on any improvement it collapses back to the narrowest (k <- 1). MECH-527's escalating breadth under continued stuckness with decay after resolution is therefore an already-formalised algorithm, not a novel structure.

The trigger in VNS is failure to improve after search at the current level -- not any measure of ambiguity or uncertainty among candidate solutions. This is an independent formal precedent for keying perturbation to non-resolution rather than to near-ties, matching MECH-527 and not MECH-440.

Because a well-known algorithm already has this shape, presenting the escalation/decay dynamic as a new mechanism would over-claim novelty. What is genuinely open in MECH-527 is whether a cognitive architecture implements it, not whether the control structure is a sensible one.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Strong methodological support that computational claims require reproducible, inspectable artifacts; this aligns with MECH-900 trajectory-integrity evidence discipline but is indirect to REE-specific mechanisms.

MECH-CBBL-PROPOSED.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=7 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.871

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: fMRI + eye-tracking study with the directly architecturally-load-bearing finding: choice-induced preference change becomes BEHAVIOURALLY RELEVANT only for choices that were REMEMBERED, and remembering is associated with hippocampus activity. This is the cleanest available empirical link between commit-record (hippocampus) and downstream belief revision cost. dlPFC and precuneus predict preference change online during decision-making. Source quality high (J Neurosci, fMRI + eye-tracking + memory probe). Mapping fidelity is the highest of any entry in the pull because the experimental design directly probes the architectural prediction: post-commit representational shift requires the agent to retain the record of having committed.
failure_signatures: Choices that are NOT remembered do NOT produce behaviourally relevant preference shifts -- meaning the lock requires the commit record. This is precisely the prediction of the commit-boundary mechanism. If the lock occurred independently of the commit record, the proposed mechanism would be wrong.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Prospective 1-year cohort study (n=131 first-episode schizophrenia patients in Vellore, India; n=115 with follow-up data) showing that DUP and changes in insight during the first 6 months strongly predicted outcome (relapse / functional impairment), controlling for baseline measures. Anthony David is senior author (developer of the SAI insight scale). Source quality is high. Mapping fidelity is the issue: DUP is a proxy for cumulative commit-boundary exposure under the delusion, but it also covaries with severity, comorbid use, social stigma, and access barriers; the paper does not separate enacted from non-enacted delusional content. So this supports the prediction that earlier intervention is better but does not isolate the proposed mechanism from prior-strength accounts.
failure_signatures: DUP correlates with many things besides number of typed commit-boundary crossings; the predictive relationship between DUP and insight trajectory is consistent with the proposed mechanism but also with severity-only accounts and with prior-strength accounts. The study design cannot distinguish.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative review by the originator of the memory distrust syndrome (MDS) construct, with a detailed case study of a 32-year-old man who falsely confessed to murder under interrogation and developed enduring belief in the confessed content. Documents the three-type taxonomy (voluntary, pressured-compliant, pressured-internalized) and the contextual + dispositional risk factors for the internalized type. Strong source quality. Mapping fidelity is high for the proposal: pressured-internalized false confession is a near-pure naturalistic instance of belief lock under coerced commit. Transfer risk is moderate because the case-series literature is interpretive rather than experimental.
failure_signatures: Pressured-internalized false confession is described as 'apparently quite rare', so the strong-form prediction (every coerced commit produces internalisation) is not what the literature shows; the proposed mechanism must accommodate the role of additional vulnerabilities (state factors like sleep deprivation, isolation, suggestibility, intellectual ability) that gate when commit-boundary crossing converts to durable belief lock.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: EEG study with proper control showing a frontocentral negative deflection at ~60 ms post-response that resembles error-related negativity. Amplitude correlates with subsequent preference-change magnitude. Rest-state long-range temporal correlations in frontocentral cortex predict both the evoked response and the preference change. Source quality good (J Neurosci, peer-reviewed); mapping is one step removed (ERN-like signal at the choice, not at the post-commit revision attempt) but supports the architectural picture: the act of committing engages performance-monitoring circuitry whose strength predicts how much the agent's representation will subsequently shift.

ErbB4 deficiency in TRN neurons enhanced cortical drive, improving within-modality target detection but impairing cross-modal attention switching -- a double dissociation that establishes the TRN circuit as a genuine sensory gate rather than a generic arousal mechanism. Reversal of the TRN phenotype by selective manipulation of cortico-TRN synapses causally confirmed the circuit. This directly supports Q-019's sensorium loop (loop 1), which posits that TRN or equivalent structure gates what the system attends to. Confidence is somewhat reduced by the mouse-to-human transfer and by the fact that TRN's relationship to the limbic BG loop specifically (as opposed to sensory gating generally) requires extrapolation.
failure_signatures: If TRN were a non-specific arousal modulator rather than a topographic sensory gate, then ErbB4 manipulation should affect all sensory selection tasks uniformly -- enhanced performance in within-modality AND across-modalities tasks, or deficits in both. The double dissociation (enhanced within, impaired across) falsifies non-specific arousal accounts.

If cortico-TRN input were not the critical control signal, then manipulating the GluA4 AMPA receptor at cortico-TRN synapses should not rescue the behavioral phenotype. The rescue experiment demonstrates that the cortical drive onto TRN SOM neurons is causally necessary for the normal balance of sensory selection and attentional flexibility.

Q-019's sensorium loop predicts that TRN is part of a separate loop from the thought and action commitment loops. If TRN simply relayed all thalamic signals uniformly, there would be no topographic selectivity and no double dissociation. The within-vs-across-modalities dissociation is the behavioral signature of a topographic gate, not a unified one.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational, heavily replicated lesion dissociation from the Balleine lab. Provides the single cleanest instance of the 'dissociable lesion signature' Q-019 makes central to the three-gate hypothesis: excitotoxic lesion of the dorsolateral striatum abolishes habit formation (behaviour reverts to outcome-devaluation-sensitive goal-directed control) while lesion of the dorsomedial striatum leaves habit intact -- a double dissociation of two anatomically distinct striatal territories serving distinct control modes. Confidence held below 0.8 because the DMS/DLS axis is goal-directed-vs-habitual, which maps onto the sensorimotor/action-commitment leg of Q-019 (loop 3 and its automaticity gradient) but is not a 1:1 image of the full sensorium/thought/motor triad, and because rodent instrumental habit must transfer to the REE commit-gate construct.
failure_signatures: If commit-gating were implemented by a single convergent gate rather than separable territories, then removing the putative habit/sensorimotor territory should degrade action selection globally rather than selectively abolishing outcome-insensitive (habitual) responding while sparing goal-directed control -- the opposite of what the DLS lesion produces.

If the DLS territory were a generic motor-output stage rather than a distinct gating locus, DLS lesion should impair lever-pressing capability generally; instead it leaves responding intact but restores outcome sensitivity, indicating loss of a specific control mode, not a motor deficit.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Landmark Nature paper (Halassa lab) using optogenetic gain- and loss-of-function plus prefrontal electrophysiology in mice to establish that the mediodorsal (MD) thalamus sustains rule-specific PFC representations by amplifying local intracortical connectivity, without itself relaying categorical rule information -- a thalamic control of functional cortical connectivity dissociable from information relay. This directly grounds Q-019's thought-loop substrate claim, which posits the MD thalamus as the thalamic gate that maintains and protects thought-level (associative) representations. Confidence held at 0.68 because Q-019's specific functional attribution to MD is 'prevents bleed-back into sensorium', whereas Schmitt demonstrates a sustaining/amplifying role; the two are compatible but not identical, and mouse PFC-to-REE-E3 transfer is non-trivial.
failure_signatures: If the thalamus were purely a relay (the single-gate-friendly view in which loops share one undifferentiated thalamic pass-through), then enhancing or suppressing MD activity should scale information throughput uniformly; instead MD manipulation selectively changes rule-representation specificity and behavioural performance without relaying categorical content, indicating a dedicated control function.

If maintenance of thought-level representations required no separate thalamic gate, broadly enhancing PFC excitability should preserve or improve rule specificity; instead it diminishes specificity and performance, showing that non-specific cortical drive is not a substitute for targeted MD amplification.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Solid Dunnett-lab lesion study that adds a third dissociable striatal territory to the established DMS (goal-directed) / DLS (habit) pair: the ventrolateral striatum (VLS) is shown necessary for using a Pavlovian stimulus-outcome association to guide behaviour, while sparing both instrumental goal-directed action and habit. Taken with the DMS/DLS literature, it evidences a three-way functional parcellation of the striatum -- three territories with dissociable lesion signatures -- which is the parcellation the three-gate reading of Q-019 predicts over a single convergent gate. Confidence held at 0.6 because the striatal axis here (goal-directed / habit / Pavlovian-incentive) is not the same axis as Q-019's sensorium / thought / motor-commitment triad; it supports dissociability-of-territories in principle rather than the specific three loops.
failure_signatures: If the striatum implemented a single convergent selector, an excitotoxic lesion of any one subregion should produce a graded global deficit across instrumental and Pavlovian control; instead the VLS lesion selectively impairs Pavlovian-stimulus-guided responding while leaving instrumental goal-directed action and habit intact -- a selective, not global, signature.

If the three striatal territories were functionally redundant, VLS loss should be compensated by DMS/DLS; the persistence of the specific Pavlovian deficit indicates non-redundant, dissociable functions.

Rats showed clear goal-value behavioral sensitivity while dorsal CA1 place cells did not modulate firing by reward magnitude. This supports the hypothesis that dorsal hippocampus provides a value-neutral spatial substrate, with value encoding occurring elsewhere. Confidence is moderate because the finding is null (no modulation) in a specific subregion and task, and the dorsal/ventral distinction means it is compatible with the Jimenez/Knudsen evidence rather than contradicting it.

High source quality (Science, in vivo CA1 dendritic recordings combined with slice validation). Evidence direction is mixed because BTSP simultaneously supports MECH-073 (value gets written into hippocampal geometry) and supports Resolution A for Q-020 (the writing is done by external calcium plateau triggers, not by HPC computing value). The key architectural implication: hippocampal place field geometry is written by external events, supporting ARC-007's passive-geometry reading while showing the geometry is not value-neutral.
failure_signatures: CA1 place fields can be formed in a single trial by behavioral-timescale synaptic potentiation of inputs that were not coincident with postsynaptic firing.
Calcium plateau potentials (driven by external inputs, not by local computation) act as the write event that potentiates preceding inputs over seconds-long windows.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: High source quality (Neuron, large-scale virtual reality recordings, head-fixed mouse with shifting reward contingencies). Strong mapping fidelity for MECH-073: a dedicated stable population of CA1/subiculum cells encodes reward proximity across environments — this is the most direct evidence that hippocampal circuitry contains a value-coding channel, directly challenging ARC-007 'no value computation.' Transfer risk is moderate: virtual reality head-fixed mouse, but the reward-selective population was stable across environment remapping which strengthens generalizability.
failure_signatures: A small, stable population of CA1/subiculum cells fires selectively near reward zones across different virtual environments, even when place cell remapping is complete.
Reward-selective cells form a distinct channel separable from place-coding cells, suggesting a dedicated hippocampal subpopulation for value-zone encoding.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: High source quality (Nature Neuroscience, rodent tetrode, well-replicated). Moderate mapping fidelity: the paper shows reward-driven reorganization of hippocampal place fields, which directly evidences MECH-073 (valence intrinsic to map geometry) and weakens ARC-007's strict no-value position. However, the reorganization mechanism is consistent with Resolution A (external signals writing into HPC geometry via plasticity) — the paper does not isolate whether HPC computes reward or receives it. Transfer risk is moderate: spatial navigation task, rodent CA1.
failure_signatures: Place field remapping toward goal locations occurs during reward learning, showing hippocampal geometry is not value-neutral.
SWR reactivation of remapped fields during post-learning rest predicts subsequent spatial memory, linking map reorganization to consolidated value-shaped geometry.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Barrett et al. 2016 propose that depression is fundamentally a disorder of allostasis, characterised as a 'locked-in' brain that has become relatively insensitive to sensory context. The locked-in dynamic is a positive feedback loop: dysfunctional interoceptive predictions lead to large prediction errors, which increase reliance on prior predictions (because sensory signals are deemed unreliable), which further amplifies errors. The behavioral consequence is progressive withdrawal from approach behaviors -- behaviors that could provide disconfirming evidence are avoided, preventing updating of the dysfunctional priors. This is Q-021's Pathway A dynamics made explicit: when the approach/drive system fails to generate updating signals, the agent becomes locked into avoidance and quiescence. The paper directly supports the claim that pure avoidance produces behavioral flatness by describing the clinical trajectory of this process. Confidence 0.72 because the paper is theoretical and the active inference framing requires translation to REE's architecture.
failure_signatures: If behavioral avoidance in depression were driven primarily by excessive fear or threat signals (heightened harm-avoidance) rather than by failure of approach drives to update dysfunctional priors, Q-021's framing of pure-avoidance as sufficient for flatness would need revision.

If the locked-in feedback loop could be broken purely by harm-avoidance recalibration (without restoring approach drive), the necessity of approach signals for preventing quiescence would be weakened.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Stephan et al. 2016 provide a hierarchical Bayesian framework in which depression emerges from persistent interoceptive prediction errors that shift metacognitive beliefs toward allostatic self-inefficacy: the agent believes its internal regulation will fail, withdraws from effortful approach behaviors, and enters a state of behavioral quiescence that is functionally protective but catastrophically disabling. This is precisely Q-021's Pathway A clinical analog: when drive regulation fails or is chronically violated, the agent converges on low-action policy as the minimum-prediction-error strategy. The behavioral flatness is not a bug -- it is the optimal policy for an agent whose internal model predicts that approach will not reduce drive (self-inefficacy). Confidence 0.73 because this is a theoretical framework paper, not primary experimental data, and the connection to REE's pure-avoidance training requires additional inferential steps.
failure_signatures: If depressive behavioral quiescence were primarily driven by excessive harm-avoidance (heightened NoGo signals) rather than by failure of approach drives, Q-021's Pathway A framing would be incomplete and this paper's self-efficacy framework would not map cleanly.

If agents with intact approach drives but disrupted homeostatic prediction (high interoceptive prediction error) did not show behavioral flatness, the interoceptive inference pathway to quiescence would be empirically unsupported.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Culbreth et al. 2020 link avolition to reduced effort allocation in schizophrenia, correlating laboratory effort-cost decision making with daily-life motivational experience measured via ecological momentary assessment. The paper shows that individuals with greater avolition show reduced willingness to expend effort for reward in the laboratory, and that this laboratory measure predicts reduced goal-directed activity in daily life. Critically, the paper finds neural correlates in striatal activation deficits during effort allocation -- the wanting/approach circuitry. This provides behavioral and neural evidence for Q-021: agents with impaired approach drives (wanting circuitry) show flattened behavioral profiles both in structured laboratory tasks and in naturalistic daily-life settings. The behavioral flatness extends beyond the laboratory and constitutes genuine generalized policy flattening. Confidence 0.70 because the paper does not ablate approach drive specifically (it studies a patient population rather than an experimental training manipulation).
failure_signatures: If avolition in schizophrenia were driven by elevated harm-avoidance (patients avoid effort because they fear failure) rather than by absent approach drive (patients simply do not have motivational pull toward goals), the Q-021 Pathway A interpretation would need revision.
If the effort-avoidance in avolition were fully explained by cognitive load or resource depletion rather than motivational drive failure, the link to approach signal absence would be indirect.
