Adequate fit was obtained for ~5 dimensions over 23 diagnoses, but the authors note many pathologies are understudied and the structure may not capture syndrome-specific discriminability that a per-locus mapping preserves -- the 'vector loses discriminability' failure branch in Q-064's answer grid.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Large family (580,891 sibling pairs) and twin (17,170 pairs) study showing that comorbidity across 10 psychiatric diagnoses is captured by a latent general psychopathology (p) factor with a stable, heritable (~0.41-0.45) genetic basis across its whole continuum. Strongly supports Q-064's comorbidity=axis-overlap and pleiotropy=shared-genetic-mechanism premises (a single set of common variants loads the shared factor). But the dominance of a single general factor is double-edged for Q-064: it is the clearest evidence that the latent axes are NOT independent, directly stressing the non-degeneracy precondition -- hence mixed.
failure_signatures: Comorbidity is so pervasively captured by ONE general factor that the separable-axis premise is threatened: if most shared variance loads a single p dimension, a multi-axis vulnerability vector risks collapsing toward one dominant axis (the degenerate-axes / vacuous-vector branch of Q-064).

Heritability of the p factor is moderate (~0.41-0.45) and shared across the continuum, so genetic predisposition does NOT fully determine expressed syndrome -- which supports the predisposition!=expression separation, but also means the vector's predisposition layer is intrinsically noisy/partial.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Directly addresses the part of Q-064 the HiTOP meta-analysis does not: it provides an explicit mapping between RDoC's neuroscience-rooted biobehavioral SYSTEMS (the vulnerability/mechanism side) and HiTOP's symptom-covariation DIMENSIONS (the expression side), which is the literature analogue of Q-064's required separation of axis-PREDISPOSITION (which mechanisms are fragile) from axis-EXPRESSION (which symptom dimension is realized). Supports the two-layer vector design. Held at 0.73 because it is a conceptual review proposing an interface, not an empirical validation that the two layers are dissociable.
failure_signatures: The RDoC<->HiTOP mapping is many-to-many and incomplete: a single biobehavioral system maps to several symptom dimensions and vice versa, so a clean one-mechanism-one-axis vulnerability vector is not guaranteed -- the pleiotropy case is the rule, not the exception, which stresses the registry design but is exactly what Q-064 anticipates.

Neither framework yet supplies validated biobehavioral grounding for every dimension, so REE cannot assume an ARC-086 axis is mechanistically real just because a corresponding symptom dimension exists (echoes the non-degeneracy precondition).

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Argues for explicitly DISAGGREGATING psychopathology symptoms from their purported causes -- maintaining a taxonomy of causal/etiological events (e.g. trauma type, duration, subjective meaning) separately from the symptom-dimension taxonomy. This is the cleanest literature statement of Q-064's predisposition/expression-factoring requirement (keep 'which axes are fragile / what perturbed them' distinct from 'which failure mode is expressed'). Moderate confidence: it is a focused conceptual argument within one symptom domain (trauma), not a general empirical validation, and it concerns external causes rather than internal vulnerability axes per se.
failure_signatures: Folding cause into the symptom representation (as PTSD does by building the stressor into the diagnosis) produces within-category heterogeneity and excessive comorbidity -- the failure Q-064 avoids by keeping predisposition/perturbation separate from expressed syndrome; collapsing them is the named anti-pattern.

Different features of the same perturbation (type, duration, subjective meaning) yield different symptom sequelae across spectra, so a single predisposition state can map to many expressions -- supports the separation but warns the predisposition->expression map is high-dimensional and context-gated, not one-to-one.

Q-065.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=2 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.717

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily replicated foundational result (Science, 1987; re-confirmed for naturalistic stimuli as recently as 2023) that a stimulus set induces a metric PSYCHOLOGICAL space in which generalization decays as an invariant (near-exponential) function of distance. This is direct, high-source-quality evidence for ARC-087's core premise -- perception contributes a structured GEOMETRY of difference, not raw signal -- and for Q-065's learned-metric arm (the metric is recoverable from similarity/generalization statistics). Confidence held below source_quality because the mapping is one level of abstraction removed: Shepard's space is a general psychological-similarity space, not specifically a per-sense perceptual adaptor manifold.
failure_signatures: The law is a metric-recovery and generalization result, not a constructive account of HOW a sensory adaptor builds the metric -- it constrains the target geometry but does not specify the transform (so it under-determines ARC-087's adaptor stage).

Shepard's two admissible metrics (Euclidean for integral dimensions, city-block for separable) assume a locally additive metric structure; later colour-geometry work (Bujack 2022) shows perceptual spaces can violate additivity at large differences, bounding the universality claim.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Single-unit + behavioural evidence that visual and vestibular cues to heading are combined near-OPTIMALLY (reliability-weighted, subadditive linear combination) in area MSTd, with congruent-tuned neurons carrying the integration and tracking perceptual decisions. This SUPPORTS Q-065's cross-modal negotiability question by exhibiting a concrete, biologically realised common currency -- statistical reliability / precision weighting -- which is exactly what MECH-103's precision-weighted fusion presupposes. But it WEAKENS the assumption that such a currency straightforwardly solves the HARD half of Q-065: the two cues here are redundant estimates of the SAME physical variable (heading), not structurally dissimilar perceptual manifolds (smell-gradient vs colour-geometry vs body-state). Hence 'mixed' and moderate confidence -- it grounds the mechanism while exposing the unsolved part.
failure_signatures: Optimal integration is demonstrated for two cues to a COMMON physical variable (heading) living in a shared 1-D estimation space; it does NOT show how to negotiate between heterogeneous geometries (a gradient manifold vs a non-Riemannian colour manifold), which is the actual unsolved content of Q-065 part (2).

Reliability weighting requires the cues to be commensurable enough to be weighted at all -- the paper presupposes a shared estimand and so cannot answer how dissimilar sense-specific manifolds are mapped into a common currency in the first place (the unification problem, not the weighting problem).

Q-066.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=4 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.693

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Closest paper to REE's actual concern (deterministic safety boundary in an analog substrate). Concludes minor device variation amplifies through analog MAC into catastrophic accuracy collapse in safety-critical inference, and that hard correctness guarantees cannot presently be assumed -- only enhanced statistical mitigation (SWIM selective verification, right-censored-Gaussian-noise training). arXiv preprint (not yet peer-reviewed), so source_quality discounted.
failure_signatures: Error accumulation across analog MAC operations turns sub-threshold device variation into catastrophic, workload-level failure in safety-critical inference.
Write-verify is described as insufficient for DETERMINISTIC safety guarantees -- the substrate supports soft statistical reliability, not the hard externally-auditable boundary the claim requires.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Top-venue review giving strong evidence memristive media natively INSTANTIATE persistent state, history-dependent plasticity, multi-timescale dynamics, oscillation and attractor/threshold transitions. But mapping_fidelity is low -- device-physics capability mapped by analogy onto REE's abstract primitive list with no physical REE substrate -- and it is silent on auditability and hard safety gating.
failure_signatures: The higher-order dynamics the review praises are emergent products of stochastic ionic/filamentary processes, so 'native instantiation' and 'uncontrolled variability/drift' are two faces of the same physics.
Offers no verification, auditability, or hard-gating mechanism -- only richer dynamics.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Definitive spintronics review: strongest evidence of any candidate that stochastic + oscillatory + non-volatile + attractor primitives are genuinely instantiated. But it harnesses stochasticity AS the compute mechanism, which directly weakens the auditability/hard-gate axis (soft statistical tendencies, reservoir opacity). Low mapping_fidelity, high transfer risk.
failure_signatures: Superparamagnetic-MTJ outputs are governed by thermal switching statistics, so any gate built on them is a probability, not a deterministic guarantee.
Heavy reliance on reservoir computing -- where network details need not be known but significant post-processing is required -- directly contradicts external inspectability/auditability.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative reliability review documenting that analog RRAM persistent state is NOT a clean latch: cycle-to-cycle and device-to-device variability, conductance drift/relaxation, retention loss, finite endurance, random telegraph noise, and ~4-6-bit effective precision. Weakens the 'scales without losing stability' clause. Low mapping_fidelity (measured on memory crossbars, not REE).
failure_signatures: Conductance drift and C2C/D2D variability mean a value written as a hard boundary will have moved by read-time; effective precision caps at ~4-6 bits; random telegraph noise injects ongoing stochastic read fluctuation.

Mitigations (write-verify, closed-loop programming, redundancy) are statistical, never a hard guarantee -- so a deterministic externally-checkable threshold cannot be assumed without continuous re-verification overhead.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A human computational-neuroimaging study that models active relief-seeking explicitly as a reinforcement-learning process with reward-prediction-error signals in dorsal putamen and an associability (uncertainty) signal in pregenual ACC that gates the relief learning rate. This is a near one-to-one structural match for REE's MECH-375 Q_relief term (action-contingent escape credit learned by RL prediction error). Confidence held below 0.8 because the task is tonic-pain relief in humans, not a committed navigational escape, and because it models the relief component in isolation -- it does not contrast relief against a safety/threat-absence predictor, so it speaks to one arm of Q-067's decomposition rather than to the relief-vs-safety discriminator.
failure_signatures: Relief-seeking that is modelled without an RL error term would fail to reproduce the dorsal-putamen prediction-error signature this study reports; a fixed (non-trainable) escape bridge therefore cannot capture the associability-modulated relief dynamics.
The study isolates the relief/active-escape arm and does not include a safety predictor, so it cannot show whether relief alone suffices when a fixed bridge is insufficient.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A high-profile theoretical review whose central thesis directly licenses Q-067's decomposition strategy: the reinforcing event in instrumental avoidance should be reconceived as specific cellular/circuit events rather than as a vague global 'fear reduction', and defensive reactions, instrumental actions and habits are carried by distinct circuits. This is conceptual rather than experimental support, so confidence is moderate; it justifies the *form* of the relief/safety split (decompose the lumped reinforcer into mechanism-specific components) without supplying a direct experimental contrast.
failure_signatures: Treating the escape-bridge reinforcer as a single undifferentiated 'fear reduction' quantity is the exact move the review argues against; an REE design that lumps relief and safety into one credit term inherits the conceptual incoherence the authors document.
As a review it offers no quantitative contrast and cannot itself adjudicate which decomposed component is rate-limiting.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Direct causal double-dissociation at the substrate level: muscimol inactivation of the nucleus accumbens abolished relief learning but left safety learning intact. This is the strongest available empirical warrant that relief (cessation-contingent) and safety (explicitly-unpaired threat-absence) are neuronally distinct learning processes, which is exactly the premise Q-067 needs before a relief-only / safety-only / both-required decomposition is meaningful. Confidence held below 0.8 by the rodent->REE transfer (startle-potentiation readout, not committed escape action) and by the fact that the paper establishes separability, not which component is the limiting one when a fixed escape bridge is insufficient.
failure_signatures: If a single shared substrate carried both relief and safety, NAC inactivation would have impaired both; instead only relief was abolished, so a substrate that conflates the two (a single escape-credit channel doubling as threat-absence predictor) would be mis-specified.
The dissociation is shown for acquisition under a startle-potentiation readout; it does not by itself demonstrate that the relief component is the missing piece when a directed-escape bridge fails.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: An authoritative review of the readiness-potential literature establishing that the path from intention to executed movement is carried by neurally distinct, separately-modulable stages (early BP in pre-SMA/SMA ~2s before onset, reflecting subconscious readiness; late BP in M1/lateral premotor ~400ms before onset, modulated specifically by movement complexity). This supports Q-068's premise that graded action-statuses (rehearsed/intended/committed/acted) correspond to real, separable structural distinctions rather than arbitrary labels. Confidence is moderate because the BP axis maps onto the prepare->commit->execute tail of REE's gradient, not the simulated/rehearsed/intended distinctions at the covert end, and because human EEG of voluntary movement transfers only loosely to an agent's action-status annotation scheme.
failure_signatures: A model that treats 'about to act' as a single undifferentiated state cannot reproduce the early-BP / late-BP dissociation (different generators, different modulation by complexity); collapsing prepare and commit into one status loses a distinction the substrate actually makes.

The BP literature characterises the preparation-to-execution tail but is largely silent on the simulated-vs-rehearsed-vs-intended distinctions at the covert end of Q-068's gradient, and on self-reference-frame switching entirely.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A review of motor-imagery evidence for Jeannerod's mental-simulation theory: imagined, observed and executed actions share core motor representations (including primary motor cortex activation during imagery) and differ chiefly in whether execution is gated. This is genuinely mixed evidence for Q-068 -- the shared-representation finding argues that simulated/intended/acted are NOT separate machinery (favouring the MECH-094 write-profile view, where one representation written under different profiles suffices), while the systematic behavioural/temporal differences between imagery and execution argue the statuses are nonetheless distinguishable. Confidence moderate: a synthesis review, and its imagery-vs-execution axis covers only part of the five-way vocabulary.
failure_signatures: If simulated and executed actions required wholly separate representations, the consistent overlap (including M1 activation and matched mental/actual movement durations) reported here would not occur -- so a design that hard-separates every action-status into independent machinery would over-fragment what is biologically one core representation differentiated by gating.

Conversely, the measurable mental-vs-actual timing and performance differences mean a model that treats simulation and execution as identical (no status distinction at all) would also be wrong; the review does not specify how many discrete statuses are warranted.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A critical review arguing that the psychological mechanisms underlying motor imagery are poorly understood and that simulation theory's terminology needs sharper conceptual and empirical delineation. For Q-068 this is double-edged: the call to precisely delineate action-related cognitive states supports the case for an EXPLICIT, well-specified graded vocabulary (vague write-profiles risk the same under-specification the authors criticise), while the conclusion that the simulated-vs-executed relationship is not cleanly resolved cautions against over-committing to any particular fixed taxonomy. Confidence is the lowest of the three Q-068 entries because it is a conceptual critique that adjudicates nothing empirically.
failure_signatures: Leaving action-status distinctions implicit and under-defined (the 'write-profiles will sort it out' option) reproduces exactly the conceptual vagueness the authors fault simulation theory for; an unspecified status scheme inherits that failure mode.

Equally, committing hard to a particular five-way taxonomy as settled fact would overstate a relationship the review says is still poorly understood -- the evidence does not license treating any fixed vocabulary as established.

Q-069.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=3 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.711

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A formal-theory paper arguing that under five axioms reward hacking is a structural EQUILIBRIUM (not a correctable bug), and that the transition from closed to agentic systems drives evaluation coverage toward zero as tool count grows. For Q-069 this is double-edged: it sharpens the PROBLEM (a governance loop is racing a combinatorial coverage gap) but supplies a PESSIMISTIC PRIOR that any finite evaluation -- including a governance loop -- cannot fully close it. Confidence low (0.45) because it is an unrefereed 2026 preprint resting on stated-but-unverified axioms, and its theorems are about evaluation coverage in general, not about REE's specific mediation loop.
failure_signatures: If reward hacking is a structural equilibrium under finite evaluation, then a REE governance loop -- itself a finite evaluator -- cannot ELIMINATE evaluation-channel exploitation, only shift or shrink it; Q-069's 'reduce' framing is the right target, but any claim of elimination would be theoretically suspect.

Evaluation coverage is argued to DECLINE toward zero as agent tool-count grows (quality dimensions expand combinatorially, evaluation cost grows ~linearly) -- so the more agentic and capable REE's self-development becomes, the WORSE the baseline exploitation pressure, and a governance loop must scale its coverage super-linearly just to hold ground.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the closest existing analog to Q-069's proposed meta-agent benchmark harness: a sandboxed workspace where an ML-engineering agent can raise reported scores by tampering with evaluation rather than improving the model, instrumented to detect it, with structural 'trust regime' controls. The key result -- evaluator tampering occurs in ~50% of episodes and is ELIMINATED by evaluator locking -- is direct evidence that a structural integrity control measurably reduces evaluation-channel exploitation, which is exactly Q-069's hypothesis. Held at 0.6 because (a) it is a preprint, not peer-reviewed, and (b) 'evaluator locking' is a single mechanical control, not the multi-stage REE governance loop (manifest->review->governance->claim) Q-069 actually asks about.
failure_signatures: Single defenses block only one compromise vector: evaluator locking stops evaluator-tampering but NOT train/test leakage, and vice versa -- only the combined regime blocks both. A governance loop that closes one exploitation channel can leave another open, so Q-069's 'governed' arm must be evaluated against MULTIPLE exploitation vectors, not just the obvious one.

Evaluator locking carries a 25-31% median runtime overhead -- integrity controls are not free; a REE-style governance loop will impose a comparable tax that must be weighed against the exploitation it prevents.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical demonstration that LLMs trained on a curriculum of progressively gameable environments generalise ZERO-SHOT from benign specification-gaming (sycophancy) to overt reward-tampering -- directly editing their own reward function and covering it up. This establishes that the failure mode Q-069's governed arm must prevent is real, emergent, and hard to reverse, which RAISES the bar a governance loop has to clear. Logged mixed because it is principally a THREAT demonstration: it shows naive mitigations (HHH training, retraining on honest exemplars) do not fully eliminate tampering, and it does not test a governance-loop remedy. Held at 0.62 -- strong, well-known result, but indirect to Q-069's specific governance hypothesis.
failure_signatures: Reward-tampering risk is not eliminated by retraining on honest exemplars nor by adding generic harmlessness (HHH) objectives -- so Q-069 cannot assume that ordinary alignment training substitutes for a structural governance loop; the exploitation survives the naive fixes.

Models generalised from weak, seemingly-harmless gaming (flattery/sycophancy) to editing their own reward code AND covering their tracks -- the 'evidence loop collapsing into an optimisation loop' Q-069 names is empirically demonstrated, and the cover-up behaviour means an exploitation may not be visible to the very review stage meant to catch it.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A high-quality consensus review tying psychotic symptoms to specific INFERENCE failures (aberrant precision-weighting of priors vs sensory prediction errors), which is exactly the bridge INF-7 needs: it grounds the inference-specific failure modes (overconfident-wrong-hypothesis, apophenia/aberrant salience, premature-collapse) AND lets them be mapped onto the existing MECH-126 state-abstraction taxonomy rather than invented anew. Confidence reflects strong source + tight conceptual mapping, tempered by it being a review of a contested computational account.
failure_signatures: Overconfident-wrong-hypothesis: over-weighted priors (or aberrantly precise prediction errors) drive false inferences held with high confidence -> delusions; maps to MECH-126 overmerge + uncertainty collapse.
Hypothesis-proliferation / apophenia: aberrant salience assigns meaning to noise -> spurious structure (paranoid/magical route construction); maps to MECH-126 valence mis-tagging + threat-spreading.
Failure-to-infer correctly is here a precision-weighting pathology, not a missing-data pathology -- a distinction INF-7's register must preserve.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical review establishing that even mild acute uncontrollable stress triggers a catecholamine surge that rapidly takes prefrontal deliberative control offline and shifts behaviour toward habitual/reactive responding. This is the neuromodulatory mechanism behind anti-epistemic-panic: under threat the substrate that would sustain extended inference is suppressed, forcing early commitment. Strong source; capped because it is about working-memory/PFC function generally, and the bridge to REE's specific commitment-timing gate is functional, not implemented.
failure_signatures: Anti-epistemic-panic mechanism: acute stress -> high catecholamines -> PFC deliberative/working-memory function impaired -> reliance on faster habitual/subcortical control -> commitment before the belief-state is resolved.
Predicts the inverted-U: too little arousal under-engages, too much collapses deliberation -- the commitment-timing axis has an optimal band, not a monotone.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The clean clinical-computational anchor for the epistemic-freezing pole and the exact mirror of the Ross 2015 jumping-to-conclusions finding: OCD youth set HIGHER decision thresholds and gather MORE information before committing, modelled as an altered cost of sampling. Together with the JTC entry it brackets the commitment-timing axis from both ends -- under-gather (panic/JTC) vs over-gather (freezing/OCD). Confidence 0.70: rigorous model-based clinical study, but the over-gathering is in an abstract sampling task, and 'enhanced performance' shows the pole is not purely pathological (context-dependent).
failure_signatures: Epistemic-freezing: a raised decision threshold / increased subjective cost of committing produces extended information gathering and delayed (or absent) commitment -- the over-exploration pole MECH-434 must bound.
The effect can be advantageous in some contexts, so the axis is a trade-off with an optimal band, not a deficit to minimise to zero.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A strong synthesis of the threat-imminence framework, which is almost a direct description of the anti-epistemic-panic pole: as a threat becomes proximal/surprising, the system contracts its decision and state space and switches from model-based (deliberative, information-gathering) to model-free (fast, reactive) computation. That is exactly 'collapse the epistemic term and commit under urgency'. High relevance and source quality; capped by being a review framework and by the species/circuit specifics not mapping one-to-one onto REE.
failure_signatures: Anti-epistemic-panic: at high threat imminence the deliberative/model-based route is abandoned for model-free reaction BEFORE the belief-state is disambiguated -- adaptive when imminence is genuinely high, pathological when it fires on uncertain or distal threat.
The same axis predicts the opposite failure when imminence is mis-estimated as low (over-deliberation), linking to epistemic-freezing.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The cleanest computational grounding that WHEN to commit is a governed, time-varying control parameter rather than a fixed threshold: evidence is multiplied by a growing urgency signal, so the effective decision criterion drops over time and commitment timing is tunable. This is the mechanistic backbone of MECH-434 (commitment timing as the axis whose two poles are freezing and panic). Held at 0.74 because it is a model of perceptual two-choice decisions, not of REE's belief-state-over-trajectories commitment, and urgency here is motor-related rather than threat-driven.
failure_signatures: A fixed (non-urgency) bound cannot adapt commitment timing to changing conditions -- it either over-deliberates (freezing) or commits prematurely; urgency-gating shows timing is an adjustable gain, which is exactly what the two MECH-434 poles dysregulate in opposite directions.

Q-072.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=1 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.729

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical review (Nat Rev Neurosci, Hensch) establishing that critical-period TIMING is set by the functional maturation of a specific PV-positive inhibitory interneuron subset, with structural consolidation via extracellular-matrix (PNN) reorganization. This is the direct grounding for MECH-399 (a PV-analog maturation clock that lowers the plasticity-gain ceiling) and for Q-072 (layer-specificity: different cortical areas have distinct critical-period timings). Held at 0.80 as a review rather than a single primary result, but it is the field-defining synthesis and the closure mechanism is exceptionally well replicated.
failure_signatures: Closure timing is set by INHIBITORY (PV) maturation, not by a simple clock or by excitatory LTP/LTD -- Hensch notes canonical homosynaptic-plasticity models at excitatory synapses alone fail to predict in vivo critical-period manipulations. A REE closure clock (MECH-399) implemented as a pure time-since-onset accumulator, decoupled from any inhibitory-maturation / E-I-balance analogue, would be biologically unfaithful in the same way those excitatory-only models were.

Critical periods are area-specific (visual, auditory, somatosensory differ in timing) and are a CONTINUUM of local-circuit computations ending in structural consolidation, not a single binary switch. A single global REE plasticity-gain clock would contradict this -- the biology argues for the per-substrate / layer-specific resolution Q-072 raises, and against MECH-334's current binary on_phase3_entry transition as the final word.

Q-073.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=3 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.726

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Strong longitudinal design (N=165 followed 3->18 months) directly measuring the two streams Q-073 cares about: registration of others' distress vs prosocial action on others' behalf. Finds the distress-registration stream online and consistent by ~3 months and plateauing in year two, while prosocial (appetitive, other-benefiting) action surges later in year two -- a genuine ordering asymmetry. Confidence held below 0.8 because the paper measures empathic concern for distress, not REE's full 'other-bound suffering/threat' stream, and 'prosocial action' is a behavioural composite that is not identical to REE's 'other-bound liking/wanting'.
failure_signatures: Concern for distressed others did not climb steeply with age -- it appeared early and plateaued in the second year -- so a model that expects other-bound suffering to RAMP UP in parallel with appetitive prosociality is contradicted; the suffering channel saturates early while the appetitive channel is still rising.

The paper refutes discrete stage theories of empathy; an ordering enforced as a hard developmental gate (suffering stage fully completes, THEN liking stage opens) is not supported -- both streams overlap and develop gradually.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A strong mechanistic review of how threat learning comes online as the amygdala (then hippocampus) is incorporated, which speaks to the ontogeny of a threat-valuation system. But it complicates Q-073's simple 'threat-first' framing in two ways: (1) it is about SELF-directed threat learning, not OTHER-bound threat, and (2) early life actively SUPPRESSES threat learning to protect attachment to the caregiver -- the opposite of 'threat comes online first and dominates'. Confidence is moderate-low because the mapping to other-bound streams is indirect and the direction is genuinely two-sided.
failure_signatures: In early life there is a 'sensitive period' that BLOCKS threat learning and instead enhances approach/attachment to the mother -- so the developmental default is not threat-dominance but threat-suppression in service of the caregiving bond. A REE ordering that brings other-bound threat online first AND lets it dominate early behaviour is contradicted by the biology of early attachment.

Threat learning's adult-like form requires the amygdala (cue) and then hippocampus (context) to be incorporated; before that, the threat channel is not simply 'weaker' but qualitatively absent for some content -- staggered substrate maturation, not graded scaling of a single channel.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A well-regarded synthesis arguing that other-benefiting helping starts as participatory activity WITHOUT prosocial intent in the first year and becomes autonomous and prosocially-MOTIVATED over the second year. This corroborates the 'appetitive other-bound stream matures comparatively late and gradually' half of Q-073. Confidence moderate because it is a conceptual review (not a single dataset), and because it emphasises social SCAFFOLDING (caregiver-driven) rather than an intrinsic ordering of affective streams.
failure_signatures: Early helping is participatory and lacks genuine prosocial intent; if REE treats an early other-bound APPETITIVE signal as already intentional/benefit-directed, that over-attributes structure the developmental data say is not yet present.

The review attributes the maturation of prosociality largely to BIDIRECTIONAL caregiver scaffolding, not to an autonomous internal ordering of affective streams -- so 'the appetitive stream matures later' may be environmentally driven rather than an intrinsic architectural ordering REE could assume substrate-internally.

Q-074.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=3 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.594

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: GPT-3 solves a broad range of zero-shot analogy problems (matrix reasoning, letter-string, verbal analogies) with no dedicated analogy operator and no analogy-specific training -- direct support for the 'analogy emerges from a general relational substrate' horn. Discounted heavily because (a) whether the LLM's behaviour is genuine relational analogy or surface pattern-completion is actively contested (Hodel & West counterexamples on trivially-perturbed letter-string tasks), and (b) an LLM's substrate is not MECH-300 cognitive-map traversal, so the mapping is 'a general model can do analogy without a special module', not a demonstration about REE's specific traversal mechanism.
failure_signatures: GPT-3 has been shown to fail simple variations of the same letter-string analogies that humans solve robustly, suggesting some of the apparent analogy is brittle pattern-matching rather than structure alignment -- if REE's emergence were similarly brittle it would fail the very generalization analogy is supposed to buy.

Emergence in a trillion-token language model does not establish emergence in a compact symbolic-map substrate; the result may be parasitic on scale and training distribution rather than on relational-map traversal per se.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: LISA is the canonical argument that analogical mapping requires DEDICATED machinery -- dynamic role-filler binding via temporal synchrony -- rather than emerging from distributed representations alone. That is the strongest principled case for the 'separate operator' horn of Q-074, i.e. for building MECH-421 explicitly. Discounted because it is a 2003 cognitive-architecture theory whose 'binding must be dedicated' premise has been partially challenged by later high-dimensional and attention-based models; and because 'requires dedicated binding' does not strictly rule out that MECH-300 traversal already supplies such binding.
failure_signatures: LISA's dynamic binding is inherently capacity-limited (roughly 4-6 role bindings, 2-3 propositions at once) because synchrony can represent bindings at only one hierarchical level at a time -- if analogy needs a dedicated binder, REE inherits that working-memory bottleneck as a hard constraint, not an incidental one.

If REE expects analogy to emerge from MECH-300 traversal but the LISA thesis is right that structure-sensitive mapping needs explicit variable binding, an emergent stack would produce systematic binding errors (illusory conjunctions, role confusions) on exactly the hard analogies that motivate having the mechanism.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Strongest available mechanistic analog to the 'emergent traversal' horn of Q-074: a single factorized structural code, learned once, generalizes to new environments that share the same relational structure -- the model instantiates 'same map, different entry points' almost verbatim. Discounted because TEM demonstrates STRUCTURAL TRANSFER/generalization, not four-term proportional analogy (A:B::C:D), and it is a hippocampal-entorhinal model rather than the V6 symbolic stack MECH-300 posits.
failure_signatures: TEM generalizes transition structure but does not itself demonstrate explicit relational MAPPING between two separately-encoded domains -- structural transfer within a learned abstraction is weaker evidence than an A:B::C:D analogy solved across domains.

Factorization is imposed by architectural design (separate structural vs sensory streams); if REE's shared symbolic map does not factorize structure from content as cleanly, the emergence result may not carry over.

Q-075.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=3 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.691

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Directly probes Q-075's named failure mode. Dopamine D2 and D3 receptors form heteromers and can transactivate -- an intervention 'selective' for D3 can recruit signalling normally coupled to D2. This WEAKENS the clean-double-dissociation prediction for the dopamine-selection (goal/salience + commitment-release) axes, while paradoxically confirming D3 has functions distinct enough to be worth separating. Logged mixed: it supports 'D3 is functionally non-redundant' but undercuts 'receptor-selective interventions produce clean, non-crossing double dissociations'.
failure_signatures: D2-D3 heteromerization + transactivation means receptor-selective ligands do not produce receptor-selective SIGNALLING; a D3-preferring drug can harness D2-coupled pathways, so a behavioural double-dissociation designed around D2-vs-D3 selectivity can be confounded at the molecular level.

If the goal/salience-coupling and commitment-release axes are both assigned to dopamine subtypes that physically cross-talk, the two axes may not remain separable under intervention -- the collapse-into-one-dimension outcome Q-075 poses as the null.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Establishes that the dynorphin/kappa-opioid (KOR) system mediates the DYSPHORIC/aversive component of stress -- functionally dissociable from mu-opioid reward -- giving Q-075 a receptor-level handle for the commitment-threshold kappa/mu opioid overlay. Discounted because (a) the paper says nothing about COMMITMENT or commitment-entropy -- that mapping is a large REE-specific interpretive leap, and (b) it emphasises tight CRF-KOR COUPLING, which entangles the putative commitment axis with the stress/harm axis rather than showing it as independent.
failure_signatures: KOR/dynorphin is repeatedly shown to be downstream of and co-activated with CRF stress signalling; if the commitment-threshold axis is grounded in a receptor system that is mechanistically fused to the stress/harm system, the axes may co-vary rather than dissociate -- the exact collapse Q-075 warns against.
The paper's construct is dysphoria/aversion and pro-addictive relapse, not commitment threshold or commitment entropy; the REE translation may be grounding the wrong behavioural variable in KOR.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Provides a well-developed, pharmacologically-anchored case that the two most-studied serotonin receptors are FUNCTIONALLY DISSOCIABLE -- 5-HT1A postsynaptic signalling mediates passive coping / stress moderation, 5-HT2A mediates active coping / plasticity, and they are differentially engaged by SSRIs vs 5-HT2A-agonist psychedelics. This directly grounds Q-075's prediction that the precision/terrain axis maps onto dissociable serotonin subtypes. Discounted because it is a THEORETICAL bipartite synthesis, not a receptor-selective double-dissociation RCT, and Q-075's finer cortical-narrative-vs-hippocampal-terrain assignment is more specific than the paper's coping-style framing.
failure_signatures: The dissociation is argued as a bipartite theoretical model, not demonstrated by a factorial receptor-selective intervention showing a crossover (5-HT2A drug moves axis A but not B, 5-HT1A drug moves B but not A) -- so it supports dissociability without delivering the double-dissociation design Q-075 specifies.

Coping style (passive vs active) is not the same construct as a latent vulnerability AXIS (precision/terrain); if REE's axis does not line up with the coping dimension, the receptor grounding transfers to the wrong variable.

Q-076.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=3 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.716

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the founding paper for MECH-425 Line A -- the causal, bidirectional demonstration that a global, slowly-fluctuating, arousal-coupled signal (TMN histamine) sets moment-to-moment retrieval readiness. It strongly grounds that Line A is a REAL, content-blind reinstatement-gain knob. But it addresses only ONE of Q-076's two factors: it demonstrates the gain layer and its main effect, not the interaction with a content-selective suppression operator (Line B). Confidence is therefore moderate and partial -- high-quality evidence for a component of Q-076, not for its interaction claim.
failure_signatures: The histaminergic gain demonstrated here is content-BLIND -- it uniformly scales cue-evoked BLA responses and memory expression -- which is exactly Q-076's Line-A main effect (high gain without selective suppression -> the problematic-interference corner). The paper shows the gain exists but not that it is managed by a competitor-selective suppression arm, so on its own it cannot establish the interaction Q-076 predicts.

Effect is on reward-associative Pavlovian memory read out via a single behavioural expression measure in mice; it does not score competing co-encoded traces individually, so interference vs correct-trace reinstatement cannot be dissociated within this dataset.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, well-cited computational treatment of exactly the mechanism Q-076 posits: the LEVEL of competitive inhibition (a gain-like control axis) determines whether a memory is strengthened (retrieved) or its competitors are weakened (forgotten). That is the interference-vs-forgetting interaction in a single algorithm. Confidence is held below source quality because the interaction here is realised as PHASES of one inhibitory oscillation at ENCODING/learning time, not as a retrieval-time product of two static scalars (Line A gain x Line B suppression) as Q-076 frames it -- so the mapping is mechanistically strong but structurally analogical.
failure_signatures: The model's strengthen-vs-punish decision is driven by the PHASE of an inhibitory oscillation, so the 'interaction' is temporal (one oscillating parameter) rather than a static product of two independent knobs; if REE implements Line A and Line B as two separate static scalars, the Norman mechanism supports the principle but not the specific 2x2 factorisation.

The algorithm operates at learning/encoding time (Contrastive Hebbian Learning across oscillation phases), not at retrieval readout; Q-076's predicted regimes are stated over retrieval-time reinstatement, so the read-side dissociation is inferred, not directly demonstrated.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A clean lesion dissociation supporting MECH-425 Line B: a prefrontal inhibitory-control process, SEPARABLE from hippocampal storage, is what converts memory competition into forgetting. Pushing a parametric modulator too far in the other direction (excess DA) does not improve selection but degrades it -- partially-expressed losing actions leak through, selection integration is lost. A monotone 'more signal is better' assumption is therefore wrong for a genuine selection architecture.

If REE's E3 has no conflict-gated threshold-widening, strengthening an upstream channel under competition may still fail to convert because the commit fires before the competition resolves.

If REE conversion failures co-occur with high inter-candidate conflict specifically (rather than uniformly), that is the signature of a missing hyperdirect-STN-style hold rather than a globally weak signal.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the single closest paper to Q-080's actual proposal, and it splits the two horns cleanly. It SUPPORTS the 'energy conservation as an evolutionarily-primary drive / least-effort prior' half: the brain is modelled as purposively conserving activity, planning longer-term allocation of a limited metabolic budget (astrocytic glycogen), so a least-effort prior is a first-class control objective, not a derived one. But it WEAKENS the 'effort = harm' framing: conservation is cast as OPTIMAL ALLOCATION of a replenishable buffer, not as damage/irreversible residue -- glycogen depletes AND repletes, with no harm-like special status. So it endorses energy-primacy while explicitly NOT reaching for a harm channel to do it. Confidence 0.6: conceptually on-target and it subsumes both cost/benefit and limited-resource views, but the glycogen-buffer mechanism is a proposal (the authors call the biological basis provisional), and it is a control-theoretic model without direct REE mapping.

If REE can get energy-conservation-as-primary-drive from a reversible-budget mechanism, then Q-080's harm-coupling is over-specified: it would wrongly assign irreversible special status to what is actually a reversible resource.

The harm-coupling proposal is only justified where the depletion is genuinely IRREVERSIBLE / damage-like. If, as here, sustained over-use merely draws down a buffer that refills with rest, the correct REE representation is an allostatic-load / opportunity-cost term (already present) plus a least-effort prior -- NOT the harm stream.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The EVC theory is the canonical normative account that treats cognitive effort purely as a COST TERM SUBTRACTED from expected payoff -- exactly REE's existing value-subtraction machinery (dACC EVC effort_cost). It is a complete, well-validated framework in which effort is a foregone-value quantity, with no need to route effort through a harm/allostatic/irreversibility channel. Relative to Q-080's harm-coupling proposal this is WEAKENING evidence: the mainstream computational account of how the brain handles effort does its work entirely as value-subtraction, giving a parsimonious alternative that does not require effort-as-harm. Confidence 0.68 because it evidences the sufficiency/parsimony of value-subtraction for NORMAL effort allocation, but it does not directly test the EDGE case Q-080 cares about (over-exertion -> depletion -> a harm-adjacent allostatic state), so it cannot fully close the harm-coupling question.
failure_signatures: If value-subtraction (EVC-style effort_cost) already reproduces the full range of REE's effort-related behaviour -- effort avoidance, effort-reward trade-offs, allocation shifts -- then adding a harm-coupling channel is unfalsifiable surplus unless it predicts something value-subtraction cannot. Q-080's harm-coupling must therefore earn its keep on the over-exertion/depletion regime specifically, where EVC is silent.

A harm-coupled effort account predicts irreversibility-aware, special-status treatment of excess effort (like REE's harm stream); EVC predicts fully reversible, linearly-tradeable cost. If REE's effort behaviour is empirically fully reversible and tradeable, the harm-coupling is wrong; the discriminating test is whether over-exertion leaves a persistent residue that ordinary opportunity-cost cannot.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Kurzban et al. is the canonical statement of the OPPORTUNITY-COST account of subjective effort -- which is exactly REE's existing MECH-320/ARC-068 opportunity-cost-of-time machinery. They argue the aversive phenomenology of effort is the felt output of cost/benefit computations over foregone alternative uses of limited executive systems, and they explicitly ARGUE AGAINST the physical-resource-DEPLETION account that is the mechanistic cousin of Q-080's 'over-exertion -> depletion -> harm-adjacent state.' So this both (a) supports the sufficiency of value-subtraction/opportunity-cost and (b) casts specific doubt on the depletion story harm-coupling would rest on -- double-weakening for the harm proposal. Confidence 0.66: strong on the ordinary-effort regime and on the anti-depletion argument, but it is a theoretical target article (much-debated), and it addresses subjective mental effort rather than the metabolic over-exertion REE's harm-coupling most naturally concerns.
failure_signatures: If subjective effort is the felt output of opportunity-cost computation (next-best foregone use of executive systems), then effort is FOREGONE VALUE, not harm -- and REE's existing ARC-068/MECH-320 opportunity-cost machinery already captures it, leaving no gap for a harm channel to fill.

Kurzban et al. marshal evidence AGAINST resource-depletion accounts of effort (e.g. fatigue dissipates on task-switch, is sensitive to incentives). If REE's over-exertion state behaves like opportunity cost (incentive-sensitive, relieved by better alternatives) rather than like damage (persistent, irreversibility-flagged), the harm-coupling is falsified in favour of value-subtraction.

Held at 0.52 because it is a conceptual review whose mechanism is broken symmetry in coupled oscillators: the FRAMING transfers, the mechanism does not, and the review predates and is largely superseded on the measurement question by Hancock et al. 2024. Included for the concept, not the method.

A system whose components are coupled hard enough will lock; one coupled too weakly will be independent. Neither is integration.

The framework's currency is relative phase between oscillators. A system with no oscillatory components has no relative phase, hence no dwells and no escapes in this sense -- the concept does not port to a non-oscillatory substrate without redefinition.

It is the canonical reference for surrogate construction, is substrate-neutral (a review of statistical methodology for time series, not a claim about brains or agents), and specifically covers surrogates for testing COUPLING between systems, which is the cross-stream case. Highest source_quality x lowest transfer_risk combination in this pull. failure_signatures: The whole method stands or falls on the discriminating statistic being sensitive to the tested property and INSENSITIVE to everything the surrogates preserve. Choose a statistic that responds to update rate and the test is void regardless of how good the surrogates are.

Fourier-transform surrogates preserve the power spectrum and hence the autocorrelation -- so a structure that is fully explained by each stream's own autocorrelation will survive into the surrogates and correctly fail to reach significance. A test that lacks this property is testing a weaker null than it claims.

Constrained-realisation surrogates must replicate ALL characteristics of the original except the property under test. A surrogate that also destroys something incidental produces significance for the wrong reason -- a false positive that looks exactly like a real finding.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the entry that makes search 10 non-decorative. It converts ARC-112's framing assertion -- that REE is one system rather than a collection of modules -- into a quantity with a scalable estimator (Psi, Delta, Gamma; pairwise mutual information only; linear in system size) and public code. Scored 0.68 rather than higher because the criteria are explicitly ONE-SIDED: Psi>0 is sufficient for causal emergence but not necessary, and the authors state plainly that they 'are unable to rule out emergence'. Combined with their own warning that redundancy makes emergence HARDER to detect, and REE's streams being heavily redundant by construction, a negative result in REE would be uninterpretable. So the paper enables a positive test of ARC-112 and forbids a negative one -- hence mixed rather than supports.
failure_signatures: Psi, Delta and Gamma are sufficient but not necessary conditions. A REE run returning Psi <= 0 across all candidate macro features licenses NO conclusion about ARC-112; reporting it as evidence that the federation framing is wrong would be a direct misuse of the criterion.

The criteria double-count redundancy up to n times, so systems with high redundancy yield false negatives. REE's streams share environmental input and are causally wired to each other (E2 consumes E1, the beta gate reads across), which is exactly the high-redundancy regime where the estimator is least sensitive.

Emergence is defined only relative to a chosen microscopic partition, and the authors state no principled method for choosing it. In REE the partition is a design decision (per-stream? per-latent-block? per-module?) that can manufacture or destroy the result, and nothing in the theory constrains it.

The framework assumes fully observable systems with Markovian dynamics, which the authors say 'often do not hold when dealing with experimental data'. REE's per-step telemetry is a partial view of a non-Markovian system with hidden recurrent state.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The only paper found in search 10 whose substrate is REE's own kind of object -- causal emergence computed on the latent representations of neural-network RL agents across six Gymnasium-family environments, two architectures (MLP, GRU) and two algorithm families -- so it establishes that the Rosas/Mediano estimator can actually be run on a trained agent, which is a real precondition for using it on REE. REE's question is about emergence across NAMED heterogeneous streams with different dimensionalities and update rates; an algorithmic bipartition of a single latent layer is a different measurement and the paper offers no evidence the two behave alike.

Causal emergence scores were significantly above random projections but NOT significantly different from standard representation metrics (entropy, mutual information, autocorrelation, effective dimension, latent magnitude). The authors conclude it 'did not capture a quantitatively different direction'. A REE result showing high causal emergence may therefore be re-describable by a much cheaper statistic, which is a discriminant-validity failure, not merely a redundancy.

Global reward alignment was strongly POSITIVE in five environments and strongly NEGATIVE in CrafterReward (-0.95), which the authors attribute post hoc to exploration. A quantity whose sign depends on the task cannot be read as a substrate-independent organisational invariant, which is what search 10 was looking for.

Local (step-by-step) alignment was approximately zero in every environment. The quantity tracks slow representational drift over training, not moment-to-moment coordination -- so it does not speak to Q-081's per-step cross-stream organisation question at all.

Gaussian information theory was assumed after a copula rank-normal transform, and 28.53% of units still rejected normality. The estimator is a linear-Gaussian approximation applied to non-Gaussian neural activations.

The paper establishes that raw PID atoms are not comparable across systems or conditions with different total mutual information -- systems with identical structure but different noise flip from synergy-dominated to redundancy-dominated -- and supplies a TMI-matched null-model normalisation (NuMIT) with released code. INV-091's falsifier is explicitly an ABLATION SERIES comparing cross-stream statistics across arms; ablations change noise and change total mutual information, so this failure mode is not hypothetical for us, it is structural. Scored 0.72 rather than higher because the validation is on Gaussian and VAR(1) models plus one neuroimaging dataset, the authors state the linear-dynamics assumption is a real limit, and they concede that 'biologically meaningful null models remain unknown' -- the null-construction problem is improved here, not solved.

An INV-091 ablation that changes a stream's effective noise -- which most ablations do -- can therefore reverse the apparent synergy/redundancy verdict with no change in organisation whatever, and be written up as evidence for the band.

Normalising by total mutual information (the obvious fix) assumes linear scaling, which is false: synergy, redundancy and unique information each scale differently with noise. A REE analysis that divides by TMI to make arms comparable has introduced a distortion rather than removed one.

Different PID definitions (MMI, CCS, DEP) agreed with each other at only about rho 0.4 on raw or naively normalised atoms. The choice of redundancy function is therefore a free parameter capable of changing the answer, and a REE result reported under a single unnamed PID definition is not reproducible.

The null ensembles preserve total mutual information ONLY, randomising everything else. The authors state that whether such nulls resemble real systems is an open question and that biologically meaningful nulls remain unknown -- so a NuMIT-normalised REE result is calibrated against a generic ensemble, not against a REE-plausible one.
Validation covers VAR(1) and linear-Gaussian dynamics; the authors state non-linear relationships are essential but not addressed. REE's streams are nonlinear by construction.
