recent_entries.confidence_rationale: ADAT is particularly relevant to SD-009 because it uses category labels (action types) as the supervisory signal for contrastive learning, rather than unsupervised augmentation consistency as in CURL. The ADAT hypothesis -- that representations trained to discriminate action-type categories capture the features that matter for control decisions -- is structurally identical to SD-009's hypothesis that representations trained to discriminate event-type categories (hazard present/absent/neutral) capture the features that matter for harm evaluation. Both approaches share the view that the latent space should be organised by categorical distinctions that are functionally meaningful for the task, and that a CE or contrastive-CE auxiliary loss over those categories is the appropriate mechanism to impose this organisation. ADAT's superior performance over CURL (1.24x over CURL's HNS on Atari) suggests that category-supervised contrastive learning is stronger than unsupervised augmentation-based contrastive learning -- providing additional support for SD-009's choice of a supervised CE loss. Confidence moderated by modality gap and by the fact that ADAT's categories are actions (input-side) while SD-009's categories are environmental event types (output-side, what the encoder must detect).
failure_signatures: ADAT uses action labels as the categorical supervisor: states that share the same action are pulled together in latent space. SD-009 uses event-type labels: observations are pulled together based on the environmental category (hazard vs. safe). These are different categorical dimensions. In ADAT, the hypothesis is that action-relevant features are the most important; in SD-009, the hypothesis is that harm-relevant event features are the most important for z_world specifically.
ADAT was tested on Atari and ProcGen visual RL benchmarks. The generalisation to REE's gridworld state encoding (lower-dimensional, different observation statistics) is untested.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: CURL directly demonstrates that adding a contrastive auxiliary objective to an RL encoder dramatically improves the representational quality and sample efficiency of the agent, with almost no change to the RL algorithm itself. The mechanism is the same as SD-009's CE auxiliary loss: a discriminative objective is added to the encoder's training signal that forces it to maintain categorical structure it would otherwise discard. In SD-009, the CE loss classifies event types (hazard present, absent, neutral); in CURL, contrastive NCE maximises agreement between augmentations of the same observation. Both approaches address the same fundamental failure mode: reconstruction and prediction losses alone do not force the encoder to maintain any particular categorical organisation of the latent space. Confidence is moderated because CURL uses contrastive self-supervised learning (no explicit label supervision) while SD-009 uses a supervised CE loss over event categories; these are related but not identical mechanisms. The sample efficiency gain in CURL (1.9x over prior methods) is strong empirical evidence that the mechanism is effective.
failure_signatures: CURL's contrastive objective is defined over augmented pairs (positive pairs = augmentations of the same observation), not over categorical event labels as in SD-009. If the relevant category structure is not captured by augmentation invariance (e.g., two different event types that look superficially similar under augmentation), CURL's contrastive objective would not preserve it. SD-009's CE loss explicitly targets event-type categories that are not derivable from augmentation structure alone.

CURL was demonstrated on Atari and DeepMind Control Suite visual tasks. REE uses a simple gridworld where the pixel space is much lower-dimensional. The sample efficiency argument is more pressing for high-dimensional visual RL than for the gridworld setting.

This is the paper the SD-009/MECH-100 prose has been leaning on for its biological grounding, registered here for the first time against SD-009 and with a VERIFIED citation (the prose cited a non-existent 'Murray et al. 2004, TICS 8:56-61'; the MECH-100 record.json that did exist carried the right authors/year/venue but a wrong title, a wrong DOI and a PMID pointing at an unrelated hepatology paper -- see metadata_correction in that record and evidence/planning/sd009_murray_citation_and_mech100_currency_review_2026-08-09.md). On the substance: Murray, Bussey and Saksida argue that perirhinal cortex -- the apex of the ventral visual stream for object knowledge -- represents feature CONJUNCTIONS that support discrimination between objects sharing many features, and that this representational structure is shaped by discrimination demands rather than falling out of passive exposure to input statistics. That supports the general half of SD-009 (a world-state encoder needs a discriminative training pressure, not reconstruction alone) but NOT the specific half that SD-009 actually asserts -- that the pressure must be a DEDICATED event-type CE head. Confidence is set at 0.50, below the 0.62 the same paper carries against MECH-100, for two reasons that are specific to SD-009 rather than to the source: (1) SD-009 is a design decision naming one particular head, and this review speaks to the necessity of categorical discrimination pressure in general, which SD-070's own grounding heads already supply; (2) V3-EXQ-897 (2026-08-08) measured the marginal contribution of the dedicated event-CE head over SD-070's other grounding heads at null-to-negative on 3/3 seeds, so the literature and the experiment now bear on different granularities of the same claim and the literature should not be read as covering the gap.
failure_signatures: The review's argument is that perirhinal representations are shaped by DISCRIMINATION DEMANDS in general, not by a dedicated category-classification head in particular. If any discriminative training pressure suffices -- which is what SD-070's hazard/resource-presence and distance-bucket grounding heads already supply -- then this paper supports SD-070's recipe and says nothing in favour of SD-009's additional event-CE head.

The biological mechanism is experience-dependent plasticity across development and long-run task training in intact animals; SD-009 is an auxiliary cross-entropy head trained inside a short P0 phase. Alignment is conceptual, not mechanistic.

Perirhinal cortex sits at the ventral-stream/MTL boundary and carries mnemonic as well as perceptual function. If the correct biological analog of z_world is earlier ventral stream (V4/posterior IT), the mapping is mislocated -- the same caveat the MECH-100 entry records.

If z_world's event-type decodability under SD-070 turns out to be inherited from the static scene-structure targets rather than from any event-level pressure at all, the object-discrimination framing of this review would be the wrong biological frame for SD-009 specifically.

Provides experimental dissociation of affective and sensory-discriminative pain processing using an elegant mood-vs-attention design. Mood manipulation selectively modulated ACC and medial thalamus (affective stream) while attention modulation affected anterior insular cortex; odor-induced positive mood decreased pain unpleasantness but not intensity. This double dissociation supports the SD-010 architectural claim that harm's affective and discriminative channels can be independently modulated. Confidence capped at 0.70 because the study tests modulation rather than baseline stream separation, and uses a non-pain-stimulus manipulation.
failure_signatures: The dissociation found is between mood and attention modulation, not between the two ascending streams directly. It is possible to read the result as showing two modulatory systems rather than two independent sensory channels.
The study uses odor-induced mood and heat pain; generalization to the harm-signal context in REE is not guaranteed.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: German-language review establishing cortical pain representation across parallel networks: S1 for discriminative aspects, ACC for affective aspects, with distinct first-pain (S1-dominant) vs second-pain (ACC-dominant) temporal profiles. The first-pain/second-pain distinction directly instantiates the A-delta (fast, discriminative) vs C-fiber (slow, affective) separation at the cortical level. Confidence slightly lower than Willis 1997 due to language barrier limiting detailed extraction and the review predating modern connectomics.
failure_signatures: If S1 cortex turns out to encode affective qualities of pain as strongly as discriminative qualities, the clean separation motivating SD-010 becomes less compelling.
German-language source; abstract only reviewed in English -- extraction is from English abstract.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative comprehensive review of spinal nociceptive pathways documenting the anatomically distinct lateral (neospinothalamic, A-delta, VPL-S1/S2) and medial (paleospinothalamic, C-fiber, intralaminar thalamus-ACC/insula) streams. This dual-pathway architecture is the direct biological basis for SD-010's design decision to separate z_harm from z_world. Confidence capped below 0.9 because the mapping from biological pathway anatomy to a computational latent separation requires a conceptual translation step.
failure_signatures: If the lateral/medial distinction turns out to be an oversimplification with heavy cross-talk at thalamic level, the clean stream separation assumed by SD-010 may not hold.
The review covers both human and animal data; some findings are rodent-only and may not generalize to primate nociceptive organization.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative primate review documenting the OFC subdivision into distinct value-coding pathways, with the amygdala-OFC interaction supplying affective valence and lateral OFC + IT cortex supplying outcome-identity (sensory-discriminative) information. Source quality high (NRN, both authors are canonical primate-decision-making researchers). Mapping fidelity strong: REE's SD-010 (sensory-discriminative harm) / SD-011 (affective harm) split lines up almost directly with the literature's OFC-medial-vs-lateral / amygdala-vs-IT-cortex pathway distinction. The literature does NOT explicitly frame these as 'arbitration weight inputs' (the closest framing is 'value-component contributions to choice'), so REE's MECH-312-d affective-stream-modulation framing is a closely related but slightly extended interpretation.
failure_signatures: The Murray-Rudebeck framework is descriptive (which OFC subregion does what) rather than algorithmic (how the affective and discriminative streams combine into a choice).
Cross-species transfer caveats: most primate OFC literature is macaque; rodent OFC is partially homologous but the medial-vs-lateral functional dissociation is less crisp.

The review treats lesion-driven dissociations (after-amygdala-lesion behaviour vs after-OFC-lesion behaviour) as the primary evidence; the algorithmic combination rule is inferred rather than directly measured.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational, heavily replicated mechanistic review establishing that the learned-helplessness phenotype is gated by stressor UNCONTROLLABILITY and instantiated by dorsal-raphe 5-HT sensitization + CRF, with vmPFC controllability-detection as the inhibitory gate. Directly anchors the SUFFERING pole of the differentiation: the stop/withdrawal here is an aversive, controllability-contingent escape-failure -- categorically not an effort/energy accumulator. High source_quality; mapping is to the ANTECEDENT and SUBSTRATE contrast rather than to a numeric REE metric, so mapping_fidelity is strong-but-conceptual.
failure_signatures: If a fatigue/stop-recover signal were registered on the SD-011 suffering side, it would inherit controllability-gating and DRN/CRF aversive semantics that the biology assigns ONLY to uncontrollable aversive stress -- mis-attributing an energy-budget stop to a harm/escape-failure mechanism.

Helplessness-driven withdrawal does NOT remit with rest (it requires controllability experience or pharmacological reversal); any model that lets rest dissipate a suffering-side stop signal contradicts this literature.

High mapping_fidelity to the proposed REE primitive because the model IS the proposed primitive; transfer_risk low because it is already an abstract control-theoretic accumulator, not a species-specific circuit.

Incentive does not abolish the accumulator; it rescales slopes/bounds (lets the agent 'work closer to exhaustion'). A model where high reward simply switches fatigue off would contradict the data.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Well-cited review reframing mental fatigue as an adaptive cost/benefit recalibration -- fatigue signals that the energetical cost of continued effort now outweighs expected reward, motivating disengagement toward more rewarding alternatives, rather than reflecting depleted resources or aversive mood. Grounds fatigue's antecedent (accumulated effort + opportunity cost) and its disengagement consumer (ARC-078) as DISTINCT from suffering's aversive-uncontrollable antecedent. Source quality good (review, not primary data); mapping is conceptual.
failure_signatures: Treating fatigue as pure resource depletion ('out of fuel') rather than a cost/benefit signal predicts fatigue should be insensitive to incentive -- contradicted; fatigue-driven disengagement is reversible by raising reward, which is the signature of a value-recalibration, not an empty tank.

If fatigue were a negative-valence aversive signal (suffering-like), it would not preferentially redirect behaviour toward MORE rewarding alternatives; the data frame it as an opportunity-cost reallocation.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Neurocognitive framework casting fatigue as a MOTIVATIONAL signal (effort/opportunity-cost recalibration in dACC/anterior insula/lateral PFC) rather than energy depletion, and distinguishing transient STATE fatigue (waxes/wanes with cognitive or motor exertion) from persistent TRAIT fatigue/chronic exhaustion -- the state/trait split that separates a recoverable homeostatic stop from clinical aversive-mood conditions. Directly supports fatigue's distinctness from suffering/depression and its SD-012 placement. Review-level evidence; mapping conceptual.
failure_signatures: Modelling fatigue as energy depletion mispredicts its recovery profile and its incentive-sensitivity; the framework requires fatigue to act as a value/cost signal feeding effort-based decision systems.

Collapsing transient state-fatigue into trait/clinical exhaustion (or into anhedonia/depression) erases the recoverable-stop-recover dynamic that distinguishes the homeostatic signal from suffering-driven withdrawal.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical homeostatic-accumulator model: Process S rises monotonically as a function of prior wakefulness and falls during sleep, indexed by EEG slow-wave activity and linked to adenosine accumulation -- a homeostatic deficit variable whose antecedent is TIME-ON-TASK / metabolic expenditure, explicitly independent of aversive experience or controllability. Grounds the slow, sleep-pressure variant of fatigue/stop-recover on the SD-012 homeostatic side and supplies the recovery dynamic that suffering-withdrawal lacks. Foundational model; mapping is to the antecedent/dynamics, not a REE metric.
failure_signatures: Any account that lets a suffering/SD-011 stop signal recover by 'sleeping it off' borrows Process S dynamics it does not have: Process S recovery is specific to the homeostatic accumulator, not to aversive-uncontrollable stress.

Modelling fatigue with no recovery integrator (stop-only) omits the defining feature of Process S -- the exponential decline during sleep that resets the accumulator; fatigue without a recover phase is mis-specified.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Wang et al. (2021) prove formally that a policy learned from confounded observational data -- where unobserved context induces spurious correlations between actions and outcomes -- does not recover the true interventional value function. The paper derives tight upper bounds on the regret achievable using observational data alone, and shows that these bounds are strictly worse than what is achievable with interventional data under the same confounders. This directly supports SD-013: E2_harm_s trained on observational rollouts in confounded states cannot recover the interventional distribution P(z_harm_s | do(a)). The paper proposes deconfounding via adjustment estimators that require either instrumental variables or explicit interventional samples -- the RL equivalent of the counterfactual perturbation steps ARC-033 mandates. Confidence is moderate rather than high because the paper addresses value function estimation (policy evaluation) rather than forward model training; the mapping requires treating E2_harm_s as the entity that must estimate interventional quantities rather than a policy critic.
failure_signatures: If E2_harm_s is trained on confounded observational data without explicit interventional perturbation steps, the learned model will encode P(z_harm_s | z_t, a_behavioral) rather than P(z_harm_s | do(a)). Wang et al. show this bias is formally non-zero and scales with the degree of confounding -- in highly confounded states (the agent's behavioral policy correlates strongly with ambient harm patterns), causal_sig will be systematically underestimated or reversed.

The paper demonstrates that simply increasing the volume of observational data does not reduce confounding bias -- the bound on policy regret due to confounding is irreducible without adjustment. More observational rollouts from the same confounded behavioral policy will converge to the wrong interventional distribution, not toward it.

The deconfounding adjustment requires either an instrument (a variable that influences action but not outcome except through action) or interventional samples where the confounding correlation is broken. In the REE setting, executing a_cf from the same confounded state serves as the interventional sample -- breaking the behavioral policy's correlation with harm and providing the identifiable contrast needed for causal_sig.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Venkatesh and Malikopoulos (2025) directly address the problem that is most proximate to SD-013: model-based RL under confounding. They prove that transition and reward models learned from confounded observational data are fundamentally inconsistent -- they do not converge to the interventional quantities needed for planning under state-based policies. This is the closest available computational paper to the SD-013 claim, which is specifically about a forward model (E2_harm_s) rather than a policy. The paper's central negative result -- that conventional model-learning from confounded data misrepresents the effect of candidate policies -- directly instantiates SD-013's claim about causal_sig. The proposed remedy (surrogate MDP with proximal adjustment) is technically different from ARC-033's counterfactual perturbation approach, but the necessity argument (observational model is insufficient) is the same. Confidence is moderate because the paper is an arXiv preprint (not peer-reviewed at top venue) and the specific model class (forward model for harm stream) differs from the paper's setting (reward/transition models for planning).
failure_signatures: Venkatesh and Malikopoulos show that a transition model learned from confounded offline data generates systematically biased predictions for any action that deviates from the behavioral policy. For E2_harm_s, this means that z_harm_s predictions for a_cf -- which by definition deviates from the agent's behavioral policy -- will be biased toward the behavioral policy's harm-correlated outcomes. The causal_sig = E2_harm_s(z_t, a_actual) - E2_harm_s(z_t, a_cf) will compress toward zero because both predictions are biased by the same confounding pattern.

The paper establishes that the learned model is inconsistent: it does not converge to the true interventional distribution P(s' | do(a)) even with infinite observational data. This is a qualitatively stronger failure than noise or approximation error -- the bias is structural and irreducible without adjustment. In the REE context, this means no amount of additional observational training will produce a reliable E2_harm_s without counterfactual perturbation data.

The paper notes that conventional maximum likelihood model-learning in confounded C-MDPs fails because the behavioral policy's correlation with the unobserved context corrupts the model's implicit assumptions about action-outcome independence. E2_harm_s training using standard next-step prediction loss on confounded trajectories makes exactly the assumptions the paper proves are invalid.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the primary reference cited in the SD-013 claim notes. Scholkopf et al. (2021) provide the foundational theoretical argument that statistical models trained on observational trajectories learn the correlational distribution P(z_harm_s_next | z_t, a) rather than the interventional distribution P(z_harm_s_next | do(a)), and that these distributions diverge in confounded states. The paper establishes that performing an intervention changes the data distribution in ways that make predictions from purely statistical models inaccurate -- this is the core argument SD-013 translates to E2_harm_s. The paper is a high-impact Proceedings of the IEEE review article by leading researchers in causal ML, giving it both authoritative status and broad synthesis value. The mapping to SD-013 is highly direct because the paper explicitly discusses forward models and i.i.d. assumptions. Confidence is higher than the other entries because this paper is the theoretical source from which SD-013's formulation was derived.
failure_signatures: Scholkopf et al. establish that statistical learning assumes i.i.d. data drawn from a fixed distribution. When an agent's own actions change the environment (i.e., when the agent intervenes), the distribution shifts. E2_harm_s trained on observational trajectories will produce incorrect predictions for actions that differ from the behavioral policy's distribution -- especially in confounded states where action and harm are spuriously correlated. The failure is not a matter of generalization; it is a matter of the learned distribution being the wrong distribution.

The paper explicitly discusses that interventional questions -- P(outcome | do(action)) -- are more challenging than prediction questions -- P(outcome | action) -- because interventions take the system out of the i.i.d. setting. An E2_harm_s that treats both a_actual and a_cf as prediction queries on the same distribution will compute a causal_sig that conflates causal and correlational contributions.

The paper notes that identifying the interventional distribution from observational data requires either additional assumptions (e.g., no unobserved confounders, known causal graph) or interventional data. In environments where the agent's policy is correlated with harm-proximal states, the no-unobserved-confounders assumption is violated, making observational-only training insufficient for causal_sig estimation.

failure_signatures: Anticipation of increasing punishment did NOT activate NAcc; punishment-anticipation activated medial caudate instead. Excitement-as-NAcc-signature is positive-valence-specific, not arousal-general.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Direct primate single-unit evidence that anticipatory activity in lateral habenula and DA neurons is heterogeneous: tonic activity is reward-preferring (motivational value); phasic activity at task onset responds to both rewarding and aversive tasks similarly (motivational salience). Two dissociable anticipatory signals coexist within the same neurons. Strong support for the principle that anticipatory affect is multi-channel; supports the architectural-distinction premise behind VALENCE_EXCITEMENT.
failure_signatures: If REE collapses anticipatory affect into a single channel (e.g. VALENCE_WANTING amplitude), it cannot reproduce the tonic/phasic dissociation that real DA / habenula neurons exhibit. A single-channel architecture is biologically wrong; the question is just how many channels.

SD-015.confidence_rationale: exp=4 entry(s), lit=13 entry(s), exp_conf=0.5, lit_conf=0.785

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The architectural-resolution paper for the labeled-line vs distributed-coding tension. Models the hippocampus as having TWO pathways with different computational roles: monosynaptic (entorhinal -> CA1 direct) supports statistical learning / similarity-preserving regularities; trisynaptic (entorhinal -> DG -> CA3 -> CA1) supports per-episode pattern separation / labeled-line-like specificity. This is direct biological licensing for OPTION C (hybrid) in the SD-049 verdict: a substrate with both a similarity-preserving distributed embedding pathway AND a labeled-line-like per-instance pathway. Source quality high (peer-reviewed Phil Trans, Schapiro/Norman/Botvinick lab triumvirate). Mapping fidelity strong: the architectural commitment is exactly what option C licenses. Transfer risk moderate -- model is hippocampus-internal architecture, REE encoder is a single MLP head, so the bi-pathway architecture would need to be re-instantiated at the encoder level rather than transplanted.
failure_signatures: Option A choice produces strong per-cell pattern-separation (good for labeled-line / one-hot identity) but no similarity-preserving statistical-learning capacity. Predicted V3-EXQ-514 signature: high identity-recovery accuracy + low cross-cell-instance generalisation = trisynaptic-only failure mode in this paper's framework.

Option B choice produces strong similarity-preserving distributed coding but loses per-instance specificity. Predicted signature: low identity-recovery + good similarity-structure inferences = monosynaptic-only failure mode. The wanting/liking dissociation MECH-229 cares about may pass on similarity grounds but fail on identity-recovery.

Option C hybrid licensed by this paper would predict that BOTH signatures pass: high identity-recovery + similarity structure preserved. The architecture is biologically grounded in two known anatomical pathways. If V3-EXQ-514 ARM_2 fails on either dimension, the architecture may need explicit two-head implementation rather than a single z_resource encoder.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Direct single-unit OFC recording in macaque during economic choice. Shows OFC encodes good identities and values in juice-based 'labeled lines' -- distinct neural populations encode distinct juice identities. This is THE most architecturally direct evidence for option A's labeled-line / one-hot identity coding at the OFC level. Confidence high on source quality (Padoa-Schioppa lab, peer-reviewed Curr Biol). Mapping fidelity strong: 'good identity' in this paper maps cleanly onto SD-049's resource-type identity. Transfer risk moderate -- macaque OFC vs REE substrate, but the architectural primitive (per-juice-identity neural populations) is the cleanest precedent.
failure_signatures: If option A wins (one-hot slot identity coding) and ARM_2 still fails to produce goal_resource_r >= 0.5 at V3-EXQ-514, the labeled-line architecture is not the bottleneck -- check identity-classifier head training (P0 phase) and the supervision signal quality, not the architectural choice.

If labeled-line representation produces brittle generalisation across distinct grid configurations of the same type, REE may need to add the similarity-preserving layer that Schapiro 2016 substrate requires (i.e. fall back to option C hybrid).

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: MVPA-based dissociation of identity-specific (lateral OFC) vs identity-general (vmPFC) reward representations in human classical conditioning with food odors. Mixed verdict because the finding has two parallel implications: (a) OFC carries distributed pattern-based identity codes (favours option B/C: similarity-preserving embedding), AND (b) the dissociation suggests separate substrates for identity-specific and identity-general value (consistent with option A's labeled-line + magnitude split). Source quality high (PNAS, replication-track lab). Mapping fidelity strong: human OFC, future reward identity, exactly the architectural variable SD-049 cares about. Transfer risk moderate -- human vs REE rodent-analog, but the principle is general.
failure_signatures: If pattern-based identity coding is the dominant biological signature (not labeled-line), option A's one-hot slot may underfit -- it cannot capture similarity structure across types. Falsifier signal at V3-EXQ-514: option A produces low identity-recovery on held-out cell configurations because each cell-instance becomes its own labeled line.

If lateral OFC vs vmPFC dissociation is the architectural signature REE should reproduce, the implementation may need TWO heads: one for identity (option A's slot) and one for identity-general value (vmPFC analog). This is a legitimate Phase 2 design refinement that this paper licenses.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical paper. Single-unit human MTL recordings. Direct evidence that biological identity coding can be sparse and explicit at the single-unit readout level. Nature publication, Caltech + UCLA epilepsy patient series. The mapping to z_resource is partial: this is the readout end of the system, not the substrate that produces it. Confidence weighted toward source quality (peer review, replicability, large neuron yield) but reduced for transfer risk: the human MTL paradigm is visual-identity invariance, not goal/resource-identity in a rodent-grid-world analog. Mapping fidelity is moderate -- 'sparse explicit code' is the relevant architectural signature for option A, but the substrate that produces it is almost certainly distributed (cf. Schapiro 2016/2017 cross-tag).
failure_signatures: If the SD-049 z_resource encoder produces sparse identity-like activation (option A: one-hot slot + magnitude), the structural-readout signature this paper documents is what the validation experiment should look for: high response selectivity at one type per unit, low across-type generalisation. Failure to find this signature with option A indicates the encoder is not learning the supervision target.

Concept cells in this paper fired even to letter strings of the named individual -- the identity code is amodal. If REE's z_resource fails to generalise across e.g. food-the-cell vs food-the-spatial-bias, option A's labeled-line architecture is too rigid to capture this and option B/C's similarity-preserving embedding is structurally the right move.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Direct evidence that hippocampus learns higher-order temporal community structure in a way that requires sensitivity to overlapping associations -- i.e. distributed similarity-preserving codes, not labeled-line per-item codes. The community-structure paradigm has no per-transition variance in transition probability, so the regularity is genuinely higher-order and cannot be captured by labeled lines alone. Strong evidence WEAKENING option A's labeled-line-only architecture and supporting option B's learned similarity-preserving embedding. Source quality high (Schapiro lab, peer-reviewed Hippocampus, replicated in 2017 modeling paper). Mapping fidelity moderate -- the paradigm is sequential item exposure with community-graph transition structure, not goal-resource identity in a grid world, but the architectural primitive (distributed similarity-preserving substrate) transfers cleanly.
failure_signatures: If option A is chosen and ARM_2 fails to produce wanting != liking trajectory dissociation despite passing identity-recovery, the failure mode is the absent similarity structure -- option A's one-hot slot cannot represent that food and water are both consummatory while novelty is not. The structural prediction this paper licenses is that representations of types within the same superordinate category (consummatory) should be closer than across-category types (consummatory vs novelty). Option A cannot produce that structure; option B and option C can. If V3-EXQ-514 ARM_2 fails wanting!=liking with option A, the recommendation is to upgrade to option C hybrid.

If hippocampus is modulating z_resource through the upstream replay path, the substrate that reaches z_resource is distributed-and-similarity-preserving regardless of whether z_resource ITSELF is one-hot or embedding. This may produce silent failures with option A: identity recovers fine, but the similarity-rich upstream signal is lost at the encoder bottleneck.

SD-016.confidence_rationale: exp=6 entry(s), lit=8 entry(s), exp_conf=0.4, lit_conf=0.782

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the strongest available empirical demonstration that separation and completion are performed by DIFFERENT STAGES on the SAME input, and it is the key entry for the SD-016 H2 (structured retrieval unit) leg rather than for H3. Its methodological strength is the simultaneity: recording DG and CA3 at once during a local-global cue conflict removes the usual confound of comparing separately-recorded populations under nominally-matched conditions, and it lets the authors show DG input to CA3 was severely disrupted WHILE CA3's own output stayed coherent. That is a within-animal, within-session dissociation, which is a much harder result to explain away than the region-by-region comparisons that preceded it. Confidence is held below the Espinoza entry for two reasons: the mapping to SD-016 is architectural-by-analogy (REE has no DG/CA3 stage separation to map onto, so the paper motivates BUILDING one rather than validating an existing design), and the double-rotation cue-conflict paradigm is a specific spatial-navigation manipulation whose relationship to REE's safe-vs-dangerous context distinction requires an inferential step the paper does not license directly.
failure_signatures: Separation and completion are ANTAGONISTIC operations, and the paper's framing is that CA3 arbitrates between them. A single-stage selection mechanism (SD-016's current design) has no place to put that arbitration and may be structurally incapable of achieving both -- pushing toward separation degrades retrieval of a stored association from a partial cue, and pushing toward completion collapses distinct contexts together. The uniform-selection saddle may be what 'maximum completion / zero separation' looks like from the outside.

CA3's behaviour depends on the RELATIVE STRENGTH of its internal attractor dynamics against its external inputs (Knierim & Neunuebel 2016 make this explicit). A retrieval unit with no recurrent/attractor component has no internal dynamics to weigh against input, so the separation-completion balance is not a parameter it possesses -- it is fixed implicitly by the architecture.

DG's pattern separation in this study is expressed via changes in FIRING RATE of place-modulated granule cells rather than by recruiting non-overlapping cell populations; Leutgeb et al. 2007 found the population-recruitment mechanism in CA3 but not DG. A REE design that assumes 'separation == disjoint slot selection' imports only one of the two biological mechanisms and may miss rate-coded separation entirely.

The result is obtained in a cue-CONFLICT paradigm (local and global reference frames placed in opposition), which is an unusually strong perturbation. It does not establish that the same separation/completion division operates under ordinary, non-conflicting input.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the single strongest biological reference for the SD-016 H3 (hard/competitive selection) leg, and it is unusually direct: it does not merely assert that the dentate gyrus performs winner-take-all selection, it measures the connectivity statistics that would be REQUIRED for a WTA circuit and shows the dentate gyrus has them while neocortex does not. 9098 tested connections across 270 slices via up to octuple simultaneous patch-clamp is exceptional methodological quality for a connectivity study. Mapping fidelity is high but not maximal: the paper establishes that the ARCHITECTURE affords WTA, not that WTA selection is observed in behaving animals, so the REE translation ('build the competitive operator into the circuit rather than hoping a downstream loss induces it') is licensed structurally rather than functionally. Transfer risk moderate-low: the finding is an architectural/statistical property of a microcircuit, which is the level REE is actually importing from, so the usual rodent-to-artificial-agent worry bites less than it would for a behavioural result. Weighted toward mapping_fidelity per the skill's guidance for architectural claims.
failure_signatures: Lateral inhibition dominance is a property of the DENTATE GYRUS specifically -- in neocortex, entorhinal cortex and presubiculum, recurrent inhibition is equally or more abundant than lateral inhibition, which the authors state 'would seem incompatible with efficient pattern separation'. So competitive selection is not a generic property of cortical circuits that REE can assume; it is a specialisation that must be deliberately built.

Recurrent inhibition (a unit inhibiting itself) is argued to be actively COUNTER-PRODUCTIVE for WTA because it suppresses potential winners. A naive REE implementation that applies an undifferentiated inhibition/normalisation term across all slots (including self-inhibition) may reproduce the failure mode rather than the fix.

Unitary GC->PV EPSPs (mean 1.79 mV) were measured in vivo to be insufficient to trigger a spike alone against a 10.3 mV threshold gap -- the competitive mechanism depends on SPATIAL SUMMATION across many converging units, so a competitive operator over too few slots (or with too weak convergence) may not engage at all.

Reciprocal GC-PV motifs were NOT significantly enriched, contrary to the neocortical prior the authors tested against. An REE design that imports 'the standard cortical E-I motif' would import the wrong statistics.
The recordings are in vitro slice at ~22 C in juvenile mice (P20-44); connection probabilities may differ in adult, awake, behaving conditions.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the most directly IMPLEMENTABLE reference in the pull: it is a spiking-network model that states the winner-take-all selection rule as an explicit, reproducible mechanism (per-cluster feedback inhibition, with survival determined by whether a unit's time-averaged excitatory:inhibitory conductance ratio exceeds a threshold), rather than describing WTA qualitatively. That makes it useful as a specification for the H3 operator in a way the electrophysiology papers are not. Confidence is held at 0.66 rather than higher for two independent reasons. First, source quality: Physical Review E is a solid physics venue but this is a modelling paper with no new empirical data, and it inherits rather than tests the WTA premise -- it explains HOW WTA arises given an assumed circuit, it does not establish THAT the dentate gyrus does WTA. Second, mapping fidelity: the model's competition is organised into lamellar clusters each with one basket cell, and the mechanism depends on conductance-based spiking dynamics with a meaningful time axis, none of which has a counterpart in SD-016's single-tick feedforward tagger over 16 slots. The value here is the ALGORITHMIC SKELETON (relative-drive competition against a shared inhibitory pool, thresholded, yielding sparse survival), which transfers; the biophysics does not.
failure_signatures: The WTA outcome in this model depends on a THRESHOLD on the E-I conductance ratio: units above R_th survive, all others go silent. A selection mechanism implemented with a soft/graded competition term but no effective thresholding non-linearity may reproduce the uniform-mixing outcome rather than sparse selection -- which is precisely the SD-016 418d/e/i failure signature (an auxiliary diversification loss on a plain softmax achieved population-level diversity without breaking the entropy ceiling).

Competition is LOCAL to a lamellar cluster (one basket cell per cluster), not global across the whole granule-cell population. A single global inhibition/normalisation term over all 16 SD-016 slots is a different architecture from the modelled one, and the paper gives no reason to expect it behaves equivalently.

The model reports that mossy-cell death and adult-born immature granule cells both perturb the WTA competition -- i.e. the sparse-selection regime is sensitive to the composition of the competing population, not robust to it. An REE slot array whose slots have heterogeneous or drifting effective gain may not sit in the WTA regime at all.
Sparsity in the model is ~5% activation of granule cells. Scaled to 16 slots this is below one slot, so the modelled operating regime does not straightforwardly instantiate at SD-016's slot count.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Included deliberately as the entry that constrains how far the other four can be pushed, and it earns its place by changing a design recommendation rather than merely adding caution. It supports the pull's central thesis -- that pattern separation is produced by STRUCTURAL circuit properties rather than by a downstream objective -- while reassigning which structural property matters: the authors argue the primary mechanism is expansion into a higher-dimensional space with SPARSE CONNECTIVITY, and that sparse ACTIVITY and lateral inhibition are secondary contributors rather than the core. That directly qualifies the Espinoza/Kim reading and it bears on the SD-016 design, because SD-016's retrieval layer is dimensionality-REDUCING (z_world dim 32 -> 16 slots) whereas every biological circuit reviewed here is strongly expansive. Direction is 'mixed' rather than 'supports' because the paper simultaneously strengthens the H2 leg and undercuts a naive H3-only reading. Confidence 0.74 reflects a high-quality synthesis review in a top venue by authors with the relevant modelling expertise, discounted because it is argument and synthesis rather than new measurement, and because its cross-circuit comparative frame (cerebellum, mushroom body, DG) means not every conclusion is hippocampus-specific.
failure_signatures: The paper's central structural claim is EXPANSION with sparse connectivity: cerebellar granule layer, insect mushroom body and dentate gyrus all map inputs into a much LARGER population than the input layer. SD-016 does the opposite -- it maps a 32-dim z_world onto 16 slots, a contraction. If expansion is the primary mechanism, then no choice of selection operator over 16 slots recovers it, and both H3 and H2 as currently scoped may be attacking a secondary variable. This is the single most consequential finding in this pull for the portfolio's design.

The authors explicitly state that recent findings 'have questioned long-held ideas' about how these circuits perform pattern separation -- so the Marr-lineage framing that the V3-EXQ-898 autopsy used as its biological reference is itself contested, and should not be treated as settled ground truth.

Decorrelation and sparse activity are argued to be neither necessary nor sufficient for pattern separation in general; a design that optimises a decorrelation/divergence metric (which is close to what SD-016's C1b context-divergence instrument measures) may improve the metric without improving the downstream associative-learning function the separation is FOR.

The relevant benefit of pattern separation in the authors' framing is facilitating associative learning IN THE PRESENCE OF TRIAL-TO-TRIAL VARIABILITY. SD-016's acceptance criteria (C1 entropy, C1b context-divergence) measure representational properties, not learning facilitation under noise, so a pass on both could still leave the functional benefit undemonstrated.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This entry exists to prevent the pull from being a one-sided case for the mechanism the V3-EXQ-898 autopsy already favoured, and it is the strongest available statement of the dissenting position: that the theoretical support and empirical evidence for the DG-as-pattern-separator theory 'are not strong', and that 'binding' of different types of incoming sensory information better captures the DG's contribution to memory encoding. Its direct relevance to SD-016 is sharp, because BINDING is arguably a better description of what SD-016's ContextMemory is actually for -- associating a context cue with hazard-relevant content -- than separation is. Confidence 0.61 rather than higher because this is a minority position argued in a review rather than demonstrated with new data, it predates the strongest connectivity evidence in this pull (Espinoza 2018) which materially strengthens the case it argues against, and the authors' positive alternative (binding) is specified far less precisely than the theory they criticise -- which limits how much design guidance it can actually supply. It is weighted here as a genuine and well-argued caution, not as a refutation.
failure_signatures: The core critique is that 'pattern separation' as used in the behavioural literature (discriminating similar contexts) and as defined computationally (orthogonalising overlapping input patterns) are DIFFERENT claims routinely conflated. SD-016's C1b context-divergence instrument measures the computational sense; the claim's actual functional motivation (vmPFC-like anticipatory hazard response) is behavioural. A pass on the computational instrument does not establish the behavioural function, and the two must not be reported as if they were one result.

If the DG's primary role is BINDING rather than separation, then engineering competitive/sparsifying dynamics into SD-016's retrieval could be actively counterproductive -- sparsification discards the conjunctive combination of inputs that binding requires. The H3 leg would then be expected to produce low entropy AND degraded downstream terrain/action performance, which is a specific, falsifiable prediction worth instrumenting for rather than a vague caution.

The authors conclude the empirical evidence for pattern separation is 'not strong', which means the biological-reference triage in the V3-EXQ-898 autopsy rests on a contested rather than settled literature. The autopsy's framing of the REE tagger as a 'formal-definition import' of pattern separation may therefore be importing a definition whose biological reality is itself disputed.

Much of the behavioural evidence for DG pattern separation comes from adult-neurogenesis manipulations, which have effects on excitability, network sparsity and mood-related behaviour beyond any separation-specific role -- so the causal attribution to separation specifically is weaker than the literature's confident vocabulary suggests.

SD-017.confidence_rationale: exp=3 entry(s), lit=18 entry(s), exp_conf=0.656, lit_conf=0.909

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: High-profile Nature paper with direct unit recordings; the finding (local cortical populations enter sleep-like OFF periods while the animal is behaviourally awake) is exactly the observation that falsifies a single-global-scalar model of sleep state. Reduced from highest only because the transfer to an artificial agent with no cortical topography is architectural rather than direct.
failure_signatures: If REE's eventual sleep-need signal is a single global scalar and the substrate is later found to need per-subsystem consolidation at different rates, this entry predicts the global scalar will average away exactly the demand differences that should drive routing -- diagnostic: compare per-region staleness spread against the single MEL value at cycle entry; a wide spread under a mid-range global MEL is the signature.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative Nature Reviews synthesis proposing the local/emergent account of sleep regulation, with a formal model of cortical-column synchronisation. Theory rather than a single decisive experiment, hence 0.85 rather than higher; its empirical companion in this pull is Vyazovskiy 2011.
failure_signatures: If REE later builds per-region sleep need by SUBDIVIDING a global scalar (top-down allocation of a fixed budget) rather than AGGREGATING per-region demand upward, Krueger predicts the wrong dynamics: regions with genuinely high demand cannot exceed their share, so consolidation saturates. Diagnostic: check whether per-region offline effort sums to a constant across arms with different demand profiles.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical review of the sleep-predation literature by the four authors who established the field. Directly addresses the question the chip asked (should safety gate sleep) and is broad rather than single-species, hence high confidence.
failure_signatures: If a safety term is added to REE sleep onset as a hard boolean AND and a run in a persistently hazardous environment shows sleep NEVER firing, Lima 2005 (with Lima & Bednekoff 1999) says this is a modelling error, not a correct trade-off -- real animals sleep anyway under chronic risk. Diagnostic: sleep-cycle count as a function of hazard density; a floor at zero for high density is the signature.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative Neuron review by the originators of the flip-flop switch model, integrating circuit anatomy with dynamics. Names the three-way homeostatic/circadian/allostatic decomposition explicitly, which is the organising claim of this synthesis's Verdict 1.
failure_signatures: If REE folds a graded safety response directly into MECH-286's boolean AND (e.g. by tuning threat_tonic_threshold) rather than adding a separate continuous term, Saper's architecture predicts chatter: a threshold near the operating point produces rapid permit/refuse oscillation across steps. Diagnostic: count permit-state flips per unit time near threshold; high flip rates are the signature of a missing stabiliser.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Landmark Nature paper with a clean quantitative behavioural manipulation (group edge vs centre) and directional eye-orientation data. The graded, facultative control of sleep depth under risk is exactly the shape question the synthesis needed answered.
failure_signatures: If REE implements a safety term as an all-or-nothing permit and shows a bimodal sleep distribution (full cycles or none) across a hazard gradient, Rattenborg predicts this is wrong-shaped: the biological response is monotone-graded in risk. Diagnostic: sleep duration/depth as a function of threat magnitude should be continuous and monotone, not a step.

SD-018.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=2 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.721

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Howe et al. 2013 provides the strongest available biological evidence for a dedicated reward-proximity encoding circuit in the striatum that cannot be derived from sensory prediction alone. Dopamine ramps emerge as animals approach distant rewards, scaling with distance and value -- yet the sensory environment is invariant during approach (nothing changes until contact). This is the direct biological analog of SD-018's claim that z_world trained on sensory prediction loss cannot encode resource proximity. High source quality (Nature); the mapping is reasonably tight given that REE's CausalGridWorldV2 has similarly invariant sensory scenes until resource contact.
failure_signatures: The dopamine ramp has been subsequently debated: Costa et al. 2025 finds ramp and ACh signals are dissociated, while other groups debate whether the ramp reflects VTA firing or local circuit mechanisms. If the ramp is a local circuit phenomenon (not pure DA neuron ramping), it might be recoverable from context signals rather than requiring a dedicated head.
In the rodent maze paradigm, the ramp emerges through extended training. An untrained agent may not exhibit proximity encoding even with an explicit head if the training signal is too sparse.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Costa et al. 2025 provides mechanistic evidence that NAc dopamine ramps during motivated approach are not coincidental with ACh changes, suggesting the ramp is a distinct approach-drive signal rather than a secondary byproduct of neuromodulatory co-release. This supports SD-018's claim that resource proximity encoding is architecturally separate from sensory/world prediction. However, the paper also notes ongoing controversy about whether DA ramps reflect VTA neuron firing or local circuit mechanisms, which if resolved in favor of local circuits would weaken the claim that a dedicated projection system is required. Rated mixed rather than supports to reflect this mechanistic uncertainty.
failure_signatures: If dopamine ramps are primarily driven by local cholinergic interneuron modulation rather than VTA axonal firing, the ramp signal could in principle be derived from contextual computations in NAc rather than requiring a separate upstream proximity encoder. This would weaken the SD-018 argument that z_world cannot develop proximity sensitivity without an explicit auxiliary head.

DA and ACh were 'largely independent' in this study -- which could indicate the ramp is not robustly coupled to behavioral state in all conditions, reducing its reliability as a sustained proximity signal.

SD-019.confidence_rationale: exp=3 entry(s), lit=5 entry(s), exp_conf=0.658, lit_conf=0.881

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative review by the leading investigator in pain affect dissociation research, published in Science. Directly addresses the dual-pathway architecture: direct spinal-to-limbic inputs (via paleospinothalamic/medial thalamus) alongside the cortico-limbic route through somatosensory cortex. The existence of a direct paleospinothalamic input to the ACC/limbic system -- bypassing S1 -- provides explicit anatomical grounding for why z_harm_a can carry information unavailable in z_harm_s. The 'secondary affect' construct (emotions about future implications of pain) also maps cleanly onto the motivational urgency and commitment-modulation function ascribed to z_harm_a. Confidence slightly below the Rainville empirical paper because this is a review synthesising rather than generating primary data.
failure_signatures: If the 'direct' spinal-to-limbic pathway is quantitatively minor in humans (as some lesion studies suggest), z_harm_a could still be functionally downstream of z_harm_s and hence recoverable from it with a learned transformation.

The review does not resolve whether temporal integration in z_harm_a is a property of the input stream (C-fiber slow accumulation) or of the cortical attractor dynamics in ACC; both would produce nonredundancy, but by different mechanisms with different experimental signatures.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Landmark PET study with direct experimental manipulation (hypnotic suggestion selectively altering unpleasantness without changing intensity). Clean double dissociation: ACC activity tracks unpleasantness, S1 activity tracks intensity. This maps with very high fidelity onto the SD-019 claim that z_harm_a (affective/motivational) and z_harm_s (sensory-discriminative) are representationally nonredundant -- the two streams are dissociable in the direction predicted. High source quality (Science, 1997, repeatedly replicated). Mapping fidelity is strong but not perfect: hypnotic modulation is a cognitive-top-down manipulation rather than a bottom-up test of stream architecture, and the study uses heat pain applied to the hand rather than tissue-damage-driven harm.
failure_signatures: If ACC solely mediates unpleasantness via top-down attentional modulation rather than being a structural node in an independent nociceptive pathway, then the nonredundancy demonstrated here would be context-dependent rather than a substrate property.
Subjects show variable hypnotic susceptibility; a low-susceptibility cohort might fail to show the dissociation, suggesting individual differences in stream separability.

Warm (non-noxious) condition activates S1 without strong ACC activation, which is consistent -- but also shows the dissociation is strongest at noxious intensities, leaving open whether the separation holds across the full range of stimulus levels relevant to REE training.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Landmark Science review by Woolf and Salter on activity-dependent plasticity in nociceptive spinal circuits. Directly addresses the temporal summation mechanism (wind-up) produced by C-fiber afferent input: repeated slow unmyelinated C-fiber volleys cause progressive amplitude increases in dorsal horn neuron responses via NMDA-receptor-mediated central sensitization. This phenomenon does not occur with A-delta (fast, myelinated) fibers at comparable inter-stimulus intervals. The A-delta pathway encodes instantaneous intensity; the C-fiber pathway drives temporal integration through wind-up and subsequent central sensitization. This mechanistically grounds SD-019's core claim that z_harm_a (the affective/motivational stream, receiving predominantly C-fiber input via the paleospinothalamic route) accumulates over time in a history-dependent manner that cannot be reconstructed from instantaneous z_harm_s values. Confidence is high given source quality (Science, Woolf is the field's principal investigator of central sensitization) and the direct relevance of wind-up to the temporal-integration property. Slight attenuation: wind-up is a spinal cord phenomenon whereas z_harm_a is implemented at higher levels; the nonrecoverability constraint in REE is stronger than spinal wind-up alone requires.
failure_signatures: Wind-up requires specific stimulation frequencies (>0.3 Hz) for C-fibers; below this rate, temporal summation does not accumulate. If the harm event rate in CausalGridWorldV2 training episodes is too low, the temporal integration property of z_harm_a may not be reliably triggered.

Central sensitization is partly reversible via pharmacological blockade (NMDA antagonists), which suggests the temporal integration effect is not hardwired but contingent on NMDA plasticity. REE's z_harm_a uses a harm-history FIFO buffer -- a different implementation that does not require ongoing NMDA dynamics.

Some A-delta afferents project via the paleospinothalamic route too, reducing the clean separation between A-delta/neospinothalamic and C-fiber/paleospinothalamic that the REE dual-stream architecture assumes.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Highly influential review by A.D. (Bud) Craig establishing the lamina I spinothalamocortical pathway as the substrate for interoception -- the sense of the physiological condition of the body. Craig identifies the posterior and anterior insula (reached via lamina I --> VMpo thalamus) as the primary cortical terminus for the affective/homeostatic body state signal, structurally distinct from S1/S2 (reached via dorsal horn --> VPc thalamus --> neospinothalamic route). The insular pathway is dominated by C-fiber and small A-delta afferents carrying warm, itch, and homeostatic pain signals -- precisely the input types characterized by temporal integration (C-fiber slow accumulation) rather than instantaneous intensity discrimination (A-delta sharp pain). This covers a distinct angle not present in Price 2000 (which focuses on ACC) or Rainville 1997 (which focuses on ACC vs S1): Craig's contribution is to establish the INSULA as the primary cortical representation of the body's affective/interoceptive state, receiving input via an entirely separate thalamic nucleus (VMpo) from the sensory-discriminative S1/S2 pathway (which receives via VPc). This maps the z_harm_s --> z_harm_a nonredundancy onto the VPc-->S1/S2 vs. VMpo-->insula anatomical split, providing an additional, orthogonal biological support. Confidence slightly lower than Price/Rainville because: (1) Craig's claim that VMpo is a dedicated interoceptive relay is contested in the primate literature; (2) the lamina I --> VMpo pathway specificity is better established in non-human primates than in rodents, creating higher transfer risk to CausalGridWorldV2; (3) the role of the insula as THE primary interoceptive cortex vs. one of several convergence zones remains debated.

The lamina I --> VMpo --> insula pathway may overlap with the lamina I --> mediodorsal thalamus --> ACC pathway that Price 2000 emphasises for pain affect; both pathways may carry similar information, meaning this entry and Price 2000 may not be as independent as their focus on different cortical targets implies.

If z_harm_a's computational role maps more strongly onto the ACC-mediated motivational urgency (Price 2000) than onto the insula-mediated body state representation (Craig 2003), the mapping fidelity of this entry would be reduced.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Landmark clinical case series documenting pain asymbolia -- the selective abolition of the affective and motivational response to pain following insular cortex and SII lesions, while the sensory-discriminative capacity (detection, localization, intensity rating) remains intact. Six patients are described with lesions involving the dominant hemisphere insular cortex and secondary somatosensory cortex (SII). All patients could reliably detect noxious stimuli, localize them, and produce verbal pain intensity ratings, but showed markedly reduced or absent aversive responses: no distress, no avoidance behavior, no complaints of suffering, and sometimes active approach to the painful stimulus. This is the EXACT clinical dissociation that SD-019 requires at the computational level: z_harm_s (sensory-discriminative) remains intact while z_harm_a (affective-motivational) is selectively ablated. Berthier et al. interpret the syndrome as a 'sensory-limbic disconnection' -- the sensory pathway to S1/S2 remains functional, but the route from sensory areas through the insular cortex to limbic structures is severed, preventing the affective response from being driven by sensory harm signals. This provides the strongest direct clinical support for the claim that z_harm_s and z_harm_a are nonredundant: an organism can have normal z_harm_s with a functionally ablated z_harm_a, and the ablation maps to a specific anatomical circuit (insula/SII region) rather than to sensory cortex. Price 2000 references pain asymbolia as supporting evidence but does not provide primary clinical data -- this entry provides the primary source. Confidence slightly below Rainville 1997 because: (1) small n=6 case series without matched controls; (2) no DOI (1988 paper); (3) lesion localization precision limited by 1988 CT/MRI standards; (4) behavioral assessment of pain asymbolia is complex and may conflate multiple constructs including attention and emotional expression.
failure_signatures: If pain asymbolia reflects a deficit in emotional expression or in the motor output of aversive behavior rather than in the encoding of pain affect itself, then the dissociation may not map cleanly onto z_harm_s/z_harm_a -- the patient might still encode z_harm_a internally but fail to translate it into behavior.

Insular/SII lesions are large and heterogeneous in this case series; the syndrome could reflect damage to several functionally distinct regions simultaneously, making it difficult to attribute the dissociation specifically to a z_harm_a circuit component.

Some pain asymbolia patients retain pain-related autonomic responses (heart rate, galvanic skin response) despite absent behavioral distress, suggesting that harm signals can still modulate some systems even when overt affective behavior is abolished -- the ablation of z_harm_a's behavioral output may not equal total absence of the affective representation.

Review by Melzack (gate control theory co-originator) covering the core biological mechanism that SD-022 is designed to instantiate: pain signals persisting in the CNS after the peripheral source is removed or blocked. Phantom limb pain is the canonical example -- pain perceived in an absent limb, without ongoing peripheral input, arising from central sensitization and cortical reorganization. This is the precise analogue of z_harm_a remaining elevated after z_harm_s drops to near-zero when an agent leaves a hazard zone. Preemptive analgesia evidence (blocking the afferent barrage before injury prevents later chronic pain) shows that the central state is written at injury time and persists independently. High source quality; mapping to SD-022 is close but the translation from human chronic pain to a simulated 4-limb grid-world agent requires explicit acknowledgement of the proxy gap.
failure_signatures: Phantom limb pain involves cortical reorganization over weeks-to-months, whereas the SD-022 limb damage model resets much faster (heal_rate=0.002/step, healing within ~500 steps). The timescale mismatch is a proxy risk: the REE body-state mechanism may be too fast to produce the representational persistence that makes phantom limb pain informative.

In humans, peripheral nerve block after established chronic pain often does not resolve the pain, suggesting CNS autonomy -- but in healthy subjects the same block does resolve acute pain. SD-022 needs to produce persistent z_harm_a even in 'healthy' (non-damaged) training conditions, not just under pathological central sensitization.
Central sensitization requires repeated or sustained noxious input to establish; REE training episodes may not be long enough to produce the requisite synaptic potentiation.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Clinical review documenting the high comorbidity of chronic pain and PTSD, with evidence that each condition amplifies the other. This supports SD-022's 'failure mode' framing: persistent z_harm_a in the absence of current threat corresponds to the PTSD hypervigilance state -- a body that remains in a threat-state even when the external world is safe. The mutual-maintenance model (PTSD and chronic pain share neural substrates including heightened amygdala reactivity and impaired extinction) provides biological grounding for the failure mode. Lower confidence than Melzack 2001 because this is a clinical-comorbidity review without direct mechanistic experiments, and the mapping to z_harm_a specifically (rather than the broader threat state) requires several inferential steps.
failure_signatures: The mechanisms linking PTSD and chronic pain are correlational; the shared neural substrates (amygdala, insula, ACC) are the same regions that process both conditions, but this does not demonstrate that the body-state channel (z_harm_a) is the mediating variable rather than a higher-level cognitive appraisal.

PTSD-induced chronic pain amplification may involve cognitive reappraisal and attention mechanisms that are absent in the REE agent architecture; the model may not produce the analogous failure mode even with SD-022 implemented.

SD-023.confidence_rationale: exp=1 entry(s), lit=4 entry(s), exp_conf=0.125, lit_conf=0.838

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: FAIL with weakening direction

Schultz et al. 1997 demonstrated that primate dopamine neurons shift their activity from encoding the reward itself to encoding the earliest predictive cue in the chain. After conditioning, dopamine responds at the first conditioned stimulus (CS1) that predicts a later CS2 which predicts reward -- not at the reward delivery. This is the canonical biological demonstration that predictive signals travel backward in time to the most distal available cue. This directly supports the MECH-216 component of SD-023: Landmark B (placed near resources) is intended to fire E1's predictive wanting signal BEFORE resource proximity rises. The TD-learning framework formalises exactly this: a predictive representation arising at a distal environmental feature that co-occurs reliably with a downstream reward. The confidence is moderate rather than high because the TD/dopamine mechanism is about learning temporal associations, whereas SD-023 requires E1 to learn these associations from gradient texture -- an additional learning step not directly evidenced here.
failure_signatures: Schultz et al. 1997 describes dopamine-level prediction error signals, not LSTM world-model prediction. E1 in REE is a sensory prediction error machine, not a value-learning machine. The temporal structure argument is valid, but the specific mechanism (TD error in DA neurons vs. sensory prediction error in E1 LSTM) is different.

The cue-reward transfer in this work depends on explicit Pavlovian pairings: the CS must reliably co-occur with reward. Landmark B in SD-023 is placed near resources but may not co-occur perfectly, especially if resources are consumed and respawn. If the pairing is noisy, the predictive signal may not emerge.
This paper does not address whether the gradient texture itself (as opposed to a discrete CS) is sufficient to drive predictive coding in a non-dopaminergic world-model system like E1.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Yaghoubi et al. 2026 directly demonstrates that hippocampal neurons shift their temporal coding from reward-encoding to predictive-cue encoding as learning progresses. Over weeks of training, place cells active at the reward site gradually moved their peak firing backward in time to events preceding the reward. A temporal difference model of place field evolution successfully replicated this shift. This is strong evidence that the hippocampus operates as a learning predictive map, not a static spatial register. This supports SD-023 in two ways: (1) the hippocampal world model is inherently predictive and will develop anticipatory representations IF appropriate distal predictive cues exist in the environment -- precisely what Landmark B provides; (2) the TD-place-field model is directly analogous to E1's LSTM world-model learning from temporal sequences in world_obs. The paper was published January 2026, making it highly current. Confidence is slightly attenuated because the study concerns reward-predicting place cells specifically, while SD-023's Landmark B is a non-reward landmark near resources -- but the principle (structured environment enables predictive temporal coding) transfers cleanly.
failure_signatures: The backward shift in Yaghoubi et al. 2026 depends on the agent repeatedly visiting the same trajectory. In CausalGridWorldV2, if the agent does not develop consistent routes near Landmark B, the temporal displacement of the predictive signal may not emerge.

The study observes predictive coding for reward itself -- the place fields shift backward relative to a fixed reward location. Landmark B in SD-023 is predictive of resource proximity, not a reward signal per se. If the agent does not assign motivational value to resources (z_goal not firing), the hippocampal-analogous predictive remapping may not occur.
This is a 2026 paper; methodological critique and replication are still pending.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: O'Keefe and Burgess 1996 demonstrated that place cell firing fields are geometrically anchored to environmental boundaries and walls. Even neutral geometric features (walls of rectangular enclosures with no intrinsic reward value) determine the location and shape of each place field. When walls were stretched, place fields elongated proportionally. This directly supports the SD-023 claim that neutral landmark objects with characteristic spatial gradients are necessary environmental features -- the biological evidence shows that geometry and environmental texture (not reward alone) structure hippocampal world-model representations. However, the paper uses geometric walls rather than discrete objects with gradient fields, so the translation to Landmark-A/B objects in CausalGridWorldV2 requires an extrapolation step.
failure_signatures: The study uses rectangular walls as the primary environmental feature, not discrete objects with gradient fields. The REE Landmark A/B design relies on point-source or zone-bounded gradient objects, which are qualitatively different from wall-distance tuning.

Place cells fire at a single preferred location in a given environment regardless of whether the agent has encountered a reward there. SD-023 requires that landmark gradients provide temporal structure for E1 prediction, which goes beyond the spatial firing shown here.
The boundary-vector model derived from this work predicts that place fields near walls exist for allocentric navigation -- not that they provide predictive temporal signals to an LSTM world model.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This paper provides the most direct biological grounding for SD-023's core claim. Wang et al. 2020 showed that ~40% of place field edges concentrate near surface-texture boundaries -- well above the chance rate of 33% -- even when textures were flat and presented no physical barrier or navigational obstruction. Neural population vectors decorrelated more sharply across texture boundaries than within texture zones. This establishes that hippocampal spatial representation is sensitive to environmental texture (not just walls, rewards, or explicit landmarks) at a fine-grained level. The SD-023 proposal that gradient fields around Landmark objects provide E1 with environmental texture to structure its world model is directly supported: if texture alone (without reward or navigational function) modulates hippocampal representations, then adding texture-gradient objects is ecologically motivated and architecturally coherent. The study is in rats on tracks and platforms, limiting direct transfer to a grid-world LSTM, but the principle is clear.
failure_signatures: The paper shows that texture boundaries affect where place field edges fall, but it does not show that texture per se generates temporal prediction signals. SD-023 requires that E1's LSTM uses gradient texture to form anticipatory predictions, not just to segment space.
The effect size is modest: only ~40% of edges near boundaries vs. 33% chance. The representation is sensitive to texture but not dominated by it.
The study uses 1D tracks and 2D platforms in laboratory conditions -- far from the rich multi-object CausalGridWorldV2 environment envisioned by SD-023.
