recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the paper SD-024's own notes cite as its biological grounding, and it does carry that weight: local D1-receptor blockade in CA1 prevents reward-driven place-cell reorientation and produces perseveration. It earns a solid but not high confidence because it establishes that DA gates reward-relevant REMAPPING, which is a weaker and different statement than DA producing local representational EXPANSION -- the claim's actual mechanism.
failure_signatures: Blocking D1 receptors locally in CA1 prevented place-cell reorientation to the rule-relevant spatial dimension and produced perseveration -- the animal kept using the old reference frame. This is precisely SD-024's declared 'perseveration' failure mode, but note it arises here from DA BLOCKADE, whereas SD-024 predicts perseveration from DA locked HIGH. The claim's failure-mode taxonomy may have the sign inverted, or may be describing a different perseveration.

Learning impairment and representational failure were inseparable in this design: the animals that failed to remap also failed to learn, so the experiment cannot say whether the map change causes the behaviour or vice versa.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A well-controlled direct test of the strong form of SD-024 that comes out negative: no general over-representation of goals by place fields in CA1 or CA3, and no modulation of place-cell activity by goal VALUE, in animals whose behaviour demonstrably tracked that value. Confidence is high enough to matter for governance but not higher, because the design dissociates goal location from reward consumption -- which is arguably a manipulation that removes the very DA-delivery event SD-024 says does the allocating.
failure_signatures: Rats reliably preferred the higher-value goal, yet place-cell firing was not modulated by goal value -- behavioural value sensitivity dissociated cleanly from map-level value coding. If REE's benefit terrain shows density scaling with benefit_magnitude, that is a point of divergence from this dataset, not a point of convergence.

No general over-representation of goals was found by place fields in either CA1 or CA3, contradicting the phenomenon SD-024 takes as its starting point. Goal-related activity appeared instead as OUT-OF-FIELD ramping during the waiting period -- a rate/timing code at the goal rather than a reallocation of spatial resource toward it.

The authors' interpretation is that the dorsal hippocampal map is value-FREE and links to value represented elsewhere. Taken at face value this contradicts SD-024's architectural premise that the hippocampal residue field is where reward-scaled representational expansion should live.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Directly on-target as a computational existence proof that reward-location over-representation and its dynamic shift can be generated by a simple reward-distance-dependent modulation -- SD-024's phenomenon, reproduced in silico. But it is mixed rather than supporting because the mechanism it uses is a dynamic GAIN on existing units in a continuous attractor network, which is exactly the alternative SD-024's weight-independent density discriminator is designed to rule out. It is simultaneously the best available proof-of-concept and the sharpest statement of the confound.
failure_signatures: Over-representation and its shift to a relocated reward were reproduced without any change in the number or placement of representational units -- a distance-dependent gain on a fixed attractor population sufficed. Any REE measurement that reads density off activity or weights will therefore not discriminate SD-024's allocation mechanism from a gain mechanism.

The model is not fit to or validated against recorded data; it reproduces a qualitative phenomenon in 1D tracks and 2D square arenas. Its 5-10 cm over-representation zone is a model output, not a measured constraint, and should not be imported as a scale for da_jitter_radius.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The strongest available causal test of the exact dependency SD-024 asserts: a VTA dopaminergic signal in CA1 is what sustains reward-location over-representation, and optogenetically removing it collapses the over-representation. High source quality (Nat Commun, 2-photon calcium imaging plus circuit-specific inhibition, converging manipulations). Confidence is held below 0.9 because the paper measures over-representation as place-field COUNT/reliability in a real CA1 population, whereas SD-024 asserts a specific implementational route (extra RBF centers allocated per DA-scaled reward event) that the paper neither confirms nor excludes.
failure_signatures: When reward expectation is extinguished, over-representation of reward locations vanishes while the animal remains engaged with the environment -- so an implementation that keeps expanded density after reward removal (SD-024's 'craving' failure mode) is biologically off-pattern, not merely suboptimal.

Loss of the dopaminergic reward-proximity signal increases place-field remapping throughout the whole environment and reduces trial-to-trial reliability -- i.e. removing DA does not simply flatten the map locally, it destabilises it globally. An REE ablation that shows only a local density change may be under-modelling the mechanism.

failure_signatures: If REE collapses information value into ordinary reward/water value, it misses the source's central dissociation between intrinsic information value and extrinsic reward value.
If SD-025 is read as directly validated by this source, it overclaims: Bussell et al. do not test hippocampal representational density, familiarity discounting, or CEM trajectory scoring.

If MECH-314b remains a broadcast scalar across candidates, this paper cannot rescue it; the source motivates a separable information-value axis, but REE still needs a per-candidate uncertainty/information readout to affect action selection.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The L3 capacity anchor: Cowan's wide-ranging synthesis argues the pure capacity limit of the focus of attention is a small fixed number averaging about 4 chunks (3-5), distinct from Miller's compound 7. This grounds two things the deliberation roadmap needs: (1) a principled prior on SD-046's slot count N (2-4, not arbitrary), and (2) the capacity-limited-selection premise behind SD-027/MECH-254's top-k gate. Held to 0.62: the transfer from human STM chunks to goal slots / selected latents is an analogy across domains, and Cowan's 'focus of attention' is not goals specifically; it bounds the count without being measured on goal maintenance.

The capacity is a CENTRAL focus-of-attention limit, with non-capacity-limited stores (activated LTM) alongside it; an REE design that treats all maintained goals as occupying the capacity-limited focus would over-constrain, when biology allows many activated-but-not-focal goals plus a small focal set.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The resource-model counterweight to Cowan's fixed-slot view: Bays & Husain show visual WM capacity is NOT a fixed number of items but a limited resource shared dynamically across all items, with allocation biased by attention and saccade targets, and the proportion allocated to each item setting its PRECISION (a power law). Mixed direction by design: it SUPPORTS the capacity-limited and precision-weighted-selection premises behind SD-027/SD-028/MECH-254, but CHALLENGES SD-046's discrete-fixed-slot framing -- the honest tension the node should carry. Confidence 0.58 reflects the productive disagreement plus visual-WM->goal-slot transfer risk.
failure_signatures: If SD-046 commits to N discrete equal-capacity slots, Bays & Husain predict that is the wrong idealisation: a shared flexible resource means adding a 3rd or 4th active goal does not give it a full slot -- it dilutes the precision of ALL goals, so the marginal goal is represented poorly rather than fully. A fixed-slot SD-046 would mis-predict graceful degradation.

Resource allocation is biased toward saccade/attention targets; an REE arbitrator that allocated equal resource across slots regardless of which is being acted on would not match the biology -- the acted-on goal should draw disproportionate precision.

MOSAIC's responsibility-signal mechanism for selecting among multiple paired models is theoretically clean but empirically under-specified; if SD-003-prereq adopts a multi-stream architecture (one E2_x per reafferent stream), the routing/selection mechanism is the next architectural question and is not solved here.

Forward-model errors are used both for trajectory correction and for credit assignment in the paper's account. SD-029 uses the residual specifically for agency attribution; the paper does not separate these two roles and a clean separation may be an REE-specific design problem.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical primate-substrate review of corollary discharge (CD) -- the efference-copy infrastructure that any forward-model comparator architecture (SD-029, MECH-256, and the SD-003-prereq substrate work generally) presupposes. Crapse and Sommer survey single-unit, microstimulation, and inactivation evidence across saccadic, vocalisation, locomotor, and reach systems and arrive at the unifying claim: copies of motor commands are routed to sensory and parietal structures so that predicted sensory consequences can be subtracted from incoming reafference. That is precisely the architectural shape SD-003-prereq has to instantiate -- an efference-copy pathway feeding a forward model whose output is differenced against the realised stream. Confidence is high on source quality (Curr Opin Neurobiol, NIH-funded, widely cited) and moderate-to-high on mapping fidelity: the paper directly evidences the substrate (a_actual must be distributed to the forward model alongside the realised stream), but it stops short of formalising the comparator residual the way MECH-256 does, and it makes no architectural commitment about whether the forward model is single-pass or two-pass.
failure_signatures: When CD pathways are silenced (e.g. inactivation of the MD thalamic relay carrying the saccadic CD), monkeys lose the ability to compensate for self-generated sensory change -- they treat reafferent shifts as if they were externally caused. This is the substrate-level instantiation of the SD-003 failure mode: without an efference-copy input, the comparator cannot distinguish self-caused from world-caused change.

CD signals are distributed across many circuits with different latencies and modality profiles; a single forward model is unlikely to suffice across streams. This supports MECH-256's stream-agnostic framing (one comparator per reafferent stream) over a monolithic E2 comparator.

The review notes that CD does not always equate to a clean efference copy -- some signals are pre-motor predictions, others are post-motor. A comparator architecture that assumes a_actual is the only input may miss intention-level prediction signals that the brain actually uses.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality review (Trends in Neurosciences, Heinricher lab has canonical authority on RVM circuit). Mapping fidelity is moderate: the paper definitively characterises the PAG/RVM mechanism as behavioural-state gating via ON/OFF cells, NOT efference-copy comparator -- this weakens the hypothesis that PAG/RVM IS the nociceptive comparator substrate but does not undermine MECH-256 itself (behavioural attenuation of self-generated pain, shown by Lalouni 2020 in this corpus, is real). The paper supports the existence of a rich, regulated descending nociceptive control system, while implying the efference-copy mechanism operates at a different anatomical level (spinal dorsal horn / somatosensory cortex, via corticospinal collaterals).
failure_signatures: PAG/RVM ON/OFF cell firing is governed by behavioural state (arousal, stress, defensive motivation) and opioid tone, NOT by motor command prediction -- the system does not implement efference-copy cancellation of predicted nociception from a_actual.
If MECH-256 were implemented primarily in PAG/RVM, the clinical literature would predict that lesioning PAG/RVM abolishes self-generated pain attenuation; the paper does not support this specificity.

Molecular identification of RVM cell types produces conflicting behavioural results, indicating the system's modulatory function is more context-sensitive and less mechanistically clean than a forward-model comparator.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Seymour (2019) establishes pain as a precision-weighted prediction-error signal within a reinforcement-learning / active-inference framework. This is compatible with MECH-256's residual-comparator framing but operates at a higher computational level: MECH-256 proposes a per-step forward-model residual on a specific latent stream (z_harm_s), while Seymour frames pain as the global prediction-error signal that drives behavioural learning and control across timescales. Mapping fidelity is moderate -- the frameworks are architecturally convergent (both use prediction-error logic) but differ in scope (MECH-256: per-step, stream-specific; Seymour: multi-timescale, distributed). Transfer risk is low (theoretical framework with strong empirical anchoring). Confidence capped at 0.61 because Seymour's framework does not directly test or confirm the efference-copy comparator mechanism on a per-step basis -- it provides a higher-level computational motivation.
failure_signatures: Seymour frames pain as a learned-expectation prediction error, not as a per-step forward-model residual from motor efference copy -- if the efference-copy mechanism were the PRIMARY driver of self-pain attenuation, Seymour's framework would need substantial refinement to accommodate within-trial (single-step) timescales.

The precision-signal framework emphasises the role of descending modulation in shaping EXPECTED precision of pain signals (prior over precision), which is more consistent with PAG/RVM contextual gating than with the motor-efference-copy comparator -- the two mechanisms are parallel in the biological system.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Supplies the DETECTION MECHANISM for the V3 proxy and ties it to REE's existing substrate. The comparator model holds that the sense of agency arises when (and only when) the comparator detects that predicted sensory feedback matches actual feedback; mismatch yields loss/attribution-elsewhere of agency. REE already instantiates exactly this form in SD-029 (residual = observed - predicted action outcome). A blocked-agency signal is the sustained/integrated comparator MISMATCH on the action-outcome channel attributed to external constraint. The paper genuinely supports SD-029's comparator role, so SD-029 is co-tagged. Confidence held at 0.66: it is a theoretical/philosophy paper defending the comparator account (vs Synofzik's multifactorial weighting), focused on schizophrenic alien-control rather than blocked action per se, so the mapping is by mechanism-analogy.
failure_signatures: The comparator yields a binary-ish agency/no-agency readout; a blocked-agency AFFECT signal additionally requires (a) attributing the mismatch to an EXTERNAL constraint rather than own motor error, and (b) gating on RETAINED goal/capacity -- a bare comparator mismatch is necessary but not sufficient, so REE must add the attribution + capacity gate on top of SD-029.

Synofzik et al.'s multifactorial-weighting critique (that actual sensory consequences are not always needed for the sense of agency) is a live alternative; if agency in REE is sometimes inferred from intention/context rather than realised-outcome comparison, a pure comparator-mismatch detector would miss or misfire on those cases.

SD-030.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=4 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.809

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A well-cited neurocognitive model that decomposes body-ownership into exactly the components REE posits for the self-model: a pre-existing stored body model, online multisensory integration modulated by that model, and a referral step that yields the ownership experience -- with a named cortical division of labour (right TPJ incorporeability test, S2 online body representation, posterior parietal/ventral premotor recalibration, right posterior insula subjective ownership). The model-against-internal-model-of-the-body structure is a faithful biological analogue of SD-030's self-comparator and ARC-081's stored self-slot. Held below 0.7 because it is a review/model synthesis (not a single decisive experiment), and the INV-064 ordering mapping is weak.
failure_signatures: Body-ownership requires a pre-existing stored model of the body to gate which external objects are even incorporeable; without a prior self-model there is no referral step -- this is the structural prerequisite SELF-1 (stateful z_self) must satisfy before SD-030/MECH-215 can attach, and it fails if z_self is only an instantaneous EMA snapshot.

Ownership is computed as multisensory input weighted against the internal body model; when the two conflict beyond tolerance, incorporation fails -- a comparator-with-tolerance, matching SD-030's residual gate and failing exactly where the residual exceeds threshold.

The right posterior insula carries the subjective-ownership signal; if the interoceptive partner is absent the multisensory match can occur without the felt-mine experience -- predicting a dissociation that a purely exteroceptive self-model (no MECH-214 interoceptive channel) would suffer.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, massively replicated psychophysical demonstration that the felt boundary of the bodily self is a recalibratable inference over multisensory inputs, not a fixed given. This is strong direct support for the ARC-081 stance that z_self is a constructed, malleable object-representation rather than a privileged primitive. Confidence is held below 0.7 because the mapping from a perceptual ownership illusion to REE's latent z_self plasticity is an analogy at the representational level, not a measurement of REE's actual comparator.
failure_signatures: If z_self were an unrevisable body-state primitive rather than an inferred object, synchronous visuo-tactile stimulation of an external object could not capture ownership -- the rubber-hand effect shows the self-boundary is re-inferred from current evidence, exactly what ARC-081 requires and what a fixed-latent z_self would forbid.

The illusion requires temporally congruent multisensory input; asynchronous stroking abolishes it -- i.e. ownership is gated by a prediction/observation match, which is precisely the SD-030 comparator signature and fails when the match is broken.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The direct conceptual anchor for SD-030: optimal motor control relies on internal representations of the ACTUAL, DESIRED, and PREDICTED states of the limbs/world, and breakdowns in the predicted-vs-actual comparison produce specific agency pathologies (delusions of control, anarchic hand, phantom limbs). This is the forward-model-self architecture SD-030 instantiates as residual_self, and the E2-self-transition half of MECH-215. High mapping fidelity to the mechanism; held at 0.70 because it is a review/framework rather than a single decisive experiment and the human-clinical-to-REE transfer is at the functional-role level.
failure_signatures: When the predicted state of the motor system diverges from the actual state beyond the comparator's reach, the action is no longer attributed to the self -- the delusion-of-control / passivity signature, which SD-030 predicts as a self-stream residual exceeding the attribution threshold.

Awareness of action is built on motor-command (efference) streams, not only sensory feedback; phantom-limb movement illusions arise from the command stream alone -- so a self-model lacking an E2-self forward prediction (efference-copy analogue) cannot represent agency at all, the MECH-215 (2) prerequisite.

Only certain components of the internal representation reach awareness; impairing the predicted-state component selectively breaks agency while leaving movement intact -- a dissociation a single undifferentiated z_self could not produce.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The fuller review behind the 2002 TICS framework, with the added value of a localisation claim: representations of the CURRENT and PREDICTED state of the motor system are in parietal cortex, while representations of INTENDED movements are in prefrontal/premotor cortex. This dissociates the predicted-state machinery (SD-030 comparator substrate) from the intention/goal machinery (E3-side), which is exactly the separation REE draws between the self-forward-model and the goal/viability evaluator. Held at 0.68 because the lesion synthesis is correlational and the parietal/prefrontal localisation is coarse relative to REE's z_self/z_goal split.
failure_signatures: Phantom-limb and anosognosic movement illusions are driven by motor-command streams in the ABSENCE of sensory confirmation -- a self-model that represents agency from intention alone, with no observed-self to compare against, will hallucinate successful action, the failure SD-030's residual is meant to catch.

Damage dissociates 'predicted current state' (parietal) from 'intended movement' (prefrontal/premotor); collapsing these into one representation -- as V3 does by running E2 on combined z_gamma with no z_self stream -- removes the distinction agency depends on.

Delusions of control arise when intention and the felt consequence of action are no longer properly linked: the comparator between intended and achieved self-state has failed, the MECH-215 (2) E2-self-transition prerequisite breaking.

SD-031.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=3 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.583

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the sharpest and most precisely-targeted counterweight in the pull, and it lands on SD-031's structure rather than on its periphery. The authors draw a distinction REE has not explicitly made: NARROW sense of agency (associated with movements) versus BROAD sense of agency (associated with environmental events). They then argue that the comparator model was developed from, and is evidentially supported by, studies of sensory consequences NARROWLY tied to movements -- while standard experimental paradigms in fact study only BROAD agency. Their conclusion is that the comparator model is not a satisfactory account of sense of agency, that narrow SoA is equally well explained by a simpler motor-signal model, and they report two experiments that failed to induce illusory narrow SoA where the comparator model predicts it should be inducible. This matters for SD-031 specifically because z_world is by definition the BROAD stream -- environmental consequences, 'the door opened because of me' -- and SD-031 proposes to apply a comparator architecture precisely there, which is the extension these authors argue is unwarranted. Confidence 0.69: peer-reviewed, argument is directly on point, and it is the exact structural objection SD-031 must answer; discounted because it is primarily a theoretical/negative-result paper whose empirical component is two null illusion-induction experiments (informative but limited), and because an argument against a comparator as a model of conscious AGENCY EXPERIENCE is not automatically an argument against a comparator as a functional attribution MECHANISM.
failure_signatures: The comparator model's evidential support comes from narrow (movement-tied) sensory consequences, but it is routinely applied to broad (environmental-event) agency, where that support does not extend.
Two experiments designed to induce illusory narrow sense of agency in healthy participants failed to do so, contrary to comparator-model prediction.
For narrow sense of agency a simpler motor-signal model explains the data equally well, so the comparator's extra machinery is not licensed by parsimony.
Conflating narrow and broad agency lets a model validated on one be credited with explaining the other.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Directly relevant to SD-031's 'single-pass' qualifier, which is the part of the claim most exposed to disconfirmation. Using a bias-free two-alternative forced-choice control-detection task with staircased difficulty (accuracy held at 70%) and signal-detection measures (d', meta-d') across 40 participants, the authors identify TWO distinct processes underlying first-order detection of control: one based on instantaneous sensory predictions for the current movement, and one based on detection of a regular motor-visual relation ACROSS A SERIES of movements. The first is a single-pass comparator of essentially SD-031's form; the second is a temporally-extended regularity detector that a single-pass residual cannot implement. Methodologically strong (bias-free d', staircase control, SEM, n=40, Haggard lab). Confidence 0.66 rather than higher because the paradigm again uses visuomotor object control rather than general world-state consequences, and because the dual-process decomposition is inferred from an individual-differences/SEM analysis rather than from direct manipulation of each process.
failure_signatures: First-order detection of control decomposes into at least two processes -- an instantaneous per-movement sensory prediction and a cross-trial motor-visual regularity detector -- so a purely instantaneous comparator captures only part of the attribution signal.

Metacognitive sensitivity was NEGATIVELY correlated with the predictive-process component, contradicting the hypothesis that detection of control relies on metacognitive monitoring of a predictive circuit and suggesting the predictive comparator operates unconsciously.

Large individual differences in metacognitive sensitivity persisted even when first-order sensitivity was experimentally equated, so aggregate agency measures can mask heterogeneous underlying mechanisms.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The strongest available support for SD-031's core architectural bet: that self-versus-other attribution of EXTERNAL consequences is carried by a signal that is separable from the sensorimotor stream that produced the action. Using MVPA on a paradigm where self-agency evolves gradually with sensorimotor experience, the authors decode self-other attribution from sensorimotor, posterior parietal, anterior insular and higher visual cortices, and -- critically for SD-031 -- show a DISSOCIATION of preference: right supramarginal gyrus (inferior parietal lobe) is most sensitive to self-other attribution, while bilateral precentral gyri and left IPL dominantly reflect sensorimotor information. That preference dissociation is the load-bearing finding, because it is the biological analogue of SD-031's decision to give z_world its own comparator rather than reading attribution off the motor/self stream. Peer-reviewed, methodologically strong (MVPA with an explicit preference analysis rather than a single contrast). Confidence held to 0.72 by modality distance -- BOLD decodability establishes that the information is PRESENT in a region, not that the brain computes it as an explicit subtractive residual of a forward-model prediction, which is the specific functional form SD-031 asserts.
failure_signatures: Self-other attribution information is distributed across several regions rather than localised to one comparator, so a single-site or single-stream readout will under-detect it.

Regions carrying attribution information and regions carrying sensorimotor information overlap substantially; only a preference analysis separates them, so a design without such a contrast will confound the two.
Decodability of attribution from a region does not establish that the region computes attribution as an explicit prediction-minus-observation residual.

SD-032a.confidence_rationale: exp=1 entry(s), lit=20 entry(s), exp_conf=0.575, lit_conf=0.856

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative review by the Palmiter lab on PBN CGRP neurons as a general alarm system relaying interoceptive distress (visceral malaise, taste, temperature, pain, itch) to forebrain. The bidirectional architecture -- PBN CGRP suppresses appetite and routes negative valence to amygdala -- is the substrate inverse of the override question: PBN CGRP is what hunger-driven override has to overcome. For REE, this characterises the mechanism that drives the harm-stream lock in V3-EXQ-471 (PBN-analog driving sustained z_harm_a). Confidence high because the review is by the lab that defined the circuit.
failure_signatures: PBN CGRP activation produces ANOREXIA (suppressed feeding) -- the threat -> reduced food intake direction is mediated by this pathway, which is what override has to break.
PBN CGRP routes alarm to extended amygdala, hypothalamus, and thalamus simultaneously -- another broadcast pattern, this time on the threat side.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the most direct biological analogue of the V3-EXQ-471 catatonia scenario yet published. Mice toggle dynamically between food seeking and self-preservation as predation threat varies, and increasing caloric need (the override signal) re-engages food seeking under threat through identified AgRP -> BNST and AgRP -> LH circuits. Crucially, predator-responsive PMd-CCK neurons SUPPRESS AgRP activity, not via z_harm-side modulation -- so the threat -> feeding suppression is an active circuit, not just a competing scalar. Confidence high because the architecture maps cleanly onto SD-012/SD-036 and identifies specific output pathways the V3 model can implement.
failure_signatures: Predator threat suppresses AgRP (hunger) activity rather than just competing with it -- suggesting threat-driven hypophagia is an active inhibition, not arbitration loss.
Override of threat by hunger requires increased caloric need; the override signal scales with deprivation, supporting graded rather than threshold drive amplification.
AgRP -> BNST and AgRP -> LH are distinct output channels for threat-overriding food seeking; suggests at least two-target broadcast rather than single output.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Structural neuroimaging in Prader-Willi syndrome (the canonical clinical model of pathological insatiable hunger) shows hypothalamic volume changes correlating with BMI. PWS is the human existence proof for what happens when the hunger-override system runs without a regulatory shutoff: the patient eats relentlessly despite obesity and metabolic harm. For V3, this is a clinical phenotype where the override authority's regulatory layer is missing, producing a sustained drive_level that cannot be arbitrated down. Confidence moderate-high because the clinical phenotype is well-characterised but the imaging-genotype-behaviour mechanistic chain is correlational.
failure_signatures: Insatiable hunger despite obesity -- when override authority lacks regulatory shutoff, drive_level remains saturated regardless of metabolic state.
Hypothalamic structural alteration correlates with BMI -- the substrate of the override regulator is altered in a graded way, supporting graded rather than all-or-nothing regulator function.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Definitive circuit-tracing paper showing VMHdm SF1+ neurons send collateral projections that produce DIFFERENT defensive behaviours via DIFFERENT downstream targets: VMHdm -> dlPAG drives immobility/freezing; VMHdm -> AHN drives avoidance. This is the canonical demonstration that a single upstream broadcast splits at downstream nodes into distinct behavioural commits, exactly the architecture SD-032a SalienceCoordinator should arbitrate. Confidence high because the dissection is causal (optogenetic terminal stimulation) and uses fluorescent retrograde tracers to identify true collateral projections.
failure_signatures: Single VMHdm cell sends collaterals to multiple downstream targets, each driving a distinct defensive sub-behaviour -- broadcast architecture from single source.
Different terminal stimulation produces different behaviour from the SAME upstream population -- arbitration happens downstream, not at the source.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Recent Anderson-lab paper showing VMHdm population dynamics encode predator imminence as a continuous variable, with anti-correlated subpopulations encoding threat-presence vs threat-absence. The ramp/decay dynamics of these populations directly characterise what an upstream-of-PAG harm signal looks like in vivo, and the existence of an anti-correlated 'safety' subpopulation is direct evidence that the harm vs no-harm decision is computed in VMHdm population dynamics rather than purely downstream. Confidence high because the imaging is large-scale GCaMP across many cells and the analysis cleanly separates encoding subpopulations.
failure_signatures: Anti-correlated 'threat-on' and 'threat-off' subpopulations in VMHdm -- the hypothalamus itself implements a winner-take-all arbitration before broadcasting downstream.
Continuous population coding of imminence -- threat is not binary at the source; thresholding happens downstream (consistent with MECH-279).

SD-032b.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=14 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.853

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Directly tests whether the pain PE signal in ventral anterior insula is pain-specific or a general aversive-event signal by crossing painful stimuli with aversive pictures in a cross-modal expectation paradigm. Pain-specific PE, not general aversiveness, drives the ventral anterior insula integration. Strong design, clean fMRI dissociation. Most relevant for arguing that the pain forward model must be modality-specific at the integration stage.
failure_signatures: A fully shared aversive-event forward model is falsified by modality-specific PE signals.
If a single forward model generated both pain PE and non-pain aversive PE, ventral anterior insula should respond to both; it does not.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Most REE-relevant paper in the pull. Builds a biophysical predictive-coding model with S1 (sensory-discriminative) and ACC (affective-emotional) as two coupled but distinct populations, fit to rat LFP data from both regions. This is essentially the computational architecture REE is proposing with E2_harm_s (SD-032b's upstream sensory predictor) and E2_harm_a (upstream affective predictor) as two coupled populations. Direct empirical + computational grounding.
failure_signatures: A single unified pain forward model is falsified: S1 and ACC populations have distinct temporal dynamics and require separate model variables.
A fully decoupled parallel model is also weakened: the paper models S1 and ACC with explicit coupling terms, not as independent populations.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Synthesis commentary comparing two independent cross-modal pain-expectancy studies (Sharvit 2018, Fazeli & Buchel 2018). Argues explicitly that the anterior insula runs sensory-specific predictive models, with analogous but dissociable machinery for pain, disgust, and other aversive modalities. Lower weight than empirical entries because it is a commentary/review, but valuable for the architectural synthesis it provides.
failure_signatures: A single cross-modal aversive predictive model is falsified by sensory-specificity of the anterior insula PE.
Does not directly test within-pain stream separation.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Single most informative paper in the pull. It decomposes insula PE signals into modality-independent (unsigned, anterior insula, pain and sound) and modality-specific (signed, dorsal posterior insula, pain only). This is exactly the shape of architecture needed to distinguish 'shared trunk' from 'fully separate' forward models. Large N (47), within-subject design, PLoS Biology peer review. Directly resolves the biological architecture question.
failure_signatures: A single modality-shared forward model is falsified: signed pain-specific PE is topographically distinct from general unsigned aversive PE.
A set of fully independent per-modality forward models is also weakened: the unsigned anterior-insula PE is shared across pain and sound, suggesting some common surprise computation.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: EEG temporal/spectral characterisation of pain predictive coding. Shows alpha-to-beta activity reflects expectation, and gamma activity is negatively modulated by prediction errors. The finding that pain PE inverts the typical sensory-cortex gamma-PE signature (which normally increases with PE) suggests pain uses a distinct computational dialect even within predictive coding. Useful but not architecturally decisive -- it says 'pain PC uses different oscillatory code' rather than 'pain has N forward models'.
failure_signatures: If pain forward prediction used the same oscillatory code as visual/auditory PC, these data would show positive gamma PE modulation; they show the opposite.
Does not falsify either the shared-substrate or parallel-substrate architecture directly.

SD-032c.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=3 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.768

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical review establishing AIC as the re-representation locus of interoceptive state, with direct autonomic and affective efferents. Provides the biological grounding for SD-032c's claim that AIC integrates z_harm_a with interoceptive baseline (drive_level). Mapping fidelity is moderate: Craig's framework focuses on awareness and subjective feeling, not on the urgency-interrupt / mode-switch function specifically; that extension requires Menon & Uddin 2010.
failure_signatures: If AIC activity is primarily a readout of body state (awareness) rather than a trigger for mode changes, SD-032c's urgency-interrupt role is ungrounded.
If interoceptive salience in AIC does not integrate with harm signals (z_harm_a) but with a separate pain-specific pathway, the proposed convergence mechanism needs revision.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Provides direct optogenetic causal evidence that aIC → mPFC pathway signals incorrect trial outcomes, elevates mPFC updating on subsequent trials, and restores adaptive mode-switching in stressed animals. This is the closest available empirical paper to the SD-032c urgency-interrupt hypothesis: aIC detects salient negative events and fires a control signal to prefrontal cortex that triggers behavioral mode revision. Confidence moderated by preprint status and the fact the study addresses cognitive set-shifting rather than harm-salience urgency per se.
failure_signatures: If aIC signals all outcome valences (not specifically salient negative events), its role is general prediction-error reporting rather than urgency interrupt.
If the pathway effect is on working memory updating rather than network mode switching, SD-032c may need to be reframed as a PFC-update signal rather than a mode-switch trigger.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Directly provides the network-level model that SD-032c instantiates: AIC as integral hub performing (1) bottom-up detection of salient events, (2) switching between large-scale networks (task-positive vs default-mode) when a salient event is detected, (3) strong coupling with ACC for rapid motor system access. This maps precisely onto SD-032c's urgency-interrupt specification: detect z_harm_a salience > threshold, fire switch trigger to SD-032a salience coordinator. Mapping fidelity is high for the mode-switch function; transfer risk is the network vs module abstraction gap.
failure_signatures: If AIC's mode-switching function is mediated by a distributed network property (not by a locally-computed salience threshold), SD-032c's AICAnalog as a local threshold module is architecturally wrong.
If the switch is always active (continuous modulation) rather than threshold-gated (urgency interrupt), the event-driven architecture of SD-032c is incorrect.

SD-032d.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=4 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.832

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Mixed evidence because the paper's finding refines rather than cleanly supports the straightforward picture of PCC as a mind-wandering biomarker. Short attentional lapses (mean 1.7 s) during a continuous task did NOT show the expected PCC/DMN activity increase; instead they showed increased dACC/SMA activity consistent with a recovery-of-responsiveness process, and decoupling of external attention networks. Important for SD-032d because it argues the PCC-stability / mind-wandering linkage is more specific than the coarse 'PCC rises when attention lapses' reading would suggest. Confidence moderate: small n (17 subjects with enough lapses), novel finding requiring replication.
failure_signatures: If a ree-v3 PCC-analog is simply a 'mind-wandering detector' that rises during any attentional lapse, the Zaky 2024 finding predicts this will mistakenly flag mind-blanks as mind-wandering. SD-032d's stability scalar is tied to task-success EMA and offline-recency, not to a raw lapse signal -- which may be the correct architectural choice, but needs the distinction made explicit.

If V3-EXQ-447 produces pcc_stability behaviour that does not distinguish sustained inattention from brief mind-blanks, the architecture under-specifies the functional distinction Zaky 2024 establishes. A future refinement might add a 'lapse type' classifier or a faster-timescale component to PCCAnalog.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Multivariate fMRI evidence that PCC contains separable-but-overlapping subregions whose connectivity profiles each echo a different large-scale brain network (DMN, frontoparietal control, attention). Supports SD-032d's framing of PCC-analog as a posterior hub whose computational signature is integration-across-networks rather than performing any single within-network function. Confidence moderate-to-high: the finding is robust but the REE mapping onto a single stability scalar compresses the multi-network heterogeneity the paper is explicitly highlighting.
failure_signatures: A PCC-analog implementation that reads only one input network (e.g. only offline-recency or only fatigue) contradicts Leech 2012's finding that PCC subregions echo multiple distinct networks. pcc_stability in PCCAnalog currently folds success EMA + drive_level + offline-recency into one scalar; if V3-EXQ-447 shows that ablating any one of these eliminates the stability signal, the architecture is too brittle and closer to a single-network read than to Leech's multi-network hub.

Conversely, if the paper's hub framing is correct, a PCC-analog that is purely a passive readout of other substrates (no integrative computation) would fail the Leech 2012 prediction -- PCC subregions show characteristic combined signatures, not simple averages of their inputs.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Direct fMRI dual-regression evidence that PCC fractionates into ventral (DMN-integrated, deactivates with task demand) and dorsal (increases anticorrelation with cognitive control network as task load rises) subregions. This is exactly the architectural distinction SD-032d presumes -- a PCC-analog whose business is not itself performing cognitive control, but modulating the balance between internal-directed and external-directed attention. Moderate-to-high confidence: the ventral/dorsal dissociation is robustly replicated, but the specific mapping to a scalar stability parameter in [0, 1] is a computational simplification the paper does not make.
failure_signatures: A PCC-analog that only represents DMN-like internally-directed cognition (ventral function) and ignores the dorsal task-load-dependent coupling will fail to modulate MECH-259's switch threshold -- because the dorsal signal is precisely what tracks cognitive demand.

If ree-v3's PCC-analog produces a stability scalar that is invariant to task load, it contradicts the Leech 2011 finding that dorsal PCC's integration with control networks is load-dependent. That would indicate pcc_stability is driven by a spurious feature (e.g. only fatigue) rather than the full set of SD-032d inputs.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Single-unit recordings in macaque PCC (CGp) showing firing rates are suppressed during task engagement and elevated during inattention, with elevated firing predicting errors and slow responses. This is the primate electrophysiology counterpart to the human fMRI DMN deactivation finding. Directly supports SD-032d's role: PCC-analog arithmetic should reflect the internal-external attention balance. High confidence because the electrophysiology grounds the fMRI inference in single-neuron firing, and the predictive relationship between PCC firing and upcoming errors is strong behavioural evidence for a functional coupling to task engagement.

Generalisation depends on structural preservation. If task structure changes, vmPFC representations do NOT preserve their similarity geometry. This means the 'rich' content vmPFC carries is structure-specific, not modality-general -- one structure produces one geometry, a different structure produces a different geometry. Mapping z_goal directly into vmPFC would force vmPFC to encode many distinct structures simultaneously, which is incompatible with the single-structure-at-a-time finding.

If the bracketing mechanism is specific to the habitual mode, the support generalises only to one of the operating modes SD-034 needs to handle, and the planned-mode closure mechanism remains unspecified.

Optogenetic disruption of IL activity prevents habit *formation*, not necessarily habit *closure / release*. The closure-as-release function is one ARC removed from what was tested.

Direct and indirect pathways are concomitantly active at sequence initiation but diverge during execution -- a two-pathway structure REE collapses into a single commitment-gated routing variable. The duration of the sustained signal is set by execution/behavioural state, not by a standalone timer.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Directly anchors the OVER-MAINTENANCE psychiatric pole of the BG-3 column: catatonia (stupor, rigidity, stereotypies) framed as impaired inhibitory control / over-engagement of the basal-ganglia INDIRECT (No-Go) pathway via reduced GABAergic tone and D2 dysfunction. failure_signatures: Catatonia's clinical picture is multi-determined (GABA, D2, glutamate, serotonin, ACh) and treatment-responsive to benzodiazepines; reducing it to 'the commitment latch failed to release' is a deliberate simplification that omits most of the syndrome's neurochemistry.

The review is a narrative synthesis, single author, lower-tier venue -- it proposes a unifying indirect-pathway framework rather than demonstrating it; it grounds the DIRECTION of the over-maintenance pole, not a quantitative duration law.

The reversal window in the paper is short and evidence-bounded; a REE latch whose release is set by a tuned refractory parameter (not by an evidence/processing deadline) can over- or under-shoot this window with no biological constraint pinning the duration.

Directly diagnostic for the 603g failure shape and the most decision-relevant entry in this review. It establishes that signaled active avoidance is a TWO-component problem -- Pavlovian freezing reactions and instrumental avoidance actions are mutually exclusive competing responses -- and that learning to avoid REQUIRES infralimbic prefrontal cortex to inhibit central-amygdala-driven freezing. Marked MIXED (not supports): it supports wiring the amygdala as an avoidance-learning driver, but it simultaneously shows the current REE substrate (SD-035 salience + MECH-279 freeze gate, with NO prefrontal reaction-suppression / instrumental-competition layer) would reproduce the un-trainable avoidance signature. Confidence 0.78: strong primary causal lesion study with clean statistics, conserved circuit; mixed direction reflects that the most important content is a missing-mechanism warning.
failure_signatures: If the freeze reaction is not actively suppressed, it competes with and blocks instrumental avoidance: ilPFC lesions (removing the suppression) INCREASED conditioned freezing (main effect of lesion F(1,14)=14.78, p=0.002) and decreased avoidance, while CeA lesions (removing the freeze source) reduced freezing and FACILITATED avoidance. A REE substrate with a freeze gate (MECH-279) but no reaction-suppression layer is the ilPFC-lesion condition -- it will freeze instead of learning to avoid (the 603g G_H 0/3 signature).

Avoidance learning is described as recruiting ilPFC to inhibit CeA-mediated defense; if REE's avoidance leg has no homologue for this prefrontal inhibitory gating, the Pavlovian-instrumental conflict ('early trials of AA training are characterized by a conflict between mutually exclusive responses to the CS') is never resolved and the instrumental response never consolidates.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Primary mechanistic study pinning the developmental onset of fear/avoidance learning to a measurable substrate change: long-term synaptic plasticity becomes inducible in the basolateral amygdala only after PN10, gated by maturation of GABAergic inhibition (picrotoxin reverts mature slices to the immature, non-plastic state). This is the substrate-level correlate of the Debiec & Sullivan developmental review, and it directly supports the autopsy claim that the avoidance-learning leg is gated by a substrate property, not by training budget. Confidence 0.70: strong, specific mechanism, but slice electrophysiology in rat pups, and the GABAergic-gating story is one (well-supported) account among several maturational changes.
failure_signatures: If avoidance/fear learning could be induced before the amygdala substrate became plastic, the tight correspondence between learning onset (PN10-12) and the emergence of inducible LTP would be broken -- and the substrate-readiness framing of the 603g failure would lose its clearest mechanistic anchor.

If GABAergic inhibition were irrelevant to gating plasticity, the picrotoxin reversal (mature slices reverting to the immature non-plastic state) would not occur; this would weaken the specific 'inhibitory maturation gates avoidance learning' mechanism that REE could borrow.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical review (Sullivan group) establishing that mammalian hazard-avoidance learning is NOT present at birth but emerges gradually across postnatal development, gated by amygdala maturation (~PN10) and modulated by parental buffering of the HPA/corticosterone axis. This is direct biological grounding for the V3-EXQ-603g autopsy's core reading: the survival/hazard-avoidance LEARNING leg is a developmentally-acquired competency, not a property an agent has at substrate-init. Confidence held at 0.74 (not higher) because the mapping from a developmental sensitive-period switch to an RL curriculum stage is an analogy, not an isomorphism: REE has no homologue of the corticosterone/attachment switch, and the review is rodent-centric.
failure_signatures: If hazard-avoidance learning were available immediately at substrate initialisation (as the 603g Stage-H design implicitly assumed by expecting an isolated stage to train within budget), the strong developmental gating documented here (no amygdala-dependent avoidance learning before PN10; GABAergic/plasticity immaturity) would have no analogue and the developmental-curriculum reading would be unsupported.

If the survival leg's failure to train were purely a budget/episode-count problem rather than a missing developmental scaffold, the review's finding that the SUBSTRATE itself (amygdala plasticity) must first mature before any amount of conditioning produces avoidance would not apply.

Mice toggle dynamically between food seeking and self-preservation as predation threat varies, and increasing caloric need (the override signal) re-engages food seeking under threat through identified AgRP -> BNST and AgRP -> LH circuits. Crucially, predator-responsive PMd-CCK neurons SUPPRESS AgRP activity, not via z_harm-side modulation -- so the threat -> feeding suppression is an active circuit, not just a competing scalar. Confidence high because the architecture maps cleanly onto SD-012/SD-036 and identifies specific output pathways the V3 model can implement.
failure_signatures: Predator threat suppresses AgRP (hunger) activity rather than just competing with it -- suggesting threat-driven hypophagia is an active inhibition, not arbitration loss.
Override of threat by hunger requires increased caloric need; the override signal scales with deprivation, supporting graded rather than threshold drive amplification.
AgRP -> BNST and AgRP -> LH are distinct output channels for threat-overriding food seeking; suggests at least two-target broadcast rather than single output.

Direction is MIXED because PWS supports SD-037's predicted SATURATED-OVERRIDE phenotype at the behavioural level (compulsive drive pursuit despite negative consequences) but the mechanistic story is genetic/upstream of orexin (paternal 15q11-q13 imprinting defect, hypothalamic dysfunction broader than orexin alone).
