recent_entries.confidence_rationale: PASS with supporting direction

The strongest and most decision-relevant literature finding for SD-079, and it cuts both ways. It confirms that removing a shared common mode from a set of signals is a decisive, non-cosmetic operation that transforms an inflated all-positive similarity distribution into a differentiated one -- SD-079's central mechanism. But it also establishes ANALYTICALLY, not merely empirically, that after such a removal the similarity values must sum to a negative value and are distributed approximately centred on zero. That makes the specific downstream evidence SD-079 cites for success -- that the MECH-292 goal_match_floor now excludes 9 of 24 anchors and the MECH-339 outshining gate is now nonzero on 9 of 24 -- partly a mathematical consequence of centering rather than a demonstration that those absolute gates now select on motivational relevance. Confidence held at 0.62: source quality is high and the analytic component transfers exactly, but the empirical apparatus (BOLD, seed-voxel correlation, breath-holding) is far from a hippocampal anchor pool, so transfer risk is substantial.
failure_signatures: After subtraction of a common mode, the similarity values to a given reference must sum to a negative value, and the empirical distribution of those values becomes bell-shaped and centred on zero. Any ABSOLUTE threshold applied downstream of centering therefore partitions the pool at a location largely determined by the centering operation itself, not by the content of the cue -- so 'the gate is now live' and 'the gate is now meaningful' are different claims, and only the first is demonstrated by an exclusion count.

Negative similarity values produced by centering can be spurious: the paper shows in simulation that small phase differences between signals are sufficient to produce negative correlations after global regression, and concludes that global signal regression is most likely the cause of the anti-correlated networks previously interpreted as intrinsic brain organisation. The analogous REE risk is that centered goal_match values below zero are read as active dissimilarity between a goal and an anchor when they encode nothing of the sort.

The interpretation of any structure discovered only after common-mode removal is called into question by this paper's central argument. A REE result of the form 'the centered arm shows differentiation that the raw arm does not' is necessary but not sufficient; it needs a check that the differentiation tracks something independently identifiable, not merely that it exists.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Supports SD-079's premise on strong empirical footing -- across three independent datasets plus 47 task contrasts from the Human Connectome Project, removing a shared widespread component demonstrably improves anatomical specificity and reduces spurious structure. But the paper's central result is that a SINGLE global mean estimate captures only one kind of widespread coherent structure, and that an iterative cluster-based estimator (DiCER) removes more of it and better preserves genuine task-related structure. SD-079 uses a single scalar-alpha EMA mean vector, which is the class of estimator this paper finds incomplete. Confidence 0.55 because mapping fidelity is the weakest of the four entries in this pull: the evidence is about the sufficiency of an estimator in a spatiotemporal imaging pipeline, and the argument that it generalises to an online latent baseline is structural rather than demonstrated.
failure_signatures: A single global-mean estimate is only effective against specific kinds of widespread coherent structure. The paper reordered carpet plots to expose cluster structure and found a greater diversity of widespread signal deflections than previously recognised, varying across time and across participants, of which global signal regression removes only some -- so 'the common mode has been subtracted' does not entail 'the common mode has been removed'.

Removal of a shared component can distort between-group comparisons of the resulting connectivity measures. The REE analogue is arm-vs-arm comparison: an ON arm and an OFF arm differing in whether centering is applied are not merely differing in one term, since centering alters the distribution of every downstream match, and a between-arm delta can therefore reflect the estimator rather than the mechanism under test.

The common mode is not necessarily stationary in form. The paper reports that the precise form of widespread deflections varies across time and participants, so an estimator tuned on one regime can under-remove in another -- the direct analogue of SD-079's own finding that alpha 0.02 lags a drifting z_goal (spread 0.0942 / 0.1508 / 0.3319 across seeds 101/202/303) while 0.05 tracks it.

SD-080.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=3 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.797

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Directly on point for the ISOLABILITY of the action-side deficit: the paper ablates state embeddings and action embeddings separately and reports that 'action embeddings alone improve the sample efficiency and peak performance of model-free RL on control from low-dimensional states'. That is the precise counterfactual SD-080 needs, because the spike's control showed z_world DOES vary and world_forward DOES become state-dependent -- i.e. the REE deficit is action-side-only, exactly the arm this paper isolates. Held below 0.8 because the learning objective is forward prediction over action SEQUENCES in continuous control, whereas REE's O is a per-step, 5-discrete-action space, and the paper's downstream consumer is model-free RL rather than a CEM planner.
failure_signatures: The paper's action embedding is trained by forward prediction -- predicting the resulting state from (state embedding, action-sequence embedding). A representation trained this way is state-conditioned by construction. REE's action_object_head takes z_world as input but, being frozen at initialisation, produces output that is 99.5% a function of the action label alone, so it fails the defining property of a dynamics-aware embedding while retaining its input signature.

The benefit here is measured as sample efficiency and peak performance on continuous control, not as planning quality inside the embedding. If REE reproduces this experiment it must not assume the two transfer: a CEM planner that refits a sampling distribution inside O could in principle be helped or hurt by a learned geometry in ways a policy-gradient learner is not.

The paper's action embeddings are of action SEQUENCES, deliberately, because the informative dynamics structure lives at the multi-step level. REE's action objects are single-step. If the consequence structure that matters is multi-step, then even a fully-trained single-step REE action_object_head would not recover what this paper shows to be useful -- SD-080's fix as currently framed may be necessary but not sufficient.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Included deliberately as the counterweight to the two supporting entries: it is the strongest available demonstration that a randomly initialised, never-trained encoder can be not merely adequate but PREFERABLE for a downstream geometric computation, outperforming ICM and RND on DeepMind Control Suite. It therefore weakens the inference 'frozen and random, therefore useless'. But it does NOT weaken SD-080's actual finding, because RE3's random encoder is a random encoder OF THE INPUT and its output varies with the input, which is what makes the k-NN entropy estimate meaningful -- whereas REE's frozen head has measured r2_explained_by_action_alone = 0.9947, i.e. it discards its state input almost entirely. Confidence is moderate because the entry's value is analytic (it sharpens what SD-080's defect IS) rather than directly evidential about REE.
failure_signatures: RE3 shows that random-projection geometry is preserved well enough for k-NN distance computations, which sharpens SD-080 into a stronger claim than 'the head is random': a random projection of (z_world, a) should have INHERITED some of z_world's variation, yet the spike measured between-state variance of about 6e-05 against a z_world total variance of 0.0031. The collapse is therefore attributable to initialisation scale or architecture, not to randomness as such -- and a fix that only 'connects the gradient' without diagnosing why the state input is being annihilated may not resolve it.

If a frozen random encoder is sufficient for the downstream consumer's purpose, adding a learned one can be pure cost. RE3's authors explicitly motivate the random encoder on compute grounds -- no gradient updates through it. Any REE experiment repairing SD-080 must therefore measure the cost side as well, and must include a frozen-but-non-collapsed control arm, not only frozen-vs-learned.

The property RE3 needs from its encoder is only that distances be approximately preserved. The property SD-004 needs from O is far stronger: that distance MEAN similarity of world-effect, so that actions with the same consequence embed alike. Random projection gives the first and cannot give the second. An REE experiment that validates only distance-preservation in O would pass while leaving the SD-004 specification unmet.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: High mapping fidelity: the paper's learned action-representation space is the same object SD-004 specifies for O -- a low-dimensional action space whose geometry is induced by observed consequences (inverse dynamics over state transitions), with the policy searching IN that space. The paper's central empirical result is precisely the counterfactual SD-080 asserts: agents whose action space carries no learned consequence structure degrade as the action set grows, while the learned-representation agent does not. Confidence is held below 0.85 because the demonstrated gains are for LARGE finite action sets (2^4 to 2^12; thousands of actions in the recommender domains), whereas REE's action_dim is 5 -- the paper does not establish that the deficit bites at that scale, and the SD-080 spike measured the representation, not a performance decrement.
failure_signatures: An action space with no learned consequence structure cannot support inference about the outcome of an untried action from the outcomes of similar tried actions -- the paper's stated mechanism for generalisation. A frozen random action-object head therefore gives the CEM no basis for generalising across the action-object neighbourhood it searches.

The paper's baselines (actor-critic, DPG) degrade monotonically as the action set grows from 2^4 to 2^12 while the learned-representation agent holds performance. This predicts that the SD-080 defect is scale-dependent and may be near-invisible at REE's action_dim = 5, so a null result in a small-action-space REE experiment would NOT license concluding the frozen head is harmless.

The representation is learned by supervised inverse dynamics, NOT by the policy-gradient signal. This means the deficit cannot be repaired merely by letting the existing REE training paths reach the head: the training paths that currently miss it are reward/prediction paths, and the paper's own argument is that a supervised-transition objective is what makes the representation low-variance and learnable.

SD-082.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=8 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.832

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the closest available engineering precedent for SD-082(i), and the match is close enough to be structural rather than analogical. The dueling architecture computes a per-action head output and then subtracts the mean of that head across the action set -- 'Q(s,a) = V(s) + (A(s,a) - (1/|A|) sum_{a'} A(s,a'))' -- for two stated reasons that map one-to-one onto SD-082's two problems. First, IDENTIFIABILITY: the naive sum is 'unidentifiable in the sense that given Q we cannot recover V and A uniquely', because a constant can be added to one stream and subtracted from the other with no change in output. That is precisely the SD-082 pathology in reverse -- a shared additive component across the candidate set that the output cannot distinguish from zero, so gradient never resolves it. Second, OPTIMISATION STABILITY: the mean form is preferred over the max form because 'the advantages only need to change as fast as the mean, instead of having to compensate any change to the optimal action's advantage'. So mean-subtraction across a candidate/action set is not a REE invention or a hack around SD-008; it is an established, empirically validated primitive whose adoption was justified by the same reasoning SD-082 gives. Confidence high on source quality (ICML 2016 Best Paper, large-scale empirical validation across the Atari suite, and the mean-aggregation choice is specifically credited in the paper's own ablation reasoning) and high on mapping fidelity for component (i). Held below 0.85 because the paper says nothing about component (ii) -- it has no bounded output and no saturation problem -- and because dueling's shared component is an unidentifiable degree of freedom in the OUTPUT parameterisation, whereas SD-082's is a dominant structure in the INPUT.
failure_signatures: The dueling mean-subtraction is applied to the head's OUTPUT (the advantage stream), whereas SD-082(i) applies it to the head's INPUT (the candidate world summaries, before rule_bias_head). These are not equivalent. Subtracting the input mean is a linear reparameterisation only for the linear part of the head; the SD-033a head is a nonlinear MLP, so centering the input changes which region of the nonlinearity each candidate lands in -- a change dueling's argument does not cover and cannot underwrite. If the head's first-layer nonlinearity is where the differentiation is actually being lost, input-centering may shift rather than solve the problem.

Dueling networks subtract the mean to fix an identifiability problem that exists REGARDLESS of the input geometry -- it is a property of the V + A parameterisation. SD-082's common mode is a contingent property of a specific broken encoder (SD-008). The dueling precedent therefore does NOT license SD-082 as a permanent architectural commitment; it licenses it as a read-out-stage mitigation. If SD-008 / SD-070 are ever repaired at the encoder, the dueling analogy gives no reason to keep the centering, and it should be re-ablated rather than inherited.

The paper's stability argument is about the relative rate at which advantages must change, in a value-based off-policy setting with a replay buffer and target network. SD-082's head trains under on-policy REINFORCE in a short P1 window (70 episodes was already shown insufficient at the clamp). Neither the stability claim nor the sample-efficiency gains transfer to that regime, so nothing here predicts that centering alone makes the head trainable in the budget available -- it predicts only that the shared-component degeneracy is removed.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the only source found that empirically compares the three bounding strategies SD-082 is choosing among, and it splits cleanly: it CONFIRMS SD-082's diagnosis and CONTRADICTS SD-082's chosen remedy. Confirms: their 'zeroing gradients' condition -- zero the gradient for any parameter already at its limit -- is functionally the clamp's flat region, and it failed, with 'Unstable learning ... in one of the two zeroing gradient agents' and the remaining stable agent showing 'clear results of not learning'. That is an independent replication of the V3-EXQ-822 null (70 episodes of REINFORCE moving nothing at the clamp), from a different algorithm, task and codebase. Contradicts: their 'squashing gradients' condition IS SD-082(ii) -- 'A squashing function such as the hyperbolic tangent (tanh) is used to bound the activation of each parameter' -- and it ALSO failed: 'parameters stayed within their bounds, but squashing functions quickly became saturated', and 'The resulting agents take the same discrete action with the same maximum/minimum parameters each timestep.' That end-state -- every output pinned at the same rail, no differentiation -- is the exact pathology SD-082 exists to remove, recurring under SD-082's own fix. Only their third option, inverting gradients (downscale approaching the bound, invert on exceeding it), worked. Confidence 0.74: high source quality and unusually high mapping fidelity for the specific mechanism, discounted because the pressure regime differs in a way that may be decisive (see caveat) and because n=2 agents per condition in a RoboCup domain is thin.
failure_signatures: PRIMARY RISK TO SD-082(ii). Tanh squashing was tried and failed by saturation: 'Given the observed proclivity of the critic's gradients to push parameters towards ever larger/small values, it is no surprise that squashing function quickly become saturated and never recover.' 'Never recover' is the operative phrase -- tanh's gradient is non-zero everywhere but decays exponentially, so sustained one-directional pressure produces a soft-saturated state that is practically as dead as a clamp and, unlike a clamp, gives no diagnostic signal that it has happened. SD-082's readout_init_scale (0.25) addresses only the INITIAL operating point; it does nothing to prevent drift into saturation over a training window. V3-EXQ-822a could therefore reproduce the 822 null with a non-zero-but-collapsing prop_delta and be misread as a partial success.

The acceptance criterion for V3-EXQ-822a (on_prop_delta_mean >= 0.001 with an ON>OFF contrast) is a WINDOW-MEAN and is blind to this failure mode. A run that starts in tanh's responsive band (as readout_init_scale intends) and saturates partway through P1 will have a healthy early prop_delta and a dead late one, and can clear 0.001 on the mean while ending in exactly the state SD-082 was built to prevent. Recommended instrumentation before or alongside 822a: log the per-tick saturation fraction (share of candidates with |bias_raw| > bias_scale) and the head grad-norm as TIME SERIES over P1, not just window means, and check the trend rather than the average.

Zeroing gradients also failed by OVERFLOW, not only by non-learning: 'parameters still overflow their bounds', hypothesised to arise from 'gradients applied to other parameters pi != p which inadvertently allow parameter p to overflow' (observed a dash power of 120 against a maximum of 100). This is a warning about coupled multi-output heads: bounding one output per-element does not keep the others in range when the head is shared. The SD-033a bias head emits a per-candidate vector from shared parameters, so per-candidate bounding does not guarantee per-candidate control of where each candidate sits relative to the bound.

Only inverting gradients succeeded in this comparison, and SD-082 did not consider it. If 822a shows saturation drift, the literature's actually-successful option is an untried DESIGN ALTERNATIVE for SD-082 (downscale the gradient as bias_raw approaches +/- bias_scale, invert if it exceeds), not a novel invention. Recording it here so that a 822a failure routes to a known alternative rather than to a fresh substrate-design cycle.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the strongest available biological grounding for SD-082's premise -- not for the fix, but for the structure the fix assumes. Kaufman et al. decompose M1/PMd population responses and find robust 'condition-invariant' components whose magnitude and time course are nearly identical regardless of which reach was made, and critically that the largest such component is much larger than any tuned component, i.e. it explains more of the structure in individual-neuron responses than the movement-identity signal does. That is a measured biological instance of exactly the geometry SD-008 describes in z_world and SD-082 must defeat at the read-out: a single large shared vector dominating the population, with the discriminative (condition-dependent) content relegated to a much smaller subspace. The paper further reports the condition-invariant components occupy dimensions ORTHOGONAL to the tuned components, which is the load-bearing detail for SD-082(i): if the common mode is orthogonal to the differentiated residual, subtracting it removes the dominant variance without destroying the discriminative signal -- the precondition for centering being a repair rather than a lossy projection. Confidence is high on source quality (Shenoy/Churchland population-geometry programme, dPCA-based decomposition, primate electrophysiology) and moderate on mapping: the paper is descriptive about a population geometry, not prescriptive about a read-out, and it never tests whether a downstream decoder saturates.
failure_signatures: The orthogonality result is a property of the M1/PMd population under a reaching task, established by dPCA on trial-averaged data. SD-082 assumes the SD-008 z_world common mode is likewise near-orthogonal to the differentiated candidate residual. That has NOT been measured in REE. If the common mode in z_world is instead partially aligned with the candidate-discriminative direction, mean-subtraction removes real signal along with the offset, and prop_delta could come up non-zero while carrying less rule information than the raw path -- a failure invisible to the V3-EXQ-822a acceptance criterion (on_prop_delta_mean >= 0.001), which tests only that propagation is non-vacuous, not that it is faithful.

The paper's condition-invariant signal is functional, not nuisance: its timing predicts most of the trial-by-trial reaction-time variance. So in the biology, the large shared component CARRIES INFORMATION (when to move) rather than being an artefact to discard. SD-082 subtracts the analogous component unconditionally. If any REE quantity of interest is encoded in the across-candidate mean summary -- an overall urgency, salience or commitment level -- centering at the read-out destroys it, and the loss would show up not in prop_delta but in some other downstream behaviour.

Kaufman et al. subtract nothing in a working control loop; the decomposition is an offline analysis of recorded data. The paper therefore provides no evidence that a nervous system implements common-mode subtraction as an online operation at a read-out stage, which is the specific mechanistic assertion SD-082 makes about lateral PFC.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This entry supports SD-082's PRINCIPLE and undercuts its FORM. Support: Louie et al. show that neurons in monkey lateral intraparietal cortex do not encode the absolute value of an option but a relative value 'explicitly dependent on the values of the other available alternatives', including alternatives outside the response field, and that this context-dependence is 'precisely described by divisive normalization'. So the general architectural commitment SD-082 makes -- that a per-candidate quantity feeding choice should be computed relative to the rest of the candidate set rather than absolutely -- is how a real decision circuit works, not a convenience. This matters because SD-082's centering is otherwise open to the objection that it discards information the agent might need. Undercut: the measured cortical operation is DIVISIVE gain control (scale by a denominator summing the alternatives' values), not SUBTRACTIVE mean removal. These have different consequences under exactly the regime SD-082 operates in. Divisive normalization rescales a near-collinear set without changing its poor angular separation, whereas subtraction removes the shared offset and amplifies the residual -- so the paper's mechanism would NOT have repaired the V3-EXQ-822 structural zero, and the paper is therefore evidence for context-relative coding in general and against the claim that SD-082's specific arithmetic is the biologically attested one. Confidence 0.61: strong primate electrophysiology, but the form mismatch is central rather than peripheral to what SD-082 asserts, and the area is LIP rather than lateral PFC.
failure_signatures: FORM MISMATCH, and it is not cosmetic. Divisive normalization scales a set of values by a common denominator; subtractive centering removes a common addend. Under the SD-008 regime these come apart decisively: dividing a set of near-collinear vectors (min cosine 0.963) by a scalar leaves them just as collinear, so a divisive read-out would have reproduced the V3-EXQ-822 structural zero, while subtraction is what rescues it. SD-082 therefore cannot claim divisive normalization as its biological warrant. If SD-082's architecture doc or claims.yaml entry is ever read as 'normalization is canonical in cortex, therefore SD-082 is biologically grounded', that inference is invalid -- the canonical cortical operation is the one that would NOT have worked here.

Louie et al.'s normalization is over the values of concurrently available ALTERNATIVES and is reported in baseline firing rates as well as stimulus-driven activity, i.e. it is a persistent property of the circuit. SD-082's centering is gated on K >= 2 candidates and computed per tick with no memory. A single-candidate tick therefore receives no centering at all, so the read-out's input statistics change discontinuously with candidate-set size. Nothing in this paper (or in SD-082's validation plan) tests whether that discontinuity matters, and a mixed-K episode could show tick-to-tick bias instability that the window-mean prop_delta would average away.

OPEN DISAGREEMENT WITH A SIBLING ENTRY IN THIS SAME DIRECTORY, recorded rather than resolved. The earlier entry 2026-07-29_sd_082_divisive_normalization_canonical_carandini2012 (landed REE_assembly e41e28d6f3) reads normalization as supporting BOTH SD-082 components at once, on the ground that normalization 'discounts the pooled common drive AND bounds the response smoothly'. This entry argues the discounting half does not transfer, because divisive scaling of a near-collinear set does not improve its angular separation. Both are partly right and the reconciliation is a real refinement: divisive normalization DOES fix the SATURATION half (dividing by a denominator that pools the alternatives pulls an over-driven set back into dynamic range, which is exactly the clamp-rail problem) but does NOT improve the SIGNAL-TO-COMMON-MODE RATIO (for summaries x_i = c + delta_i with c >> delta, division returns (c + delta_i)/(sigma + Kc), preserving the small relative differences instead of exposing them). Subtraction addresses both halves; division addresses one. So SD-082(i)'s subtractive choice is better-motivated than the Carandini entry implies and better-motivated than pure form-mismatch would suggest -- but the biological attestation covers only the weaker operation. Governance should not treat either sibling entry as settling this; the discriminating measurement is REE-side (the angle between the common mode and the candidate-discriminative direction), not literature-side.

The paper's headline behavioural consequence of normalization is IRRATIONALITY -- context-dependent violations of rational choice, where the presence of a third option changes the preference between two others. If SD-082's centering imports the same context-dependence into the candidate bias, then the bias becomes a function of which other candidates happen to be in the set on that tick. That is arguably correct as biology and is a hazard for any REE claim that treats the bias as a stable per-candidate property. It should be checked before SD-082's centering is inherited by consumers beyond the SD-078 path.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Included for the subject-level grounding SD-082's architecture doc explicitly rests on -- 'corticostriatal rule-to-action mapping: a selected rule/context representation must gate a motor bias for the selection to have behavioural consequence; selection without a trained read-out to action is inert.' Muhammad et al. recorded across four connected areas while monkeys applied abstract 'same'/'different' rules to a hold-or-release response, and found rule information and response information co-represented in lateral PFC, premotor cortex and dorsal striatum, with negligible rule coding in inferior temporal cortex. That is direct primate evidence that abstract rule signals reach the structures that select actions rather than remaining confined to a rule-representing area -- the premise that makes SD-082's read-out a necessary component rather than an optional one, and that makes V3-EXQ-822's structural zero a genuine architectural defect rather than an acceptable design. But the paper also complicates SD-082's assumed direction of flow, and that is why the direction is mixed rather than supports: rules and behavioural responses 'were reflected most strongly and, on average, tended to be earlier in the PMC followed by the PFC and then the STR'. Premotor cortex leading prefrontal cortex is the opposite of the serial PFC-computes-rule-then-biases-action architecture that SD-082's data flow diagram encodes. Confidence 0.58: solid primate electrophysiology at the level of area-wise information content, but it evidences the EXISTENCE and DISTRIBUTION of a rule-to-action pathway, not the FORM of any read-out, and it says nothing at all about common-mode geometry or output bounds -- the two things SD-082 actually changes.
failure_signatures: DIRECTIONALITY. Rule and response signals appeared earliest and most strongly in PREMOTOR cortex, then PFC, then striatum. SD-082's data-flow diagram is strictly serial and prefrontal-first: CandidateRuleField -> rule_state -> LateralPFCAnalog.compute_bias -> E3 per-candidate score_bias. If the biology is closer to concurrent or premotor-led rule/action coding, then SD-082 correctly identifies that a read-out must exist while getting its architectural placement wrong, and no amount of tuning at the LateralPFCAnalog read-out would reproduce the biological computation. This is not a defect that V3-EXQ-822a can detect -- 822a tests whether propagation is non-vacuous, which a wrongly-placed-but-functional read-out would pass.

The paper resolves rule and response coding at the level of area-wise information content and latency, with no measurement of the geometry of the population code and no test of how a downstream area reads it. It therefore cannot discriminate between ANY of the candidate read-out mechanisms SD-082 chose among -- raw versus centered input, hard clamp versus scaled tanh are all equally consistent with these data. Citing it as support for SD-082's mechanism (as opposed to SD-082's necessity) would be an overreach.

The task uses two abstract rules ('same'/'different') and a binary hold-or-release response, so the candidate set has cardinality two and there is no meaningful 'across-candidate mean' to speak of. SD-082's centering is gated on K >= 2 and its benefit is expected to grow with candidate-set size (V3-EXQ-822 had max_live 16 rules). This paradigm is at the extreme low end of that range and provides no evidence about the many-similar-alternatives regime that is precisely where the common-mode pathology bites.

Rule coding was negligible in inferior temporal cortex while perceptual identity information was strongest and earliest there -- a clean dissociation showing the rule pathway is selective, not a broadcast. If REE's rule_state is read by consumers that should NOT see it, this paper is a reason to check that selectivity; SD-082 adds a consumer without any stated gating on which downstream structures may read the rule signal.

SD-087.confidence_rationale: exp=1 entry(s), lit=4 entry(s), exp_conf=0.253, lit_conf=0.816

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: FAIL with weakening direction

Strong, well-replicated ICLR result with a mechanistic (Fisher-Information) account, and it is the single closest published analogue to the branch-(a) hypothesis in SD-087's evidence_quality_note: that a training signal must be present from the START of training, because the early transient fixes effective connectivity that later training cannot redistribute. Held below 0.8 because the substrate is supervised vision CNNs rather than an RL harm-value regression head, and because the paper's own dissociation (only deficits that perturb LOW-LEVEL statistics are irreversible) is a criterion REE has not yet evaluated for the harm_surprise_pe target.
failure_signatures: Deficits that do not alter low-level input statistics (the paper's vertical-flip control) produce NO lasting impairment and are fully recovered with further training. If the harm_surprise_pe teaching target changes only the regression target for z_harm_a and leaves the encoder's low-level input statistics untouched, this paper does NOT predict irreversibility, and branch (a) does not follow automatically from V3-EXQ-856's negative result.
The critical-period effect is reported to depend on network size; a small harm-stream head may sit outside the regime where information plasticity is lost at all.

Information Plasticity is measured on the Fisher Information Matrix of the weights, which V3-EXQ-856 did not instrument -- so the mechanism this paper proposes is currently unfalsifiable against REE's own run.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative review from the group that established the infant threat-learning sensitive period, and it is the only entry in this pull that speaks to REE's brain-like-construction principle: in biology the aversive teaching signal genuinely does have a developmental ONSET, which is the strongest available naturalistic support for branch (a). But it is scored mixed and held near 0.5 because the same review documents that the switch is GATED AND REVERSIBLE in the juvenile window -- maternal presence can reinstate attachment learning at PN10-15 -- which argues against reading V3-EXQ-856's null as irreversibility. Rodent-infant to artificial-agent transfer is also the largest leap in this pull.
failure_signatures: The infant threat system is not merely 'off then on': between roughly PN10 and PN15 the pup can SWITCH between the attachment and amygdala-dependent threat systems, controlled by maternal presence and stress-hormone levels. A teaching signal that can be gated back and forth within a window is evidence AGAINST strict irreversibility, and therefore against the strongest reading of branch (a).

The developmental onset here is driven by maturation of amygdala circuitry and the end of the stress hyporesponsive period -- an exogenous biological clock. An artificial agent has no such clock, so 'the signal must arrive at the right time' may have no REE-side referent at all; the REE analogue would have to be curriculum position, which SD-087's scope_note already flags as an unresolved raw-warmup scope condition.
This is a review of rodent work; it aggregates findings rather than testing the specific proposition that a teaching signal introduced late fails to reshape an already-trained valuation.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Highest source quality in this pull -- Nature, replicated across architectures, optimizers, activation functions, batch norm and dropout, and including an RL (PPO Ant) demonstration. But the mapping to SD-087 is the loosest of the three computational entries: plasticity here is lost over THOUSANDS of sequential tasks, whereas V3-EXQ-856 flipped one flag once inside a single training run. Confidence is therefore set by mapping_fidelity, not by venue.
failure_signatures: Plasticity loss in this paper accrues over a very long horizon (substantial loss by the 2,000th Continual ImageNet task; up to 25% of units dead after 800 Permuted-MNIST tasks). A single mid-run flag flip is a far shorter horizon, so the mechanism may simply not have had time to operate in V3-EXQ-856 -- meaning this paper can explain a null result only if REE's harm head is already deep into a plasticity-degraded regime, which has not been measured.

Loss of plasticity was 'substantially eased by L2-regularization, particularly when combined with weight perturbation'. If REE's substrate already applies weight decay to the harm head, the predicted effect is attenuated and this entry's support for branch (a) weakens correspondingly.

The paper's diagnostic is unit death and loss of representational diversity, not target mis-specification. An agent whose z_harm_a is saturated because it was trained on the wrong target is not obviously the same failure as an agent whose units have died.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Highest mapping_fidelity of the computational entries because the substrate matches: this is deep RL agents trained on a progressively growing replay buffer, which is structurally what REE's agent is. The paper establishes that early experience preferentially shapes the representation and impedes later learning, and -- unusually for a supporting citation -- it supplies a directly portable remedy (periodic partial resets) that can be turned into the next SD-087 experimental arm.
failure_signatures: Primacy bias is defined over the DATA the agent trains on (early, near-random exploration transitions), not over a change in the teaching TARGET. Discarding a value function overfitted to early data is not the same operation as discarding a representation fitted to the wrong harm target, so the remedy may transfer even where the diagnosis does not.

The paper's headline evidence is that resets IMPROVE performance, which is an intervention result; it does not directly measure irreversibility of an un-reset agent. A reader could accept every result here and still hold that V3-EXQ-856's null is explained by branch (b), an encoder or environment defect.

Gains were demonstrated in sample-limited regimes (Atari 100k, DeepMind Control Suite). REE's harm-stream curriculum is not obviously sample-limited in the same way, and the effect size of resets outside that regime is not established here.

SD-091.confidence_rationale: exp=0 entry(s), lit=5 entry(s), exp_conf=0, lit_conf=0.776

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational human claustrum isolation + resting-state functional connectivity study showing extensive connectivity to cognitive-control cortex (ACC, PFC, parietal) and task-onset-specific activation during a conflict task -- directly grounds the 'which pathways are available to open/attenuate' component of SD-091's topology-control axis. Confidence held at moderate because the task-related finding is a transient, onset-locked signal rather than a sustained coalition, which is itself an important caveat for MECH-481's persistence/dissolution timing (Gamma_t).
failure_signatures: Claustrum was significantly activated at task onset during high-conflict conditions but NOT during the remainder of the difficult condition -- an early-transient rather than sustained-recruitment profile, which complicates any assumption that coalition instantiation, once triggered, persists for the duration of the demand.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A clean, preregistered-replicated causal dissociation of confidence from objective accuracy, showing that low subjective confidence -- independent of actual task difficulty -- causally increases information-seeking behaviour. This is strong direct support for SD-091's foundational premise (a metacognitive signal must be able to alter subsequent processing, not merely represent uncertainty). Confidence held at moderate rather than high because the single undifferentiated information-seeking response tested here cannot discriminate between REE's own Arm 2 (parametric-only) and Arm 4 (typed coalition) accounts -- it evidences that SOME control-enactment link exists, not that it takes the graph-valued, typed-coalition form MECH-481 specifically proposes.
failure_signatures: The 'information seeking' behaviour measured is a single, undifferentiated action (sampling more of the same evidence stream) rather than recruitment of a qualitatively different processing system -- exactly the kind of result MECH-481's own falsifier design (Arm 2 vs Arm 4) is built to disambiguate, and this study's single-task, single-response-type design cannot make that discrimination.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Direct human fMRI evidence (n=55) that claustrum activates during periods of increased cognitive demand across four distinct, well-validated cognitive-control paradigms (Stroop, AX-CPT, cued task-switching, Sternberg working memory), coinciding with task-positive cortical network activation -- solid support that the claustrum's involvement generalizes across task TYPES rather than being tied to one narrow paradigm. Confidence is capped at moderate because the paper reports claustrum recruitment scaling with cognitive DEMAND, not evidence that the recruited configuration differs qualitatively by demand TYPE -- a distinction load-bearing for MECH-481 but not addressed here.
failure_signatures: Claustrum activation is reported as occurring 'particularly during times of increased cognitive demand' across all four tasks -- a profile consistent with a generic difficulty/arousal-scaling signal (which would look like Arm 2, parametric-only, in MECH-481's falsifier) and not distinguishable, on this data alone, from a genuinely typed, task-specific coalition signature (Arm 4).

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Directly validates, at the level of formal network control theory, that topology-level flexibility (which functional connectivity patterns a fixed structural network can access) is a real, separately-measurable dimension distinct from static connection strength -- good general support for SD-091's core architectural bifurcation. Marked 'mixed' rather than 'supports' because the mechanism it identifies (distributed boundary controllability of structural hub nodes) is a competing account to MECH-481's specific claustrum-centric, discretely-triggered coalition-instantiation mechanism -- it shows topology-level flexibility can emerge from network structure itself, without necessarily requiring a dedicated instantiation hub or an upstream typed-demand classifier.
failure_signatures: The flexibility this paper measures is a developmental, trait-level property of a region's structural embedding (boundary controllability), correlated with age -- not a task-triggered, on-demand reconfiguration event caused by a metacognitive control signal. If REE's coalition control turns out to look more like this (an emergent property of the substrate's own connectivity structure) than like a discrete gating mechanism, MECH-481's framing of coalition instantiation as something the control plane actively 'requests' and 'assembles' may be over-specified relative to what the brain actually needs.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: This is the source thought's own central citation and the primary published articulation of the 'network instantiation' account -- direct architectural support for SD-091's parameter/topology distinction. Confidence is capped at moderate because the account is explicitly presented as a synthesis with 'testable predictions' rather than a settled mechanism, and it does not itself address the TYPED (demand-specific) recruitment MECH-481 requires -- it proposes one generic instantiation function, not a taxonomy of coalition templates.
failure_signatures: The review itself notes that prior claustrum models (salience detection, multisensory binding, top-down attention, cognitive control) were mutually incompatible and required active reconciliation -- convergence on the network-instantiation account is not yet an established consensus, only the authors' proposed synthesis.

The model specifies that frontal cortex directs claustrum-mediated network instantiation but does not specify a mechanism for how different control DEMAND TYPES would produce qualitatively different instantiated networks, which is the specific gap MECH-481 needs closed.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A foundational, empirically-measured (Tileworld) result directly relevant to the intake's own falsifiability worry (Section 12): whether ordinary intention-reconsideration policies, without any general relational topology, already suffice. It is mixed rather than a clean support/weaken: it argues FOR needing richer machinery specifically under high environmental dynamism, and AGAINST needing any extra machinery under low dynamism, where a single scalar (rate of world change) already predicts agent effectiveness well. Confidence is mid-range because it is a 1991 simplified simulated-world study (Tileworld, single-level planning) with substantial transfer risk to REE's substrate, but the finding itself is a widely-replicated cornerstone of the BDI/agent literature, not a one-off result.
failure_signatures: In the low-dynamism regime (rate of world change gamma <= ~1 in the paper's units), a 'bold' agent that never reconsiders its committed plan achieves the same effectiveness (E close to 1) as any more elaborate reconsideration strategy -- i.e. in a large, non-trivial regime of environments, ordinary hierarchical goal-following with NO reconsideration of structure at all is already optimal, which directly weakens the case that a general relational topology is NEEDED (as opposed to merely helpful) for effective behaviour in general.

The paper's entire manipulation is a single scalar environmental parameter (rate of world change) and a single scalar agent parameter (planning-steps-before-replanning); it has no representation of relation TYPES at all (no requires/enables/conflicts-with), so it cannot be read as evidence FOR the specific typed-topology extension -- only as a baseline showing how much can be explained without positing one.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: A formal, peer-reviewed (ICML) treatment that gives exactly one of the intake's proposed relation types -- 'enables' -- a precise mathematical definition (an affordance restricts the state-action space to where a given intent is achievable) and proves planning-loss bounds from using that restricted structure instead of the full model. Confidence held at 0.62 because it formalizes only ONE relation type in isolation, is a pure ML-theory paper with no neural/biological mapping, and does not address multi-relation-type co-representation or discovery/revision through action.
failure_signatures: The paper defines and analyzes a single affordance/intent relation at a time; it does not construct or analyze a graph with multiple co-present, qualitatively distinct relation types (requires, enables, conflicts-with, etc.) over the same state-action space, so it cannot speak to whether such a multi-relation structure is tractable or useful the way a single-relation affordance model is shown to be.

Affordances in this paper are given or learned from a fixed data distribution and then used to restrict planning; the paper does not model an agent discovering a NEW affordance/relation mid-episode as a side effect of pursuing an unrelated goal, which is the 'discovery through action' mechanism central to the intake's Section 8 formulation.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Not a defensive-behavior or orienting study -- included as a deliberate CONTRAST anchor for what a genuinely sub-theta-cycle (Option C) persistence window looks like in real decision-making data, so its own commitment-reversal window (a few hundred ms) can be checked against the multi-second defensive-freezing entries elsewhere in this directory. Direction coded mixed because it neither directly supports nor weakens SD-099 -- it calibrates what fast-decision-commitment timescales actually look like, and the answer sharpens the contrast rather than closing it.
failure_signatures: This paradigm shows that when a biological decision-making system genuinely operates on a sub-second commitment window, that window is reported in the low hundreds of milliseconds (a few hundred ms), not the 60-125ms range Option C proposes -- so even the fastest well-characterized human decision-commitment literature does not land inside Option C's own range, a further data point against reading Option C's magnitude as biologically typical.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Directly quantitative, well-powered (n=58 mice, 44+14 by response type) primary measurement of exactly the transition this claim's persistence window concerns -- the fast defensive-orienting/escape response and the duration of the ensuing defensive state before the animal is free to resume normal behavior. Held below 0.8 because the paradigm measures freezing-state duration, not a specifically DECISIONAL (approach vs withdraw) bias, and is rodent/innate-defense rather than a graded valence-gated choice.
failure_signatures: A design that assumes the post-orienting defensive bias clears within ~100ms (Option C, less than one theta cycle) is contradicted by two orders of magnitude by this paradigm's measured freezing-state duration (21-28s).

Escape ITSELF is fast (154ms latency, <1s duration) -- if SD-099's window were meant to model the ballistic motor act rather than the ensuing defensive STATE, sub-100ms would be defensible; conflating the two is the likely source of an under-estimate.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Standard, well-cited review of the Sokolov-lineage human psychophysiological orienting response literature, giving the classical multi-second time course of the ORIENTING EPISODE itself (Q1b's cross-check quantity) rather than the post-decision persistence question (Q1) directly. Confidence held at moderate because it is a review synthesizing others' data rather than a primary quantitative source, and because it characterizes autonomic/attentional orienting components, not a behavioral action-selection bias.
failure_signatures: If SD-099's post-orienting bias window were meant to be much SHORTER than the orienting episode it follows, that would be a novel and unsupported claim -- every human psychophysiological component of the orienting response reviewed here (cardiac deceleration, electrodermal response, late positive potential) unfolds and resolves on a multi-second timescale, not a sub-200ms one.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Triangulates the Shang 2018 seconds-scale finding with a second, independent, graded-threat paradigm (freezing duration scales with looming urgency, 630ms to 7.9s) and adds a distinct spatial-persistence measure (4.6s), but the direction is coded mixed because the paper's central finding -- that defensive behavior is state-dependent/re-entrant on shelter availability, updating within 1-2 trials -- argues against 'fixed duration' as the right primitive at all (bears on Q2, not just Q1).
failure_signatures: The fastest measured freezing-state duration in this paper (629.9 +/- 100.0 ms, rapid-looming/shelter-closed condition) still lands almost exactly at Option A's own lower bound (625ms), not inside Option C's 60-125ms range -- a second independent triangulation point against the sub-theta-cycle reading.

Defensive strategy (freeze vs. flee) reversed COMPLETELY within a single subsequent trial once the shelter route was reopened -- a fixed-duration bias window is a worse model of this system than an evidence/state-gated one; a rigid tick-count may be the wrong primitive regardless of which magnitude is chosen.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Not one of the three papers the source thought cited -- surfaced via the broader search this pull was instructed to run for the convergent 'shared dynamical motifs / task-independent computational primitives' pattern. Directly relevant because its two-system architecture (a 'what' system that identifies which computation is needed, a 'how' system, a low-rank RNN, that executes it) is structurally the closest thing found in this search to MECH-503's proposed role-selection-then-binding split, evaluated with a real functional benefit (continual learning without catastrophic forgetting, forward/backward transfer, rapid generalization to novel tasks). Confidence held at 0.55, well below the three named papers, because it is an unreviewed arXiv preprint (posted 2025-10-23) with no biological validation at all -- pure computational demonstration that the split is USEFUL when engineered in, not evidence that brains (or REE's eventual substrate) are organized this way.
failure_signatures: Preprint status: no peer review, no independent replication found in this pull, and no biological grounding whatsoever -- this is engineering evidence that a what/how split is a good design choice for continual learning, not evidence that it is how any biological or REE-relevant system actually solves the problem.

The paper's 'what' system explicitly builds a vocabulary of task components via unsupervised structure discovery across many training episodes; it is not shown to perform MECH-503's harder single-shot or few-shot role selection under a typed demand classification, so the transfer to MECH-481's already-typed ControlDemandType setting is not directly tested.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Included specifically to answer this pull's instruction to check whether reusable-computational-motif findings are a convergent pattern across independent lines of work, not a single-paper result. This paper finds cross-task and cross-model reusable 'algorithmic primitive' vectors in large language model reasoning traces (Traveling Salesperson, 3SAT, AIME math, graph navigation), which is the same qualitative phenomenon (SD-101's role/content separability) surfacing in a THIRD, structurally unrelated substrate (transformer-based LLM latent reasoning) beyond the two already covered by the three named papers (rodent/primate cortex, vanilla RNNs). Confidence held low-moderate: unreviewed preprint, and the domain (symbolic multi-step reasoning in LLMs) is a much larger transfer-risk jump to REE's proposed embodied control-plane binding mechanism than any other entry in this pull.
failure_signatures: Unreviewed arXiv preprint (posted 2025-10-23 per its arXiv ID), no peer review or independent replication identified in this pull.

The 'primitives' are derived via function-vector methods from clustering internal activations post hoc, on four abstract symbolic-reasoning benchmarks (TSP, 3SAT, AIME, graph navigation) -- a domain with essentially no structural resemblance to REE's proposed control-plane role/content binding for embodied cognitive operations (maintain, compare, accumulate, retrieve, etc. over agent state), so any transfer of this finding to REE is a very loose analogy at the level of 'reusable structure exists in transformer latents,' not a claim about the same mechanism.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Direct primate neurophysiology (monkeys switching between three compositionally related tasks) with a design purpose-built to test compositional reuse of neural subspaces, verified via the full verbatim abstract from Princeton's institutional repository. Confidence set moderately high because the finding directly supports SD-101's coalition/binding distinction at the representational level (shared sensory and motor subspaces, task-specifically engaged) and adds a mechanism the source three papers together only partially cover: an explicit account of how the animal SELECTS which shared subspace to engage (iteratively updating an internal belief about the current task), which maps onto MECH-503's proposed 'select reusable motif' step more directly than either other paper. Held below 0.8 because -- based on available abstract/secondary-source text -- the paper does not report a direct causal (lesion/microstimulation) test of subspace-selectivity, and the three tasks were 'compositionally related' by design rather than testing recombination onto a genuinely novel, untrained task (MECH-503's stronger Test C).
failure_signatures: The three tasks monkeys switch between were explicitly designed by the experimenters to be compositionally related (sharing sensory and motor subspaces by construction), which is well-suited to demonstrating that shared subspaces CAN be reused across related tasks but does not test the harder claim MECH-503's Test C requires -- rapid transfer to a task that was never trained on at all, recombining motifs in a genuinely novel configuration.

No causal perturbation (lesion, microstimulation, or optogenetic) evidence was identified in the available abstract/secondary sources confirming that disrupting a shared subspace produces the task-specific behavioral deficit the correlational subspace-engagement finding would predict; the evidence assembled here is representational/correlational (population geometry, engagement patterns tied to belief updating), not causal.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: Purely computational (artificial recurrent networks trained on ~20 related tasks), which removes biological-transfer risk but also means it speaks only to what is DYNAMICALLY POSSIBLE and learnable, not what the brain (or REE's eventual substrate) actually does. Confidence set relatively high within that scope because the paper directly demonstrates all three components MECH-503 needs to be plausible: (1) reusable dynamical motifs (attractors, decision boundaries, rotations) recur across tasks, (2) lesioning the units implementing a motif produces a computation-specific (not global) deficit, and (3) motifs are recombined/reconfigured to support fast transfer learning on tasks not seen in the original training set -- the closest available proxy for MECH-503's Test C (recombination on a genuinely novel task).
failure_signatures: The reused motifs are discovered post hoc via dynamical-systems analysis of a network that was NOT explicitly architected with a separate role-selection/content-binding mechanism -- the network learns to share dynamical structure as an emergent consequence of multi-task training, not because an explicit binding layer was built in. This means the paper demonstrates the PHENOMENON MECH-503 wants to exploit but does not test MECH-503's SPECIFIC mechanism (an explicit typed binding step distinct from coalition/topology instantiation) against an alternative architecture lacking it.

Motif discovery requires restricting unit activation functions to be non-negative for the clustering analysis to cleanly recover discrete motif-bearing clusters -- an analysis-enabling constraint on the model, not a claim about biological unit properties, and a caveat on how cleanly 'a motif = a cluster of units' generalizes outside this specific network class.

recent_entries.confidence_rationale: The paper's own abstract directly states the finding the source thought cites: mice reuse specialized neuronal subspaces (prefrontal, parietal) across task phases carrying different bound content, and silencing specific clusters in RNNs constrained to the recorded neural data disrupted specific computations. Verified independently via Semantic Scholar's indexed abstract (not just the source thought's paraphrase) -- the abstract text matches the thought's characterization closely, including the RNN lesion result. Held below 0.75 because the causal claim in mice themselves (as opposed to the RNN model fit to the data) is not yet tested: three independent secondary-source summaries (AZoLifeSciences, MedicalXpress, TechExplorist) each state that optogenetic/inhibition perturbation of the live circuit is explicitly future work, not a result in this paper -- so the strongest causal evidence for 'reusable module' status is currently confined to the data-constrained model, not the animal.
failure_signatures: The causal (silencing) demonstration that a subspace's disruption produces a computation-specific deficit is performed in an artificial RNN constrained to fit the recorded neural data, not via direct perturbation of the mouse circuit itself -- live-animal optogenetic/inhibition testing of the same clusters is explicitly stated (in secondary press coverage of the paper) as planned future work, not a result reported here.

Only two functionally distinct subspaces (stimulus-processing, memory-maintenance) and two regions (mPFC, PPC) are characterized in one task (delayed match-to-sample with delayed report); the paper does not test whether a subspace generalizes to a THIRD, structurally different task or content type, which is the stronger claim SD-101/MECH-503 would need for full generality.

The PBWM model independently motivates a multi-gate BG architecture with functionally distinct input gate (sensorium), maintenance gate (thought loop), and output gate (action commitment), all implemented via the canonical striatum-SNr-thalamus-PFC disinhibition loop. Strong mapping fidelity to Q-019 sensorium and commitment gates; moderate transfer risk as this is a computational model not direct anatomy.

This paper is the clearest statement in the PBWM tradition of parallel BG loops across motor, cognitive, and limbic domains with shared canonical circuit logic — directly motivating anatomically separable sensorium, thought-loop, and action-commitment gates. Affective weighting via amygdala/ventral striatum supports REE hippocampal affective residue mechanism. Strong support for Q-019.

Provides the strongest anatomical evidence for a dedicated BG circuit serving the action commitment gate function. The IFC-STN hyperdirect pathway is anatomically validated (DWI tractography, 7-9/10 subjects) and functionally distinct from the canonical striato-pallidal Go pathway. The key architectural point: the commit gate uses a different BG pathway (STN-based) than the thought-loop gate (SNr-based), supporting anatomical separability.

Beta oscillations as a context-sensitive dynamic gate across BG circuit functions provides direct oscillatory grounding for distinct gate timing. Functional dissociation of beta roles (sensorium admission, cognitive hold, action inhibition) supports separate loop gates. STN hyperdirect stop signal via beta resynchronization maps to action commitment gate. Moderate transfer risk as oscillatory interpretation is contested.

Provides anatomical grounding for the 'thought loop' substrate (default network = internal simulation system), and the functional anticorrelation between default network and externally-directed attentional systems supports the loop separation requirement. However, the paper does not address BG gating mechanisms directly, and the mapping to Q-019's three-gate architecture requires a bridging claim (default network is what the thought loop gate regulates). Indirect support; not a direct BG gating paper.

The TRN push-pull gating mechanism is the most direct biological instantiation of the sensorium gate in the three-gate model. The TRN selects which sensory/thalamic channel gains access to cortical processing — this is precisely the sensorium loop's function. Malsburg synapse / transient assembly concept grounds the thought loop's rapidly reconfigurable binding requirement. Moderate transfer risk from 1984 theory paper (predates modern BG-thalamic understanding and oscillatory frameworks).

Blakemore et al. provide a detailed forward-model account of agency detection: the sense of agency arises from comparing the predicted sensory consequences of a motor command (efference copy via internal forward model) with the actual sensory feedback. When prediction matches outcome, the movement is experienced as self-caused; when they diverge, the cause is attributed externally. The temporoparietal junction (TPJ) is identified as the critical comparator locus. This directly grounds MECH-095: the TPJ-equivalent comparator between efference-copy-predicted z_self change and observed z_self change is the mechanism by which SD-003 counterfactual attribution can cleanly separate self_delta from world_delta.

Goodale & Milner (1992) is the canonical paper establishing the dorsal/ventral visual stream distinction. The dorsal stream (V1→MT→posterior parietal cortex) processes spatial location, egocentric coordinates, and action-relevant information at high temporal resolution. The ventral stream (V1→V4→inferotemporal cortex) processes object identity, allocentric relationships, and sustained perceptual representations. This anatomical distinction directly grounds MECH-096: the observation encoder requires two output heads corresponding to these streams, not a single encoder with a learned routing gate. A learned gate is insufficient because the two streams process structurally different information at different temporal resolutions — collapsing them degrades the z_self/z_world split back toward z_gamma conflation.

Rizzolatti et al. (1997) characterise peripersonal space (PPS) as a dynamically updated near-body region with distinct neural processing in premotor area F4 and parietal area 7b/VIP. PPS neurons respond to stimuli within reaching distance, encode objects in body-part-centered (egocentric) coordinates, and gate motor responses to near-body events. This directly grounds MECH-097: the commit boundary coincides with the PPS boundary, where z_self (body-centered) and z_world (allocentric) first interact. In CausalGridWorld, contamination occurs exactly at this boundary — the agent's foot contacts the cell. PPS is dynamically updated (scales with tool use, motor reach, attentional state), consistent with z_beta modulating commitment thresholds (ARC-016).

Lopez & Blanke provide the comprehensive anatomical and functional account of the thalamocortical vestibular system needed to ground ARC-017's VESTIBULAR stream tag. Key findings: (1) multiple thalamic nuclei relay vestibular signals (ventroposterior complex, ventroanterior-ventrolateral complex, intralaminar, posterior nuclear group) — these contain multisensory neurons integrating vestibular, proprioceptive, and visual signals; (2) the parieto-insular vestibular cortex (PIVC) is the core vestibular cortical region, with additional projections to somatosensory cortex (areas 2v, 3av), intraparietal sulcus, posterior parietal cortex (area 7), MST, frontal cortex, and hippocampus; (3) vestibular signals influence self-motion perception, spatial navigation, internal models of gravity, and bodily self-consciousness. This directly grounds the VESTIBULAR stream as distinct from both SELF_SENSORY/proprioception (joint/muscle state) and WORLD (exteroceptive content), with its own thalamo-cortical relay to parietal and MST areas that inform z_self's spatial frame.

Nath & Beauchamp demonstrate that STS functional connectivity with auditory cortex increases when auditory input is more reliable (less noisy), while connectivity with visual cortex increases when visual input is more reliable — and these changes occur even with rapidly fluctuating reliability. This is the neural correlate of precision-weighted multisensory integration. For MECH-103, this is the key piece: different exteroceptive modalities do not simply sum their contributions to E1's world latent — they contribute with weights proportional to their current reliability. This is exactly the precision-gating mechanism described in MECH-103. The dynamic nature (changes word-by-word) confirms this is an active, online weighting process rather than a fixed architecture.

Venezia et al. demonstrate a functional anterior-posterior gradient within STS: auditory speech produces largest BOLD in anterior STS, visual speech in posterior STS, and audiovisual (multisensory) stimuli in mid-STS. This spatial organisation shows that different exteroceptive modalities are processed via distinct streams that converge at a shared integration zone. The mid-STS preferentially responds to multisensory stimulation and speech over non-speech — consistent with MECH-103's claim that different modalities contribute differently to E1's world latent via their own encoder pathways. The gradient from modality-specific (posterior/anterior) to multimodal (mid) maps onto a multi-pathway encoder architecture converging on a shared latent.

Zhang et al. use direct intracranial sEEG recordings (42 patients, n=42 electrodes in STS/STG) to demonstrate that STS responses to audiovisual speech are 40% faster in latency and 18% larger in amplitude than auditory-only responses. Crucially, a subpopulation concentrated in mid-posterior STS responds to both auditory (71ms latency) and visual (109ms latency) speech — demonstrating that the STS integrates modality-specific inputs that arrive at different times. This directly grounds MECH-103: different exteroceptive modalities contribute to E1's world latent via convergent pathways with different temporal profiles and amplitudes. The precision-weighted fusion aspect (more reliable modality contributes more) is consistent with the STS acting as a reliability-sensitive integrator.

Canonical high-quality review in a premier journal. Directly documents hippocampal-cortical dialogue during NREM SWS as the mechanistic basis of memory consolidation; covers sharp-wave ripple replay, thalamo-cortical sleep spindles, and slow oscillation coordination. Maps cleanly onto MECH-030's core claim that offline consolidation uses hippocampal-cortical replay while suppressing active online processing. Confidence docked slightly because the REE sleep mode is explicitly V4 scope, adding transfer risk.

Seminal synaptic homeostasis hypothesis (SHY) paper; high source quality and wide replication. The core claim -- that waking net potentiates synapses and sleep globally downscales them to restore SNR -- maps directly onto MECH-030's precision recalibration and mode boundary recalibration functions. Confidence docked because SHY is a population-level homeostatic account, not a selectivity account, and REE needs selective residue recalibration (genuine harm preserved), which SHY does not explicitly address. V4 scope gap adds further transfer risk.

This is a theoretical integration paper (Hobson + Friston) casting REM sleep within active inference / predictive coding. Source quality is good -- both authors are prominent -- but the paper is more theoretical synthesis than primary data review, and the predictive coding interpretation of REM is not universally accepted. The key claim (REM as offline precision recalibration that updates the generative model's priors) maps onto MECH-030's mode boundary recalibration function. Confidence docked for theoretical nature of the source, contested status of the REM-predictive-coding account, and V4 scope gap.

Walker & Stickgold is a high-quality Annual Review paper covering sleep and memory consolidation broadly. The mixed direction reflects an important asymmetry: the paper supports the general consolidation function of sleep (alignment with MECH-030's core claim) but also documents failure modes -- maladaptive consolidation and intrusive replay -- that reveal the ARC-020 invariant ('genuine harm must not be erased') is not automatically satisfied by the biological sleep process. PTSD-related evidence shows that offline consolidation can amplify and distort, not just recalibrate, traumatic memory traces. This constitutes a genuine challenge to the REE assumption that sleep mode will reliably enforce the commit boundary and produce constructive recalibration.
failure_signatures: Offline consolidation can strengthen and distort traumatic memories rather than recalibrating them (PTSD model).
REM sleep intrusions during NREM can disrupt the orderly hippocampal-cortical transfer, impairing rather than supporting mode boundary recalibration.
Sleep-dependent consolidation of fear memories may lock in maladaptive action schemas, not just episodic content.
Fragmented sleep (REM disruption) impairs emotional memory processing, suggesting the offline phase is not robust to partial implementation.

entries.confidence_rationale: PASS with supporting direction

Canonical review articulating metastability as the core operating principle of large-scale brain dynamics: the brain transiently dwells in attractor-like states and transitions between them with characteristic dwell-time distributions. Directly supports MECH-047's claim of mode-commitment hysteresis. Mapping from whole-brain attractor dynamics to REE's three cognitive modes is structurally faithful. Main transfer risks are from network-level dynamics to the discrete mode-manager abstraction and from resting-state to task-engaged circuits.

Empirically rigorous task-fMRI paper showing that cognitive transitions are better described as continuous trajectories through a low-dimensional neural manifold than as discrete switches between labelled states. This directly challenges MECH-047's discrete mode-switching architecture and the sharp hysteresis gate. However, the paper also shows that neuromodulator activity (especially LC-NE proxy via pupillometry) predicts position along the manifold, which is partially consistent with MECH-047's arousal-gating component. Net: the continuous manifold finding weakens the discrete-mode assumption; the neuromodulator-position correlation provides partial support for the gating claim.
failure_signatures: cognitive_mode_transitions_are_continuous_not_discrete
no_sharp_switching_boundary_identified

entries.confidence_rationale: Empirical resting-state fMRI study using a hidden Markov model to identify transient brain states and their transition probabilities. The finding of hierarchical temporal organisation -- with fast micro-states nested inside slower macro-states -- directly supports MECH-047's claim that mode transitions are not instantaneous and carry switching costs. The hierarchical structure provides an empirical basis for distinguishing sub-mode fluctuations from genuine mode transitions. Main caveat: resting-state only; task-engaged dynamics and causal role of LC-NE are not directly addressed.

Canonical and highly cited review (>4000 citations) articulating LC-NE's role in adaptive gain modulation and the phasic/tonic LC firing distinction as a neural mechanism for switching between exploit and explore modes. Directly provides the neuromodulatory substrate for MECH-047's LC-NE arousal transition gate. Mapping to REE's mode-switching threshold is tight: phasic LC bursts = transition-enabling events; tonic LC baseline = background switching probability. Main caveat is that Aston-Jones & Cohen frame switching as exploit/explore rather than the three-mode REE taxonomy.

Major review directly addressing the functional role of theta-phase/gamma-amplitude coupling across human cortex, hippocampus, and prefrontal circuits. Provides both the mechanistic account (slow oscillation phase organises fast-oscillation bursts) and the cognitive function (enabling communication across spatial and temporal scales between hierarchically distinct systems). The packaging-for-higher-level-read-out mechanism is explicit and maps cleanly to MECH-089's ThetaBuffer. Slightly higher confidence than Lisman & Jensen (2013) for MECH-089 because this review covers the general cortical case, not just rodent hippocampal spatial coding, reducing species-transfer risk.

Influential review directly articulating the 'status quo' function of beta oscillations across motor and cognitive circuits — specifically distinguishing beta as a signal that maintains current state against change, not merely an idle rhythm. High source quality and conceptual precision; the framing directly maps to MECH-090's committed-sequence gating. Main transfer risk: the review argues beta reflects a top-down maintenance signal but does not directly distinguish internal-update blocking from output-propagation blocking, which is the REE-specific claim.

Foundational paper establishing the ERD/ERS framework and the 'idling rhythm' interpretation of beta: beta synchronizes when a cortical area is not engaged in active processing and desynchronizes during voluntary movement. This challenges MECH-090 in an important way -- if beta is primarily an idling/disengagement rhythm, then elevated beta during a committed sequence would indicate the motor cortex is *not* engaged, which contradicts the committed-maintenance gating account. Confidence 0.55 reflects genuine tension: the evidence against is real but the idling interpretation applies most clearly to sensorimotor beta, while MECH-090 targets prefrontal/BG beta during cognitive commitment -- a distinction subsequent work (Engel & Fries 2010; Helfrich & Knight 2019) explicitly makes.
failure_signatures: beta_as_idle_not_commitment
sensorimotor_beta_desynchronizes_during_action

entries.confidence_rationale: Keysers and Gazzola review strong evidence that the same cortical regions (premotor cortex, SII/parietal operculum, insula) are active both when an agent performs an action, emotion, or sensation AND when observing another perform the same -- i.e. self and other share neural representations. This directly challenges the clean z_self/z_world split: if the neural substrate for self-action and observed-action are overlapping rather than dissociated, strict computational separation of self and world streams is harder to maintain. Evidence is rated mixed rather than weakens because the overlap is partial and consistent with a competitive rather than fused representation, and because the mirror system primarily concerns action observation/understanding, not world-state modelling per se. The paper is high quality (>700 citations) and the phenomenon is robustly replicated.
failure_signatures: shared_self_world_representation
partial_overlap_in_z_self_z_world_substrates

entries.confidence_rationale: Wolpert and Kawato's MOSAIC model provides a well-established computational account of motor control via modular paired forward and inverse models. The forward model explicitly predicts the sensory consequences of self-generated actions without modelling world state. This is the canonical biological basis for a z_self stream (efference copy + forward prediction) that is computationally separable from a z_world stream. The paper is widely cited and the forward-model mechanism has substantial empirical support in cerebellar and parietal cortex. Confidence limited by the gap between motor control specifics and the broader latent-space architecture of SD-005.

Farrer and Frith directly dissociate the neural correlates of self-agency attribution from world-state/other-agency monitoring using fMRI. The anterior insula activates for self-caused actions; the right TPJ/inferior parietal cortex activates for other-caused (external) events. This double dissociation provides direct empirical support for separate neural substrates processing self-attribution (z_self domain) vs external-cause attribution (z_world domain). Well-cited study (>700 citations) in a high-quality empirical neuroscience venue. Confidence limited by the fact that the TPJ finding concerns other-person attribution specifically, not general world-state modelling, requiring an inferential step to z_world.
