entries.confidence_rationale: Directly demonstrates that serotonin gates hippocampal sharp wave ripples (SWRs), the primary neural correlate of offline memory consolidation/replay. When 5-HT is elevated, SWRs are masked; when 5-HT is washed out, SWRs reappear. This is highly consistent with MECH-203's proposal that falling 5-HT during SWS releases replay: low tonic 5-HT is the permissive condition for replay execution. Source quality is good (peer-reviewed empirical, top neuropharmacology journal). Mapping fidelity is good because SWR masking is exactly the mechanism by which benefit-tagged episodes could be sequentially gated for replay. Transfer risk is moderate (rat hippocampal slices in vitro to in vivo sleep states).
failure_signatures: In vitro slice preparation -- does not capture in vivo state dynamics or the ascending dorsal raphe modulation of 5-HT tone

Masking is receptor-mediated (5-HT1A + 5-HT2A/C) but does not address which episodes are preferentially unmasked during low-5-HT windows -- selectivity for benefit-dense experiences is not demonstrated
LTP was still inducible during high 5-HT -- encoding and replay may not be as cleanly separated as MECH-203 assumes

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly demonstrates in vivo that DRN 5-HT population activity is not monotonically low during NREM but oscillates at 0.01-0.05 Hz, with inverse correlation to EEG power fluctuations. This shows that NREM sleep is not a single 5-HT-off state but contains dynamic sub-states with alternating serotonin activity. Relevant to MECH-203 because it suggests the benefit-salience tagging signal (tonic 5-HT) continues to modulate in real-time during NREM, potentially creating windows of differential replay eligibility. Source quality high (Journal of Neuroscience, in vivo fiber photometry). Mapping fidelity moderate -- the oscillatory activity is characterised but its functional role in replay prioritization is not directly tested.
failure_signatures: Optogenetic and SSRI silencing of the 5-HT oscillation did not abolish EEG fluctuations -- serotonin tracks NREM states but does not generate them, weakening a causal role for 5-HT in organizing replay windows
The oscillatory 5-HT pattern during NREM is not shown to correlate with SWR occurrence or replay content
Mouse fiber photometry -- population-level signal, not single-unit; cannot resolve individual neuron subtypes or projection targets

entries.confidence_rationale: The most directly relevant paper found. Demonstrates in vivo that ultraslow 5-HT oscillations (<0.05 Hz) in the hippocampus create a phase relationship with sharp wave ripples: ripples occur preferentially on the falling phase of 5-HT oscillations during NREM, with higher-power ripples clustering near the peak during NREM specifically. This is precisely the mechanism MECH-203 requires -- 5-HT level at the time of consolidation determines replay salience, with falling 5-HT phases permitting and prioritizing higher-power (more content-rich) SWRs. Source quality high (eLife peer-reviewed, in vivo). Mapping fidelity high: the ripple-phase relationship is exactly the gating mechanism MECH-203 predicts.
failure_signatures: Ripple phase-locking to falling 5-HT is demonstrated during NREM and wake -- not specific to NREM only, which weakens the sleep-specific replay consolidation claim

Higher-power ripples cluster near the 5-HT peak (not falling phase) during NREM -- this means the highest-salience replay may occur when 5-HT is still elevated, not at the trough; the direction is partially counterintuitive
Arousal markers (microarousals, EMG peaks) also cluster on the rising phase -- 5-HT oscillations may be tracking arousal substates rather than specifically regulating memory consolidation
The specific episodes that are replayed during falling-5-HT phases (whether benefit-dense vs harm-dense) are not characterised

entries.confidence_rationale: Demonstrates that serotonin release during NREM sleep oscillates at 0.01-0.03 Hz (infraslow) in the dentate gyrus, inversely phase-coupled to DG glutamatergic neuron activity. Genetic ablation of 5-HT1a receptors in dentate granule cells impairs both the oscillation and fear memory recall. This directly links serotonin's NREM modulation to memory consolidation outcomes. Source quality high (eLife, in vivo, genetic manipulation with behavioral readout). Mapping fidelity moderate -- the paper tests fear memory consolidation (harm-valenced), not benefit-relevant replay specifically, requiring inference about generalization.
failure_signatures: Tested specifically in the dentate gyrus, not CA1 where SWRs predominantly occur -- DG infraslow oscillation may be a distinct process from CA1 ripple-dependent replay
Fear memory consolidation (contextual fear conditioning) is harm-valenced, not benefit-valenced -- the transfer to benefit-salience tagging (the core MECH-203 claim) requires generalization
The infraslow oscillation is in opposite phase to 5-HT release -- serotonin inhibits DG activity through 5-HT1a; whether this facilitates or gates downstream CA1 replay is not established
Genetic 5-HT1a ablation is a chronic manipulation -- does not resolve whether acute 5-HT level during waking determines replay priority

entries.confidence_rationale: Proposes that tonic serotonin reflects average punishment rate, which supports the terrain stage (MECH-186) of INV-052. The apparent tension with MECH-187 resolves once cue-triggered incentive salience (wanting on proximate contact) is distinguished from global approach vigour (how actively the organism seeks). Cools modulates vigour -- correct and expected. MECH-187 concerns whether a detected benefit triggers wanting, which is dissociable from vigour in Berridge's framework. The Cools account refines rather than challenges INV-052.
failure_signatures: If MECH-187 is measured only by navigation success or approach frequency, it conflates wanting with vigour and remains ambiguous under Cools predictions.
The vigour/wanting dissociation is assumed not directly tested -- if cue-triggered wanting and global vigour are not separable in the substrate, the Cools challenge to MECH-187 would be real.

entries.confidence_rationale: Explicitly frames tonic serotonin as an opportunity benefit for the passage of time and quiescence signal -- the closest extant literature articulation of the MECH-186 tonic floor concept. The opponency framework explains why 5-HT cannot be replaced by phasic dopamine for sustained benefit orientation. However, the paper's emphasis is on approach/avoidance balance rather than the three-stage terrain/transduction/maintenance dissociation INV-052 requires.
failure_signatures: Serotonin-dopamine relationship exhibits competitive, cooperative, and interactive modes depending on context -- the simple tonic floor metaphor may underspecify the actual regulatory architecture
Tonic 5-HT's role in quiescence and patience may be dissociable from benefit terrain maintenance, creating a potential mapping overextension in INV-052's terrain stage claim

entries.confidence_rationale: Comprehensive review treating serotonin as a unified affective control signal across appetitive and aversive motivated action, with explicit treatment of asymmetries between reward and punishment statistics that explain why a tonic 5-HT floor is needed. The review does not use REE's three-stage language but provides the computational and empirical grounding for exactly that structure.
failure_signatures: Serotonin's role in aversive processing is only a partial mirror of dopamine's role in reward due to natural asymmetries in reward vs punishment statistics -- implying a tonic regulatory role cannot be straightforwardly derived from phasic dopamine analogies
The review notes that behavioural data in humans on serotonin's role remains inconsistent, limiting confident mapping from rodent/invertebrate computational models

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly models 5-HT as a pruning/inhibition signal in sequential decision-making under aversive prediction; reduced 5-HT tone leads to cascading negative prediction errors, consistent with benefit terrain collapse. But the paper models 5-HT primarily as aversive-suppressor rather than benefit-orientation maintainer — the tonic floor concept is implicit rather than the paper's explicit focus.
failure_signatures: Reduced serotonin fails to prune decision trees away from aversive branches, causing cascading negative prediction errors and behavioural disengagement
Behavioural inhibition collapse under low 5-HT maps onto sustained failure to maintain goal-directed pursuit in harm-laden environments

entries.confidence_rationale: Demonstrates that a distributed pattern including both dorsal posterior insula and dorsal anterior cingulate cortex is required to capture physical pain -- neither structure alone is sufficient. The fact that the neurologic pain signature spans both insula (sensory-discriminative) and ACC (affective-evaluative) regions, and that this distributed pattern predicts pain better than either region alone, is indirect evidence for the coordinated dual-stream architecture MECH-220 requires. Transfer risk: the paper characterises a multivariate *pattern*, not a directed *connectivity* relationship; hub coordination is not directly tested.
failure_signatures: If the pain signature could be reduced to a single region (e.g. posterior insula alone) without loss, the dual-stream coordination argument would be weakened
If the ACC component of the signature reflected only motor preparation rather than affective valuation, the harm-load mapping would be undermined

entries.confidence_rationale: Highly influential theoretical synthesis establishing the insula-ACC salience hub model. Four-mechanism framework directly maps to MECH-220 hub functions. Transfer risk: pain is not the primary focus; the paper addresses salience broadly. Mapping is structural/mechanistic, not pain-specific.
failure_signatures: The hub model treats insula and ACC as coordinating partners -- if they were truly independent with no cross-stream influence, the salience network framing would not hold
If the insula-ACC coupling only reflects co-activation rather than directed coordination, the hub interpretation is weakened

entries.confidence_rationale: Primary empirical data demonstrating that ACC and insula form a distinct resting-state network (salience network) dissociable from executive control. Functional coupling between these structures is shown to track affective state (anxiety), directly supporting the affective-modulation-of-sensory-gain dimension of MECH-220. Transfer risk: resting-state paradigm, not nociception task; affective covariate is dispositional anxiety, not acute harm urgency.
failure_signatures: If the salience network found here reflected only attentional set rather than affective amplification, the mapping to hypervigilance-gated sensory precision would be weakened
If ACC-insula coupling proved to be epiphenomenal rather than causal in the salience response, the hub coordination claim would be undermined

entries.confidence_rationale: The strongest direct empirical evidence for MECH-220's hypervigilance pathway among the four entries. The study demonstrates that (1) anterior insula prestimulus activity predicts pain classification under threat, and (2) anticipatory pain increases functional connectivity between anterior insula and midcingulate cortex (MCC/ACC). This is precisely the mechanism MECH-220 predicts: z_harm_a urgency (instantiated here as threat context) gates z_harm_s precision (instantiated as the probability of classifying a near-threshold stimulus as painful). Transfer risk is modest: the manipulation is threat-induced anticipatory state rather than endogenous affective urgency.
failure_signatures: If the prestimulus insula effect reflected general attentional readiness rather than affective gain modulation, the precision-gating mapping would be weakened
If the insula-MCC coupling increase under threat proved to be a byproduct of motor preparedness rather than sensory gain, the hub interpretation would need revision

entries.confidence_rationale: The paper explicitly frames depression as triggered by situations combining harm AND absence of crucial resources or viable plans -- a structural ratio logic. The same harm level WITH resources should not trigger depression, per the framework. However, this is evolutionary theory, not empirical test, and the ratio is qualitative not parametric.
failure_signatures: No empirical test of the resource-availability modulation claim.
Evolutionary framework does not map cleanly to computational attractor dynamics.
Crucial resource is not operationalised or quantified.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the only paper in this set that explicitly uses attractor state language for depression and proposes a computational model in which the balance between reward and non-reward input -- not absolute non-reward -- determines which attractor state wins. The reciprocal inhibition architecture directly implies that sufficient reward input prevents the non-reward attractor from engaging. Both reducing non-reward and increasing reward are valid interventions. Confidence limited by: model operates at neural circuit level (OFC), not environmental resource density; ratio threshold not parametrically specified; does not distinguish hazard/harm from non-reward.
failure_signatures: Model operates at neural circuit level -- does not specify environmental resource density as the parameter.
Ratio threshold is not parametrically defined in the model.
Harm and non-reward are not cleanly distinguished -- hazard exposure and reward absence are treated as functionally equivalent inputs.

entries.confidence_rationale: The paper explicitly frames anhedonia as arising from 'dysfunctional interactions between stress and brain reward systems' -- an interaction model, not a pure stress-load model. Critically, it reports that chronically stressed animals that successfully acquired appetitive behaviour showed protection against dopamine transporter reductions, suggesting active reward engagement buffers against stress-induced anhedonia. This is a direct analogue of the hazard/resource ratio claim. However, the paper does not explicitly formulate a ratio threshold, does not use attractor/bifurcation language, and does not test whether fixed hazard + sufficient reward prevents the depressive state. The support is structural-conceptual rather than parametric.
failure_signatures: The paper does not frame the interaction as a ratio with a threshold -- it describes a directional interaction effect without a tipping-point formulation.
No explicit test of whether sufficient reward exposure at fixed stress level prevents the depressive transition.
The protective effect of reward engagement is reported as a secondary finding, not the paper's main hypothesis.

entries.confidence_rationale: First study to apply an axiomatic 'adaptive coding' approach to pain PE in anterior insula, demonstrating that left dorsal anterior insula responds to the unexpectedness of pain delivery relative to local context rather than absolute pain magnitude. This is a direct empirical instantiation of SD-020's claim that z_harm_a encodes surprise (PE) not raw accumulated harm. Confidence is slightly below Horing 2022 due to smaller sample (19 subjects) and the specific 'adaptive coding' framework being less established than standard PE modelling, though the axiomatic approach is well-validated in value/reward literature.
failure_signatures: If adaptive coding in anterior insula reflects only the context-dependence of sensory gain (adaptation) rather than prediction error per se, the PE interpretation could be questioned.
If the effect is not replicated in larger samples, the small-n limitation (N=19) would become more serious.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct empirical demonstration of the anterior/posterior insula dissociation: anterior insula tracks predictive coding signals (expectation + PE), posterior insula tracks stimulus intensity. This is the strongest pre-Chen fMRI evidence that anterior insula (the biological anchor of z_harm_a) encodes PE rather than raw magnitude. High source quality (eLife, open access, Buchel lab), large enough sample (30 subjects), probabilistic paradigm allowing clean PE extraction. Slight confidence reduction because skin conductance and pupil dilation were used as peripheral PE proxies rather than independent fMRI PE regressors, but the paradigm logic is sound.
failure_signatures: If replications found anterior insula tracked absolute intensity rather than PE in identical paradigms, the dissociation claim would fail.
If the anterior/posterior gradient reflects only temporal dynamics (sustained vs. transient) rather than computational role (PE vs. intensity), this would weaken the mapping to z_harm_a.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strongest pre-Chen direct evidence for SD-020. Explicitly shows anterior insula encodes unsigned (absolute) intensity PE irrespective of modality -- i.e., aversive surprise regardless of whether the aversive event is pain or sound. The 'unsigned' qualifier is critical: this is modality-unspecific aversive surprise, exactly the signal SD-020 proposes for z_harm_a. Large sample (47 subjects), cross-modal paradigm (pain + loud sound), 3T fMRI with SCR. Also demonstrates pain-selective signed PE in posterior insula, providing within-study support for the anterior/posterior dissociation.
failure_signatures: If anterior insula PE signals were driven solely by attentional orienting rather than learning (i.e., if they disappeared in conditions where attention was controlled), the unsigned PE interpretation would be weakened.

If the modality-independence implies that anterior insula cannot distinguish harm-PE from any aversive-PE, this would suggest z_harm_a conflates harm and non-harm aversive surprise -- a potential problem for SD-020's specificity assumption.

entries.confidence_rationale: Influential theoretical review arguing that pain-matrix activity (including insula) reflects salience/surprise detection rather than pain-specific processing. Directly supports the SD-020 claim that affective harm encoding tracks unexpectedness rather than raw magnitude. Confidence is moderate because it is a review/theoretical position paper rather than direct empirical measurement of PE coding, and does not itself quantify the PE component — that empirical work came in later studies building on this framework.
failure_signatures: If insula responses were shown to correlate purely with nociceptive intensity irrespective of saliency, this framework would be undermined.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-resolution 7T brainstem fMRI study directly imaging PAG and RVM responses during placebo analgesia in humans, confirming that greater placebo ability correlates with differential PAG column activation and RVM engagement. Adds specificity missing from earlier lower-resolution studies: the lateral/dorsolateral PAG (rather than ventrolateral) is engaged during placebo, suggesting non-opioidergic mechanisms may also contribute. Directly relevant to SD-021's precision-downweighting claim because it shows the brainstem circuit is sensitive to top-down expectation states in humans with high anatomical resolution.
failure_signatures: The lateral PAG result (rather than vlPAG) may indicate non-opioidergic, serotonergic, or noradrenergic descending mechanisms, which would complicate the clean opioid-gating story in SD-021.
If placebo ability is a trait variable rather than a state that E3 commitment can invoke, the mechanism may not be trainable via commitment-gating in the way SD-021 proposes.

entries.confidence_rationale: Comprehensive review synthesising evidence that the brainstem PAG-RVM descending system is the hub through which cortical states (expectation, attention, emotion) modulate sensory pain. Directly maps onto SD-021's architecture. Confidence reflects the review nature (no new primary data) and the fact that the expectation-specific PAG activation findings reviewed here pre-date the pharmacological confirmation (Eippert 2009), slightly reducing causal certainty.
failure_signatures: If the PAG activations during anticipation reviewed here reflect threat-preparation (defensive arousal) rather than top-down analgesic gating, the descending inhibition framing would be incomplete.
If dlPFC-PAG coupling reflects attention rather than commitment-gated suppression, the mapping to E3 commitment requires revision.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational anatomical review establishing the PAG-RVM-spinal cord descending inhibitory axis as a distinct pathway that can be engaged top-down. Directly grounds the claim that there is a dedicated descending channel capable of suppressing nociceptive throughput. Lower confidence cap because the paper predates modern human imaging and does not address commitment or voluntary action specifically.
failure_signatures: If PAG stimulation produces analgesia only via motor/avoidance effects rather than sensory suppression, the descending inhibitory interpretation weakens.
If RVM on-cells and off-cells are not separable in humans, the bidirectional framing loses precision.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the key human fMRI + pharmacological dissection paper establishing that top-down cortical expectation (rACC) activates the PAG-RVM descending inhibitory axis via opioid mechanisms. Naloxone abolishes both rACC-PAG coupling and the behavioural placebo effect, providing a clean double dissociation. Directly supports the mechanism proposed in SD-021. Confidence is high but not maximal because placebo is not identical to voluntary goal-directed commitment -- it is belief/expectation-based, not yet motor-commitment-gated.
failure_signatures: If naloxone's effect is non-specific (e.g., anxiolytic rather than opioidergic), the descending modulation interpretation weakens.
If placebo analgesia and commitment-gated analgesia use different cortical origins (rACC vs. pgACC/dACC), the direct mapping to SD-021 would need revision.

entries.confidence_rationale: This experiment holds the hazard (social defeat stress) fixed across groups and varies the resource environment (standard vs enriched housing), then measures depression-like outcomes. This is structurally the closest available empirical operationalisation of Q-034's prediction: same hazard, higher resource density → protected from depression attractor. Enriched mice showed significantly fewer defeat-induced depressive-like behaviors and maintained FosB/DeltaFosB expression in reward-processing regions (infralimbic cortex, nucleus accumbens, amygdala). The infralimbic cortex lesion experiment demonstrates that the enrichment effect is circuit-mediated, not merely a physical activity confound. Confidence is moderate rather than high because enrichment bundles multiple resource types (novelty, social interaction, exercise, object exploration) without isolating reward-density per se; the stress was social defeat (a qualitatively different stressor from hazard_harm exposure in REE); and no parametric threshold was identified.
failure_signatures: Enrichment confounds reward density, novelty exposure, physical exercise, and social complexity -- it is not possible to attribute the protective effect to reward availability alone.
No parametric manipulation of enrichment level -- the study compares enriched vs standard vs impoverished housing, not a continuous resource gradient.
No threshold identified: the study shows protection at one enrichment level but does not characterise the dose-response relationship.
Social defeat stress is qualitatively different from the harm_exposure hazard in CausalGridWorldV2 -- the attacker's agency introduces uncontrollability components beyond simple hazard density.

entries.confidence_rationale: The paper provides strong conceptual support for Q-034 by demonstrating that controllability -- not stressor intensity -- is the key parameter determining whether an aversive event produces depression-like passivity and anxiety. Identical inescapable shocks leave rats with lasting anhedonia and fear; escapable shocks of the same intensity do not. Controllability maps onto resource access in the REE Q-034 framing: an agent with access to effective coping actions (resources) can modulate its exposure to harm, even under fixed hazard. The vmPFC-DRN gateway mechanism (controllability detection suppresses DRN serotonin → prevents learned helplessness) is directly analogous to the hypothesis that sufficient benefit_exposure prevents the depression attractor. Confidence is moderate rather than high because the paper does not frame the effect as a ratio, does not hold hazard intensity constant while varying resource density parametrically, and the controllability manipulation conflates resource access with efficacy expectations.
failure_signatures: The paper does not test a hazard/resource ratio formulation -- controllability is a categorical manipulation (escapable vs inescapable), not a parametric variation of resource density at fixed hazard.

The mechanism is primarily serotonergic (DRN 5-HT) and vmPFC-mediated, not mesolimbic dopaminergic -- transfer to the INV-053 attractor (which is dopamine-weighted) requires an additional bridging step.

Controllability confounds resource access with expectancy learning -- it is not possible from this literature alone to determine whether the protective effect is caused by reward receipt, by the act of responding, or by the cognitive representation of controllability.

entries.confidence_rationale: This review consolidates the mechanistic evidence that chronic stress suppresses mesolimbic dopamine reward processing (blunted NAc dopamine release, reduced D1/D2 receptor sensitivity, VTA firing changes) and that this suppression is the proximal cause of anhedonia in depression. The review explicitly frames reward-system modulation as a stress-coping mechanism, not merely a downstream casualty, supporting the claim that reward availability is a functional variable in stress response -- not simply an unrelated comfort factor. The NAc dopamine system's dual sensitivity to reward and aversive stimuli positions it as precisely the integrator a hazard/resource ratio model requires. Confidence is moderate: the review provides mechanistic grounding for the dopaminergic attractor hypothesis (INV-053) and establishes that reward-system state tracks stress exposure, but does not test the ratio formulation or threshold directly. It is a narrative review without primary data.
failure_signatures: The review does not test or propose a hazard/resource ratio formulation -- it describes directional effects of stress on reward without a threshold or tipping-point model.
Narrative review without primary data or meta-analytic pooling -- confidence in specific quantitative claims is limited.

The review emphasises that acute stress can transiently activate the dopamine system (salience signal), which could superficially argue against the depression-attractor model if the sustained chronic component is not clearly distinguished.

This is the paper explicitly cited in claims.yaml for MECH-116's frontal-hippocampal theta synchronisation grounding. The key finding directly supports MECH-116: working memory trial outcomes (correct vs. error) were predicted by theta-phase locking between hippocampus and mPFC, not by mPFC firing rates. This dissociation is important -- it implies that the coupling mechanism (theta synchrony), not the sustained-firing rate of individual neurons, is the critical variable for successful goal maintenance across delays. For MECH-116, this shifts some explanatory weight from 'E1 hidden state alone' to 'E1 recurrence coupled to hippocampal theta rhythm via ThetaBuffer' (ARC-032) -- which is consistent with the claim's full formulation. Confidence is 0.80: the paper used a spatial delayed non-match-to-sample task (rats), and the relevant unit is theta-phase entrainment, not goal-context content per se.
failure_signatures: If theta coherence differences between correct and error trials were epiphenomenal (driven by arousal or locomotion speed rather than goal maintenance), the working-memory-specific interpretation would be undermined
If mPFC firing rate modulation was simply too noisy to detect in the recording method used, the dissociation (theta coherence but not firing rate predicts performance) might be artifactual
If the task-relevant information was being maintained in hippocampus alone and mPFC was only receiving, not jointly maintaining, this would weaken the bilateral recurrence story in MECH-116

entries.confidence_rationale: Jones and Wilson 2005 established the foundational result that theta rhythms in the 4-12 Hz band coordinate hippocampal-prefrontal interactions specifically during working-memory-demanding spatial navigation, but not during simple locomotion or non-memory behavior. Both CA1 and mPFC neurons showed enhanced theta phase-locking during working-memory-requiring trials, and CA1-mPFC spike correlations were selectively elevated during the same periods. This directly supports the ThetaBuffer coupling mechanism in MECH-116: the hippocampal-to-E1 theta channel (ARC-032) is functionally engaged precisely when goal-context maintenance is required. Confidence is 0.76: the task is spatial (T-maze alternation), the mPFC role is ambiguous (decision-making vs. goal maintenance), and causality is not established.
failure_signatures: If increased hippocampal-mPFC theta coherence during spatial memory trials reflects task difficulty or arousal rather than specifically goal-context maintenance, the mapping to MECH-116's working memory substrate would be indirect
If the mPFC neurons being entrained are motor-planning neurons rather than memory-maintenance neurons, the analogy to E1 goal-context storage would be weakened
If theta coupling is only present during the decision point (T-junction) and not during the delay or approach phase, it would suggest decision integration rather than sustained goal maintenance

entries.confidence_rationale: This paper directly tests whether hippocampal theta sequences encode current goals, finding that look-ahead distance in theta sequences varies with goal proximity: sequences project further ahead when the goal is distant and closer when the goal is near. Goal-specificity is the key contribution -- theta sequences are not merely a spatial compression artifact but carry goal-modulated predictive content. For MECH-116, this supports the claim that hippocampal theta carries goal-context information, not just spatial location information, and that this content modulates E1's forward-prediction horizon. Confidence is 0.73: the paper is about place-cell theta sequences in rats, and the REE translation to abstract goal-context maintenance in E1 requires a significant conceptual jump. The 'goal' in the rat task is a valued food location -- a simpler structure than MECH-116's goal representation.
failure_signatures: If look-ahead in theta sequences is solely determined by running speed and route length rather than by goal value or identity, the goal-specific interpretation would collapse to a purely spatial/motor account
If goal modulation of theta sequences is only present at the goal approach phase and not during the earlier journey, it would suggest goal anticipation rather than sustained goal representation
If the effect is replicated by value (reward magnitude) rather than goal identity, the mapping to goal-context content in MECH-116 would be weakened

Landmark Nature paper providing first direct optogenetic proof of Go/NoGo pathway asymmetry: D1 direct pathway activation increases locomotion and approach; D2 indirect pathway activation elicits freezing, bradykinesia, and behavioral suppression. Directly demonstrates that the two channels are not redundant -- excitation of one does not substitute for the other. Bilateral D2 MSN activation produced a parkinsonian state (pure suppression / quiescence), precisely matching ARC-030's prediction that pure NoGo architecture produces behavioral flatness.
failure_signatures: If D1 and D2 pathways had symmetric or additive effects, bilateral D2 activation would not produce quiescence distinct from D1 activation.
If pure NoGo architecture were sufficient for goal-directed behavior, D2-activation animals would still initiate goal-directed locomotion -- they did not.

entries.confidence_rationale: Influential review demonstrating that nucleus accumbens dopamine (operating via D1/Go pathway) is specifically required for effort-based approach behavior -- not for hedonic 'liking' or appetite per se. Accumbens DA depletion selectively impairs effortful approach (cost-based decisions) while leaving basic food intake intact. This dissociation directly supports ARC-030: the Go/D1 sub-channel is specifically needed to drive approach under cost, while avoidance signals (D2/NoGo) alone produce quiescence in effortful contexts.
failure_signatures: If D1/Go pathways were not required for approach, DA depletion would not selectively impair effortful approach while sparing free-choice consumption -- but this is exactly what Salamone's lab showed.
If NoGo sub-channel alone could sustain goal-directed behavior, animals with accumbens DA depletion would still exert effort to obtain preferred rewards -- they do not.

entries.confidence_rationale: Major translational review linking animal models of accumbens DA depletion to clinical syndromes of anergia, psychomotor retardation, and apathy in depression, schizophrenia, and Parkinson's disease. The clinical syndromes are characterized precisely as the behavioral flatness that ARC-030 predicts from pure-NoGo architectures: motivation for effortful approach is selectively impaired while aversive sensitivity and avoidance remain relatively intact. This translational bridge strengthens the claim that symmetric Go/NoGo architecture is an architectural necessity, not a design option.
failure_signatures: If pure NoGo/avoidance were sufficient for goal-directed behavior, anergia and apathy would not emerge when dopamine-mediated Go signaling is impaired while avoidance sensitivity is preserved.
If Go and NoGo were equivalent and interchangeable, treating anergia with DA agonists (D1/Go restoration) would not selectively restore approach while leaving avoidance behavior intact.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly tests the approach/avoidance asymmetry at the reinforcement learning level: optogenetic stimulation of D1 MSNs (direct/Go pathway) induced persistent positive reinforcement; stimulation of D2 MSNs (indirect/NoGo pathway) induced transient punishment/suppression. These are qualitatively distinct outcomes, not merely different magnitudes of the same signal. This is the key evidence that Go and NoGo sub-channels carry non-exchangeable information -- exactly what ARC-030 requires.
failure_signatures: If Go and NoGo were symmetric, both D1 and D2 stimulation would produce equivalent learning effects of opposite sign. Instead, D1 produced persistent reinforcement while D2 produced only transient punishment -- a qualitative asymmetry.
If a pure NoGo architecture were sufficient, D2 stimulation alone would support normal learning; it produced only transient punishment without persistent reinforcement.

entries.confidence_rationale: Human lesion study (anterior temporal lobectomy with hippocampal resection) demonstrating that hippocampal damage impairs model-based planning in a two-step decision task, with impairment magnitude correlating with right hippocampal lesion size. Provides direct human causal evidence for the hippocampal-planning system in MECH-163. Coauthors include Daw (the computational RL theorist behind the model-free/model-based dissociation framework), increasing the rigor of behavioral classification. Confidence reduced slightly by unilateral lesion design and confound of overall temporal lobe damage.
failure_signatures: model-based planning impaired in hippocampal resection patients
impairment correlates with right hippocampal lesion size
planning and spatial memory covary in controls but not patients

entries.confidence_rationale: Causal evidence via muscimol inactivation in rats directly linking dorsal hippocampus to model-based planning behavior, using formal algorithmic behavioral analysis to distinguish planning from habitual S-R responding. High mapping fidelity to MECH-163's claim that hippocampal-planned system is required for model-based behavior. Rodent-to-human transfer risk moderate.
failure_signatures: hippocampal inactivation impairs model-based but not model-free behavior
effect specific to planning trials requiring multi-step internal model use

entries.confidence_rationale: Optogenetic dissociation directly contrasts VTA vs SNc dopamine neurons in instrumental reinforcement using multiple behavioral tasks in the same study. VTA dopamine imbues flexible, persistent, goal-directed motivational value; SNc dopamine supports time-limited, inflexible, action-specific habit-like learning. This is the cleanest available empirical dissociation of the SNc/dorsal-striatum vs VTA/ventral-striatum axis central to MECH-163. High source quality; mapping fidelity high for the dopaminergic dissociation component.
failure_signatures: VTA dopamine activation sufficient for flexible motivational value attribution
SNc dopamine activation produces non-scalable, action-specific S-R reinforcement
only VTA (not SNc) imbues cues with persistent pursuit value

This is the canonical theoretical paper on cerebellar forward models by the field's leading researchers. It characterizes the cerebellar forward model as compensating for sensory feedback delays (tens to hundreds of ms) -- a fundamentally short-horizon, one-step predictive function. The forward model predicts the immediate next state given efference copy, not a multi-step rollout. This directly weakens MECH-070's claim that E2 (cerebellar analogue) has a longer planning horizon than E1 (cortical analogue). The evidence direction is weakens-the-original-claim, and aligns with EXQ-132/EXQ-212 experimental findings. Confidence reflects the foundational authority of the source and the directness of the mapping.
failure_signatures: E2_degrades_faster_across_horizon
cerebellar_model_short_horizon_only

entries.confidence_rationale: Comprehensive synthesis of hunger/satiety neuroendocrine systems and their bidirectional modulation of mesolimbic dopamine. Directly maps to SD-012's drive_level scaling of benefit signals: hunger mediators (AgRP/NPY, LH orexin, ghrelin) enhance dopaminergic reward sensitivity in proportion to energy deficit; satiety mediators (GLP-1, POMC, leptin) suppress it. The bidirectional scaling is precisely what SD-012's effective_benefit = benefit_exposure * (1 + drive_weight * drive_level) formalises. Transfer risk moderate because the review is rodent-centred and the mapping to a discrete architectural parameter (drive_weight) is inferential rather than directly demonstrated.
failure_signatures: If dopamine reward modulation by hunger were uniform (not graded by drive magnitude), the drive_weight scaling in SD-012 would lack biological grounding.
If satiety suppression of dopamine were absolute (full silencing rather than graded reduction), the sated-state effective_benefit ~ benefit_exposure prediction would not hold.
Evidence is primarily from rodent pharmacology and optogenetics; translation to artificial agents is inferential.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality review in Science that synthesises the current state of neurocircuit understanding for diverse motivated behaviours. The paper's core thesis -- that drive-state-specific circuits modulate VTA dopamine neuron activity to reinforce goal-directed actions matching homeostatic need -- is the biological statement that SD-012 formalises computationally. The proposal that common approach/avoidance mechanisms underlie diverse drive states supports SD-012's generalisation of food-energy drive to arbitrary goal-seeking agents. Transfer risk is moderate: the review is empirically grounded in rodent feeding/drinking circuits, and the VTA-dopamine-reinforcement framing is proximal but not identical to REE's z_goal seeding architecture.
failure_signatures: If diverse motivated behaviours do not share VTA-dopamine modulation as a common substrate, SD-012's generalisation from food drive to arbitrary goal-directed behaviour would require independent justification.
If drive-state circuits modulate dopamine in a discrete (on/off) rather than graded manner, the continuous drive_level scaling in SD-012 would overspecify the architecture.

If the reinforcement function of VTA-DA is not separable from drive-state encoding (i.e., the same neurons do both), there would be no clean architectural separation between z_goal seeding and z_world reward prediction error.

entries.confidence_rationale: Demonstrates that a distinct dopamine population (ZI-DA, not VTA-DA) encodes hunger-driven motivational vigor specifically during food approach. These neurons activate during approach, inhibit during consumption, and track drive state (fasting). This is mechanistically relevant to SD-012: drive_level modulates the vigor (approach motivation) of benefit-seeking, separate from the hedonic value of consumption. The vigor-tracking role of ZI-DA is a candidate biological substrate for the drive_weight scaling in SD-012's effective_benefit formula. Transfer risk is moderate -- ZI is a non-canonical dopamine system whose homologue in artificial architectures is not established. Confidence reduced because the paper is circuit-level (rodent optogenetics/chemogenetics) and does not directly address the computational mechanism by which drive scales reward signals.
failure_signatures: If motivational vigor is regulated entirely by VTA-DA rather than ZI-DA, the circuit specificity finding would not generalize and the relevance to SD-012's scalar drive modulation would be indirect.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical theoretical paper on cerebellar forward models. It characterises the cerebellar forward model as a one-step delay-compensation device: it receives efference copy, predicts the next sensory state to bridge the feedback delay, then hands back to the sensory system. The paper explicitly does not assign multi-step rollout to the cerebellum -- that role belongs to higher cortical structures. This directly supports MECH-231's reformulation: E2 operates as a short-horizon efference-copy forward model whose prediction accuracy degrades faster than E1's across multi-step horizons, consistent with a cerebellar 1-step transition predictor. Confidence is slightly higher than for the MECH-070 weakening entry because the direction now aligns with rather than opposes the source's characterisation.

This 2021 review explicitly assigns short-horizon implicit prediction to the cerebellum and longer-horizon contextual reasoning to prefrontal cortex. The paper characterises the cerebellar forward model as computing rapid online corrections by predicting the next body state from efference copy, while prefrontal cortex handles belief integration and judgment at longer timescales. This directly supports MECH-231's claim that E2 (cerebellar analogue) is the shorter-horizon system and E1 (cortical analogue) is the longer-horizon system -- i.e., E2's prediction accuracy should degrade faster across multi-step horizons. The confidence is similar to the MECH-070 weakening entry; the timescale distinction is clear and the anatomical assignment is explicit, though the REE transfer remains indirect.

This review provides a quantitative upper bound on cerebellar predictive capacity: up to approximately 1 second for skilled movement prediction. This directly supports MECH-231's core assertion that E2 operates as a short-horizon predictor. A sub-second biological bound maps to a small number of discrete steps in a grid-world environment, consistent with a 1-step transition predictor architecture. The paper also notes that temporal precision is a key distinguishing feature of cerebellar processing relative to cerebral cortex, reinforcing the E2 < E1 horizon ordering. Confidence is slightly higher than the 0.65 from the MECH-070 weakening entry because the quantitative bound now directly supports the corrected claim rather than opposing it.

This paper demonstrates empirically and theoretically that a model trained on observational trajectories will learn the correlational distribution P(a|x) -- not the interventional distribution P(a|do(x)) -- and that this mismatch causes failures under distributional shift. This is exactly SD-013's core claim: E2_harm_s trained on observational rollouts learns the correlation between agent presence and ambient harm, not the causal mechanism. The paper's proposed remedy -- targeted environment interaction (interventional probing) -- directly instantiates the ARC-033 requirement for explicit counterfactual perturbation steps in E2_harm_s training. Confidence is moderate rather than high because the paper addresses policy learning (imitation) rather than forward model training; the mechanism of observational bias is formally analogous but the instantiation differs. The paper demonstrates causal confusion across control and driving domains, providing empirical breadth.
failure_signatures: If E2_harm_s is trained without counterfactual perturbation steps, it may learn to encode correlational regularities between the agent's presence in hazard-proximal states and elevated harm signals -- exactly the pattern de Haan et al. identify as causal misidentification. The model would then predict elevated z_harm_s whenever the agent is near a hazard zone, regardless of whether the agent's action caused the harm or harm would have occurred anyway.

The paper shows that adding more correlated observational features without interventional disambiguation can make causal confusion worse, not better. An E2_harm_s trained on richer observational data from confounded environments may have higher apparent predictive accuracy but more severely biased causal_sig estimates.

Resolution requires targeted interventions that 'break' the spurious correlation -- in SD-013 terms, executing a_cf from the same confounded state and observing the z_harm_s outcome. Without this, the observational symmetry cannot be broken and causal_sig will remain compressed.

Wang et al. (2021) prove formally that a policy learned from confounded observational data -- where unobserved context induces spurious correlations between actions and outcomes -- does not recover the true interventional value function. The paper derives tight upper bounds on the regret achievable using observational data alone, and shows that these bounds are strictly worse than what is achievable with interventional data under the same confounders. This directly supports SD-013: E2_harm_s trained on observational rollouts in confounded states cannot recover the interventional distribution P(z_harm_s | do(a)). The paper proposes deconfounding via adjustment estimators that require either instrumental variables or explicit interventional samples -- the RL equivalent of the counterfactual perturbation steps ARC-033 mandates. Confidence is moderate rather than high because the paper addresses value function estimation (policy evaluation) rather than forward model training; the mapping requires treating E2_harm_s as the entity that must estimate interventional quantities rather than a policy critic.
failure_signatures: If E2_harm_s is trained on confounded observational data without explicit interventional perturbation steps, the learned model will encode P(z_harm_s | z_t, a_behavioral) rather than P(z_harm_s | do(a)). Wang et al. show this bias is formally non-zero and scales with the degree of confounding -- in highly confounded states (the agent's behavioral policy correlates strongly with ambient harm patterns), causal_sig will be systematically underestimated or reversed.

The paper demonstrates that simply increasing the volume of observational data does not reduce confounding bias -- the bound on policy regret due to confounding is irreducible without adjustment. More observational rollouts from the same confounded behavioral policy will converge to the wrong interventional distribution, not toward it.

The deconfounding adjustment requires either an instrument (a variable that influences action but not outcome except through action) or interventional samples where the confounding correlation is broken. In the REE setting, executing a_cf from the same confounded state serves as the interventional sample -- breaking the behavioral policy's correlation with harm and providing the identifiable contrast needed for causal_sig.

entries.confidence_rationale: Venkatesh and Malikopoulos (2025) directly address the problem that is most proximate to SD-013: model-based RL under confounding. They prove that transition and reward models learned from confounded observational data are fundamentally inconsistent -- they do not converge to the interventional quantities needed for planning under state-based policies. This is the closest available computational paper to the SD-013 claim, which is specifically about a forward model (E2_harm_s) rather than a policy. The paper's central negative result -- that conventional model-learning from confounded data misrepresents the effect of candidate policies -- directly instantiates SD-013's claim about causal_sig. The proposed remedy (surrogate MDP with proximal adjustment) is technically different from ARC-033's counterfactual perturbation approach, but the necessity argument (observational model is insufficient) is the same. Confidence is moderate because the paper is an arXiv preprint (not peer-reviewed at top venue) and the specific model class (forward model for harm stream) differs from the paper's setting (reward/transition models for planning).
failure_signatures: Venkatesh and Malikopoulos show that a transition model learned from confounded offline data generates systematically biased predictions for any action that deviates from the behavioral policy. For E2_harm_s, this means that z_harm_s predictions for a_cf -- which by definition deviates from the agent's behavioral policy -- will be biased toward the behavioral policy's harm-correlated outcomes. The causal_sig = E2_harm_s(z_t, a_actual) - E2_harm_s(z_t, a_cf) will compress toward zero because both predictions are biased by the same confounding pattern.

The paper establishes that the learned model is inconsistent: it does not converge to the true interventional distribution P(s' | do(a)) even with infinite observational data. This is a qualitatively stronger failure than noise or approximation error -- the bias is structural and irreducible without adjustment. In the REE context, this means no amount of additional observational training will produce a reliable E2_harm_s without counterfactual perturbation data.

The paper notes that conventional maximum likelihood model-learning in confounded C-MDPs fails because the behavioral policy's correlation with the unobserved context corrupts the model's implicit assumptions about action-outcome independence. E2_harm_s training using standard next-step prediction loss on confounded trajectories makes exactly the assumptions the paper proves are invalid.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the primary reference cited in the SD-013 claim notes. Scholkopf et al. (2021) provide the foundational theoretical argument that statistical models trained on observational trajectories learn the correlational distribution P(z_harm_s_next | z_t, a) rather than the interventional distribution P(z_harm_s_next | do(a)), and that these distributions diverge in confounded states. The paper establishes that performing an intervention changes the data distribution in ways that make predictions from purely statistical models inaccurate -- this is the core argument SD-013 translates to E2_harm_s. The paper is a high-impact Proceedings of the IEEE review article by leading researchers in causal ML, giving it both authoritative status and broad synthesis value. The mapping to SD-013 is highly direct because the paper explicitly discusses forward models and i.i.d. assumptions. Confidence is higher than the other entries because this paper is the theoretical source from which SD-013's formulation was derived.
failure_signatures: Scholkopf et al. establish that statistical learning assumes i.i.d. data drawn from a fixed distribution. When an agent's own actions change the environment (i.e., when the agent intervenes), the distribution shifts. E2_harm_s trained on observational trajectories will produce incorrect predictions for actions that differ from the behavioral policy's distribution -- especially in confounded states where action and harm are spuriously correlated. The failure is not a matter of generalization; it is a matter of the learned distribution being the wrong distribution.

The paper explicitly discusses that interventional questions -- P(outcome | do(action)) -- are more challenging than prediction questions -- P(outcome | action) -- because interventions take the system out of the i.i.d. setting. An E2_harm_s that treats both a_actual and a_cf as prediction queries on the same distribution will compute a causal_sig that conflates causal and correlational contributions.

The paper notes that identifying the interventional distribution from observational data requires either additional assumptions (e.g., no unobserved confounders, known causal graph) or interventional data. In environments where the agent's policy is correlated with harm-proximal states, the no-unobserved-confounders assumption is violated, making observational-only training insufficient for causal_sig estimation.

The paper provides computational evidence that cooperation and intelligence co-evolve: selection for cooperative strategies selects for greater cognitive capacity, and vice versa. This bidirectional relationship is consistent with ARC-026's direction (intelligence does not crowd out cooperation). However, the mechanism is Machiavellian -- intelligence is selected because it enables better exploitation/navigation of social games, not because it specifically expands benefit-gradient sensitivity. The 'mixed' direction reflects that the paper supports the coexistence claim but does not support the specific asymmetric-scaling sub-claim (approach gradients grow faster than contact avoidance).

This is the most direct empirical test of the comparator hypothesis available in the neuroimaging literature. By parametrically rotating a virtual hand away from the subject's actual movement direction (0 degrees = perfect match, 25 degrees = partial mismatch, 50 degrees = large mismatch, 100% other = no correspondence), the study shows that right inferior parietal lobe activation increases monotonically with the degree of motor-sensory discrepancy. Insula shows the reverse. This dose-response relationship between prediction error magnitude and inferior parietal activation is precisely what a comparator mechanism predicts -- and exactly what MECH-095 requires for graded residue attribution in REE.
failure_signatures: If MECH-095 were wrong and the inferior parietal were simply a social cognition region, activation would not be parametrically modulated by the continuous motor-visual discrepancy angle.

The finding that agency experience degrades gradually rather than suddenly (as discrepancy increases) suggests the REE comparator should produce a graded confidence signal, not a binary switch -- important for how AgencyComparator output is used in residue gating.

entries.confidence_rationale: Meta-analysis across neuroimaging studies with quantitative coordinate comparison (ALE); distinguishes body-ownership from sense-of-agency networks. Mixed for MECH-095: validates that agency has a dedicated neural substrate dissociable from ownership, but challenges TPJ as the primary locus -- the IPL is ownership-specific, not agency-specific. The agency-specific network is SMA/premotor, raising the possibility that the REE AgencyComparator is positioned too far downstream.
failure_signatures: If the sense-of-agency network is primarily premotor/SMA rather than TPJ, the REE AgencyComparator may need to be positioned at an earlier architectural stage than MECH-095 currently specifies.
The shared insula activation (body-ownership AND agency) may be more relevant to REE's z_self monitoring than the IPL, which is ownership-specific.

entries.confidence_rationale: Farrer & Frith provide a clean, direct fMRI dissociation: anterior insula activates when subjects experience themselves as the cause of an action; inferior parietal cortex activates when they experience another person as the cause. This double dissociation is exactly what MECH-095 predicts -- the comparator region (here: inferior parietal / TPJ) activates specifically when self-attribution fails and external attribution is triggered. The paradigm is tightly controlled (same motor task and same visual stimuli across conditions; only the attribution changes), making this strong causal evidence rather than correlational.
failure_signatures: If TPJ/inferior parietal were not the comparator but instead a general salience region, it would activate for both self- and other-caused conditions -- the study finds the opposite.

If EXQ-121 AgencyComparator failure (AUC_COMP_ON < AUC_COMP_ABLATED) reflects a scale/training problem rather than a conceptual error, this paper's evidence for the underlying neural mechanism remains intact.

entries.confidence_rationale: Two-photon calcium imaging study with large cell counts, causal optogenetic manipulation, and within-session reward relocation providing strong internal controls. Directly shows a dedicated LEC population for goal approach whose representations shift immediately to reward identity rather than absolute spatial position. The key SD-015 implication is that the navigator encodes 'which reward' (type/identity signal) rather than 'where reward was last seen' (positional signal), which is exactly why z_resource must be reward-type-centric rather than position-centric. Confidence bounded because the 1D virtual track limits generalization to the high-dimensional spatial scenarios in CausalGridWorld, and the task contains no object-type variation (single reward identity), so the paper speaks to reward-relative coding generally rather than multi-object-type discrimination.
failure_signatures: If LEC goal-approach populations also encode absolute spatial position strongly (not just reward-relative position), then the 'what' stream interpretation weakens and a dedicated object-type encoder becomes less motivated.
If hippocampal CA1 already encodes goal approach signals through a different mechanism (e.g., remapping), LEC's role might be redundant with spatial representations rather than complementary to them.

entries.confidence_rationale: Multi-region simultaneous recording in rats performing a multisensory object-discrimination task, allowing direct comparison of object-identity coding across the hierarchy. Key finding supporting SD-015: object identity is encoded in sensory cortex (V2L) but NOT in perirhinal cortex, and NOT reliably in hippocampus during sampling -- only afterwards, amodally, following reward. This dissociation suggests object identity representation and motivational/reward coding are handled by distinct circuits, consistent with SD-015's argument that z_resource must be a dedicated object-type encoder separate from reward/goal circuitry. Confidence bounded by limited recording sites (four regions only) and the fact that the task involves object discrimination at a fixed location rather than navigation toward randomly-respawning resources.
failure_signatures: If perirhinal cortex were found to strongly encode object identity in a navigation task where animals must approach objects, SD-015's architecture would need to place z_resource retrieval at the perirhinal rather than IT/sensory cortex stage.

If hippocampus were shown to encode object identity robustly during the approach phase (before reward), it would suggest z_world itself may carry sufficient object-type information, undermining the need for a separate z_resource.

entries.confidence_rationale: Review paper synthesizing electrophysiology and lesion evidence across multiple species. Directly describes a dedicated object-identity stream (LEC) that is anatomically and functionally separate from the spatial stream (MEC), paralleling the z_resource / z_world split proposed in SD-015. Confidence bounded by the fact that the LEC 'what' stream is not purely object-type identity -- it also carries egocentric relational and temporal information -- so the mapping is directional rather than isomorphic.
failure_signatures: If LEC neurons encode raw positional information as strongly as object identity, the 'what' stream argument weakens and the motivation for a separate z_resource encoder is reduced.
If hippocampal place cells downstream encode object type independently of location even without LEC input, then z_resource could be derived from z_world rather than requiring a separate encoder.

entries.confidence_rationale: Demonstrates that the hippocampus itself encodes valence (anxiety/avoidance), not just neutral context for amygdala to label. Ventral CA1 contains 'anxiety cells' that drive avoidance via the vCA1->LHA pathway. This challenges the traditional view that hippocampus only provides context. For REE, it means the harm residue field having valence directly in the hippocampal terrain is biologically accurate. But the paper only addresses negative valence (anxiety), not approach/wanting — so it speaks to one half of the asymmetry.
failure_signatures: Anxiety cells were enriched in vCA1->LHA projection neurons but NOT in vCA1->BA projection neurons. The amygdala-projecting hippocampal cells were context-encoding, not valence-encoding.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct optogenetic manipulation of engram cells in DG and BLA with valence reversal paradigm. High source quality (Nature, Tonegawa lab, rigorous controls). The key finding — DG engrams are valence-flexible while BLA engrams are valence-fixed — maps directly onto the REE distinction between hippocampal terrain (which should be updatable) and amygdala valence tagging (which is more rigid). Moderate mapping fidelity because REE's wanting/liking distinction is not identical to the fear/reward reversal tested here, but the structural principle (hippocampus = flexible context, amygdala = fixed valence) is directly relevant.
failure_signatures: BLA engrams could not be switched from fear to reward or vice versa — this challenges any architecture that assumes amygdala valence representations are as malleable as hippocampal ones

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct empirical evidence that local hippocampal dopamine controls place cell reorientation to represent reward-relevant spatial dimensions. Blocking D1 receptors locally prevented both the place cell remapping AND the learning. This is the strongest direct evidence that dopamine doesn't just enhance memory consolidation — it actively reshapes the hippocampal map to align with reward structure. Highly relevant to the REE question of how wanting/reward information enters the terrain.
failure_signatures: D1 receptor blockade caused perseveration — the map froze on the old reward-relevant dimension and could not reorient. This suggests dopamine is required for map updating, not just map formation.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical theoretical paper proposing the hippocampal-VTA functional loop. The model describes the downward arm (hippocampus novelty signal -> subiculum -> accumbens -> ventral pallidum -> VTA) and upward arm (VTA DA release -> hippocampus, enhancing LTP). This directly supports the REE architecture question: approach valence reaches hippocampus via dopaminergic modulation of plasticity, not direct valence injection. The mechanism is representational sharpening (enhanced LTP at reward-associated locations), not explicit positive valence tagging. High influence paper but theoretical — the specific loop has been partially confirmed but the complete circuit is still debated.
failure_signatures: The complete loop (hippocampus -> subiculum -> NAc -> VP -> VTA -> hippocampus) has not been fully validated as a single functional circuit in vivo
