entries.confidence_rationale: Kay et al. demonstrate that hippocampal neural activity cycles continually at 8 Hz between two distinct alternative future representations -- one possible-future per ~125ms cycle. This is the strongest direct evidence in the literature that hippocampal theta-cycle content is *non-stationary across cycles* and toggles between alternatives. That is partial support for MECH-294 (theta cycles do carry distinct content packets) but partial weakening (the demonstrated architecture is one-content-per-cycle alternation rather than four-content-per-cycle joint binding -- closer to Colgin-style serial multiplexing than to MECH-294's joint packet). Confidence 0.71: direct rodent evidence in Cell, but architectural fit is ambiguous.
failure_signatures: The Kay et al. architecture is *alternation* between content streams across cycles -- one possible future per cycle, with cycles toggling at 8 Hz. MECH-294 claims joint binding within one cycle. These are competing architectural hypotheses; if Kay et al.'s alternation pattern is the dominant theta-content scheme, MECH-294's joint-packet claim is incorrect.

The two streams demonstrated are alternative possible futures (left maze path vs right maze path) -- both planning content but of the *same content type* (path). MECH-294 needs four streams of distinct content types. The same-content-type alternation may not generalise to heterogeneous-content joint binding.

The paper finds the alternation is constant during running, not gated by decision moments. That suggests the architecture is structural (always cycling) rather than task-dependent (binding when planning is needed). MECH-294's predictions about when packets are bound (during commit windows / planning episodes) are not directly supported.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct demonstration that olfactory cue (lateral entorhinal cortex / LEC) and spatial-context (CA1) ensemble activity co-evolve during associative learning, with theta-band coherence (20-40 Hz) developing specifically between lateral CA1 and LEC. This is one of the closest results in the literature to MECH-294's joint-binding hypothesis: two semantically-distinct content streams (olfactory cue + spatial context) become phase-coherent in the same theta-organised window during the learning of their conjunction. Confidence 0.78 -- direct rodent multi-region recording, Nature publication, but only two streams, both encoding/retrieval rather than the planning content (goal/action/risk) MECH-294 most needs.
failure_signatures: Igarashi et al. demonstrate two-stream binding (olfactory cue + spatial context) in the LEC-CA1 circuit. MECH-294 needs four-stream binding (goal + action + risk + state). The paper does not test whether more than two streams can be jointly bound within one theta window.

The bound streams are sensory cue + spatial context, both encoding-side content. MECH-294's four streams include action proposals and risk estimates -- planning-side content -- which arrive from regions (BG, amygdala, ACC) not recorded in this paper.

The coherence result is at 20-40 Hz, in the boundary between high theta and low gamma. The paper does not directly characterise the within-theta-cycle gamma sub-slot structure, so the joint-binding architecture is inferred from the coherence pattern, not directly observed.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical empirical demonstration that CA1 gamma fractionates into slow (~25-50Hz, CA3-coupled, memory) and fast (~60-100Hz, MEC-coupled, current position) bands locked to distinct theta phases. That theta-locked content routing is the strongest substrate evidence for MECH-294. Capped at 0.82 because the result is across-cycle segregation, not within-cycle joint binding, and the streams are homogeneous spatial/memory content -- not the four heterogeneous streams MECH-294 needs.
failure_signatures: The paper's headline finding is across-cycle segregation: slow and fast gamma occur 'mostly on different theta cycles'. That pattern is closer to a serial-multiplexing architecture than to MECH-294's within-cycle joint-binding architecture.

The two demonstrated streams are both spatial/memory and both sourced from hippocampal-system upstream. MECH-294's four streams are heterogeneous in content type and sourced from non-hippocampal regions; the gamma-routing scheme may not generalise.
The paper does not address whether downstream consumers read multiple content streams jointly within one phase-aligned window, which is the consumer-side architecture MECH-294 needs.

entries.confidence_rationale: Pfeiffer & Foster demonstrate that hippocampal place-cell sequences encode trajectories from current location to remembered goal locations *before* navigation begins, supporting the broader claim that hippocampal sequences carry planning content (path proposals from current state to goal). This supports MECH-294's framing that state_summary, goal_latent, and an implicit action_proposal (the trajectory) co-exist in hippocampal sequence content. Confidence 0.70: the paper's primary sequences are SWR-associated rather than theta-cycle sequences, so the binding-window evidence is for a different oscillatory regime than MECH-294's theta-cycle window. This is a partial-support / oblique-evidence entry.
failure_signatures: The hippocampal sequences here are sharp-wave-ripple (SWR) replay events, not theta-cycle sequences. SWR events are 100-200ms compressed sequences during pauses; theta cycles are 100-150ms cycles during active behaviour. The two oscillatory regimes have different content and different downstream consumers, so the paper's evidence is oblique to MECH-294's theta-cycle binding-window claim.

The streams co-encoded in the sequence are start location and goal location -- both spatial -- with the action proposal implicit in the trajectory shape. MECH-294 needs four explicit semantically-distinct streams. The Pfeiffer & Foster evidence implicates two-stream binding at most.
The paper does not address risk content at all. Whether risk_estimate would be co-encoded in the same hippocampal sequences is unaddressed.

entries.confidence_rationale: Wikenheiser & Redish demonstrate that hippocampal theta-cycle place-cell sequences carry goal-relevant content -- the look-ahead distance of theta sequences scales with the distance to the rat's current goal. This is direct evidence that goal_latent is theta-locked and theta-cycle-resolved, which is one of the four content streams MECH-294 needs to bind. Confidence 0.74: direct unit-level rodent evidence, Nature Neuroscience, but the paper demonstrates only one of MECH-294's four streams (goal) being theta-locked; it does not address whether goal content is co-bound with action/risk/state content in the same theta cycle.
failure_signatures: The paper demonstrates goal-content theta-locking. MECH-294 needs goal + action + risk + state co-bound in one cycle. Single-stream theta-locking is necessary but not sufficient evidence.

Theta sequences here are place-cell sequences (location representations modulated by goal). MECH-294's action_proposal and risk_estimate streams are not place-cell content -- they are content sourced from BG and amygdala/ACC respectively. Whether those streams are theta-locked is not addressed.

The look-ahead-scales-with-goal-distance result is a content-modulation effect, not a binding-window effect. The paper does not test whether the goal latent is co-readable with other content types in the same theta-cycle window.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical Neuron review of theta-gamma multiplexing and the closest theoretical anchor for MECH-294. Lisman & Jensen explicitly argue that theta-gamma cross-frequency coupling forms a code for representing multiple items in an ordered way within a single theta cycle, with different gamma subcycles carrying different content. That is precisely the substrate MECH-294 needs. Confidence held at 0.74 because the review's canonical examples are homogeneous content (multiple spatial items, working-memory list items) rather than heterogeneous content streams (goal_latent + action_proposal + risk_estimate + state_summary). The theta cycle as a multi-content binding window is asserted in the review's framing; the specific REE four-content packet is an extrapolation.
failure_signatures: The review treats the multi-item code as ordered serial slots within a theta cycle (item 1 in gamma cycle 1, item 2 in gamma cycle 2, etc.). MECH-294 needs simultaneous heterogeneous-content binding -- four different content types co-occurring in one phase-aligned window, not four members of the same content type in serial gamma sub-slots. The review does not distinguish these architectures and does not provide direct evidence for the heterogeneous-binding case.

Lisman & Jensen's primary mechanistic case is hippocampal CA1 working-memory load, where the multiple items are spatial locations or list elements -- all of the same type. They do not address whether semantically distinct streams (goal vs risk vs state vs action) can be co-bound within a single theta cycle, nor what would distinguish a multi-content packet from a sequence of single-content packets at theta-cycle resolution.

The proposed coding scheme is sequence-organising (which gamma cycle within theta carries which item). MECH-294's claim is binding-organising (a single phase-aligned window holds heterogeneous content jointly). These are computationally different operations and the review's evidence does not directly discriminate between them.

entries.confidence_rationale: Hasselmo's review is the canonical theoretical anchor for the idea that distinct theta phases carry functionally distinct operations -- encoding on one phase, retrieval on the opposite phase, with the cholinergic/synaptic-current state of CA1 differing between phases. That establishes the principle that one theta cycle naturally carries multiple distinct operational contents at distinct phases, which is the architectural pattern MECH-294 generalises. Confidence 0.66: theoretical/computational, not direct multi-region recording, and the contents Hasselmo distinguishes are 'encoding' and 'retrieval' (two operational modes of the same content) rather than four semantically distinct content streams.
failure_signatures: Hasselmo's distinction is between two functional *modes* (encoding vs retrieval) that operate on the same content type. MECH-294 needs distinct *content types* (goal vs action vs risk vs state) carried in distinct phase windows. These are different architectural claims and the review's evidence does not directly distinguish them.
The review is largely a synthesis of computational modelling and cholinergic pharmacology in CA1; it does not provide direct in-vivo demonstration of multiple content streams within one theta cycle.

The two-phase encoding/retrieval scheme is binary (one phase or the other). MECH-294 needs at least four sub-windows per cycle. The review does not address how a four-slot architecture would be implemented or whether it is biologically plausible at theta resolution.

entries.confidence_rationale: Companion failure-mode prediction to Adams 2013 in a different clinical context. Autism's perceptual symptoms (sensory hypersensitivity, intolerance of uncertainty, repetitive behaviour as precision-driven prior assertion) are framed as systematic miscalibration of precision-weighting -- in particular, an over-precise sensory channel relative to the precision of priors. Tag (c) inferential support plus tag (d) failure-mode evidence. Confidence 0.64 reflects that this is a theoretical framing rather than empirical measurement, and that competing accounts (Bayesian-prior-strength accounts, weak-central-coherence) make different but overlapping predictions. Particularly relevant for MECH-269b because Lawson et al. do mention per-modality precision differences -- the closest available gesture toward per-stream precision in the clinical literature.
failure_signatures: Lawson et al. frame autism as imbalanced precision, but they do not commit to whether the imbalance is global (one precision parameter mis-set everywhere) or per-stream (different streams have different mis-set precisions in different patients). MECH-269b's per-stream V_s is consistent with the latter and the paper gestures at it (different sensory modalities show different sensitivities) but does not demonstrate it.

Hippocampal involvement is not a focus of the paper -- it is centred on cortical sensory-prior balance. The symmetric-application question (does autism manifest in both hippocampal proposer and cortical world-model precision?) is unaddressed. Tag (d) measurement gap.

Theoretical framing rather than empirical demonstration. Competing accounts (notably weak-central-coherence and enhanced-perceptual-functioning) make overlapping predictions and are not directly adjudicated.

entries.confidence_rationale: The paper formalises attention as inference about precision -- specifically, the precision (inverse uncertainty) of sensory channels that supply data to higher-level inference. This is the closest available precedent for MECH-269b's per-stream V_s gating: precision is set per channel, varies dynamically with state, and modulates how strongly that channel's prediction error drives downstream representations. Tag (a) direct support for cortex-side per-channel precision gating. Confidence held at 0.70 because the paper is computational -- it shows that this precision-is-attention scheme reproduces psychophysical and electrophysiological observations -- but it does not provide direct biological measurement of per-stream gain modulation, and again does not address hippocampal symmetry.
failure_signatures: Feldman & Friston frame precision optimisation as state-dependent and modality-general. They do not commit to a position on whether each anatomically-distinguishable sensory stream has its own precision parameter, or whether one global precision schedule modulates all streams together. MECH-269b's per-stream V_s is consistent with the former interpretation but the paper allows the latter.

The framework is cortical and attentional. It does not engage with the question of whether the same precision signal that gates cortical sensory channels also gates hippocampal proposer anchor selection. The symmetric-application claim is therefore not tested here -- this is a measurement gap (tag d).

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational synthesis showing that the cortical column's six-layer microcircuitry implements predictive coding with precision-weighted prediction errors. Directly grounds the cortex-side of MECH-269b: superficial-layer pyramidal cells are the substrate for prediction-error signals whose gain (precision) is modulated by NMDA / classical-modulatory interneuron populations and by feedback connections. This is (c) inferential-strong support: the cortex is wired to gate the contribution of each prediction-error stream by a precision parameter, which is exactly the architectural primitive MECH-269b requires on the E1/E2 side. Confidence held at 0.72 because the paper does not measure per-stream precision specifically (it argues at the column level) and does not address symmetric application across hippocampal vs cortical modules at all.
failure_signatures: Bastos et al. argue that precision is encoded by post-synaptic gain on superficial pyramidal cells reporting prediction error, but they do not specify whether the gain factor can be set independently per modality or per content-stream within a single column. The MECH-269b assumption that V_s is per-stream rather than per-region is consistent with their framework but is not directly demonstrated.

The paper says nothing about the hippocampus or about whether the hippocampal proposer's anchor-selection logic uses the same precision signal as cortical prediction-error gating. The symmetric-application claim (b) is not addressed at all here -- this is a gap in the evidence base, not a contradiction.

entries.confidence_rationale: Clinical-pathological corroboration of the precision-weighting framework: hallucinations, delusions, sensory-attenuation deficits, catatonia, and abnormal eye movements are all unified as expressions of aberrant precision. The paper supplies an indirect failure-mode prediction that is highly relevant to MECH-269b's wired-but-inert hypothesis: when precision on prediction-error channels is mis-set, downstream consumers receive technically-correct but contextually-wrong PE signals, and behavioural revision is impaired in characteristic ways. Tag (c) inferential support plus tag (d) failure-mode evidence. Confidence 0.66 reflects clinical-mapping caveats (the syndromes are heterogeneous and the precision model is one of several competing accounts) and the fact that the paper does not directly measure per-stream precision in psychosis or the hippocampal-cortical symmetry.
failure_signatures: Adams et al. argue that aberrant precision on sensory or prior beliefs produces specific psychopathological syndromes (hallucinations from over-precise priors, delusions from systematic precision errors, catatonia from collapsed precision on motor priors). This is a failure-mode prediction that supports the MECH-269b architectural claim by showing what happens when precision is mis-set; but it is indirect support, not direct measurement.

The paper is largely silent on whether the same precision parameter that mis-fires in psychosis is used by the hippocampal proposer. Hippocampus is mentioned briefly (in the context of memory and pattern completion) but the symmetric-application question is not engaged.

Clinical mapping is heterogeneous: not all psychotic patients have the same precision profile, and the precision-weighting account competes with dopamine-signal-to-noise and aberrant-salience accounts. The supportive force is therefore at the framework level, not at the level of any single empirical measurement.

entries.confidence_rationale: The strongest direct hit in the anchor list. Kanai et al. argue that cortical hierarchies require a dedicated thalamic substrate (pulvinar) to deliver per-cortical-area modulatory gain control on prediction errors -- effectively, a per-region precision signal that selects which cortical streams contribute to ascending Bayesian inference. This is tag (a) direct cortex-side per-stream precision gating, biologically grounded in pulvinar circuitry, and explicitly framed as a route by which inference-content (driving, first-order) is dissociated from precision-context (modulatory, second-order). MECH-269b's V_s is essentially this precision channel, applied to E1 / E2 streams. Confidence 0.78 reflects high mapping fidelity for the cortex side and the explicit anatomical proposal; symmetric-application novelty (vs hippocampal proposer) remains unaddressed.
failure_signatures: Kanai et al. propose pulvinar-mediated precision gating but treat the precision parameter as set per cortical area, not per latent content stream within an area. MECH-269b's per-stream specialisation (z_world, z_self, z_harm_s independently gated) requires a finer granularity than this paper provides; the paper supplies an upper-bound substrate but does not demonstrate the specific resolution.

The hippocampal-cortical symmetry question is silently passed over. The paper's frame is cortical hierarchies plus thalamus; hippocampal anchor selection is not discussed, and so the symmetric-V_s-application claim of MECH-269b cannot be confirmed or denied from this evidence -- it is a measurement gap.

entries.confidence_rationale: The closest available precedent for tag (b) symmetric application of a reliability signal across two computationally-distinct world-model systems. Daw, Niv & Dayan propose that prefrontal model-based and dorsolateral-striatal model-free control compete for behavioural output via uncertainty-based arbitration -- each system is deployed where it should be most accurate. This is the only paper in the anchor list that engages directly with the symmetric question MECH-269b asks: when two distinct architectures (model-based vs model-free; or by analogy, hippocampal proposer vs cortical world-model) hold different opinions about a state, can a single uncertainty signal arbitrate between them? Confidence held at 0.58 because the analogy is structural rather than direct: Daw et al. arbitrate between two action-selection systems, not between hippocampal-proposer and cortical-forward-prediction streams within a planning loop. The principle (uncertainty as arbiter of cross-system contribution) maps; the specific mechanism does not.
failure_signatures: Daw, Niv & Dayan arbitrate between two distinct *action-selection* systems (PFC model-based vs DLS model-free). MECH-269b proposes V_s gates contributions to a *single* shared planning loop from two complementary substrates (hippocampal proposer + cortical world-model). The structural analogy holds (uncertainty-as-arbiter) but the specific architecture is different.

The paper does not test the prediction that the same uncertainty signal driving arbitration is also computed and consumed in the hippocampus -- they treat hippocampus as a contributor to the model-based system rather than as an architecturally-distinct precision-gated module. Tag (b) symmetric-cortical-vs-hippocampal precision gating is implied but not tested directly.

Computational paper without direct biological measurement of the arbitration signal. The framework has been extended in subsequent work but the symmetric-precision claim of MECH-269b remains a forward extension rather than a direct empirical inheritance.

entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical empirical demonstration that the human nervous system performs reliability-weighted (precision-weighted) multimodal integration: visual and haptic estimates are combined in proportion to their inverse variances. This is direct behavioural evidence that the brain computes per-stream reliability -- the empirical foundation that MECH-269b's per-stream V_s formalises and extends. Tag (c) strong inferential support: the per-stream precision parameter that MECH-269b proposes is psychophysically demonstrable in humans for at least the sensory-modality case. Confidence 0.74 reflects that this is direct empirical support for per-stream precision in cue integration but does not extend to forward-prediction gating or to the hippocampal-cortical symmetry.
failure_signatures: Ernst & Banks demonstrate per-modality precision in cue integration -- visual and haptic. The extension from cue integration (combining current sensory estimates) to forward-prediction gating (combining model-generated predictions weighted by per-stream reliability) is a forward-extrapolation that this paper does not directly test.

The paradigm is psychophysical and does not engage with planning, rollouts, or hippocampal proposer dynamics. The symmetric-application claim (that the same per-stream reliability signal gates both hippocampal anchor selection and cortical forward predictions) is not addressable from this evidence -- tag (d) measurement gap.

Two modalities only. The generalisation to many simultaneous streams (z_world, z_self, z_harm_s, z_harm_a, z_goal in REE) is a mathematical extension that the paper supports in principle but does not directly demonstrate.

entries.confidence_rationale: Comprehensive 2014 review consolidating a decade of hedonic-hotspot mapping across NAc shell and ventral pallidum, with anatomical specificity (rostrodorsal NAc shell hotspot ~1mm cubed; posterior VP hotspot in caudal half) and corresponding 'coldspots' where mu-opioid stimulation suppresses liking. Explicit distinction between hedonic generators (limited, spatially circumscribed) versus wanting/incentive generators (larger, more distributed). For MECH-295 this provides the substrate-level evidence that liking-stream is a real, distinct, anatomically discrete generator -- not a downstream readout of wanting. Confidence 0.74: review article (not primary), but consolidates the strongest available data with clear anatomical mapping. The necessity link is asserted theoretically but not directly tested in this paper.
failure_signatures: If liking and wanting were the same signal at different sites, no anatomical hotspot/coldspot dissociation should be observable; the review documents that they are.

If the liking-stream were a passive consequence of wanting activation, the same circuits should generate both; the review documents distinct generator regions and discrete control by mu-opioid, kappa-opioid, delta-opioid, cannabinoid and orexin signalling.

entries.confidence_rationale: DAT-knockdown mice with chronically elevated synaptic dopamine show increased motivated approach and consumption of sucrose ('wanting' increased) but unchanged orofacial hedonic reactions ('liking' unchanged). This is the canonical demonstration that wanting can be amplified independently of liking -- which is the wanting/liking-dissociation background MECH-295 builds on. For MECH-295's specific necessity claim (liking required for drive-to-approach), this paper is mixed: it shows wanting can be elevated without elevating liking, which on a strict reading would weaken the necessity claim (drive-amplified approach occurred without elevated liking). However, the mice have NORMAL liking, not absent liking; the experiment is one-tailed (push wanting up, look at liking) rather than the symmetric test (block liking, look at whether drive-amplified wanting still produces approach). Confidence 0.70: high source quality, classical wanting/liking dissociation, but interpretive ambiguity for MECH-295's specific necessity claim.
failure_signatures: If MECH-295 strong reading were correct (liking activation NECESSARY for drive-to-approach), then any elevation of wanting/approach should be accompanied by elevated liking; Pecina 2003 shows wanting elevated with liking unchanged.

If MECH-295 weak reading is correct (liking is the bridge that propagates drive into approach but baseline liking is sufficient -- only the LINK is necessary, not the level), then wanting can be amplified by tonic dopamine without further liking elevation; this paper is consistent with that reading.

entries.confidence_rationale: The foundational incentive-learning paper, demonstrating across multiple instrumental devaluation experiments that an outcome's current motivational value influences instrumental responding ONLY IF the animal has previously experienced that outcome in the relevant motivational state. A drive shift (e.g. hunger -> sated) does not automatically reduce approach to a previously rewarded lever; the animal must consume the outcome under the new state before approach behaviour updates. This is the cleanest behavioural demonstration that drive-state changes do not directly rewire approach -- they must propagate through experienced hedonic value (the liking-stream) before reaching action selection. This is precisely MECH-295's necessity claim, articulated in pre-Berridge instrumental-conditioning vocabulary. Confidence 0.80: foundational source, multiple converging experiments, direct mechanistic mapping to MECH-295, but the experimental paradigm is different (instrumental devaluation rather than cue-driven approach under drive amplification).
failure_signatures: If drive amplification could produce approach without routing through experienced hedonic value, animals should reduce approach to a previously rewarded lever immediately upon a drive-state change (sated -> hungry not relevant; relevant: shift in outcome value); Dickinson & Balleine show they don't until they have experienced the outcome under the new state.

If MECH-295's necessity claim is wrong, then incentive-learning experiments should show drive-shift effects on instrumental responding without intervening outcome experience; the paradigmatic finding of this paper is that they do not.

entries.confidence_rationale: Primary, anatomically precise demonstration that a circumscribed cubic-millimetre region of NAc medial shell (the 'hedonic hot spot') is sufficient to amplify orofacial liking reactions to sucrose when activated by the mu-opioid agonist DAMGO. Outside the hot spot, DAMGO infusions in the rest of medial shell produced increases in food intake (wanting) WITHOUT increases in liking reactions -- a within-shell anatomical dissociation of wanting and liking substrates. This directly supports the architectural premise of MECH-295 that liking has its own dedicated substrate (tag b: liking encoding). It does not prove the necessity link between liking and approach (the experiment increases liking pharmacologically; it does not block liking and observe approach failure), but it establishes that liking is encoded by a specific, separable circuit -- a prerequisite for any 'liking is required intermediate' claim. Confidence 0.78: high source quality, direct anatomical evidence, but the experiment increases rather than ablates liking, so it is one logical step removed from the necessity claim.
failure_signatures: If liking and wanting were generated by the same neural population, mu-opioid stimulation of the hot spot should increase both equivalently; the paper shows the spatial distribution differs.
If REE's liking-stream were a passive readout of drive level, no dedicated anatomical substrate should exist; this paper shows one does.

entries.confidence_rationale: Comprehensive Neuron review of the pleasure system as a network of interacting hedonic hotspots (NAc shell, VP, parabrachial, OFC) with a documented architecture in which liking signals modulate motivational and decision processes. The review explicitly addresses the question of whether wanting can occur without liking and treats liking as a critical input to motivational decision-making rather than a passive afterglow. For MECH-295 this is the cleanest theoretical articulation of the necessity claim available in the literature, anchored to the substrate evidence (hotspots) and the dissociation evidence (DAT-knockdown, dopamine-depleted rats). Confidence 0.76: high-impact venue, theoretically explicit on the architectural role of liking, but a review (not primary), and the strong necessity claim is asserted with caveats rather than directly tested.
failure_signatures: If the brain's reward architecture were a single value signal with no separable liking generator, the network of hedonic hotspots and coldspots described in this review would not be observable; it is.

If liking were merely a downstream readout of consummatory contact and contributed nothing to upstream decision-making, OFC pleasure coding (Kringelbach 2005) and OFC influence on choice would not show subjective-pleasantness modulation of value-based selection; the review documents that they do.

entries.confidence_rationale: Single-unit recording in ventral pallidum (VP) showing that the SAME neurons encode hedonic value (taste palatability) and incentive salience (cue-evoked motivational firing), and that these two codes are dynamically linked: the hedonic firing pattern at receipt is what causes the cue-evoked wanting pattern to track current physiological state (sodium-depleted vs sated). This is among the cleanest direct electrophysiological evidence that liking provides the input signal that lets a wanting-coding circuit appropriately gate cue-driven approach -- which is the structural claim of MECH-295. Confidence 0.82: high-quality single-unit data, direct mechanistic mapping (palatability shift => cue-firing shift), but the experiment uses a homeostatic-shift paradigm (sodium depletion) rather than a hedonic-blockade paradigm, so the necessity is shown by drive-state-dependent palatability gating wanting, not by direct liking ablation.
failure_signatures: If liking and wanting were generated by entirely separate neural populations, VP units that fire to palatability at receipt should not also be the units that fire to predictive cues; Smith 2011 shows they are.

If drive amplification (sodium depletion) drove approach directly without routing through hedonic recoding, the cue-evoked VP firing pattern should change immediately on the deficit signal alone; the data show the cue firing pattern updates only after the reincoded palatability has been experienced.

Direct hunger-versus-predator behavioural toggling experiment with cell-type-specific manipulation in the LH-PMd-PAG-AgRP loop. PNAS-tier methods, large effect sizes, and a circuit-level mechanism that maps closely onto MECH-280's prediction: rising metabolic drive raises the effective freeze threshold so the agent transitions from threat-driven avoidance to active foraging. Mapping is one step removed (the substrate paper centres PMd-CCK and AgRP rather than LH-orexin specifically), so confidence is high but not maximal.
failure_signatures: If the freeze-to-foraging transition were a hard switch rather than a graded threshold, alpha_override could be replaced by a binary gate without behavioural cost; this paper documents graded transitions.

Predator presentation acutely inhibits AgRP neurons, so the override is not simply 'hunger wins' -- threat suppresses hunger signal upstream and the override has to overcome that competition. A naive MECH-280 implementation that ignores this competition will under-predict freeze persistence under acute (rather than sustained) threat.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct circuit evidence for an LH-to-pons GABAergic projection that engages food approach -- the existence proof for the active-coping override channel MECH-280 names. PNAS-tier cell-type-specific optogenetic dissection in mouse. Mapping is closer than de Araujo Salgado in the sense that LH is the named source, but farther in that the downstream target is peri-LC dorsal pons rather than PAG -- the projection biases active engagement rather than directly raising a freeze threshold.
failure_signatures: If the override channel were a single LH-to-PAG synapse, optogenetic LH-to-pons activation should leave PAG-mediated freezing intact; this paper documents that LH-to-pons activation by itself drives food approach, suggesting the active-coping override may operate via parallel routes (LH-to-pons for engagement, LH-to-PAG for threshold) rather than a single bottleneck.

The projection is GABAergic. If MECH-280 in REE is implemented as excitatory drive on theta_freeze, the sign of the underlying biology is opposite -- the override engages by disinhibition rather than by direct excitation.

entries.confidence_rationale: Identified-cell single-unit recordings in freely-moving rats covering the full sleep-wake-active behaviour cycle. Establishes the ~5x active/quiet recruitment ratio and the episode-scale firing kinetics that anchor MECH-280's sustained_threat_window and recruitment_threshold parameters. High-quality primary evidence with cell-identification controls.
failure_signatures: If orexin neurons fired episodically rather than tonically across behavioural states, MECH-280's sustained_threat_window EMA-style integration would be the wrong substrate; the recordings show sustained elevation across whole episodes of active waking, supporting an integration-window model.

Sensory-evoked transient activation is sub-second; if MECH-280's override_signal kinetics matched these transients, override authority would dissipate too quickly to produce sustained foraging-under-threat. The episode-scale carry-over the recordings document is what justifies the slow EMA decay (decay_rate = 0.05).

entries.confidence_rationale: Single-author Nature Reviews piece by the discoverer of orexin, characterising orexin neurons as intrinsically depolarised and recruited under high-effort / high-demand conditions, with downstream gain on PAG / locus coeruleus / VTA in the 1.3x-3x firing-rate band. Directly supports MECH-280's claim that orexin is the broadcast-override scalar driving recruitment under sustained metabolic demand and threat, and gives the alpha_override scalar an order-of-magnitude anchor.
failure_signatures: If orexin neurons fired uniformly across behavioural states, MECH-280's recruitment_threshold would have no biological referent; the review documents a ~5x active/quiet ratio which provides the threshold's biological grounding.

The 1.3x-3x downstream excitability gain is the order-of-magnitude anchor for alpha_override. If MECH-280's validation factorial sets alpha_override outside this band (e.g. 5x), the claim is going beyond what the biology supports.

entries.confidence_rationale: Comprehensive review of orexin's role in stress/panic states, including its bidirectional effect on PAG (panic-promoting in dorsolateral/dorsomedial PAG, escape-permissive in ventrolateral PAG). Supports the existence of an orexin-PAG modulatory channel and its recruitment under stress, but the bidirectionality is a real challenge to MECH-280's single-scalar formulation. Mixed direction reflects this -- the channel exists, but the sign depends on PAG subcolumn, which MECH-280 currently collapses.
failure_signatures: MECH-280 treats theta_freeze as a single scalar modulated by a single override gain. The orexin literature documents that orexin in dorsolateral/dorsomedial PAG promotes panic-class active responses while orexin in ventrolateral PAG is permissive of escape. Without PAG subcolumn substrate, MECH-280 cannot represent the panic-versus-goal-directed-active-coping distinction.

Orexin antagonists block panic-class responses without abolishing baseline freezing -- consistent with multiplicative gain on freeze threshold rather than a hard switch. This is supportive of the MECH-280 multiplicative formulation but argues for restricting the gain to specific PAG subregions rather than applying it uniformly.

Trends in Cognitive Sciences review of two decades of fMRI, lesion, intracranial recording, and effective-connectivity evidence on hierarchical control in lateral PFC. Distinct entry from the existing 2026-04-19 indexing (which tagged this paper for the PFC-subdivision-architecture question -- where rules go in lateral PFC). This entry addresses the orthogonal SD-033a A2 question: what training signal shapes the rule-bias projection? The review's most direct contribution to A2 is in Box 2 (corticostriatal gating), citing fMRI evidence that 'reward prediction errors related to learning a second order rule modulated fMRI activation in prePMd and a spatially proximate subregion of the caudate nucleus' -- i.e., RPE-driven training signal propagated through corticostriatal-thalamic loops, not through direct cortico-cortical credit assignment. The review's broader framing (separable frontal networks rather than a unitary controller) further constrains A2: a single-target training signal applied uniformly to a single bias head is an architectural mismatch; biology recruits multiple parallel networks each with its own learning dynamics. Confidence held at 0.74 because source quality is high (TiCS review, dual-author synthesis with strong methodological coverage) but the RPE-via-corticostriatal-loops finding is referenced rather than primary, and the network-separability framing does not uniquely identify SD-033a's A2 implementation choice -- it constrains the design space without selecting one option. Mixed direction reflects the dual reading: supports RPE-driven training (a specific A2 implementation choice) AND constrains the implementation away from a single uniform gradient (challenges any naive trained-head-with-one-target approach).
failure_signatures: Box 2's cited RPE-modulated prePMd/caudate finding is one fMRI study referenced within a broader review; if the underlying study has not been replicated cleanly across paradigms, the strength of the RPE-driven training-signal claim weakens. The review presents this as one piece of evidence in a converging picture, not as a settled finding.

The review's separable-networks framing argues against a unitary controller. If V3 implements SD-033a as a single trained head with a single target, this is a known biological mismatch -- biology likely uses multiple parallel networks with distinct learning rules. The review does not make the mismatch fatal (a unitary V3 head is a simplification, not a falsification of the architecture) but it does argue that any V3 implementation should be honest about the simplification.

The review focuses on hierarchical control and rostro-caudal abstraction in lateral frontal cortex as a whole, not on the specific question of how a projection from a rule-holding mid-DLPFC region to action-selection circuits is shaped by training. The transfer from 'corticostriatal loops mediate hierarchical control with RPE signals' to 'SD-033a's score_bias head should be trained by RPE' requires architectural inference beyond what the review directly tests.

The Outstanding Questions box explicitly flags 'How do learning and experience impact the hierarchical functional organization of the frontal lobes?' as an open question. The review does not claim to settle the training-signal question; it sketches the relevant evidence and identifies it as a future-research direction.

entries.confidence_rationale: Three-lab synthesis (Mansouri / Freedman / Buckley) at NRN, directly framed around 'dynamic emergence of abstract rules in primate cognition, and the distributed neural network that supports abstract rule formation, maintenance, revision, and task-dependent implementation.' The review is the strongest existing source for the position that rule representations are NOT innate -- they form during training and are shaped by experience. For SD-033a A2 specifically (on what training signal is the rule-bias projection shaped?), the review supports the trained-head alternative against the frozen-random landing -- biology grows the substrate, it does not start from a randomly-initialised projection that never updates. However, the review does NOT specify a unique training signal. It documents emergence under reinforcement learning paradigms, supervised category-judgement paradigms, and matching-rule paradigms with very different feedback structures, and notes that representational features (proportions, latencies, generalisation) vary across these training regimes. The mixed direction reflects this: clear support for trainable emergence, no commitment to which training signal SD-033a should use. Confidence held at 0.78 because the source quality is very high (NRN, three-lab review, directly on-topic) but the mapping to SD-033a's specific bias-projection-head architecture is moderate (the review describes lateral-PFC rule emergence at the population level, not the projection-onto-action-selection level that score_bias represents). The existing PFC-subdivision-architecture entry on this same paper (2026-04-19, MECH-261/ARC-035) covered the rule-substrate location question; this entry covers the orthogonal training-signal-emergence question and is appropriately tagged to SD-033a + MECH-262.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct primate PFC LFP + multi-unit recording during a working memory task. Authors (Lundqvist, Buschman, Miller at MIT Picower) show that PFC working memory is NOT sustained continuous spiking but rather brief, discrete bursts of narrow-band gamma (45-100 Hz) that vary in time and frequency, accompanying encoding and re-activation of remembered items. Beta oscillations (20-35 Hz) occur in brief bursts and reflect a default state interrupted by encoding/decoding -- they may gate access to and prevent sensory interference with working memory. For SD-033a A3 (persistence dynamics: gate-modulated EMA vs recurrent activity vs synaptic-hold), this is the strongest empirical challenge to the recurrent-spiking-persistence alternative: working memory representations are reactivated discretely, not held continuously. The implication for SD-033a is two-edged: (1) the 'continuously-active recurrent GRU' alternative is biologically suspect, and (2) the 'decay and refresh' functional character of an EMA is closer to the burst-and-refresh dynamic Lundqvist documents than continuous spiking is. However, the EMA does not capture the gamma/beta gating semantics, which Lundqvist argues are central. Confidence held at 0.78 because source quality is high (Neuron, primate electrophysiology, large sample) but the paper is one side of a still-contested empirical debate (Constantinidis et al. 2018 directly disputes the interpretation; see partner entry).
failure_signatures: If subsequent reanalysis or replication shows that the gamma bursts Lundqvist et al. report are an artefact of LFP sampling or trial alignment rather than a genuine working-memory mechanism, the empirical foundation for the discrete-burst alternative collapses and the recurrent-spiking-persistence view (Constantinidis et al. 2018) prevails. The dispute remains active.

The paper studies single-item working memory representations, not rule-selective persistence. Rule maintenance may use different dynamics from item memoranda. SD-033a's rule_state is conceptually closer to a maintained policy than a maintained item, so transfer from item-memory bursts to rule-bias persistence is non-trivial.

The gamma/beta gating mechanism Lundqvist proposes is more structured than SD-033a's EMA. The EMA captures 'decay and refresh' but not the explicit gamma-burst gating semantics; if those gating semantics turn out to be necessary for distractor-resistance (MECH-262 signature ii), the SD-033a EMA is an over-coarse abstraction.

Beta bursts in this paper reflect a 'default state' interrupted by encoding/decoding, which is conceptually adjacent to but not identical to the SalienceCoordinator write_gate('sd_033a') in V3. Mapping the biological gating onto V3's mode-conditioned gate is reasonable but not directly tested.

entries.confidence_rationale: Multi-author Journal of Neuroscience opinion / dual-perspective response paper authored by leading proponents of the persistent-activity view (Constantinidis at Wake Forest, Funahashi at Kyoto -- the Funahashi-Bruce-Goldman-Rakic 1989 line of work, Daeyeol Lee at Yale, Arnsten at Yale). Direct rebuttal to Lundqvist, Herman, & Miller's competing 'Delay Activity, Yes! Persistent Activity? Maybe Not' published in the same JNeurosci dual-perspective slot. The argument: persistent spiking activity generated in PFC during delay periods of working memory tasks represents information about stimuli held in memory and determines working memory performance. Alternative models depending only on rhythmicity of discharges (Lundqvist 2016) or exclusively on short-term synaptic plasticity (Mongillo 2008) are inconsistent with the neurophysiological data. For SD-033a A3: this paper argues that the recurrent-activity-persistence alternative is well-supported by primary neurophysiology and that the discrete-burst (Lundqvist 2016, partner entry) and synaptic-hold (Mongillo 2008, existing entry) alternatives both fail to capture necessary aspects of the data. This pushes the SD-033a review toward the GRU-recurrent alternative and away from the EMA landing, which functionally resembles short-term plasticity more than continuous spiking. Confidence held at 0.74 because the paper is an opinion / dual-perspective rebuttal (vs primary empirical evidence) and the seven authors are aligned with one side of an active dispute -- balanced reading requires both this and Lundqvist 2016.
failure_signatures: If the dual-perspective debate (Constantinidis et al. 2018 vs Lundqvist, Herman, Miller 2018) is later adjudicated decisively in favour of the discrete-burst interpretation (e.g. by direct causal manipulation showing that brief silencing of spiking does not collapse working memory), this paper's argument that 'persistent spiking is necessary and sufficient' weakens to 'persistent spiking is one component'. SD-033a A3 should not over-commit to the recurrent-spiking alternative on this paper alone.

The paper argues against short-term-plasticity-only models. SD-033a's EMA is functionally closer to short-term plasticity (silent synaptic facilitation in Mongillo 2008) than to continuous recurrent spiking. If Constantinidis et al. are correct that pure synaptic-plasticity models fail, the EMA inherits some of that critique -- it captures decay-and-refresh but lacks any continuous-spiking component.

Most of the cited evidence is from spatial working memory tasks (Funahashi-Bruce-Goldman-Rakic-style oculomotor delay tasks). Rule-selective persistence may use different dynamics than spatial item memory. The transfer from spatial-WM persistent spiking to rule-bias projection dynamics requires architectural inference beyond what the paper directly tests.

The seven-author lineup represents the persistent-spiking school of thought. The paper is a forceful summary of one position in a contested literature, not an adjudication. SD-033a A3 implementation choice should not rest on this paper alone.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality empirical paper combining macaque PFC single-unit recordings with a trained recurrent-network model that reproduces the population dynamics. The paper demonstrates that PFC implements context-dependent input selection at the population-dynamics level: the same physical sensory input is integrated toward choice when context flags it as task-relevant and is suppressed when context flags it as irrelevant. This is direct evidence that the rule/context signal is read out as input-selective gating rather than as a uniform multiplicative gain across all input or candidate dimensions, which is the closest empirical analogue available for the A1 landing in SD-033a. Held below 0.85 because the task is two-input integration, not multi-candidate trajectory selection -- the input-selection result generalises to candidate-selection only by analogy, not by direct mapping.
failure_signatures: The Mante 2013 result concerns selection among input dimensions (motion vs colour), not among multiple action candidates. If the bias projection in SD-033a operates on output candidates (trajectories) rather than input dimensions, the analogy from input-selective gating to per-candidate bias is one ARC of indirection -- and a uniform-gain readout is in principle still consistent with input-selective integration upstream.

The trained-RNN account argues that selection and integration are unified within a single dynamical process. If the V3 SD-033a abstraction (a static rule_state held in lateral PFC then projected via a single Linear layer) is too static to capture the dynamical-process-level selection mechanism Mante 2013 proposes, neither the A1 landing nor the A1 alternative may be the right level of description; SD-033a may be missing a recurrent gating component.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality empirical paper using time-resolved population pattern analyses on macaque PFC during a rule-conditional decision task. Direct evidence that the response to a choice stimulus diverges into different decision-related population states depending on the current rule -- i.e., the same stimulus drives stimulus-specific AND rule-specific evolution of the population code. This is the strongest available evidence that bias projection is rule-conditional at the candidate-state level rather than a uniform gain. Held below 0.85 because (a) the task uses 2 rules and a small candidate set, so the per-candidate-vs-uniform-gain question lives close to the ceiling of what 2x2 designs can resolve, and (b) the paper interprets the dynamics through a short-term-synaptic-plasticity lens, which is more relevant to the A3 question than to A1 directly.
failure_signatures: Stokes 2013 uses a 2-rule, small-candidate-set design. With only 2 rules and a limited stimulus set, the rule-conditional divergence in choice-state could be implemented either by per-candidate weighting OR by a uniform gain that interacts with stimulus-specific dynamics already present in PFC -- the experimental design does not strictly discriminate.

The paper's interpretation centres on short-term synaptic plasticity as the mechanism for highly flexible tuning. If that interpretation is correct, the SD-033a static-bias-head abstraction (whether per-candidate or uniform) is missing the synaptic-plasticity component entirely, and the A1 question may be misposed at the level SD-033a operates.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality empirical paper (Nature 2001, single-unit recordings in macaque lateral PFC during a same/different rule task). Directly relevant to SD-033a's rule_state representation: a substantial fraction of PFC neurons coded the abstract rule independent of stimulus identity. For A1 specifically, however, the evidence is mixed. Rule-selective single units demonstrate that distinct rule states produce distinct PFC activity patterns (which is necessary for any rule-conditional bias projection, per-candidate or uniform), but the paper does not measure how that rule signal is read out by downstream choice circuits -- so it cannot discriminate between a rule-modulated uniform gain and a rule-modulated per-candidate weighting at the projection step. Held below 0.8 because the projection granularity question is one ARC removed from what was actually recorded.
failure_signatures: Rule-selective single units in PFC are necessary but not sufficient evidence for the per-candidate bias landing of SD-033a. If downstream readout treats the population rule signal as a single scalar (e.g. via low-rank projection onto a one-dimensional rule axis), the same single-unit data would be compatible with the uniform-gain alternative.

Wallis 2001 measured rule coding during a same/different decision with two abstract rules; SD-033a's bias projection question concerns multi-candidate trajectory selection in E3. The paper does not exercise the multi-candidate regime, so its evidence on per-candidate vs uniform-gain projection is at best indirect.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational behavioural paper (six experiments, J Exp Psychol Gen 2000) establishing backward inhibition: when an abstractly-defined task set is intentionally abandoned, returning to it within a short window produces measurable response-time costs. The effect (a) survives a control for negative priming (Experiment 2), (b) is tied to top-down sequential control (Experiment 3), (c) accounts for residual shift costs (Experiment 4), and (d) occurs even with preplanned task sequences (Experiment 5). This is the most direct empirical analogue available for the SD-034 closure operator's 'temporary No-Go on the just-completed rule_state' specification: there is a real, measurable, behaviourally-defined refractory period on re-entry to a recently-abandoned task set in healthy humans. Held below 0.9 because (a) the effect is RT-cost-level rather than a hard No-Go gate, and (b) the mapping from 'abandoned task set' to 'completed rule_state' is conceptually adjacent but not strictly identical -- closure on satisfaction (SD-034) is not the same operation as forced abandonment (Mayr & Keele).
failure_signatures: Backward inhibition is a graded RT cost, not a hard No-Go. If SD-034 implements closure as a hard refractory gate (binary admit/reject on the just-completed rule_state for N ticks), the biological signature is more accurately a temporarily lowered admission probability rather than a strict block. A hard-gate implementation would over-specify what the biology actually does.

Mayr & Keele's experiments use forced/intentional task abandonment (the cue switches the task), not closure-on-satisfaction. SD-034's closure operator is supposed to fire when the agent detects that a committed rule_state has been satisfied by its own behaviour. The mechanism that produces refractoriness on intentional abandonment may or may not generalise to closure-driven release; this is a transfer-risk flag.

The paper does not localise the inhibitory mechanism to OFC/ACC. If the backward-inhibition signature originates in basal ganglia or supplementary motor cortex rather than in PFC/ACC sequence-completion machinery, the SD-034 architectural commitment to OFC/ACC-located closure may be misplaced even though the No-Go signature is supported.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong empirical paper combining single-unit recording in rat sensorimotor striatum and infralimbic cortex with selective optogenetic disruption (Neuron 2013, Graybiel lab). The headline finding is that habit crystallization requires *both* a striatal action-bracketing pattern (start-spike + stop-spike framing the routine, insensitive to reward devaluation) and a separately-developing infralimbic ensemble that closely tracks habit state, with optogenetic disruption of infralimbic activity preventing habit formation. For SD-034 closure operator, the start/stop-bracketing pattern is the closest direct neural analogue of the 'detect committed sequence completion' function, complementing Barnes 2011 (advance-cued action-boundary patterns) by showing that the same bracketing structure spans purposeful->habitual transitions. Held below 0.85 because (a) bracketing is detected at action-routine boundaries rather than at rule_state satisfaction specifically, and (b) the OFC/ACC-located closure SD-034 commits to is not the structure recorded here.
failure_signatures: The dual operator framework localises completion-detection to sensorimotor striatum + infralimbic cortex, not OFC/ACC. SD-034 names OFC/ACC sequence-completion cells as the substrate (Schuck 2016 / Rich & Shapiro 2009 in the existing entries). If the closure operator is anatomically distributed across striatum + IL + OFC/ACC, SD-034 may need to elevate from a single-substrate commitment to a multi-region operator -- and the V3 implementation would then need to decide which substrate carries the canonical 'done' token.

The bracketing pattern in Smith & Graybiel 2013 is for *habitual* routines (overtrained, devaluation-insensitive). SD-034's closure operator is meant to fire on rule_state satisfaction in flexible / planned mode as well -- not just for crystallised habits. If the bracketing mechanism is specific to the habitual mode, the support generalises only to one of the operating modes SD-034 needs to handle, and the planned-mode closure mechanism remains unspecified.

Optogenetic disruption of IL activity prevents habit *formation*, not necessarily habit *closure / release*. The dual operator paper does not directly test what happens when an infralimbic ensemble that has crystallised around a habit needs to release commitment on satisfaction. The closure-as-release function is one ARC removed from what was tested.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational computational paper (Psychological Review 2014) developing the OPAL model of striatal direct (D1) and indirect (D2) pathway opponent dynamics. The model formalises how the same dopaminergic state (tonic + phasic) produces asymmetric effects on Go-pathway (D1) and NoGo-pathway (D2) actor representations, generating bistable choice dynamics. For MECH-266's commitment to asymmetric hysteresis, OPAL is direct architectural support: the same neuromodulator level produces different effects on enter vs exit because enter-mode-A and exit-mode-A involve different actors with opposite dopamine sensitivities. Note: this paper is also cited under SD-034 (closure operator / OPAL); the framing here is specifically MECH-266's hysteresis question rather than SD-034's release-and-No-Go question. Held below 0.85 because the model is RL-actor-level and does not directly map onto SD-033's operating_mode register at the architectural-mode level.
failure_signatures: OPAL is an RL-actor-level model: D1/D2 dynamics operate on action representations during learning, not on operating-mode registers per se. The mapping from 'D1/D2 opponent dynamics produce bistability in actor preferences' to 'asymmetric hysteresis in mode-state' is by analogy across levels of description. If the operating_mode register lives at a different architectural level (e.g. global state shared across actions), the OPAL mechanism may not transfer directly.

The asymmetry in OPAL is between Go and NoGo pathways for a *single action*, not between enter and exit thresholds for a *single mode*. MECH-266 specifies enter vs exit thresholds on the same operating mode -- a different decomposition. The two are computationally related (both produce bistable dynamics under DA modulation) but mathematically distinct.

OPAL focuses on the learning dynamics. The hysteresis MECH-266 cares about is at the decision/control timescale, not the learning timescale. If the decision-level mode-state hysteresis is implemented differently from the learning-level D1/D2 opponent dynamics (e.g. via a different cellular or circuit mechanism), the OPAL architecture may be supportive only at the metaphor level rather than at the implementation level.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality review (Neuroscientist 2008) by Roshan Cools on the paradoxical role of dopamine in motivational and cognitive control. Synthesises evidence that the same dopaminergic manipulation produces opposite effects depending on baseline state (the inverted-U / sweet-spot framing), and that distinct dopaminergic systems (mesolimbic, mesocortical, nigrostriatal) have dissociable roles. For MECH-266 (asymmetric mode hysteresis: distinct enter vs exit thresholds per operating mode), the paper supports the architectural commitment that mode transitions are not symmetric -- the same DA level produces different transition probabilities depending on which mode the system is currently in, and the relevant DA target depends on the cognitive function. Held below 0.8 because the paper is a review rather than a specific test of asymmetric thresholds, and the mapping from 'baseline-dependent paradoxical DA effects' to 'asymmetric Schmitt-trigger thresholds per mode' is one ARC of indirection.
failure_signatures: Cools 2008 frames the DA-effect dependence on baseline state primarily in terms of inverted-U dose-response curves, not in terms of explicit Schmitt-trigger threshold asymmetry. If the underlying mechanism is purely a smooth inverted-U sensitivity curve rather than a hysteretic two-threshold gate, MECH-266's specific commitment to enter-vs-exit threshold asymmetry may be over-specified relative to what the review supports.

The dissociation across mesolimbic/mesocortical/nigrostriatal DA systems means MECH-266's 'mode' may need to be elaborated into multiple parallel mode registers per substrate, rather than a single global operating_mode. SD-032a SalienceCoordinator currently holds a single mode -- this paper flags that biology may require per-substrate mode tracking.

Individual-difference effects in Cools 2008 (some individuals benefit, some are impaired by the same dopaminergic drug) imply that MECH-266's threshold parameters may be subject-specific rather than population-canonical. SD-033 / MECH-266 V3 implementation that fixes thresholds at population means may miss the substantial individual variation the biology shows.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational computational paper (Nat Neurosci 2018) developing the prioritized-memory-access account of hippocampal replay. The model formalises replay content as a function of two utility components -- need (probability of visiting a state in the near future) and gain (the expected improvement in future choice from updating that state's value) -- and unifies seemingly disparate replay phenomena (planning, learning, consolidation) under a single normative account in which replay content is conditioned on the agent's current goals and behavioural context. For MECH-267 (HippocampalModule.propose_trajectories conditioned on operating_mode in addition to world_state), this is direct architectural support: the same hippocampal substrate produces different proposal content depending on the current task / behavioural context. Held below 0.9 because the model is normative-computational rather than directly mechanistic, and the mapping from 'replay content varies with goals' to 'trajectory proposal conditioned on operating_mode' is one ARC of indirection (operating_mode is a mode-state-level variable; goal/need/gain are task-state-level variables).
failure_signatures: Mattar & Daw frame conditioning of replay content in terms of need and gain -- both task-state-level / value-level variables, not mode-state-level variables. MECH-267 specifies conditioning on operating_mode (an architectural-mode signal from SD-032a SalienceCoordinator). If the biological mechanism conditions only on task-state variables and not on operating-mode-level variables, MECH-267 may need to elaborate to specify which mode-relevant signals enter the hippocampal proposal mechanism.

The paper is normative-computational: it predicts what replay content *should* be if the brain optimises future decision quality. The strict empirical claim that hippocampus *implements* this prioritization is supported but not fully demonstrated -- alternative substrates (PFC, cortico-hippocampal interactions) could also realise the optimisation. If hippocampus is one component of a distributed proposal-generation system, MECH-267's substrate commitment may be too narrow.

The model assumes a value function over states. Goal-conditioning enters through the value function (need depends on the current task's reward distribution). MECH-267 may need to specify how operating_mode modulates the value function consulted by HippocampalModule.propose_trajectories rather than parameterising mode-conditioning as a separate input.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong empirical paper (Nat Neurosci 2015, Redish lab) recording hippocampal theta sequences in rats during a value-guided decision-making task. The headline finding is that the look-ahead distance of theta-cycle place-cell sequences scales with the distance to the current goal: longer look-ahead on journeys to distant goals than on journeys to proximal goals, with sequence content predictive of the animal's destination. Look-ahead becomes uniform on goal arrival regardless of starting location. This is direct empirical evidence that the within-cycle hippocampal trajectory representation is conditioned on the agent's current goal -- precisely the within-mode conditioning MECH-267 specifies. Held below 0.9 because the paper measures goal-conditioning at the within-replay-cycle scale (theta sequences), not at the proposal-content / candidate-trajectory level the V3 HippocampalModule operates on, and the conditioning signal in this study is goal-distance rather than operating-mode per se.
failure_signatures: Theta sequences are within-cycle hippocampal phenomena, ~120ms timescale. The V3 HippocampalModule.propose_trajectories operates at the trial-level proposal-generation scale. If the goal-conditioning observed at the theta-sequence scale does not aggregate to a corresponding shift at the trial-level proposal scale, the support is at the wrong timescale for MECH-267's V3 spec.

The conditioning signal in Wikenheiser & Redish is goal *distance*, not operating *mode*. These are related (mode-state changes typically alter goal hierarchies which alter goal-distance representations) but distinct. The paper supports goal-conditioning of hippocampal sequences but does not directly support mode-conditioning -- the same animal may be running with the same operating-mode but different goal-distances.

The task is spatial navigation in rats. Generalising from rat goal-conditioned theta sequences to REE's goal-conditioned trajectory proposals over a more abstract action space requires a transfer step: the structure-of-content analogy (the hippocampus represents what comes next, conditioned on what it is trying to achieve) holds, but the implementation specifics may not.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong empirical paper (Neuron 2008, Procyk lab) recording single-unit and high-gamma LFP activity in macaque ACC during a task that alternates exploration and exploitation periods. The headline finding for MECH-268 is that ACC neurons produce specific signals at the *first reward* (the end of exploration / commitment to exploitation), and that *those signals disappear in subsequent identical-outcome trials within the exploitation period*. This is the single most direct empirical demonstration of dACC signal saturation under repeated identical outcomes available in the primate literature. The signals re-appear at trial initiation (a transfer comparable to dopaminergic-neuron learning phenomena), indicating that the saturation operates on the outcome-evaluation channel specifically. Held below 0.9 because the saturation is observed in the context of exploration->exploitation transitions rather than as a general fact about repeated outcomes, and the specific signal that saturates may not be exactly the 'pe' channel MECH-268 specifies.
failure_signatures: The saturation in Quilodran et al is observed during exploitation periods following a discovered reward source. If MECH-268's saturation is meant to apply to all repeated identical outcomes regardless of behavioural context (e.g. during habit-mode behaviour where the same neutral outcome repeats), the support generalises only by extension. Whether the same saturation mechanism operates outside the exploration->exploitation transition context is empirically untested.

The signal that disappears in exploitation is described as 'specific to the first reward / end of exploration', which is closer to a phasic surprise / commitment signal than a tonic prediction-error signal. MECH-268 specifies saturation on the dACC `pe` signal. If the empirically-saturating signal is instead the surprise / commitment signal, MECH-268's V3 implementation that habituates the pe channel may be targeting the wrong signal type.

The transfer of signal from outcome-time to trial-initiation in exploitation periods is reminiscent of dopaminergic learning phenomena (cue-anticipation transfer). This raises a possible alternative explanation: the saturation may not be a habituation but rather a temporal-shift of the signal to an earlier predictive cue. If so, MECH-268's implementation as habituation-under-repetition would be incorrect even though the surface behavioural signature looks the same.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational fMRI paper (Nat Neurosci 2007, Behrens / Rushworth) demonstrating that ACC signal weight on each new outcome scales with the optimal Bayesian estimate of environmental volatility. Under low volatility (stable / predictable / repeated outcomes), the ACC signal weight diminishes; under high volatility (changing reward contingencies), the signal weight increases. Across the population, individual variation in ACC activity correlates with individual learning rate. This is direct empirical evidence for MECH-268's commitment that dACC conflict / prediction-error signals saturate under repeated identical outcomes -- the saturation here being the volatility-modulated downweighting under stable outcome statistics. Held below 0.9 because the paper measures fMRI BOLD rather than single-unit activity, the saturation framing is volatility-modulated rather than a strict cap, and the relevant ACC signal is a learning-rate adapter rather than a 'pe' signal in the strict sense.
failure_signatures: The saturation here is implemented as a Bayesian learning-rate adapter (signal weight scales inversely with stability) rather than as a strict habituation cap. If MECH-268 specifies a hard saturation cap on the dACC pe signal under repetition, the volatility-adaptive downweighting Behrens 2007 demonstrates is a softer mechanism. The two would produce similar behavioural signatures under most repetition regimes but diverge under (a) sudden change after long stable runs and (b) outcomes that are noisy but unchanging in central tendency.

Behrens et al measure fMRI BOLD signal in ACC, which aggregates across multiple cell types and signal kinds. The paper's central finding is consistent with MECH-268 but does not localise the saturation mechanism to specific cell populations or specific signals (pe, conflict, surprise, attention-for-learning). MECH-268's V3 implementation that places saturation specifically on the dACC pe signal is one resolution step finer than what Behrens demonstrates.

The paper is correlational on the saturation-vs-learning-rate axis: ACC activity correlates with optimal volatility estimate, and ACC variation predicts learning rate variation. Causal manipulation (lesion / stimulation) is not provided. If ACC saturation is a downstream readout of an upstream saturation mechanism elsewhere, the dACC localisation in MECH-268 may be a measurement artefact rather than a localisation claim.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational fMRI paper (Neuron 2009, Behrens / Rushworth lab) demonstrating that frontopolar cortex tracks the relative advantage of switching to a foregone alternative when choices are made voluntarily, while ventromedial PFC encodes the value of the current decision. This is direct support for MECH-264 (counterfactual-value tracking by the FPC analog): FPC carries the running estimate of unchosen-option value relative to chosen, with FPC functional connectivity changing at the moment of switching. Interindividual variation in FPC signal predicts behavioural switch propensity. Pairwise chosen-vs-alternative computation (not K>=2-way as MECH-265 specifies) -- this paper supports MECH-264 cleanly and MECH-265 only partially. Held below 0.9 because the paper measures BOLD rather than single-unit and the chosen-alternative pairwise structure does not directly demonstrate K>=2-way set-monitoring.
failure_signatures: Boorman 2009 implements counterfactual evaluation as pairwise chosen-vs-single-alternative. MECH-265 specifies K>=2 alternatives as a set. The FPC signal in this paper does not directly speak to K>=2-way monitoring; whether the same substrate scales is empirically open.

The vmPFC vs FPC functional dissociation (vmPFC = current, FPC = counterfactual) is correlational. If the dissociation is task-design-specific (the paper uses a 4-option voluntary-switch bandit), generalisation to other counterfactual-monitoring contexts is not strict.

FPC-vmPFC functional connectivity changes are timed at switching. If the BOLD signature is a switch-execution signal rather than a counterfactual-evaluation signal, MECH-264's commitment to counterfactual *tracking* (continuous) versus counterfactual *triggering* (phasic) would be empirically underdetermined.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong empirical paper (PNAS 2015) reporting bilateral selective lesion to frontal pole cortex (FPC) in macaques tested on a Wisconsin Card Sorting Test analog and related tasks. Critically, the paper provides a *causal* lesion phenotype rather than correlational fMRI: FPC-lesioned monkeys show a specific, dissociable phenotype -- (a) no impairment in following rule switches within WCST, (b) augmented post-conflict cognitive control adjustment, (c) BETTER memory for relevant rule across distractions, but the authors propose FPC's primary role is *disengaging* executive control from current task and redistributing it to novel sources of reward. This is direct causal support for the architectural commitment that FPC operates as a 'disengage-and-explore' module rather than as a current-task executive control module. Held below 0.9 because the lesion phenotype is complex (paradoxically improved on some measures) and the interpretation as 'disengagement' is theoretical rather than directly measured.
failure_signatures: The FPC lesion produced a paradoxical improvement on distractor-resistance: lesioned animals were BETTER at remembering the relevant rule across distractions. If SD-033e's FPC analog is supposed to support current-task focus, the lesion phenotype directly contradicts that role. The disengagement interpretation reconciles this -- FPC normally redirects executive control AWAY from the current task -- but it implies the FPC analog should NOT be tightly coupled to current-task focus.

FPC and PCC are studied together but show different effects. The PCC lesion is uninformative for SD-033e specifically. If SD-033e's commitment is too tightly bound to FPC alone, the broader rostral-network architecture may be missed.

The interpretation as 'disengagement and exploration' is post-hoc theoretical synthesis rather than direct empirical measurement. Alternative interpretations (e.g., FPC as a generic conflict / novelty detector with explore/exploit-orienting downstream effects) are not strictly excluded.

entries.confidence_rationale: Major Nature Reviews Neuroscience review (2017) by Mansouri, Koechlin, Rosa & Buckley synthesising primate FPC physiology, lesion, and human imaging evidence. The central thesis is that FPC's role is monitoring the significance of *current and alternative goals*, with humans further specialising in *parallel monitoring of multiple goals*. This is the strongest direct architectural support for MECH-265 (relative-importance monitoring across competing goals): the review explicitly argues that primate FPC monitors competing goal hierarchies in parallel, with the human elaboration enabling the simultaneous tracking that distinguishes human cognition from non-human primates. Held below 0.9 because the review is synthesis rather than primary data, and the human-vs-non-human-primate distinction creates transfer risk for REE which is computational, not biological.
failure_signatures: The review's central thesis (parallel monitoring of multiple goals as a uniquely human FPC specialisation) means MECH-265 may be specifying a function that requires more architectural elaboration than V3 supports. If the parallel-monitoring component is the human-specific elaboration of a more basic FPC role, V3 SD-033e may inherit only the basic role.

The review draws together findings that disagree on functional specialisation of FPC subregions (medial vs lateral, BA 10 vs BA 9). The integrative synthesis the review proposes is theoretical rather than empirically resolved; SD-033e should not lock to any particular subregional decomposition.

The argument that FPC enables uniquely human cognition is not directly testable. SD-033e's V3 implementation that adds an FPC analog to a non-biological agent is implicitly committing to the claim that the relevant computational function (parallel goal monitoring) can be implemented even without the human-evolutionary-specific cytoarchitecture. Whether this transfer is principled is open.
