entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational theoretical review (Trends Cogn Sci 2007) presenting the gateway hypothesis: rostral PFC (BA 10) supports mechanisms that switch attention between environmental stimuli (external) and self-generated / maintained representations (internal). Medial BA 10 favours external engagement; lateral BA 10 favours internal cognition. For SD-033e this provides the architectural foundation: the FPC analog should switch between externally-driven (current task / environmental) and internally-driven (counterfactual / planning) modes of operation. Held below 0.8 because the paper is theoretical / synthesis rather than a specific test, and the medial-vs-lateral mapping onto MECH-261 operating_mode is by analogy.
failure_signatures: The gateway hypothesis specifies a continuous-modulatory mechanism (attention switching between external and internal) rather than a discrete-switching mechanism. SD-033e's V3 implementation question (how does the FPC analog enter / exit different operating modes) is one ARC removed from what Burgess 2007 specifies.

Medial vs lateral BA 10 dissociation has been challenged by subsequent work (e.g. Mansouri 2017 review) that emphasises a more graded functional specialisation. SD-033e shouldn't lock implementation to a strict medial/lateral split.
The paper draws heavily on neuropsychological case studies and fMRI of multitasking. Generalisation to REE's operating-mode architecture is by structural analogy.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational theoretical paper (Trends Cogn Sci 2007) proposing an information-theoretical account of executive control in lateral PFC, with hierarchically-ordered control signals organised along the anterior-posterior axis. Posterior PFC handles sensorimotor mappings; rostral PFC handles increasingly abstract / branching / nested control. For SD-033e this provides the architectural framing in which the FPC analog sits at the rostral end of the executive-control gradient -- at the most abstract / branching / counterfactual level. Held below 0.8 because the framework is theoretical / synthesis rather than a specific empirical test, the gradient is one organising principle among several (Badre & Nee 2018 challenge / refine the strict A-P gradient), and the mapping from Koechlin's information-theoretical control levels to MECH-264/265 / SD-033e operating modes is by structural analogy.
failure_signatures: The strict A-P gradient framing has been challenged by subsequent work (Badre & Nee 2018) which argues for a more graded / integrated organisation. SD-033e should not lock to a strict A-P localisation as if it were decided.

The information-theoretical framework specifies hierarchically-ordered control signals but does not directly address counterfactual evaluation or competing-goal monitoring. MECH-264 and MECH-265 are specific architectural commitments that this paper supports only at the framework level.

The gradient is described as continuous; SD-033e's operating-mode commitment is discrete. The mapping requires the assumption that operating modes correspond to discrete bins of an underlying continuous gradient -- a workable simplification, not a derived prediction.

entries.confidence_rationale: Replicates and extends the error-likelihood account: ACC encodes error likelihood and predicted error magnitude (the product = expected risk). Supports the framing that dACC operates as a downstream consumer of upstream predicted-state estimates -- if those estimates are wrong, dACC has nothing legitimate to weight by. Older fMRI study, indirect for the V_s/MECH-269b mechanism specifically; included as a foundational anchor rather than a strong test.
failure_signatures: ACC's behavioural-control signal is a function of upstream predicted error likelihood and magnitude; if those upstream predictions are stale or non-credibly anchored, the ACC signal will track the stale prediction faithfully and produce no behavioural revision -- consistent with Q-040's wired-but-inert hypothesis.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong single-unit evidence from macaque dACC that surprise/unsigned-RPE responses drive trial-to-trial behavioural adjustment, AND that these responses collapse when upstream probability estimates are hidden -- directly supporting the architectural reading of Q-040 that dACC behavioural-revision is contingent on credible upstream predictions. Mapping is solid for the SD-032b adaptive-control consumer mechanism, but transfer from RPE-clarity (probabilities hidden) to V_s-anchored forward predictions is an extrapolation, not a measurement. Indirect for the specific MECH-269b prediction.
failure_signatures: When upstream probability cues are absent or unclear, dACC neuronal responses to outcomes are reduced and the corresponding behavioural-adjustment signature attenuates -- the SD-032b control loop is wired but its drive collapses without a credible upstream estimate.

entries.confidence_rationale: Causal microstimulation evidence in macaque ACC under varying feature-uncertainty conditions, plus single-unit recordings showing ACC neurons track error history more strongly under uncertainty. ACC stim impaired the 'optimizing exploration and use of prediction errors to reduce uncertainty' specifically under high feature uncertainty, which is the closest available analogue to the V_s-uncertainty regime Q-040 proposes. Mapping is good for the SD-032b adaptive-control consumer; the upstream V_s mechanism is not directly probed.
failure_signatures: ACC microstimulation under high feature uncertainty disrupts adaptive RL by impairing the use of prediction errors to reduce uncertainty -- consistent with Q-040's prediction that dACC behavioural revision is uncertainty-modulated and breaks down when upstream uncertainty handling is disrupted.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct causal disconnection evidence: contralateral OFC + ventral hippocampus lesion impairs reversal learning despite each region individually intact, while neither unilateral lesion alone produces the deficit. This is the cleanest available analogue in the literature for the wired-but-inert architectural pattern Q-040 articulates. Mapping is good (hippocampus -> OFC pathway is functionally analogous to V_s-anchored upstream -> downstream forward-model/decision consumer); transfer risk is moderate (rodent spatial reversal -> REE harm-navigation, OFC -> dACC).
failure_signatures: OFC and ventral hippocampus each remain individually functional after unilateral lesion, but contralateral disconnection of the two impairs reversal learning -- the downstream decision/error machinery cannot drive behavioural revision when the upstream-to-downstream state pathway is broken, which is the architectural pattern Q-040 predicts for V_s gating restricted to the proposer.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct lesion-based causal evidence in the canonical orexin-KO narcolepsy model. Bilateral amygdala lesions sharply reduce emotion-triggered cataplexy without disturbing baseline sleep-wake architecture. Anterograde/retrograde tracing maps the projection (CeA GABAergic neurons -> vlPAG, LPT, LC, DRN) -- exactly the brainstem motor-tone targets MECH-281 names. Mapping fidelity to the motor-coupling axis is high; transfer risk from mouse to a generic REE coupling claim is moderate.
failure_signatures: If amygdala (specifically CeA GABAergic) projections to brainstem motor-tone nuclei are intact, emotion-triggered loss of motor activation (cataplexy-analog) persists in orexin-deficient animals -- consistent with MECH-281's prediction that the motor-coupling failure runs through amygdala arbitration rather than through z_harm computation itself.

Lesioning amygdala does not abolish baseline sleep-wake structure -- so a model that conflates the wake-stability axis (MECH-286) with the motor-coupling axis (MECH-281) would over-predict the lesion effect.

entries.confidence_rationale: Recent (2023) review consolidating CeA / BLA / BNST contributions to cataplexy with explicit framing of emotion -> motor-coupling failure under orexin loss. Lower than Burgess because it is a review rather than primary data, but the mapping to MECH-281's specific claim (BLA/CeA as a canonical downstream target of override_signal) is unusually clean -- this is the framework Sardar et al. propose.
failure_signatures: If CeA, BLA, and BNST contributions to cataplexy are dissociable (e.g., CeA-only lesion replicates the full effect), then MECH-281 may be over-specified by naming the entire amygdala complex; the relevant gain target would be narrower.
The Sardar review notes residual gaps: human functional imaging in cataplexy is sparse, so primate-level confirmation of the rodent circuit remains pending.

entries.confidence_rationale: Recent (2023) single-author review consolidating the multi-target orexinergic gain framework: orexin modulates monoaminergic/cholinergic systems, brainstem REM-atonia generators, and limbic emotion-processing circuits. Directly relevant framing for MECH-281's claim that orexin gates coupling at multiple downstream sites. Confidence is moderate because it is a review and a single-author one rather than primary data.
failure_signatures: If orexin's anticataplectic effect can be fully reproduced by manipulation at a single downstream site (e.g., amygdala alone), MECH-281's multi-target framing is over-specified.

The Koyama review notes that the relative contribution of monoaminergic vs cholinergic vs limbic targets is still debated -- if future work cleanly dissociates them, the architectural commitment to BLA/CeA arbitration as the canonical motor-coupling target may need refinement.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct optogenetic and chemogenetic causal evidence in mouse narcolepsy model. Identifies the DRN-serotonin -> amygdala projection as the route through which orexin's anticataplectic effect propagates. Strongly relevant to MECH-281 and to the cross-link with the 5-HT goal-pipeline gain cluster (MECH-186/187/188). Mapping fidelity is high; transfer risk is the standard rodent-to-architecture concern.
failure_signatures: Optogenetic inhibition of DRN-5HT terminals in the amygdala blocks the anticataplectic effect of orexin signaling -- so a model that locates the entire override authority in orexin alone (without 5-HT mediation) is incomplete.

Chemogenetic activation of amygdala increased cataplexy; chemogenetic inhibition decreased it -- the amygdala output gain is causally bidirectional, consistent with MECH-281's prediction that the override scales rather than silences.

entries.confidence_rationale: Within-paradigm comparison of HPC vs OFC ensemble coding on the same task. Both regions carry task-state representations but with complementary emphases: OFC tracks current task position selectively (only behaviourally relevant distinctions), HPC supports prospective memory states. Supports MECH-263's framing of SD-033b as a behaviour-relevant cognitive map (rather than a complete enumeration of states), and clarifies the HPC/OFC division of labour for ree-v3's hippocampal + E2 architecture. Slightly lower confidence because the contribution to MECH-263 is more about characterising the substrate's selectivity than testing core falsifiability criteria.
failure_signatures: If OFC ensembles distinguished EVERY task state regardless of behavioural relevance, this would weaken MECH-263's specification that the cognitive map carries 'structural roles each state plays in the current task' -- since structural role is task-defined, not exhaustive. Zhou 2019b finds OFC selectively distinguishes behaviourally-relevant states, which is consistent.

If HPC and OFC carried identical task-state codes, MECH-263's separation of SD-033b (OFC structured outcomes) from hippocampal task representation would be ill-motivated. The complementarity finding supports the architectural separation.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct human-fMRI test of the devaluation-sensitivity criterion that MECH-263's falsifiability hinges on. Identity-specific reward patterns in lateral posterior OFC are selectively altered for the sated food but retained for the non-sated food, demonstrating that OFC encodes outcome IDENTITY rather than just scalar value, and that this representation is updated by changes in outcome value. Functional connectivity to vmPFC predicts behavioural choice -- supporting the SD-033b -> SD-033c handoff architecture.
failure_signatures: MECH-263 specifies devaluation-sensitivity as a key criterion: 'if the value of outcome o changes while the state-action -> outcome mapping does not, behaviour changes appropriately because the outcome representation itself is structured.' Howard & Kahnt provide exactly this evidence in humans.

MECH-263 also asserts a falsification criterion: 'if SD-033b activity encodes scalar value without discriminating between same-value / different-outcome-identity states... the OFC/vmPFC dissociation does not carry.' Howard & Kahnt rule this out for humans -- lateral posterior OFC encodes outcome identity that is dissociable from value.
Connectivity from OFC to vmPFC predicts behavioural choice -- a structural test of the SD-033b -> SD-033c information flow MECH-263 implies.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct empirical test of the OFC-as-cognitive-map-of-state-space hypothesis. Population decoding shows the vast majority of OFC neurons contribute to state representation, the rate of state-evidence integration predicts behavioural adaptation, and outcome predictions depend on accuracy of state representations. Maps cleanly onto MECH-263's two co-present framings (state-space map + outcome prediction). Single species (rat), single task (odour-guided block transitions); core finding generalises but quantitative parameters do not transfer to REE directly.
failure_signatures: If OFC encoded outcome predictions independently of state representations, MECH-263's claim that 'specific-outcome queries are resolved against the cognitive map' would be weakened. The Stalnaker 2021 finding that outcome-prediction quality covaries with state-representation accuracy directly supports the hierarchical relationship MECH-263 asserts.

If state representations were uniform across neurons (i.e. a small dedicated subpopulation rather than a distributed code), this would constrain the substrate model of SD-033b but not falsify MECH-263. Stalnaker reports that state coding is broadly distributed, consistent with SD-033b being an ensemble-level representation.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct neural test of MECH-263's central architectural commitment: that value and structured task representation co-exist in OFC as DISSOCIABLE components rather than as competing alternatives. The paper explicitly frames the value-vs-cognitive-map debate as a false dichotomy and demonstrates both components in the same ensembles. This is the strongest available evidence for MECH-263's 'co-present framings of the same substrate' formulation.
failure_signatures: If OFC ensembles encoded only value (a scalar) and not task structure, MECH-263's cognitive-map framing would collapse and SD-033b would reduce to SD-033c (scalar value). The paper rules this out: ensembles distinguish task positions of identical value.

If OFC ensembles encoded only task structure with no value signal, MECH-263's specific-outcome-prediction framing would be weakened. The paper rules this out too: a value signal is recoverable from the same ensembles.

The paper's central finding -- multiplexed but dissociable codes -- is exactly what MECH-263 predicts. A failure mode would be finding the two representations are inseparable (same neurons coding inseparable mixtures); the paper instead finds dissociable axes.

entries.confidence_rationale: Concise mechanistic review explicitly framing Hcrt as a neuromodulator that operates across both negative-valence (chronic stress, hyperarousal) and positive-valence (compulsive drug-seeking) dysregulated states. The bivalence is exactly the architectural commitment that distinguishes SD-037 from a simple threat-gating module: SD-037 commits to integrating drive+threat and outputting an override that can swing toward either threat-active coping or drive-active goal seeking. Source quality moderate-high (Curr Opin Neurobiol, de Lecea co-author). Mapping fidelity high at the architectural level. Confidence held at 0.74 because this is short-format review evidence rather than direct experimental measurement.
failure_signatures: If Hcrt acted only on threat or only on reward, SD-037's commitment that the override_signal integrates BOTH drive and threat context would be weakened. Giardino & de Lecea explicitly position Hcrt as bivalent across stress and reward pathways.

entries.confidence_rationale: Major review (J Intern Med, three established orexin investigators including de Lecea who co-discovered hypocretin) that explicitly characterises the orexin system in language that maps almost one-to-one onto SD-037: a hub that integrates diverse internal-state inputs (circadian, metabolic, emotional valence) and conveys arousal-modulating signals via widespread excitatory projections to multiple output regions. Source quality is very high; mapping fidelity is also high because the paper itself uses the integrator-and-broadcaster framing that SD-037 commits to. Confidence is held below 0.9 because the paper is a narrative review, not a quantitative test of REE's specific claim that the override REWEIGHTS rather than REPLACES downstream harm signals.
failure_signatures: If REE override_signal silenced rather than reweighted z_harm at downstream commit gates, this would diverge from Hcrt biology; Jacobson et al. emphasise that Hcrt acts as a gain modulator on downstream targets, not a relay that replaces their input.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct causal experiment (microinjection of orexin-A into NAc shell in rats) demonstrating that orexin amplifies both 'wanting' (motivated intake) at all NAc shell sites and 'liking' (hedonic orofacial reactions) at a specific rostral hotspot. This is a clean test of the bridge between an orexin signal and downstream drive->goal-seeding behaviour, which is the SD-037 commitment that the override authority gates the drive->z_goal seeding pathway. Source quality high (Neuropsychopharmacology, Berridge lab). Mapping fidelity moderate-high: the experiment manipulates orexin tone directly at a downstream consumer node (NAc shell), so the causal chain matches the SD-037 'override_signal reweights/permits goal-seeding' architecture. Confidence held below 0.85 because the paper measures hedonic and consummatory reactions, not the full SD-037 commit-gate reweighting of z_harm under simultaneous threat.
failure_signatures: If orexin tone in downstream consumers were neutral with respect to drive-driven goal seeking, SD-037's drive->goal seeding bridge would be unsupported. Castro et al. show the opposite: orexin causally amplifies motivated intake.

The hotspot/coldspot dissociation (rostral hedonic enhancement vs uniform 'wanting' enhancement) implies that override effects are not spatially uniform; SD-037's scalar override_signal is a simplification.

entries.confidence_rationale: Clinical review of PWS hyperphagia mechanism. Direction is MIXED because PWS supports SD-037's predicted SATURATED-OVERRIDE phenotype at the behavioural level (compulsive drive pursuit despite negative consequences) but the mechanistic story is genetic/upstream of orexin (paternal 15q11-q13 imprinting defect, hypothalamic dysfunction broader than orexin alone). PWS is therefore a phenotype anchor for SD-037 falsifiable secondary, not a mechanistic confirmation. Source quality moderate (J Endocrinol Invest review). Mapping fidelity moderate -- behaviour matches, mechanism does not exactly match.
failure_signatures: If PWS hyperphagia did NOT include the canonical features of failed satiety arbitration plus persistent drive pursuit despite negative outcomes, SD-037's saturated-override falsifiable would lose its clinical anchor.
PWS mechanism is clearly upstream of orexin alone -- multiple hypothalamic systems are disrupted -- so MIXED evidence direction reflects honest mechanistic mismatch.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational paper establishing that hippocampal sequences during sharp-wave ripples come in two distinct directional flavours: reverse (post-run, evaluative) and forward (pre-run, anticipatory). Provides the temporal structure MECH-057b relies on for completion as a discrete detectable event -- the run-end reverse-replay marks completion of the just-finished sequence. Mapping to MECH-057b is partial: the paper documents the post-completion evaluative pulse but does not test that this pulse acts as a candidacy gate. Marked mixed because it strongly supports the claim that completion is a detectable discrete event, but does not directly address suppression of non-completing candidates.
failure_signatures: If reverse and forward replay were not temporally bound to run-end and pre-run pause epochs, the framing of completion as a discrete event-marker would weaken.
If pre-run forward replay did not contain the upcoming trajectory, the candidacy framing would lack temporal anchoring.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct in-vivo demonstration that hippocampal place-cell sequences emit goal-biased trajectory candidates before goal-directed navigation. Mapping fidelity is high for MECH-057b's claim that hippocampal sequence completion (here: full goal-reaching trajectory generation) is what makes a candidate eligible for downstream selection. Source quality is exceptional (Nature, large rodent ensemble, novel start/goal pairs as a control). Transfer risk is moderate: rats in an open arena with a single goal type, and the read-out structure (BG / E3) is inferred rather than measured here.
failure_signatures: If only fragmentary sequences (not goal-reaching) appeared, MECH-057b's gate-on-completion framing would be weakened.
If sequence emission were equally biased on novel-start-and-novel-goal pairs that the animal had never solved, the inference that completion verification gates candidacy would be undermined.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct measurement of joint hippocampal-prefrontal replay during pause-then-decide epochs, showing that coordinated replay distinguishes correct future paths from alternatives -- which is the candidate-versus-discarded distinction MECH-057b is concerned with. Source quality is very high (Neuron, simultaneous HPC and PFC ensembles, longitudinal learning across the same animals). Mapping fidelity is good: the paper directly addresses the read-out structure (PFC) that MECH-057b implies must receive only promoted candidates.
failure_signatures: If PFC ensembles tracked all replayed paths equally regardless of correctness, the candidacy-gate framing would be weakened.
If learning never produced a forward-replay shift toward correct future paths, the proposal-promotion mechanism would lack a learning signature.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct evidence that hippocampal theta sequences modulate their look-ahead extent based on goal distance and on whether the animal is mid-journey vs at-goal. The on-arrival contraction of look-ahead is the strongest piece for MECH-057b's framing: when the goal is reached, candidate generation stops extending forward, consistent with a completion-detection mechanism gating further candidacy. Mapping fidelity is moderate -- the paper measures look-ahead extent, not explicit candidacy suppression -- but the convergence with Pfeiffer & Foster gives mutual reinforcement.
failure_signatures: If theta sequence look-ahead were invariant to goal distance, the candidacy-gate framing (proposals tuned to complete on the current goal) would be weakened.
If on-arrival look-ahead remained extended in the same way as during journeys, the gate would not appear to detect completion.

entries.confidence_rationale: SEP is the canonical philosophy reference (high source quality). Kant's perfect duties are the closest historical analogue to context-independent action requirements -- exactly Q-026's question form. But the mapping to REE is indirect: REE's five axioms (INV-025..029, INV-042) are not Kant's, and Kant's specific perfect duties (no lying, no suicide) do not derive from REE's axioms straightforwardly. Even Kant himself, per the entry, concedes that judgment is required for application -- weakening the very 'context-independent' force that Q-026 asks about. Useful for framing the question, not for answering it.
failure_signatures: Kant explicitly concedes that 'judgment is often required to determine how these duties apply to particular circumstances,' which means even on the strongest historical version of context-independent ethics, pure context-independence at the action level is not preserved.

Kant's perfect duties are derived from a contradiction-in-conception test on universalised maxims, not from the existence-of-self / existence-of-world / shared-world axioms that ground REE; the derivation routes are different and the conclusions may not coincide.

entries.confidence_rationale: SEP is canonical (high source quality). Ross's framework is the dominant modern alternative to Kantian absolutism, and it directly addresses the form of Q-026 by arguing that no action is context-independently required: prima facie duties are universal but actual duty is always settled comparatively in context. This is a substantive challenge to the very form of Q-026, so the relevance to the question is high even though the mapping to REE's specific axioms is indirect.
failure_signatures: Ross argues that determining one's actual duty in any concrete situation 'rests with perception' and yields only 'probable opinion, never certainty' -- which directly undermines any reading of Q-026 that expects a list of strictly required actions independent of context.

On Ross's view, an act's actual rightness 'belongs to it in virtue of its whole nature and of nothing less than this' -- meaning the complete contextual situation is non-eliminably part of what makes an action obligatory. Q-026's 'independent of context' clause is, on this reading, asking the wrong question.

entries.confidence_rationale: Selective lesion study (rat) dissociating anterior from posterior medial OFC and showing that anterior mOFC is specifically required for inferring action-dependent outcome representations when those outcomes are unobservable -- exactly the specific-outcome prediction function SD-033b framing (i) requires. Combines retrograde tracing (anterior mOFC has stronger projections to nucleus accumbens core) with functional lesion behaviour (PIT, devaluation, outcome-specific reinstatement). Strong direct test of the substrate function. Confidence reduced from 0.85 because (i) rat OFC mapping to primate/human OFC is imperfect and (ii) the dissociation is within mOFC rather than between OFC and adjacent vmPFC, so the paper speaks to substrate localisation more than to the OFC/vmPFC functional split SD-033b vs SD-033c assumes.
failure_signatures: If anterior and posterior mOFC lesions produced indistinguishable deficits on outcome-specific reinstatement, the proposed functional dissociation would collapse and the substrate-localisation claim would weaken.
If the action-outcome inference deficit in anterior mOFC lesions could be reproduced by lesions outside mOFC, the substrate-specific-outcome-prediction mapping would lose its specificity.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct human fMRI test of the Wilson/Niv 2014 hypothesis. Multivariate pattern classification decodes 16 task states from OFC activity, including states that are unobservable from sensory input. Decoding accuracy correlates with behavioural performance and predicts individual errors. This is the strongest single empirical test in humans that the OFC-analog holds a structured state-space representation, which is exactly what SD-033b framing (ii) requires. Confidence high; reduced from 0.9 because fMRI MVPA infers representational content rather than directly reading neural code, and the 16-state task structure is a specific paradigm whose generalisation to richer task spaces is empirically open.
failure_signatures: If OFC pattern decoding accuracy did not correlate with behavioural state-tracking accuracy, the cognitive-map interpretation would be undermined and OFC activity could be a downstream readout rather than the state representation itself.

If OFC could not decode unobservable states (only sensory-driven ones), the paper's central claim about hidden-state disambiguation would fail and SD-033b's role for the substrate in partial-observability scenarios would be unsupported.

entries.confidence_rationale: Highly cited unifying theory paper (Niv/Schoenbaum collaboration) that proposes OFC supplies a state-space labeling for RL elsewhere in the brain. This is the canonical theoretical statement of the OFC-as-cognitive-map view that SD-033b's framing (ii) directly imports. Source quality very high; mapping fidelity strong because the paper's task-space abstraction is essentially what SD-033b calls the task-structure cognitive map. Confidence reduced slightly because the paper is theoretical synthesis rather than direct empirical demonstration -- empirical confirmation comes from Schuck 2016 and the Zhou/Stalnaker entries on MECH-263.
failure_signatures: If OFC's contribution to RL turned out to be value caching rather than state-space labeling, the cognitive-map framing would collapse and SD-033b's framing (ii) would not be supported.
If task states could be reliably inferred without OFC even when they are unobservable from sensory input, the proposed unique role of OFC in disambiguating hidden states would be falsified.

entries.confidence_rationale: The most important cautionary citation for SD-003-prereq. Synofzik and colleagues argue that the comparator model alone -- the architectural target SD-003-prereq is built around -- is insufficient to explain sense of agency, and propose a two-step account in which a multifactorial feeling of agency feeds a separate conceptual judgement. The paper does not deny that the forward-model comparator is necessary; it argues it is not sufficient. For governance, this means MECH-256 should be treated as a building block of self-attribution rather than as the full mechanism, and SD-003-prereq architectural work should make room for downstream cue-integration and conceptual modules. Direction is mixed (supports the substrate's necessity, weakens its sufficiency). Confidence is moderated by the paper's conceptual rather than empirical character.
failure_signatures: Cases of preserved sense of agency under high comparator residual (e.g. compensated motor noise, tool use after adaptation) imply that residual alone cannot drive agency attribution -- additional cue-integration must be doing real work.

Cases of disrupted sense of agency under apparently low comparator residual (e.g. some schizophrenia passivity phenomena) imply that the comparator can be intact while agency fails, locating the failure mode upstream or downstream of the residual.

Sense of agency for thoughts (no motor efference copy) shows that an agency mechanism exists in domains the comparator model cannot reach -- so any REE self-attribution architecture needs a non-motor branch that does not depend on E2_x.

The paper's two-step structure is conceptually motivated but computationally underspecified -- adopting it as an architectural target risks importing under-determination into the REE design rather than constraining it.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational TICS review establishing the cerebellum as a forward/inverse internal-model substrate. Directly evidences the architectural pattern that SD-003-prereq presupposes: a structure that takes efference copy + current state and outputs predicted next sensory state, the exact computational role of E2_x in MECH-256. The MOSAIC framing (multiple paired models with responsibility signals) supports SD-029's stream-specific framing over a monolithic forward model. Confidence is moderated by the motor-to-interoceptive transfer required to map this onto the harm-stream comparator (SD-029) and by the paper's age -- subsequent work has refined and distributed the forward-model story beyond cerebellum.
failure_signatures: Cerebellar lesion does not eliminate sense of agency, only its motor-precision component -- this constrains how completely a cerebellar-style forward model can carry the full self-attribution role.

MOSAIC's responsibility-signal mechanism for selecting among multiple paired models is theoretically clean but empirically under-specified; if SD-003-prereq adopts a multi-stream architecture (one E2_x per reafferent stream), the routing/selection mechanism is the next architectural question and is not solved here.

Forward-model errors are used both for trajectory correction and for credit assignment in the paper's account. SD-029 uses the residual specifically for agency attribution; the paper does not separate these two roles and a clean separation may be an REE-specific design problem.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical primate-substrate review of corollary discharge (CD) -- the efference-copy infrastructure that any forward-model comparator architecture (SD-029, MECH-256, and the SD-003-prereq substrate work generally) presupposes. Crapse and Sommer survey single-unit, microstimulation, and inactivation evidence across saccadic, vocalisation, locomotor, and reach systems and arrive at the unifying claim: copies of motor commands are routed to sensory and parietal structures so that predicted sensory consequences can be subtracted from incoming reafference. That is precisely the architectural shape SD-003-prereq has to instantiate -- an efference-copy pathway feeding a forward model whose output is differenced against the realised stream. Confidence is high on source quality (Curr Opin Neurobiol, NIH-funded, widely cited) and moderate-to-high on mapping fidelity: the paper directly evidences the substrate (a_actual must be distributed to the forward model alongside the realised stream), but it stops short of formalising the comparator residual the way MECH-256 does, and it makes no architectural commitment about whether the forward model is single-pass or two-pass.
failure_signatures: When CD pathways are silenced (e.g. inactivation of the MD thalamic relay carrying the saccadic CD), monkeys lose the ability to compensate for self-generated sensory change -- they treat reafferent shifts as if they were externally caused. This is the substrate-level instantiation of the SD-003 failure mode: without an efference-copy input, the comparator cannot distinguish self-caused from world-caused change.

CD signals are distributed across many circuits with different latencies and modality profiles; a single forward model is unlikely to suffice across streams. This supports MECH-256's stream-agnostic framing (one comparator per reafferent stream) over a monolithic E2 comparator.

The review notes that CD does not always equate to a clean efference copy -- some signals are pre-motor predictions, others are post-motor. A comparator architecture that assumes a_actual is the only input may miss intention-level prediction signals that the brain actually uses.

entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative philosophical reference that names a canonical short list of categorical prohibitions (killing innocents, torture, using persons as mere means, lying, breaking promises) and motivates them via agent-centered and patient-centered structures. The mapping to REE's Q-025 is real but indirect: REE's five axioms (INV-025-029) are not the standard Kantian/deontological starting points -- they include irreducible uncertainty, world-existence, and love-as-care-investment, which the SEP entry does not derive prohibitions from. The article supports the broader thesis that 'a coherent ethics implies categorically forbidden acts' but does not tell us which list falls out of REE's specific axioms. Confidence is held below 0.5 because the mapping_fidelity from SEP's deontology to INV-025-029 is partial.
failure_signatures: Threshold deontology suggests the list of categorically forbidden acts is not stable under sufficiently catastrophic counterfactuals -- a feature any REE answer must engage with rather than ignore.
Agent-centered vs patient-centered framings yield overlapping but non-identical lists, so 'forbidden by the axioms' may not pick out a single deterministic set without further commitments.

entries.confidence_rationale: The Formula of Humanity provides the closest direct philosophical analogue to Q-025's question structure: it derives a list of categorically forbidden acts (suicide, lying promises, deception, treating others as mere means) from prerequisites of rational agency itself -- the same kind of structural derivation REE attempts from INV-025-029. The mapping is real and load-bearing for INV-026 (self as prerequisite) and INV-028 (others as co-inhabitants). However, Kant grounds his derivation in autonomous rational will, whereas REE grounds it in a richer set of prerequisites including world-existence (INV-027), irreducible uncertainty (INV-025), and care-investment (INV-029). Confidence is held just below 0.5 because (a) the mapping is structural-analogical rather than direct, and (b) Kant's specific list does not exhaust what REE's axioms would derive (e.g. acts that destroy the shared world fall under INV-027/028 but are not centrally Kantian).
failure_signatures: Kant's derivation famously over-generates prohibitions (e.g. lying to a murderer at the door) and under-generates in cases involving non-rational beings; if REE inherits the same structure naively, it inherits the same failure modes.
The Formula of Humanity is silent on most of what INV-027 (world existence) and INV-029 (love) would forbid, so leaning on Kant for Q-025 risks importing only a subset of the answer.

entries.confidence_rationale: Mouse causal study showing MSN-subtype-specific synaptic plasticity in DMS direct pathway is required for habit formation, alongside the well-established DLS plasticity story. Demonstrates that even within a single striatal subdomain, parallel pathways (direct vs indirect) carry distinct functional roles. Supports Q-019's segregation premise but is one mechanistic study, so confidence is moderate.
failure_signatures: If Q-019's three-gate model assumes that DMS = thought loop and DLS = action commitment loop with no further internal segregation, this paper complicates that picture: DMS itself contains direct/indirect MSN subtypes with distinct roles in habit formation. The three-gate model may need a finer-grained substrate description.

The chemogenetic rescue compromised acquisition but not expression -- so the role of DMS direct-pathway plasticity is in habit formation, not habit execution. This temporal split is not currently in Q-019's formulation.

entries.confidence_rationale: Computational model paper proposing biologically-motivated PFC-MD circuit that achieves rapid context inference and continual learning via thalamic gating of context-irrelevant PFC neurons. Supports the thought-loop substrate hypothesis with a working artificial system, but is a model -- not a direct empirical test. Mapping fidelity is good for the gating mechanism but moderate for Q-019's full three-gate claim.
failure_signatures: If the thought loop's gating is implemented through residue-field weighting rather than thalamic winner-take-all, the model's specific Hebbian + adaptive thresholding mechanism is one biological implementation -- not the only one. The paper does not exclude alternative thalamic gating substrates.

Continual learning success in the model relies on MD-like gating preventing catastrophic forgetting across tasks; if REE's tasks share more structure than the model assumes, the gating story may be less critical.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct transsynaptic and intersectional genetic dissection of cross-loop connectivity in mouse. Tests the 'ascending spiral' hypothesis that mediates DMS->DLS handover. Finds strong evidence for closed parallel loops and only weak functional cross-loop influence (open loops do not modulate tonic dopamine firing). High source quality, but rodent-only. Mapping fidelity to Q-019's tri-loop architecture is good for the segregation question; less direct on the limbic loop specifically (paper focuses on associative vs sensorimotor).
failure_signatures: If REE adopts a strict 'closed loop' interpretation that forbids any cross-loop information flow, this paper does find functional open-loop synapses -- they just fail to modulate tonic dopamine. So 'fully isolated channels' overstates the biology.
The paper studies DMS/DLS (associative/sensorimotor) but not the ventral/limbic loop directly; Q-019's three-gate architecture would need separate evidence for ventral-to-dorsal spirals.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality 2024 review by the Halassa lab synthesising thalamocortical evidence with a Bayesian/hierarchical framing. Directly relevant to the thought loop's MD substrate and its role in regularising flexible PFC computation. Mapping fidelity is strong for the thought loop component of Q-019; weaker for the sensorium and action commitment loops, which involve different thalamic nuclei (reticular, VL).

Action sequences result in trajectories through cognitive space, simulated via sequential coding (theta sequences) in hippocampus. This is the framework anchor for the architectural reading that hippocampal codes -- including theta sequences -- operate across abstraction levels. Confidence 0.82: theoretical review rather than primary empirical paper, but the synthesis is canonical and the anchor empirical work is reviewed in the same paper.
failure_signatures: The framework is theoretical / integrative. The specific empirical claim that 'theta sequences span abstract cognitive spaces with hierarchical levels at different resolutions' is supported by anchor papers cited in the review (Constantinescu 2016 conceptual grids; Schuck 2016 task-stage decoding; Bao 2019 etc.) but the synthesis paper itself is not a primary empirical demonstration.

The 'hierarchical levels' Bellmund et al. describe are different RESOLUTIONS of the cognitive map (zoom levels), not different SUBSTRATE LEVELS in the action-decomposition sense (motor primitives vs chunks vs options). The architectural mapping requires that the same primitive supports both senses of hierarchy, which is plausible but not directly defended in this paper.

entries.confidence_rationale: Nat Neurosci paper, single-unit recording in rat HPC during awake behaviour and sleep. Direct evidence that AWAKE replay reactivates stored representations from REMOTE experiences (a previous environment), as commonly as it reactivates current-environment trajectories. This breaks the dichotomy that 'awake replay = current experience, sleep replay = stored traces' -- both states reactivate stored representations. The finding has architectural consequences for distinguishing waking vs sleep theta function and grounds REE's MECH-272 routing gate (which switches stream weights between waking and sleep states) at the empirical level.
failure_signatures: The 'remote' experiences are still spatial trajectories from a different physical environment, not abstract / type-level / option-level remote content. Whether awake replay can reactivate non-spatial stored traces (e.g. social interactions, abstract task structures) is a separate empirical question that Frank lab and others have addressed in subsequent work but not in this paper.

The paper does NOT directly support a strong functional dissociation between waking and sleep replay -- it shows the OPPOSITE: stored representations are reactivated in both states. This complicates any architectural commitment to 'sleep theta carries higher-abstraction content than waking theta'. The functional difference may be quantitative (sleep replay rate, replay quality, gamma synchrony per Carr 2012) rather than qualitative (different content domains).

entries.confidence_rationale: Neuron paper, single-unit recording in rat HPC during a two-sequence behavioural task with controlled experience frequency manipulation. Direct empirical evidence for compositional replay: forward AND backward replay of behavioural sequence B occurred when rat had been performing A for 10+ minutes (i.e. NOT current experience). Replay of nonlocal B was MORE frequent when B was infrequently experienced. Replay also constructed never-experienced novel-path sequences. This directly supports the user's architectural reading that hippocampal replay is compositional / generative, not just experience-replication. Confidence 0.85 reflects strong empirical methodology and direct mapping to MECH-285 / MECH-292 / MECH-293.
failure_signatures: The novel-path sequences observed are spatial trajectories within the same physical environment. Whether replay constructs novel sequences across abstract / type-level / option-level dimensions (i.e. whether the compositional capacity extends from spatial-paths to abstraction-graphs) is plausible but not directly demonstrated.

Replay frequency was inversely related to experience frequency for the *non-current* sequence -- but this is a counterintuitive result that complicates simple staleness-priority accounts. The MECH-285 priority-weighted sleep replay sampler currently uses staleness, not inverse-experience-frequency. The two are correlated but not identical, and getting this wrong could mismatch the substrate behavior.

entries.confidence_rationale: Neuron paper, dual-site CA3 + CA1 LFP and single-unit recording in awake and quiescent rats. Direct evidence that transient slow-gamma (20-50 Hz) synchrony coordinates CA3-CA1 networks during sharp-wave ripple replay events. Higher slow-gamma synchrony predicts higher quality replay. This grounds the gamma-as-coordination-clock reading and provides the neural mechanism by which content gets ordered within a replay packet. Confidence 0.82: strong methodology, direct mechanistic claim, but the result is about replay (SWR-associated) gamma rather than waking-theta gamma -- the architectural translation requires noting which gamma regime is which.
failure_signatures: The slow gamma the paper measures is during sharp-wave ripple replay events (20-50 Hz, transient, SWR-associated), NOT the gamma nesting during waking theta cycles that MECH-089 specifies (which is mid-gamma 40-80 Hz / fast gamma 60-150 Hz, theta-locked, behavioural-state-active). The architectural translation requires distinguishing which gamma regime indexes which content -- not directly resolved by Carr 2012.

The paper does not directly speak to abstraction-level scaling. It establishes the gamma synchrony mechanism for replay coordination but does not test whether gamma synchrony quality varies with content abstraction (chunked vs atomic, type-level vs instance-level).

entries.confidence_rationale: Nat Neurosci paper, single-unit recording in rat HPC, the canonical empirical anchor for adaptive theta-sequence content. Three direct findings: (1) theta sequence path length extends FARTHER ahead during acceleration / higher running speed and farther behind during deceleration, (2) sequence length is directly related to theta cycle length AND number of gamma cycles in it, (3) theta sequences represent the environment in segments / 'chunks'. This is the strongest possible support for the user's architectural prediction that theta packaging scales with substrate abstraction. Confidence 0.88 because the methodology is decisive and the mapping to REE's MECH-089 + MECH-294 substrates is direct.
failure_signatures: The chunking the paper measures is in spatial-trajectory terms (running speed, path length). Whether the same theta-cycle adaptive packaging scales with non-spatial abstraction levels (action chunks per SD-045, type-instances per SD-040, options per SD-042) is plausible but not directly demonstrated. The scaling parameter is observable behavioural state (running speed), not a substrate-vocabulary state.

The paper does not test the prediction that ADDING new abstraction substrates would change theta-cycle content. It establishes the adaptive-packaging mechanism, not the substrate-dependence prediction. The user's architectural prediction extends the Gupta-Redish framework but is not directly tested in this paper.

entries.confidence_rationale: Sunstein's article is the canonical legal-philosophy treatment of how to define and act under 'irreversibility' when the agent does not have certainty about whether harm is irreversible. He distinguishes two operational conceptions (option-value and qualitative-distinctiveness) and proposes the Irreversible Harm Precautionary Principle, which is exactly the kind of principled-without-certainty answer Q-027 is asking for. Source quality is high (peer-reviewed flagship law review by a leading regulatory theorist). Mapping fidelity is moderate -- the framework is built for environmental and public-health regulation, not for a computational agent's harm signal -- and transfer risk is real because REE has no equivalent of the regulatory option-purchasing market. The paper supports the existence of such a definition without giving REE one it can directly adopt.
failure_signatures: Sunstein argues that 'irreversibility' has no single coherent definition and offers two distinct operational conceptions (option-value vs. qualitative-distinctive loss), so any REE definition that picks one will inherit specific weaknesses of that conception.

Sunstein explicitly notes that 'irreversible harms are sometimes on all sides of social problems', meaning a precautionary rule that always favours preserving optionality can itself foreclose options. A naive translation to REE would risk freezing the agent on both sides of any uncertainty-laden harm choice.

The Irreversible Harm Precautionary Principle works by 'purchasing an option to prevent the harm at a later date'. REE has no obvious analogue for purchasing options against future foreclosure -- the architectural translation is non-trivial and the paper does not provide it.

entries.confidence_rationale: SEP entry is canonical, peer-edited, and synoptic over the contemporary literature. It maps cleanly onto the meta-level of Q-027: Q-027 is partly an empirical-uncertainty problem (will this harm in fact be irreversible?) and partly a normative-uncertainty problem (is this category of harm in fact ethically distinctive?). The entry's main approaches -- My Favorite Theory, expected moral value, lexical priority -- give REE a menu of formal options for how to act when it is not sure whether a harm is irreversible. Mixed direction because the entry is also the source of the strongest objections to each option (intertheoretic comparisons, fanaticism, near-bound risk-seeking), so it both supports and constrains an answer to Q-027. Mapping fidelity is low-moderate because the entry is about choosing among full moral theories rather than about classifying harm severity inside a single theory.
failure_signatures: The entry argues that lexical-priority approaches (which would give irreversible harms absolute precedence over reversible ones) are 'implausibly fanatical' because they let arbitrarily small probabilities of irreversible harm dominate every decision. A naive REE rule that hard-prioritises any harm tagged irreversible inherits this objection.

Expected-moral-value approaches require intertheoretic comparisons of choiceworthiness across moral theories, which the entry treats as an unsolved foundational problem. Q-027 cannot just defer to expected-moral-value to handle irreversibility uncertainty without inheriting that unsolved comparison problem.

The entry identifies cluelessness about long-term consequences as a structural source of deep uncertainty -- meaning REE may be unable to estimate, even probabilistically, whether a given action's consequences are irreversible at long horizons. Any definition of irreversibility that depends on long-horizon forecasts is exposed to this failure mode.

entries.confidence_rationale: IEP is a peer-reviewed reference work but lower-tier than SEP, which is the main reason source quality is held moderate. (Corrected 2026-08-14: this rationale originally also cited the entry as unsigned. It is not -- it is signed by Tanja Rechnitzer, University of Bern, published 2020-03-25 per the site's own metadata. The numeric confidence and confidence_components below are left untouched pending governance re-scoring, so read them as still resting partly on the withdrawn premise.) The article is directly relevant to Q-027 because it explicitly addresses the question of whether the precautionary principle requires certainty about irreversibility (it does not -- it requires only a plausible threat) and surveys decision-theoretic operationalisations (maximin, minimax regret) that REE could in principle adopt. Mapping fidelity to REE's architectural primitives is low because the entry stays at the policy level. The entry's most useful contribution is the explicit framing of the under-precaution / over-precaution trade-off, which is the same trade-off Q-027 must navigate.
failure_signatures: The entry warns that strong formulations of the precautionary principle can produce 'paralysis' -- prohibiting both action and inaction when irreversible harms are on every side. A REE rule that always escalates harm tagged 'possibly irreversible' would inherit this paralysis failure mode.

The entry notes that weak formulations of the precautionary principle become trivial -- they reduce to advice the agent already has from any consequence-sensitive ethics. So if REE's Q-027 answer is too weak, it adds no protective structure beyond what the existing harm signal provides.

The IEP entry is a tertiary reference work, lower-tier than SEP, so specific phrasings should be traced to the primary literature it cites (Resnik, Hansson, Sunstein, Steel, Sandin) rather than cited from it directly. Treat it as scaffolding, not as authoritative. (Corrected 2026-08-14: this signature originally read 'not signed and not dated in the visible metadata'. Both premises were wrong -- the entry is signed by Tanja Rechnitzer and dated 2020-03-25. The citation caution survives on tier alone.)

entries.confidence_rationale: Williams's paper is a foundational and continuously cited primary source on moral conflict and the moral-residue argument; it is the source the McConnell SEP entry (separately filed in this directory) cites as the canonical statement of the moral-residue position. Source quality is high (peer-reviewed proceedings, reprinted by CUP, 60 years of citations). Mapping fidelity is moderate: Williams's argument about the persistence of moral demands after choice maps cleanly onto the question of what REE should do with a defeated INV-026 or INV-028 after axiom-conflict resolution, but Williams writes about emotion and human moral phenomenology, which translates only loosely to a computational agent's residue field.
failure_signatures: Williams's argument depends on the phenomenological reality of agent-regret -- a class of negative emotion that the agent has *qua agent* about the unchosen option. REE has no obvious analogue of emotion, so a translation has to be made on functional rather than phenomenological grounds. Any naive port that pretends REE 'feels regret' is overclaiming.

Williams explicitly attacks the standard moral-philosophy move of resolving conflict by arguing one ought was 'only prima facie' or 'pro tanto' or otherwise eliminable. He treats this as a way of making the conflict disappear that misses what is morally important. A REE answer that resolves axiom conflict by reducing one axiom to merely-defeasible status inherits this objection.

The argument is phenomenological-philosophical rather than mechanistic. It does not specify what residue-laying mechanism agents in fact have, only what an adequate account of conflict-resolution must preserve. Implementing Williams's lesson in REE requires architectural design Williams does not provide.

entries.confidence_rationale: SEP is the canonical reference work and McConnell is the long-standing author of this entry. The entry directly surveys the philosophical question Q-028 is asking: when an agent faces conflicting obligations, what should it do? It distinguishes obligation-dilemmas from prohibition-dilemmas, surveys hierarchical-ordering solutions and the Williams/Marcus moral-residue argument, and explains why standard deontic logic struggles to allow real dilemmas. Mixed direction: the entry both supports the position that REE may need a hierarchical or disjunctive resolution rule (constructive) and constrains that position by surveying long-standing objections to every proposed resolution. Mapping fidelity is moderate -- the entry is about human moral conflict, REE's axioms are not classical deontic constraints, and Q-028's specific self-vs-other case is only one of many the entry treats.
failure_signatures: The entry argues that standard deontic logic principles (Principle of Deontic Consistency: 'an action cannot be both obligatory and forbidden'; Principle of Deontic Logic) generate logical contradictions when combined with genuine moral dilemmas. Any REE answer that treats the axioms as classical deontic constraints inherits this contradiction-generation problem.

W. D. Ross's argument against strict hierarchical ordering (cited approvingly in the entry) directly challenges any REE answer that hard-codes one axiom as lexically prior to another -- promise-keeping does not always outweigh harm-prevention, and analogously INV-026 self-preservation does not always outweigh INV-028 shared-world ethics.

The Williams/Marcus moral-residue position (also surveyed) implies that even when REE makes the right choice between self and other, the unchosen obligation leaves a residue that the agent should track. A naive REE resolution rule that simply picks one axiom and discards the other loses this residue and so loses something philosophically important.

entries.confidence_rationale: Large UK QResearch nested case-control (~284,000 patients) replicating and extending Gray 2015 with class-specific hazard estimates -- bladder antimuscarinics, antidepressants, antiparkinson drugs, antipsychotics, and antiepileptics each carrying their own AOR. Class-specific decomposition begins to disentangle the question implicitly because anticholinergics differ in CNS penetration and dosing time-of-day. Still cannot directly test the REM-mediation hypothesis without sleep data, so capped below 0.85.
failure_signatures: Class-specific AORs differ widely (1.29 to 1.70) but the paper does not partition the difference into pharmacokinetic vs pharmacodynamic vs sleep-effect components, so a sleep-mediated reading of the bladder antimuscarinic AOR=1.65 is not formally tested.

The clinical bottom line ('switch from oxybutynin to mirabegron should reduce dementia risk') is what Q-031 wants to validate, but the paper offers only the prerequisite -- bladder antimuscarinics carry an elevated AOR -- not the post-switch test. A natural experiment of beta-3 substitution has not been published in this design.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong prospective cohort (ACT, n=3434, 7.3y mean follow-up, computerised dispensing data so dose is well-measured) with a clear monotonic dose-response between cumulative anticholinergic TSDDs and incident dementia. Directly anchors the cumulative-dose limb of Q-031, but the design cannot dissociate REM-mediated from diurnal-cholinergic-deficit pathways; that limit pulls the score below 0.85.
failure_signatures: Cumulative dose alone is a coarse exposure marker -- it conflates daytime cholinergic blockade (relevant to Pathway 2, MECH-175) with sleep-period blockade (relevant to Pathway 1 / MECH-173 nocturnal REM suppression). The study cannot tell the two apart.
TSDDs are calibrated to a generic standardised daily dose, not to plasma half-life or CNS penetration, so two equally-dosed drugs with very different sleep-period CNS exposure are pooled.

entries.confidence_rationale: Carefully designed local microdialysis-with-blockade study (n=32 freely behaving rats) showing that scopolamine microperfusion of the subceruleus does not eliminate REM sleep, in contrast to longstanding cholinergic-induction theories. ACh modulates state transitions and hippocampal theta but is not required for REM generation. This is mechanistically important: it weakens the simplest 'ACh-block --> REM-suppression' story Q-031 pathway 1 leans on, because the relevant ACh effect on REM is a transition / theta modulator rather than a generator. Direction-of-effect for Q-031 is therefore mixed: it does not deny pathway 1, but it constrains the size and kind of REM disturbance you can attribute to chronic anticholinergic blockade.
failure_signatures: REM is NOT abolished by scopolamine microperfusion at the SubC. So 'anticholinergics suppress REM' is at most a partial story -- chronic systemic anticholinergic blockade probably reduces REM phasic intensity and theta strength rather than abolishing REM, which means the magnitude of the REM-suppression-years that Q-031 pathway 1 attributes to anticholinergics is smaller than a naive reading of clinical scopolamine studies suggests.

If the anticholinergic effect on REM is dominated by transition reinforcement and theta modulation rather than total REM amount, then PSG-measured REM% may not be the right mediator to track. Mediation analyses using REM% as the mediator could under-detect the true mediation effect.

entries.confidence_rationale: Framingham Heart Study Offspring cohort with 19y maximum follow-up, home PSG measurement of REM%, and a clean signal: 9% increased dementia hazard per 1% reduction in REM. Robust to multiple covariate adjustments and to lag-window sensitivity. The signal is REM-specific (NREM stages did not predict). This is the single best human evidence that REM% itself tracks dementia risk -- the central premise of MECH-173 / Q-031 pathway 1. Held below 0.85 because n=32 incident cases is modest and the paper documents association, not mediation; it does not measure anticholinergic exposure.
failure_signatures: REM% is associated with dementia, but the paper cannot tell whether REM disturbance is a cause, a prodrome, or a downstream marker of the same neurodegeneration that produces dementia. Reverse causation is partially addressed by excluding early converters but not eliminated.

The paper does not measure anticholinergic exposure, so it cannot test whether anticholinergic-induced REM suppression has the same dementia signature as endogenous REM reduction. The mediation chain ACh-block -> REM-suppression -> dementia is plausible but untested in this dataset.

entries.confidence_rationale: Small (n=8) randomised crossover PSG study showing that transdermal scopolamine -- a clinically used muscarinic antagonist -- suppresses phasic REM activity and REM density at the lowest commercial dose. This is the substrate-level mechanism plausibility evidence for Q-031 pathway 1: anticholinergic drugs do measurably alter REM-related signal in healthy humans. But the study is small, young-adult, and short, so its transfer to elderly chronic-use anticholinergic patients is a real leap.
failure_signatures: n=8 healthy young men is a tiny sample with limited power; phasic REM measures (REM density, total REM activity) reach significance, but tonic REM measures (duration, latency) do not -- which complicates the simple 'scopolamine suppresses REM' reading.

The study is single-night, low-dose, healthy young adults. Q-031 cares about decades of nightly anticholinergic exposure in older adults with comorbidities -- the transfer from this acute experimental result to the chronic clinical context is large.

Scopolamine is not the most common chronic anticholinergic: most Q-031-relevant exposures are bladder antimuscarinics (oxybutynin, tolterodine) or tertiary tricyclics. CNS penetration profiles differ; the substrate evidence here is genus-level not species-level.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct AD-side test of MECH-172's prediction. AD patients can in fact acquire a perceptual-motor sequence under errorless conditions, demonstrating that the procedural-learning channel is functional even when episodic memory has substantially failed. Mapping fidelity is good; transfer risk is low. Source quality is moderate -- specialty journal, modest sample. The errorless qualification is a real wrinkle: it is not unconditional preservation, it is preservation when error monitoring is offloaded.
failure_signatures: If MECH-172 were wrong and AD's pathology degrades both systems together, AD patients would fail the SRT in errorless conditions too. They did not.

Errorless > errorful in AD specifically (not just generally) suggests an interaction between feedback monitoring and procedural acquisition that the simple architectural-separation reading does not predict.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, much-replicated double dissociation in matched neurological patient groups. Source quality is high (Science, controlled clinical comparison, foundational paper); mapping fidelity is strong because the architectural separation REE asserts (model-free habit vs declarative attribution) is the same separation Knowlton operationalised. Transfer risk is moderate -- amnesic group is mostly diencephalic/medial-temporal lesions rather than AD specifically, so AD-relevance is by inference not direct measurement.
failure_signatures: If REE's architectural separation were wrong, amnesics would also be impaired on probabilistic classification (they were not).
If habit learning required a hippocampal/cortical consolidation pipeline, Parkinson patients with intact MTL would still acquire it (they did not).

entries.confidence_rationale: Recent (2025) human study with the right design: PSG + MRI + CSF biomarkers + 2-year cognitive follow-up across CN/MCI/AD. SO-theta-burst and SO-spindle coupling progressively disrupt across the disease continuum and predict subsequent decline. This is the human counterpart to Benthem 2020's mouse mechanism and substantially reduces the transfer risk of the broken-consolidation premise. n=93 is moderate but the longitudinal design strengthens the inference.
failure_signatures: If MECH-172's premise that AD degrades the offline consolidation pipeline were wrong, SO-spindle coupling should not disrupt progressively along the disease continuum (it does), should not be linked to amyloid/tau/APOE burden (it is), and should not predict cognitive decline (it does).

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct, well-controlled clinical test of the HD half of MECH-172's double dissociation. The feedback-vs-paired-associate manipulation is the right test for whether striatum is specifically required for the model-free RL component (it is). Mapping fidelity is high because the paper isolates the HD/striatal-loss limb that MECH-172 invokes. Source quality is solid (Neuropsychologia, n=18 early-HD with matched controls). Transfer risk is moderate -- early HD already includes 50% caudate MSN loss, so the striatal-causation inference is reasonable.
failure_signatures: If MECH-172's architectural separation were wrong, HD patients should be impaired on the paired-associate (declarative) version too. They were not.

entries.confidence_rationale: Supplies the mechanistic substrate for MECH-172's central premise -- that the consolidation pipeline (specifically SWR-DW and spindle-DW coupling) is broken in AD. This is the broken-pipeline limb of MECH-172's architectural argument. Source quality is high (Curr Biol, multi-electrode array, McNaughton lab); mapping fidelity is good but the model is 3xTg mouse (amyloid + tau), not human early AD. Transfer risk is moderate-to-substantial.
failure_signatures: If MECH-172's premise that AD specifically degrades the offline consolidation pipeline were wrong, AD mice should show normal SWR-DW coupling (they did not) and behavioral spatial learning would not correlate with that coupling (it does).

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct test of the precision-mediates-responsibility bridge. Coercion is a precision/agency manipulation; medial frontal gyrus activity tracks the preserved sense of accountability across that manipulation. Mapping to MECH-025b is good but not perfect -- coercion alters the act-selection precision/control axis MECH-025b cares about, but Caspar's primary IV is social-coercion context rather than precision per se. n is moderate; PLoS One is open-access standard.
failure_signatures: If the precision-responsibility bridge MECH-025b proposes were absent, medial frontal activity should not track preserved agency/responsibility under coercion (it does).
If responsibility were a purely post-hoc social attribution unrelated to action-selection processes, the bridge to volition-related cortex would not appear -- but it does appear specifically there.

entries.confidence_rationale: Philosophical critique of Greene's dual-process model of moral judgment. Relevant to MECH-025b because the precision-responsibility bridge implicitly assumes a process->content mapping similar to Greene's (high precision/deliberation -> higher responsibility). Kahane argues this mapping is empirically unsupported, that controlled processing in 'utilitarian' judgment may actually reflect moral deliberation independent of utilitarian content. Tempers MECH-025b's bridge by warning against tying processing mode directly to moral conclusions.
failure_signatures: If MECH-025b's bridge committed to a strong process->content mapping (high precision -> particular moral verdict), Kahane's critique would directly apply. The bridge actually committed to is weaker (precision -> responsibility weight), but the warning still applies to extensions that would tie precision to specific moral verdicts.

entries.confidence_rationale: Comprehensive integrative review proposing the Agency in Brain Disorders Framework (ABDF). Maps prospective vs retrospective agency cues, top-down vs bottom-up. Useful framework for understanding how MECH-025b's precision-responsibility bridge might break in disorder, but the review aggregates many heterogeneous patient populations and does not directly test the bridge. The review explicitly notes there is no robust treatment for aberrant agency across disorders, partly because the cognitive mechanisms remain poorly synthesised -- which weakens an unconditional reading.
failure_signatures: If MECH-025b's precision-responsibility bridge were the only operative mechanism, disorders should show coupled disturbance of precision and responsibility. Malik documents dissociations -- e.g. schizophrenia shows aberrant agency without clear changes in attributed responsibility, OCD shows preserved agency with hyperactive responsibility -- which suggest the bridge is one mechanism among several.

entries.confidence_rationale: The cleanest available test of MECH-187's serotonin-modulates-DA-gain mechanism in vivo. Bailey shows that 5-HT2C-selective ligand SB242084 increases vigor and persistence on demanding work, that this is reflected in striatal DA potentiation specifically in dorsomedial striatum (not NAc reward signaling), and that the effect is dissociable from generalised activity or reward-value changes. Source quality is high (J Neurosci, Cheer/Simpson collaboration, voltammetry + microdialysis + behaviour); mapping to MECH-187's gain-on-incentive-salience reading is good but with a wrinkle: the DA potentiation is in DMS, not NAc, which is the canonical incentive-salience locus in MECH-187's framing.
failure_signatures: If MECH-187 were only operative at NAc incentive salience, SB242084 effects on vigor should not show DMS-specific DA potentiation -- they do, which suggests the gain modulator reaches multiple striatal subregions with different functional consequences.

If 5-HT2C action were unrelated to motivational gain, SB242084 should affect general activity / reward perception too -- it specifically does not. The dissociation strengthens the gain-modulator reading.

entries.confidence_rationale: Adds important nuance to MECH-187. The DRN 5-HT inhibition of operant responding requires VTA-targeted 5-HT plus an SSRI; the NAc-targeted 5-HT path is not sufficient. This relocates a major component of the 5-HT-DA interaction upstream (at VTA, the source of DA neurons) rather than downstream at the NAc target. MECH-187's NAc-locus framing needs to be qualified or extended.
failure_signatures: If MECH-187's mechanism were primarily NAc-target 5-HT signalling, optogenetic stimulation of 5-HT terminals in NAc should suffice to reduce operant responding -- it does not. The behavioural effect requires VTA-targeted 5-HT signalling.

If 5-HT and DA were straightforwardly oppositional in the operant-response axis, the SSRI requirement would not appear -- it does, suggesting the 5-HT effect is amplitude/duration-dependent rather than gating.

entries.confidence_rationale: Provides synapse-level mechanism for MECH-187 at the canonical NAc locus. DA and 5-HT each filter excitatory inputs to NAc MSNs in input-specific patterns that overlap but differ. The DA + 5-HT joint action recapitulates the behavioural effects of methamphetamine and MDMA. This is the substrate-level account MECH-187 needs: how does 5-HT modulate the gain on DA at the NAc target, in mechanistic terms. Source quality is very high (PNAS, Malenka lab, Deisseroth tools, multi-method).
failure_signatures: If 5-HT and DA operated through the same input-channel filter, MECH-187's gain story would be redundant -- but they target overlapping but distinct input sets (5-HT reduces PVT, vHip, BLA inputs; DA reduces PVT only), supporting MECH-187's claim that 5-HT contributes a separable gain dimension.
If MECH-187 were wrong about modality, optogenetic input inhibition tests should not reproduce drug-induced behavioural effects; they did (PVT->cocaine-CPP enhancement; mPFC->MDMA-sociability).

entries.confidence_rationale: INV-043 is explicitly philosophical (architecture necessary but not sufficient; received caregiving as developmental requirement for ethical agency). Care ethics, especially Noddings, makes the most direct philosophical case for INV-043's structural commitment: ethical action originates in the memory of being cared-for. The IEP entry is a peer-reviewed reference work that consolidates Noddings, Gilligan, Tronto, Held, Kittay -- a useful single anchor. Confidence is bounded by (a) the philosophical-not-empirical nature of the source and (b) substantive critiques of care ethics (essentialism, parochialism) that bound how strongly INV-043 can lean on this tradition.
failure_signatures: If INV-043's architectural-necessary-not-sufficient framing were wrong, care ethics' developmental-relational core could not provide it any philosophical traction. The traction is real (Noddings explicitly grounds ethical action in 'the memory of being cared-for'), but care ethics' own internal critiques (essentialism, parochialism) constrain how much weight INV-043 can put on it.

entries.confidence_rationale: Provides the structural-brain substrate for INV-043's claim. Adult Romanian adoptees (n=67) show 8.6% reduction in total brain volume vs nondeprived UK adoptees (n=21), with TBV negatively correlated with deprivation duration. The structural changes statistically mediate the relationship between deprivation and adult ADHD/IQ outcomes. This is the structural counterpart to the clinical-trajectory paper (Sonuga-Barke 2017); together they make the case that the developmental window leaves architectural trace that subsequent enrichment does not erase.
failure_signatures: If INV-043 were wrong and the architecture is fully malleable post-window, brain structure should normalise after extended adoptive-family enrichment. It does not -- a quantifiable structural deficit persists into adulthood.
If the brain-structure changes were unrelated to functional outcomes, mediation tests should fail. They held -- TBV reduction statistically mediated both lower IQ and higher ADHD symptoms.

entries.confidence_rationale: ERA is the closest-to-natural-experiment longitudinal evidence available for INV-043. Children with >6 months of severe institutional deprivation followed to ages 22-25 show persistent elevation in ASD-like symptoms, disinhibited social engagement, inattention/hyperactivity, mental health service use, lower educational attainment, unemployment -- despite years of nurturing adoptive families. Architecture (intact, since they recover IQ) was not sufficient; the early caregiving period was load-bearing. This is the strongest empirical anchor for INV-043's necessity claim.
failure_signatures: If INV-043 were wrong and architecture alone were sufficient (given subsequent good caregiving), the >6mo group should look like the <6mo group + UK controls in young adulthood. They do not -- the deprivation effect persists across the developmental trajectory.

entries.confidence_rationale: Adds a circuit-architecture dimension Q-019's existing 14-entry review does not cover: the Arkypallidal pallidostriatal feedback loop, a comparatively recently characterised GABAergic projection from a subpopulation of GPe neurons back to dorsal striatum. This is one of the largest extrinsic GABA inputs to dorsal striatum and operates as a feedback inhibition mechanism. For Q-019, this reshapes the architectural debate -- if BG circuits include direct feedback from GPe back to striatum, neither pure parallel-segregated nor pure single-gate models are quite right; the architecture is closed-loop with feedback inhibition.
failure_signatures: If Q-019's three-loop architecture were strictly parallel and segregated, the Arkypallidal feedback projection from GPe back to striatum would not exist. It does, and it is one of the largest GABA inputs to dorsal striatum -- which forces any candidate Q-019 architecture to include feedback within each loop and possibly cross-loop interactions.

entries.confidence_rationale: Recent (2025) computational arbitration of Q-019's competing models. Leblois shows that BG-thalamo-cortical adaptation requires strong recurrent closed-loop dynamics, not feedforward-only architecture. The model integrates anatomical, physiological, and behavioural evidence and demonstrates how closed-loop architecture + attractor dynamics + dopamine-dependent plasticity together explain how BG plasticity contributes to movement adaptation that does not require BG output for execution. This favours the closed-loop, multi-component reading of BG architecture that Q-019's three-gate model is one instance of, and weakens pure feedforward single-gate accounts.
failure_signatures: If Q-019's architecture were purely feedforward (single feedforward gate or three feedforward gates), Leblois shows the model could not explain how reward-driven adaptation transfers to movements that no longer require BG output. The closed-loop recurrent dynamics are required.
