Operational instantiation of FEP for the explore-exploit dilemma: agents minimise expected free energy, which decomposes cleanly into extrinsic value (utility) and epistemic value (information gain). The paper provides simulations showing this framing reproduces both directed exploration and softmax-style noise as Bayes-optimal precision parameters. Direct support for R1 both-channels-needed verdict from a computational theoretical anchor.
failure_signatures: If active inference's epistemic-value formulation is wrong, any MECH-314 instantiation that uses information-gain as the curiosity signal (vs novelty-bonus a la Wittmann 2008 or learning-progress a la Schmidhuber) loses its theoretical grounding.
If the precision-as-confidence framing is wrong, REE's existing precision-modulation substrates (MECH-269b, SD-032b) would also be affected since they share the same theoretical commitment.

entries.confidence_rationale: Major Neuron Perspective synthesising the curiosity / information-seeking literature across psychology + neuroscience. Argues that 'curiosity' is best understood not as a unitary mechanism but as a family of motivations for information-seeking with overlapping but distinguishable behavioural and neural signatures. Provides the framing that R1 should be answered by treating curiosity as a structured channel that operates ALONGSIDE noise, not as a replacement.
failure_signatures: Treating 'curiosity' as a single substrate with a single threshold (the temptation in REE's MECH-216 schema-readout-wanting framing) will fail to capture the heterogeneity Kidd & Hayden document; the substrate may need multiple sub-mechanisms for different curiosity flavours (perceptual / epistemic / diversive).

An REE substrate that conflates information-seeking with noise will fail to reproduce ethological-context-dependence of curiosity that Kidd & Hayden emphasise (curiosity is not a temperature parameter -- it is goal-shaped).

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct behavioural-modeling demonstration in humans (Princeton lab) that BOTH directed information-seeking AND random decision noise contribute to exploration; horizon manipulation dissociates the two. Highest-relevance single paper for R1 (structured-vs-noise verdict) -- the data force the both-channels-needed reading. Confidence not 1.0 because it is a single behavioural paradigm (Horizon task), and primate / lesion replication is more limited than the human modelling.
failure_signatures: Either-or arguments for behavioural diversity (curiosity-only or noise-only) are predicted to fail to explain horizon-dependent shifts in both information-seeking AND decision noise that this study quantifies.

An REE substrate that implements only structured curiosity (no stochastic floor) should fail to reproduce the random-exploration component of the longer-horizon condition; one that implements only noise should fail to reproduce the directed information-seeking component.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational FEP review establishing the unified-action-perception-learning framework that grounds the structured-exploration arm. Loaded venue (NRN) and high-impact theoretical contribution. Confidence not higher because FEP-as-empirical-substrate is contested in the literature -- the paper makes a unified-theory claim that is not itself directly testable; downstream empirical predictions are testable but mostly via active-inference instantiations (cf. Friston 2015 PMID 25689102).
failure_signatures: If FEP is fundamentally wrong about the substrate of exploration (epistemic-value-as-free-energy is not a real biological computation), the structured-exploration arm of ARC-065 loses its primary theoretical grounding; only the noise arm (Faisal 2008) and pragmatic curiosity instantiations (Schmidhuber/Pathak) remain.

REE substrates that make precision-minimisation a load-bearing computation (MECH-269b V_s rollout gating, SD-032b dACC adaptive control with PE-precision modulation) implicitly endorse the FEP framework; if FEP is wrong they are at risk too.

entries.confidence_rationale: fMRI dissociation in healthy humans: frontopolar cortex + intraparietal sulcus selectively active during exploratory decisions; striatum + vmPFC during exploitative. The paper introduces the standard computational characterisation of the explore-exploit dilemma that the rest of the field uses. Key R2 evidence: there is a distinct cortical substrate for exploration (not just the dopaminergic exploitation circuit). Confidence high but not maximal because fMRI cannot dissociate the curiosity-bias channel from the noise channel within the frontopolar BOLD signal.
failure_signatures: If REE has only an exploitation circuit (E3 score-aggregation + GoalState seeding) without a separate diversity-generation pathway, the model should fail to produce frontopolar-equivalent activation patterns during the explore phases of behaviour.

If diversity generation in REE is not separable from exploitation but emerges from noise alone (R1 noise-only verdict), then no substrate should map onto the frontopolar/vmPFC double dissociation Daw 2006 reports.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct hippocampal place-cell recording in freely-moving rats showing forward-trajectory sequences predicting future goal-directed paths. Provides one of the substrate candidates for behavioural diversity generation -- hippocampal forward sequences as the option-proposal mechanism. Already cross-referenced by REE substrates MECH-292 ranked ghost-goal bank, MECH-293 awake ghost-goal probes; this paper grounds the relevance to ARC-065 specifically.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that generates behavioural diversity only through downstream stochastic / curiosity channels (no proposal-side mechanism) will fail to reproduce the goal-biased trajectory-proposal pattern Pfeiffer & Foster document.

If hippocampal-replay-driven proposal is REDUNDANT in REE (covered by existing CEM trajectory generation + MECH-293 ghost-goal probes), this paper would predict no additional diversity-generation capacity from a separate proposal-side mechanism.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational integrative theory grounded in monkey neurophysiology + computational modelling. Establishes the LC-NE tonic/phasic dual-mode framework that has anchored the explore-exploit-circuit literature for two decades. Highest-relevance R2 paper (which biological circuit generates diversity) and the load-bearing R4 paper (continuous vs triggered: LC-NE provides BOTH tonic background and phasic triggered modes -- not a clean either/or).
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that does not implement an arousal-mode-switch analog (continuous tonic baseline gain + phasic triggered transitions) will fail to reproduce LC-NE-style mode-shift signatures: gradual increase in decision noise as task utility wanes, then phasic sharpening on task-relevant stimuli.

If LC-NE-equivalent functionality is REDUNDANT in REE (collapsible into existing dACC / SD-037 substrates), the model should still recover Aston-Jones-style behavioural signatures from those existing substrates; if not, ARC-065 needs a separate arousal-mode-switch claim.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational NRN review documenting that biological neural systems are intrinsically stochastic from molecular to behavioural levels, and that the nervous system has co-evolved both noise-counter mechanisms AND noise-as-feature mechanisms (e.g., stochastic resonance, exploration). Key R1 evidence for the noise-arm: behavioural variability is partly an irreducible substrate property, not a separately-engineered exploration channel.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that treats action selection as fully deterministic (no policy noise floor) will fail to reproduce the trial-to-trial variability biological agents exhibit even on highly-trained tasks.

If noise is the ONLY source of behavioural diversity (R1 noise-only verdict), this review would predict that all behavioural-diversity signatures could be reproduced by tuning a single temperature parameter -- which Wilson 2014 falsifies behaviourally.

entries.confidence_rationale: fMRI evidence in healthy humans that striatal activity underlies novelty-based choice even when novelty is unrelated to outcome value. Demonstrates that perceptual novelty drives choice via a striatal substrate, providing direct R2 anchor for one curiosity sub-flavour (novelty-driven). Key: the paper shows novelty-driven choice produces measurable individual differences -- a falsifiable signature.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that lacks novelty-driven choice bias should fail to reproduce striatal-equivalent activation during novel-option choice and should fail to show individual-difference variation in novelty susceptibility.

If novelty-driven choice is REDUNDANT with general curiosity (MECH-216 schema-readout-wanting), this paper would predict that lesioning the schema-readout pathway eliminates the novelty signature -- a testable cross-mechanism prediction.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong primary electrophysiology paper. Demonstrates that hippocampal place-cell sequences during awake quiet periods replay not just current-environment trajectories but remote-environment trajectories from past experiences. This means the brain has an online mechanism (during awake quiet periods, not just sleep) for re-processing trajectory data from earlier episodes. Direct R3 anchor for the online-extraction-arm of bottom-up rule discovery.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that does NOT have an online during-awake-pause replay mechanism for the trajectory record will fail to reproduce Karlsson 2009's signature: spontaneous reactivation of remote-environment trajectories during quiet periods, available for downstream learning.

If ARC-064's bottom-up extraction is sleep-replay-only (R3 verdict offline-only), it cannot accommodate the Karlsson 2009 awake-replay finding -- some bottom-up processing must happen online during awake behaviour.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong primary electrophysiology paper. Recordings during overtraining show striatum acquires action-bracketing chunking patterns rapidly while infralimbic cortex develops habit-tracking patterns slowly; optogenetic disruption of infralimbic activity during overtraining prevents habit crystallisation. Direct R2 anchor for striatum-as-behavioural-pattern-extraction substrate (the bottom-up rule discovery analog) plus R4 input on which arbitration variable matters (practice-length, not uncertainty alone).
failure_signatures: An REE substrate without a striatum-analog action-chunking mechanism will fail Smith & Graybiel 2013's signature: rapid acquisition of action-bracketing patterns during overtraining, with sensitivity to running automaticity but insensitivity to reward devaluation.

If ARC-064's bottom-up rule extraction does not develop a stable substrate-level signature over training (in REE: stable rule-cluster representations after extended episodes in similar contexts), the substrate is not 'crystallising' rules the way the dorsolateral striatum does in Smith & Graybiel.

If MECH-312's arbitration variable is purely uncertainty-based (Daw 2005), it will fail to capture the practice-length-driven habit takeover Smith & Graybiel demonstrate; arbitration may need to track time-on-task / repetition-count as well.

entries.confidence_rationale: Authors' own review of the action-chunking + habit-formation field they helped build. entries.confidence_rationale: The Cooper-Shallice contention scheduling model is the cognitive-neuroscience tradition's canonical formal account of *schemas* competing for execution -- a parallel ancestor lineage to the AI options framework, with the same essential structure (action-schemas as competing units, with activation, gating, and termination), but anchored in patient data (action-disorganisation syndrome). Mapping fidelity to ARC-062 and MECH-312 is HIGH but the inheritance is mixed because the model is largely descriptive rather than mechanistic-quantitative. If REE's MECH-312 arbitration cannot reproduce analogous failure modes (sequence errors, perseveration, capture errors) under selective ablation, the schema/contention-scheduling reading of MECH-312 is weakened.

The schema tradition predicts a Supervisory Attentional System (SAS) that overrides contention scheduling for novel/non-routine situations -- this is a candidate framing for ARC-062's gated_policy. If REE has no SAS-like override and the gated_policy is fully integrated into the same arbitration substrate, that is a divergence.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical bridge paper between options/HRL formalism and biological-substrate mapping. It maps options-framework primitives (option, sub-policy, termination, policy-over-options) to dorsolateral PFC, OFC, basal-ganglia, and dopamine signals. For Pull 4's vocabulary-mapping question this is the load-bearing paper showing that the AI options vocabulary already has a worked-out neural mapping -- exactly what REE's rule-apprehension cluster has been independently sketching. Confidence not higher because the neural mapping is suggestive rather than mechanistic in the EXQ-substrate-validation sense, and several of the predictions remain debated (especially the OFC role).
failure_signatures: If REE's MECH-318 (rule-state-abstraction) cannot be plausibly identified with the OFC role Botvinick 2009 proposes, the inheritance pathway from this paper to MECH-318 is weak.

If REE's ARC-062 cannot be mapped to the dorsolateral-PFC policy-over-options role this paper anchors, the gated_policy interpretation as option-selection machinery is in tension with the canonical neural reading.

entries.confidence_rationale: The Wang 2018 meta-RL framing reads context-conditioned policy as a *learned learning algorithm* hosted in PFC recurrent dynamics, with dopamine acting as a slower training signal that shapes the recurrent network into one that can rapidly adapt to new tasks. This gives REE a unified vocabulary for ARC-062 (top-down rule application = meta-learned context-conditioned policy) and the OFC-cognitive-map of MECH-318 (= the recurrent latent state that implements the inner-loop algorithm). Confidence not higher because the meta-RL framing is one of several competing accounts (Wang and Botvinick's Nat Neurosci paper has been challenged on specific dopamine claims) and because it does not naturally model online-vs-offline timing.
failure_signatures: Meta-RL predicts that PFC recurrent dynamics carry sufficient task-state information to support context-appropriate behaviour without a separate explicit rule-state-abstraction substrate. If REE's V3 substrate cannot be made to support context-conditioned behaviour using only recurrent latent dynamics (no MECH-318), the meta-RL account is the more parsimonious one and MECH-318 is potentially redundant.

Meta-RL learning relies on a slow outer-loop training signal (dopamine in the biological reading); if REE's training schedule does not generate analogous slow shaping signals, the inner-loop adaptation that the framework requires will not emerge.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the deliberate counter-current paper. Botvinick and Plaut show that a single recurrent connectionist network can reproduce all the routine-sequential-action behaviour the Cooper-Shallice schema-hierarchy model produces -- including the action-disorganisation-syndrome lesion patterns -- *without any explicit schema hierarchy*. Context is encoded in distributed, recurrent state. This directly weakens the architectural commitment that REE's ARC-062/064/MECH-318 cluster needs an explicit rule-state-abstraction substrate at all. Confidence is calibrated to weakens-direction: this paper is a serious challenge to the explicit-rule-abstraction view, but it has not won the field -- subsequent options/HRL literature continues to assume explicit hierarchical decomposition.
failure_signatures: If REE's existing latent-stack representations (z_world, z_self) when given recurrent dynamics are sufficient to support routine sequential action without an explicit MECH-318 substrate, then MECH-318 is a redundant claim and the relevant Pull 2 R2 verdict is wrong.

Botvinick-Plaut 2004 predicts that recurrent connectionist networks lesioned in their representational substrate will produce ADS-like patterns indistinguishable from schema-hierarchy lesions. If REE's V3 substrate cannot reproduce ADS-like patterns under representational lesion, the connectionist account is the more parsimonious one and MECH-318 should be questioned.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the foundational options framework paper -- the canonical citation for any work on temporally abstract policies. If REE's ARC-064 bottom-up rule discovery produces representations that cannot be translated into options, the claim that 'rule apprehension is policy machinery in different vocabulary' is falsified.

entries.confidence_rationale: RL^2 is the foundational ML implementation of meta-RL. It demonstrates that a recurrent network trained on a distribution of MDPs learns, in its hidden state, a fast inner-loop RL algorithm that adapts to new MDPs without weight updates. For Pull 4 it grounds the Wang 2018 biological-mapping paper in a concrete, well-tested ML framework that REE could adopt directly. Confidence not higher because RL^2 is a preprint that did not get accepted at ICLR (in the published form) and because the empirical demonstrations are simulated bandit/maze tasks rather than the long-horizon continuous-state regimes REE cares about.
failure_signatures: If REE's recurrent latent stack, trained on a distribution of tasks/contexts, does not learn to encode within-episode adaptation policy in its hidden state, the meta-RL transfer fails.

RL^2 known failure mode: the hidden state has limited capacity and meta-learns a *task-distribution-specific* algorithm rather than a general one. If REE adopts RL^2 vocabulary, it inherits this limitation.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the foundational schema-tradition paper that introduced the dual-mechanism architecture (contention scheduling + supervisory attentional system) underpinning four decades of executive-function neuroscience. entries.confidence_rationale: Solway et al. give a normative theory for what makes a behavioural hierarchy optimal -- one that balances task-decomposition entropy with sub-policy reusability -- and provide four behavioural experiments showing humans spontaneously discover hierarchies close to the optimum. entries.confidence_rationale: The option-critic architecture closes the gap between Sutton-Precup-Singh 1999 (formalism) and ARC-064 (we need an option-discovery algorithm). Option-collapse (Bacon 2017's known failure mode: discovered options become trivially short or trivially identical) is the exact REE-side failure pattern observed in V3-EXQ-543 (ARM_1c seed-2 byte-identical to baseline). The diagnostic signatures match across paradigms; the inherited diagnostic tool here is the option-collapse literature.

entries.confidence_rationale: The Wang 2018 meta-RL framing reads context-conditioned policy as a *learned learning algorithm* hosted in PFC recurrent dynamics, with dopamine acting as a slower training signal that shapes the recurrent network into one that can rapidly adapt to new tasks. This gives REE a unified vocabulary for ARC-062 (top-down rule application = meta-learned context-conditioned policy) and the OFC-cognitive-map of MECH-318 (= the recurrent latent state that implements the inner-loop algorithm). Meta-RL learning relies on a slow outer-loop training signal (dopamine in the biological reading); if REE's training schedule does not generate analogous slow shaping signals, the inner-loop adaptation that the framework requires will not emerge.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the deliberate counter-current paper. Botvinick and Plaut show that a single recurrent connectionist network can reproduce all the routine-sequential-action behaviour the Cooper-Shallice schema-hierarchy model produces -- including the action-disorganisation-syndrome lesion patterns -- *without any explicit schema hierarchy*. Context is encoded in distributed, recurrent state. This directly weakens the architectural commitment that REE's ARC-062/064/MECH-318 cluster needs an explicit rule-state-abstraction substrate at all. Confidence is calibrated to weakens-direction: this paper is a serious challenge to the explicit-rule-abstraction view, but it has not won the field -- subsequent options/HRL literature continues to assume explicit hierarchical decomposition.

If REE's V3 substrate cannot reproduce ADS-like patterns under representational lesion, the connectionist account is the more parsimonious one and MECH-318 should be questioned.

entries.confidence_rationale: RL^2 is the foundational ML implementation of meta-RL. It demonstrates that a recurrent network trained on a distribution of MDPs learns, in its hidden state, a fast inner-loop RL algorithm that adapts to new MDPs without weight updates. For Pull 4 it grounds the Wang 2018 biological-mapping paper in a concrete, well-tested ML framework that REE could adopt directly. Confidence not higher because RL^2 is a preprint that did not get accepted at ICLR (in the published form) and because the empirical demonstrations are simulated bandit/maze tasks rather than the long-horizon continuous-state regimes REE cares about.
failure_signatures: If REE's recurrent latent stack, trained on a distribution of tasks/contexts, does not learn to encode within-episode adaptation policy in its hidden state, the meta-RL transfer fails.

RL^2 known failure mode: the hidden state has limited capacity and meta-learns a *task-distribution-specific* algorithm rather than a general one. If REE adopts RL^2 vocabulary, it inherits this limitation.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational empirical demonstration that awake-quiescent hippocampal replay carries content in a temporally-reversed order relative to waking experience. This is the single cleanest piece of evidence that the substrate has a structural property (reverse temporal order) which downstream regions could in principle use as a discriminative signal to distinguish replay-driven inputs from waking inputs -- exactly the substrate-level marker MECH-094's hypothesis-tag would need. Source quality very high (Nature, Wilson lab). Mapping fidelity moderate-to-high (the discriminative-signature exists; whether downstream regions actually USE it as a write-gate is not demonstrated here).
failure_signatures: Foster & Wilson demonstrate the discriminable signature exists but do not test whether any downstream region gates writes on the basis of replay vs waking temporal direction.

The reverse-replay phenomenon is observed during awake quiescent rest immediately after experience, not during arbitrary simulation -- the timing constraint may be too tight for REE's general simulation-mode tag.

entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative review of the canonical SWR substrate and its dual role (retrieval-for-immediate-use vs consolidation). Strong source quality (Nature Reviews Neuroscience, Frank lab). Mapping fidelity is moderate -- the review describes that SWRs route hippocampal content to downstream cortical targets, but does NOT describe a categorical write-gate that distinguishes 'rule applied during simulation/replay' from 'rule applied during waking action' in the specific REE sense (a per-rule tag carried by the simulated trajectory that suppresses the post-commit write channel). The biological substrate has the timing and the routing machinery REE needs, but the literature treats SWR-content downstream effects as continuous strength modulation, not as a discrete simulation-mode tag. Evidence direction MIXED because the substrate exists but the specific REE mechanism (categorical gate) is not what the literature reports.
failure_signatures: Joo & Frank treat SWR-mediated hippocampal-to-cortical communication as a continuous-strength routing event, not as a categorical simulation-vs-action distinction in the receiving cortex's write rules.
The review does not describe any biological substrate that suppresses arbitration-weight updates specifically during replay relative to waking action.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational empirical demonstration that humans optimally track environmental volatility and use it to modulate learning rates, with ACC encoding the volatility estimate. Source quality high (Nature Neuroscience, Rushworth lab). Mapping fidelity is moderate -- Behrens 2007 is the cleanest existing-literature analog for REE's V_s machinery (a substrate-level signal that tracks how trustworthy the world model currently is and modulates downstream learning weights), BUT the resolution is wrong. Behrens 2007 tracks GLOBAL volatility (one volatility estimate per task), whereas REE's V_s is per-region: each region carries its own freshness signal that propagates to rules indexed in that region. This is the key place where REE genuinely diverges from the literature.
failure_signatures: Behrens 2007 estimates volatility at task scope, not at per-region or per-context scope. The closest behavioural extension (Bouton-style contextual renewal) treats context as a categorical retrieval cue, not as a continuous freshness scalar.

The ACC volatility signal in Behrens modulates LEARNING RATE on the global value estimate. REE's V_s modulates RULE TRUST -- whether the rule should be applied at all in this region. These are related but functionally distinct.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical review of context-dependent extinction and renewal effects. Supports REE's premise that per-region/per-context model trust is a real biological phenomenon; weakens the strong-claim version that the literature already has the continuous-scalar machinery REE proposes.

The framework concerns acquisition/extinction of CS-US associations, not the broader REE notion of rule-arbitration weight modulation.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct empirical demonstration that human arbitration between model-based and model-free systems is governed by a cost-benefit calculation (additional accuracy gained vs cognitive cost paid), not by uncertainty alone. This is the cleanest existing-literature evidence that the multi-variable arbitration combination rule REE needs is multiplicative-cost-style rather than uncertainty-only additive. Source quality high (Gershman lab, Psychological Science). Mapping fidelity strong: REE's MECH-312 needs to combine uncertainty + practice/maturity + diversity-pressure + V_s into arbitration weights, and Kool/Gershman/Cushman demonstrate that the human substrate already does combine multiple variables (uncertainty + cost + reward) in a non-trivially-non-additive way.
failure_signatures: The Kool/Gershman/Cushman 2017 paper is two-controller (model-based vs model-free), not three-or-more-controller. The combination rule it documents may not generalise cleanly to REE's 3-channel (uncertainty + practice + diversity) arbitration.

The cost-benefit framing privileges metabolic/cognitive cost as the modulating variable; REE's modulating variables (V_s, practice maturity, diversity pressure) do not map cleanly to cost. The combination rule may need REE-specific adaptation.

entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative primate review documenting the OFC subdivision into distinct value-coding pathways, with the amygdala-OFC interaction supplying affective valence and lateral OFC + IT cortex supplying outcome-identity (sensory-discriminative) information. Mapping fidelity strong: REE's SD-010 (sensory-discriminative harm) / SD-011 (affective harm) split lines up almost directly with the literature's OFC-medial-vs-lateral / amygdala-vs-IT-cortex pathway distinction. entries.confidence_rationale: Computational + EEG/fMRI demonstration that arbitration between Pavlovian and instrumental control is dynamically modulated within a single session, and that the modulation is governed by an inferred controllability variable that is itself a separate computation from per-channel reliability. This is the closest existing-literature evidence that >2-channel arbitration with multiple modulating variables (controllability + reliability + Pavlovian bias) is the norm rather than the exception in biological arbitration. Source quality high (Gershman lab, PLOS Comp Bio). Mapping fidelity moderate -- supports REE's MECH-312 multi-variable claim but the specific channel set (Pavlovian + instrumental) is different from REE's (uncertainty + practice + diversity).
failure_signatures: The Pavlovian-vs-instrumental arbitration framework treats Pavlovian responses as bias terms that competes with instrumental control, not as a co-equal arbitration channel. REE's MECH-312 with 3+ channels of equal status is structurally different.
Controllability inference is itself a Bayesian latent-state estimate; REE has not committed to a normative Bayesian framework for V_s or for arbitration weights more generally.

entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative review of the canonical SWR substrate and its dual role (retrieval-for-immediate-use vs consolidation). Strong source quality (Nature Reviews Neuroscience, Frank lab). Mapping fidelity is moderate -- the review describes that SWRs route hippocampal content to downstream cortical targets, but does NOT describe a categorical write-gate that distinguishes 'rule applied during simulation/replay' from 'rule applied during waking action' in the specific REE sense (a per-rule tag carried by the simulated trajectory that suppresses the post-commit write channel). The biological substrate has the timing and the routing machinery REE needs, but the literature treats SWR-content downstream effects as continuous strength modulation, not as a discrete simulation-mode tag. Evidence direction MIXED because the substrate exists but the specific REE mechanism (categorical gate) is not what the literature reports.
failure_signatures: Joo & Frank treat SWR-mediated hippocampal-to-cortical communication as a continuous-strength routing event, not as a categorical simulation-vs-action distinction in the receiving cortex's write rules.
The review does not describe any biological substrate that suppresses arbitration-weight updates specifically during replay relative to waking action.

Mapping fidelity strong: REE's SD-010 (sensory-discriminative harm) / SD-011 (affective harm) split lines up almost directly with the literature's OFC-medial-vs-lateral / amygdala-vs-IT-cortex pathway distinction. The literature does NOT explicitly frame these as 'arbitration weight inputs' (the closest framing is 'value-component contributions to choice'), so REE's MECH-312-d affective-stream-modulation framing is a closely related but slightly extended interpretation.

This entry mainly cross-supports the Murray-Rudebeck stream-separation argument from a different angle (cortical-coordination-of-significance-evaluation rather than primate-OFC-anatomy).

Canonical ACC lesion study showing that excitotoxic anterior cingulate lesions in rats reverse high-effort/high-reward preference toward low-effort/low-reward on a T-maze cost-benefit task. This is foundational evidence that ACC carries effort-cost computation, but the readout is about WILLINGNESS-TO-EXPEND-EFFORT-FOR-A-SPECIFIC-REWARD (i.e. cost-benefit weighing in the presence of an active goal), not about general capacity-keyed action drive that ARC-066 names. The user briefing cites the canonical Walton 2003 J Neurosci paper as an ACC effort/vigor anchor; on close reading, the paper supports ACC's role in effort-cost computation more cleanly than it supports ARC-066's specific function. Mapped as mixed: the ACC effort-cost machinery is plausibly recruited in service of any vigor scalar, but the paper's direct evidence is for goal-directed effort allocation, which is closer to existing SD-032b dACC adaptive-control / ARC-068 opportunity-cost territory than to ARC-066. Confidence reflects this scope mismatch.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that does not represent effort-cost as a substrate-level computation will fail to reproduce Walton's lesion pattern: differential preference for high-effort options should disappear under simulated ACC ablation. ARC-066 is not the right substrate for this -- SD-032b (dACC adaptive control) is the closer existing relative.

If ARC-066's child mechanism is wired to depend on ACC integrity, the model should simulate the Walton 2003 lesion-reversal pattern; if the ARC-066 substrate is correctly attributed to mesolimbic DA, the lesion-reversal should still occur (DA-mediated activational state recruits ACC for cost-benefit computation), but ARC-066's primary signal should survive ACC ablation.

entries.confidence_rationale: The Behavioral and Brain Sciences target article that grounds the BAS (behavioural approach / activation system) as a tonic personality dimension keyed to dopaminergic VTA-NAcc-PFC circuitry. Depue & Collins propose that individual differences in extraversion / agency reflect a tonic-baseline difference in this system, with low BAS = anhedonic inertia and high BAS = generalised drive-to-act. This is the strongest support for the ABSTRACT-LEVEL architectural commitment ARC-066 makes (capacity-keyed target-free action drive as a substrate-level function), but the paper is conceptual and trait-level rather than mechanistic. Confidence reflects: strong abstract-level support, weak mechanistic detail, no direct empirical test of the target-free claim. Together with Niv 2007 / Salamone & Correa / Beierholm 2013, this paper closes the substrate identity (DA-keyed) + abstract-level commitment (target-free) cluster.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that does not implement a target-free behavioural-approach scalar will fail to reproduce the inter-individual variation Depue & Collins describe: low-BAS-equivalent agents should show generalised behavioural inertia even in the presence of preserved harm avoidance and target-specific wanting. This is the clinical phenotype of anhedonic / abulic depression that Depue & Collins anchor to.

If ARC-066 is wired such that its scalar collapses onto target-specific wanting (MECH-216) under all conditions, the model will fail to reproduce the Depue & Collins distinction between BAS reactivity (response to specific incentives) and BAS tonic baseline (general drive).

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct human-pharmacological causal test of Niv 2007's prediction that the average reward rate drives vigor via dopamine. Double-blind, three-arm design (placebo / L-DOPA / citalopram) in 90 healthy subjects on an odd-ball discrimination task with experimentally varied reward. Result: the relationship between average reward rate and response vigor (faster RTs at higher reward history) was significantly stronger under L-DOPA than placebo. This is the load-bearing human empirical anchor for the R1 DA-vigor substrate attribution and converges with Niv 2007's theoretical formalism. Confidence weighted down from a higher value by two caveats: (1) L-DOPA elevates both tonic and phasic DA, so the dissociation Niv 2007 specifically claims (TONIC DA encodes avg reward rate) is not cleanly tested; (2) the readout is RT-on-discrimination, which is closer to vigor-of-execution than to act-vs-not-act selection.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that does not implement an avg-reward-rate-modulated action-vigor scalar will fail to reproduce the Beierholm pattern: under simulated L-DOPA-equivalent gain on the scalar, the coupling between reward history and action density should strengthen.

If the ARC-066 child mechanism is wired to a single-episode reward integrator (fast window), it will fail Beierholm's design implicitly: the L-DOPA effect emerged on within-session integration of reward history across many trials, indicating a long-window scalar.

entries.confidence_rationale: Pre-registered as a primary anchor for ARC-066 with the explicit gloss that LC-NE tonic mode provides a directional bias TOWARD action (distinct from MECH-313's noise function). The 2005 theoretical framework is consistent with that reading at the conceptual level (tonic mode = disengagement + search for alternatives = directional shift toward exploration / action). However, the same authors' subsequent direct empirical test (Kane et al. 2017, separate entry) found LC-NE tonic effects are noise-mediated, not directional. This entry is therefore mixed: the 2005 theoretical paper is the original architectural anchor for the LC-NE-direction reading of ARC-066, but the 2017 follow-up by the same group weakens that reading. The lower confidence (0.62 vs the 0.84 it received as the LC-NE-substrate anchor in ARC-065) reflects the R2-verdict downgrade: this paper is now evidence for what ARC-066 is NOT (i.e., not an LC-NE-direction function distinct from MECH-313).
failure_signatures: If REE attempts to instantiate ARC-066 as an LC-NE-direction analog based on the Aston-Jones & Cohen 2005 framework, it will fail to compose with MECH-313 (already substrate-landed as the LC-NE noise floor). The original theoretical disambiguation between phasic-mode-as-exploitation and tonic-mode-as-exploration was shown by Kane 2017 to collapse the 'tonic-mode-as-exploration' channel into a noise effect, which is what MECH-313 already implements.

If a future child mechanism for ARC-066 cites Aston-Jones 2005 as primary substrate evidence without citing Kane 2017 as the disambiguating empirical test, governance review should flag the omission. Current evidence supports MESOLIMBIC DA (Salamone, Niv) as the ARC-066 substrate, not LC-NE.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the load-bearing R2 paper. Kane et al. ran a direct causal test of the Aston-Jones LC-NE-tonic-mode prediction in rats using DREADDs to selectively elevate LC tonic activity, and explicitly modelled whether the resulting earlier patch-leaving was best explained by (a) increased decision noise or (b) a directional bias on the leave threshold. The published finding is unambiguous: noise-best-explanation, no detectable directional shift. This is the strongest available empirical evidence on whether LC-NE tonic mode provides a SEPARATE directional-action-bias function distinct from MECH-313's noise floor. The verdict is that LC-NE tonic mode is one mechanism (noise), not two -- pushing ARC-066's substrate attribution AWAY from LC-NE and TOWARD mesolimbic DA / BAS.
failure_signatures: If REE attributes ARC-066 to an LC-NE-direction substrate analog, it will fail to reproduce Kane 2017's empirical pattern. The published evidence is that LC-NE tonic effect on patch-leaving is noise-mediated, not direction-mediated -- a directional-bias-only LC-NE mechanism would produce a different pattern (consistent leave-threshold shift, reduced variance) than what Kane observed.

If a future REE child mechanism for ARC-066 is wired with LC-NE-mediated gain modulation, it should be expected to compose redundantly with MECH-313 (which already covers LC-NE noise), and the Kane 2017 caveat means the directional-bias function would have no clear biological substrate to anchor it.

entries.confidence_rationale: Salamone & Correa make the cleanest published case for dissociating mesolimbic DA's role in BEHAVIOURAL ACTIVATION / EXERTION OF EFFORT / SUSTAINED TASK ENGAGEMENT (the activational dimension) from its role in HEDONIC value or consummatory liking. The dissociation is grounded in decades of pharmacology data (DA antagonist / accumbens DA depletion experiments) showing instrumental / preparatory / approach behaviour is selectively impaired while consumption is preserved. This is load-bearing for R1: it gives ARC-066 a mesolimbic DA substrate that is target-INDEPENDENT (about behavioural activation generally) rather than tied to specific reward delivery. Slightly weakened by the paper's exclusively rodent/primate pharmacology grounding -- the human version of this dissociation is in companion papers (Treadway, Beierholm, Chong) not in Salamone & Correa directly.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that wires ARC-066 to the same mechanism as z_goal-driven wanting (specific-target seeking) will fail to reproduce the Salamone & Correa dissociation: DA depletion should selectively impair effortful instrumental responding while leaving consummatory choice intact. If REE collapses these into one substrate, the dissociation cannot be reproduced.

An REE substrate that ties ARC-066 to hedonic 'liking' (MECH-295) will fail: the literature is explicit that DA effort-vigor activation is dissociable from hedonic value. ARC-066 should compose with but not be substituted for liking.

entries.confidence_rationale: Theoretical-formal anchor for the average-reward-rate / tonic-DA / vigor account. The opportunity-cost derivation makes the architectural commitment of ARC-066 mathematically explicit (a long-run average reward rate enters the cost-benefit equation as an additive cost on time-spent-passive, equivalently an additive bonus on time-spent-acting). Companion empirical paper Beierholm 2013 provides the human-pharmacological causal test, which is the reason this is not the highest-confidence entry on its own. Cited >2200 times; load-bearing for R1 substrate-attribution and R3 implementation-shape verdicts.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that does not maintain a long-window average-reward-rate integrator will fail to reproduce Niv's vigor-as-opportunity-cost predictions: response latencies should shorten as the average reward history rises, even when the local reward expectation is unchanged. Without ARC-066, REE has no signal that produces this scaling -- z_goal targets are local, not history-integrated.

If the ARC-066 child mechanism uses a fast (single-episode) reward-rate integrator instead of a slow (across-episode) one, the vigor signal will collapse onto z_goal and fail Niv's distinguishing prediction that vigor is set by long-run reward history independent of any specific currently-pursued target.

Nature Reviews Neuroscience transdiagnostic synthesis of apathy and anhedonia using effort-based decision-making framework. Highest-relevance R5 paper -- it provides the substrate framing (frontostriatal circuits: VTA -> ventral striatum / NAcc / ventral pallidum -> mPFC / dACC) for what an ARC-067 ablation phenotype maps onto clinically. Critically: distinguishes apathy (motivation/effort failure) from anhedonia (reward-experience failure) at substrate level, which constrains the R5 cross-reference. Source quality very high; mapping fidelity strong for R5 anchor; transfer risk moderate.
failure_signatures: If ARC-067 ablation produces a phenotype that LOOKS like anhedonia (reward-experience flattening, MECH-295 liking-channel collapse) rather than apathy (effort-allocation failure, action-pressure absence), then ARC-067 is being mistakenly mapped onto a reward-experience substrate rather than an action-recruitment substrate. The R5 verdict is that ARC-067 ablation should produce APATHY-like signatures specifically -- effort-allocation failure under preserved reward-experience -- not generic anhedonia.

If the substrate underlying clinical apathy is not located in the frontostriatal circuit Husain & Roiser identify, the R5 cross-reference will need to anchor on a different substrate class, but the apathy-vs-anhedonia distinction itself remains valid at the phenotype level and constrains the cross-reference.

entries.confidence_rationale: Empirical paper differentiating boredom from neighbouring negative emotions (sadness, anger, frustration, disappointment, regret) on appraisal, action-tendency, and feeling dimensions. Key R5 anchor: boredom is mild in negative valence, low in arousal, low in perceived challenge AND low in perceived meaningfulness; the meaning-deficit and attention-deficit signatures are jointly distinctive. Critically for ARC-067: boredom motivates re-establishment of meaningfulness, NOT generic stimulation -- this constrains the engagement-rate estimator. Source quality moderate (peer-reviewed, top-tier emotion journal, multi-experiment empirical), mapping fidelity strong for the differentiation question, transfer risk modest.
failure_signatures: An ARC-067 substrate that produces a HIGH-arousal aversive (rather than the low-arousal aversive van Tilburg & Igou observe empirically) will fail the differentiation test against frustration and anger -- those are also engagement-failure signals but with high-arousal signatures. The boredom aversive must be specifically low-arousal-but-action-recruiting, which is unusual and requires explicit substrate.

If the boredom-driven action-pressure recruits any-stimulation rather than meaningful-stimulation, the substrate will reproduce stimulation-seeking but not the meaning-seeking signature van Tilburg & Igou identify as distinctive. This boundary distinguishes ARC-067 from MECH-314a striatal novelty bonus -- novelty alone is not enough to discharge boredom under van Tilburg's account.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct fMRI study of induced boredom against sustained-attention and resting-state controls. Key finding for R3: boredom and sustained-attention conditions both show anticorrelated anterior insula activity relative to DMN posterior regions, distinguishable from rest. The anterior insula deactivation in boredom is the load-bearing anatomical anchor for routing-channel verdict. Source quality moderate-high (peer-reviewed neuroscience venue, video-based mood induction methodology); mapping fidelity strong for R3 routing; transfer risk moderate because fMRI BOLD signatures translate indirectly to REE substrate routing.
failure_signatures: An ARC-067 substrate that does not anatomically locate the boredom-aversive in an AIC-analog component (i.e., routes the engagement-rate aversive through the same substrate as homeostatic deficit signals like SD-012, rather than through the affective harm stream SD-011) will produce a different network-level signature than Danckert & Merrifield observe -- predicting that an REE-fMRI analog (residue-write distribution, channel utilisation patterns) should not match the boredom signature.

If boredom is implemented through MECH-216 predictive-wanting variants (target-conditioned), the network signature should look more like striatal/vmPFC reward-circuit activity than the AIC-deactivation Danckert observes -- the distinction matters for disambiguation against MECH-216.

entries.confidence_rationale: Functional review arguing that boredom serves an adaptive role: motivating pursuit of new goals when the current goal is no longer beneficial. The functional-role argument is convergent with van Tilburg & Igou 2017 but framed at a coarser level (goal-pursuit-shift rather than meaning-seeking-action). Source quality moderate (open-access journal, peer-reviewed but lower-tier than Psych Review or Emotion); high relevance to R1 functional account but the mechanism specification is less detailed than van Tilburg or Westgate. Mapping fidelity strong for the goal-shift framing.
failure_signatures: An ARC-067 substrate that produces aversive pressure but no goal-shift behaviour (the agent merely sits and feels the aversive without changing direction) fails Bench & Lench's functional account -- boredom is supposed to drive the agent off its current trajectory toward an alternative, not merely to register dissatisfaction.

If the boredom-driven goal-shift is indiscriminate (any new goal, regardless of expected value), the substrate produces erratic switching rather than the value-sensitive shift Bench & Lench describe. This boundary distinguishes ARC-067 from a pure stimulation-seeking mechanism.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational Nature Reviews piece on HPA-axis stress regulation. High source quality, but mapping to ARC-067 is INDIRECT -- the paper does not address boredom specifically; it addresses physical and psychological stress more generally. Relevance is for the R2 chronic-timescale verdict and as substrate context for the R5 anhedonia/abulia anchor: chronic understimulation regimes produce HPA-axis dysregulation, which is one candidate substrate-mapping for the chronic-anhedonic-flatness pole of the timescale split. Direction is 'mixed' because the paper neither directly supports nor weakens ARC-067; it provides substrate context but the specific mapping to chronic boredom is inferential.
failure_signatures: If ARC-067's chronic timescale is implemented as a simple slow-extension of the acute mechanism (single-substrate, two-rate-constant model) and the chronic substrate maps onto HPA-axis-like dysregulation, the predicted ablation signature should resemble HPA-related anhedonic phenotypes (cortisol-flat-affect signatures). An ARC-067 substrate without a chronic-axis component will fail to reproduce these phenotypes if R2 splits the timescales.

If chronic understimulation does NOT engage HPA-axis substrates in REE-analogous ways, the chronic-pole of the R2 split needs a different substrate framing (purely-cortical accumulator, dopaminergic mesolimbic, etc.) -- this paper bounds but does not settle the substrate.

entries.confidence_rationale: Eleven-study Science paper showing that participants find spending 6-15 minutes alone with their thoughts so aversive that many self-administer electric shocks rather than continue. Directly demonstrates the architectural commitment ARC-067 names: doing-nothing is not neutral, it is actively aversive enough to recruit costly action. Behavioural-aversive evidence is the strongest possible support short of direct neuroimaging. Source quality very high (Science, multiple replications across 11 studies); transfer risk modest because the demonstration is on enforced disengagement rather than lifelong-low-engagement steady state.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that treats no-op as zero-cost (no aversive accumulation under enforced disengagement) directly fails to reproduce the Wilson 2014 finding. The agent should prefer a costly action (analog: a small-but-nonzero z_harm cost or resource cost) to continued no-op when no other action is available.

If the boredom aversive accumulates only over very long timescales (chronic / sessions only), the substrate will fail Wilson's 6-to-15-minute experimental window -- the acute timescale must produce measurable aversive within tens of episodes, not just over hundreds. This supports R2's acute/chronic timescale split.

entries.confidence_rationale: Top-tier theoretical paper in Psychological Review proposing the Meaning-and-Attentional-Component (MAC) model. Decomposes boredom into two semi-independent profiles: (a) attentional misfit (cognitive demands vs available resources, both under- and over-stimulation), and (b) meaning misfit (activities vs valued goals, or absence of valued goals). The two-component decomposition is the load-bearing R1 finding -- it forces the verdict away from a single-cause functional account toward a compositional one. Source quality very high; mapping fidelity high for the architectural shape; transfer risk modest.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that implements only a single-component boredom (engagement-rate aversive, no meaning component) will fail to discriminate between MAC-attentional and MAC-meaning profiles -- e.g., it will collapse over- and under-stimulated boredom into one signal when MAC predicts they should arise from different substrates with different downstream signatures.

If the MAC two-component decomposition is correct, a discriminative test pair should hold: under-stimulation arms (low cognitive demand, low novelty) and meaning-violation arms (high engagement but goal-incongruent task) should both produce boredom-like behaviour, but with separable internal signatures. An ARC-067 substrate that implements only the engagement-rate channel will fail the meaning-violation arm.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational definitional paper that synthesises psychodynamic, existential, arousal, and cognitive theories of boredom into a single attention-anchored construct: 'the aversive experience of wanting, but being unable, to engage in satisfying activity.' Highest-relevance R1 paper for the functional-emotion-engagement-search account. Mapping to ARC-067 is direct: the architectural commitment that prolonged low-engagement is itself aversive maps onto Eastwood's 'wanting-to-engage-but-unable' definition. Source quality strong (peer-reviewed integrative review in Perspectives on Psychological Science); transfer risk modest because the construct is human-introspective and the REE substrate is computational, but the functional shape transfers cleanly.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that does not produce action-pressure under sustained low-engagement (well-fed, safe, familiar, no z_goal) will fail to reproduce the Eastwood 'wanting-to-engage-but-unable' phenomenology and thus will not exhibit the boredom-driven exploratory behaviour Eastwood treats as definitional.

If the ARC-067 mechanism is implemented as inverted novelty (novelty-bonus going negative when novelty rate is low), the substrate will incorrectly mark genuinely novel-but-non-interactive territory as engaging, which Eastwood's definition rules out -- the agent is bored if it wants engagement but cannot achieve it, regardless of stimulus novelty.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct biological grounding for the dual-systems architecture (DLS habit / DMS goal-directed) that MECH-163 names. Yin & Knowlton synthesise the lesion + outcome-devaluation evidence that operationalises the goal-directed-vs-habit distinction. Source quality high (Nat Rev Neurosci, ~5000 citations). The R3 LOAD-BEARING verdict for the synthesis -- this paper anchors that the dual systems exist with substrate-distinct loci, and provides the framework within which ARC-071 names the planned->habitual transition mechanism. Mapping fidelity is the load-bearing component.
failure_signatures: DLS lesions PRESERVE goal-directed control even after overtraining -- if ARC-071 substrate is removed, the agent should fall back cleanly to MECH-163 planned-system control without breakdown of behaviour. This is a sharp falsifiable prediction.

Habit formation signature is impervious-to-outcome-devaluation -- ARC-071-formed chunks should be selectable based on context-cue-match even when the chunked-sequence's outcome value drops. If REE chunks remain value-sensitive after composition, ARC-071 implementation is wrong substrate-locus.
DMS and DLS operate in parallel during transition with interdependency -- ARC-071 implementation must NOT be a clean either/or switch; the two systems coexist and compete during learning.

entries.confidence_rationale: The empirical paper that closes the chunk-level mapping Yin & Knowlton 2006 left implicit. Recordings in DLS and infralimbic cortex during overtraining show distinct time courses for chunk crystallisation; selective optogenetic disruption of IL during overtraining PREVENTS habit formation. This is causal manipulation, not just correlational. Settles R3 (transition mechanism) at the chunk-substrate level and supplies the R5 chunk-dynamics evidence (chunks form, dissolve, reform across timescales). High mapping fidelity to ARC-071's composition direction. Source quality high (Neuron, optogenetic causal, multi-region recording).
failure_signatures: Infralimbic cortex disruption prevents habit formation -- ARC-071 substrate is NOT just striatum-analog; a cortical (IL-analog) component is required. Pure-striatal ARC-071 implementations will fail to chunk.

Striatal task-bracketing pattern is reward-devaluation-INSENSITIVE while IL pattern remains reward-sensitive late -- the two operators have different evaluation properties. ARC-071 implementation must distinguish the chunk-execution pattern (devaluation-insensitive) from the chunk-maintenance pattern (devaluation-sensitive).

Chunks form, dissolve, and reform across overtraining -- ARC-071 must support chunk DISSOLUTION (not just formation). The slot's notes mention this implicitly via ARC-070; the synthesis should pin the dissolution-vs-decomposition relation explicitly.

entries.confidence_rationale: Decade-after follow-up to Graybiel 1998 with substantially more empirical evidence available. Reframes chunking as the output of an evaluative-brain process: circuits mediating evaluation of actions gradually lead to selection of particular behaviors that, through chunking, become habits. The evaluative-circuit framing matters for ARC-071's outcome-consistency requirement -- chunking is not just repetition but repetition-conditioned-on-evaluation. Source quality high (Annu Rev Neurosci review by the field's lead author). Mapping fidelity 0.85 -- gives more parametric grounding than 1998 but also broadens scope to ritual/compulsion territory beyond ARC-071's policy-composition slot.
failure_signatures: Habits and rituals share substrate with addiction and OCD -- ARC-071 implementation should expect failure modes mirroring these clinical signatures (chunks-without-evaluation, chunks-resistant-to-decomposition).
The evaluative circuit is upstream of chunking -- ARC-071 must be downstream of (or gated by) an evaluation-of-outcomes signal, not standalone.

entries.confidence_rationale: The load-bearing source for R4 (chunks-of-chunks recursion). Botvinick et al. extend the options framework to deep behavioural hierarchies and map components onto prefrontal substrate (rostro-caudal and orbital prefrontal). Provides both formal grounding for recursive chunking and biological-constraint evidence for natural depth limits. Source is in Cognition not TiCS as the briefing pre-registered; same lead author published a related paper in TiCS 2008. Mapping fidelity 0.78 -- direct on hierarchy and recursion; the prefrontal-substrate detail is REE-relevant via vmPFC analog.
failure_signatures: Behavioural hierarchy is divisible into discrete tasks containing subtask sequences containing simple actions -- ARC-071 should permit recursion (chunks-of-chunks) up to 2-3 levels in healthy operation; deeper hierarchies are biologically rare and likely unstable.

Hierarchical organisation maps onto rostro-caudal prefrontal substrate -- ARC-071 implementation must respect grain-substrate matching (deeper hierarchy = more rostral substrate); collapsing to flat substrate will fail to express the hierarchy.

Reusable subroutines (options) require both an initiation set and a termination condition -- ARC-071 chunks need explicit context-keyed initiation triggers (when does the chunk fire?) and termination conditions (when does the chunk complete?); pure repetition-counter implementations without these will produce mis-fired chunks.

entries.confidence_rationale: Human fMRI evidence for the multi-substrate chunking machinery -- putamen supports concatenation (chunking IN), frontoparietal cortex supports segmentation (chunking OUT, ARC-070-direction). This is the cleanest human-substrate paper for R2 (substrate locus): chunking is NOT one substrate but at least two operating at different phases. Source quality high (Neuron, 3-day longitudinal fMRI design with dynamic network analysis). Mapping fidelity 0.80 -- the concatenation / segmentation distinction maps directly onto ARC-071 / ARC-070 within the family doc.
failure_signatures: Chunking is two processes (concatenation / segmentation), not one -- ARC-071 (composition) and ARC-070 (decomposition) are not redundant or symmetric inverses; they have substrate-distinct implementations. The family doc's symmetric framing should be tightened.

Putamen supports concatenation; frontoparietal cortex supports segmentation -- ARC-071 substrate is putamen-analog (DLS), ARC-070 substrate is frontoparietal-analog (vmPFC + parietal). Substrate non-redundancy is empirically grounded.

Chunking process differs between early and late training phases -- the segmentation (ARC-070) process happens more early in learning, concatenation (ARC-071) happens more late. Trigger asymmetry within the cluster matches the pre-registered fast-decomposition vs slow-composition framing.

entries.confidence_rationale: Cleanest formal analog of policy composition. The options framework gives ARC-071 the formal vocabulary -- options are exactly chunked-primitive equivalents (closed-loop policies with initiation set, termination condition, and internal policy). Source quality high (founding paper, ~6000 citations, Sutton-Precup-Singh). The mapping is formal-not-biological, which is the dominant caveat: ARC-071 needs to instantiate options-like structure in REE substrate, not just reproduce options on top of REE primitives.
failure_signatures: Options have three required fields: policy, initiation set, termination condition -- ARC-071 chunks cannot be just a sequence; they must carry context-keyed initiation and completion conditions. Pure-sequence implementations without these will mis-fire.

Options-discovery is the open problem in hierarchical RL -- the options framework SUPPLIES the formalism but does NOT settle how options are discovered. ARC-071's biological-trigger commitment (repetition + outcome consistency) is the biology-side answer to the discovery problem; the formal framework does not constrain it.

Options compose with primitive actions interchangeably -- ARC-071 chunks must be selectable in the same selection step as their constituent primitives, not in a separate hierarchy-only selection step.

entries.confidence_rationale: Load-bearing R6 source -- weakens the assumption that biology cleanly distinguishes real-executed from imagined/replayed in the chunking write path. Joint hippocampal-striatal reactivations during sleep, with hippocampal activity LEADING ventral striatal replays, drive sleep-dependent motor sequence consolidation including chunk crystallisation. This means biology DOES allow replay-driven plasticity in the chunking circuit -- sleep-replay is part of the chunking machinery, not gated out of it. ARC-071's strict MECH-094 hypothesis_tag=False gating is therefore biologically MORE CONSERVATIVE than reality, which has substantive safety-vs-realism tradeoff implications for REE. High mapping fidelity (this is the question R6 asks); high source quality (Hippocampus journal, well-replicated finding).
failure_signatures: Sleep replay drives motor consolidation INCLUDING chunk-level changes -- biology does NOT cleanly gate the chunking write path against replay. ARC-071 implementation in REE can either (a) be MORE CONSERVATIVE than biology by enforcing strict hypothesis_tag=False gating (current MECH-094 design), trading off some realism for safety; or (b) permit replay-driven chunking, matching biology but exposing the agent to hallucinated-chunk risk.

Hippocampal-striatal coupling during sleep is reward-prediction-biased -- if ARC-071 permits replay-driven chunking, it should be VALUE-CONDITIONED (only consolidate replays of high-reward sequences). REE's analog would be E3-score-conditioned replay-chunking.

REE has a pre-existing architectural gap registered here -- biology says sleep replay does chunk, MECH-094 says simulation must not chunk. This is a substantive conflict the synthesis should escalate as a NEW REE GAP, not just a parameter choice.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational reference establishing the chunking-of-action-repertoires construct in the striatum. Cited >2000 times. Direct mapping to ARC-071's compose-on-repetition commitment. Substrate identity (striatum) and direction (sequence -> single performance unit) both nailed. Mapping fidelity is the dominant component; the only caveat is that the 1998 paper proposes the construct rather than testing it experimentally, so source_quality is rated on conceptual rigour and subsequent empirical validation rather than primary data in the paper itself.
failure_signatures: ARC-071 must accumulate over (sequence, outcome) pairs, not over (sequence) alone -- Graybiel 1998 is explicit that S-R learning shapes the chunked unit; without outcome-keyed accumulation the slot is mis-specified.
Recoding-of-cortically-derived-information happens within the striatum, not in cortex -- ARC-071 substrate must be a striatum-analog, not a generic policy-cache.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct human-behavioural evidence for spontaneous chunking with quantified chunk-size constraints (typically 2-4 items, sometimes 5). This is the load-bearing R5 source for parameterising the outcome-consistency threshold and the chunk-size budget. The reference-time-gap operationalisation (chunks identified by inter-element-time clustering) is a clean behavioural signature ARC-071 implementations can mirror. Source is the original Sakai paper, though the briefing mistakenly placed it in Curr Op Neurobiol (it is in Exp Brain Res). Mapping fidelity 0.78 -- the chunk-size-budget evidence translates directly; the reference task is finger-sequence learning so the motor-chunk grain is fine-grained.
failure_signatures: Chunks are typically 2-4 items, sometimes 5 -- ARC-071 should default to small-grain chunks; chunks-of-15 are biologically unusual and likely indicate over-aggressive accumulator parameters.

Chunks are identified by inter-element TIME GAPS -- ARC-071's chunk-execution signature should emit a faster within-chunk timing than between-chunk timing; this is a direct behavioural test of whether chunks formed.
Subjects spontaneously chunk during sequence learning without instruction -- ARC-071 implementation should fire automatically, not require explicit goal-driven chunking instruction.
