entries.confidence_rationale: Direct biological grounding for the dual-systems architecture (DLS habit / DMS goal-directed) that MECH-163 names. Yin & Knowlton synthesise the lesion + outcome-devaluation evidence that operationalises the goal-directed-vs-habit distinction. Source quality high (Nat Rev Neurosci, ~5000 citations). The R3 LOAD-BEARING verdict for the synthesis -- this paper anchors that the dual systems exist with substrate-distinct loci, and provides the framework within which ARC-071 names the planned->habitual transition mechanism. Mapping fidelity is the load-bearing component.
failure_signatures: DLS lesions PRESERVE goal-directed control even after overtraining -- if ARC-071 substrate is removed, the agent should fall back cleanly to MECH-163 planned-system control without breakdown of behaviour. This is a sharp falsifiable prediction.

Habit formation signature is impervious-to-outcome-devaluation -- ARC-071-formed chunks should be selectable based on context-cue-match even when the chunked-sequence's outcome value drops. If REE chunks remain value-sensitive after composition, ARC-071 implementation is wrong substrate-locus.
DMS and DLS operate in parallel during transition with interdependency -- ARC-071 implementation must NOT be a clean either/or switch; the two systems coexist and compete during learning.

entries.confidence_rationale: The empirical paper that closes the chunk-level mapping Yin & Knowlton 2006 left implicit. Recordings in DLS and infralimbic cortex during overtraining show distinct time courses for chunk crystallisation; selective optogenetic disruption of IL during overtraining PREVENTS habit formation. This is causal manipulation, not just correlational. Settles R3 (transition mechanism) at the chunk-substrate level and supplies the R5 chunk-dynamics evidence (chunks form, dissolve, reform across timescales). High mapping fidelity to ARC-071's composition direction. Source quality high (Neuron, optogenetic causal, multi-region recording).
failure_signatures: Infralimbic cortex disruption prevents habit formation -- ARC-071 substrate is NOT just striatum-analog; a cortical (IL-analog) component is required. Pure-striatal ARC-071 implementations will fail to chunk.

Striatal task-bracketing pattern is reward-devaluation-INSENSITIVE while IL pattern remains reward-sensitive late -- the two operators have different evaluation properties. ARC-071 implementation must distinguish the chunk-execution pattern (devaluation-insensitive) from the chunk-maintenance pattern (devaluation-sensitive).

Chunks form, dissolve, and reform across overtraining -- ARC-071 must support chunk DISSOLUTION (not just formation). The slot's notes mention this implicitly via ARC-070; the synthesis should pin the dissolution-vs-decomposition relation explicitly.

entries.confidence_rationale: Theoretical anchor for R3 (hierarchy depth) and R5 (decomposition as cascaded control). Koechlin & Summerfield's cascade model formalises the rostro-caudal hierarchy as a sequence of nested control signals: premotor cortex selects sensorimotor responses, posterior LPFC selects S-R mappings according to immediate context, anterior LPFC selects context-mappings according to current episode. This is a clean information-theoretic decomposition of executive control into multiple levels, complementing Badre & D'Esposito 2009's empirical review. R3 multi-level verdict gets a second strong anchor; R5 (bottleneck-state vs error-driven) gets indirect support because cascaded control is a structural -- not error-driven -- decomposition framework. Lower confidence than Badre because Koechlin's empirical anchor is narrower (specific cascading-control tasks) and the model has been partially refined by subsequent work.
failure_signatures: An ARC-070 child-MECH that uses ONLY error-driven decomposition (no structural / level-keyed component) will fail to reproduce Koechlin's cascading control phenomena, where decomposition follows the structure of the task hierarchy regardless of momentary prediction error. The mechanism likely needs both an error-driven trigger AND a structural / level-keyed substrate.

If REE's rule-apprehension layer (ARC-062) operates only at the chunk grain output by ARC-070's decomposition, the architecture will lose the multi-level rule-application signature Koechlin documents -- different rules apply at different cascade levels, and the rule-apprehension layer should be sensitive to level.

entries.confidence_rationale: Substrate-level anchor for the pattern-separation machinery that supports decomposition. Schapiro et al. show the hippocampus implements complementary learning systems WITHIN itself -- the trisynaptic pathway (entorhinal cortex -> dentate gyrus -> CA3 -> CA1) supports episodic memorisation through pattern-separated representations, while the monosynaptic pathway (entorhinal cortex -> CA1) supports statistical learning of regularities. This dual machinery is the substrate on which decomposition operates: pattern-separation makes the chunked primitive separable into discriminable sub-elements, statistical learning makes the regularities across primitives apprehensible. Indirect ARC-070 anchor: it grounds the claim that the hippocampus has the substrate to support both grain levels (episodic chunks via trisynaptic, statistical patterns via monosynaptic). Lower confidence because the mapping to decomposition-on-prediction-failure is multi-step and the paper itself addresses memory rather than rollout directly.
failure_signatures: If REE's hippocampal rollout substrate uses only one representational pathway (e.g. only pattern-separated discrete primitives), it will fail to support the multi-grain decomposition Schapiro et al. document as native to the hippocampus. The substrate likely needs both pattern-separated discrete representations (for chunked primitives) and overlapping statistical representations (for grain-invariant rules across primitives).

If decomposition operates only on the discrete-primitive pathway without engaging statistical regularities, the rule-apprehension layer (ARC-062) reading the decomposed sequence will lose the grain-invariant rule signature -- the same pattern is encoded at multiple grains in the hippocampus, and ARC-062 should be able to read whichever grain is most predictive.

entries.confidence_rationale: Computational anchor for R5 (bottleneck-state vs error-driven decomposition verdict). McGovern & Barto's diverse-density subgoal discovery is the canonical computational treatment of bottleneck-state decomposition: a state is a subgoal candidate if it appears on many paths to a successful outcome (a 'doorway' connecting strongly-connected regions). The mechanism produces hierarchical decomposition by carving the state-action graph at bottleneck states and inserting options. R5 verdict consequence: bottleneck-state and error-driven framings are NOT the same mechanism in the McGovern-Barto formulation -- bottlenecks are STATISTICALLY identified (frequency on paths) rather than PE-driven. This is a substantive architectural alternative the synthesis must adjudicate. evidence_direction=mixed because the paper supports the EXISTENCE of decomposition machinery in computational systems but its specific mechanism (statistical bottleneck discovery) is NOT what the biological-anchor papers favour for ARC-070's primary trigger -- the synthesis recommends PE-driven primary with bottleneck-aware secondary as a fallback design rather than McGovern-Barto's primary scheme.
failure_signatures: If REE's ARC-070 child-MECH uses ONLY a statistical-frequency bottleneck-discovery mechanism without an error-driven trigger, it will produce decomposition only for repeatedly-visited graph topologies and will miss the imagination-side / one-shot decomposition the biological literature documents.

If REE's ARC-070 ignores the bottleneck-state framing entirely and uses only PE-driven triggers, it will fail to capture the natural decomposition structure of state spaces with strongly-connected regions linked by narrow doorways -- a class of problems where McGovern-Barto's mechanism specifically excels.

entries.confidence_rationale: Load-bearing anchor for R2 (the LOAD-BEARING verdict of this pull). Schacter / Addis / Buckner consolidate the empirical evidence that imagining future events recruits substantially the same core neural network (medial PFC, medial temporal lobe / hippocampus, retrosplenial / posterior cingulate, inferior parietal lobule) as remembering past events. This is the strongest available empirical anchor for ARC-070's commitment that imagination-side processing shares substrate with observation-side processing -- shared neural network is a NECESSARY (though not sufficient) condition for shared event-segmentation machinery. Combined with Zacks 2007's theoretical framework, this paper supplies the empirical half of the R2 verdict.
failure_signatures: If REE substrate uses an entirely separate imagination-side processing pipeline disjoint from MECH-288 event_segmenter, the design will violate the core constructive-episodic-simulation finding that observation and imagination share a single neural substrate. Such a design would predict that lesions to the observation-side event segmenter would NOT impair imagination-side segmentation; the literature predicts the opposite.

If ARC-070 fires on a fundamentally different signal class than MECH-288 (e.g. one uses prediction error and the other uses bottleneck-state distance), the architecture would predict a dissociation that the constructive-simulation literature has not observed. Both directions of the bidirectional substrate must read from the same predictive engine.

entries.confidence_rationale: Load-bearing anchor for R1 (PE-as-trigger), R2 (shared substrate for segmentation across streams), and R5 (error-driven boundary signal). Zacks 2007 is the foundational theoretical statement of event segmentation theory: perceptual systems continuously make predictions and a transient prediction-error pulse is the canonical event-boundary signal. The mathematical structure -- a running event model whose error pulses gate a re-segmentation update -- maps directly onto ARC-070's commitment that low-V_s (= prediction error on a chunk's region) triggers re-segmentation of the rollout proposal stream. Strong source quality (foundational Psych Bull review, >2000 citations), strong R1/R5 mapping. R2 mapping is partial: the 2007 paper states the framework but the explicit observation/imagination shared-substrate evidence is more directly carried by Schacter Addis Buckner 2008 (companion entry).
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that uses a constant-grain rollout proposal stream without a prediction-error-conditioned re-segmentation step will fail to reproduce Zacks-style boundary-locked computational events. The event-segmentation framework's core empirical signature is a transient PE-locked re-segmentation pulse, which ARC-070 (with V_s as the trigger) is designed to instantiate.

If the ARC-070 child mechanism uses only mid-execution prediction error (not pre-commitment / simulation-side error) it will fail to reproduce the imagination-side segmentation phenomena that the broader event-segmentation literature has documented across observed and imagined activity streams. A simulation-only segmentation gate is required.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct mechanistic anchor for the imagination-side rollout substrate. Pfeiffer & Foster show rat hippocampus generates brief place-cell sequences before goal-directed navigation that encode future trajectories from current location to remembered goal -- the rodent analog of REE's hippocampal rollout substrate (ARC-007 / SD-002). The trajectories elaborate dynamically as the agent approaches prediction-relevant cues, which is precisely the imagination-side substrate that ARC-070 needs to operate on. Strong source quality (Nature, single-unit electrophysiology with clean methodology). Mapping fidelity moderate-strong: the paper does not directly demonstrate decomposition-on-prediction-failure but it does demonstrate the substrate (forward sweeps) on which ARC-070's decomposition would operate.
failure_signatures: If REE's hippocampal rollout substrate produces only static / single-shot trajectories without the kind of dynamic elaboration Pfeiffer & Foster document, ARC-070 cannot operate on the substrate as designed -- decomposition presupposes a forward-sweep mechanism that produces variable-grain trajectories. The substrate (ARC-007 hippocampal proposals) needs to support the dynamic-elaboration property documented here.

If the forward-sweep mechanism is constant-grain (single-action timesteps with fixed temporal compression), ARC-070's variable-grain decomposition will not have a substrate to operate on. The hippocampal rollout substrate needs to support multi-grain trajectory representation, consistent with Pfeiffer-Foster's evidence of cues elaborating sequence content.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational anchor for R3 (hierarchy depth verdict). Badre & D'Esposito review anatomical, neuroimaging, electrophysiological and developmental findings supporting a multi-level functional hierarchy along the rostro-caudal axis of frontal cortex. Anterior regions encode more abstract action representations; posterior regions encode more concrete motor specifications. The hierarchical decomposition direction (abstract intention -> concrete motor act) is exactly the inverse of REE's chunk-to-primitive composition direction, so ARC-070's decomposition direction is grounded in the same anatomical substrate. R3 verdict (multi-level vs single-level decomposition) is settled in favour of multi-level by this paper's evidence: the brain instantiates AT LEAST 3-4 levels of action abstraction along the rostro-caudal axis, and the corresponding mechanism shape for ARC-070 is multi-level chunk -> sub-chunk -> primitive recursion, not single-level chunk-to-primitive only.
failure_signatures: An ARC-070 child-MECH that supports only single-level decomposition (chunk -> primitive, with no chunk-of-chunks recursion) will fail to match the multi-level hierarchical organisation Badre & D'Esposito document in frontal cortex. The mechanism design must support recursive decomposition with practical recursion bounds.

If the implementation places all decomposition operations at a single anatomical / computational locus (no functional differentiation across abstraction levels), the design will lose the predictive structure of the rostro-caudal gradient and any rule-apprehension layer (ARC-062) reading the decomposed sequence will lose the abstraction-level signal that the hierarchy carries.

This is the canonical Kolling-lab review that the ARC-068 briefing cites as 'Kolling 2015' (it appeared online December 2015, in print 2016 as Curr Opin Neurobiol 37:36-43). Critical to R1 substrate-boundary disambiguation: Kolling explicitly argues that dACC carries MULTIPLE signals including a 'search value' / average-environmental-value signal that is the architectural ancestor of both SD-032b's foraging_value and ARC-068's opportunity-cost-on-rest. Direction is `mixed` rather than `supports` because the paper documents that the same brain region (dACC) carries the foraging-comparator signal AND the trajectory-difficulty signal AND a model-updating signal -- which weakens the case for a clean trajectory-score-level vs mode-switch-level architectural separation. The Shenhav 2016 commentary (PMID 27580609, separate entry) directly disputes Kolling's interpretation. Confidence moderated for that interpretive contestation.
failure_signatures: If REE implements ARC-068 as a clean architectural separation from SD-032b (different substrate, different signals, different timescale), Kolling 2016's 'multiple signals in same cortical area' framing weakens that separation -- biology has the dACC computing several related signals at once, not separating them onto different substrates. The architectural separation may be a design choice rather than a biological commitment.

Kolling 2016's 'search value' is computed from the AVERAGE environmental value (the value of alternatives currently available), not from the long-run REWARD HISTORY (Niv 2007). If REE picks the Niv kernel for ARC-068 and the Kolling kernel for SD-032b, the synthesis must explicitly separate the two -- Kolling's review does not separate them.

If the dACC search-value signal IS what biology uses for both functions, then ARC-068 may be a re-implementation of SD-032b under a different name. The synthesis must arbitrate carefully on R1; this paper alone cannot license either separation or absorption.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical Salamone-Correa review establishing that accumbens dopamine mediates the ACTIVATIONAL aspect of motivation -- the willingness to expend effort against work-related response costs -- separable from primary reinforcement / hedonic reward. This is the load-bearing anchor for R4 (effort-cost vs opportunity-cost separation): Salamone's cost is a movement-energy / response-cost term, NOT an opportunity-cost-on-time term. The two are dissociable. The paper supports ARC-068 indirectly by showing that the activational scalar Niv 2007 attributes to opportunity-cost-on-time has a parallel but DISTINCT effort-cost-on-action substrate (also DA-mediated). For REE this licenses keeping ARC-068 architecturally separate from MECH-258 (cingulate.precision_weighted_pain_PE) effort-cost machinery while acknowledging both terms ride on the same DA system.
failure_signatures: If REE collapses ARC-068 (opportunity-cost-on-time) into the existing effort-cost machinery (MECH-258 et al), Salamone's framework predicts the resulting agent will fail to dissociate the two: DA-depleted Salamone animals reallocate FROM high-effort high-reward TO low-effort low-reward, but they retain primary appetite for food. An REE substrate that conflates effort-cost and opportunity-cost will not reproduce this dissociation under simulated DA depletion (e.g. parametric reduction of the relevant scalar).

If ARC-068 is instantiated as a movement-energy cost (Salamone's term) rather than a time-foregone-reward cost (Niv's term), it will fail to fire in the well-fed-safe-familiar regime where no movement is being attempted -- Salamone's term scales with movement; ARC-068's must scale with elapsed time independent of motor activity.

If the implementation lumps opportunity-cost and effort-cost into a single signed scalar, the agent's response to environmental changes will be non-physiological: Salamone's effort-cost responds to action requirements (ratio schedule), Niv's opportunity-cost responds to reward history (rate of reward). They have different temporal kernels; collapsing them produces a kernel that is neither.

entries.confidence_rationale: The Shenhav lab's empirical reinterpretation of the dACC-foraging-value signal as choice-difficulty tracking. Direction `weakens` for ARC-068's reliance on the dACC-foraging-value substrate as a clean biological anchor for opportunity-cost-on-rest. If Shenhav is right, the dACC signal Kolling identified is generic choice-difficulty rather than a dedicated foraging-value computation, and ARC-068's biological grounding becomes the Niv 2007 mesolimbic-DA tonic-scalar substrate (not a cingulate signal at all). Confidence moderate because the question is genuinely contested -- this is one side of an active debate, not a settled finding. R1 verdict critically depends on this paper's interpretation prevailing.
failure_signatures: If Shenhav's choice-difficulty interpretation is correct, the SD-032b dACC foraging_value computation does not have the substrate-grounding the implementation_note attributes to it. Both SD-032b and ARC-068 lose their dACC-as-foraging-substrate anchor; ARC-068 falls back to Niv's mesolimbic-DA substrate, SD-032b loses its principal anchor.

If Shenhav is partially correct (dACC carries both signals but choice-difficulty dominates), the multi-signal framing of Kolling 2016 holds with a different signal weighting -- ARC-068 and SD-032b can still be architecturally separate but the dACC connection for either is weaker than literature commonly assumes.

If Kolling is correct and Shenhav's reinterpretation is wrong (choice-difficulty signals are confounds, not the primary dACC computation), then SD-032b's foraging-value anchor holds -- but ARC-068's separation from SD-032b still has to lean on the timescale / kernel argument (Niv long-run vs Kolling current-environmental), not on substrate.

entries.confidence_rationale: Critical empirical paper for R2 (reward-rate kernel verdict). Constantino & Daw directly test the marginal-value-theorem opportunity-cost-as-learned-threshold model against temporal-difference learning, in a human patch-foraging task with parametric variation of opportunity cost across blocks. The MVT threshold-learning rule (long-window historical avg-reward over previous rewards) wins decisively over TD. This is the load-bearing empirical evidence that the kernel for opportunity-cost computation IS a long-window historical average, not a fast TD-style estimator. Confidence high because the empirical question (which kernel?) is precisely R2, the design is parametric, the human-behavioural readout is direct, and the result is decisive. Slight discount because the task is a foraging task -- there is task-conditioning that ARC-068's always-on framing does not have, so the kernel-form transfers but the always-on regime is one step removed.
failure_signatures: If REE implements ARC-068 with a fast TD-style kernel (single-trial / single-episode integrator), Constantino & Daw's data predict the agent will fail to track block-wise opportunity-cost changes the way humans do -- humans behave according to a slow MVT threshold-learning rule, not a fast TD update.

If the EMA window for ARC-068 is set at the wrong timescale (too short -- collapses onto z_goal-local; too long -- becomes essentially constant across the agent's lifetime), the ARC-068 child mechanism will not match Constantino & Daw's per-block adjustment behaviour. The empirical recommendation: a window covering tens of episodes / minutes of agent-time, scaling with the block-length of the environment.

If REE attempts to layer multiple kernels (current + historical, per the user's R2 question) without principled aggregation, the resulting estimator may not match either single-kernel prediction. Constantino & Daw test single-kernel models; the multi-kernel architectural question is not addressed.

entries.confidence_rationale: Theoretical anchor for the felt phenomenology side of opportunity cost: the experience of effort / disengagement / 'wasting time' is reframed as the output of a cost-benefit computation in which the next-best alternative use of the relevant computational mechanism enters as opportunity cost. This is the closest existing-literature analogue to the user-observed phenomenology that triggered ARC-068 registration ('felt pull of I am wasting time'). Confidence moderated because the paper is explicitly THEORETICAL (BBS target article with peer commentary; Westbrook & Braver commentary published alongside) and the empirical predictions are partial -- the framework licences ARC-068 but does not isolate it from effort-cost (Salamone) or boredom (ARC-067) at mechanism level. Lit-conf weight is reduced rather than higher because R4 (effort vs opportunity cost separation) is precisely the question this paper deliberately collapses.
failure_signatures: If REE implements ARC-068 as a pure opportunity-cost-on-time scalar with no effort-cost-on-action term in parallel, the Kurzban framework predicts the agent will fail to display the asymmetric performance-degradation-with-time-on-task signature that motivates the felt-effort literature. The two terms compose; an opportunity-cost-only architecture is incomplete.

If ARC-068 is implemented at the trajectory-score layer but the upstream subjective-effort signal is missing, the agent will not produce the disengagement-when-better-alternative-becomes-available behaviour Kurzban models -- ARC-068 alone does not generate the disengagement signal, only the bias against passive trajectories.
Kurzban's framework is silent on the temporal kernel (long-window vs short-window vs current-task); R2 cannot lean on this paper without supplementing with Niv 2007 or Constantino & Daw 2015.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational theoretical anchor for the entire ARC-068 framing. Niv et al. derive an average-reward reinforcement-learning model in which the long-run average rate of reward acts as an opportunity cost on time; this IS the architectural shape ARC-068 commits to, expressed in REE language as `score(no_op) -= avg_reward_rate * time_consumed`. The same paper grounds the ARC-066 vigor side and the ARC-068 opportunity-cost side as TWO FACES of the same scalar — load-bearing for R3 collapse arbitration. Confidence higher than the 0.83 weighting in the parallel ARC-066 entry because for ARC-068 the readout (cost-on-rest) IS what the paper formalises (whereas for ARC-066 the readout was a vigor-on-action by-product). Weighted on heavy mapping fidelity for an architectural claim.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that omits a long-window average-reward-rate scalar will fail to reproduce the Niv prediction that response latencies / no-op-trajectory selection track reward history independent of any specific currently-pursued target. Without ARC-068, REE has no signal that produces this scaling.

If the ARC-068 child mechanism uses a fast (single-episode) reward integrator rather than a slow (across-episode) one, it will collapse onto z_goal-local computations and the agent will not exhibit the well-fed-safe-familiar action gradient the family registers.

If ARC-068 is implemented WITHOUT a corresponding ARC-066 vigor-on-action term (or unified signed scalar), the score-function asymmetry implied by Niv's derivation is broken: the same average-reward scalar should both penalise rest AND inflate action-vigor; an asymmetric implementation will not match the pharmacology data Niv reviews.

Authoritative review synthesising the random-vs-directed-exploration literature. Explicitly states the dual-system conclusion: humans use a COMBINATION of random and uncertainty-directed exploration strategies that rely on different brain systems, have different developmental trajectories, and are sensitive to different task manipulations. The synthesis claim is the load-bearing one for Q-043 — the question of how to weight the two mechanisms presupposes that both are real, and Schulz & Gershman 2019 collect the cumulative evidence for that premise across behaviour, neuroimaging, pharmacology, and TMS.
failure_signatures: As a review, Schulz & Gershman 2019 does not add primary evidence; it synthesises Daw 2006 + Wilson 2014 + Zajkowski 2017 + Warren 2017 + Gershman 2018, all of which are sibling entries in this lit-pull. The independent evidence weight should be the primary papers, not this review — to avoid double-counting I keep the confidence moderate.
The review does not commit to a calibration verdict — it endorses the dual-system architecture but leaves the relative-weight question open. For Q-043 this is informative-but-non-resolving.

entries.confidence_rationale: Pharmacological dissociation: atomoxetine (a norepinephrine reuptake blocker) selectively modulates random but not directed exploration. This is exactly the dissociation Q-043 needs to ground MECH-313 in LC-NE. The 'mixed' direction (not pure 'supports') reflects that the SIGN of the effect was opposite to what an adaptive-gain model would naively predict — atomoxetine REDUCED random exploration instead of increasing it. The paper offers three plausible explanations (non-linear tonic-NE/performance relationship, interaction with other neuromodulators, phasic-vs-tonic mismatch) but cannot adjudicate among them. The substrate-level selectivity is solid; the directional prediction needs more work.
failure_signatures: Atomoxetine REDUCED random exploration; an Aston-Jones-Cohen-style adaptive-gain model predicts the opposite (tonic NE elevation increases task disengagement and exploratory behaviour). The directional mismatch means the MECH-313 ≈ LC-NE-tonic mapping in REE is more nuanced than a simple monotone relationship between NE level and noise floor weight.

n=22 healthy adults, within-subject crossover; the effect is significant on random exploration only and the effect size on directed exploration was near zero. As with Zajkowski 2017, the selectivity rests partly on a null result for directed exploration.
Atomoxetine acts on NE reuptake throughout cortex, not specifically on LC tonic firing; its effect could conceivably reflect cortical NE rather than LC dynamics specifically.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational fMRI dissociation: frontopolar cortex (and intraparietal sulcus) preferentially active during exploratory choices in a four-armed bandit; striatum and vmPFC active during exploitative choices. Establishes the neural substrate distinction that Q-043 presupposes — a directed/uncertainty-driven system separate from a value/exploit system. Source quality high (Nature, large-cohort fMRI with computational model fit); mapping fidelity moderate because the paper does not directly contrast a state-independent noise mechanism (MECH-313) against a state-dependent uncertainty-bonus mechanism (MECH-314) — it dissociates exploration from exploitation, leaving the within-exploration sub-decomposition to later work.
failure_signatures: Daw 2006's computational model used a softmax (exp-of-value) policy with no explicit uncertainty bonus on choice — instead, exploration was driven by the temperature parameter and Kalman-filter variance feeding indirectly into value updates. This means the paper alone cannot adjudicate whether the frontopolar-cortex effect they observed was driven by a state-independent noise floor (MECH-313 analog) or by a state-dependent uncertainty bonus (MECH-314 analog). Later work (Zajkowski 2017, Warren 2017, Gershman 2018) was needed to make that within-exploration distinction.

entries.confidence_rationale: Causal evidence for the substrate split. Inhibitory rTMS over right frontopolar cortex selectively reduces directed exploration in Wilson's Horizon task while leaving random exploration intact. The selectivity is what makes this the cleanest available evidence that the two exploration strategies in human behaviour are not just statistical artifacts of one underlying mechanism — they are mechanistically dissociable at the level of cortical lesions. This is the load-bearing causal anchor for the existence of MECH-314 as a frontopolar uncertainty-bonus mechanism distinct from MECH-313 noise floor.
failure_signatures: The TMS dissociation is between directed exploration and random exploration as operationalised in the Horizon task. It does not directly identify the random-exploration substrate (e.g., LC-NE) — it just shows that whatever drives random exploration is not the right frontopolar cortex. Warren 2017's atomoxetine study is needed to pin down the NE side.

n=24 healthy adults; TMS effects are modest in absolute magnitude and the random-exploration null is a null result, which is logically weaker than a positive double-dissociation. The paper acknowledges this and frames the conclusion as 'at least partially dissociable' rather than fully independent.

entries.confidence_rationale: Behavioural foundation for the directed/random exploration distinction. The Horizon task manipulates how many future choices a subject will make (horizon=1 vs horizon=6); a planning horizon longer than one trial should increase BOTH information-seeking (because future trials can exploit what was learned) AND decision noise (if randomness is a separate exploration strategy). Wilson et al. find both effects: under horizon=6 subjects show higher information-bias AND higher decision-noise relative to horizon=1. The two strategies are independently controllable — a defining behavioural signature that they are mechanistically separable, which is exactly the premise Q-043 needs.
failure_signatures: The Horizon task uses small (n<200) cohorts and two-armed bandits with fixed reward distributions per game; the directed-vs-random dissociation has been replicated but the effect size for the noise component is smaller than for the directed component, leaving room for interpretation that random exploration is partly a residual measurement artifact rather than a genuinely separate strategy.

Wilson 2014 does not pin down the biological substrate of either strategy; it only establishes that BOTH are present in human behaviour as independently tunable knobs. The substrate-attribution work (directed -> frontopolar, random -> LC-NE) is done by Zajkowski 2017 and Warren 2017.

entries.confidence_rationale: Most directly on-topic for Q-043. Gershman shows that uncertainty-bonus algorithms (state-dependent shift, MECH-314 analog) and sampling/Thompson-style randomisation algorithms (state-independent shift, MECH-313 analog) make distinguishable predictions: uncertainty bonuses shift response BIAS as a function of uncertainty, whereas sampling shifts response SLOPE (decision noise). Two behavioural experiments find evidence for BOTH bias and slope changes, and a hybrid model is the best quantitative account. Direct positive evidence that the calibration zone Q-043 hypothesises exists — both mechanisms are needed for human-level behavioural fit.
failure_signatures: Gershman's experiments use simple two-armed bandits with explicit reward/info trade-offs, not anything like SD-054 reef substrate. The hybrid-best-fit finding is at the algorithmic level; it does not pin down which (w_313, w_314) combination is optimal — it shows only that neither extreme (uncertainty-bonus-only, sampling-only) suffices.

The model comparison uses BIC/AIC, which is sensitive to parameter count; a more flexible single-mechanism model could in principle approximate the hybrid fit. Replication in further task structures would strengthen the inference.

entries.confidence_rationale: The unification candidate. Friston et al. propose expected free energy as a single quantity from which both pragmatic (extrinsic) value and epistemic (intrinsic/curiosity) value derive as components. Under this framework, novelty bonuses, uncertainty bonuses, and learning-progress bonuses are all task-conditional readings of the same epistemic-value computation with different priors over which states are 'informative'. This is direct evidence for the COLLAPSE-ALL outcome of Q-044 — three flavours = one mechanism. The 'mixed' direction reflects that the framework is formal and unifying at the theoretical level but the empirical evidence that the brain implements expected-free-energy minimisation as a single unified computation (rather than as three parallel substrates) is much thinner.
failure_signatures: Active inference is a normative framework that explains why an optimal agent should compute a unified epistemic value. It does not establish that the brain actually implements this normative computation as a single substrate rather than as three parallel approximations. Empirical neural evidence for a unified epistemic-value signal is sparse; the more abundant evidence (Wittmann 2007, Daw 2006) supports SUBSTRATE-LEVEL distinctions across novelty and uncertainty even if the underlying normative quantity is unified.

The formal correspondence between expected free energy and Schmidhuber-style learning progress is loose; active-inference epistemic value is typically formulated as information gain (KL divergence between prior and posterior beliefs), not as expected decrease in prediction error per se. So even at the theoretical level, the collapse Friston 2015 proposes is between novelty-as-information and uncertainty-as-information, not necessarily collapsing learning-progress in.

entries.confidence_rationale: Review synthesising the human-exploration literature with explicit attention to algorithmic-architectural distinctions: random vs directed exploration; structure-aware exploration that exploits correlations between options. The review also touches on the developmental dissociation between random exploration (adolescent peak) and directed exploration (adult-stable), which is the kind of empirical signature that would be expected if 314a/b/c are independent substrates. For Q-044 the review weakly supports the three-substrates outcome at the algorithmic-class level, while leaving the implementation-level dissociation open.
failure_signatures: Schulz & Gershman 2019 do not directly address the three-way distinction between novelty / uncertainty-driven curiosity / learning-progress curiosity. Their primary dichotomy is random vs directed exploration, with structure-aware exploration as a third axis. The fit to Q-044's MECH-314a/b/c carving is approximate, not exact.

As a review it inherits the caveats of its primary sources and should not be weighted too heavily to avoid double-counting evidence already captured by Daw 2006 (Q-044 sibling entry) and Wittmann 2007.

entries.confidence_rationale: Anchor for MECH-314b (frontopolar uncertainty-driven curiosity) as a substrate distinct from MECH-314a (striatal novelty, Wittmann 2007) and MECH-314c (learning progress, Kaplan & Oudeyer 2007). Daw 2006 isolates frontopolar cortex as the locus of exploratory decisions in a four-armed bandit — a decision driven by Kalman-filter uncertainty over each arm's payoff. The substrate is anatomically distinct from the SN/VTA novelty locus and from the cortical microcircuit that Kaplan & Oudeyer propose for learning-progress signalling.
failure_signatures: Daw 2006 collapses all exploration into a single binary classification (exploratory vs exploitative) on each trial. Within-exploration sub-types (novelty-driven, uncertainty-driven, learning-progress-driven) are not separately measured. The fact that frontopolar BOLD tracks exploration in a Kalman-uncertainty paradigm does not establish that frontopolar is exclusively the substrate for uncertainty-driven exploration as opposed to other curiosity flavours.

The paper uses a stationary-bandit task; novelty is not manipulated independently of uncertainty (every arm is uncertain in proportion to how few times it has been sampled, so novelty and uncertainty are confounded by design).

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational paper for the learning-progress (MECH-314c) flavour. Kaplan & Oudeyer propose that intrinsic motivation tracks expected DECREASE in prediction error — not raw uncertainty, not raw novelty, but the rate at which learning is happening. They hypothesise tonic dopamine as the learning-progress signal and a cortical microcircuit hierarchy as the computational substrate. The 'support' direction is for the existence of learning-progress as a distinct curiosity flavour with its own algorithmic content; confidence is moderate (0.62) because the proposal is theoretical/computational, with no direct human empirical test of the tonic-dopamine ↔ learning-progress mapping. The Schmidhuber/Pathak tradition the ARC-065 family doc cites runs in parallel without empirical neural anchoring.
failure_signatures: Kaplan & Oudeyer 2007 is theoretical/computational; the predictions about tonic dopamine and microcortical circuits have not been directly validated in human or primate experiments. Empirical tests of learning-progress signalling in dopamine systems are sparse.

Learning progress and uncertainty are correlated in many tasks (uncertainty decreases as learning progresses; the rate of decrease IS learning progress). Distinguishing them experimentally requires tasks where uncertainty plateau (e.g., irreducible noise regions) and learning-progress regions are dissociated — this is not standard practice in the human curiosity literature.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct fMRI evidence that the SN/VTA dopaminergic midbrain is activated by novelty anticipation, in the same circuit that codes reward anticipation. The hippocampus also shows anticipatory and encoding responses to novel stimuli. This provides the anchor for MECH-314a (striatal novelty) as a distinct substrate from frontopolar uncertainty-driven curiosity (MECH-314b, Daw 2006). The fact that the SN/VTA novelty signal sits in the dopamine system — rather than in frontopolar cortex — supports the architectural premise that novelty is a separate flavour with its own substrate.
failure_signatures: Wittmann 2007 shows SN/VTA responds to novelty anticipation and to reward anticipation but the paper itself does not establish that the novelty signal is computationally distinguishable from the reward signal at the population level. If they share circuitry, an account in which both are the same prediction-error variable just over different content (Kakade & Dayan 2002) cannot be ruled out from this paper alone.
fMRI BOLD has low temporal resolution; phasic vs tonic dopaminergic patterns that may carry distinct content cannot be separated.

entries.confidence_rationale: Causal lesion evidence in macaques: ACC-lesioned monkeys fail to sustain rewarded responses or integrate risk and payoff in dynamic foraging, while remaining able to detect and correct individual errors. This dissociates ACC's role in INTEGRATING ACTION-OUTCOME HISTORY from error-detection. Direct empirical support for the substrate-distinct side of Q-045: ACC computes something specific (history-integration on the action-outcome relation) that is qualitatively different from a noise floor. Confidence high (0.81): causal lesion in primates, peer-reviewed in Nature Neuroscience, mechanistically explicit. Direction tagged 'supports' on Q-045 substrate-distinctness.
failure_signatures: If REE's MECH-260 is implemented as a generic recency-discount on the value buffer (exponential forgetting), the 4-arm ablation should show 260-OFF reproducing Kennerley's ACC-lesion phenotype: failure to sustain rewarded responses (because there is no history-integration substrate to lean on). If 260-OFF instead shows preserved value-history learning, MECH-260's implementation is too narrow -- it is doing only anti-recency, not the broader ACC-role of action-outcome history integration that Kennerley identifies.

If the Q-045 collapse outcome is adopted (MECH-313 and MECH-260 collapsed into one substrate), the combined regulator must reproduce Kennerley's dissociation: ACC-lesioned monkeys CAN detect immediate errors but CANNOT sustain history-based responses. This is a within-substrate dissociation that a uniform noise-floor primitive cannot reproduce -- noise affects all decisions uniformly. Supports substrate-distinct.

If REE has no analogue of action-outcome history integration at all (i.e. MECH-260 is purely anti-recency without an underlying history-integration substrate), the 4-arm ablation will fail to reproduce Kennerley's pattern in 260-OFF arms -- the absence will be invisible because there was no history-integration to remove.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the missing MECH-260 anchor paper flagged in the arc_065 synthesis (2026-05-10 entry: 'Citation lookup was ambiguous and the specific dACC-anti-recency-suppression Scholl paper was not retrieved in this pull'). It directly identifies dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, frontal operculum/anterior insula, and lateral anterior prefrontal cortex as the substrate suppressing irrelevant recent-reward bias on choice -- the substrate-level evidence for MECH-260. Supports Q-045 on the SUBSTRATE-DISTINCT side: dACC is doing something computationally specific (gating which reward signals influence value) that is not just noise. Confidence high (0.82): high-quality human fMRI with explicit computational decomposition of bias vs anti-bias contributions.
failure_signatures: If REE's MECH-260 implementation is a generic recency-discount on the value buffer (exponential forgetting), it will not reproduce Scholl's pattern: in Scholl, dACC does not REMOVE recent reward information, it SUPPRESSES the inappropriate influence of one class of recent reward (hypothetical/irrelevant) on choice while preserving learning from another class (real/informative). The mapping is to a SELECTIVE-suppression substrate, not a forgetting kernel.

If MECH-260 fires unconditionally on every recent choice, it will produce excessive anti-recency that prevents any reward-history-based learning at all -- the opposite failure mode from monomodal collapse. Scholl's data require that dACC anti-recency be GATED by some signal of irrelevance (in their task, the real/hypothetical label; in REE, presumably a signal of perseveration or stuck-policy). Without that gate, MECH-260 is mis-calibrated.

If REE collapses MECH-260 with MECH-313 (the Q-045 collapse outcome), the four-arm ablation should predict that 313-only produces the same behavioural profile as 260-only because they are 'the same mechanism viewed two ways'. Scholl's data weakens this prediction: dACC's suppression signal is content-specific (which trial-feature is irrelevant) in a way that a noise-floor cannot reproduce -- noise affects all features uniformly. If the 4-arm ablation in REE shows 313-only and 260-only producing INDISTINGUISHABLE diversity-with-discrimination patterns, that is evidence that REE's MECH-260 has lost the content-specificity Scholl observed and is operating as noise.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct evidence that dACC (and three other regions) hold multiple value representations on different timescales of recency, organised as systematic gradients across the cortex. This is computationally INCOMPATIBLE with the 'dACC anti-recency is just a noise floor' hypothesis -- noise has no temporal structure. The dACC substrate is doing something far more elaborate than what MECH-313 (LC-NE noise) does. Supports the SUBSTRATE-DISTINCT side of Q-045. Confidence moderate-high (0.79): high-quality human fMRI in Nature Communications, but the link to anti-recency specifically (rather than multi-timescale value in general) is by inference rather than direct demonstration.
failure_signatures: If REE implements MECH-260 as a single anti-recency timescale (e.g. exponential discount with one decay constant), it will fail to reproduce Meder's spectrum: the dACC substrate holds value estimates at MULTIPLE temporal scales simultaneously, organised as a cortical gradient. A single-timescale anti-recency cannot generate the dynamic switching Meder observes when the environment changes. MECH-260's implementation note should consider whether the V3 substrate needs to instantiate a multi-timescale spectrum or whether a single timescale captures enough.

If MECH-313 and MECH-260 are collapsed into a single regulator (the Q-045 collapse outcome), the combined substrate would have to instantiate multi-timescale temporal structure -- which a noise-floor primitive cannot do. The fact that dACC holds a temporal spectrum is constructive evidence against collapse: the LC-NE noise substrate and the dACC value-timescale substrate are doing different things at different temporal granularities.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct circuit-level test of how LC-NE input and ACC output jointly control behavioural variability in rats. Transgenic perturbation isolates LC -> ACC as the causal pathway for strategic-vs-stochastic mode switching. The paper is the load-bearing empirical anchor for Q-045: it argues against full independence of the LC-NE noise substrate (MECH-313) and the ACC anti-recency substrate (MECH-260), because LC-NE acts THROUGH ACC to suppress history-based decisions. Direction tagged 'mixed' because Q-045 framed the two as parallel substrates; this paper says LC drives, ACC mediates -- partial collapse at the circuit level, not full independence. Confidence high (0.84): in vivo causal perturbation in transgenic rats, peer-reviewed in Cell, direct relevance to the substrate-coupling question.
failure_signatures: If REE treats MECH-313 (LC-NE tonic noise floor) and MECH-260 (dACC anti-recency) as fully orthogonal axes with independent control, the 4-arm ablation will show 313-only and 260-only producing comparable behavioural diversity. Tervo predicts an ASYMMETRY: lesioning ACC (analogue to MECH-260 OFF) leaves the LC-driven stochastic-mode-switch upstream signal intact but with no downstream effector, so the agent should fail to enter stochastic mode under unbeatable-competitor conditions. Lesioning LC-NE (analogue to MECH-313 OFF) removes the trigger but leaves ACC's normal history-tracking intact, so the agent should over-rely on history-based strategy and likewise fail to enter stochastic mode -- but for a different reason. Same end-state behaviour by two different mechanisms.

If REE's MECH-313 implements a state-INDEPENDENT noise floor (always-on), and MECH-260 implements a state-DEPENDENT recency penalty (only fires when recency is detected), the 4-arm dissociation will work as designed. But if both are implemented as 'just add gaussian noise on the policy logits with different temporal kernels', they will collapse functionally even though they are architecturally distinct -- the falsifier will fail to dissociate them and produce both-OFF / 313-only / 260-only / both-ON rankings that are statistically indistinguishable from each other.

If REE has no analogue of the LC -> ACC directional input (i.e. MECH-313 and MECH-260 are not wired together at the circuit level), the 4-arm experiment will fail to reproduce Tervo's central finding: in their data, ACC normal engagement is SUPPRESSED during stochastic mode, suggesting that LC-NE not only enables variability but actively gates ACC offline. REE should predict the same -- both-ON should look behaviourally MORE like 313-only than like 260-only, because LC dominance suppresses ACC contribution in the stochastic regime.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical computational-theory paper assigning distinct uncertainty-computation roles to NE (UNEXPECTED uncertainty from context-switches) and ACh (EXPECTED uncertainty from known cue unreliability). Indirectly supports Q-045's substrate-distinct verdict: NE is doing something computationally specific (unexpected-uncertainty signalling) that is qualitatively different from a recency-weighted anti-recency penalty. Supports a model where MECH-313's LC-tonic noise floor is a specific computational primitive, not a generic noise generator. Confidence moderate (0.74): canonical and heavily cited theoretical synthesis, but theoretical rather than empirical, and Yu-Dayan's NE role is unexpected-uncertainty rather than tonic-noise-floor specifically -- MECH-313 lives in a slightly different functional niche than the Yu-Dayan NE role.
failure_signatures: If REE implements MECH-313 as generic state-independent Gaussian noise on policy logits (the simplest noise-floor instantiation), it will not reproduce the unexpected-uncertainty signalling that Yu & Dayan attribute to NE -- a noise floor cannot detect context switches, which is what NE's unexpected-uncertainty role requires. The current MECH-313 substrate is closer to the noise-floor framing than to the unexpected-uncertainty framing. This may be an under-specification of MECH-313 that the Q-045 4-arm ablation surfaces: if 313-only fails to produce stochastic-mode-like behaviour under unbeatable-opponent conditions (Tervo's regime), it would be evidence that MECH-313's noise-floor primitive is too generic -- it needs an unexpected-uncertainty trigger.

If MECH-313 and MECH-260 are collapsed into one substrate (Q-045 collapse outcome), the combined regulator would have to instantiate BOTH the noradrenergic role (unexpected-uncertainty / mode-switching) AND the cingulate role (anti-recency / history-tracking). Yu & Dayan's framework treats these as computationally distinct -- they require different temporal kernels, different update rules, different gating conditions. Collapsing them produces an architecture that cannot reproduce the Yu-Dayan dissociation under simulated NE-vs-ACC pharmacology. Supports the substrate-distinct side.

entries.confidence_rationale: non_contributory -- excluded from scoring

Foundational theoretical anchor for the Bayesian latent-cause inference candidate flavour of MECH-316. The latent-cause framework -- task-state inferred as a hidden variable that explains the joint statistics of observations and rewards -- is one of the three implementation candidates Pull 1 surfaced (alongside successor-representation and structure-learning). Source quality is high (Curr Opin Neurobiol, Gershman + Niv are the field leads), and the mapping to MECH-316's cross-episode regularity extraction role is direct: the same machinery that extracts latent causes across episodes is what MECH-316 names. Mapping fidelity is high for the architectural-function claim; transfer risk moderate because the paper covers a broader theoretical landscape than MECH-316 narrowly needs.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that builds MECH-316 as raw successor-representation tabular updates (no inference over hidden task-state) will fail to reproduce the rapid context-switching behaviour Gershman & Niv anchor to latent-cause inference -- specifically the ability to revert to a previous policy when an old context cue re-appears.

If MECH-316 is implemented without an inference-over-hidden-causes step, the agent should fail at tasks where the optimal policy depends on a non-stationary hidden variable that has only an indirect observable correlate.

If the Bayesian latent-cause framing is the correct implementation flavour for MECH-316, then ablating the inference machinery should produce specifically the behavioural signatures of confused-context responding (renewal, summation failures) that the framework anchors -- not a generic regularity-extraction deficit.

entries.confidence_rationale: Targeted 2017 Gershman review extending the 2010 Curr Opin Neurobiol framework with a specifically context-as-causal-inference treatment. The paper organises five distinct functions of context (occasion-setting, configural, modulator, hierarchical, generative) under a single Bayesian umbrella in which different causal-structure interpretations of the training history give rise to different downstream behaviours. Direct relevance for MECH-316 is the operationalisation step: instead of stopping at 'latent-cause inference is the framework', Gershman 2017 commits to specific structural alternatives that the inference is selecting among, which is what a substrate-design pass actually needs. Mapping fidelity is high; confidence held below 0.80 because the paper covers extinction / renewal / partial reinforcement specifically and the transfer to REE's behavioural-trajectory regularity-extraction is a step removed.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that hard-codes a single context-function (e.g. always treats context as an occasion-setter) will fail behavioural tests that require switching between context-functions when the underlying causal structure changes -- exactly the dissociation Gershman 2017 anchors as evidence the Bayesian framework explains data that single-function models cannot.

If MECH-316 cannot adjudicate between competing causal-structure interpretations of the trajectory record, it will display brittle behaviour at regime transitions: either over-generalising across regimes or over-segmenting within them.

If V3-EXQ-543c-successor multi-rule-context substrate testing shows that the agent fails to discover the appropriate context-function for a given regime even when the substrate is in place, the candidate substrate is likely an SR-only flavour rather than a latent-cause-inference flavour.

entries.confidence_rationale: Davachi-tradition 2015 review of hippocampal temporal-order and statistical-learning operations -- the empirical-substrate anchor for the cross-episode regularity-extraction role MECH-316 names. The paper synthesises Davachi-lab and adjacent fMRI work showing that hippocampus (specifically the trisynaptic-pathway-side and the CA1 region) supports order preservation through prediction-error-modulated and context-dependent encoding. Direct mechanistic relevance: the operations the review describes (prediction-based binding, context-driven segmentation, statistical-learning of co-occurring items) are the same operations MECH-316 needs the substrate to perform. Venue note: the user's brief named J Neurosci as the venue; the closest existing Davachi 2015 hippocampal-statistical-learning review is in Trends in Cognitive Sciences instead. Substantive content matches what the brief intended; venue is documented in mapping_caveat. Confidence moderate (0.74) because the paper is a review and the direct experimental anchors are spread across the Davachi lab's primary papers.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that supports cross-episode regularity extraction but does NOT modulate encoding by prediction error will fail the Davachi-style behavioural signatures: temporal-order memory should be specifically impaired at prediction-error boundaries and preserved within prediction-coherent runs.
If MECH-316 is implemented without a context-driven segmentation step, the agent should fail to recover order memory across context-boundaries that humans handle robustly.

If the hippocampal-statistical-learning substrate is the correct biological anchor, then ablating prediction-error signals (analogous to lesioning the dopaminergic input to hippocampus) should produce a specific Davachi-style impairment in order memory, not a generic memory deficit.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational empirical anchor for the attention-modulated RL candidate flavour of MECH-316. The third of the three implementation flavours Pull 1 surfaced (alongside latent-cause inference and successor-representation). The paper combines a multidimensional-bandit behavioural paradigm with simultaneous fMRI to show that a bilateral attentional control network (IPS, precuneus, dlPFC) selects which dimensions of a complex stimulus are relevant for predicting reward; this representation-learning operation effectively reduces the input dimensionality so that downstream RL machinery can converge on the optimal policy. Direct relevance for MECH-316: the attention-modulated flavour reads MECH-316 as 'selectively attend to the relevant dimensions of the trajectory record' rather than 'extract a full posterior over latent causes' or 'build a full state-occupancy SR table'. The empirical anchor is strong (J Neurosci, fMRI + behaviour, definitive author team). Confidence kept at 0.82 (high) because the paper directly establishes the substrate role; the only mapping caveat is the human-laboratory bandit-paradigm vs REE's trajectory-record substrate transfer.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that builds MECH-316 as full-dimensional successor-representation will fail to scale to multidimensional environments -- exactly the failure mode Niv et al. anchor: undimensionality-reduced RL is exponentially slow.

If MECH-316 is implemented without an attention/dimensionality-reduction mechanism, the agent should show specifically the slow-convergence signature on multidimensional behavioural tasks that Niv et al. anchor in their behavioural data.

If the attention-modulated-RL flavour is the correct implementation for MECH-316, then ablating the attention selection step should produce a generic slowdown across all multidimensional tasks rather than the specific causal-inference failure mode the Bayesian flavour predicts.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational anchor for the structure-learning candidate flavour of MECH-316 -- the fourth implementation flavour Pull 1 surfaced (alongside latent-cause inference, successor-representation, and attention-modulated RL). Kemp & Tenenbaum's hierarchical-Bayesian framework for discovering which structural form (tree, ring, chain, partition, dominance hierarchy) best describes a given dataset is the ambitious version of the cross-episode regularity-extraction claim: not just 'extract the regularities' but 'extract the discrete structural form that organises the regularities'. Direction is MIXED because the framework is computationally well-defined and influential, but the structure-learning flavour is the most demanding (and least biologically-anchored) of the four candidate implementation flavours. The empirical evidence that REE -- or biological brains generally -- perform structure-learning at this level of explicitness is thin. Confidence 0.62 reflects this: the paper is foundational for the algorithmic candidate, but the biological-plausibility of the strong reading is genuinely contested.
failure_signatures: If MECH-316 is implemented under the strong structure-learning flavour but the underlying biology does NOT in fact maintain an explicit hypothesis space over discrete structural forms, the substrate will fail to reproduce the qualitative form-discovery signatures Kemp & Tenenbaum's framework predicts -- specifically the discrete switching between hypothesised forms as evidence accumulates.

If structure-learning is what MECH-316 names, then the agent should display Kemp-Tenenbaum-style form-discovery: starting with the simplest structural form and switching to richer forms as evidence accumulates against the simpler ones. Failure to display this signature falsifies the strong reading.

If the simpler attention-modulated or latent-cause flavours suffice, then the additional commitment to a structural-form hypothesis space is unnecessary -- and the structure-learning reading of MECH-316 should be rejected as overdetermined.

entries.confidence_rationale: Load-bearing direct empirical anchor for the dorsolateral-striatum action-chunking substrate of MECH-317. Martiros et al. provide the most-direct primary evidence for the start-stop bracketing signature that Smith & Graybiel 2013/2016 (already in Pull 1) anchor at the review level. The novel finding here is the inverse activity pattern of SPNs vs interneurons -- both classes are coordinated to mark the beginning and end of chunked sequences but with opposite firing dynamics. The substrate-implementation implication is that MECH-317 needs to support not just bracket detection but a two-population coordination structure that anchors the bracket. Source quality is high (Curr Biol, Graybiel-lab primary empirical, in vivo single-unit recording). Mapping fidelity strong for the substrate-identification claim; transfer risk moderate because the chunking signature in REE has to be measured on action-distribution entropy troughs rather than direct neuronal recording.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that builds MECH-317 as a single chunk-detection signal will fail to reproduce the inverse-activity-pattern signature Martiros et al. anchor -- the substrate needs at least two coordinated populations / signals that bracket the chunk asymmetrically.

If MECH-317 is implemented without explicit start-stop bracket signatures (action-entropy troughs at chunk boundaries with mid-chunk entropy elevation), the agent should fail to show learnable temporal structure on a repeating-sequence task like SD-054 reef forage-approach-retreat.

If the bracketing signature is the correct biological anchor for chunking, then ablating the bracket-detection step should specifically impair sequence-acquisition rather than producing a generic action-selection deficit.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational anchor for the options framework -- the canonical computational treatment of temporal abstraction in RL. Sutton, Precup & Singh define an option as a triple <initiation-set, intra-option policy, termination-condition>; the framework establishes that option-based hierarchical RL is mathematically tractable under the semi-MDP extension. Direct relevance for MECH-317: this is the field-standard formalisation of what 'behavioural pattern compression' could mean computationally. The three-field option structure aligns with the two-population striatal biology Martiros et al. anchor (initiation/termination = SPN bracket signal; intra-option policy = interneuron continuation signal). Confidence 0.82 reflects foundational status, with the only caveat being that the framework is normative rather than substrate-prescriptive -- many substrate implementations could realise the same option structure.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that builds MECH-317 without explicit initiation-set / termination-condition fields will fail to support the semi-MDP-style temporal-abstraction tractability the framework guarantees -- specifically, planning over chunked units becomes ill-defined without explicit termination conditions.

If MECH-317 is implemented as a flat-action sequence-detector (no option triple), the agent should fail at tasks where chunked behaviour must be terminated based on a state-condition rather than after a fixed number of steps.

If the options-framework formalisation is the correct computational target, the agent's chunks should be detectable as semi-MDP transitions in the behavioural record (rather than fixed-length action-blocks or pure state-transition clusters).

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational anchor for gradient-based option discovery -- the canonical learnable-options computational treatment. Bacon, Harb & Precup derive policy gradient theorems for the options framework, enabling end-to-end learning of intra-option policies, termination functions, AND the policy-over-options from a single scalar reward signal. Direct relevance for MECH-317: this is the algorithmic candidate for option-discovery as an implementation flavour. Confidence 0.78 reflects that the framework solves a real problem (autonomous option discovery without hand-engineering or sub-goal specification) but the empirical record of option-critic in practice is mixed -- option-collapse and option-degeneracy are documented failure modes that the original paper anticipates but does not fully resolve.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that implements MECH-317 via option-critic-style gradient discovery is vulnerable to option-collapse (all chunks become identical) or option-degeneracy (chunks become arbitrarily short or arbitrarily long). The original paper anticipates these failure modes but does not fully resolve them.

If MECH-317 is implemented with option-critic-style termination-function gradients but without an explicit deliberation cost (Harb et al. 2017 follow-on), the termination probabilities tend to converge to terminating-everywhere (zero-length options) -- a known mode collapse in the option-critic literature.

If the gradient-discovery substrate produces options that successfully reproduce hierarchical behaviour on a benchmark but fail to transfer to a related task with shared substructure, the option-discovery has captured task-specific patterns rather than generalisable behavioural primitives.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational normative anchor for what makes a behavioural hierarchy optimal -- the criterion against which option-discovery substrates should be evaluated. Solway et al. provide a mathematical account (drawing on information-bottleneck arguments) of which decompositions of a task into chunked sub-units are optimal, and behaviourally confirm in four experiments that human learners spontaneously discover those optimal hierarchies. Direct relevance for MECH-317: this is the normative target against which the various implementation flavours (option-critic, DIAYN, hand-engineered options, substrate-driven repetition triggers) should be compared. Confidence 0.80 reflects strong source quality (PLOS Comput Biol, Barto-Niv-Botvinick team) and direct relevance to the cluster question.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that produces options which fail to match the Solway-et-al optimal hierarchy criterion will be inefficient -- the chunks won't decompose the task in the information-theoretically-correct way.

If MECH-317 produces chunks but the chunks do NOT correspond to bottleneck states or transition-rich segments of the trajectory record, the option-decomposition is unlikely to support transfer learning across related tasks.

If the substrate is producing options that match the normative-optimal criterion, behavioural validation should show humanlike spontaneous-discovery signatures (the four experiments anchored in Solway 2014 produced testable predictions about which decompositions human subjects converge on).

entries.confidence_rationale: DIAYN (Diversity is All You Need) is one of the strongest examples of diversity-driven skill discovery -- the third candidate implementation flavour for MECH-317 alongside option-critic gradient discovery and substrate-driven repetition triggers. The method learns a family of distinguishable skills by maximising the mutual information between a skill-index and the resulting trajectory distribution, without any reward signal. Direction is MIXED because the framework is influential and useful for unsupervised pre-training, but the discovered skills are NOT the same thing as MECH-317's behavioural chunks: DIAYN skills are diverse-by-design (the optimisation objective explicitly rewards behavioural distinguishability), whereas MECH-317 chunks should be useful-by-context (compressing repeated behavioural patterns into reusable units). The architectural commitments are different and may even be opposed. Confidence 0.62 reflects this dual position.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that implements MECH-317 via DIAYN-style diversity-driven skill discovery will produce maximally-distinguishable skills, NOT the repeated-behavioural-pattern compression MECH-317 actually names. The two objectives are not aligned and may even be opposed.

If MECH-317 is implemented with DIAYN-style mutual-information objectives, the agent should produce skills that are mutually-exclusive in behaviour space -- but the resulting skills are not chunks of repeated patterns; they are diversity-engineered pre-training primitives.

If DIAYN-style discovery is used as a PRETRAINING phase (to establish a diverse skill base) followed by repetition-driven chunk-formation (MECH-323) selecting which skills become chunks, the combined architecture could work -- but neither paper provides this combined design and substrate-design risk is elevated.

entries.confidence_rationale: Load-bearing primary anchor for the meta-reinforcement-learning interpretation of MECH-318's rule-state abstraction substrate. Wang et al. propose that prefrontal cortex operates as a free-standing learning system trained by the dopamine system to perform meta-RL within an episode -- the recurrent network's hidden state functions as the rule-state abstraction the task identity gets encoded into. The paper directly addresses the W1-W5 properties the MECH-318 absorption check audited against the existing ree-v3 substrates. Source quality is high (Nat Neurosci, top-tier venue, DeepMind + Botvinick lab). Mapping fidelity strong for the rule-state-encoding role. Transfer risk moderate because the deep-RL substrate the paper uses is one step removed from REE's PFC-analog architecture.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that builds MECH-318 with topology-only recurrence (E1 LSTM treated as a possible host) but without a multi-task training distribution and without rule-context-shaping training signal will fail to encode rule-state in the hidden state -- which is what the MECH-318 absorption check (2026-05-10) already identified as the W2 gap.

If MECH-318 is implemented but the agent fails to display within-episode adaptation at rule-switch points on a multi-rule-context substrate, the substrate is probably topology-correct but training-signal-deficient.

If Wang et al.'s reading is the right framing for MECH-318, then training the substrate across a multi-rule-context distribution should produce a recurrent state that decodes rule-context -- not a generic latent-stack representation that has rule-context as one component among many.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational AI-tradition anchor for recurrent meta-RL. Duan et al. propose that rather than designing a fast RL algorithm, one should represent the algorithm as an RNN whose weights are learned slowly by a general-purpose RL algorithm. The RNN's hidden state encodes the state of the 'fast' algorithm on the current MDP; the RNN's recurrent dynamics are the algorithm's update rule. The architecture maintains hidden-state continuity across episodes within a task instance -- the W5 property that the MECH-318 absorption check identifies as not absorbed by any current REE substrate. Confidence 0.78 reflects the foundational status balanced against the deep-RL paradigm gap; the paper anchors the W5 property specifically.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that builds MECH-318 as a recurrent network but resets the hidden state every episode (which all current REE candidates -- E1 LSTM, SD-033a, MECH-269 -- do) will fail to reproduce the cross-episode evidence-accumulation signature that Duan et al. anchor as the defining property of RL^2.

If MECH-318 is implemented with per-episode hidden-state reset, the agent should adapt within an episode but not across episodes -- a behavioural signature that distinguishes the within-V3 portion of MECH-318 (which IS absorbed into SD-033a + ARC-062) from the cross-episode portion (which is NOT absorbed and may be V4-scope).

If RL^2-style hidden-state continuity is the correct biological framing for MECH-318, then cross-episode hidden-state preservation should produce specifically faster adaptation to a recurring task instance across episodes -- and ablating the cross-episode connection should produce same-task slow re-learning every episode.

entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative TCS review of the fast-vs-slow meta-RL framework, by the team that produced both Wang 2018 and (Botvinick was supervisor for) the broader meta-RL-as-PFC research programme. The paper synthesises four years of post-2015 work on what makes deep RL more sample-efficient (episodic-memory augmentation, meta-learning, model-based RL); for MECH-318 the relevance is the explicit discussion of how recurrent hidden-state can serve as a fast-learning substrate that the slow weight-learning shapes. Confidence 0.78 reflects the secondary-review status (synthesis rather than primary anchor) balanced against authoritative source and direct on-topic content.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that builds MECH-318 without coupling to episodic-memory retrieval (the fast-recall complement to slow weight-learning) will produce a less sample-efficient agent than Botvinick et al.'s framework predicts.

If MECH-318 is implemented as a pure-recurrent-meta-RL substrate without episodic-memory augmentation, the agent should show the deep-RL sample-inefficiency that Botvinick et al. anchor as the motivating problem.

If the broader fast-and-slow framework is the right reading for MECH-318, then the substrate should integrate with the existing REE episodic-memory substrates (MECH-269 anchor sets, MECH-292/293 ghost-goal bank) rather than displacing them.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct primate-empirical anchor for rule-state inference in frontal cortex. Sarafyazd & Jazayeri record from dorsomedial frontal cortex (DMFC) and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) in monkeys performing a task where negative outcomes arise either from stimulus-judgement errors or from covert switches in the stimulus-response contingency rule. Both regions encode evidence supporting a rule-switch, and the ACC functions downstream of DMFC -- specifically encoding the inference that a covert rule-switch has occurred (as distinct from a within-rule judgement error). This is the most-direct primate single-unit empirical evidence to date for rule-state inference as a function of frontal cortex, which is exactly the role MECH-318 names. Confidence 0.84 reflects the high source quality (Science, primate single-unit) and direct mechanistic relevance.
failure_signatures: An REE substrate that builds MECH-318 without an inference step that distinguishes 'rule-switch occurred' from 'within-rule error occurred' will fail to reproduce the DMFC-ACC dissociation Sarafyazd & Jazayeri anchor -- specifically, the substrate should be able to attribute negative outcomes to the right causal source.

If MECH-318 is implemented but the substrate treats every negative outcome as a rule-switch signal, the agent should display the over-switching failure mode (constantly re-inferring rules; never settling). Conversely, if the substrate cannot detect genuine rule-switches at all, it should display the under-switching mode.

If the Sarafyazd-Jazayeri DMFC-then-ACC sequential architecture is the right framing for rule-inference, then ablating the DMFC-analog component should prevent rule-switch detection, while ablating the ACC-analog component should preserve detection but prevent action on it.
