Gumbel-Softmax directly addresses differentiable sampling of categorical variables, which is relevant to REE's first-action-class boundary. It is a later-option paper, not a reason to replace the current CEM path during the 563b repair. The immediate repair can be non-differentiable support instrumentation and minimal one-hot support preservation.
failure_signatures: If first-action class is treated only as an emergent argmax of a continuous decoder, CEM may never sample behaviourally meaningful categorical alternatives.
A differentiable categorical sampler would be premature if the live failure can be measured and repaired with default-off support guards.

entries.confidence_rationale: The tutorial is the standard peer-reviewed account of CE/CEM as elite-set refitting of a sampling distribution. It directly explains why final CEM candidates can lose support: the method is designed to concentrate probability mass around high-performing elites. The mapping to REE is algorithmic rather than biological, so it supports the diagnosis and instrumentation need more strongly than any particular repair.
failure_signatures: If the elite set contains only one first-action class, ordinary CEM refit can concentrate the next proposal distribution on that class and erase downstream choice support.
A support-preserving repair that changes the score function rather than the proposal distribution would not address the collapse mode implied by elite-set refitting.

entries.confidence_rationale: This preprint is useful because it names local-minima convergence as a CEM concern and uses Gaussian mixture models to encourage exploration of the design space. The source is less established than the CEM tutorial or iCEM paper, and it is not an MPC or categorical-action paper. It weakly supports considering mixture proposal distributions as a later option, not as the first V3 repair.
failure_signatures: A unimodal CEM proposal can become trapped around one basin even when other basins remain relevant.
A mixture proposal may be overkill if the immediate failure is only missing first-action categorical support in a small action space.

entries.confidence_rationale: iCEM is directly about CEM as an MPC trajectory optimizer. Its repairs are conservative and proposal-side: temporally correlated action sequences, memory, momentum/refit variants, and executing evaluated best actions. It does not solve categorical first-action support, but it supports the design stance that CEM repairs should preserve proposal quality and instrumentation rather than adding a new motivational term.
failure_signatures: Independent per-timestep CEM samples can generate incoherent proposal surfaces that do not explore useful trajectory alternatives.
MPC variants that execute an unevaluated mean action can obscure which evaluated candidate actually carried the selected action support.

entries.confidence_rationale: Information-theoretic MPC provides a close sampling-based control analogue in which trajectory weights and entropy/control-cost structure matter, rather than only hard elite survival. This supports using entropy/support diagnostics and weak bias dose-response measurements. It is not direct evidence for changing REE's CEM implementation to MPPI.
failure_signatures: A hard elite-only planner can erase lower-ranked alternatives before downstream biases have a chance to act.
If the score range dwarfs the bias range, a support surface may exist but remain behaviourally immovable under naturalistic bias magnitudes.

Phil Trans B review by Frank lab; proposes that the fundamental hippocampal function is generating hypothetical experiences and thoughts -- a broader claim than memory retrieval. Directly addresses the question of hippocampus as option generator vs. archive. Good source quality (Phil Trans B themed issue); strong mapping fidelity to ARC-007. Limited primary data specific to behavioural sequence retrieval.
failure_signatures: The imagination framing is under-constrained: firing patterns corresponding to alternatives to actual experience are shown, but the functional role in guiding specific choices is not always established.
The review acknowledges that many of the 'imagination' firing events may be epiphenomenal with respect to behaviour.

entries.confidence_rationale: Simultaneous hippocampal-prefrontal ensemble recording in rats during spatial alternation learning. Direct evidence that hippocampal forward replay (during immobility pauses) co-occurs with prefrontal readout of correct future paths and is coordinated across both regions. The reverse/forward asymmetry with learning stage is strong mechanistic evidence for the cue-retrieval model. High source quality (Neuron, in vivo electrophysiology); high mapping fidelity.
failure_signatures: The study uses a constrained linear track / Y-maze, so the generalisation to open-field novel-combination trajectory planning (as in Pfeiffer & Foster 2013) is uncertain.
Causal role of prefrontal readout in guiding decisions is correlational at this stage -- prefrontal sequence activity tracks correct paths but causal necessity is not proven.

entries.confidence_rationale: eLife in-vivo electrophysiology; demonstrates theta sequences in prefrontal cortex nested within behavioural sequences, coordinated with hippocampal theta sequences that encode alternatives for deliberation. The critical finding is that hippocampal theta sequences encode alternatives (not just current location) and are coordinated with prefrontal sequences that predict upcoming choices -- direct support for the PFC cue / hippocampal option-retrieval model.
failure_signatures: During error trials, the coordination between hippocampal alternatives and prefrontal upcoming-choice representations was preserved at the theta level -- suggesting this coupling is robust but not sufficient to prevent errors.
The causal direction (PFC cueing hippocampus vs. hippocampus informing PFC) cannot be resolved from correlation data alone.

entries.confidence_rationale: Buckner 2010 is one of the canonical reframings of hippocampal function away from pure episodic memory retrieval toward prospective prediction and imagination. Very high citation count; synthesises both rodent (preplay/replay) and human (fMRI prospection) literatures. Strong mapping to the claim that hippocampus is a cue-indexed sequence store for future trajectories rather than a passive archive. Transfer risk low.
failure_signatures: Review does not provide direct evidence that hippocampal sequence events are actually used online to guide specific goal-directed choices -- the mechanistic link between hippocampal prospection and action selection remains indirect in the human fMRI literature.

entries.confidence_rationale: Jadhav lab review in Hippocampus; explicitly frames hippocampal-prefrontal interactions via replay and theta sequences as the mechanism for context-dependent memory retrieval and decision-making. Directly addresses the cue-differentiation requirement by arguing that PFC-hippocampal theta interactions at different learning stages mediate different retrieval modes. Good source quality; high mapping fidelity.
failure_signatures: The review is primarily phenomenological -- the causal roles of replay vs. theta sequences in guiding PFC activity are proposals awaiting closed-loop intervention evidence.
The framework relies on the assumption that replay content is read out by PFC, but the mechanism for this readout is not established.

entries.confidence_rationale: Miller & Cohen 2001 is one of the most cited papers in cognitive neuroscience (~8000+ citations). The core claim -- that PFC maintains goal and context representations that provide top-down bias signals to downstream areas -- is precisely the frontal cue gating mechanism in Topic 3. Source quality exceptional. Mapping fidelity very high: the 'bias signal' model is the REE ARC-016 claim about PFC providing context that shapes hippocampal retrieval.
failure_signatures: The original formulation emphasises sensory and motor routing, less explicitly the hippocampal memory retrieval pathway -- the extension to hippocampal option retrieval requires citing subsequent work (Jadhav, Tang).
Lesion and single-unit data available in 2001 were largely from non-human primates on working memory tasks; the generality to naturalistic behaviour is assumed.

failure_signatures: The review is primarily phenomenological -- the causal roles of replay vs. theta sequences in guiding PFC activity are proposals awaiting closed-loop intervention evidence.

entries.confidence_rationale: PNAS empirical study with strong experimental manipulation (testosterone-induced premature babbling); direct mechanistic demonstration that motor production phase gates sensory phase onset. High source quality; mapping fidelity moderate because it is zebra finch vocal learning not general motor exploration, but the logic of action-before-template applies broadly.
failure_signatures: Finding is specific to vocal learning in songbirds; it is unclear whether the same babbling-gates-sensory-template logic applies to limb motor exploration.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical high-citation review in Annual Review of Neuroscience. Establishes the convergent architecture of basal ganglia-driven motor exploration in both avian and human vocal learning, with a strong auditory-motor feedback loop argument. High source quality and conceptual mapping fidelity to the developmental bootstrapping story. Transfer risk moderate because some features (critical period rigidity, BG role) are better established in birds.
failure_signatures: Language meaning, abstraction, and flexible associations are acknowledged as not analogous between birds and humans, limiting how far the birdsong model generalises.
How auditory feedback of self is actually processed in forebrain areas remains unclear in both species.

entries.confidence_rationale: Computational model combining spiking neural network, STDP reinforcement, and a human-like vocal tract; directly models canonical babbling emergence. The finding that reward modulation (not random noise) drives increasing canonical syllable frequency is highly relevant to the developmental bootstrapping claim. Source quality moderate (PLoS ONE computational; not replicated). Mapping fidelity good because the model explicitly instantiates the action-repertoire-bootstrapping-through-reward claim.
failure_signatures: Model relies on external reward (caregiver contingent response) which may not be the primary driver in all developmental contexts.
Simulation only; no direct comparison with longitudinal infant data on babbling diversity trajectories.

entries.confidence_rationale: Recent review in Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences; argues that canonical babbling represents the emergence of three-way coordination (motor, respiratory, vocal) not mere random vocalisation. The progressive coordination framing is relevant to the bootstrapping story. Source quality moderate-good (review, not primary data). Mapping fidelity good: the paper explicitly argues that babbling is a coordinated calibration milestone.
failure_signatures: The paper is a perspective/review with limited primary data; the mechanistic claim about respiratory rhythm as the coordination scaffold is proposed rather than experimentally demonstrated.

entries.confidence_rationale: Behavioural Brain Research; systematically separates social vs. novelty enrichment components and their effects on impulsivity and behavioral flexibility (reversal learning). Finding is mixed: social enrichment decreased impulsive choice but increased regressive errors; novelty enrichment increased impulsive choice; both reduced never-reinforced errors. The nuanced dissociation is informative but also complicates a simple 'more enrichment = more flexibility' narrative.
failure_signatures: Social enrichment increased regressive errors in behavioral flexibility (more perseveration on previously-rewarded options), which is the opposite of the expected result if social enrichment boosts hippocampal option diversity.
The specific direction of the flexibility effect depends on the enrichment type -- a simple 'more exploration = better flexibility' account is not supported.

entries.confidence_rationale: Behavioural pharmacology study; demonstrates that post-weaning isolation rearing specifically impairs reversal learning (new-strategy acquisition phase) but not initial acquisition learning in rats. This is the monostrategy signature: the isolation-reared animal learns one strategy but cannot update it. Source quality moderate (small n, pharmacological intervention focus); mapping fidelity good for the specific claim that impoverished early exploration -> rigid behavioral repertoire.
failure_signatures: Isolation rearing impairs social experience as well as environmental exploration; the specific contribution of motor/sensory exploration deprivation vs. social deprivation cannot be separated.
Clozapine remediation suggests the effect is dopaminergic/prefrontal, but this does not establish the hippocampal trajectory store as the locus of the deficit.

Nature Scientific Reports study; n=71 infants (high-risk HR and low-risk LR for ASD) with Motion Capture from 1-2 months; validated against a 1,445 infant sibling dataset. Key finding is that context-inflexibility (not raw variability level) is the pathological signature. This directly bears on REE's diversity mechanism design: the target is context-appropriate variability, not maximum entropy. High source quality; mapping fidelity strong because the operationalization of healthy vs pathological exploration maps directly to REE's diversity acceptance criteria.
failure_signatures: The HR group does not uniformly develop ASD -- only a subset, limiting causal inference.
Head movement is used as the primary motor proxy, which may not generalize to limb or whole-body motor variability patterns.
The ASD pathway may be atypical in ways specific to social development; the logic may not transfer cleanly to non-social behavioral flexibility.

entries.confidence_rationale: EMG study of n=40 full-term infants from 1 week to 6 months; longitudinal within-subject design with 12 muscles measured across ipsilateral/contralateral limb pairs. Directly tracks the transition from uncorrelated to coordinated spontaneous limb activity. Source quality moderate (Neuroscience Letters, not top-tier); mapping fidelity good because the progressive emergence of inter-limb coordination is the mechanism underlying the random-to-structured transition REE needs to understand.
failure_signatures: Study is purely observational EMG; no intervention, so causal direction of the correlation increase (maturation vs experience-driven) is unresolved.
Spontaneous vs voluntary distinction is operational only (spontaneous = no salient external trigger), not mechanistically verified.

entries.confidence_rationale: Nature Communications Biology empirical study using RGB-D motion capture (n=20 infants, 270+ spontaneous movement units) with synthetic comparison datasets. Directly measures kinematic space coverage and acceleration distributions. High source quality; mapping fidelity is strong because the finding -- that spontaneous movements are optimized for maximal dynamic excitation, not goal achievement -- directly supports the REE claim that action diversity generation precedes and bootstraps capability formation. Transfer risk low because human infant data.
failure_signatures: Analysis is confined to arm movement; it is unclear whether the same dynamic-excitation optimization logic extends to lower-limb or whole-body locomotor exploration.
Comparison was against reaching-like motions, not other spontaneous movement types; the design assumes a clear spontaneous/goal-directed dichotomy that may not be clean in naturalistic settings.

entries.confidence_rationale: Neurobiologically constrained spiking neural network model (six brain area maps; excitatory/inhibitory; STDP + Hebbian + dopamine-modulated reward). Two-phase model -- Hebbian self-organization first, dopamine-reward consolidation second -- directly formalizes the babbling-to-action-consolidation pipeline. Source quality moderate (Brain Sciences is broad; model is simulation only). Mapping fidelity strong because the two-phase architecture (exploration then reward-consolidation) is exactly what REE needs for its infant-stage substrate. A pure reward-from-birth architecture would skip phase 1 and produce no option diversity.
failure_signatures: Simulation only; no direct comparison with infant neurophysiological data on cell assembly formation.
Dopamine is used as a global reward signal -- this may not capture the context-specific neuromodulation required for flexible repertoire formation.
The model is tested only on hand action acquisition; generalization to whole-body or locomotor repertoires is unverified.

entries.confidence_rationale: Invited review in Frontiers in Psychology; synthesizes empirical literature on infant motor variability vs noise. The core proposal -- that infants increase motor variability when facing information-gathering opportunities -- is directly testable and well-supported by cited studies. Source quality moderate (Frontiers, review paper). Mapping fidelity strong because it operationalizes the distinction between noise-floor variability and exploration-driven variability, which is exactly the distinction REE's diversity acceptance criteria must make.
failure_signatures: The review is theoretical; the proposed guiding principle (infants increase variability for information-gathering) is not yet directly tested in a large-scale empirical study.
The mechanisms proposed remain somewhat underspecified -- the review identifies what the signal is (context-modulated variability) but not how the infant generates it neurally.

entries.confidence_rationale: Topics in Cognitive Science review + robotic experiment by Oudeyer (FLOWERS team) and Linda Smith (Indiana developmental psychology). The robot experiment showing ordered developmental stages from curiosity-driven learning (first affordances, then vocal interaction) directly evidences that progress-seeking intrinsic motivation is sufficient to generate a structured curriculum without external design. entries.confidence_rationale: Moderate-to-good evidence for the core REE infant-stage design question. The paper's central finding -- that learning-progress curiosity (not novelty per se) produces emergent developmental stage ordering in robots -- is the best available evidence for MECH-314c specifically. However, this is a theoretical review with robotic demonstrations rather than controlled experiments, and the robotics context involves richer multi-modal environments than REE's current gridworld. The finding that developmental curriculum emerges automatically from progress-driven curiosity (rather than hand-designed staging) has direct implications for REE infant-stage design.
failure_signatures: Pure novelty bonuses (visit novel states) do not produce emergent developmental stage ordering -- the agent visits all states equally and does not dwell in regions where learning is currently productive.

Learning-progress curiosity requires the environment to contain a natural difficulty gradient: if all tasks are equally hard or all equally easy, the progress signal is flat and provides no gradient for developmental sequencing.

The emergent curriculum observed in the robot experiments depended on environmental structure (objects with affordances, vocal interaction partners) that the agent could explore and gradually master -- in a featureless environment, no developmental structure emerged.

entries.confidence_rationale: Good biological evidence that environmental enrichment -- not just exploration drive -- is necessary for the downstream learning flexibility that curiosity-driven exploration is supposed to produce. The finding that enriched environments produce CA3 place cells with greater spatial tuning and enhanced contextual remapping provides a mechanistic account of why environment structure matters beyond the novelty signal itself. Mapping fidelity is moderate: the REE substrate's hippocampal residue field has parallels to place cell remapping, but REE does not implement adult neurogenesis. The key REE-relevant finding is the causal arrow: enrichment -> better representational flexibility, not just exploration -> better representations.
failure_signatures: Rats reared in impoverished environments develop CA3 representations that are less flexible -- they fail to disambiguate similar contexts even when they later explore normally.

The effect of enrichment on memory flexibility was abolished by temozolomide treatment (reducing neurogenesis), suggesting the mechanism requires structural hippocampal change, not just increased activity.
Enrichment during a sensitive early period (not equivalent adult experience alone) produced the strongest effects -- timing and environmental structure interact.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality Nature Reviews Neuroscience paper providing the most current synthesis of primate circuits for curiosity. Directly supports the biological grounding of MECH-314a (novelty-based) and MECH-314b (uncertainty-driven) as distinct sub-mechanisms, not reducible to each other. The developmental angle -- how curiosity-related behaviours arise during postnatal development -- is directly relevant to the REE infant-stage question. High source quality, good mapping fidelity for the circuit-separation question (Q-044).
failure_signatures: Curiosity circuits that only track novelty (recent vs. not-recent) are distinct from circuits that track uncertainty (resolution of predictive uncertainty) -- conflating the two produces mechanisms that each fail to capture the full biological function.

Curiosity-related behaviours in primates arise during postnatal development and are shaped by the richness of environmental experience -- the biological evidence implies that a fixed novelty bonus without environmental structure will not generate genuine curiosity-like exploration.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational paper directly instantiating MECH-314c (learning-progress curiosity via forward-model PE). High source quality (ICML, highly cited). Mapping fidelity is moderate: the REE substrate uses e3._running_variance as the PE proxy rather than a dedicated learned feature space, which is Phase-1 approximation. The stochastic environment failure mode Pathak 2017 identifies is directly REE-relevant: a random causal grid world with intrinsic novelty only could exhibit the same failure unless the environment has structure the agent can learn to predict.
failure_signatures: In stochastic environments prediction error stays high even after optimal learning, producing an endlessly high curiosity signal that does not track real learning progress -- the environment randomness is indistinguishable from learnable structure.
When the learned feature space is poor, prediction error measures noise rather than meaningful state transitions, misdirecting exploration.
Curiosity alone (without any task reward) is insufficient to solve tasks requiring goal-directed persistence -- it drives coverage, not completion.

entries.confidence_rationale: Critical evidence for ARC-065 / MECH-314 design. The positive finding (curiosity alone achieves surprisingly good performance on 54 benchmarks) strongly supports the functional value of prediction-error-based exploration bonuses. The noisy TV finding is the most important cautionary result: it shows that a maximally curious agent in a structurally poor environment (one with accessible irreducible randomness) exploits the noise source rather than exploring useful state space. This directly addresses the user's central question: novelty_bonus_weight at maximum is insufficient if the environment has random attractors.
failure_signatures: Noisy TV problem: agents presented with an unpredictable stochastic stimulus (TV showing random pixels) fixate on it and stop exploring, because maximum curiosity is maintained by the noise source.

Random features are sufficient for game benchmarks that align with the curiosity objective, but learned features generalize better to novel configurations -- novelty_bonus on random features is environment-specific, not general.

Curiosity-driven learning produces high coverage in environments where the agent's actions have learnable consequences; it produces fixation in environments where irreducible randomness is accessible.

Environments where curiosity aligns well with task reward tend to have structured causal relationships between agent actions and state transitions -- the alignment is not guaranteed and breaks in distractors-rich environments.

entries.confidence_rationale: JMLR comprehensive survey; provides the most complete taxonomy of curriculum learning approaches for RL available. Directly relevant to REE's curriculum design question. Mapping fidelity moderate: this is a survey paper, not an empirical study, so it provides framework and classification rather than specific evidence for behavioral diversity. The key contribution for REE is identifying which curriculum design choices are relevant to the monostrategy problem and which are not.
failure_signatures: Curriculum approaches that only vary task difficulty (easy-to-hard) without varying task diversity can still produce monostrategy if all easy and hard tasks require the same strategy -- curriculum must vary behavioral relevance across tasks, not just difficulty.

Transfer between curriculum tasks requires shared structure in the state or action space; if REE's diversity curriculum introduces tasks that are behaviorally orthogonal to the target environment, the transferred policies may not compose correctly.

Source task selection (which tasks to put in the curriculum and in what order) is often the hardest part of curriculum design -- the survey notes this is largely unsolved for automatic curriculum generation.

entries.confidence_rationale: ICLR publication; strong theoretical result (unique optimum = even state-space partition); multiple robotic benchmarks confirm diverse skill emergence. Mapping fidelity is high for ARC-065 (behavioral diversity generation). The REE analog -- using mutual information between context and visited states to prevent mode collapse -- is structurally identical to DIAYN's objective. Main caveat: DIAYN operates in pre-training (no task reward); REE needs diversity during task learning, which is harder.
failure_signatures: Skills may fail to scale to very high-dimensional observation spaces, suggesting MI-based diversity objectives need a compact behavioral embedding (not raw observations) to work in REE's latent space.

Some behaviors remain suboptimal even after training (e.g., ant forward locomotion). DIAYN can learn orthogonal skills that are individually suboptimal rather than the dominant-plus-diverse structure REE needs.

DIAYN requires domain knowledge to incorporate priors about task-relevant features -- without this, the diversity objective may reward modes that are irrelevant to the task (undirected diversity problem).

entries.confidence_rationale: NeurIPS 2020 spotlight. Introduces DvD (Diversity via Determinants), which measures population diversity as the volume of a behavioral embedding manifold via the log-determinant of the kernel matrix. Critical finding: traditional pairwise diversity methods suffer from cycling and redundancy -- only volume-based measures prevent degeneracy. Mapping fidelity is high for ARC-065 (what 'effective' diversity means operationally). Caveat: operates on a population of agents, not a single policy with context variable; direct translation to REE's single-agent CEM requires adaptation.
failure_signatures: Pairwise distance-based diversity measures (e.g. mean L2 distance between policies) suffer from cycling: a population can have high mean pairwise distance but still cluster into a few degenerate modes. Volume-based measures are necessary to catch this failure mode.

Explicitly boosting diversity often hurts performance when reward-landscape exploration is not needed -- REE should not apply diversity pressure uniformly throughout training but adaptively (DvD uses online learning to modulate diversity weight).

Behavioral embeddings that are domain-specific or handcrafted introduce an inductive bias that shapes which diversity modes are captured; REE's embedding must be tuned to capture route-mode diversity, not just action diversity.

entries.confidence_rationale: JMLR publication (submitted 2017, published 2022); grounded in developmental robotics and infant curiosity research; demonstrates automatic curriculum generation through learning progress maximisation across a parameterised goal space. Highly relevant to REE's infant-stage substrate problem: IMGEP's learning-progress-driven curriculum prevents monostrategy by actively seeking goals where the agent is currently making progress, rather than goals where it has already converged. Maps onto ARC-066 (tonic vigor) and ARC-072 (hippocampal cue-indexed goal repertoire). Main caveat: IMGEP's goal space is explicitly parameterised and continuous; REE's goal space is more implicit.
failure_signatures: Learning-progress-based goal selection can stall if the agent reaches a plateau on all current goals simultaneously -- the system needs a mechanism to invent new goals or expand the goal space when progress is zero everywhere.

IMGEP requires the agent to have already learned to pursue some goals before it can generate a useful learning-progress curriculum. A cold-start agent with no goal representation cannot initialise the system -- suggests IMGEP-like curricula require a bootstrapping phase (infant babbling analog) before they can generate diversity.

Without an explicit goal-space parameterisation, learning progress is not computable. REE's implicit goal representation (residue field wanting) needs to be made explicit enough to track per-goal progress for an IMGEP-like curriculum to operate.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational quality-diversity paper, extremely highly cited; introduces the behavioral descriptor / feature map concept that has become the standard approach to structural diversity preservation. Directly relevant to ARC-065. Core finding: maintaining a map of the best solution found per behavioral descriptor cell structurally prevents monostrategy by forcing the archive to retain high-quality solutions across the full behavioral space. Mapping fidelity moderate: MAP-Elites is a population/archive algorithm, not a single-policy algorithm; however the behavioral descriptor concept is directly applicable to REE's candidate evaluation.
failure_signatures: MAP-Elites requires a user-specified behavioral descriptor space. If the descriptor does not capture the behaviorally relevant dimensions of variation (e.g. specifying 'limb usage' for a robot but the relevant diversity axis is 'route taken'), the archive will be diverse on the wrong dimensions and monostrategy on the relevant ones.

Within each cell of the archive, MAP-Elites only retains the single best solution by fitness -- it does not maintain diversity within a cell. This means it enforces between-cell diversity but not within-cell diversity.
MAP-Elites scales poorly in very high-dimensional behavioral descriptor spaces (curse of dimensionality in the archive grid).

entries.confidence_rationale: NeurIPS 2020; strong zero-shot transfer results; decision-theoretic grounding (minimax regret) for curriculum generation. Relevant to REE's environment design question: enriching the reef with competing attractors is necessary but not sufficient; the curriculum of which attractors are salient must match the agent's current capabilities. PAIRED shows that environments calibrated to the edge of agent competence (regret-based) prevent monostrategy by constantly exposing weaknesses. Mapping fidelity moderate: PAIRED targets environment generation, REE's problem is within a fixed environment; the curriculum insight is extractable but the full algorithm is not directly applicable.
failure_signatures: Adding competing attractors to an environment does not prevent monostrategy if the agent's current policy makes one attractor overwhelmingly dominant -- the agent needs to encounter the competing attractors at a difficulty level where they are also tractable. Enriched environments without difficulty calibration produce the same monostrategy as unenriched ones.
Minimax adversarial environment design (without the regret correction) produces environments the agent cannot solve at all -- pure difficulty maximisation is as harmful as no diversity pressure.
Regret-based design requires a second (antagonist) agent as a counterfactual baseline -- computationally expensive for REE's current single-agent setup.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational quality-diversity paper, extremely highly cited; introduces the behavioral descriptor / feature map concept that has become the standard approach to structural diversity preservation. Directly relevant to ARC-065. Core finding: maintaining a map of the best solution found per behavioral descriptor cell structurally prevents monostrategy by forcing the archive to retain high-quality solutions across the full behavioral space. Mapping fidelity moderate: MAP-Elites is a population/archive algorithm, not a single-policy algorithm; however the behavioral descriptor concept is directly applicable to REE's candidate evaluation.
failure_signatures: MAP-Elites requires a user-specified behavioral descriptor space. If the descriptor does not capture the behaviorally relevant dimensions of variation (e.g. specifying 'limb usage' for a robot but the relevant diversity axis is 'route taken'), the archive will be diverse on the wrong dimensions and monostrategy on the relevant ones.

Within each cell of the archive, MAP-Elites only retains the single best solution by fitness -- it does not maintain diversity within a cell. This means it enforces between-cell diversity but not within-cell diversity.
MAP-Elites scales poorly in very high-dimensional behavioral descriptor spaces (curse of dimensionality in the archive grid).

entries.confidence_rationale: JMLR comprehensive survey; provides the most complete taxonomy of curriculum learning approaches for RL available. Directly relevant to REE's curriculum design question. Mapping fidelity moderate: this is a survey paper, not an empirical study, so it provides framework and classification rather than specific evidence for behavioral diversity. failure_signatures: Curriculum approaches that only vary task difficulty (easy-to-hard) without varying task diversity can still produce monostrategy if all easy and hard tasks require the same strategy -- curriculum must vary behavioral relevance across tasks, not just difficulty.

Source task selection (which tasks to put in the curriculum and in what order) is often the hardest part of curriculum design -- the survey notes this is largely unsolved for automatic curriculum generation.

entries.confidence_rationale: NeurIPS 2020; strong zero-shot transfer results; decision-theoretic grounding (minimax regret) for curriculum generation. Relevant to REE's environment design question: enriching the reef with competing attractors is necessary but not sufficient; the curriculum of which attractors are salient must match the agent's current capabilities. PAIRED shows that environments calibrated to the edge of agent competence (regret-based) prevent monostrategy by constantly exposing weaknesses. Mapping fidelity moderate: PAIRED targets environment generation, REE's problem is within a fixed environment; the curriculum insight is extractable but the full algorithm is not directly applicable.

Enriched environments without difficulty calibration produce the same monostrategy as unenriched ones.

Regret-based design requires a second (antagonist) agent as a counterfactual baseline -- computationally expensive for REE's current single-agent setup.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality theoretical review from a leading lab (NYU Infant Action Lab, Adolph) synthesizing decades of empirical work. Mapping fidelity to INV-055/INV-073 is strong: the core claim that behavioral flexibility requires extensive varied motor experience before reinforcement narrows the repertoire directly evidences both invariants. Transfer risk is low -- the developmental substrate (motor-sensory exploration epoch, posture-specific learning, error-as-information) maps cleanly to REE's infant stage design requirements. Confidence capped at 0.78 rather than higher because the paper does not address valence or reward learning directly -- only the affordance/motor side of INV-055.
failure_signatures: Affordance learning is posture-specific: experience as a crawler does not transfer to walking. REE's infant stage would need to support multiple action-posture modalities (or a single abstract motor interface) to avoid re-learning per new capability layer.

Environmental variation is necessary for flexibility: an impoverished training substrate (few object types, fixed layouts, no surface diversity) would produce a narrow option library even with long training time.

entries.confidence_rationale: Well-powered cross-sectional study (N=102) directly testing how experience with different locomotor postures (crawling vs walking) shapes affordance-guided avoidance behavior. The posture-specificity finding -- that crawling experience, but not walking experience, predicts drop-off avoidance in walkers -- is directly relevant to INV-073 (exploration epoch must cover all action modalities) and INV-055 (harm/benefit geography accumulation is posture-specific). The additional finding that longer crawling experience accelerates recalibration to walking posture suggests a cumulative exploration benefit. Confidence at 0.70: study is cross-sectional, uses a specific and dramatic affordance (drop-off avoidance), and does not address the reward/benefit side of INV-055's valence map requirement.
failure_signatures: Affordance learning is posture-specific and does not transfer across locomotor mode: the cliff avoidance learned through crawling only partially transfers to walking, requiring active recalibration. REE's infant stage would need to expose the agent across its full action repertoire, not just a single locomotor policy.
The paper addresses harm avoidance only (drop-off geography), not benefit discovery. REE's INV-055 requires both harm/benefit geography accumulation -- the benefit side is unaddressed here.
Cross-sectional design: causal relationships between crawling experience and affordance learning are inferred, not experimentally verified.

entries.confidence_rationale: Cross-sectional study using the validated AHEMD-IS tool (Affordances in the Home Environment for Motor Development - Infant Scale). N=251 children 18-42 months. Finding: home environment affordance richness significantly predicted personal-social, problem-solving, and communication skills -- not just motor outcomes. This is relevant to INV-055/INV-073 because it demonstrates that affordance diversity in the training environment has downstream effects beyond the motor domain, supporting the claim that the infant stage curriculum richness determines the breadth of the later-stage repertoire. Confidence moderated to 0.65: cross-sectional design cannot establish causality; confounds (SES, education) are noted; the affordance measure is parental self-report; and the paper covers children older than the critical infant window for affordance bootstrapping.
failure_signatures: Cross-sectional design cannot establish causal direction: it is possible that more capable children elicit richer affordance provision from parents, reversing the causal arrow.
SES confounds: all AHEMD-IS dimensions are significantly influenced by socioeconomic status, making it difficult to isolate the affordance richness effect from resource availability effects.
Age range (18-42 months) is post the critical infant window hypothesized for REE: affordance effects may be smaller or saturated earlier.

entries.confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed empirical study, well-powered (experimental vs control design), published in the leading infancy journal. Key finding -- 83% of 6-month-olds increased vocal rate when vocalizations were contingently rewarded with visual feedback -- directly evidences the infant capacity for rapid accidental discovery of action-outcome contingencies. Confidence capped at 0.73: the study does not document the positive affect/valence change upon discovery, only the behavioral change, leaving the 'accidental benefit contact seeds z_goal' part of MECH-189 supported by inference rather than direct measurement.

No measurement of affective state change upon discovery: the study tracks vocalization rate only. The internal state change (motivation, wanting, goal formation) upon contingency detection is inferred, not measured.
The contingency is single-action-to-single-outcome: REE needs multi-action affordance repertoires, which the mobile/iPad paradigm cannot straightforwardly address.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical highly-cited review (~3000 citations) establishing the wanting/liking dissociation with strong experimental evidence. The dissociation is directly relevant to REE's SD-014 valence architecture (VALENCE_WANTING vs VALENCE_LIKING as distinct channels) and to MECH-189 (benefit contacts seed goal anchors). Confidence at 0.72: this is an adult/rodent neuroscience paper; the developmental (infant-stage) application is theoretical transfer. Positive hedonic reactions to sweet taste at birth are noted, but the wanting/liking dissociation in infants specifically is not tested here.
failure_signatures: The wanting/liking dissociation is established in adult animals and humans; its application to the infant learning window requires additional inference -- there is no direct evidence that these systems are independently operational in early infancy.
The paper focuses on pharmacological manipulation (dopamine depletion, benzodiazepines) -- the naturalistic developmental context of REE's infant stage is not directly addressed.

Hedonic 'liking' reactions to sucrose are present from birth, but whether the NAcc-mediated wanting signal is functional as early as 2-3 months (the critical mobile paradigm window) is not established here.

entries.confidence_rationale: Meta-analysis of 34 empirical studies finding positive relationship between pretend play and social competence in early childhood (ages 3-8). Two key moderating findings: (1) studies measuring *quality* of pretend play find stronger correlations with social competence than studies measuring *quantity*, and (2) the relationship weakens with age. These moderating effects are directly relevant to ARC-049 (bilateral frame tag): social competence requires bilateral frame maintenance, and quality of pretend play (whether the child maintains the play frame with a partner) is the relevant dimension, not just frequency. The age-related weakening is consistent with other competencies eventually saturating. Confidence moderate-high: meta-analytic synthesis across 34 studies, no specific effect size retrieved for the overall r value, limiting quantitative mapping.
failure_signatures: Studies measuring quantity of pretend play (hours of play) find weaker correlations with social competence than studies measuring quality (how well the child maintains the bilateral play frame with partners) -- this distinguishes social-competence-relevant pretend play from mere activity.
Solitary pretend play shows lower correlations with social competence than social pretend play -- consistent with the bilateral frame requirement: ARC-049 requires a partner to be fully exercised.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical theoretical paper establishing the decoupling/metarepresentation framework for pretend play. Leslie's decoupling mechanism -- creating a metarepresentational copy that suspends reference, truth, and existence relations -- maps directly onto REE's hypothesis tag (MECH-094). The framework is widely replicated and remains the dominant theoretical account. Confidence is high for the theoretical mapping (REE's hypothesis tag IS a decoupling mechanism). Confidence not maximal because the paper is theoretical (no direct neurobiological substrate specified) and some aspects of Leslie's 'PRETEND' operator remain contested (Jarrold et al. 2010 show pretense understanding can occur without full metarepresentation).
failure_signatures: If pretend play required full metarepresentation, children with theory-of-mind delays would show zero pretend play -- but autism literature shows partial pretend play even with ToM deficits, suggesting the decoupling mechanism is separable from full propositional metarepresentation.

The PRETEND operator in Leslie's framework is unitary; REE predicts a two-tag system (hypothesis tag + play frame tag) that must co-operate -- this is a REE-specific elaboration beyond what Leslie's original framework entails.

entries.confidence_rationale: Compared pretend play in autism (N=28), other developmental disorders (N=24), and typical children (N=26). Key finding: children with autism showed significant deficits in ToM but not EF measures, and ToM (not EF) best predicted pretend play deficits; generativity (one EF measure) showed a secondary role. This supports MECH-198's implication: pretend play failure maps primarily onto the hypothesis tag / metarepresentational decoupling system (ToM-associated), not onto general executive function. This gives REE the ability to distinguish two mechanistically distinct failure modes: ToM-deficit (missing hypothesis tag co-operation) vs. EF-deficit (frame maintenance cost). The autism model also grounds MECH-200/201 failure signatures in developmental deficit data.
failure_signatures: Children with autism who pass EF measures still show pretend play deficits -- EF is not the gating prerequisite; ToM/metarepresentational decoupling is. This contradicts executive function accounts of pretend play development.

Even with ToM deficits, some children with autism produce simple object substitution pretense -- suggesting the play-frame tag (ARC-049, behavioral/intentional level) is partially intact while the hypothesis-tag system (MECH-094) is selectively impaired.

entries.confidence_rationale: ERP study showing that pretense reasoning and false belief reasoning recruit distinct neural processes in 6-8 year olds: pretense elicits an early parietal P2 (incongruence detection) and negative frontal slow wave (intention processing); false belief elicits the characteristic late positive fronto-central slow wave (metarepresentation). This challenges the strong Leslie account of pretend play and false belief sharing the same neural substrate. For REE, this is mixed evidence: it supports that the play-frame tag and the hypothesis tag are distinct cognitive operations (consistent with ARC-049 + MECH-094 being separate mechanisms), but conflicts with a simple 'pretend play exercises false-belief architecture' story. The study uses 6-8 year olds (past the pretend play acquisition window) and ERP is indirect measure of neural substrate.
failure_signatures: If pretend play and false belief shared the same neurocognitive substrate, ERP components should be identical in polarity, latency, and topography -- the observed differences (early/parietal/negative for pretense vs late/fronto-central/positive for FB) argue against substrate identity.

The negative frontal slow wave for pretense reasoning is attributed to 'intention processing' (simpler mentalistic process) rather than full metarepresentation -- suggesting children process others' pretense through behavioral-intentional cues without necessarily engaging the full hypothesis_tag+play_frame system.

entries.confidence_rationale: Large longitudinal cohort (N=1426 from the Longitudinal Study of Australian Children) showing that higher pretend play ability at age 2-3 predicts fewer internalising (anxiety, withdrawal) AND externalising (aggression, hyperactivity) problems at ages 4-5 and 6-7, after controlling for SES, maternal mental health, language, and attachment. Crucially, emotional regulation does NOT mediate the relationship, implicating other mechanisms. This directly evidences INV-061/MECH-200/201: pretend play skill at the developmental window (2-3 years) predicts adult-trajectory mental health outcomes that REE maps to frame-confusion failure modes (internalising = synthetic-reads-as-real derealization/anxiety cluster; externalising = impulsivity/commitment-without-evaluation cluster). The non-mediation by emotional regulation is a meaningful negative finding that constrains mechanistic accounts.
failure_signatures: Emotional regulation does not mediate the pretend play -> mental health relationship -- if frame-distinction skill were simply a downstream effect of emotion regulation, emotional regulation should fully mediate. Its failure to mediate supports an independent frame-distinction mechanism.

The relationship covers both internalising AND externalising outcomes -- if it were purely about anxiety (one failure direction), only internalising effects would appear. The dual direction is consistent with REE's two failure modes: real-reads-as-synthetic (MECH-200, derealization/mania) and synthetic-reads-as-real (MECH-201, anxiety/delusion).

entries.confidence_rationale: Empirical demonstration that pretend play and counterfactual reasoning use the same underlying cognitive machinery: children transfer newly learned causal structure into pretend scenarios at the same rate as into explicit counterfactuals, and the correlation persists after controlling for age, general cognitive development, and executive function (r=0.38, p<0.05). This directly evidences MECH-198's claim that pretend play exercises counterfactual representation. The causal coherence finding -- children in pretend mode make causally valid interventions on the pretend system -- supports the REE claim that play frame does not suppress causal/simulation learning, only stake-reality. Sample is preschoolers, relatively small N, single lab; confidence moderate-high.
failure_signatures: If pretend play and counterfactual reasoning were entirely separable cognitive systems, the correlation after EF controls should be near zero -- the residual r=0.38 argues against full separability and favors a shared imaginative capacity.

Children who do not engage in causally coherent pretense (e.g. treating pretend scenarios as arbitrary) show reduced counterfactual transfer, suggesting causal coherence maintenance during play is a prerequisite for the training benefit.

entries.confidence_rationale: Demonstrates that working memory and inhibitory control each partially mediate the relationship between counterfactual thinking and false belief performance in 3-5 year olds (N=76). This establishes the executive function prerequisites for counterfactual cognition in the same age window as pretend play emergence. The specific dissociation of working memory and inhibitory control as separable mediators maps onto the dual demands REE places on the hypothesis_tag system (maintaining the synthetic representation in working memory while inhibiting the real-consequence pathway). Confidence moderate-high: direct measurement of EF components, but correlational design limits causal inference about the developmental order.
failure_signatures: After controlling for both working memory and inhibitory control, counterfactual reasoning still accounts for unique variance in false belief, suggesting a residual representational capacity (Leslie's PRETEND operator; REE's hypothesis tag) beyond pure EF.

3-year-olds show floor performance on both counterfactual and false belief tasks -- the 3-to-4 year developmental jump correlates with EF maturation, placing the pretend play / commitment architecture calibration window at age 3-4.

Transfer risk is moderate because the paper addresses moral obligation broadly, not games-with-rules specifically. Mapping fidelity is high for the developmental claim but requires extension to the play frame context.
failure_signatures: The paper's focus is moral obligation, not play frame maintenance -- the game context is one example among many.
Theoretical review without new primary data; empirical claims rely on cited studies.
The we > me self-regulation mechanism may apply more to cooperative play (ARC-049 full bilateral) than to early games-with-rules at age 3-4.

entries.confidence_rationale: RCT with 3-month follow-up directly comparing EF outcomes across play types (movement, puzzle, language play). High source quality for design. Mapping fidelity is moderate: the study uses play categories that do not directly map to Piaget/Smilansky play types, but the finding that rule-based structures within play drive EF gains -- regardless of specific play type -- directly evidences MECH-197's mechanism claim. Transfer risk is low.
failure_signatures: Working memory effects of movement play were not maintained at 3-month follow-up -- play-type specificity for WM is weak.
Play categories (movement, puzzle, language) do not directly map to the sensorimotor/constructive/pretend/rule-games taxonomy, limiting direct MECH-197 mapping.
No active control matched for adult engagement -- facilitator effects cannot be fully ruled out.

entries.confidence_rationale: Longitudinal study (3 timepoints: baseline, post-intervention, 8-month follow-up) testing 32 specifically designed games targeting inhibitory control, working memory, and cognitive flexibility. Key finding -- sustained EF improvements at 8 months -- is relevant to DEV-NEED-013 (games-with-rules training). Source quality is moderate (Frontiers in Psychology). Mapping fidelity is moderate: the designed games include rule-based structures but are not specifically games-with-rules in the Piagetian sense. Transfer risk is low.
failure_signatures: Games were adult-designed and administered (60 daily sessions), not naturalistic peer games -- social coordination and bilateral frame-maintenance are not being trained.
Effect sizes between T1 and T2 (immediately post-intervention) were not significant; only T1-T3 (8-month) effects reached significance -- medium-term consolidation rather than immediate transfer.
No active control matched for adult game-facilitation -- cannot rule out general engagement effects.

entries.confidence_rationale: Provides direct empirical evidence for continuous frame monitoring at 3 months of age -- infants track multimodal game structure moment-by-moment and respond with reduced engagement when structure is altered mid-game. This is the earliest developmental evidence for continuous frame monitoring rather than discrete boundary detection. Transfer risk is moderate because 3-month-old mother-infant games are far from peer rule games. Mapping fidelity for Q-035 is high in terms of directionality (evidence for ongoing monitoring) but involves a large developmental step.
failure_signatures: Study uses 3-month-old infants in mother-infant dyads -- this is sensorimotor play, not games-with-rules, making the direct REE mapping indirect.
Game structure alteration was adult-imposed (researcher removed sound or gesture) rather than partner-generated violation; does not test bilateral enforcement.
Effects are on engagement metrics (limb movements, gaze) not protest or repair -- normative enforcement is not present at this age.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong empirical design testing a nuanced prediction: children should monitor not just rule compliance but also strategic rationality (trying to win), both of which are normatively required in competitive games. Finding that 5-year-olds but not 3-year-olds grasp the dual-level structure maps to MECH-197's developmental timeline. High source quality (Max Planck group, JECP). Mapping fidelity is high for ARC-049/INV-059 and for the frame complexity increase at games-with-rules stage.
failure_signatures: Three-year-olds only protested rule breaches from irrational opponents, not from rational ones -- full dual-level understanding comes after age 3, consistent with MECH-197 but indicating late timing.
Many 3-year-olds refrained from protesting altogether, suggesting partial understanding only.
Puppet-as-opponent paradigm may not fully capture naturalistic peer game dynamics.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct empirical test of children's sensitivity to normative rule structure in games. High source quality (Developmental Psychology, Max Planck group). Mapping fidelity is strong: the key finding -- children distinguish game-constitutive violations from identical acts outside the game context -- maps directly onto ARC-049's co-maintained context tag (the frame determines normative status of actions). The bilateral enforcement finding (children police violations on third parties) supports INV-059. Transfer risk is low: human child developmental data maps cleanly to REE's developmental curriculum claim.
failure_signatures: Two-year-olds showed normative responses at a less explicit level than three-year-olds, suggesting shared-frame normativity is not fully consolidated before age 3.
The study used simple experimenter-introduced games, not naturalistic peer play -- ecological validity of frame co-maintenance outside adult-structured contexts untested.

entries.confidence_rationale: Feldman's review synthesises evidence that parent-infant synchrony -- the temporal matching of affective behavior across the dyad -- has physiological precursors in neonatal oscillator systems (sleep-wake cyclicity, cardiac vagal tone) and predicts self-regulation, symbol use, and empathy across childhood. Crucially, synchrony is characterised as a continuous, temporally-matched process (not episodic): it requires ongoing monitoring of the partner's state to maintain the match. The biological grounding of synchrony in oscillatory systems (shared with sleep-wake regulation) is directly relevant to REE's model of frame monitoring as a biological rhythm. Moderate-high confidence: comprehensive review, strong empirical base, but as a review it synthesises heterogeneous methods. The connection to DEV-NEED-015 (caregiver protection function) is strong: synchrony failure predicts psychopathology trajectories.
failure_signatures: Review paper -- individual effect sizes vary widely across synthesised studies.
Synchrony operationalisation varies across studies (concurrent, sequential, patterned); the monitoring mechanism underlying synchrony is inferred rather than directly tested.
The physiological precursor story (neonatal oscillators -> social synchrony) is correlational, not mechanistic.

entries.confidence_rationale: Gergely and Watson develop the social biofeedback theory: contingency detection is a dedicated mechanism (not derived from general learning) that infants use to track whether caregiver responses are temporally and probabilistically contingent on infant behavior. The mechanism detects the degree of contingency, maximises toward high-contingency partners, and uses contingency to build secondary representations of emotional states. This provides the mechanistic substrate for continuous frame monitoring: the contingency detection module is the primitive monitoring mechanism. Theoretical paper -- confidence is limited by lack of direct experimental evidence in this paper, but the framework has been supported by a large experimental literature. Directly grounds INV-059 (mutual frame maintenance as necessity) in a biologically-based mechanism.
failure_signatures: This is primarily a theoretical paper; empirical support comes from cited studies rather than novel data.
The theory focuses on dyadic contingency with a caregiver, not mutual peer-play frames -- the 'bilateral' aspect of ARC-049 is not directly addressed.
The contingency-detection module is posited as specialized but its neural substrate and developmental origin are left unspecified in this paper.

entries.confidence_rationale: Cross-sectional study across 2-, 4-, and 6-month-olds in organized vs. disorganized peekaboo. Two-month-olds show no differential response to organized vs. disorganized structure -- they are sensitive only to the presence of a social partner. Four-month-olds show the monitoring upgrade: they smile more and gaze less in organized games, suggesting they now track the narrative envelope (timing and structure) of the interaction, not just its presence. This provides a developmental timeline for when monitoring CONTENT escalates from primitive contingency-detection (present by 2-3 months) to structure-sensitive monitoring (present by 4 months). Strongly relevant to MECH-197's claim that play type progression adds content-complexity without switching on monitoring.
failure_signatures: Cross-sectional design (not longitudinal) so individual developmental trajectories are not captured.
The organized/disorganized peekaboo manipulation confounds timing with narrative coherence -- hard to isolate whether infants are monitoring timing per se or overall predictability.
Sample size is moderate (36 infants across three age groups, 12 per group).

entries.confidence_rationale: This study tracks within-episode dynamics during the still-face period using hierarchical linear modelling. Infant social bidding (smiling while gazing at parent), gaze, and smiling all decrease significantly over time within the still-face episode, while cry-face increases. This dynamic is the first rigorous quantification of what happens during continuous monitoring of a contingency failure: infants do not simply detect the frame violation at onset and then hold steady -- they show a progressive response trajectory across the episode. This is key evidence that the monitoring is ongoing and drives graded behavioral responses, not just a one-shot violation detector. Changes within the episode predict attachment and internalizing problems -- establishing individual difference validity.
failure_signatures: Hierarchical linear modelling captures population-level trajectories, not individual monitoring cycles -- cannot determine sampling rate of the monitoring process.
The progressive bidding decrease could reflect fatigue or affect regulation cascades rather than monitoring-driven inference.
Still-face confounds contingency monitoring with face-processing and social stress -- cannot isolate monitoring contribution.

entries.confidence_rationale: The double-video replay paradigm isolates temporal contingency from affective content: infants watched either a live video feed of their mother (contingent) or a replay of the same mother's behavior from minutes earlier (same face, same vocalizations, identical content but time-shifted, non-contingent). Two-month-olds showed reduced positive affect and gaze during replay despite identical visual content. This dissociates contingency detection from content recognition, showing that the monitoring system tracks the time-relationship of responses, not just their presence. This is the clearest evidence that temporal contingency monitoring is operational at 2 months. Replicated by Stormark and Braarud (2004) with the same double-video method.
failure_signatures: Original study had small N (four 2-month-olds in early version); later replications have larger samples.
The closed-circuit TV setup introduces some ecological artificiality versus face-to-face interaction.
Some replication attempts found the effect smaller or less consistent than the original, raising questions about the exact temporal window of sensitivity.

entries.confidence_rationale: The foundational still-face paradigm demonstrates that infants as young as 3-4 months immediately detect when a caregiver's interactive behavior violates the expected contingency structure of face-to-face play. Infants respond with reduced positive affect, social bidding, and eventual withdrawal -- not just at play boundaries but during the unresponsiveness itself. This is classic evidence that continuous monitoring (not just boundary detection) is operational from early infancy. The original paper has been replicated hundreds of times across cultures. High source quality. Mapping fidelity is high: the paradigm directly tests whether infants track within-episode contingency, not just episode transitions.
failure_signatures: The SFP disrupts adult behavior entirely (not just content changes mid-game), so it does not isolate monitoring from detection of partner state change.
Cannot distinguish whether infants monitor frame state continuously or only sample it at high frequency.
Still-face collapses contingency and affect -- the monitoring signal and the affective channel are conflated.

entries.confidence_rationale: This study provides a developmental onset boundary for continuous social contingency monitoring: 1-month-olds do not discriminate Normal, Non-Contingent, and Imitation interaction conditions; 3-month-olds do (gazing longer in imitation, smiling more in normal vs. non-contingent). The developmental transition between 1 and 3 months pins the emergence of the monitoring architecture to a narrow window, before pretend play, theory-of-mind, or language. High quality journal, within-study comparison design, clean manipulation. Directly addresses when the monitoring capacity comes online.
failure_signatures: Single lab, relatively small N per age group.

The three conditions (Normal, Non-Contingent, Imitation) conflate contingency and timing -- Imitation is contingent but time-delayed, making it hard to isolate what dimension 3-month-olds are sensitive to.
Does not track within-episode dynamics -- cannot determine whether monitoring is continuous or periodic sampling.

entries.confidence_rationale: Recent Frontiers paper directly addressing play-frame integrity in robot-mediated play activities with children. Operationally distinguishes genuine play (pleasant, voluntary, intrinsically motivated) from non-play (externally imposed, therapeutically directed). Uses observational behavioral measures (sustained engagement, cooperative behaviors, emotional regulation, skill transfer) rather than parametric metrics -- these are qualitative but ecologically valid. Supports INV-058 (play is structurally necessary; without bounded low-stakes context, exploration requires harm acceptance) and INV-059 (bilateral frame maintenance). Relevance to ARC-049 comes from the six-step design process which implicitly describes a co-maintained frame: the robot environment and the child both sustain play conditions. Mapping fidelity moderate -- the framework is prescriptive/design-oriented, not metric-oriented.
failure_signatures: No formal metrics are defined for play frame integrity -- the paper uses qualitative observation and practitioner feedback, which are not operationalizable as DEV-NEED gate criteria.
The paper does not address frame breakdown operationally -- play vs non-play is treated as a design property (activity design = play mode), not as a detected state that can collapse.
Sample sizes are small and participant characteristics are difficult to capture -- ecological validity comes at the cost of statistical rigor.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical empirical study with ethogram-based quantification of play frame maintenance signals across three canid species. Non-random placement of play bows relative to ambiguous actions operationally defines frame integrity measurement. High source quality (Behaviour journal, widely cited). Moderate transfer risk from animal ethology to REE because the play bow is a motor signal, not a latent-space tag -- the mapping requires the additional claim that bilateral signal architecture is functionally analogous. Important for INV-059 (bilateral frame maintenance necessity) and ARC-049 (co-maintained context tag) because it shows empirically that frame maintenance signals are timed to prevent confusion at the transition point between play and non-play actions.
failure_signatures: Recent work (Rooney et al. 2016, Ward et al. 2023) finds no evidence for metacommunicative function of play bows -- bows may re-initiate play after pauses rather than clarify ambiguous actions, which would weaken the frame-punctuation interpretation.
The study addresses animal canids, not children or robots -- transfer to bilateral tag architecture in REE requires assuming structural analogy that the paper does not establish.
Frame breakdown signatures (escalation to real aggression) are identified narratively but not formally measured in a transition-detection framework.

entries.confidence_rationale: ICLR-published computational framework demonstrating that diverse skills can be acquired without reward by maximizing mutual information I(S;Z) between states and skill identifiers. The discriminability metric operationalizes rollout diversity measurement: skills are diverse to the extent that a discriminator can reliably identify which skill generated a given state sequence. This provides a concrete diversity metric for the DEV-NEED gate. However, DIAYN does not model play frames -- all skill learning is real-signal (states are real environment states) -- and the mutual information metric measures discriminability rather than strategy-calibration separation. Mapping fidelity to MECH-195 is moderate: DIAYN separates what-skill from how-well-skilled (the two entropy components) but does not separate strategy structure from magnitude calibration in the REE sense.
failure_signatures: DIAYN skills are learned without reward -- this is not analogous to play (which uses synthetic rewards). The absence of reward in DIAYN is a methodological choice; play's synthetic reward is a frame-maintenance mechanism. The analogy is structural, not mechanistic.
Mutual information I(S;Z) measures discriminability of state distributions, not strategy quality or calibration accuracy. A skill can be highly discriminable but poorly calibrated.
State coverage (skill state distributions being spread across the state space) is used as a proxy for diversity but may conflate geometric coverage with behavioral strategy diversity.

entries.confidence_rationale: Empirically demonstrated computational system (real humanoid robot) achieving automatic curriculum via competence-progress measurement. The competence-progress metric -- rate of change in success rate within sliding windows over goal regions -- is operationally defined and non-Goodharted: it selects for regions where learning is active, not for regions where performance is already high or already near chance. Direct relevance to INV-060 (play dominates childhood; type progresses by subsystem competence) and MECH-197 (stage progression tracks competence dependencies). Source quality high (JMLR). Mapping fidelity moderate because IMGEP uses goal-region competence rather than play-mode competence specifically.
failure_signatures: IMGEP does not distinguish play mode from non-play mode -- all exploration is treated as intrinsically motivated, without a separate frame signal architecture.
Competence progress metric is continuous; stage transitions are not formally gated -- the curriculum is self-organizing but does not produce discrete stage certificates.
Diversity of the learned repertoire is measured implicitly by goal coverage, not by an explicit behavioral characterization metric -- this conflates exploration coverage with behavioral diversity.

entries.confidence_rationale: Well-specified review synthesizing infant and robot developmental data. Stage metrics (retention interval, reactivation window, generalization tolerance, means-end revaluation) are operationally concrete and cross-validated across species. Moderate transfer risk because the robot blueprint is architecturally schematic rather than implemented end-to-end. Mapping fidelity to INV-060 (play dominates child phase, progression by subsystem competence) is indirect -- the paper does not explicitly discuss play as the mechanism, only sensorimotor contingency sensitivity. Strong alignment with MECH-197 stage ordering via the 3-month, 6-month, 9-month, 24-month developmental pivots.
failure_signatures: The paper does not define discrete gated stages with formal threshold criteria -- progression is described as continuous accumulation of matching events, not as a pass/fail stage gate.

Competence-calibration separation is implicit, not formally defined: the finding that 7-month-olds have bidirectional contingency knowledge but cannot use it in action selection shows dissociation, but no metric distinguishes the two channels.
Blueprint architecture is schematic (Mannella 2018 instantiation) rather than a validated metric framework usable as a developmental readiness gate.
