Recent (2025) single-unit + causal optogenetic Nature paper showing basal-ganglia OUTPUT (SNr) bidirectionally and movement-specifically licenses AND suppresses ongoing forelimb movements in real time. Establishes the EFFECTOR for maintenance-time motor-program release exists at the BG-output / motor-latch level and is continuous and granular, distinct from slow goal-level disengagement. Strong source; transfer risk elevated by mouse-to-REE-latch gap and because the paper frames pauses as movement-enabling rather than the release per se.
failure_signatures: Falasconi frame SNr firing PAUSES as movement-ENABLING (release of a movement) and INCREASES as suppression -- the sign convention is movement-specific and bidirectional, so a naive 'increase = abort' reading is wrong; the abort of a committed program is the increase-firing suppression on that specific movement channel.

Suppression is movement-specific (one neuron pauses for movement A while increasing to suppress A when movement B runs) -- a global non-specific brake would be the wrong model for a targeted commitment release.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, high-quality psychophysics + bounded-accumulation model directly demonstrating that an ALREADY-INITIATED action is revised/reversed by post-decisional evidence still in the processing pipeline. Maps tightly onto the 592f reach axis (release of an already-committed action on continued degraded decisiveness). Mapping fidelity high; transfer risk moderate (perceptual-decision reach task vs REE commitment latch, but the structural primitive -- post-commit evidence can abort -- is exactly the gap).
failure_signatures: The reversal is graded and evidence-driven (bounded accumulation continues post-decision), NOT a one-shot threshold flag -- a Schmitt-style K-consecutive-ticks-below-floor release at the latch would discard the continued-accumulation dynamics this paper shows are the mechanism.

Changes of mind improve accuracy when the initial decision was erroneous but can also wrongly reverse a correct decision; a maintenance-time release driven by transient low decisiveness risks premature abort of a correct-but-hard commitment.

entries.confidence_rationale: Causal human STN-DBS evidence that the STN mediates a fast, NON-SELECTIVE (global) cortico-motor brake triggered by an EXTERNAL stop signal. entries.confidence_rationale: Causal human intervention (STN-DBS ON/OFF within-subject) plus EEG + drift-diffusion modeling showing the STN dynamically modulates the decision/commitment threshold in real time and that disrupting the STN removes the brake (impulsive responding). Directly grounds ARC-063's availability-vs-expression DISTINCTION: the basal ganglia provide a selective, dynamic GATE on which frontal representations are UPDATED/maintained (become available), separate from selecting the final action. Gating is binary/selective per stripe in the model; ARC-063's tolerance gate is graded/threshold-based -- the model grounds the gating FUNCTION but not the graded-tolerance form (the threshold papers cover the graded part).

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong human empirical + causal (DBS reversal) evidence that a frontally-set, STN-implemented threshold scales with conflict -- the exact mechanism ARC-063's tolerance-gate borrows. Confidence held mid by mapping caveat: it is a response/decision (drift-diffusion) threshold, not a rule-AVAILABILITY threshold; REE extends the mechanism to a new target.
failure_signatures: The measured threshold is a motor-response evidence-accumulation bound (drift-diffusion boundary), not a gate on which abstract RULE becomes available; mapping the STN conflict-threshold onto rule-availability is an architectural extension, not a demonstrated identity.

STN DBS REMOVED the adaptive coupling (produced impulsive choice), so the mechanism is necessary for the adaptive threshold -- a REE tolerance-gate without an STN-analog dynamic-adjustment pathway would predict the same impulsive failure mode.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical computational model showing cortical conflict drives a DYNAMIC, adaptive threshold via the cortico-subthalamic-pallidal loop -- grounds ARC-063's adaptive-threshold (not fixed) requirement. Confidence mid: it is a response-selection model, not rule-availability, and is a simulation rather than direct measurement.
failure_signatures: The threshold modulated is on response EXECUTION timing, not on rule availability; the model has no representation of abstract rules competing for admission.

The model predicts that without the STN dynamic-threshold pathway, multiple competing options produce premature responding -- so a REE tolerance-gate lacking an adaptive (conflict-sensitive) component, not just a fixed bar, would fail under rule competition.

entries.confidence_rationale: Behavioural + optogenetic confirmation that the ~1s NAc synaptic eligibility-trace window governs a reward-sensitive period -- bridges the synaptic mechanism (Brzosko) to behaviour and to biologically plausible RL eligibility traces. Mid confidence: NAc Pavlovian reward, not rule-level credit.
failure_signatures: The reward-sensitive window is ~1s and tied to NAc presynaptic activity for a sensorimotor event -- ARC-063 rule-evidence traces are presumed to operate over much longer, rule-relevant horizons, a timescale gap this paper does not address.
Establishes credit timing for a sensorimotor cue->reward association, not for a rule that organised the behaviour.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical experimental demonstration of a synaptic eligibility trace: a delayed dopamine signal retroactively converts STDP depression to potentiation, solving the distal-reward credit problem. Directly grounds the biological mechanism for ARC-063 element (iv) per-action evidence-trace credit. Held below top band because it credits a SYNAPSE, not a labelled rule.
failure_signatures: The credited unit is a synapse with a ~1s eligibility window, not an abstract rule; ARC-063's rule-level evidence-trace credit is an extension of this synaptic mechanism, not a demonstrated rule-level instance.
Hippocampal slice + NMDA/PKA-dependent; whether the same retroactive-credit mechanism operates on cortical/PFC rule_state representations is untested here.

entries.confidence_rationale: Lesion evidence that frontopolar cortex selectively supports crediting RECENT outcome trends to update the active contingency model (vs cumulative history) -- grounds the frontal contribution to crediting the currently-active rule/model for recent outcomes. Mixed/mid: it is contingency-model updating, not credit to a distinct rule object, and is correlational at the rule level.
failure_signatures: Frontopolar lesion abolished recent-trend extrapolation but left cumulative reward learning intact -- so a REE rule-field that credited only cumulative history (no recent-trend channel) would reproduce the lesion deficit, i.e. ARC-063 needs a recent-trend credit pathway distinct from cumulative accumulation.
The credited entity is a reward-contingency model, not an explicit rule; mapping to per-rule credit is an extension.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical demonstration that PFC single neurons explicitly encode abstract rules that generalise to novel stimuli -- direct evidence that a rule is a represented quantity with a neural substrate, grounding the existence of an ARC-063 CandidateRule representation. Held below top band: it shows rule CODING, not a FIELD of competing candidate rules with tolerance/eligibility attributes.
failure_signatures: Demonstrates that rules ARE encoded, but with only two rules in effect -- it does not show a population holding MANY candidate rules simultaneously, nor the per-rule attributes (tolerance, context-tags, evidence) ARC-063 requires.
Rule coding is reported at the single-neuron level; whether a distributed FIELD with graded availability exists is not addressed here (Weber 2023 subspace entry covers the population geometry).

entries.confidence_rationale: Review arguing the subiculum transforms granular hippocampal codes into memory SCHEMAS encoding environmental + task-imposed behavioural regularities, with subicular->mPFC outputs facilitating rule-guided action. Grounds a schema-cell substrate for the field's bottom-up 'in' face + the rule_state->mPFC output path. Held mid: review (not primary), spatial/behavioural schemas, mapping to a CandidateRule field is interpretive.
failure_signatures: Schemas here are spatial/behavioural-pattern regularities (boundaries, axes, pre/post-choice zones), not the affect-weighted, tolerance-gated CandidateRules ARC-063 specifies; the schema-to-rule mapping is interpretive.
It is a review synthesising existing findings, not a primary demonstration of a rule field; weight is conceptual.

entries.confidence_rationale: Human intracranial evidence that mixed-selective PFC populations hold multiple task variables in DISTINCT low-dimensional subspaces, partitioning to minimise interference -- the representational geometry that lets multiple candidate rules coexist in one field without collapse. Mid-high: task variables (past/present states), not labelled rules; geometry transfers by analogy.
failure_signatures: The coexisting representations are past vs present task states, not multiple candidate RULES; ARC-063 assumes the same subspace-partitioning geometry scales to a field of rules, which is an extrapolation.

Interference between coexisting codes incurs a behavioural switch cost even when resolved -- so a CandidateRule field holding many rules should predict residual switch/interference costs, a falsifiable consequence.

entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical statement of the binding problem and the claim that conjoining separable features into a coherent object REQUIRES focal attention -- pre-attentive feature maps are registered in parallel but their conjunction is a serial, attention-gated act. This directly grounds ARC-006's design constraint that 'binding is attention-gated' (entities_and_binding.md), the single most load-bearing and most-cited part of ARC-006. Discounted from the top band because illusory conjunctions and serial conjunction search are behavioural signatures whose strict serial/parallel dichotomy was later softened (Wolfe's Guided Search, the 2019 40-years retrospective), and because the theory is about within-moment perceptual binding, not the across-time persistence ARC-006 also asserts.
failure_signatures: The strict serial-conjunction / parallel-feature dichotomy was empirically softened by later work (Guided Search; the 2019 special issue); a REE binding stage modelled as a hard serial bottleneck would over-commit to the 1980 form of the theory.

FIT addresses within-moment feature CONJUNCTION (what binds into one object now), not across-time entity PERSISTENCE (whether it is the same object later) -- so it grounds ARC-006's binding clause but not its persistence clause (Kahneman/Scholl entries carry persistence).

Illusory conjunctions show binding can FAIL without attention -- a REE system that merges features feedforward without an attention/precision gate would predict mis-binding the theory says should occur.

entries.confidence_rationale: The foundational multiple-object-tracking demonstration: observers track ~4-5 target items among identical moving distractors, which Pylyshyn explains with FINST visual indexes -- a small set of pre-conceptual pointers that INDIVIDUATE and stick to objects across motion without encoding their features or locations. This grounds two ARC-006 properties at once: entities are SPARSE (a hard ~4-5 index limit) and PERSISTENT/bindable (the index sticks to the same token through motion). It also grounds the token-instance individuation MECH-045 needs. Held mid-band because the items are featureless identical dots (it isolates individuation/tracking but says nothing about feature BINDING per se), the capacity limit is debated, and it is human psychophysics.
failure_signatures: The tracked items are identical featureless dots, so the paradigm isolates pure INDIVIDUATION+tracking and is silent on feature binding -- it cannot ground ARC-006's bindable-feature-bundle clause, only its sparse-persistent-token clause.

The ~4-5 index capacity is a strong, debated empirical limit; a REE that hard-codes a small fixed slot count would inherit a specific psychophysical number whose generality (and dependence on speed/spacing) is contested.

FINST indexes are pre-conceptual location-trackers that explicitly do NOT carry identity/feature content; treating them as full object files over-reads the construct -- indexing is necessary for, but distinct from, the object-file buffer.

entries.confidence_rationale: A review whose thesis is, almost verbatim, MECH-044: the hippocampus rapidly, continuously and obligatorily forms associations among disparate elements across space and time AND enables comparison of stored representations against current input -- i.e. relational binding AND comparison, extending beyond long-term storage into ongoing cognition. The mapping to MECH-044 is the tightest in this pull. Held below the top band because it is a review (synthesis of eye-movement, amnesia, and fMRI evidence) rather than a single decisive experiment, and because 'continuous/obligatory online binding' is the strong end of the literature -- a falsifiable but not universally settled position.
failure_signatures: The 'obligatory, continuous, online' framing is the strong end of the hippocampal-function debate; conjunctive-coding and pure long-term-consolidation accounts contest whether binding/comparison is genuinely ONLINE or a retrieval artifact -- a REE design that wires hippocampal binding into the moment-to-moment loop adopts the contested strong reading.

The review aggregates human eye-movement, developmental-amnesia and fMRI evidence; it does not by itself isolate the binding-vs-comparison computations mechanistically, so it grounds THAT the hippocampus does relational binding+comparison, not a circuit-level HOW that REE could copy.

Relational binding here is across arbitrary elements (faces, scenes, items); it is not specifically about OBJECT-file token persistence, so it supports MECH-044 strongly but only indirectly supports the object-file clause of ARC-006/MECH-045.

entries.confidence_rationale: The foundational empirical demonstration of the object file: a temporary, token-instance episodic buffer that links successive states of THE SAME object across time and motion. The object-specific preview benefit (faster naming when prime and target are bound to one continuing object) is exactly the minimal across-time entity-persistence buffer MECH-045 posits. Robust (7 experiments, 203 subjects, ~2148 citations) and the mapping to MECH-045 is near-literal -- 'object file' is the term of art MECH-045 borrows. Held below 0.9 because the paradigm is visual psychophysics in humans, whereas MECH-045 must instantiate the buffer in a latent-stack agent, and the object file here is purely token-instance whereas REE's live z_object lineage is type-level (the gap the pull was commissioned to expose).
failure_signatures: The object file is strictly TOKEN-instance (this object, this episode); it provides no account of type/category abstraction, which is where REE's live z_resource/z_object lineage actually operates -- so this paper grounds the buffer REE does NOT yet have, not the one it has.

Object-specific benefit is fragile: it requires perceived spatiotemporal continuity of a single object; when continuity cues are removed the benefit collapses, so a REE object-file buffer cannot be a free-floating key-value store -- persistence must be gated on a continuity computation REE does not currently run.

Demonstrated for a single reviewed object across a brief preview-target interval; it does not establish persistence across long occlusions or many concurrent objects (Pylyshyn/Scholl entries cover capacity and occlusion).

entries.confidence_rationale: The load-bearing entry for the memo's central token-vs-type distinction. Five experiments (158 infants) show 10-month-olds trace numerical identity through occlusion using SPATIOTEMPORAL information (token/instance) but do NOT use property/kind information (type) to individuate -- the kind-based route emerges later (~12 months). Directly grounds the claim that true permanence is token-instance tracking, distinct from type identity. Marked 'mixed' because it simultaneously SUPPORTS the token-permanence pillar and WEAKENS the assumption that REE's type-level identity (SD-049) suffices for permanence -- REE has built the developmentally LATER, kind-based route and lacks the earlier spatiotemporal-token route permanence rests on.
failure_signatures: REE's live object identity (SD-015 z_resource + SD-049 type tag + SD-057 IncentiveTokenBank keyed by type) is PROPERTY/KIND-based -- the route Xu & Carey show develops LATER and is NOT what young infants use to track identity through occlusion. REE has the inverse developmental order: it implements type-based identity but lacks the spatiotemporal token-tracking that permanence actually requires.

Spatiotemporal individuation requires representing distinct locations/trajectories of a token across an occluding gap (e.g. an object that goes behind a screen and a second that comes out the other side => two objects). REE's stores encode neither a per-token trajectory nor a 'how many distinct objects' count -- the ghost bank keys by anchor, the incentive bank by type; neither performs numerical individuation.

The dissociation means a fourth per-object store built for permanence on the existing TYPE key would reproduce REE's gap rather than close it: the unit for permanence must be a spatiotemporally-tracked token, not a category.

entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical statement of the core-knowledge object principles (cohesion, continuity, contact). The CONTINUITY principle -- an object traces exactly one connected path through space and time -- IS the formal content of permanence: an object cannot wink out and reappear, so it must be represented as continuing through occlusion. High mapping fidelity to ARC-006's 'persistent' clause and to the permanence pillar's spatiotemporal-continuity criterion. Confidence below 0.8 because it is a theoretical synthesis (the empirical weight lives in the studies it reviews) and because the principles describe perceptual INPUT analysis, not a memory buffer.
failure_signatures: The principles characterise how infants SEGMENT and INDIVIDUATE objects from surface/motion arrays at perception time; they are not a theory of how an out-of-view object is STORED. ARC-006/MECH-045 must add the buffer that continuity implies but the principles do not themselves specify.

Cohesion (a single bounded contour moving as a connected whole) maps to the object-file UNIT, but REE's z_world is engineered pre-split (MECH-278 'architectural shortcut past stage 2'), so REE currently bypasses the very segmentation the cohesion principle describes.

The principles are deliberately KIND-neutral -- they define 'bounded physical object' without sortal/category content. This is the right level for a token object-file, but it is orthogonal to REE's SD-049 TYPE-tag identity; the two address different questions and should not be conflated.

entries.confidence_rationale: Reframes Piaget's A-not-B error as a recall-plus-inhibition (prefrontal) limit on USING a representation to guide action, not a failure of the object representation itself. The hide-to-reach delay tolerated before the error grows ~2 s/month (7.5 -> 12 months); dorsolateral-PFC lesions in monkeys reproduce the error. Grounds the competence/performance -- equivalently the STORE/READOUT -- dissociation that the SD-039/MECH-292/293 ghost-goal bank embodies: a persistent store can be intact while the action-readout perseverates. Confidence 0.71: strong, longitudinally precise, lesion-corroborated, but the substrate (PFC working memory/inhibition) is not REE's (hippocampal anchored value store), so the mapping is functional-analogical.
failure_signatures: The A-not-B error is a PERSEVERATIVE READOUT failure (inability to inhibit the prepotent reach to the previously rewarded location A) under a memory delay -- the object representation can be intact while action goes to the wrong place. A permanence store that is correct can still drive wrong behaviour if its readout/selection layer perseverates.

Diamond's mechanism is prefrontal working memory + response inhibition; REE's ghost-goal bank is a hippocampal-anchor value store queried by wanting-rank. The store/readout split maps functionally but the substrate does not, so REE's analog of the A-not-B failure would live in the query/selection layer, not in PFC.

The error is delay-dependent and matures continuously; a static persistence buffer with no delay-sensitive readout would not reproduce the developmental signature, suggesting permanence in REE needs a graded, delay/decay-sensitive retrieval stage, not just a store.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational and many-times-replicated demonstration that a hidden object is REPRESENTED as continuing to exist long before Piaget's manual-search criterion. Directly grounds the existence of a persistence buffer (MECH-045): permanence is a representational competence dissociable from action. Confidence held at 0.7 rather than higher because (a) the drawbridge paradigm specifically carries a documented low-level novelty/familiarity confound (Rivera/Wakeley/Langer 1999; Cashon & Cohen 2000), and (b) the mapping from looking-time surprise to a substrate-level buffer is conceptual, not mechanistic.
failure_signatures: The drawbridge version of VOE has a known low-level confound: infants may simply prefer the larger/more-novel 180-degree rotation independent of any box representation (Rivera, Wakeley & Langer 1999). The permanence inference rests on the full VOE literature, not this paradigm alone.

Looking-time 'surprise' demonstrates that SOMETHING about the hidden object is represented; it does not specify whether the representation is a token-instance object-file, a spatial expectation, or a physical-event prediction. It cannot by itself adjudicate the token-vs-type question MECH-045 must answer.

A representation sufficient to drive differential looking is not necessarily sufficient to drive search/retrieval -- the competence (representation) / performance (action) gap (see Diamond 1985 entry) means MECH-045's buffer must be specified at the level it is consumed.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct, clean evidence that infants represent a partly-hidden object as a single connected entity -- a token-level unity inference that bridges occlusion. This is the perceptual-completion sibling of full-occlusion permanence and grounds MECH-045's persistence buffer at the unit level. Confidence 0.7 because the binding CUE the paper isolates (common motion of the visible parts) is precisely the cue REE's anchor-keyed ghost bank does NOT use -- so the paper supports the capability while exposing a mechanism mismatch in REE's current implementation.
failure_signatures: Unity was perceived from COMMON MOTION of the visible surfaces; with static, homogeneous, aligned, simple-shaped edges infants did NOT perceive a connected object. REE's persistence stores key on a spatial anchor (ghost bank) or a static type tag (SD-049), neither of which is the motion-based amodal-completion cue the infant uses.

The study tests completion of a CURRENTLY partly-visible object, not full occlusion across time -- it is the spatial-gap analog of permanence, one inferential step short of the temporal-gap (fully-hidden) case Baillargeon tests.

Common-motion binding is a perceptual-input grouping operation; it does not by itself establish a stored token that survives the object becoming fully invisible. MECH-045 must add the temporal-persistence step that this paradigm stops short of.

entries.confidence_rationale: The foundational multiple-object-tracking demonstration: observers track ~4-5 target items among identical moving distractors, which Pylyshyn explains with FINST visual indexes -- a small set of pre-conceptual pointers that INDIVIDUATE and stick to objects across motion without encoding their features or locations. This grounds two ARC-006 properties at once: entities are SPARSE (a hard ~4-5 index limit) and PERSISTENT/bindable (the index sticks to the same token through motion). It also grounds the token-instance individuation MECH-045 needs. Held mid-band because the items are featureless identical dots (it isolates individuation/tracking but says nothing about feature BINDING per se), the capacity limit is debated, and it is human psychophysics.
failure_signatures: The tracked items are identical featureless dots, so the paradigm isolates pure INDIVIDUATION+tracking and is silent on feature binding -- it cannot ground ARC-006's bindable-feature-bundle clause, only its sparse-persistent-token clause.

The ~4-5 index capacity is a strong, debated empirical limit; a REE that hard-codes a small fixed slot count would inherit a specific psychophysical number whose generality (and dependence on speed/spacing) is contested.

FINST indexes are pre-conceptual location-trackers that explicitly do NOT carry identity/feature content; treating them as full object files over-reads the construct -- indexing is necessary for, but distinct from, the object-file buffer.

entries.confidence_rationale: The foundational empirical demonstration of the object file: a temporary, token-instance episodic buffer that links successive states of THE SAME object across time and motion. The object-specific preview benefit (faster naming when prime and target are bound to one continuing object) is exactly the minimal across-time entity-persistence buffer MECH-045 posits. Robust (7 experiments, 203 subjects, ~2148 citations) and the mapping to MECH-045 is near-literal -- 'object file' is the term of art MECH-045 borrows. Held below 0.9 because the paradigm is visual psychophysics in humans, whereas MECH-045 must instantiate the buffer in a latent-stack agent, and the object file here is purely token-instance whereas REE's live z_object lineage is type-level (the gap the pull was commissioned to expose).
failure_signatures: The object file is strictly TOKEN-instance (this object, this episode); it provides no account of type/category abstraction, which is where REE's live z_resource/z_object lineage actually operates -- so this paper grounds the buffer REE does NOT yet have, not the one it has.

Object-specific benefit is fragile: it requires perceived spatiotemporal continuity of a single object; when continuity cues are removed the benefit collapses, so a REE object-file buffer cannot be a free-floating key-value store -- persistence must be gated on a continuity computation REE does not currently run.

Demonstrated for a single reviewed object across a brief preview-target interval; it does not establish persistence across long occlusions or many concurrent objects (Pylyshyn/Scholl entries cover capacity and occlusion).

entries.confidence_rationale: The most pointed paper in the pull for the memo's exact gap: it shows object tracking SURVIVES complete occlusion when the disappearance/reappearance carries accretion-deletion cues at an occluding contour, but BREAKS when items vanish in non-occlusion ways (imploding/exploding). This is direct evidence that token persistence is computed from spatiotemporal continuity cues, not from continuous visibility -- exactly the 'this object tracked through occlusion' capability MECH-045's object-file buffer must provide and REE's type-tag store cannot. Held at 0.77 (not higher) because it is human psychophysics and because it specifies WHICH cues license persistence rather than a mechanism REE can directly implement.
failure_signatures: Persistence is conditional on specific cues: tracking survives occlusion ONLY with accretion/deletion along a fixed occluding contour and breaks under implosion/explosion -- a REE object-file buffer that persists tokens unconditionally (e.g. on any temporary absence) would over-generalise beyond what the visual system actually does.
It diagnoses the CUES that signal enduring objecthood, not the buffer mechanism; REE still has to choose a representation that consumes continuity cues, which this paper does not supply.
Human visual psychophysics with abstract moving items; transfer to a latent-stack foraging agent whose 'occlusion' is a different sensory regime is non-trivial.

entries.confidence_rationale: The load-bearing entry for the memo's central token-vs-type distinction. Five experiments (158 infants) show 10-month-olds trace numerical identity through occlusion using SPATIOTEMPORAL information (token/instance) but do NOT use property/kind information (type) to individuate -- the kind-based route emerges later (~12 months). Directly grounds the claim that true permanence is token-instance tracking, distinct from type identity. Marked 'mixed' because it simultaneously SUPPORTS the token-permanence pillar and WEAKENS the assumption that REE's type-level identity (SD-049) suffices for permanence -- REE has built the developmentally LATER, kind-based route and lacks the earlier spatiotemporal-token route permanence rests on.
failure_signatures: REE's live object identity (SD-015 z_resource + SD-049 type tag + SD-057 IncentiveTokenBank keyed by type) is PROPERTY/KIND-based -- the route Xu & Carey show develops LATER and is NOT what young infants use to track identity through occlusion. REE has the inverse developmental order: it implements type-based identity but lacks the spatiotemporal token-tracking that permanence actually requires.

Spatiotemporal individuation requires representing distinct locations/trajectories of a token across an occluding gap (e.g. an object that goes behind a screen and a second that comes out the other side => two objects). REE's stores encode neither a per-token trajectory nor a 'how many distinct objects' count -- the ghost bank keys by anchor, the incentive bank by type; neither performs numerical individuation.

The dissociation means a fourth per-object store built for permanence on the existing TYPE key would reproduce REE's gap rather than close it: the unit for permanence must be a spatiotemporally-tracked token, not a category.

entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical statement of the core-knowledge object principles (cohesion, continuity, contact). The CONTINUITY principle -- an object traces exactly one connected path through space and time -- IS the formal content of permanence: an object cannot wink out and reappear, so it must be represented as continuing through occlusion. High mapping fidelity to ARC-006's 'persistent' clause and to the permanence pillar's spatiotemporal-continuity criterion. Confidence below 0.8 because it is a theoretical synthesis (the empirical weight lives in the studies it reviews) and because the principles describe perceptual INPUT analysis, not a memory buffer.
failure_signatures: The principles characterise how infants SEGMENT and INDIVIDUATE objects from surface/motion arrays at perception time; they are not a theory of how an out-of-view object is STORED. ARC-006/MECH-045 must add the buffer that continuity implies but the principles do not themselves specify.

Cohesion (a single bounded contour moving as a connected whole) maps to the object-file UNIT, but REE's z_world is engineered pre-split (MECH-278 'architectural shortcut past stage 2'), so REE currently bypasses the very segmentation the cohesion principle describes.

The principles are deliberately KIND-neutral -- they define 'bounded physical object' without sortal/category content. This is the right level for a token object-file, but it is orthogonal to REE's SD-049 TYPE-tag identity; the two address different questions and should not be conflated.

entries.confidence_rationale: Reframes Piaget's A-not-B error as a recall-plus-inhibition (prefrontal) limit on USING a representation to guide action, not a failure of the object representation itself. The hide-to-reach delay tolerated before the error grows ~2 s/month (7.5 -> 12 months); dorsolateral-PFC lesions in monkeys reproduce the error. Grounds the competence/performance -- equivalently the STORE/READOUT -- dissociation that the SD-039/MECH-292/293 ghost-goal bank embodies: a persistent store can be intact while the action-readout perseverates. Confidence 0.71: strong, longitudinally precise, lesion-corroborated, but the substrate (PFC working memory/inhibition) is not REE's (hippocampal anchored value store), so the mapping is functional-analogical.
failure_signatures: The A-not-B error is a PERSEVERATIVE READOUT failure (inability to inhibit the prepotent reach to the previously rewarded location A) under a memory delay -- the object representation can be intact while action goes to the wrong place. A permanence store that is correct can still drive wrong behaviour if its readout/selection layer perseverates.

Diamond's mechanism is prefrontal working memory + response inhibition; REE's ghost-goal bank is a hippocampal-anchor value store queried by wanting-rank. The store/readout split maps functionally but the substrate does not, so REE's analog of the A-not-B failure would live in the query/selection layer, not in PFC.

The error is delay-dependent and matures continuously; a static persistence buffer with no delay-sensitive readout would not reproduce the developmental signature, suggesting permanence in REE needs a graded, delay/decay-sensitive retrieval stage, not just a store.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational and many-times-replicated demonstration that a hidden object is REPRESENTED as continuing to exist long before Piaget's manual-search criterion. Directly grounds the existence of a persistence buffer (MECH-045): permanence is a representational competence dissociable from action. Confidence held at 0.7 rather than higher because (a) the drawbridge paradigm specifically carries a documented low-level novelty/familiarity confound (Rivera/Wakeley/Langer 1999; Cashon & Cohen 2000), and (b) the mapping from looking-time surprise to a substrate-level buffer is conceptual, not mechanistic.
failure_signatures: The drawbridge version of VOE has a known low-level confound: infants may simply prefer the larger/more-novel 180-degree rotation independent of any box representation (Rivera, Wakeley & Langer 1999). The permanence inference rests on the full VOE literature, not this paradigm alone.

Looking-time 'surprise' demonstrates that SOMETHING about the hidden object is represented; it does not specify whether the representation is a token-instance object-file, a spatial expectation, or a physical-event prediction. It cannot by itself adjudicate the token-vs-type question MECH-045 must answer.

A representation sufficient to drive differential looking is not necessarily sufficient to drive search/retrieval -- the competence (representation) / performance (action) gap (see Diamond 1985 entry) means MECH-045's buffer must be specified at the level it is consumed.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct, clean evidence that infants represent a partly-hidden object as a single connected entity -- a token-level unity inference that bridges occlusion. This is the perceptual-completion sibling of full-occlusion permanence and grounds MECH-045's persistence buffer at the unit level. Confidence 0.7 because the binding CUE the paper isolates (common motion of the visible parts) is precisely the cue REE's anchor-keyed ghost bank does NOT use -- so the paper supports the capability while exposing a mechanism mismatch in REE's current implementation.
failure_signatures: Unity was perceived from COMMON MOTION of the visible surfaces; with static, homogeneous, aligned, simple-shaped edges infants did NOT perceive a connected object. REE's persistence stores key on a spatial anchor (ghost bank) or a static type tag (SD-049), neither of which is the motion-based amodal-completion cue the infant uses.

The study tests completion of a CURRENTLY partly-visible object, not full occlusion across time -- it is the spatial-gap analog of permanence, one inferential step short of the temporal-gap (fully-hidden) case Baillargeon tests.

Common-motion binding is a perceptual-input grouping operation; it does not by itself establish a stored token that survives the object becoming fully invisible. MECH-045 must add the temporal-persistence step that this paradigm stops short of.

Well-cited review reframing mental fatigue as an adaptive cost/benefit recalibration -- fatigue signals that the energetical cost of continued effort now outweighs expected reward, motivating disengagement toward more rewarding alternatives, rather than reflecting depleted resources or aversive mood. Grounds fatigue's antecedent (accumulated effort + opportunity cost) and its disengagement consumer (ARC-078) as DISTINCT from suffering's aversive-uncontrollable antecedent. Source quality good (review, not primary data); mapping is conceptual.
failure_signatures: Treating fatigue as pure resource depletion ('out of fuel') rather than a cost/benefit signal predicts fatigue should be insensitive to incentive -- contradicted; fatigue-driven disengagement is reversible by raising reward, which is the signature of a value-recalibration, not an empty tank.

If fatigue were a negative-valence aversive signal (suffering-like), it would not preferentially redirect behaviour toward MORE rewarding alternatives; the data frame it as an opportunity-cost reallocation.

entries.confidence_rationale: Neurocognitive framework casting fatigue as a MOTIVATIONAL signal (effort/opportunity-cost recalibration in dACC/anterior insula/lateral PFC) rather than energy depletion, and distinguishing transient STATE fatigue (waxes/wanes with cognitive or motor exertion) from persistent TRAIT fatigue/chronic exhaustion -- the state/trait split that separates a recoverable homeostatic stop from clinical aversive-mood conditions. Directly supports fatigue's distinctness from suffering/depression and its SD-012 placement. Review-level evidence; mapping conceptual.
failure_signatures: Modelling fatigue as energy depletion mispredicts its recovery profile and its incentive-sensitivity; the framework requires fatigue to act as a value/cost signal feeding effort-based decision systems.

Collapsing transient state-fatigue into trait/clinical exhaustion (or into anhedonia/depression) erases the recoverable-stop-recover dynamic that distinguishes the homeostatic signal from suffering-driven withdrawal.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly supplies the SMALLEST COMPUTATIONAL FORM of a fatigue/stop-recover signal: a scalar 'cost evidence' that accumulates during effort and dissipates during rest, with an UPPER bound triggering stop and a LOWER bound triggering resume -- a hysteretic two-bound accumulator. fMRI+MEG localise it to posterior insula / ventromedial thalamus (proprioceptive-interoceptive, not aversive-mood circuitry). High mapping_fidelity to the proposed REE primitive because the model IS the proposed primitive; transfer_risk low because it is already an abstract control-theoretic accumulator, not a species-specific circuit.
failure_signatures: If REE registered fatigue as a single-threshold flag rather than a two-bound hysteretic accumulator, it would lose the 'recover' half (no lower bound to gate re-engagement) and could chatter at the stop threshold -- the model shows stop AND resume are distinct bound-crossings.
Incentive does not abolish the accumulator; it rescales slopes/bounds (lets the agent 'work closer to exhaustion'). A model where high reward simply switches fatigue off would contradict the data.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational, heavily replicated mechanistic review establishing that the learned-helplessness phenotype is gated by stressor UNCONTROLLABILITY and instantiated by dorsal-raphe 5-HT sensitization + CRF, with vmPFC controllability-detection as the inhibitory gate. Directly anchors the SUFFERING pole of the differentiation: the stop/withdrawal here is an aversive, controllability-contingent escape-failure -- categorically not an effort/energy accumulator. High source_quality; mapping is to the ANTECEDENT and SUBSTRATE contrast rather than to a numeric REE metric, so mapping_fidelity is strong-but-conceptual.
failure_signatures: If a fatigue/stop-recover signal were registered on the SD-011 suffering side, it would inherit controllability-gating and DRN/CRF aversive semantics that the biology assigns ONLY to uncontrollable aversive stress -- mis-attributing an energy-budget stop to a harm/escape-failure mechanism.

Helplessness-driven withdrawal does NOT remit with rest (it requires controllability experience or pharmacological reversal); any model that lets rest dissipate a suffering-side stop signal contradicts this literature.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical homeostatic-accumulator model: Process S rises monotonically as a function of prior wakefulness and falls during sleep, indexed by EEG slow-wave activity and linked to adenosine accumulation -- a homeostatic deficit variable whose antecedent is TIME-ON-TASK / metabolic expenditure, explicitly independent of aversive experience or controllability. Grounds the slow, sleep-pressure variant of fatigue/stop-recover on the SD-012 homeostatic side and supplies the recovery dynamic that suffering-withdrawal lacks. Foundational model; mapping is to the antecedent/dynamics, not a REE metric.
failure_signatures: Any account that lets a suffering/SD-011 stop signal recover by 'sleeping it off' borrows Process S dynamics it does not have: Process S recovery is specific to the homeostatic accumulator, not to aversive-uncontrollable stress.

Modelling fatigue with no recovery integrator (stop-only) omits the defining feature of Process S -- the exponential decline during sleep that resets the accumulator; fatigue without a recover phase is mis-specified.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct pharmacological dissociation (intra-NAc SCH23390 + AP5, separate vs co-injected, staged across acquisition/consolidation/expression) showing relief-learning acquisition requires coincident D1 + NMDA activation in the nucleus accumbens -- the same value-coding reward-circuit coincidence that mediates reward learning. Strongly supports MECH-302's core assertion that the relief-completion event reuses goal-achievement / reward-circuit machinery. Source quality high (clean within-subject pharmacology, locomotor control rules out perceptual confound). Mapping fidelity high for the 'reuses reward machinery' half of MECH-302; moderate for the downstream tag-and-release pipeline (MECH-057a/091/094), which this paper does not directly test. Transfer risk low-moderate (rat associative paradigm to REE suffering-derivative comparator).
failure_signatures: If REE modelled relief-completion as a wholly separate circuit from reward/goal-achievement, this finding would weaken that design: relief learning shares the NAc D1+NMDA coincidence mechanism with reward learning.

The D1+NMDA requirement is acquisition-specific (co-injection blocked acquisition but not consolidation or expression) -- an REE relief mechanism that gates expression on the same coincidence would be over-specified relative to the biology.

entries.confidence_rationale: Activity-dependent ensemble mapping shows the prelimbic mPFC codes context-danger associations while differential conditioning recruits additional PL+IL ensembles tied to inhibition of generalized fear -- i.e. learned context-safety is an active prefrontal representation, not mere absence of threat. Directly supports MECH-303's prefrontal substrate for a contextual passive safety store (IL expression gating; cortical contextual representation). Source quality good (ensemble-level mapping, behavioural discrimination). Mapping fidelity moderate-high: Corches evidences the prefrontal/contextual safety substrate but does not isolate the slow diffuse contextual-exposure update rule MECH-303 specifies, nor the vHipp-PL store. Transfer risk moderate (rodent differential fear conditioning to REE context-safety representation).
failure_signatures: PL codes context-DANGER and IL/PL code inhibition of GENERALIZED fear -- if REE collapsed safety into a single 'low-harm' scalar, it would miss that danger-monitoring and safety-discrimination are separable prefrontal ensembles.

Safety here is built by differential conditioning (discriminating a safe-but-similar cue from a dangerous one), not by passive non-occurrence alone -- a pure passive-exposure update rule (MECH-303 as written) may under-specify the discrimination demand this paper documents.

entries.confidence_rationale: Multi-method causal circuit dissection (viral tracing, activity mapping, fiber photometry, chemogenetics, closed-loop optogenetics) shows nucleus reuniens (NRe) inputs to basolateral amygdala (BLA) register and transmit safety signals that drive remote fear extinction: NRe-to-BLA activity rises just before freezing cessation, inhibition impairs and activation facilitates extinction. Strong support for an ACTIVE, transmitted safety-prediction signal (MECH-304's conditioned-inhibition / safety-transmission role) as a distinct circuit from threat and from relief-reward substrate. Source quality very high (causal, bidirectional, cross-validated with human imaging cited in paper). Mapping fidelity moderate: MECH-304 names a cortico-striatal encoding + IL-to-CeA expression substrate, whereas Silva adds a midline-THALAMIC (reuniens) node to BLA -- supports the active-safety-transmission premise but extends the named anatomy. Transfer risk low-moderate.
failure_signatures: Safety transmission here is THALAMO-amygdalar (reuniens->BLA), a node not currently in MECH-303/304's stated substrate (prefrontal-hippocampal / cortico-striatal + IL-CeA) -- the REE safety substrate as written may be anatomically incomplete (missing a thalamic relay).
The NRe-to-BLA safety signal is specific to REMOTE (30-day) but not recent (1-day) fear extinction -- a time-since-encoding dependence that no current REE safety mechanism represents.

If REE treated safety as identical to relief, this would weaken it: the safety-transmission circuit (reuniens->BLA, suppressing fear) is anatomically separate from the relief-completion reward circuit (NAc/VTA).

entries.confidence_rationale: Supplies the DETECTION MECHANISM for the V3 proxy and ties it to REE's existing substrate. The comparator model holds that the sense of agency arises when (and only when) the comparator detects that predicted sensory feedback matches actual feedback; mismatch yields loss/attribution-elsewhere of agency. REE already instantiates exactly this form in SD-029 (residual = observed - predicted action outcome). A blocked-agency signal is the sustained/integrated comparator MISMATCH on the action-outcome channel attributed to external constraint. The paper genuinely supports SD-029's comparator role, so SD-029 is co-tagged. Confidence held at 0.66: it is a theoretical/philosophy paper defending the comparator account (vs Synofzik's multifactorial weighting), focused on schizophrenic alien-control rather than blocked action per se, so the mapping is by mechanism-analogy.
failure_signatures: The comparator yields a binary-ish agency/no-agency readout; a blocked-agency AFFECT signal additionally requires (a) attributing the mismatch to an EXTERNAL constraint rather than own motor error, and (b) gating on RETAINED goal/capacity -- a bare comparator mismatch is necessary but not sufficient, so REE must add the attribution + capacity gate on top of SD-029.

Synofzik et al.'s multifactorial-weighting critique (that actual sensory consequences are not always needed for the sense of agency) is a live alternative; if agency in REE is sometimes inferred from intention/context rather than realised-outcome comparison, a pure comparator-mismatch detector would miss or misfire on those cases.

entries.confidence_rationale: The single strongest anchor for the V3-tractable core of the candidate stream. The Amsel-lineage frustrative-non-reward (FNR) construct is defined by the NEGATIVE DISPARITY BETWEEN OBTAINED AND EXPECTED reward -- an expectation/agency-violation antecedent, NOT noxious input -- and it carries 'aversive motivational properties' with a primary (unconditioned) component, and drives irritability/anger/aggression. That is precisely the smallest computational form the verdict proposes: a blocked-expected-outcome signal distinct from harm, with retained motivation. High source_quality (J Neurosci integrative review); mapping_fidelity high because FNR's antecedent maps almost one-to-one onto REE's z_goal/wanting-vs-realised-outcome discrepancy; transfer_risk moderate (rodent successive-negative-contrast paradigms -> REE).
failure_signatures: FNR is generated with ZERO noxious input -- a merely-omitted or down-shifted reward -- so any REE model that requires z_harm_s/z_harm_un activation to produce a blocked-agency signal contradicts the construct; the antecedent is expectation-violation, not nociception.

FNR is dissociable from the suffering/helplessness pole: it engages reward-circuit deactivation (OFC/ventral striatum/PCC) plus midcingulo-insular/amygdala/PAG ACTIVATION with retained reward-seeking (Type-2 dopamine neurons sustain seeking after non-reward) -- a model that routes blocked-expected-reward straight into withdrawal/shutdown mis-assigns the energised assert pole.

entries.confidence_rationale: Anchors the V4-SOCIAL scope boundary and supplies the verdict's cleanest dissociation. Psychological reactance is 'an unpleasant motivational arousal that emerges when people experience a threat to or loss of their free behaviors,' driving restoration of the threatened freedom; it carries anger/hostility, and crucially has 'energizing and behavior-directing properties, distinguishing reactance from learned helplessness by maintaining the individual's sense of capacity to alter their situation.' That single sentence is the controllability-axis dissociation the verdict rests on: blocked-agency-with-capacity-retained (reactance/assert) is the OPPOSITE pole to suffering/helplessness (withdraw). Human social-psychology review, explicitly V4 (needs an other-agent/source of restriction), so transfer_risk is high and confidence is held at 0.62.
failure_signatures: Reactance is explicitly NOT learned helplessness: it preserves the sense of capacity to alter the situation and energizes freedom-restoration. A REE model that routes autonomy-threat / blocked-agency into the suffering accumulator (capacity-collapse, withdraw) inverts the phenomenon.

Reactance requires a threatened FREEDOM and (typically) an agent/source imposing the restriction; the four restoration strategies (direct, by-implication, aggression-at-source, subjective reappraisal) are SOCIAL/other-agent consumers -- importing them into a single-agent V3 substrate that has no model of a coercing other would be premature (V4-scope).

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical articulation of the Pankseppian seven-system framework, in which RAGE/Anger is one of the genetically-conserved primary-process emotional systems, neuroanatomically and functionally dissociable from FEAR and PANIC/GRIEF. This is the biology-before-formal-definitions anchor for the verdict's core claim: at the most basic mammalian level the brain treats anger as its OWN command system with its own subcortical circuit (medial amygdala -> medial hypothalamus -> dorsal PAG, hierarchically organised), not a flavour of nociception or fear. Source is a high-quality review but secondary/theory-laden (ESB-evoked affect framework), and the mapping is to the DISTINCTNESS premise rather than to a numeric REE metric -- hence confidence held below 0.8.
failure_signatures: If REE collapses anger/blocked-agency into the harm register (SD-011) it contradicts the primary-process dissociation: RAGE is abolished by lesions at a DIFFERENT hierarchical locus (hypothalamus/PAG for attack) than the nociceptive medial pathway, and is evolutionarily a separate command system -- merging them repeats the SD-010->SD-011 philosophy-right/mechanism-wrong error.

RAGE (affective attack) is explicitly dissociated from SEEKING-driven 'quiet-bite' predatory behaviour; a model that conflates appetitive/instrumental pursuit with reactive anger would mis-assign the affect.

entries.confidence_rationale: Anchors the CONSUMER and REGULATION side of the candidate stream. Reactive aggression is 'a response to social threat, provocation, or frustration, strongly associated with anger,' instantiated by the amygdala-hypothalamus-PAG acute-threat circuit and INHIBITED by prefrontal control (vmPFC/vlPFC/dlPFC); it is categorically distinct from proactive/instrumental aggression (planned, goal-directed, low-arousal). That maps onto the verdict's consumer set: the blocked-agency signal drives an assert/escalate response that must be gated by a regulatory channel (REE commitment-threshold / decommit, MECH-342), and the reactive-vs-proactive split warns REE not to conflate frustration-driven assertion with planned goal pursuit. Human clinical/review source, good quality; mapping is to the consumer architecture, hence 0.74.
failure_signatures: Reactive aggression (frustration/threat-triggered, high-arousal, anger) is doubly dissociated from proactive/instrumental aggression (planned, low-arousal, goal-directed); a REE model that routes a blocked-agency signal through the ordinary goal-pursuit/E3 trajectory machinery without a distinct high-arousal assert channel would mis-model the reactive response.

Reactive aggression is normally held in check by prefrontal inhibition (reduced vmPFC volume -> more physical aggression); a blocked-agency consumer with no regulatory/decommit gate would produce unchecked escalation -- the pathological (intermittent-explosive) phenotype, not adaptive assertion.

entries.confidence_rationale: Supplies the DETECTION MECHANISM for the V3 proxy and ties it to REE's existing substrate. The comparator model holds that the sense of agency arises when (and only when) the comparator detects that predicted sensory feedback matches actual feedback; mismatch yields loss/attribution-elsewhere of agency. REE already instantiates exactly this form in SD-029 (residual = observed - predicted action outcome). A blocked-agency signal is the sustained/integrated comparator MISMATCH on the action-outcome channel attributed to external constraint. The paper genuinely supports SD-029's comparator role, so SD-029 is co-tagged. Confidence held at 0.66: it is a theoretical/philosophy paper defending the comparator account (vs Synofzik's multifactorial weighting), focused on schizophrenic alien-control rather than blocked action per se, so the mapping is by mechanism-analogy.
failure_signatures: The comparator yields a binary-ish agency/no-agency readout; a blocked-agency AFFECT signal additionally requires (a) attributing the mismatch to an EXTERNAL constraint rather than own motor error, and (b) gating on RETAINED goal/capacity -- a bare comparator mismatch is necessary but not sufficient, so REE must add the attribution + capacity gate on top of SD-029.

Synofzik et al.'s multifactorial-weighting critique (that actual sensory consequences are not always needed for the sense of agency) is a live alternative; if agency in REE is sometimes inferred from intention/context rather than realised-outcome comparison, a pure comparator-mismatch detector would miss or misfire on those cases.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical statement of the neurovisceral-integration / central-autonomic-network (CAN) framework: a prefrontal-driven reciprocal-inhibitory cortico-subcortical circuit actively maintains parasympathetic tone and is withdrawn (releasing sympathetic dominance) when the prefrontal cortex goes offline. Establishes that the recovery/restraint driver is an ENDOGENOUS CENTRAL system, not a stimulus or a conspecific -- the key premise for an offset-triggered, non-social, non-prediction recovery mechanism. It is a conceptual review (not a direct test of offset-triggered rebound), so confidence is moderate.
failure_signatures: When the prefrontal cortex is taken offline, parasympathetic inhibitory action is withdrawn and sympathetic dominance is released -- a REE rebound mechanism that depends on a prefrontal-analog driver would FAIL exactly when that analog is suppressed (e.g. under high load / committed states), so it cannot be assumed always-on.

Sustained low parasympathetic tone (low HRV) is framed as pathogenic -- a chronically failing recovery process is the disease signature, implying the REE analog must be able to fail (perseverative non-recovery) as a modelled failure mode, not just succeed.

entries.confidence_rationale: Quantifies parasympathetic reactivation as a process with its own KINETICS (heart-rate recovery + 30-s windowed rMSSD trajectories) whose RATE is set by resting vagal tone -- direct support for modelling recovery as a tunable rate parameter (the smallest-form question). Discounted because the stressor is maximal exercise, not an aversive/psychological stressor, so the transfer to a suffering-recovery process is by analogy on the autonomic-recovery-rate construct only.
failure_signatures: Parasympathetic reactivation rate depended on the exercise modality AND on resting vagal activity -- recovery rate is not a fixed constant but a context- and baseline-conditioned parameter, so a single hard-coded REE recovery_rate would mis-model agents in different states.

Reactivation was slower when resting vagal tone was lower -- a depleted baseline predicts impaired recovery, the same coupling Thayer/Mezzacappa report; a REE rebound that ignored current state would over-recover a depleted agent.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly relevant double-edged anchor: it (i) confirms vagal rebound (HRV recovery) as a discrete, separately-modelled recovery axis via piecewise growth-curve modelling of reactivity vs recovery slopes, AND (ii) shows emotional support modulates the rebound. For the candidate (endogenous, NON-social rebound) this is 'mixed': it validates the shared recovery variable and its dissociability from reactivity, but its experimental lever is social support -- which is the MECH-355 soothing side, not the endogenous trigger. That is exactly why it supports the ARCHITECTURE (sibling claims sharing one recovery target via distinct triggers) while not isolating the endogenous trigger.
failure_signatures: Greater vagal rebound was evident ONLY for women reporting high emotional support -- demonstrating that a social input can be the proximate modulator of rebound, so an endogenous-rebound experiment must hold social inputs fixed/absent to isolate the offset-triggered component (confound between MECH-355 and the sibling if not controlled).

Higher life stress predicted both greater reactivity AND faster vagal rebound (adaptation to anticipated high-stress environments) -- rebound magnitude is history-dependent, so a fixed-rate REE rebound would mis-model chronically-stressed agents.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct, canonical empirical demonstration that recovery from an acute stressor is an ACTIVE parasympathetic process (a sharp vagal surge in the first minute of recovery) occurring DESPITE residual sympathetic activation -- i.e. recovery is not merely the passive decay of the stress signal. This is exactly the dissociation the candidate claim turns on. Human psychophysiology, two experiments, replicated rebound across tasks; mapping_fidelity high for 'active offset-triggered recovery distinct from passive decay'; transfer risk is the usual physiology->latent-substrate analogy.
failure_signatures: Vagal rebound was REDUCED in men (Exp 1) and in individuals with a family history of cardiovascular disease (Exp 2) -- the rebound is a dissociable individual-difference axis, not an automatic consequence of stressor offset; a REE rebound mechanism must therefore be a gated/parameterised process, not a fixed reflex.
Rebound was tied to baroreflex-sensitivity resetting at stress onset AND offset, implying the recovery process is coupled to a homeostatic set-point reset rather than to a generic decay timer.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-resolution human fMRI dissociating a strong pattern-separation bias localized to CA3/dentate gyrus from a pattern-completion bias in CA1/subiculum/entorhinal/parahippocampal cortex. Strong, human, anatomically specific evidence that the DG performs the separation operation REE plans as MECH-147. Held below 0.85 because fMRI infers the computation from a repetition-suppression signature rather than recording sparse codes directly, and the candidate gate is about the POLICY over separation, of which DG separation is only the separate-pole effector.
failure_signatures: fMRI shows a separation-vs-completion bias by region but does not record the sparse orthogonalized codes directly; the DG sparse-encoding mechanism is inferred, not observed at single-trace resolution.
Demonstrates the separation EFFECTOR (DG) but not a control policy deciding WHEN to separate vs integrate -- supports MECH-147 (substrate) more than the allocation-gate policy.

Pattern completion in CA1/EC means the same circuit that separates also actively re-integrates; a REE design that builds separation without the complementary completion/integration pole would mis-model the system.

entries.confidence_rationale: Causal Nature study: genetically increasing adult dentate neurogenesis is sufficient to improve behavioural discrimination of similar contexts, and the literature frames impaired separation as driving OVERGENERALIZATION (linking distinct experiences that should stay distinct). This biologically motivates the intake's reality-coherence / false-linking-risk cost: insufficient separation has a real, measurable behavioural cost. Held at 0.70 because the readout is fear-context discrimination, an indirect proxy for the 'false linking' cost, and the cost is demonstrated as a failure of the separation EFFECTOR rather than as a control-plane cost term.
failure_signatures: The cost of failed separation is shown as poor contextual fear DISCRIMINATION (overgeneralization), an indirect proxy for the intake's 'inappropriate linking of unrelated traces' rather than a direct demonstration of false association.

Improvement comes from boosting a substrate (neurogenesis-driven DG separation), evidencing the cost of a weak EFFECTOR -- it does not show a control plane explicitly PRICING false-linking risk at allocation time, which is the novel REE lever.

Over-separation costs (failure to generalize) are not measured here, so the paper supports only one of the two failure poles the intake brackets; a one-sided cost term would bias the gate toward separation.

entries.confidence_rationale: Causal circuit study (Nature Neuroscience) with optogenetic/chemogenetic manipulation establishing that a higher-order cortical region (vmPFC) actively controls whether hippocampal traces are linked or kept separate, gated by contextual similarity and temporal distance. Strong source quality and direct support for the EXISTENCE of a top-down memory-allocation gate. Confidence held below 0.8 because the paper demonstrates the gate and its controller but does NOT specify a decision ALGORITHM (the genuinely novel REE lever), and the mapping from a mouse contextual-fear circuit to a REE control-plane write policy carries real transfer risk.
failure_signatures: The paper shows top-down CONTROL of linking-vs-separation but does not formalize a decision rule with explicit weighted inputs; it cannot adjudicate which gating variables REE should use beyond contextual similarity and temporal distance.

Psychiatric framing (schizophrenia, bipolar false association) is explicitly speculative translation from mouse circuit work -- no human or clinical data; must not be cited as evidence for any reality-coherence cost in humans.

Within-hours experiences merge regardless of vmPFC activity (vmPFC silencing at ~5 h apart changed nothing), so the gate is NOT a universal write controller -- it is recruited selectively over a days timescale, bounding the scope of any REE analogue.

entries.confidence_rationale: Landmark Science paper showing that a pre-existing associative schema causally accelerates assimilation of new, schema-consistent traces (one-trial encoding that becomes hippocampus-independent within 48 h). Strong support that schema_fit is a real determinant of how a new trace is integrated. Held at 0.68 because the paper measures consolidation SPEED and hippocampal-independence, not the link-vs-separate allocation decision per se; the schema_fit -> integration-pressure mapping is an inference about a related but not identical operation.
failure_signatures: The paper measures schema-accelerated consolidation (rate of hippocampal disengagement), not the binary allocate-overlapping-vs-separate decision; equating fast assimilation with the gate's integrate output is an inference.
Schema benefit is shown for schema-CONSISTENT items; the paper does not characterize how schema mismatch triggers active separation, leaving the separate-pole of schema_fit under-specified.
Rodent spatial paired-associate task; the schema construct is a learned flavour-place associative structure, narrower than the general schema_fit variable the intake proposes.

entries.confidence_rationale: Nature paper with in-vivo miniscope imaging of CA1 ensembles plus causal excitability manipulation, directly demonstrating that TEMPORAL DISTANCE between two encoding episodes determines hippocampal ensemble overlap (linking within a day vs separation across a week). This is the most direct empirical grounding for temporal distance as a first-class gating variable. Held below 0.8 because it isolates the excitability/temporal-window mechanism (a bottom-up allocation rule) rather than the top-down PFC policy, and the mapping to a REE temporal-gap weight is by analogy.
failure_signatures: The temporal-window linking here is driven by intrinsic neuronal excitability dynamics, NOT by a top-down control decision -- so this paper supports temporal distance as a VARIABLE but is silent on whether a control plane should set its weight; over-reading it as evidence for the POLICY would be a category error.

Increased excitability and short-window linking are absent in aged animals, indicating the temporal-distance effect is itself substrate-conditional and not a fixed law -- a REE temporal_gap term would inherit that state-dependence.
The effect is a memory-linking (co-recall) bias, not a demonstration of harmful false association; mapping it to a reality-coherence cost requires the separate over-generalization literature.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational and field-defining review establishing the temporal-correlation (binding-by-synchrony) hypothesis with strong cat/primate gamma-synchrony data. Direction is mixed rather than supports because the hypothesis has been seriously contested since (Shadlen & Movshon 1999 critique; debate over whether synchrony codes or merely accompanies binding). It is strong evidence that dynamic, relational binding via temporal structure is a real candidate mechanism (ARC-006), weaker as proof that synchrony IS the binding code.
failure_signatures: Synchrony may be a by-product of recurrent connectivity rather than the binding code itself (Shadlen & Movshon 1999): a downstream reader needs a mechanism to actually exploit coincidence, or the correlation is epiphenomenal -- the same 'symbol without function' failure mode 641a found in REE's streams.

The hypothesis requires that bound features drive co-varying temporal structure; if a representation's features do not co-vary in time (REE's engineered pre-split z_world), there is no temporal correlation to read.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily-replicated framework from a leading lab (Neuron) for coherence as the substrate of selective neural communication; directly names the mechanism the V3-EXQ-641a autopsy cited as 'closest'. Confidence held below 0.8 because the mapping is to the CLASS (coherence-gated routing/binding) rather than to REE's specific hippocampal-relational-binding or theta-gamma-packaging instantiation, and because CTC describes inter-areal cortical communication, not the cross-stream latent coherence REE's selection rule reads.
failure_signatures: CTC asserts that communication is effective only when sending and receiving groups are coherent; a coherence read over streams that are NOT genuinely phase/feature-bound (the V3-EXQ-641a finding: world_states<->states carry the symbol but not the bound information) would register coherence that does not gate anything causally -- exactly the 'functionally redundant with E' result.
Coherence in CTC is a consequence of rhythmic excitability windows; if REE's streams have no analog of a shared excitability rhythm, a coherence term is decorative rather than mechanistic.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong, widely-reproduced existence proof that a token-instance object-centric representation (a set of exchangeable 'slots' that competitively bind to objects) is learnable end-to-end and is the natural ML realization of the object-file / generalised z_object that ARC-080 proposes. Held below 0.8 by transfer risk: slot attention is unsupervised object discovery on image/CNN features, not drive/goal-coupled binding over REE's engineered latent streams, and a single-frame slot set does not by itself give cross-time permanence.
failure_signatures: Slot attention without a temporal/recurrent extension (e.g. SAVi) gives object-centric grouping WITHIN a frame but no token-instance persistence ACROSS occlusion -- so it grounds the binding/identity half of ARC-080 but not Pillar 1 (permanence) on its own.

Slots bind by competition over reconstruction of perceptual input; REE's z_object is detached from reconstruction and coupled to drive/goal value -- the binding pressure that makes slots specialise may be absent if REE supplies no comparable reconstruction or contrastive objective.

entries.confidence_rationale: The foundational theoretical argument (correlation theory of brain function) for WHY binding needs a dynamic temporal tag at all: static feature-cell coding suffers a 'superposition catastrophe' when multiple objects are present, so a separate binding variable is required. Strong, canonical grounding for ARC-006's premise that entities are dynamically BINDABLE structures rather than fixed conjunction cells. Held at 0.68 because it is a theoretical/modeler's argument (not empirical) and the temporal-binding solution it argues for is contested.
failure_signatures: The superposition-catastrophe argument shows static conjunction coding is INSUFFICIENT, but it does not by itself prove temporal correlation is THE solution -- competing solutions (e.g. competitive slot allocation, attention) also avoid the catastrophe. So it motivates a binding variable without uniquely selecting synchrony.

A modeler's-perspective theoretical paper: it argues for what a binding mechanism must accomplish, not what the brain demonstrably does -- empirical adjudication is elsewhere (and contested, per Shadlen & Movshon 1999).

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong, reproduced ML existence proof that slots can be TRACKED across time -- each slot persists as the same object-token frame to frame, predicted forward by a transition model. This is the persistence half that vanilla slot-attention (Locatello 2020) lacks, and it maps onto REE's shape exactly: slots + a forward predictor = SAVi, and REE's E2 IS that predictor. Held at 0.71 by transfer risk: weakly-supervised (optical-flow target + first-frame conditioning cues), synthetic video, pixel-reconstruction-driven -- REE's z_object is value-coupled and reconstruction-free over engineered latents.
failure_signatures: SAVi tracking is bootstrapped by weak supervision (optical flow as the prediction target; first-frame object-location/coordinate conditioning cues). Remove that scaffold and unsupervised temporal binding degrades -- REE would need a comparable conditioning signal (e.g. drive/goal salience seeding a slot) or the slots may not specialise/persist.
Slot persistence is maintained while the object is visible-and-tracked; full through-occlusion permanence (ARC-080 Pillar 1) is only partially addressed and remains the harder problem.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily-cited Neuron synthesis of the theta-gamma multiplexing code with broad hippocampal + cortical empirical support. Directly grounds MECH-089 (theta-gamma nesting packages E1 for E3) at near-mechanism fidelity and supplies the formal capacity argument (~7+/-2 = gamma-cycles-per-theta) that grounds the 'both mechanisms multiply representational capacity' claim in the object-binding design fork. Held below 0.8 because the capacity-extension mapping to ARC-080 is at the class level and because phase-coded multiplexing presupposes a slot/item layer REE does not yet have.
failure_signatures: Theta-gamma multiplexing presupposes discrete items to assign to gamma subcycles; with no slot/token layer (REE's current state) there are no items to multiplex and the phase code has nothing to carry -- the capacity advantage is unrealizable until slots exist.
Capacity is bounded (~7+/-2 gamma cycles per theta cycle); the scheme extends, but does not remove, a hard simultaneous-item limit.
