entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical formal treatment decomposing the value of a policy into pragmatic (reward/harm) and epistemic (uncertainty-reducing) components, so that information-gathering actions are selected even when not immediately rewarding. Directly grounds MECH-388 (epistemic action pressure as a survival-relevant viability function) and the active-inference half of L5. Confidence capped by the formalism's strong assumptions (expected-free-energy minimisation) which REE does not adopt wholesale, and by it being theory rather than a single decisive empirical test.
failure_signatures: Anti-epistemic panic: an agent weighting only pragmatic value commits under threat without sampling -- the active-inference account predicts this as failure to value epistemic gain.

Epistemic freezing: the dual failure -- over-weighting epistemic value so the agent keeps gathering information and never commits -- is the over-exploration tail the pragmatic/epistemic balance must bound.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong model+data convergence: a single generative model reproduces grid/place/band/object-vector cell phenomenology AND generalises relational structure to novel environments, recovering empirically recorded representations. Directly grounds the L2 'cognitive map = general relational inference engine' premise behind ARC-091. Tempered by being a model whose biological claims are inferential rather than directly recorded.
failure_signatures: If the hippocampal-entorhinal map were purely spatial (not a reusable relational structure), REE's 'state-as-navigable relational package, inferable across structurally-equivalent situations' framing would lose its biological warrant; TEM shows structural knowledge factorises and transfers.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical Nature single-unit study with a direct, prospective result: pre-navigation hippocampal sequences are biased toward the upcoming path to a remembered goal. Maps strongly onto INF-7/ARC-091's claim that hippocampal output supplies prospective hypotheses (L1). Held below 0.85 only by the animal->REE-architecture transfer (rat spatial trajectory vs REE's general state-as-navigable latent).
failure_signatures: If hippocampal output were pure retrieval (past trajectories only), the inference-layer framing of replay-as-hypothesis-generator would be wrong; the result instead shows future-biased, goal-directed sequences.

entries.confidence_rationale: A strong, widely-replicated demonstration that an agent learning a compact LATENT world model and improving behaviour inside imagined (model-generated) trajectories can act effectively across 150+ domains from a single config, including long-horizon sparse-reward tasks. It is the ML analogue of REE's E2/hippocampal rollout-driven inference. Confidence held to 0.65: it is a preprint, an engineering result not a neuroscience finding, and it collapses harm/goal/residue into a single reward -- precisely the design REE rejects.
failure_signatures: A model-free reactive agent (no latent model, no imagined rollouts) fails the long-horizon/partial-information tasks Dreamer solves -- the computational analogue of 'cannot infer a route from partial evidence'.

Reward-collapse: Dreamer's single scalar reward is itself a cautionary signature for REE's insistence on separated streams; super-additive value collapse would mis-tag valence (MECH-126 valence mis-tagging).

entries.confidence_rationale: The foundational formal statement of the exact problem INF-7/ARC-091 names: under partial observability the policy must map a BELIEF over hidden states (not the raw observation) to action. High source-quality (the canonical POMDP reference) and a precise normative grounding for MECH-385. Confidence capped because REE explicitly does NOT adopt exact Bayesian belief updating, so the mapping is principle-level, with real divergence in mechanism.
failure_signatures: Failure-to-infer-hidden-danger / hidden-safety is exactly the cost of acting on observation rather than belief; the POMDP framework makes precise why an observation->action policy is provably suboptimal when state is hidden.
Context loss (MECH-126): a memoryless reactive policy that ignores observation/action history is the degenerate belief-state failure the formalism rules out.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct, striking single-unit evidence that the hippocampus holds MULTIPLE competing future hypotheses in rapid alternation (~8 Hz, one per theta cycle) rather than collapsing to a single committed path. This is close to a one-to-one biological instantiation of the belief-state-hypothesis-set + provenance principle (INV-078: completed trajectory is a hypothesis, not a commitment). Strong source and tight mapping; transfer to non-spatial REE state the main caveat.
failure_signatures: Premature-collapse failure mode: if the hippocampus committed to one representation rather than cycling, it would model the 'hypothesis collapse too early / one bad explanation dominates' pathology; the healthy system instead maintains alternatives sub-second.
Hypothesis-proliferation has the opposite signature -- cycling without ever committing -- which the inference layer must bound (top-k).

failure_signatures: Premature-collapse / anti-epistemic-panic: delusion-prone individuals gather less evidence before committing to a belief (fewer 'draws to decision') -- the over-hasty-inference signature INF-7 must track -- but the effect is small and confounded, so the failure mode is real yet not cleanly separable.
Cautions INF-7 against treating each register entry as a crisp dissociable mechanism: the clinical operationalisation of 'collapse too early' is noisier than the conceptual taxonomy implies.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct, striking single-unit evidence that the hippocampus holds MULTIPLE competing future hypotheses in rapid alternation (~8 Hz, one per theta cycle) rather than collapsing to a single committed path. This is close to a one-to-one biological instantiation of the belief-state-hypothesis-set + provenance principle (INV-078: completed trajectory is a hypothesis, not a commitment). Strong source and tight mapping; transfer to non-spatial REE state the main caveat.
failure_signatures: Premature-collapse failure mode: if the hippocampus committed to one representation rather than cycling, it would model the 'hypothesis collapse too early / one bad explanation dominates' pathology; the healthy system instead maintains alternatives sub-second.

entries.confidence_rationale: A high-quality consensus review tying psychotic symptoms to specific INFERENCE failures (aberrant precision-weighting of priors vs sensory prediction errors), which is exactly the bridge INF-7 needs: it grounds the inference-specific failure modes (overconfident-wrong-hypothesis, apophenia/aberrant salience, premature-collapse) AND lets them be mapped onto the existing MECH-126 state-abstraction taxonomy rather than invented anew. Confidence reflects strong source + tight conceptual mapping, tempered by it being a review of a contested computational account.
failure_signatures: Overconfident-wrong-hypothesis: over-weighted priors (or aberrantly precise prediction errors) drive false inferences held with high confidence -> delusions; maps to MECH-126 overmerge + uncertainty collapse.

Failure-to-infer correctly is here a precision-weighting pathology, not a missing-data pathology -- a distinction INF-7's register must preserve.

entries.confidence_rationale: The direct conceptual anchor for SD-030: optimal motor control relies on internal representations of the ACTUAL, DESIRED, and PREDICTED states of the limbs/world, and breakdowns in the predicted-vs-actual comparison produce specific agency pathologies (delusions of control, anarchic hand, phantom limbs). This is the forward-model-self architecture SD-030 instantiates as residual_self, and the E2-self-transition half of MECH-215. High mapping fidelity to the mechanism; held at 0.70 because it is a review/framework rather than a single decisive experiment and the human-clinical-to-REE transfer is at the functional-role level.
failure_signatures: When the predicted state of the motor system diverges from the actual state beyond the comparator's reach, the action is no longer attributed to the self -- the delusion-of-control / passivity signature, which SD-030 predicts as a self-stream residual exceeding the attribution threshold.

Awareness of action is built on motor-command (efference) streams, not only sensory feedback; phantom-limb movement illusions arise from the command stream alone -- so a self-model lacking an E2-self forward prediction (efference-copy analogue) cannot represent agency at all, the MECH-215 (2) prerequisite.

Only certain components of the internal representation reach awareness; impairing the predicted-state component selectively breaks agency while leaving movement intact -- a dissociation a single undifferentiated z_self could not produce.

entries.confidence_rationale: The fuller review behind the 2002 TICS framework, with the added value of a localisation claim: representations of the CURRENT and PREDICTED state of the motor system are in parietal cortex, while representations of INTENDED movements are in prefrontal/premotor cortex. This dissociates the predicted-state machinery (SD-030 comparator substrate) from the intention/goal machinery (E3-side), which is exactly the separation REE draws between the self-forward-model and the goal/viability evaluator. Held at 0.68 because the lesion synthesis is correlational and the parietal/prefrontal localisation is coarse relative to REE's z_self/z_goal split.
failure_signatures: Phantom-limb and anosognosic movement illusions are driven by motor-command streams in the ABSENCE of sensory confirmation -- a self-model that represents agency from intention alone, with no observed-self to compare against, will hallucinate successful action, the failure SD-030's residual is meant to catch.

Damage dissociates 'predicted current state' (parietal) from 'intended movement' (prefrontal/premotor); collapsing these into one representation -- as V3 does by running E2 on combined z_gamma with no z_self stream -- removes the distinction agency depends on.

Delusions of control arise when intention and the felt consequence of action are no longer properly linked: the comparator between intended and achieved self-state has failed, the MECH-215 (2) E2-self-transition prerequisite breaking.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical statement and review of the constructive episodic simulation hypothesis, with converging cognitive, neuropsychological and neuroimaging evidence that remembering the past and imagining the future draw on overlapping psychological and neural processes. This is the single strongest biology anchor for ARC-085's core claim (one event-token store; simulation = forward re-composition of the same tokens replay reinstates backward). Confidence held below 0.85 because the support is for a SHARED-PROCESS / SHARED-NETWORK architecture inferred from overlap, not for a literal single addressable store, and because the review is integrative rather than a single decisive experiment.
failure_signatures: Overlap of neural substrates for past and future is consistent with a shared store but does not establish ONE store; a two-store model with shared upstream construction processes predicts the same imaging overlap, so the imaging evidence does not by itself discriminate ARC-085's single-store claim from its two-store falsifier.

The constructive system is described as error-prone (memory distortions, false recognition) -- the very flexibility that lets it simulate futures is the source of confabulation, which is the failure mode MECH-365's one-way provenance gate must contain rather than something this substrate prevents on its own.

entries.confidence_rationale: The source-monitoring framework is the foundational and still-dominant account of how the cognitive system attributes a remembered event to its origin (perceived vs imagined, internal vs external, this-source vs that-source). It directly grounds MECH-365's central design move -- that provenance is a represented attribute of an event rather than a free-floating mode bit -- and the reality-monitoring sub-case is the biological form of the committed_vs_imagined field. Held below 0.8 because the framework treats provenance as a RECONSTRUCTIVE, probabilistic attribution made at retrieval (and routinely WRONG), which is in tension with MECH-365's stronger one-way, never-violated gate; the framework supports the existence and dimensionality of the field but partly weakens the absoluteness of the gate.
failure_signatures: Source monitoring is a heuristic, reconstructive judgement made at retrieval from imperfect cues (vividness, sensory detail, cognitive-operation traces), not a stored ground-truth label -- so the human system routinely MISattributes imagined events as perceived (the source-misattribution errors that ARE confabulation/false memory). This weakens MECH-365's premise that committed_vs_imagined can be a reliably-enforced, one-way, first-class field rather than a fallible after-the-fact inference.

Because 'source' is multidimensional with indefinitely many values, a single binary committed_vs_imagined bit may be an under-specification: provenance failures occur along many axes (who said it, when, internally-generated-by-me vs by-another), not just real-vs-imagined.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong, widely-cited review establishing that sleep does not preserve all encoded information but TRIAGES it -- selectively retaining some memories and discarding others, and applying different operations (integrate into existing networks / distill overarching rules / stabilize as-learned) to what it keeps, with salience/future-relevance tags biasing what is retained. This grounds the OFFLINE write-weight principle co-constitutive of MECH-361 (selective, salience-weighted consolidation) and the existence of distinct consolidation OPERATIONS that MECH-252/253 partition. Held at 0.62 (mixed) because the review does NOT establish MECH-252/253's specific dissociation -- SWS consolidating stored-content vs REM consolidating projection-WEIGHTS; it argues for selective + operation-differentiated processing generally, a coarser claim.
failure_signatures: The review establishes selective triage and multiple consolidation operations but does NOT map operations cleanly onto SWS-vs-REM, nor onto a content-vs-weights distinction; MECH-252 (SWS consolidates goal-value content) / MECH-253 (REM consolidates template-performance into projection weights) is a finer, stage-specific and target-specific dissociation that this paper does not deliver and is the part still owed direct evidence.

Triage 'tags' for retention are described in terms of future relevance / emotional salience / explicit instruction; the mechanism by which those tags are set and read is left open, so the claim that an affect GRADIENT is the write-weight (MECH-361) is supported only at the level of 'salience biases retention', not as a graded quantitative write-weight.

entries.confidence_rationale: Compelling, convergent animal+human evidence that emotional arousal, via the basolateral amygdala (BLA) and its neuromodulatory (noradrenergic/glucocorticoid/cholinergic) inputs, MODULATES the strength of memory consolidation -- the degree of amygdala activation at encoding predicts subsequent recall. This is the biological mechanism MECH-361 names as 'affect gradient as memory WRITE-WEIGHT' and is a strong anchor for the salience/affect input to MECH-368's event-level write-authority gate. Held below 0.85 because the substrate modulates a GENERIC arousal/valence magnitude, not the per-candidate, signed affective GRADIENT MECH-361 specifies, and because it concerns the episodic/declarative write path, not the durable world-model/policy weight path that is MECH-368's under-covered target.
failure_signatures: The amygdala modulates write strength as a function of overall emotional AROUSAL (a largely scalar magnitude), whereas MECH-361 requires a per-CANDIDATE affective gradient (a vector over considered options). The BLA literature grounds 'affect scales write depth' but not 'the differential gradient ACROSS candidates is the write-weight' -- the candidate-differentiation that is MECH-361's actual novelty is not evidenced here.

BLA modulation operates on consolidation of declarative/episodic and procedural memory; it is NOT shown to gate durable updates to a predictive world-model or policy weights, which is exactly the path MECH-368 flags as under-covered. Transfer to the online model-update path is by analogy.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct behavioural demonstration of a two-factor write-eligibility mechanism: a weak experience sets a transient, input-specific 'learning tag' that yields only short-term memory UNLESS a separate novelty/salience event within a critical time window supplies the plasticity-related products that convert it to long-term memory. This is a strong biological analogue of MECH-368's separation of write-ELIGIBILITY (the tag) from write-CONSUMMATION (capture of consolidation resources), and grounds 'plasticity_eligibility' as a real gated state rather than an engineering label. Held at 0.7 because it concerns hippocampus-dependent episodic/behavioural LTM, not durable world-model/policy weight updates, and the gating variable is novelty/PRP availability rather than MECH-368's fuller f(PE, salience, residue, goal_relevance) conditioning set.
failure_signatures: Behavioral tagging gates the consolidation of episodic/behavioural memory traces; it is NOT shown to gate durable updates to a predictive world-model or action policy, the path MECH-368 flags as under-covered. The analogy to E1/E2/policy weight-writes is structural, not demonstrated.

The 'second factor' that licenses long-term write is NOVELTY-driven protein synthesis within a time window, a narrower and more passive trigger than MECH-368's active per-event gate conditioned on prediction_error, salience, residue_status, goal_relevance and plasticity_eligibility together. Tagging shows eligibility-then-capture exists; it does not show the rich multi-input arbitration MECH-368 posits.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical statement and review of the constructive episodic simulation hypothesis, with converging cognitive, neuropsychological and neuroimaging evidence that remembering the past and imagining the future draw on overlapping psychological and neural processes. This is the single strongest biology anchor for ARC-085's core claim (one event-token store; simulation = forward re-composition of the same tokens replay reinstates backward). Confidence held below 0.85 because the support is for a SHARED-PROCESS / SHARED-NETWORK architecture inferred from overlap, not for a literal single addressable store, and because the review is integrative rather than a single decisive experiment.
failure_signatures: Overlap of neural substrates for past and future is consistent with a shared store but does not establish ONE store; a two-store model with shared upstream construction processes predicts the same imaging overlap, so the imaging evidence does not by itself discriminate ARC-085's single-store claim from its two-store falsifier.

The constructive system is described as error-prone (memory distortions, false recognition) -- the very flexibility that lets it simulate futures is the source of confabulation, which is the failure mode MECH-365's one-way provenance gate must contain rather than something this substrate prevents on its own.

entries.confidence_rationale: The source-monitoring framework is the foundational and still-dominant account of how the cognitive system attributes a remembered event to its origin (perceived vs imagined, internal vs external, this-source vs that-source). It directly grounds MECH-365's central design move -- that provenance is a represented attribute of an event rather than a free-floating mode bit -- and the reality-monitoring sub-case is the biological form of the committed_vs_imagined field. Held below 0.8 because the framework treats provenance as a RECONSTRUCTIVE, probabilistic attribution made at retrieval (and routinely WRONG), which is in tension with MECH-365's stronger one-way, never-violated gate; the framework supports the existence and dimensionality of the field but partly weakens the absoluteness of the gate.
failure_signatures: Source monitoring is a heuristic, reconstructive judgement made at retrieval from imperfect cues (vividness, sensory detail, cognitive-operation traces), not a stored ground-truth label -- so the human system routinely MISattributes imagined events as perceived (the source-misattribution errors that ARE confabulation/false memory). This weakens MECH-365's premise that committed_vs_imagined can be a reliably-enforced, one-way, first-class field rather than a fallible after-the-fact inference.

Because 'source' is multidimensional with indefinitely many values, a single binary committed_vs_imagined bit may be an under-specification: provenance failures occur along many axes (who said it, when, internally-generated-by-me vs by-another), not just real-vs-imagined.

entries.confidence_rationale: Establishes the core construct MECH-366 needs: personal memories are represented from one of two viewpoints -- FIELD (first-person, original field of view) or OBSERVER (seeing oneself from outside) -- so perspective is a real, represented structural property of an episode, not just an encoding artefact of the camera. That is direct support for the existence of a viewpoint tag. Held at 0.6 (mixed) because the paper does NOT demonstrate the part MECH-366 most needs: that viewpoint is freely SWITCHABLE at retrieval independent of encoding viewpoint. It shows perspective varies with emotion/self-awareness and age of memory, which actually suggests perspective is partly determined by encoding/affect rather than arbitrarily re-set on demand.
failure_signatures: Nigro & Neisser show perspective CORRELATES with emotionality, self-awareness and memory age (older and more self-focused memories drift toward observer perspective). This is evidence that viewpoint is partly DETERMINED by encoding and emotional content, which is in tension with MECH-366's claim that viewpoint is freely switchable at retrieval INDEPENDENT of encoding viewpoint -- the independence is not demonstrated and is mildly contraindicated.

The construct is established by self-report questionnaire on naturalistic memories, with no manipulation showing a single memory can be voluntarily re-experienced from the other viewpoint on demand; switchability is inferred, not tested.

entries.confidence_rationale: Compelling, convergent animal+human evidence that emotional arousal, via the basolateral amygdala (BLA) and its neuromodulatory (noradrenergic/glucocorticoid/cholinergic) inputs, MODULATES the strength of memory consolidation -- the degree of amygdala activation at encoding predicts subsequent recall. This is the biological mechanism MECH-361 names as 'affect gradient as memory WRITE-WEIGHT' and is a strong anchor for the salience/affect input to MECH-368's event-level write-authority gate. Held below 0.85 because the substrate modulates a GENERIC arousal/valence magnitude, not the per-candidate, signed affective GRADIENT MECH-361 specifies, and because it concerns the episodic/declarative write path, not the durable world-model/policy weight path that is MECH-368's under-covered target.
failure_signatures: The amygdala modulates write strength as a function of overall emotional AROUSAL (a largely scalar magnitude), whereas MECH-361 requires a per-CANDIDATE affective gradient (a vector over considered options). The BLA literature grounds 'affect scales write depth' but not 'the differential gradient ACROSS candidates is the write-weight' -- the candidate-differentiation that is MECH-361's actual novelty is not evidenced here.

BLA modulation operates on consolidation of declarative/episodic and procedural memory; it is NOT shown to gate durable updates to a predictive world-model or policy weights, which is exactly the path MECH-368 flags as under-covered. Transfer to the online model-update path is by analogy.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct behavioural demonstration of a two-factor write-eligibility mechanism: a weak experience sets a transient, input-specific 'learning tag' that yields only short-term memory UNLESS a separate novelty/salience event within a critical time window supplies the plasticity-related products that convert it to long-term memory. This is a strong biological analogue of MECH-368's separation of write-ELIGIBILITY (the tag) from write-CONSUMMATION (capture of consolidation resources), and grounds 'plasticity_eligibility' as a real gated state rather than an engineering label. Held at 0.7 because it concerns hippocampus-dependent episodic/behavioural LTM, not durable world-model/policy weight updates, and the gating variable is novelty/PRP availability rather than MECH-368's fuller f(PE, salience, residue, goal_relevance) conditioning set.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational ethological formalisation of drive arbitration: motivational candidates compete for a single behavioural final common path because an animal cannot do more than one thing at a time, with the winner set by 'degree of competitiveness' in a causal-factor space. This is the conceptual ancestor of MECH-394's per-candidate competition and supplies the 'candidate'/'competitiveness' vocabulary REE's E3 scoring uses. Held at 0.66 because its core mutual-exclusivity axiom (behavioural classes cannot co-occur) is the winner-take-all pole that tensions with MECH-394's explicit 'soft-competitive ... not a single-axis winner' commitment, and the empirical content is 1975 dove hunger/thirst measurement.
failure_signatures: The framework axiomatises that behavioural classes are mutually exclusive (the animal does exactly one thing), giving a winner-take-all final common path. MECH-394 explicitly rejects a single-axis winner in favour of soft competition, so McFarland & Sibly anchor the WTA pole the REE policy must decide AGAINST -- it supports competition-among-candidates but not the soft-blend specifically.

Causal-factor-space isoclines are a descriptive measurement framework fitted to dove hunger/thirst; it does not specify the neural mechanism of competition, so it constrains the functional form of arbitration but is silent on implementation.

entries.confidence_rationale: The closest formal articulation of REE's drive layer: homeostatic set-points enter as priors that 'act as drives or goals to enslave action', and multiple control processes (Pavlovian, habitual, goal-directed) are cast as hierarchical contextualisations rather than competitors with a hard boundary. This grounds MECH-394's soft-competitive (not winner-take-all) framing and the homeostatic-vs-exploratory balance the claim cites loosely as 'Pezzulo 2014'. Held at 0.68 because it is a theoretical review proposing a framework, not an empirical result or a worked arbitration policy; it licenses the architecture, it does not test it.
failure_signatures: The framework dissolves the mechanistic distinction between control processes rather than specifying an explicit arbitration rule; it tells you drives-as-priors compete softly via precision-weighting but does not pin down the WTA-vs-blend decision MECH-394 must make, so it under-determines the policy.

As a normative active-inference account it predicts behaviour minimises expected free energy; if REE's substrate cannot represent the homeostatic set-points as priors with calibrated precision, the soft-competition the framework promises will not emerge and arbitration could collapse to whichever drive has the largest raw error.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct empirical demonstration that one drive (hunger) suppresses several others (thirst, anxiety, innate fear, social interaction), that the suppression is graded and context-conditional (often only when food is accessible), and that a hypothalamic node integrates internal state + external factors + anticipated yield. This is the multidrive-competition phenomenon MECH-394 asserts, measured at circuit + behavioural levels. Confidence held below 0.85 because the mapping is functional, not mechanistic -- REE has no AgRP/ARC analogue, and the paper shows hunger-over-others rather than a full N-axis arbitration policy.
failure_signatures: Hunger's dominance is context-gated: it suppresses competing drives 'often only when food is accessible', so a fixed drive hierarchy (hunger > thirst > fear) is wrong -- the ranking is conditional on affordance availability. A multidrive policy that ignores environmental affordance state would mispredict when a lower-ranked drive wins.

The paper establishes hunger-suppresses-others but does not characterise the reciprocal case (does extreme thirst or fear suppress hunger symmetrically?), so the competition geometry beyond the hunger-dominant regime is unconstrained by this evidence.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational normative theory establishing that the long-run average reward rate functions as an opportunity cost that sets a global vigour/allocation signal (reported by tonic dopamine). This supplies MECH-394 with the missing common currency an arbitration policy needs: a single scalar in which the cost of dwelling on one drive (time not spent on others) is priced. Held at 0.70 because the theory is about response vigour/latency of an already-selected action, only indirectly about which drive is selected -- the bridge from opportunity-cost-of-time to inter-drive arbitration is a reasoned extension, not the paper's own claim.
failure_signatures: The opportunity-cost signal in Niv et al. controls how vigorously/quickly to act, not which of several competing drives to pursue. Treating it as a direct arbitration signal over-reads the model: it prices the cost of time but does not by itself rank drives.

The average-reward currency is a single global scalar; if MECH-394's arbitration needs per-axis differentiated valuations (so that fear and hunger are priced on different scales), a single opportunity-cost term is insufficient and must be combined with axis-specific benefit terms.

entries.confidence_rationale: Establishes that a non-feeding behaviour (self-grooming) is a homeostatically-regulated, positively-valenced de-arousal response with a dedicated limbic circuit (vSub -> LSv -> LH), not a deficit-reduction consummatory act. This grounds SD-060's core premise that needs beyond hunger/thirst (here: a de-arousal/comfort need) are first-class behavioural-homeostatic systems. Held at 0.62 because it evidences ONE non-feeding behaviour as homeostatically regulated (evidence-by-instance), not the full register, and grooming-as-displacement is a narrower category than the exploration/play/social axes SD-060 also enumerates.
failure_signatures: The paper evidences grooming specifically as a stress-induced de-arousal behaviour; it does not show that exploration, play, social contact, or learning are each independently homeostatically integrated, so generalising from grooming to the whole SD-060 register is an inductive leap this single circuit does not license.

The circuit is engaged by emotional stress (an aversive trigger); SD-060 also posits appetitive non-terminal drives (curiosity, play) whose regulation may follow a different, non-de-arousal logic -- so the homeostatic framing demonstrated here may not transfer to the appetitive axes.

entries.confidence_rationale: non_contributory -- excluded from scoring
non_contributory -- excluded from scoring

Canonical review establishing that even mild acute uncontrollable stress triggers a catecholamine surge that rapidly takes prefrontal deliberative control offline and shifts behaviour toward habitual/reactive responding. This is the neuromodulatory mechanism behind anti-epistemic-panic: under threat the substrate that would sustain extended inference is suppressed, forcing early commitment. Strong source; capped because it is about working-memory/PFC function generally, and the bridge to REE's specific commitment-timing gate is functional, not implemented.
failure_signatures: Anti-epistemic-panic mechanism: acute stress -> high catecholamines -> PFC deliberative/working-memory function impaired -> reliance on faster habitual/subcortical control -> commitment before the belief-state is resolved.
Predicts the inverted-U: too little arousal under-engages, too much collapses deliberation -- the commitment-timing axis has an optimal band, not a monotone.

entries.confidence_rationale: The clean clinical-computational anchor for the epistemic-freezing pole and the exact mirror of the Ross 2015 jumping-to-conclusions finding: OCD youth set HIGHER decision thresholds and gather MORE information before committing, modelled as an altered cost of sampling. Together with the JTC entry it brackets the commitment-timing axis from both ends -- under-gather (panic/JTC) vs over-gather (freezing/OCD). Confidence 0.70: rigorous model-based clinical study, but the over-gathering is in an abstract sampling task, and 'enhanced performance' shows the pole is not purely pathological (context-dependent).
failure_signatures: Epistemic-freezing: a raised decision threshold / increased subjective cost of committing produces extended information gathering and delayed (or absent) commitment -- the over-exploration pole MECH-434 must bound.
The effect can be advantageous in some contexts, so the axis is a trade-off with an optimal band, not a deficit to minimise to zero.

entries.confidence_rationale: A strong synthesis of the threat-imminence framework, which is almost a direct description of the anti-epistemic-panic pole: as a threat becomes proximal/surprising, the system contracts its decision and state space and switches from model-based (deliberative, information-gathering) to model-free (fast, reactive) computation. That is exactly 'collapse the epistemic term and commit under urgency'. High relevance and source quality; capped by being a review framework and by the species/circuit specifics not mapping one-to-one onto REE.
failure_signatures: Anti-epistemic-panic: at high threat imminence the deliberative/model-based route is abandoned for model-free reaction BEFORE the belief-state is disambiguated -- adaptive when imminence is genuinely high, pathological when it fires on uncertain or distal threat.
The same axis predicts the opposite failure when imminence is mis-estimated as low (over-deliberation), linking to epistemic-freezing.

entries.confidence_rationale: The cleanest computational grounding that WHEN to commit is a governed, time-varying control parameter rather than a fixed threshold: evidence is multiplied by a growing urgency signal, so the effective decision criterion drops over time and commitment timing is tunable. This is the mechanistic backbone of MECH-434 (commitment timing as the axis whose two poles are freezing and panic). Held at 0.74 because it is a model of perceptual two-choice decisions, not of REE's belief-state-over-trajectories commitment, and urgency here is motor-related rather than threat-driven.
failure_signatures: A fixed (non-urgency) bound cannot adapt commitment timing to changing conditions -- it either over-deliberates (freezing) or commits prematurely; urgency-gating shows timing is an adjustable gain, which is exactly what the two MECH-434 poles dysregulate in opposite directions.

entries.confidence_rationale: Grounds the completion-set partner HPL-9 named for MECH-147: hilar mossy cells set the dentate excitation/inhibition balance (both an associative GC feedback loop AND feed-forward GABAergic inhibition onto GCs) that governs DG output sparsity. Confidence moderate because the paper measures synaptic plasticity / E-I balance, not pattern separation directly -- it establishes the partner circuit, not the separation consequence.
failure_signatures: The study measures MC-GC synaptic plasticity and its effect on E/I balance and GC output; it does NOT directly test that mossy-cell-mediated inhibition improves pattern separation. The link from E/I-balance control to separation is inferred (the authors note possible relevance to pattern separation and epilepsy).

entries.confidence_rationale: Grounds the completion-set partner HPL-9 named for MECH-148: theta-gamma nesting is the oscillatory code that orders items/events in a temporal sequence -- the substrate that a per-step elapsed-time tag plugs into. Confidence moderate because the scheme codes ORDERED ITEM sequences (rank), which is adjacent to but not identical with MECH-148's pure context-independent ELAPSED-TIME signal.
failure_signatures: Theta-gamma coding represents the ORDINAL position of items in a sequence (which item is 1st, 2nd, ...), not a metric elapsed-time-since-event scalar. MECH-148's pure time cells encode elapsed duration; the theta-gamma partner supplies ordering/segmentation, so the two are complementary, not interchangeable -- conflating them would mis-specify the substrate.

entries.confidence_rationale: The PRIMARY the HPL-9 partial flag named. Directly grounds MECH-207's load-bearing conjunction: prediction error disrupts sustained hippocampal representations AND the PE->updating relationship DEPENDS ON concurrent basal-forebrain (cholinergic) activation -- i.e. cholinergic co-activation is the permissive gate. Resolves the directionality ambiguity left by Hasselmo 1999; held below 0.85 by fMRI indirectness (basal-forebrain BOLD as a cholinergic proxy).
failure_signatures: Cholinergic involvement is inferred from basal-forebrain BOLD activation and hippocampal-basal-forebrain connectivity, not from a direct ACh measurement or a cholinergic manipulation -- the permissive-gate role is correlational here, not causally demonstrated.

entries.confidence_rationale: Establishes the END-STATE that ARC-090 says development compresses INTO: the default mode network is a set of interacting hubs and subsystems supporting 'internal mentation' -- self-reference, autobiographical memory, future simulation/prospection, and adaptive introspective thought -- the exact function list ARC-090 attributes to the mature internal DMN. This grounds the target of the developmental claim with mechanism/connectivity evidence. It does NOT itself test the developmental-externalisation thesis (that those functions first run externally in play), so it supports one half of ARC-090 (what the end-state is) and is silent on the other (the externalise->internalise trajectory), which is why it is paired with the Fair 2008 maturation entry.
failure_signatures: The review characterises the ADULT/mature default network; it makes no claim that DMN functions are developmentally PRECEDED by external play-based instantiation -- ARC-090's distinctive thesis is therefore unsupported by this paper alone (it grounds the end-state, not the precursor).

The fractionation into hubs/subsystems is partly inferential from functional-connectivity correlations; the mapping from 'DMN subsystem' to a discrete REE generative-modelling module is an architectural translation, not a one-to-one correspondence.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the developmental-trajectory half ARC-090 needs: using resting-state functional connectivity MRI, the default network is shown to be only SPARSELY connected in school-age children (7-9 yrs) and to INTEGRATE into a cohesive, interconnected network over development into adulthood. That the internal DMN is not present as a mature system early but assembles over development is direct support for ARC-090's framing of the internal DMN as a developmental END-STATE rather than an innate given. Confidence held below 0.8 because the data show the network MATURES; they do not show WHAT drives the maturation, and in particular do not establish that external play / self-narration is the precursor that compresses inward -- ARC-090's specific causal mechanism is beyond what connectivity maturation alone demonstrates.
failure_signatures: The study shows DMN connectivity INTEGRATES with age but is agnostic about cause -- it does not show that externalised play/private-speech experience is what drives the integration, so it supports 'the internal DMN is a developmental end-state' but NOT 'externalisation is the route to it' (ARC-090's distinctive causal thesis).

Resting-state functional connectivity maturation is a network-architecture measure, not a functional measure of when self-reference / future-simulation capacities come online behaviourally -- the inference from 'sparse connectivity at 7-9' to 'these mental functions are not yet internalised' is an additional step.

entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical integrative review of inner speech, explicitly built on the Vygotskian internalisation account (social speech -> private/egocentric speech -> condensed inner speech) and reporting the neurobiology (left inferior frontal gyrus / Broca's area as the production core; superior temporal gyrus involvement; supplementary motor and parietal contributions). It grounds MECH-380's central assertion -- that overt self-narration is the EXTERNAL phase of a cognitive-control system that later compresses inward -- with mechanism evidence rather than textbook analogy, and grounds MECH-381's compression ladder via the documented private->inner speech internalisation. Confidence held below 0.8 by the architectural-mapping step: the review describes inner speech as verbal thinking / self-monitoring / executive support, not as an arbitration-driving control surface in REE's specific sense, and REE has no spoken-language modality at all.
failure_signatures: The review documents that inner speech SUPPORTS executive function, planning, and self-regulation, but it does not establish that the external (overt) phase is functionally NECESSARY as a control surface -- the correlation between private-speech use and task performance is developmental and individual-difference evidence, not a demonstration that cognition must be externalised before it can be internalised.

Inner speech is shown to be variable (some adults report little; condensed vs expanded forms differ) -- the ladder MECH-381 asserts is a central tendency, not an obligatory sequence, which weakens any claim that the externalise-then-internalise route is the ONLY developmental path to internal control.

entries.confidence_rationale: Provides the explicit Vygotskian internalisation MECHANISM that the compression ladder (MECH-381) needs: inner speech develops through a transition between EXPANDED (full, external-like, dialogic) and CONDENSED (abbreviated, covert) forms, and the neural-correlates literature is read through that lens (low verbal-self-monitoring tasks like reciting in inner speech vs high VSM tasks like auditory verbal imagery dissociate in temporal-lobe activation). The compression-and-condensation account is the closest mechanistic statement of MECH-381's externalise->internalise axis. Confidence is moderate because the paper's primary explanatory target is auditory verbal hallucinations (a pathology of mis-attributed inner speech), so the mapping to a healthy REE control surface runs through a clinical model, and the neural evidence is correlational.
failure_signatures: The condensed/expanded framework is a theoretical integration of mixed and partly inconsistent neuroimaging findings, not a settled mechanism -- the authors themselves flag that prior studies rested on 'unexamined assumptions about the form and developmental significance of inner speech'.

The paper's account of WHEN inner speech is mis-attributed (AVHs arise from abnormalities in the condensed<->expanded transition) implies the compression ladder has a failure mode REE has not modelled: a poorly tagged self-generated control signal can be experienced as external/other, i.e. the ladder is not automatically safe.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct, converging-methods (ERP + fMRI) neuroscience test of MECH-382's exact claim: referring to oneself in the third person (self-distancing) reduces self-referential emotional reactivity -- a smaller late positive potential within the first second, and reduced medial prefrontal cortex (self-referential) activation -- and does so WITHOUT increasing cognitive-control markers (no extra stimulus-preceding negativity; no increase in cognitive-control fMRI regions). That 'alters processing of the affective/self-referential state, cheaply, without recruiting effortful control' is precisely MECH-382's framing of distancing as a low-effort arbitration-altering operator. Confidence held below 0.8 by modest sample sizes typical of ERP/fMRI studies and by the architectural step from human mPFC self-referential processing to REE's self_reference_frame vocabulary.
failure_signatures: The effect is demonstrated for down-regulating NEGATIVE affect (aversive images, negative autobiographical memories); the paper does not show third-person framing helps with the broader 'sticky high-conflict self-referential state' MECH-382 targets (e.g. unresolved prediction-error pressure), so the generalisation to arbitration-level conflict is an extrapolation.

'Without engaging cognitive control' is an inference from the ABSENCE of increases in a-priori control markers (SPN; control regions); a null on chosen markers is weaker than a positive demonstration that no control was used, so the 'low-effort' premise rests on accepting a null.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the theoretical statement of the mechanism that MECH-383 names -- the label-feedback hypothesis -- and is the 'top-down precision-control partner' the grounding task asked for. It assembles the evidence that labels exert rapid, pervasive, top-down effects on categorisation, visual discrimination, and even stimulus detection, and argues the right framework is one where labels MODULATE ongoing perceptual processing in a task-dependent, flexible way (rather than verbal vs non-verbal being separate stores). That modulatory, task-dependent framing is exactly MECH-383's 'label as control input to precision'. Confidence moderate because it is a review/position piece, not a single decisive experiment, and its 'reject the verbal/non-verbal distinction' framing is stronger than REE needs (REE only needs labels to be ONE control input among others).
failure_signatures: Label effects are described as both deep (reaching basic visual processes) AND fragile (verbal interference can nullify them) -- so a label-as-control input is state-dependent and can be knocked out by load, meaning REE could not treat it as a reliable always-on precision signal.

The review is a theoretical synthesis advocating a position (language modulates perception online); it is not itself an experiment, so it grounds the FRAMEWORK for MECH-383 rather than supplying a new decisive datum beyond the primary studies it cites.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical direct test of MECH-383's exact claim: producing a self-directed label ('saying the target name aloud') temporarily improves visual SEARCH for that target -- a perceptual-control intervention, not a post-perceptual report. The design is causal (within-subject manipulation of speaking vs not speaking the target name) and the effect is graded by name-target association strength, which matches MECH-383's framing of labels as tunable top-down signals. Confidence held below 0.8 because the manipulation is overt natural-language speech in humans and the boundary condition (speaking HURTS when the label mismatches the target) shows the control input is not free -- both relevant transfer caveats for a non-linguistic REE substrate.
failure_signatures: The facilitation reverses to IMPAIRMENT as the discrepancy between the spoken name and the visual target grows -- a mis-specified label actively degrades search, so a label-as-control input in REE would need accurate label generation to be net-beneficial (no free lunch).

The effect is on visual SEARCH (finding a known target among distractors), which is template-matching/attentional, not on detecting genuinely novel or unexpected cues -- so the paper supports the 'bias toward label-relevant cues' reading of MECH-383 more strongly than the 'novelty-gradient toward unexplained change' reading.

entries.confidence_rationale: On-domain computational corroboration of the fallible-operator / raw-episode-preservation premise: LLM agents show an experience-following property; inaccurate stored experiences propagate errors; the paper advocates regulating experience QUALITY and preserving episodic records over lossy consolidation/summarisation. Mapping fidelity high (REE is an agent), but it is an AI preprint not biology -- per biology-before-formal-definitions it supplements, does not substitute for, the biological warrant. Held at 0.60.
failure_signatures: Error propagation: an inaccurate past experience retrieved by similarity drives a similar (wrong) output -- so a consolidation step that summarises away the detail needed to judge an experience's quality REMOVES the very signal ('future task evaluations as free quality labels') needed to filter it, making lossy consolidation actively harmful in an agent loop.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong cross-species (rat + human fMRI) evidence for Trace Transformation Theory: memories lose perceptual/contextual PRECISION over time as they become schematic, with a hippocampal->mPFC shift. For INV-080 this grounds the THREAT model (consolidation transforms and loses episodic detail) but NOT the prescription (no evidence the brain preserves a recoverable raw episode) -- the biological default is detail loss, so INV-080 is biology-informed-but-not-biology-mandated. Mixed.
failure_signatures: The biological default is that detail is LOST under transformation -- gist-like schematic memory replaces perceptually-detailed episodic memory over time. So INV-080's 'consolidation_output must not replace source_episode_evidence' is a NORMATIVE engineering rule that DEPARTS from the biological default, not one biology mandates; the brain does not obviously keep a recoverable raw episode, so the warrant is for the risk, not the remedy.

entries.confidence_rationale: Grounds the 'retired' state as a first-class ADAPTIVE, regulated operation (transience enhances flexibility + prevents overfitting; goal of memory is decision-optimisation not preservation) -- supports MECH-391's retired state. But for INV-080 it is a genuine TENSION: it argues controlled forgetting/attenuation is GOOD, cautioning against a naive 'never delete' reading. Net mixed: it reframes INV-080 as 'retirement must be GOVERNED', not 'no deletion'.
failure_signatures: Transience (forgetting) is adaptive -- it enhances flexibility and prevents overfitting -- so an over-strong INV-080 that forbids ALL deletion would itself be a failure mode (hoarding outdated, overfit detail). The invariant must be read as 'no SILENT/ungoverned deletion of the evidence base', not 'no forgetting'; a memory system that never retires anything degrades decision-making.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly on the integrate-vs-separate axis MECH-391's allocation gate steers: related memories interconnect via overlapping neuronal populations; mPFC schema representations guide reactivation that promotes hippocampal integration (schema_fit input). High mapping fidelity for the 'integrate' pole; the explicit DECISION policy (when to integrate vs separate, and pricing false-linking) remains the novel REE overlay.
failure_signatures: The paper documents integration as a mechanism but does not specify WHEN integration should be withheld; it evidences only the integrate pole, so it cannot ground the cost of OVER-integration (false linking) that INV-079 and the allocation policy must price -- a one-sided grounding that, taken alone, would bias the gate toward linking.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong NRN review arguing memory is a principally DYNAMIC, reconstructive process: consolidated memories re-enter transient instability on reactivation and must re-stabilise. Directly grounds the contested state and the fallible-operator premise (re-stabilisation can alter content). The 6-state labels and allocation policy remain REE overlays, so fidelity is held below ceiling.
failure_signatures: If post-retrieval restabilisation can alter a memory's content, then a 'consolidated' state cannot be treated as immutable ground truth -- any lifecycle store that reads consolidated traces as authoritative-and-final inherits the risk that the trace was silently rewritten during a prior reconsolidation episode.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong source; grounds the 'contested' (labile-on-reactivation) state but explicitly bounds it -- reconsolidation as time-limited lingering consolidation, mostly fresh memories, blockade does not induce permanent amnesia. The labile state is real but narrower than an indefinitely re-writable 'contested' slot, hence mixed.
failure_signatures: Reconsolidation occurs mostly in relatively fresh memories and blockade of reconsolidation does not induce permanent amnesia -- so a 'contested' lifecycle state cannot be modelled as an always-available, indefinitely re-writable mode; the window is bounded and may be a tail of the original consolidation rather than a recapitulated process.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical NRN review; strong source quality. Maps onto the multi-STATE-over-time premise behind MECH-391's lifecycle store (recent hippocampus-dependent -> remote cortical), but does not itself specify a 6-label taxonomy or an allocation-decision policy, so mapping_fidelity is held mid.
failure_signatures: The review establishes that memories pass through distinct, time-dependent states with different anatomical substrates, but it does not enumerate discrete lifecycle LABELS (retained/indexed/summarised/consolidated/contested/retired) nor describe a control-plane that decides among them -- the staging is observed, the policy is a REE overlay.

entries.confidence_rationale: Cerebral Cortex fMRI study (PMID 21693491, PMC3278316), companion to the Frank & Badre 2011 computational model. Provides empirical human evidence that distinct cortico-striatal circuits learn hierarchical structure at distinct levels of policy abstraction -- contextual representations in rostral frontal cortex gate representations in caudal frontal cortex, with reinforcement learning operating at each level. This is the biology-before-formal-definitions warrant the OBJ-ABS-8 node requires for SD-042: it shows that a biological substrate genuinely learns and represents temporally/contextually nested policy abstraction in cortico-striatal loops, which is the neural precondition for an option-style library. Confidence 0.72 (deliberately below the chunking entries): the fMRI evidence is for LEVELS-of-policy-abstraction and gating, not for the Sutton-Precup-Singh option TRIPLE (initiation set / termination function / internal policy) per se, so the formal construct SD-042 imports is warranted at the architecture level but not validated component-by-component.
failure_signatures: The fMRI evidence validates that cortico-striatal circuits gate contextual representations at nested levels of abstraction; it does NOT directly evidence the three formal components of an option (initiation set, termination function, internal policy). SD-042 imports those from the RL formalism, so the biological warrant covers the hierarchy, not the option triple itself.

The analysis re-uses the Badre, Kayser & D'Esposito 2010 task via a model-based reanalysis; the abstraction levels are defined by the experimenters' policy hierarchy rather than discovered by the agent. How the brain DISCOVERS reusable option boundaries from experience -- the same open question Botvinick 2009 flags -- remains unaddressed.

Mapping fidelity is bounded by REE's gridworld: with 4 actions and short episodes there is little genuine hierarchical depth for an option library to compress, so the substrate stays V4-gated on a richer environment (tool use / social coordination / hierarchical task structure) regardless of the biological warrant.

entries.confidence_rationale: Nature primary single-unit/circuit study (PMID 20651684, PMC3477867). In a self-paced operant task, mice learning to perform a particular action sequence developed nigrostriatal neural activity that specifically signalled the INITIATION or TERMINATION of each sequence. The start/stop activity emerged with learning, was action-specific, and did not reflect interval timing, movement speed, or action value; genetically altering striatal circuit function disrupted the development of this activity and selectively impaired sequence learning. This is the direct empirical substrate for the start/stop bracketing SD-045's chunk cache depends on -- stronger and more mechanistic than the Graybiel 2008 review it complements. Confidence 0.84: very high source quality and a near-verbatim mapping onto SD-045's (state-signature -> chunk -> outcome-signature) bracketed unit; modest transfer risk (rodent motor sequence vs REE grid-world cognitive action).
failure_signatures: The start/stop signals are demonstrated for over-trained motor action sequences in mice; whether the same bracketing machinery brackets abstract / cognitive 'chunks' (e.g. 'forage at this location' as a unit) is a plausible but untested extrapolation.

Start/stop activity EMERGED only after substantial sequence learning. REE's short episodes (200-500 steps) may not accumulate enough repetition to surface a chunk-bracketing signature, which is a real design constraint on any V3 pull-forward of SD-045.

The paper localises the start/stop signal to nigrostriatal circuits broadly; it does not resolve the dorsolateral-vs-dorsomedial striatal split that SD-045 assumes when it places the chunk cache specifically in the ARC-021 dorsolateral-loop slot.

entries.confidence_rationale: Rice & Rubin show that first- and third-person visual perspectives are NOT mutually exclusive opposites: people commonly report experiencing a single memory from both perspectives, and the two ratings correlate differentially with vividness rather than trading off as a single bipolar dimension. This supports two things MECH-366 needs: (1) viewpoint is a graded, represented property that can be queried independently (not one fixed camera angle baked into the trace), and (2) it is a property distinct from the content of the episode. Held at 0.7 because the evidence is retrospective self-report rating rather than a manipulation showing on-demand switching, and the reported gender/individual differences mildly echo the encoding-dependence caveat from Nigro & Neisser.
failure_signatures: Perspective is partly an individual-differences and gender-linked variable (females report third-person perspective more often). As with Nigro & Neisser, this is a mild contra-signal to fully arbitrary, person-independent switching -- the viewpoint tag's default may be partly fixed by the rememberer, not freely re-set per retrieval.

entries.confidence_rationale: Brewin et al.'s dual-representation account of intrusive imagery is a clinical anchor that viewpoint is a represented, dissociable property and that imagined/re-experienced content carries a viewpoint that can be therapeutically shifted (e.g. moving a flashback from a field/reliving perspective to an observer perspective reduces distress). That supports MECH-366's 're-experienced from either viewpoint' clause and extends it to imagery, not just recall. Marked MIXED, not supports, because the same literature documents that traumatic intrusions often come with an INVOLUNTARY, fixed first-person reliving perspective that resists voluntary re-setting -- a direct partial contraindication to the 'freely switchable at will' reading of MECH-366.
failure_signatures: Traumatic intrusive images are characteristically involuntary and locked to a first-person reliving (field) perspective with a 'nowness' quality; the viewpoint is precisely what the patient CANNOT switch at will. This is a real-world failure mode of free viewpoint-switching and shows the switch can be blocked by the affective/encoding status of the memory -- consistent with the Nigro and Rice caveats that perspective is partly determined, not arbitrary.

The field<->observer shift that therapy induces is effortful and often requires structured intervention, not a costless retrieval-time toggle -- a faithful REE viewpoint switch may need to model the cost/eligibility of switching, not just its availability.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the switchability keystone the Nigro & Neisser entry explicitly named as the missing follow-up. St. Jacques et al. instruct participants to recall a recently encoded autobiographical event from EITHER the original (typically own-eyes) perspective or the alternative perspective, and show that adopting a novel visual perspective at retrieval is (a) possible on demand and (b) actively reshapes the phenomenology of the memory, with precuneus recruitment scaling the degree of change. This is direct evidence for the load-bearing second half of MECH-366: viewpoint is a represented property that can be re-set at retrieval, independent of the encoding viewpoint, rather than a fixed encoding artefact. Held at 0.78 rather than higher because the manipulation is instructed/voluntary in a lab paradigm and the reshaping effect means switching is not perfectly content-preserving -- which is itself architecturally interesting but slightly complicates a clean 'same token, switchable label' reading.
failure_signatures: Shifting perspective does not merely re-render the same stored episode from a new angle -- it MODIFIES the memory (emotional intensity and vividness change, precuneus activity predicts the degree of change). So MECH-366's clean picture (one event token, a switchable viewpoint label read at retrieval) is complicated: in the brain, exercising the switch writes back to the trace. A faithful REE implementation must decide whether viewpoint-switch is a pure read operation or one that legitimately updates the episode.

entries.confidence_rationale: Johnson & Raye's reality-monitoring model grounds the OTHER facet of MECH-366 named in the task: the imagined-vs-experienced viewpoint label. They show that memories carry attributes (perceptual detail, contextual richness vs records of cognitive operations) that the system uses to decide whether a memory originated externally (perceived) or internally (imagined/reasoned), and that this attribution is reconstructive and can fail. That is the biological warrant for treating imagined-vs-experienced as a represented, decidable label on an episode rather than a given. Held at 0.62 because (a) it is a 1981 theoretical model, and (b) reality-monitoring is really the imagined-vs-experienced SOURCE axis, which overlaps MECH-365/MECH-430 provenance more than the field/observer SPATIAL axis -- I am grounding one of MECH-366's two viewpoint dimensions, with explicit overlap into the provenance claims.
failure_signatures: Reality monitoring is reconstructive and fallible: the imagined-vs-experienced label is INFERRED from memory attributes at retrieval, not stored as ground truth. This grounds the EXISTENCE of an imagined-vs-experienced label but, exactly as the MECH-365 Johnson-1993 entry already recorded, leans against the absoluteness of a one-way committed-vs-imagined gate -- the brain's tag is probabilistic and can be wrong (imagined events misattributed as experienced).

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct grounding for MECH-429, which was reaped in the first ABM-9 pass as a completion-set partner with NO literature_evidence entry (lit_conf null) -- this entry closes that reap-only gap, which is exactly what the FINISH pass asked for. van Kesteren et al.'s SLIMM model proposes that medial PFC detects congruency between new information and existing neocortical schemas ('resonance') and, when congruent, routes that information into a fast mPFC-gated systems-consolidation pathway, bypassing the slow hippocampal-dependent route that incongruent information needs. That IS MECH-429's mechanism: schema-fit as a consolidation write-weight / routing variable with a fast vmPFC route. Strong fidelity; held at 0.77 because the claim that schema-fit is a SECOND write-weight axis ORTHOGONAL to affect (MECH-361) is REE's synthesis, not something this paper tests against affect.
failure_signatures: SLIMM also predicts schema-INCONGRUENT (novel) information is sometimes better remembered (the paradoxical novelty effect), via a separate route. So schema-congruence is not a monotone write-weight -- both high congruence and high novelty can boost encoding by different mechanisms. MECH-429's 'congruent is consolidated preferentially' is the central tendency, but a faithful model must represent the U-shaped congruence/novelty interaction, not a single linear schema-fit gain.

Human fMRI with a value-matched transreinforcer reversal design that isolates outcome IDENTITY from value; OFC encodes reward-identity expectations updated by midbrain identity prediction errors. Directly supports MECH-346's core premise that the goal seed is an object-identity representation, not a value scalar. Docked for BOLD-level (not single-cell) resolution and appetitive-odor task vs REE gridworld objects.
failure_signatures: Identity and value error signals in the midbrain are correlated and share a common neural origin, so an identity-only seed that ignores value covariation may be biologically incomplete.
Demonstrated for appetitive food-odor outcomes only; whether identity expectations seed a prospective goal latent for spatial/foraging objects is untested here.

entries.confidence_rationale: Primate single-unit recording showing OFC strongly encodes the IDENTITY of the chosen stimulus and that value coding is stimulus-SPECIFIC (not value independent of identity). This is direct support for what/where factorization: value is bound to object identity, so a goal seeded from the most-wanted object's identity latent is biologically faithful. Docked for macaque bandit task vs REE objects and for the seed-vs-code distinction.
failure_signatures: Value coding in OFC is stimulus-specific rather than identity-agnostic, but the chosen-value and exploration-bonus signals are encoded at only intermediate levels, so identity is not the sole determinant of the goal-relevant signal.
OFC also encodes choice location and environment value (at low levels), suggesting the seed for goal-directed behaviour integrates more than object identity alone.

entries.confidence_rationale: Conceptual/empirical review arguing that value representations are 'orphaned from their source' without object identity, and that OFC performs stimulus-specific predictive coding of both perceptual outcomes and expected values. Directly supports the design rationale of MECH-346 (seed the goal from identity, not bare value). Lower confidence because it is a review/position piece rather than a direct mechanistic test of a goal seed.
failure_signatures: The paper is a conceptual argument; it does not provide a mechanistic demonstration that an identity representation is used to generate a prospective goal latent.
Evidence base is largely olfactory; generality to non-olfactory object goals is asserted rather than demonstrated.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct neural dissociation: dopamine stimulation in nucleus accumbens enhanced ONLY the motivation/incentive-salience component and did NOT alter hedonic impact or learned-prediction signals; the incentive-salience signal to the reward-proximal cue was separable from the learned prediction value of the distal cue. This is strong, mechanistically specific support for MECH-347's 'cue-pull with no revaluation' (incentive salience independent of value-update). Docked for rat ventral-pallidum/accumbens electrophysiology vs REE latent nudge.
failure_signatures: Incentive salience enhancement required pharmacological dopamine stimulation; a purely cue-driven nudge without a gain/state signal may not reproduce the effect magnitude.

Incentive salience tracked the reward-PROXIMAL cue, not the distal predictive cue, so cue_pull strength should scale with proximity (consistent with REE's cue_recall_min_proximity) rather than mere predictive association.

entries.confidence_rationale: Microinjection + behaviour showing limbic activation dynamically amplifies attraction toward a previously-learned Pavlovian cue, making it a 'stronger motivational magnet' at the expense of a competing cue, due to stronger motivation (not habit), with sign-trackers flexibly following the cue to a new location. Maps cleanly onto cue_pull as a directional, competing, motivation-driven pull toward the cued object. Docked for rat striatal microinjection and individual-difference dependence (sign- vs goal-trackers).
failure_signatures: The cue-magnet effect was individual-difference dependent (sign-trackers vs goal-trackers) and required limbic drug activation; a uniform cue_pull may not capture this heterogeneity or its state-dependence.
Amplification was selective and competitive (one cue at the expense of another), implying cue_pull should arbitrate across competing cues rather than independently nudge toward each.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily-cited review establishing that dopamine attributes incentive salience ('wanting') to reward-related cues, dissociable from both hedonic 'liking' and associative learning, and that dopamine activation is SUFFICIENT to enhance cue-triggered incentive salience. Directly supports MECH-347's premise that a cue can pull behaviour toward an object WITHOUT a value/benefit gate or revaluation. Docked because it is a review and because REE's cue_pull lacks a dopamine-state-modulated gain analog.
failure_signatures: Incentive salience is dynamically modulated by physiological/dopamine state; a cue_pull with a fixed gain and no state modulation may not capture the amplification the biology requires.
Wanting is described as integrating Pavlovian associative information WITH physiological state signals, so a purely cue-driven nudge ignoring drive state would be an incomplete instantiation.

Strong (Nat Neurosci) causal demonstration that the plasticity window is RE-OPENABLE in adulthood: environmental enrichment restored visual acuity and ocular dominance in adult amblyopic rats, via reduced GABAergic inhibition, increased BDNF, and reduced perineuronal-net density -- and benzodiazepine inhibition-enhancement PREVENTED it. 'Mixed' because it SUPPORTS the continuous re-openable gain reading (ARC-093) and grounds the BDNF duration knob (MECH-400) while WEAKENING any binary/irreversible closure assumption. Held at 0.76: a clean adult-reopening result, but a multi-factor manipulation (enrichment) where the gain channel is inferred from the molecular correlates rather than directly gated.
failure_signatures: Closure is REVERSIBLE: an adult intervention reduced inhibition and reopened a window thought permanently shut. A REE model treating crystallization (INV-074/MECH-334) as strictly one-way and irreversible would be biologically incomplete -- the biology keeps a re-opening pathway (lower inhibition / raise BDNF / strip PNNs), which is the gain knob (ARC-093) and duration knob (MECH-400) acting in the closure-recovery direction.

The reopening was a CONFOUNDED multi-factor effect (enrichment simultaneously lowered GABA, raised BDNF, reduced PNNs); the causal weight of each factor is not separable here. A REE design that attributes reopening to a single BDNF-analog duration knob (MECH-400) would over-claim specificity relative to what this paper isolates -- it shows the factors co-move, not that BDNF alone is the lever.

entries.confidence_rationale: High source quality (Nature; in vivo whole-cell recording in adult AI) and the single best mechanistic account of HOW cholinergic gating opens a plasticity window: NB pairing causes a rapid, stimulus-specific reduction of synaptic inhibition (seconds), followed by a slow excitatory increase and an activity-dependent inhibitory rebalancing (hours) that retunes the receptive field. This grounds MECH-398's gate as a transient disinhibition event and supports ARC-093's claim that plasticity GAIN is a state-conditional, time-limited window distinct from the steady-state content signals. Held at 0.78 because the disinhibition mechanism is specific to cortical E/I microcircuitry, whereas REE's encoder has no explicit inhibitory interneuron pool -- the transfer is to the functional shape (transient window then rebalance), not the synaptic implementation.
failure_signatures: The plasticity window was OPENED by disinhibition but CLOSED by a slow activity-dependent re-increase of inhibition that rebalanced excitation -- opening and closing are coupled by the same E/I machinery. A REE design that gates the opening (MECH-398) without a coupled rebalancing/closure mechanism (MECH-399 PV clock) risks runaway excitation: the biology never leaves the window open, it always rebalances.

The disinhibition was stimulus-SPECIFIC (only the paired stimulus's inputs were affected). A global REE gain scalar that opens plasticity for the whole encoder at once would over-generalise relative to this targeted, input-specific window -- arguing for the layer/input-specific resolution Q-072 raises rather than a single global gate.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational (Nature) result that pins down a load-bearing design constraint for MECH-398: in kitten visual cortex, combined destruction of BOTH the cholinergic AND noradrenergic inputs is required to abolish ocular-dominance plasticity -- lesioning either system alone leaves plasticity intact. This is the direct evidence for the multiplicative ACh x LC-NE composition the plan specifies, and it is the cleanest support for the hard separation rule: NE/LC-NE is an INPUT to the gain gate, not the gate itself. Held at 0.79 because it is an older lesion/depletion study in kitten developmental cortex with the usual pharmacological-specificity caveats; the design constraint it supports is nonetheless durable and independently corroborated.
failure_signatures: Single-system lesions (ACh-alone or NE-alone) did NOT abolish plasticity -- only the combined lesion did. A REE gate built as a single neuromodulatory input (ACh-analog alone, or collapsing NE into the same channel) would mis-predict redundancy: the biology shows the gate is conjunctive across at least two modulatory systems, so a one-input gate is more brittle than the substrate it models.

The authors note the catecholamine neurotoxin 6-OHDA can interfere directly with ACh action, and that earlier NA-depletion results conflicted -- a cautionary signature that crude single-transmitter manipulations conflate channels. A REE implementation that does not keep the plasticity-GAIN channel architecturally separate from the content channels (MECH-313 LC-NE / MECH-203 5-HT / SD-037 orexin) risks the same conflation that produced two decades of conflicting plasticity-modulation results.
