A global REE gain scalar that opens plasticity for the whole encoder at once would over-generalise relative to this targeted, input-specific window -- arguing for the layer/input-specific resolution Q-072 raises rather than a single global gate.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, high-source-quality (Science, Merzenich lab) demonstration that basal-forebrain cholinergic activity is what ENABLES adult cortical plasticity: pairing a tone with nucleus basalis stimulation drives massive auditory-cortex remapping, while the same acoustic input without NB activation does not. This is the direct biological referent for the OPENING-side gate MECH-398 proposes -- a basal-forebrain ACh signal that gates whether sensory input is incorporated into long-term cortical representation. Held at 0.80 (not higher) because the transfer is from a phasic electrical-stimulation paradigm in rat AI to an algorithmic learning-rate scalar in REE; the mapping is to the abstract gating role, not the cholinergic pharmacology.
failure_signatures: Receptive fields were narrowed, broadened, or left unchanged depending on the acoustic parameters paired with NB activation -- the gate does not impose a fixed plasticity direction; it licenses input-driven change. A REE gain scalar that merely scales a single global learning rate (rather than letting the paired input shape WHAT is learned) would under-represent this: the biology gates plasticity ON, the content of the change still comes from the input stream.

Plasticity required PAIRING (NB activation coincident with the stimulus); NB stimulation alone or stimulus alone did not remap. A REE gate driven by a state scalar that is not temporally bound to the to-be-learned input would mislocalise plasticity -- the gating must be coincident with the encoder's exposure to the input it should incorporate.

entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical review (Nat Rev Neurosci, Hensch) establishing that critical-period TIMING is set by the functional maturation of a specific PV-positive inhibitory interneuron subset, with structural consolidation via extracellular-matrix (PNN) reorganization. This is the direct grounding for MECH-399 (a PV-analog maturation clock that lowers the plasticity-gain ceiling) and for Q-072 (layer-specificity: different cortical areas have distinct critical-period timings). Held at 0.80 as a review rather than a single primary result, but it is the field-defining synthesis and the closure mechanism is exceptionally well replicated.
failure_signatures: Closure timing is set by INHIBITORY (PV) maturation, not by a simple clock or by excitatory LTP/LTD -- Hensch notes canonical homosynaptic-plasticity models at excitatory synapses alone fail to predict in vivo critical-period manipulations. A REE closure clock (MECH-399) implemented as a pure time-since-onset accumulator, decoupled from any inhibitory-maturation / E-I-balance analogue, would be biologically unfaithful in the same way those excitatory-only models were.

Critical periods are area-specific (visual, auditory, somatosensory differ in timing) and are a CONTINUUM of local-circuit computations ending in structural consolidation, not a single binary switch. A single global REE plasticity-gain clock would contradict this -- the biology argues for the per-substrate / layer-specific resolution Q-072 raises, and against MECH-334's current binary on_phase3_entry transition as the final word.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong (Nat Neurosci) causal demonstration that the plasticity window is RE-OPENABLE in adulthood: environmental enrichment restored visual acuity and ocular dominance in adult amblyopic rats, via reduced GABAergic inhibition, increased BDNF, and reduced perineuronal-net density -- and benzodiazepine inhibition-enhancement PREVENTED it. 'Mixed' because it SUPPORTS the continuous re-openable gain reading (ARC-093) and grounds the BDNF duration knob (MECH-400) while WEAKENING any binary/irreversible closure assumption. Held at 0.76: a clean adult-reopening result, but a multi-factor manipulation (enrichment) where the gain channel is inferred from the molecular correlates rather than directly gated.
failure_signatures: Closure is REVERSIBLE: an adult intervention reduced inhibition and reopened a window thought permanently shut. A REE model treating crystallization (INV-074/MECH-334) as strictly one-way and irreversible would be biologically incomplete -- the biology keeps a re-opening pathway (lower inhibition / raise BDNF / strip PNNs), which is the gain knob (ARC-093) and duration knob (MECH-400) acting in the closure-recovery direction.

The reopening was a CONFOUNDED multi-factor effect (enrichment simultaneously lowered GABA, raised BDNF, reduced PNNs); the causal weight of each factor is not separable here. A REE design that attributes reopening to a single BDNF-analog duration knob (MECH-400) would over-claim specificity relative to what this paper isolates -- it shows the factors co-move, not that BDNF alone is the lever.

An explicit computational model whose functional form is near-identical to MECH-436: a cached, previously-learned incentive value modulated multiplicatively on-the-fly by a physiological-state gain factor (kappa-like), so that cue-triggered 'wanting' rises with the relevant appetite even without re-learning. Mapping fidelity is unusually high for an architectural/mechanism claim, which is weighted heavily; source is a foundational, well-cited model paper, knocked slightly because it is a model validated against existing electrophysiology rather than a fresh empirical test, and the transfer from rat mesolimbic Pavlovian cues to REE's coarse per-axis drive vector carries moderate risk.
failure_signatures: The state-modulation is multiplicative on a cached learned value, not additive: if REE's per-object incentive token has near-zero learned base_value the drive term cannot move the argmax (matches the V3-EXQ-514q in-run finding that a tiny per-axis drive spread cannot flip an object-score-dominated most_wanted).

Dynamic enhancement in the model is cue-SPECIFIC (raises salience of the appropriate CS without changing others); a REE implementation that applies a single scalar drive gain across all candidate objects would not reproduce the modelled selectivity.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct empirical demonstration of the exact dissociation MECH-436 names: ventral-pallidum firing to a salt-predicting cue is recomputed upward the instant the animal enters a salt-depletion state, before the salt has ever been tasted as 'liked' -- wanting is modulated by drive state independently of, and even opposite to, the liking history. Rigorous single-unit work in a high-quality venue; discounted for single-axis (sodium) scope and the rat-VP-to-REE transfer.
failure_signatures: The drive-state amplification was selective to the salt cue and immediate (first re-encounter, in extinction, before tasting) -- a REE mechanism that requires re-learning, or that spreads gain non-selectively, would not match.

The effect was demonstrated for a single, strong appetite (sodium depletion driving a large value swing); it does not establish that small or graded multi-axis drive differences produce a measurable wanting shift, which is the regime where V3-EXQ-514q found the effect collapsing.

entries.confidence_rationale: Behavioural + Fos demonstration that incentive salience attaches to a SPECIFIC, discrete object-cue (a particular inserted lever) and is REVALUABLE on the fly -- a previously-repulsive object becomes an avidly-approached motivational magnet at first re-encounter in a new state. This grounds two of SD-057's pillars: object-specific binding of incentive value, and the revaluability of the per-object token (MECH-345). Discounted because the revaluation here is driven by physiological state, so it partly overlaps MECH-436's territory rather than isolating the object-binding architecture cleanly.
failure_signatures: The object-specific incentive transformation was driven by a physiological state change (sodium depletion); the paper does not isolate object-binding from drive-state modulation, so it cannot by itself distinguish SD-057's per-object token from MECH-436's drive gain acting on a single value.
Behaviour was directed at one discrete lever-cue; the competitive selection of a most-wanted object AMONG several simultaneously-represented object tokens (SD-057's argmax-seed step) is not tested.

entries.confidence_rationale: Causal (dopamine-antagonist + fast-scan voltammetry) demonstration that incentive salience is a SEPARATE quantity from predictive value, and that it can be attributed to a discrete object-cue (the lever) versus the reward LOCATION (the food cup) -- the sign-tracker/goal-tracker split. This is the strongest available biological grounding for SD-057's central architectural move: separate goal-object (what) from goal-location (where) and bind a revaluable incentive quantity to the object identity. High source quality; mapping is conceptually strong but indirect (the paper studies individual-differences phenotypes, not an explicit per-object incentive layer).
failure_signatures: Whether incentive salience attaches to the object-cue (sign-tracking) or the goal-location (goal-tracking) is an individual-differences phenotype in this work, not a within-agent per-object layer -- so the paper supports the SEPARABILITY of object-incentive from location-prediction but does not by itself license a single architecture that maintains a per-object incentive token for every object.

Incentive-salience attribution here required dopamine-dependent learning over training; an REE per-object token that is seeded or revalued without a corresponding learning signal would diverge from this mechanism.

Causal circuit-perturbation evidence in transgenic rats that LOCUS COERULEUS (noradrenergic) input into ACC gates the switch between a strategic (model-based) mode and a STOCHASTIC (variable/exploratory) mode, and that the stochastic mode is engaged specifically under uncertainty about environmental rules (when counter-prediction cannot win) and otherwise suppressed. This is the single strongest anchor for the CDQ-002 refinement: the noradrenergic exploration signal is STATE-CONDITIONED (gated on uncontrollability/uncertainty) and SELF-ANNEALING (suppressed when a model-based strategy suffices). Causal (not merely correlational) and directly about the LC-NE -> action-variability pathway. Held at 0.82 for rodent->REE transfer and because 'stochastic mode' is a discrete gate rather than a graded per-parameter floor.
failure_signatures: If REE's tonic noise floor is implemented as an always-on, state-independent term (current MECH-313), it contradicts Tervo et al.: biologically the noradrenergic variability signal is GATED on environmental uncertainty/uncontrollability and suppressed when model-based strategy works, rather than applied uniformly.

Tervo's stochastic mode IGNORES action-outcome associations when engaged; a noise floor that perturbs selection without this gating could degrade exploitation in controllable regimes -- the REE falsifier must show the floor self-anneals where the policy is competent.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily-cited integrative theory grounded in monkey neurophysiology + modeling. Directly states the tonic LC-NE mode (the noise-floor substrate MECH-313 names) is engaged when task utility WANES and the phasic mode (exploitation) when decision utility is high, with ACC/OFC monitoring utility and driving the mode. This grounds a STATE-CONDITIONED, utility-modulated tonic exploration signal -- which is the biological warrant for refining MECH-313 toward NoisyNet's state-dependent, self-annealing noise. Confidence held below 0.85 because it is a review/theory (not a single decisive experiment) and because it supports the state-conditioned REFINEMENT, not MECH-313's currently-registered state-INDEPENDENT form.
failure_signatures: MECH-313 as registered describes a STATE-INDEPENDENT noise floor; Aston-Jones & Cohen's adaptive-gain theory holds that the LC-NE tonic exploration signal is itself conditioned on (and modulated by) task utility, so a state-independent floor is a biologically incomplete instantiation of the LC-NE mechanism MECH-313 cites.

entries.confidence_rationale: Landmark human fMRI study showing frontopolar cortex (and intraparietal sulcus) is preferentially active during decisions classified as EXPLORATORY (vs striatum/vmPFC for exploitative value-based choice), with choices fit by a computationally principled explore/exploit strategy. Grounds the ARC-065 substrate (b) frontopolar uncertainty-driven curiosity that MECH-314 names. Secondary to the MECH-313 primary; held at 0.72 because the paper establishes a DIRECTED-exploration neural substrate in general, not specifically the model-disagreement / learning-progress computational form (RND/Plan2Explore) the CDQ-002 secondary imports.
failure_signatures: Daw et al. localise exploration to frontopolar cortex but do not show the exploratory drive is computed as model-disagreement / prediction-error novelty; if MECH-314 is implemented specifically as RND/ensemble-disagreement, the biological mapping is to 'uncertainty-driven frontopolar exploration' generally, and the disagreement-specific form is a computational choice not directly evidenced here.

entries.confidence_rationale: A basal-ganglia dynamical model in which a double winner-take-all selects exactly ONE action, and learning drives a transition from an exploratory (random-action) phase to a STABLE DIRECTED phase where the agent always picks the single correct action. This is the biologically-faithful behavior of the selection gate -- diversity does NOT survive the commit; it collapses to one winner as the reward gradient strengthens. Directly weakens the reading that a per-niche-elite archive operates AT the committed argmax, and corroborates that F-dominance (MECH-439 winner-take-all collapse) is the gate's correct behavior. Moderate confidence: it is a model, and it weakens the at-argmax framing specifically, not the upstream-archive framing.
failure_signatures: The basal-ganglia selection gate is a winner-take-all that resolves to a SINGLE action and, with learning, collapses from exploratory-random to stable-directed (always one action) -- so committed-action diversity does NOT survive the selection gate; it must be preserved upstream of it.

F-dominance / single-optimum collapse at the commit (REE MECH-439) is the biologically CORRECT behavior of the selection gate, not a pathology to be fixed AT the gate -- which constrains MECH-442 to an upstream / eligible-set-restriction mechanism rather than an at-argmax per-niche store.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong, clean lesion dissociation in a well-controlled songbird system: a dedicated basal-ganglia-forebrain circuit (LMAN/AFP) generates and actively regulates behavioral variability SEPARATELY from the motor output pathway. Maps faithfully onto the MECH-442 claim that committed-action diversity is maintained by a structure distinct from the value-maximizing selector. Transfer risk is moderate (songbird vocal motor system to a grid-world E3 committed-selection locus is an analogy, not a homology), which caps confidence below 0.8.
failure_signatures: LMAN regulates variability of syllable STRUCTURE but not of syllable SEQUENCING -- the variability-generating circuit is content-specific, so a single 'behavioral-descriptor archive' may not cover all axes of behavioral diversity uniformly.

The variability circuit is upstream of / parallel to the premotor output, not an at-the-selection-gate per-niche structure -- so it does not directly evidence a per-niche-elite mechanism AT the committed argmax.

entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative review (Annu Rev Neurosci) consolidating human + animal evidence that motor variability is a regulated FEATURE -- purposeful exploration of behavior space that, coupled with reinforcement, drives learning -- not unwanted noise. Maps with high fidelity onto the MECH-442 premise that behavioral diversity must be actively maintained (not a side-effect) to be useful. Caps below 0.8 because it grounds the necessity-and-regulation of diversity, not the specific archive-survives-the-commit-gate mechanism.
failure_signatures: Variability is framed as exploration of motor space coupled to reinforcement, which is a noise-then-select picture (generate-and-reinforce), NOT a per-niche-elite archive that survives selection -- so it supports diversity-must-be-maintained without endorsing the specific MAP-Elites structure.
The review notes variability is regulated structurally (task-dependent, dimension-specific), which warns that a single uniform behavioral-descriptor may be the wrong granularity.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality cellular recording + lesion study (Cell, Datta/Sabatini) showing the dorsolateral striatum encodes the identity and ordering of a discrete repertoire of sub-second 3D behavioral motifs and is required to assemble them into sequences. Directly evidences a structured behavioral-MODULE repertoire that the basal ganglia selects over -- the closest biological analog to MECH-442's behavioral-descriptor archive. Capped because the result is about sequence COMPOSITION over a module set, not per-niche-elite preservation against a value argmax.
failure_signatures: The striatum encodes module identity/ordering and assembles sequences, but the paper does not show per-niche-elite preservation through a value-maximizing selection -- it evidences a repertoire + selection-over-it, not diversity surviving a strong reward gradient.

Module selection here is facilitated by fast direct/indirect-pathway decorrelation (a competitive gating), consistent with a winner-take-all commit rather than simultaneous multi-niche retention at the output.

entries.confidence_rationale: Computational/theoretical model formalizing the songbird two-stage architecture: a basal-ganglia tutor circuit (LMAN) injects exploratory variability AND a corrective bias, gradually consolidated into a separate motor (RA) student circuit. Supports the architectural separation of a variability/diversity generator from the committed motor output -- the structural premise behind locating MECH-442's archive upstream of / parallel to the commit. Capped because it is a model (not a measurement) and addresses tutor-student consolidation, not per-niche-elite retention.
failure_signatures: The diversity here is a variability-injection-plus-corrective-bias mechanism (explore then consolidate), not a per-niche-elite archive that survives selection -- so it supports the generator/selector separation, not the specific MAP-Elites structure.

Mismatches between the tutor (variability) signal and the student plasticity rule impair learning -- a warning that an REE diversity-injection coupled to the committed selector must be matched to the downstream learning rule or it degrades performance.

entries.confidence_rationale: A balanced review establishing that replay content is NOT a faithful re-run of dominant prior experience: it is biased toward reward, can run forward to guide future behaviour, and includes non-experienced / recombined sequences. This undercuts the premise that replay must reinforce already-dominant trajectory classes, and supports Q-055 counter-mechanism (b) that replay may be designed to sample/recombine rather than concentrate. Confidence 0.55 because it is a conceptual review (not a quantitative diversity measurement) and the same flexibility could in principle be neutral for diversity.
failure_signatures: Replay is not a veridical replay of the most-traversed path: it over-represents rewarded locations and can generate forward, recombined, or never-experienced sequences -- so a simple 'replay strengthens the dominant trace' erosion model is too crude.
Because replay can be generative/recombinative, sleep could in principle INCREASE trajectory-class diversity, the opposite of the winner-take-all worry.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the most direct literature evidence for the Q-055 erosion mechanism: in a multi-memory setting, selectively augmenting replay of one trace actively INTERFERES with consolidation of the others, and the weak memories are hit hardest. That is precisely the dynamic by which sleep could erode behavioural diversity if replay is biased toward dominant trajectory classes. Held below 0.7 because it is simulation, the 'memories' are discrete cued traces rather than a continuum of trajectory classes, and the interference is shown under exogenous cueing rather than spontaneous replay.
failure_signatures: Selectively augmenting one memory's replay during SWS interferes with consolidation of competing memories, with WEAK memories preferentially disadvantaged -- a direct competitive-interference route to diversity erosion.
The benefit is phase-gated (Down-to-Up transition); off-phase reactivation has little effect, so whichever traces happen to align with the optimal phase are strengthened at the expense of others.

entries.confidence_rationale: The cleanest counter-evidence to the Q-055 erosion hypothesis, and in humans: across wake, weak memories decay fastest, but a nap ATTENUATES that effect until forgetting rates are equalised across encoding strengths, with fast spindle density predicting the rescue of weak items specifically. If sleep selectively protects the weak/under-represented traces, its net effect on a diverse population would be DIVERSITY-PRESERVING, not winner-take-all. Confidence 0.70: strong human design with a physiological correlate, but it measures declarative word-pair retention, not behavioural trajectory diversity, so the mapping is by analogy.
failure_signatures: Contradicts a naive winner-take-all reading of sleep replay: sleep preferentially rescues WEAK traces rather than amplifying strong ones, so the net population-level effect can equalise rather than concentrate.

Effect is specific to weak items (spindles did not correlate with intermediate or strong item memory), so sleep's protective action is targeted at exactly the traces a diversity-erosion account predicts would be lost.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong, mechanistically explicit thalamocortical model directly showing that SWS slow oscillations + STDP convert hippocampal ripple input into PREFERENTIAL replay and persistent strengthening of specific cortical sequences. This is the substrate that MECH-120 invokes for the diversity-erosion arm of Q-055. Confidence held below 0.7 because it is a simulation (not behaviour), it does not measure diversity across a population of distinct trajectory classes, and 'preferential strengthening of one trace' does not by itself establish net erosion of the others.
failure_signatures: Hippocampal ripple input delivered during the slow oscillation produces input-SPECIFIC, persistent synaptic potentiation that biases subsequent replay toward the stimulated sequence -- the mechanistic basis for a winner-take-all drift if one trajectory class dominates the ripple input.
The model strengthens whichever sequence the ripple input carries; it provides no intrinsic mechanism that protects under-represented sequences from relative weakening.

entries.confidence_rationale: Provides the biological grounding for MECH-343: a basal-ganglia model in which striatal pathways estimate reward mean AND variance and transient dopaminergic novelty signals drive DIRECTED (uncertainty-conditioned) exploration, which outperforms undirected and classic UCB strategies in simulation and fits behaviour. Supports the principle that exploration should be gated to a state signal rather than applied uniformly. Held to ~0.58 because the gating signal is novelty/value-uncertainty rather than goal-difficulty/stuck-state, and it is bandit-style choice rather than the sequential blocked-path setting of Q-056.
failure_signatures: Directed (uncertainty-gated) exploration outperforms undirected exploration and classic UCB in simulation -- undirected/uniform exploration is dominated.
The biological gating signal is transient novelty/value-variance, not difficulty or goal-blockage, so it does not directly evidence stuck-state gating.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct ML analogue of MECH-343's core prediction: a state-conditioned exploration signal f(s) tied to uncertainty outperforms the constant-exploration instance f(s)=c and other fixed-schedule exploration methods (RND, UCB, NoisyNets) on hard MuJoCo tasks. Strongly relevant to the 'gated entropy > always-high entropy' half of Q-056. Held to 0.60 because the paper does NOT include a pure no-exploration arm (so the 'gated > OFF' half is untested here), the gating signal is generic uncertainty rather than REE's specific difficulty/stuck-state signal, and there is no goal/harm-constraint structure as in MECH-343.
failure_signatures: Constant exploration f(s)=c is an internal control that the adaptive (state-conditioned) variants beat -- evidence that always-on fixed exploration is dominated by conditional exploration.
Tested only on dense-reward MuJoCo; authors flag sparse-reward domains as untested, which is closer to REE's hard-goal/blocked-path regime.

entries.confidence_rationale: Important nuance for MECH-343: in humans, exploration IS modulated by uncertainty (supporting state-gated exploration over a fixed rate), but it is driven by a DILEMMA between an information-seeking motive and an avoid-the-unknown (danger) motive -- and the authors explicitly note prior evidence for uncertainty-driven exploration is mixed. This both supports the gating principle and warns that more-exploration-when-uncertain is not unconditionally adaptive, which maps onto MECH-343's harm/safety constraint. Confidence ~0.52: conceptually on-point human+simulation work, but older, restless-bandit paradigm, and indirect with respect to difficulty/stuck-state gating specifically.
failure_signatures: The evidence for uncertainty-driven exploration is explicitly described as MIXED -- a caution against assuming always-high or monotone-with-uncertainty exploration is optimal.

An avoid-the-unknown (danger) motive can SUPPRESS exploration under uncertainty, so a naive 'explore more when stuck' policy can be maladaptive when the unknown is hazardous -- directly relevant to MECH-343's no-harm-increase requirement.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality recent review in a specialist journal directly addressing how engram cells change in encoding/consolidation/retrieval from development to adulthood across hippocampus + cortical/thalamic partners. Supports Q-057's core framing that a memory trace passes through developmental gates before it can be reliably consolidated and retrieved. Confidence held below source quality because the paper is descriptive about WHICH gates exist; it does not isolate a single-cue-authority vs convergent-weak-input recall mechanism, so the mapping to the specific REE sub-question is interpretive.
failure_signatures: The review states that, compared with adults, much less is known about how or to what extent early-life memories undergo consolidation -- so any REE claim that fixes a specific developmental gate ordering is currently under-constrained by the biology.

Engram persistence depends on coordinated activity across hippocampus, retrosplenial cortex, mPFC and anterior thalamus; a single-region (CA3-only) account of cue-authority maturation may be incomplete.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong causal optogenetic evidence that infant memory traces are stored but become naturally inaccessible -- an artificial (optogenetic) cue recovers them when the natural cue cannot. This directly evidences Q-057's sub-question (1) (immature cue-authority: trace exists, natural cue lacks authority to release it) and sub-question (3) (a developmental gate stands between an encoded trace and its ability to drive behaviour). Confidence is solid for the storage-vs-retrieval dissociation; held below 0.8 because 'optogenetic recovery' is a non-physiological cue and the REE mapping to convergent-weak-input recall is interpretive.
failure_signatures: The natural retrieval cue failed to release the infant memory even though the trace was intact -- a pure cue-authority failure, not a storage failure; any REE account that attributes early cue-authority loss to absent storage would be falsified by this.
Recovery required broad reactivation of tagged hippocampal AND cortical ensembles, implying the missing ingredient is distributed reinstatement, not a single-cue CA3 readout.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical review proposing the 'memory resolution' hypothesis: broadly-tuned immature young neurons contribute different information than highly specific mature neurons. This is the cleanest literature analogue of Q-057's single-cue (broad/immature) vs convergent-weak-input (specific/mature) recall distinction, and it frames maturation as a change in recall specificity. Confidence moderate: it is a conceptual/theoretical review (2011), the maturation axis is at the cell level (young vs mature neurons), not whole-system development, and the mapping to REE cue-authority is interpretive.
failure_signatures: The paper notes a persistent reconciliation problem -- the 'pattern separation' tested behaviourally does not match the computational/electrophysiological conception -- so importing 'pattern separation/completion' vocabulary into REE without operational care risks the same equivocation.
Resolution is framed as a continuum of neuronal tuning width, not a discrete developmental gate; an REE account that posits a sharp gate before action-release may over-discretise a graded property.

entries.confidence_rationale: Classic dissociation showing that active inhibition (engaged specifically by competitive RECALL) produces forgetting that mere strengthening/re-exposure does not -- evidence that inhibition and strength-based competition are distinct mechanisms with distinct consequences. Directly supports Q-058's second sub-question (inhibition vs competition are not the same thing) and its third (the mechanism is engaged context-specifically, in the act of recall). Confidence moderate: human behavioural psychology, single classic study, indirect mapping to REE inter-field couplings.
failure_signatures: Strengthening practiced items (re-exposure) did NOT impair competitors, but competitive recall did -- so an REE model that treats competition purely as relative-strength normalisation (softmax) will MISS the inhibitory suppression that only appears when the loser is actively retrieved against.
The inhibitory effect is recall-specific: it is engaged by the act of retrieval, implying competition modes are not interchangeable across waking-action vs passive/offline regimes.

entries.confidence_rationale: First major meta-analysis directly adjudicating the inhibition vs non-inhibition (strength competition / blocking) accounts of retrieval-induced forgetting. Results LARGELY support inhibition but also surface challenging evidence, with outcome depending on how RIF is measured. This is exactly the calibration Q-058 needs: it confirms inhibition is a distinct, real mechanism, while warning the distinction is not absolute. Marked 'mixed' to faithfully represent the meta-analytic verdict; high source quality (quantitative meta-analysis) gives reasonable confidence.
failure_signatures: The inhibition account is supported on average but not universally -- the result varies with how RIF is assessed (e.g. cue-independence tests), so a binary REE design decision ('always use an explicit inhibitory edge') would over-read the evidence.

Some findings are explicable by non-inhibitory mechanisms (strength-based competition/blocking), so REE cannot assume every observed competitive interaction requires a signed inhibitory coupling rather than local softmax.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly on Q-058's first and second sub-questions: it formalises competition-through-shared-inhibition (soft WTA) and derives the parameter ranges where coupled competitive modules are stable vs where strong positive feedback risks instability. This is exactly the 'which couplings need an explicit sign vs local softmax/WTA, and what is the safety cost' question. High mapping fidelity to the computational claim; confidence held below 0.8 because it is a stability-theory/simulation paper, not a biological measurement, and it does not address decommitment or residue-based veto specifically.
failure_signatures: There is a critical trade-off: feedback strong enough to support selective amplification/decision-making is also strong enough to threaten stability -- so an REE design that simply strengthens competitive coupling to force conversion can drive the network into multistable/runaway persistent states.

Stability of a LARGE network of interconnected WTA modules is not guaranteed by stability of one module; coupling many competitive fields together can destabilise even when each field is individually well-behaved.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the biology anchor already named on the MECH-044 registration. The paper's thesis -- the hippocampus is obligatorily involved in binding disparate elements across space and time AND in the comparison of relational representations, operating online (hippocampal responses within the first ~100 ms of stimulus onset, during traditional perceptual-processing time, and with or without conscious awareness) -- is a near-paraphrase of MECH-044's claim that hippocampal systems do relational work inside the perception-action loop rather than only long-term storage. Mapping fidelity is high. Source is a synthesis/proposal review (not a single primary dataset), and the transfer from human/primate MTL to REE's engineered hippocampal-analog module is real, so confidence is held below 0.8.

The proposal that binding/comparison proceeds 'with or without conscious awareness' is the part most contested in the wider literature; if relational binding turned out to strictly require explicit, attention-gated encoding, the online perception-loop reading REE relies on would weaken.

entries.confidence_rationale: Empirical (not review) human data using the transitivity paradigm: amnesic case DA, with significant hippocampal damage, could not learn arbitrary relations (A->B, B->C, ...) and could not flexibly infer novel relations (A->C?), while older adults showed a milder relational deficit partly rescued by pre-experimental knowledge. entries.confidence_rationale: A normative theory, fit to rodent replay data, that derives exactly the two quantities MECH-443/MECH-444 posit: replay is ordered by UTILITY = gain x need, not uniformly. entries.confidence_rationale: The principled counterweight. Direct recordings, clean revaluation design.
failure_signatures: Replay content moved AWAY from the currently most-valuable outcome, falsifying any MECH-443 implementation that equates priority with reward magnitude or current behavioural preference.
The dissociation between behaviour (toward restricted outcome) and replay (away from it) means a REE priority signal read off the action-value of the committed policy would point the wrong way.

Targeted single-entry addition for MECH-446 (de-commit-authority MAGNITUDE), recommended by the claim-synthesis decomposition spec (claim_synthesis_SD-034-closure_2026-06-19.md Section 5.2 Child B). Cavanagh, Frank et al. 2011 (Nat Neurosci 14:1462-1467) is the sharpest available anchor for the SPECIFIC MECH-446 form 'the brake magnitude scales with re-commitment / conflict pressure': mediofrontal theta (a conflict signal) raises the decision threshold proportionally to decision conflict, and subthalamic-nucleus DBS REVERSES that mediofrontal influence over the threshold -- demonstrating a graded, causally-manipulable hold whose strength tracks conflict rather than a fixed binary gate. This grounds the 'committed-run-scaled refractory' magnitude lever (a long committed run / high re-commitment pressure should trigger a proportionally stronger/longer de-commit). Held at 0.72 (below the Mayr & Keele 2000 backward-inhibition entry's 0.84) because (a) the STN brake is studied on conflict-graded RESPONSE-THRESHOLD modulation during decision-making, which is conceptually adjacent to but not identical with the post-COMPLETION de-commit refractory MECH-446 specifies; (b) the magnitude-scaling-with-committed-run-length form is the natural reading of conflict-graded release, not a directly measured 'scales with prior commitment duration' result; (c) the substrate is human EEG + DBS in Parkinson's patients, a transfer step from the REE closure-plane. NON-BLOCKING: MECH-446's magnitude form is already grounded by Mayr & Keele 2000 (post-completion refractory strength); this entry sharpens the scales-with-pressure component.

The 'magnitude scales with committed-run length' form (a long committed run triggers a proportionally long de-commit) is the REE-side engineering reading; Cavanagh & Frank measure scaling with trial-by-trial decision CONFLICT, not with the duration of a prior commitment. The mapping from 'conflict pressure' to 'committed-run length' is an inference, flagged as transfer risk.

Evidence is human scalp EEG + intraoperative/therapeutic STN-DBS in Parkinson's patients. The localisation (mediofrontal cortex -> STN hyperdirect pathway) is a basal-ganglia brake, consistent with REE's MECH-090/MECH-260 BG-analog locus, but the closure-operator's OFC/ACC completion-detection side is not what this paper measures.

This is the canonical 'optimal decision threshold' paper (the Bogacz seed line). It shows the cortico-basal-ganglia circuit, with the STN computing a normalization term across ALL competing channels, exactly implements the multihypothesis sequential probability ratio test (MSPRT) -- the asymptotically optimal test for choosing among N alternatives. It is MIXED for MECH-439: it strongly SUPPORTS the framing that the BG bottleneck is fundamentally about arbitrating one channel against the WHOLE competing field (the F-monopoly is precisely a failure to normalize F against the field), but it WEAKENS the specific top-k operationalisation. The biologically-optimal STN operation is a CONTINUOUS GLOBAL NORMALIZATION over all alternatives, not a discrete near-ties shortlist truncation. By MSPRT, the principled lever is a rank-preserving renormalization of F against the competing scores -- i.e. the cluster autopsy's Reading-2 (direct F-variance rebalancing / F->eligibility demotion) -- with k=f(F-gap) as a coarse local approximation that acts only at near-ties. So the strongest biological theory of BG decision making points PAST the proposed top-k fix toward the alternative lever, which is the load-bearing finding.
failure_signatures: MSPRT optimality requires the STN to normalize each channel against the SUM over ALL alternatives on every step (a continuous global term); k=f(F-gap) only widens a discrete set at near-ties and performs no global renormalization, so it is a local approximation that cannot recover the optimal computation when F dominates the global sum -- the regime MECH-439 targets.

Under MSPRT the decision quantity is a likelihood RATIO (each option normalized by the field), so a single score that dominates the field stays dominant after normalization unless its variance/scale is itself rebalanced; this is the formal statement that near-ties set-widening cannot fix an F-monopoly and that rank-preserving F demotion (Reading-2) is the biologically-principled lever.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the causal empirical keystone for the conflict-graded decision-threshold mechanism MECH-439's fix translates, and it carries the 'Cohen' seed author. In humans, trial-to-trial increases in mediofrontal activity (EEG theta, 4-8 Hz) raised the decision threshold (evidence-accumulation bound, via drift-diffusion fits) as a FUNCTION OF CONFLICT; deep brain stimulation of the STN REVERSED this relationship, producing impulsive choice; and intracranial STN-area recordings showed increased slow-band activity during the same high-conflict decisions. So the cortico-STN conflict-graded hold is not merely simulated (Frank 2006) -- it is causally demonstrated and direction-specific (disrupt STN -> lose the conflict-dependent threshold raise -> premature commitment). That is direct support for the dependency MECH-439 names as missing. Held below 0.8 by the same temporal-bound-vs-discrete-set divergence as Frank 2006, plus a binary-choice-vs-many-action-classes scope gap (the threshold here is a two-alternative DDM bound, not a multi-class shortlist width).
failure_signatures: The measured threshold is a two-alternative drift-diffusion bound; REE's committed-action-diversity problem is over many action classes. A mechanism that raises a scalar binary bound need not widen a multi-class consideration set -- the empirical support is for the conflict->threshold link, not for the specific top-k set-widening operationalisation.

STN DBS reversing the mediofrontal-threshold relationship shows the hold is NECESSARY for conflict-dependent caution; it does not show that adding such a hold to an otherwise F-dominated selector SUFFICES to produce committed-action diversity -- necessity in the lesion direction does not establish sufficiency in the enrichment direction MECH-439 needs.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the foundational fMRI paper localising the STN to response inhibition and coining the 'hyperdirect' (right-IFC -> STN) hypothesis -- the Aron & Poldrack seed line and the source of the 'hold' / global-NoGo primitive in MECH-439's scope. It grounds the EXISTENCE and anatomy of the hyperdirect hold: the STN suppresses thalamocortical output to block response execution, and Stop-related STN activity scales with inhibition speed. It is MIXED because the mechanism it characterises is a GLOBAL, NON-SELECTIVE BRAKE (cancel ALL responses), which is the OPPOSITE of conflict-graded widening of the consideration set. MECH-439's fix is GRADED (k scales with the F-gap), aligning with the Frank/Cavanagh conflict-threshold lineage, NOT with Aron's all-or-none global stop. So Aron & Poldrack supports that the hyperdirect HOLD primitive is real and STN-mediated, while flagging that REE's GRADED use is a refinement of (not identical to) the canonical global-NoGo -- a load-bearing distinction, because a blunt global brake would suppress diversity, not create it.
failure_signatures: The canonical hyperdirect signal is a GLOBAL NoGo that cancels all responses non-selectively; applied naively to E3 it would suppress the committed action entirely (a freeze), not widen the consideration set -- the graded k=f(F-gap) is required precisely because the raw Aron global-stop is the wrong primitive for generating diversity.

Aron & Poldrack localise the hold to a STOPPING context (an external stop signal), not to value/conflict-graded action selection among competing GO options; transferring the hyperdirect hold from reactive stopping to graded committed-selection requires the Frank/Cavanagh conflict-threshold bridge and is not directly evidenced here.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical computational model of the exact mechanism MECH-439's proposed fix translates: the subthalamic nucleus (STN), driven by cortical response conflict, dynamically raises the response threshold via the cortico-subthalamic-pallidal (hyperdirect) pathway, and this matters MOST when there are multiple competing responses. That is the qualitative content of the conflict-graded hold k=f(F-gap) -- small top-score gap (near-tie / high conflict) widens the consideration window so a non-dominant stream can still win. Confidence is held below 0.8 by one load-bearing structural divergence: Frank's STN raises a CONTINUOUS, TEMPORAL threshold (it buys time within a within-trial evidence accumulator), whereas REE's lever widens a DISCRETE consideration set (top-k) at a single commit step with no within-trial temporal accumulation. The biology's hold helps only because more evidence accrues during the delay and can overturn the leading option; REE's set-widening helps only if a modulatory channel can outweigh F WITHIN the shortlist scoring. Where F still dominates the shortlist (the 654g/625e failures), widening k does not move the argmax -- precisely the gap the divergence predicts.
failure_signatures: Frank's STN hold buys TIME on a within-trial accumulator so that additional evidence can overturn the leading option; REE's E3 commit step has no within-trial temporal accumulation, so substituting top-k set-width for a temporal hold only helps if a non-F channel already outscores F within the shortlist -- where F monopolises the shortlist scoring (654g seed-44 byte-identical, 625e monostrategy) the analog of the hold is inert.

The model's benefit is contingent on there being multiple genuinely-competing cortical responses at near-equal strength; if one score (F) dominates the cortical input itself, the cortico-STN conflict signal is small and the threshold is never raised -- the diversity ceiling re-appears one level upstream, in the conflict signal, not just at the argmax.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily-cited review establishing the framework that beta-band activity/coupling indexes maintenance of the current sensorimotor or cognitive state, expressed more strongly when the status quo is intended or PREDICTED than when change is expected. This directly motivates MECH-445's mechanism shape -- a closure event (which predicts that the just-completed state should be held) elevating a beta-coupled latch. But it is a hypothesis review, not primary data, and it does not test the specific claim that a completion/closure signal drives latch elevation INDEPENDENT of an evidence-threshold commit. Mapping is analogical, so confidence is held to moderate.
failure_signatures: The review frames beta as maintaining whatever state currently obtains; it does not isolate a completion-triggered drive separable from ongoing evidence-based maintenance, so it cannot by itself adjudicate MECH-445's independence-from-natural-commit claim.

Pathologically enhanced beta produces 'abnormal persistence of the status quo' -- a caution that a closure->beta->latch path, if mis-tuned, predicts perseveration / failure to de-commit rather than adaptive holding.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct MEG+EMG empirical test (n=18) of whether beta activity/connectivity is sustained when a motor state is sustained. It is NOT: even during continuous isometric gripping, motor beta and cortico-muscular coupling occurred as short transient bursts, and sustained demand did not prolong beta-event duration. This qualifies MECH-445's 'beta coupling elevation' reading: a closure-driven latch elevation is unlikely to be a tonic beta level and must instead be cashed out as elevated burst RATE / coupling probability. Mixed rather than weakens, because the finding is fully compatible with a burst-rate implementation of the same mechanism -- it refutes only the naive tonic-maintenance reading.
failure_signatures: Motor beta and cortico-muscular beta connectivity were transient (short bursts) even when motor behaviour was sustained -- a tonic 'beta latch held high for the duration of commitment' reading of MECH-445 is not supported by the muscle-coupling data.

Sustained motor requirements did not prolong beta-event duration relative to rest, so 'closure elevates the latch' cannot be operationalised as 'closure lengthens a beta event'; it must be a change in burst rate / occupancy.

entries.confidence_rationale: Comparative ethological synthesis (Tinbergen's four questions: causation, survival value, ontogeny, phylogeny) of distress vocalisation. Crying is reconstructed as a primarily acoustic, GRADED signal that is a fairly reliable -- if imperfect -- indicator of need for care, whose primary function is to recruit caregiving, and which is subject to 'corruption through dishonesty'. This grounds the crying/distress-vocalisation half of Q-059 directly: distress vocalisation is a plausible guardrail counterpart to laughter, and -- like non-Duchenne laughter -- it is an honest-on-average signal with built-in spoofability. Held at moderate confidence because the paper is about infant-to-caregiver crying, not the adult social-field adjudication Q-059 ultimately concerns.
failure_signatures: Crying is a graded, honest-on-average signal with documented potential for dishonest exaggeration; a REE distress-vocalisation guardrail keyed on signal intensity alone would be exploitable the same way, so the guardrail must weight provenance/context, not just amplitude.

The signal's function is caregiver RECRUITMENT (an asymmetric care relationship), not symmetric peer social-field repair; importing it as a peer-level guardrail risks a category error about what relationship the signal regulates.

entries.confidence_rationale: Landmark synthetic review that establishes, as a load-bearing empirical distinction, that laughter is NOT a single monotone-affiliative signal: Duchenne (spontaneous, emotionally genuine, affiliative, contagion-promoting) versus non-Duchenne laughter, the latter co-opted for strategic, manipulative, and exclusionary uses -- the 'dark side' of laughter. This is precisely Q-059's premise that social laughter must be adjudicated as social-field repair vs damage/exclusion rather than treated as uniformly affiliative. Strong support for the QUESTION being well-posed; it does not, of course, tell REE whether to build the guardrail, only that the biological signal genuinely bifurcates.
failure_signatures: Because non-Duchenne laughter is volitional and co-optable, a REE laughter/affiliation analogue that scored all laughter as bond-positive would mis-handle exactly the exclusionary/dominance cases Q-059 flags -- the review documents that these cases are real and frequent, not edge artefacts.

Duchenne and non-Duchenne laughter share surface form but diverge in function and sincerity; any adjudicator keyed only on the acoustic/behavioural surface (not on provenance/context) will be systematically spoofable.

entries.confidence_rationale: Cross-species naturalistic review (de Waal co-author) arguing laughter is first and foremost a SOCIAL behaviour aimed at regulating social relationships -- easing social tensions and establishing social bonds -- decoupled from humour, with homologues in primates and rodents and a shared mirror-mechanism substrate for contagion. This directly supports the 'social-field repair' pole of Q-059 and reframes laughter's primitive function as relationship regulation rather than affect display, which is the framing a REE laughter/guardrail analogue would inherit. Weighted below the Gervais & Wilson entry because it emphasises the repair/bonding pole and says little about the damage/exclusion pole that makes adjudication necessary.
failure_signatures: If laughter's primitive function is relationship REGULATION (tension-easing, bond-forming), a REE analogue that models it only as a positive-affect emission misses the regulatory/contextual role and cannot represent when the same signal regulates a relationship downward (tension-raising, boundary-marking).

Contagion via a mirror mechanism means laughter spreads sub-deliberately; an REE social field with a contagious laughter analogue could propagate an exclusionary instance across agents before any adjudication stage runs, unless adjudication gates contagion.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical-computation anchor the cluster-autopsy Reading-2 needs: divisive normalization (a neuron's response divided by the summed activity of a normalization pool) recurs across V1 contrast, attention, multisensory integration AND value coding, so a 'renormalize the dominant channel against the field' lever is a documented canonical operation, not an ad hoc REE invention. It is MIXED for MECH-439 because the canonical computation has two properties that BOTH bear on the F-monopoly: (a) it is order-preserving and continuous-global -- which SUPPORTS rank-preserving F-renormalization over a discrete near-ties shortlist (the divisive ratio acts on every channel every step, not only at near-ties); but (b) it is pooled-SYMMETRIC (every unit, including the dominant one, is divided by the SAME field-built denominator) and order-PRESERVING on the numerators -- so canonical normalization, applied faithfully, KEEPS F the argmax. It compresses F's lead, it does not strip F's rank. The diversity lift therefore comes from range-compression-under-downstream-noise, NOT from F losing the commit; and REE's stronger proposed lever ('F removed from the final argmin, used as a graded eligibility envelope only') is rank-ALTERING and goes BEYOND the canonical computation. That asymmetry (pooled-symmetric divisive gain control vs single-score targeted demotion) is the load-bearing finding: the biology grounds a WEAKER, faithful version of Reading-2 (divide the whole score vector by a pooled denominator, keep a stochastic commit) whose efficacy is conditional on a downstream stochastic/temperature selection stage and on the pool composition.
failure_signatures: Canonical divisive normalization is order-preserving on the numerators: if F's drive exceeds every competitor's, F's normalized response still exceeds every competitor's. So pure Carandini-Heeger normalization, applied to REE's E3 score vector, leaves F the deterministic argmax -- it cannot by itself lift committed-action diversity. The lift requires a downstream stochastic/softmax commit whose temperature the (now compressed) F-vs-rest margin can fall below; under a hard deterministic argmax with no temperature, divisive normalization changes nothing.

The canonical computation is pooled-SYMMETRIC -- every option, F included, is divided by the SAME normalization-pool denominator. REE's proposed lever is asymmetric (demote ONLY F). A faithful divisive-norm lever must renormalize the WHOLE score vector, which compresses F's lead AND the modulatory channels' leads proportionally; the modulatory field's relative leverage rises only if the modulatory scores are EXCLUDED from (or down-weighted in) the normalization pool. Which scores enter the denominator is therefore load-bearing design, not a free choice -- get it wrong and normalization uniformly compresses everything without transferring authority to the modulatory field.

REE's stronger 'F out of the argmin / F as eligibility envelope only' operation is rank-ALTERING at the commit level (a non-F criterion picks among F-eligible candidates). That is NOT the canonical divisive computation (which is rank-preserving at every level); it needs separate justification (the quality-diversity / MAP-Elites side already filed for Child 3), and should not be claimed as 'biologically canonical' on the strength of this paper.

entries.confidence_rationale: This entry grounds the SECOND half of the autopsy diagnosis: not just that F must be renormalized, but WHERE a modulatory channel has to act to gain leverage over a normalized competition. Reynolds & Heeger show a single divisive-normalization circuit reproduces the full range of attentional effects (response-gain vs contrast-gain) depending on the size of the attention field relative to the stimulus, because attention enters by scaling the stimulus drive (numerator) BEFORE the pooled divisive normalization. The REE mapping: MECH-439's modulatory / within-class / rule-bias channels are floor-locked because they act as additive terms ON TOP of a raw dominant F; a control signal only converts to behaviour when it modulates the normalization itself (numerator gain or pool weighting), exactly as attention does here. It is MIXED because (a) it is an attention/sensory model -- transfer to a value selector leans on the canonical-computation generality claim; (b) the model is order-preserving, so attention biases the competition by changing GAIN, not by removing the dominant channel from the output -- reinforcing that the faithful REE lever is gain-on-the-normalization, not the asymmetric 'F out of the argmin'; (c) the response-gain-vs-contrast-gain reconciliation is a feature for REE (one mechanism, regime-dependent) but also a warning that the SAME modulatory input produces opposite effects depending on field/stimulus scale, so REE's modulatory leverage is regime-contingent, not guaranteed.
failure_signatures: Attention biases a normalized competition by scaling gain at the numerator/denominator, NOT by deleting the dominant channel -- the model is order-preserving. This reinforces that a modulatory channel cannot convert to committed diversity by being added on top of a raw dominant F; it must enter the normalization (numerator gain or normalization-pool weighting). REE's additive modulatory channels, which sit on top of an un-normalized F, are in the architecturally wrong place -- the 445h/485h/654g floor-lock signature.

The same attentional input produces response-gain OR contrast-gain depending on the size of the attention field relative to the stimulus. Transferred to REE, the same modulatory channel can have large or near-zero leverage on the committed action depending on the score-distribution regime (how concentrated F is, how many near-ties exist). Modulatory leverage is therefore regime-contingent, not a fixed property -- a tuning surface MECH-448's build must map, not assume.

This is a sensory-attention model; its application to a value/action selector rests on the canonical-computation generality claim (Carandini & Heeger), not on direct value-domain data. This is the canonical CAUSAL demonstration that the direct (D1, Go) and indirect (D2, No-Go) striatal pathways exert bidirectional, OPPONENT control over action: bilateral optogenetic excitation of indirect-pathway MSNs produced a parkinsonian state (increased freezing, bradykinesia, decreased locomotor initiation) while excitation of direct-pathway MSNs reduced freezing and increased locomotion, and direct-pathway activation rescued the 6-OHDA parkinsonian deficit. It is the strongest available grounding for ARC-107's claim that committed-action selection should be governed by bounded Go (promotion) and No-Go (suppression) pressures rather than by a single scalar, and it anchors the MECH-448 divergence: biology realises rank-alteration through TWO genuinely separate, oppositely-signed populations, not through a single divisively-normalised value scalar. Held below 0.8 by the species/modality transfer (mouse motor initiation vs REE's abstract committed-action-class selection) and because the paper measures gross movement vigour, not the specific 'a non-dominant value channel converts to committed action' phenomenon MECH-448/449 target.
failure_signatures: Kravitz shows Go and No-Go are SEPARATE, oppositely-signed neuronal populations whose balance sets behaviour; REE's current selector has no No-Go channel separate from the value scalar F (MECH-260 dACC suppression is channel-specific, not a bounded constitution), so the biological opponency is exactly the structure ARC-107 must add and the current argmin lacks.

The effect is on motor vigour / movement gating (freeze vs locomote), one level coarser than 'which committed action class wins'; a paper this coarse cannot, on its own, validate that a Go/No-Go constitution recovers committed-action-class DIVERSITY rather than just toggling action on/off -- that discriminant is what the REE falsifier (note s8) must carry, not the literature.

Bilateral, sustained, non-physiological excitation of an entire pathway is the manipulation; it demonstrates the pathways CAN bidirectionally control behaviour, not that the brain's normal graded Go/No-Go balance maps onto REE's per-candidate eligibility envelope -- over-reading this as 'REE needs two literal MSN populations' would be the cargo-cult failure ARC-106 G1/G2 guard against.

entries.confidence_rationale: Mink's center-surround model is the canonical statement of the exact selection STRUCTURE ARC-107 imports: the basal ganglia do not generate movement; they broadly INHIBIT competing motor programs (the surround / No-Go) while focally REMOVING inhibition from the selected one (the center / Go via disinhibition). This is precisely 'an upstream signal's strength is necessary but not sufficient -- it also needs lawful access' (design note s1): access is granted by focal disinhibition, denied to competitors by surround inhibition. It grounds MECH-449's bounded-Go-plus-bounded-No-Go constitution AND the pallidal-permission-gate framing (a winner is the one whose inhibition is released, not the one with the highest scalar). Held below 0.8 because it is a conceptual review (not a single decisive experiment) and its currency is motor programs, not abstract committed-action classes; and because the surround-inhibition idea has been partly contested downstream (the strict center-surround anatomy is debated even if the focused-selection function is robust).
failure_signatures: Mink's selection works by REMOVING tonic inhibition from the chosen program and INCREASING it on competitors; REE's argmin has no tonic-inhibition / permission layer at all -- the committed action is simply the lowest-J candidate, so there is nothing to 'release' and no surround to suppress competitors. The model names exactly the missing machinery ARC-107 must build (permission gate + No-Go surround), so a selector that only sharpens the scalar will not reproduce the function.

If the focal-release signal itself is driven by the same dominant scalar (F), then the 'center' is always F's argmax and the surround always suppresses the non-F channels -- the diversity ceiling reappears in the gating layer. Mink's function only yields behavioural flexibility if the center can be set by a channel OTHER than the monopolising score; this is the same residual-ceiling risk MECH-448 targets, relocated to the disinhibition step.

The model is about preventing UNWANTED movements (surround inhibition stops interference), not about maximising committed-action DIVERSITY; importing it naively could over-suppress and NARROW the repertoire (the bradykinesia/over-No-Go failure mode) rather than widening it -- the psychiatric failure-mode column must track this both-directions risk.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical mapping from cortico-basal-ganglia Go/No-Go (D1/D2) imbalance to specific psychiatric and neurological disorders -- exactly the ARC-106-mandated psychiatric-failure-mode column for the MECH-449 Go/No-Go constitution. It grounds the disorder analogs ARC-107 must carry: No-Go over-pressure / dopamine-depletion -> Parkinsonian bradykinesia and perseveration; Go over-pressure / excess dopamine -> impulsivity and the manic/hyperkinetic pole; OCD-spectrum and Tourette's as cortico-striatal Go/No-Go and braking pathologies; ADHD and addiction as Go/No-Go learning-asymmetry disorders. Confidence held at 0.7 because it grounds the CLINICAL MAPPING (which is what the psychiatric column needs) rather than REE-specific behaviour, and because mapping a REE selector failure to a disorder is a model-of-a-model step that ARC-106 flags as 'earned, not assumed' (a REE failure must actually match the signature, not just share a label).
failure_signatures: Maia & Frank make the failure modes BIDIRECTIONAL and dopamine-graded: too little Go (or too much No-Go) -> bradykinesia, perseveration, anhedonic action-collapse (Parkinsonian / depressive pole); too much Go (or too little No-Go) -> impulsivity, premature responding, the manic/hyperkinetic pole. This is the exact dyad MECH-448's psychiatric column names (envelope too tight -> avolition; envelope too wide -> impulsivity/mania), now sourced to a canonical clinical-computational review.

The same RL/Go-No-Go machinery underlies MULTIPLE disorders distinguished by WHICH parameter is off (learning rate asymmetry, tonic vs phasic dopamine, D1 vs D2 balance); a single REE selector knob that, when mis-set, could produce several of these signatures is a strength for clinical modelling but a risk for attribution -- the falsifier must localise which failure a given lever produces.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the foundational statement of DISINHIBITION as the basal ganglia's basic output operation: BG output nuclei tonically inhibit their motor targets, and striatal activation transiently PAUSES that inhibition, releasing (disinhibiting) the target to act. It is the precise grounding for ARC-107's 'pallidal-like permission-to-commit gate (rather than bare argmax)': commitment is granted by REMOVING a default brake, not by a candidate winning a scalar comparison. It also grounds the no-op-default design of MECH-448 (the lever is OFF/permission-denied by default; eligibility is granted, not assumed). Held below 0.8 because it is a short conceptual review (TINS), its mechanism is literal tonic GABAergic inhibition REE does not possess, and the disinhibition idea, while robust, is the simplest version of a gate that REE will implement very differently (an algorithmic permission predicate, not a released brake).
failure_signatures: Chevalier-Deniau's gate is a tonically-ON brake that striatal input pauses; REE's selector has no default brake -- the committed action is whatever minimises J, granted unconditionally. ARC-107's permission gate must therefore ADD a default-deny step (no candidate commits until permission is granted), which is a genuine structural addition, not a reweighting; a selector that keeps unconditional argmin cannot express 'permission-to-commit' however its scores are tuned.

Disinhibition only produces flexible behaviour if the pause is applied SELECTIVELY to the right target; if the same dominant signal (F) decides which target gets disinhibited, the permission gate is just argmin with extra steps and the conversion ceiling persists at the gate. The biology's flexibility depends on the striatal pattern that selects the pause being richer than one scalar -- the same precondition MECH-448 must satisfy.

Because the default state is full inhibition (nothing acts), an over-tight or mis-set permission gate yields global akinesia/avolition (nothing converts) -- the bradykinetic failure mode -- exactly the 'envelope too tight' pole MECH-448's psychiatric column names; disinhibition makes that pole the DEFAULT failure, which the falsifier's non-degeneracy / safety checks must distinguish from a genuine ceiling.

entries.confidence_rationale: Hikosaka's saccade work is the best-characterised single instance of the BG permission-gate in action, with electrophysiology: the SNr tonically inhibits the superior colliculus, the caudate disinhibits the SC to PERMIT a saccade, the STN/GPe can FURTHER enhance the SNr-SC inhibition (a No-Go strengthening), and -- crucially for ARC-107 -- the whole gate is strongly modulated by behavioural CONTEXT (working memory, expectation, attention, reward expectation). Held below 0.8 by modality specificity (oculomotor) and because reward-expectation FACILITATION of the rewarded saccade is itself a value-monopoly risk (the substrate can also collapse onto the high-value option), which is a double-edged grounding the mapping must flag.
failure_signatures: Hikosaka shows the SNr-SC permission gate is modulated by working memory, expectation, attention and reward -- multiple context channels gain access. But he ALSO shows reward expectation FACILITATES the rewarded saccade: if a single value signal dominates the caudate input, the gate preferentially opens for the high-value target and the others stay inhibited. This is the biological version of the F-monopoly: a context-modulated gate can STILL collapse onto one channel if that channel monopolises the disinhibiting input -- precisely the ceiling MECH-448 must break, now shown to exist in the substrate itself.

The gate's flexibility comes from the caudate carrying genuinely DIFFERENT context signals (memory vs attention vs reward), not one score. A REE permission gate fed only by F would reproduce the structure but none of the flexibility; the entry grounds the requirement that the eligibility/permission input be multi-channel, not the sufficiency of adding a gate.

STN/GPe can ENHANCE SNr-SC inhibition (strengthen No-Go); an over-active version is the over-braking / akinesia pole, while loss of it is premature/involuntary saccades (the impulsive pole). The same dual-direction failure ARC-107's psychiatric column tracks appears here in the oculomotor gate.

This is precisely 'an upstream signal's strength is necessary but not sufficient -- it also needs lawful access' (design note s1): access is granted by focal disinhibition, denied to competitors by surround inhibition. It grounds MECH-449's bounded-Go-plus-bounded-No-Go constitution AND the pallidal-permission-gate framing (a winner is the one whose inhibition is released, not the one with the highest scalar). Held below 0.8 because it is a conceptual review (not a single decisive experiment) and its currency is motor programs, not abstract committed-action classes; and because the surround-inhibition idea has been partly contested downstream (the strict center-surround anatomy is debated even if the focused-selection function is robust).
failure_signatures: Mink's selection works by REMOVING tonic inhibition from the chosen program and INCREASING it on competitors; REE's argmin has no tonic-inhibition / permission layer at all -- the committed action is simply the lowest-J candidate, so there is nothing to 'release' and no surround to suppress competitors. The model names exactly the missing machinery ARC-107 must build (permission gate + No-Go surround), so a selector that only sharpens the scalar will not reproduce the function.

If the focal-release signal itself is driven by the same dominant scalar (F), then the 'center' is always F's argmax and the surround always suppresses the non-F channels -- the diversity ceiling reappears in the gating layer. Mink's function only yields behavioural flexibility if the center can be set by a channel OTHER than the monopolising score; this is the same residual-ceiling risk MECH-448 targets, relocated to the disinhibition step.

The model is about preventing UNWANTED movements (surround inhibition stops interference), not about maximising committed-action DIVERSITY; importing it naively could over-suppress and NARROW the repertoire (the bradykinesia/over-No-Go failure mode) rather than widening it -- the psychiatric failure-mode column must track this both-directions risk.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical mapping from cortico-basal-ganglia Go/No-Go (D1/D2) imbalance to specific psychiatric and neurological disorders -- exactly the ARC-106-mandated psychiatric-failure-mode column for the MECH-449 Go/No-Go constitution. It grounds the disorder analogs ARC-107 must carry: No-Go over-pressure / dopamine-depletion -> Parkinsonian bradykinesia and perseveration; Go over-pressure / excess dopamine -> impulsivity and the manic/hyperkinetic pole; OCD-spectrum and Tourette's as cortico-striatal Go/No-Go and braking pathologies; ADHD and addiction as Go/No-Go learning-asymmetry disorders. Confidence held at 0.7 because it grounds the CLINICAL MAPPING (which is what the psychiatric column needs) rather than REE-specific behaviour, and because mapping a REE selector failure to a disorder is a model-of-a-model step that ARC-106 flags as 'earned, not assumed' (a REE failure must actually match the signature, not just share a label).
failure_signatures: Maia & Frank make the failure modes BIDIRECTIONAL and dopamine-graded: too little Go (or too much No-Go) -> bradykinesia, perseveration, anhedonic action-collapse (Parkinsonian / depressive pole); too much Go (or too little No-Go) -> impulsivity, premature responding, the manic/hyperkinetic pole. This is the exact dyad MECH-448's psychiatric column names (envelope too tight -> avolition; envelope too wide -> impulsivity/mania), now sourced to a canonical clinical-computational review.

OCD-spectrum and the loss of inhibitory braking map to cortico-striatal Go/No-Go pathology -- grounding ARC-107's 'OCD-spectrum braking loss' failure mode; but the review also warns these mappings are model-dependent, so a REE component's breakage must reproduce the SPECIFIC signature (e.g. perseveration with intact value learning) to earn the disorder label, not merely resemble it.

The same RL/Go-No-Go machinery underlies MULTIPLE disorders distinguished by WHICH parameter is off (learning rate asymmetry, tonic vs phasic dopamine, D1 vs D2 balance); a single REE selector knob that, when mis-set, could produce several of these signatures is a strength for clinical modelling but a risk for attribution -- the falsifier must localise which failure a given lever produces.

entries.confidence_rationale: Influential integrate-and-fire attractor model showing that a SINGLE stability parameter -- the depth of an attractor basin (set by NMDA/GABA conductances) -- controls how long a network holds a state, and that moving it in opposite directions yields opposite clinical pictures: too-shallow -> instability/distractibility, too-deep (the complementary direction the authors and Rolls' later work develop) -> over-stable/perseverative. This is the closest formal analog to REE's premise that ONE refractory/maintenance parameter sets commitment DURATION and that both psychiatric poles of the BG-3 column fall out of mis-setting it. Computational (not empirical) and about cortical working-memory attractors rather than a motor commitment latch, which caps fidelity/transfer.
failure_signatures: The model is about prefrontal/temporal working-memory and semantic attractors, not a basal-ganglia motor commitment latch; the persistence mechanism is recurrent NMDA-stabilised firing, not a refractory timer. Equating attractor depth with REE's refractory parameter is an analogy at the level of 'one stability knob, two failure poles', not a mechanistic identity.

The paper anchors the SHALLOW (distractibility/instability) pole empirically within the model; the DEEP (perseveration) pole is the complementary direction developed in the surrounding Rolls/Deco programme rather than the headline result here, so the over-maintenance pole leans on the framework's symmetry, not on this paper's primary simulation.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality in vivo basal-ganglia recordings (Costa lab, Nat Neurosci) showing two dissociable population signals that map directly onto REE's commit latch: (a) start/stop neurons that bracket a committed sequence (the commit-entry and commit-release boundaries -- SD-034's done-token / MECH-090's gate-open events) and (b) sustained/inhibited neurons whose activity persists across the WHOLE sequence and covaries with execution rate (the maintenance signal -- MECH-090 hold, MECH-342 maintenance). Mapping is functional, not mechanistic; rodent operant sequence onto an ANN routing variable. The 2010 Jin & Costa nigrostriatal start/stop paper is the same lineage and is cited in-text.
failure_signatures: Start/stop and sustained signals emerge through sequence LEARNING; they are not a fixed gate. A REE latch with a pre-set refractory parameter does not reproduce the learned, action-specific emergence of these boundaries.

Direct and indirect pathways are concomitantly active at sequence initiation but diverge during execution -- a two-pathway structure REE collapses into a single commitment-gated routing variable. The duration of the sustained signal is set by execution/behavioural state, not by a standalone timer.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong multi-region monkey recordings (PMd, M1, dlPFC, GPe, GPi; Cisek lab) showing commitment as a STATE TRANSITION off a deliberation manifold, with a rising urgency signal (baseline + slope) that sets WHEN commitment happens and pallidal activity dominated by urgency. Directly anchors MECH-090's gate-open-as-state-transition and, decisively, names the variable that sets commitment TIMING in biology -- a graded, BG-mediated urgency signal -- which is what REE's tuned refractory parameter diverges from. Mixed because it strongly SUPPORTS the latch-as-state-transition while the urgency-set timing WEAKENS any reading that a fixed refractory is the biological duration law.
failure_signatures: Commitment timing in the data is set by a graded, dynamically-rising urgency signal (BG/pallidal-mediated), not by a fixed-duration refractory. A REE latch whose release is timed by a tuned refractory parameter departs from this graded-urgency control and cannot reproduce urgency-dependent shortening/lengthening of the committed epoch.

Deciding and executing are two modes of ONE integrated dynamical system here; REE separates an E3 selection event from a downstream commit-gated routing variable, so the 'fall off the decision manifold at commitment' is modelled as a discrete gate flip rather than a continuous trajectory.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly anchors the OVER-MAINTENANCE psychiatric pole of the BG-3 column: catatonia (stupor, rigidity, stereotypies) framed as impaired inhibitory control / over-engagement of the basal-ganglia INDIRECT (No-Go) pathway via reduced GABAergic tone and D2 dysfunction. This is the clinical endpoint REE predicts for a latch whose release fails / refractory runs too long, and it ties the over-maintenance pole to the same No-Go machinery (MECH-260/MECH-449) the selection-face grounding uses. Confidence capped by venue: a single-author narrative review in a lower-tier journal, not primary data.
failure_signatures: Catatonia's clinical picture is multi-determined (GABA, D2, glutamate, serotonin, ACh) and treatment-responsive to benzodiazepines; reducing it to 'the commitment latch failed to release' is a deliberate simplification that omits most of the syndrome's neurochemistry.

The review is a narrative synthesis, single author, lower-tier venue -- it proposes a unifying indirect-pathway framework rather than demonstrating it; it grounds the DIRECTION of the over-maintenance pole, not a quantitative duration law.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, high-prestige (Nature, Shadlen lab) human psychophysics that operationalises a post-commitment reversal window -- the strongest existing biological reference for REE's de-commit authority (MECH-446) and the closure-triggered release of a commitment (SD-034). Mapping fidelity is moderate: REE's de-commit is a closure/No-Go-triggered release of a maintained latch, whereas the paper's change-of-mind is driven by evidence already in the sensorimotor processing pipeline at the moment of commitment. The shared, load-bearing point is that commitment in biology is NOT absolute -- it admits a bounded reversal/release window -- which is exactly the dynamic REE's latch must support.
failure_signatures: Change-of-mind in the paper is driven by post-commitment evidence still in the processing pipeline; REE's de-commit is triggered by a closure/completion token, not by late-arriving evidence. If REE's release is read as the same mechanism, the mapping over-claims.

The reversal window in the paper is short and evidence-bounded; a REE latch whose release is set by a tuned refractory parameter (not by an evidence/processing deadline) can over- or under-shoot this window with no biological constraint pinning the duration.
