entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, well-cited computational treatment of exactly the mechanism Q-076 posits: the LEVEL of competitive inhibition (a gain-like control axis) determines whether a memory is strengthened (retrieved) or its competitors are weakened (forgotten). That is the interference-vs-forgetting interaction in a single algorithm. Confidence is held below source quality because the interaction here is realised as PHASES of one inhibitory oscillation at ENCODING/learning time, not as a retrieval-time product of two static scalars (Line A gain x Line B suppression) as Q-076 frames it -- so the mapping is mechanistically strong but structurally analogical.
failure_signatures: The model's strengthen-vs-punish decision is driven by the PHASE of an inhibitory oscillation, so the 'interaction' is temporal (one oscillating parameter) rather than a static product of two independent knobs; if REE implements Line A and Line B as two separate static scalars, the Norman mechanism supports the principle but not the specific 2x2 factorisation.

The algorithm operates at learning/encoding time (Contrastive Hebbian Learning across oscillation phases), not at retrieval readout; Q-076's predicted regimes are stated over retrieval-time reinstatement, so the read-side dissociation is inferred, not directly demonstrated.

entries.confidence_rationale: A clean lesion dissociation supporting MECH-425 Line B: a prefrontal inhibitory-control process, SEPARABLE from hippocampal storage, is what converts memory competition into forgetting. PFC lesion REVERTS interference-induced forgetting while hippocampal lesion (storage) worsens it -- exactly the content-selective-suppression-vs-storage double dissociation MECH-425's what_would_answer describes for Line B. Confidence held at 0.52 because it grounds only the Line-B factor (not the interaction with gain), the lesion is all-or-none rather than a parametric suppression knob, and it is a mouse two-task interference paradigm rather than retrieval-time scoring of individually-tracked competing traces.
failure_signatures: PFC lesion REDUCES forgetting -- so the inhibitory operator is double-edged: normal Line-B suppression manufactures forgetting of the interfering memory. If REE applies Line B too aggressively (or without gating on genuine competition) it will suppress traces that were actually wanted, which is the mirror failure of the high-gain/no-suppression corner Q-076 warns about.

Lesion is a total ablation, not a graded suppression parameter, so the study cannot show how Line B trades off against Line A gain -- it establishes the operator exists and is separable from storage, but not the interaction term Q-076 turns on.

entries.confidence_rationale: The adjudicating entry: rather than picking a side, Johnson, Simmering & Buss argue that BOTH slot and resource accounts have real explanatory power but are limited by their focus on representations rather than PROCESSES, and offer a neurally-grounded dynamic field theory (DFT) that reproduces the same capacity-limit behaviour as an emergent property of population dynamics. This is genuinely mixed for Q-077: it validates the fork as real but reframes it, and warns that the step-vs-smooth discriminating signature may be underdetermined. High relevance to Q-077's exact wording; confidence moderate because DFT is a modelling framework whose transfer to REE's goal substrate is a design choice, not an established fact.
failure_signatures: DFT can produce EITHER a quasi-step or a smooth-dilution capacity curve depending on lateral-inhibition strength and field parameters, so a behavioural degradation curve alone may NOT cleanly discriminate slot vs resource -- Q-077's what_would_answer (step vs smooth) could be underdetermined, and REE may need to instrument the competition dynamics directly rather than infer from the fidelity-vs-N curve.

The paper's thesis is that the slot-vs-resource dichotomy is itself the wrong level of description; if REE forces SD-046 into one horn it may inherit a false dichotomy rather than the process-level mechanism (graded competition among goal fields) that actually generates the capacity limit.

entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical statement of the FLEXIBLE-resource horn of Q-077's fork, and the one the claim's own notes flag as MIXED against SD-046. It supports the resource model (no fixed item limit; a shared resource distributed by a power law; the acted-on/attended item drawing disproportionate precision) -- which directly problematises SD-046's discrete-slot framing, while remaining consistent with SD-046 holding N>=2 goals at graded fidelity. Marked mixed rather than weakens because it undercuts the DISCRETE parameterisation without contradicting the multi-slot design decision itself; confidence moderate because it is visual-WM precision, not goal maintenance, and the result is actively contested (Zhang & Luck 2008, Cowan & Rouder 2009).
failure_signatures: The power-law resource model predicts NO hard cutoff, so a discrete-slot SD-046 would produce a step function the resource account says cannot exist; if the arena shows smooth precision dilution instead, SD-046's fixed-N framing is wrong.

The result is contested: Zhang & Luck (2008) and Cowan & Rouder (2009) argue a slots-plus-averaging / item-limit model fits the same data at least as well, so Bays & Husain cannot unilaterally settle the fork -- the discriminating experiment must be run on REE's own substrate.

entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical statement of the DISCRETE-slot horn of Q-077's fork: a pure capacity limit of about four chunks in the focus of attention, defended across a wide range of paradigms. This directly supports SD-046's current discrete-slot framing (a fixed ~N of simultaneously-active goal slots). Confidence is moderate, not high, because Cowan's limit is a short-term-MEMORY chunk capacity / focus-of-attention limit, not a multi-GOAL maintenance capacity, and Cowan himself stresses the number holds only under boundary conditions that block chunking/rehearsal -- so even the slot account is soft and context-dependent, not a hard structural cap.
failure_signatures: Cowan's ~4 limit only appears under conditions that specifically BLOCK recoding items into larger chunks; when chunking or rehearsal is available the effective capacity inflates. So a fixed-N slot count in SD-046 could be an artefact of the arena's chunking boundary conditions rather than a true structural limit -- a step-function fit would need to rule out chunking of goals.

The limit is defined over passive stored chunks in the focus of attention; goals are active workstreams with drive coupling and persistence, so a chunk-capacity number may not transfer to how many goals can be simultaneously MAINTAINED and acted toward.

entries.confidence_rationale: Supports ARC-108's LOAD-BEARING PREMISE -- that the gating weights which decide how top-down context re-routes selection should be LEARNED, and that when they are, a disinhibitory gating structure emerges as the solution and is causally required for flexibility. But the paper is SILENT on ARC-108's specific mechanism: the weights are learned by gradient-based RNN training, NOT by a signed dopaminergic RPE three-factor rule with D1-LTP/D2-LTD asymmetry. So it evidences 'gating must be learned, not hand-specified' (the exact gap ARC-108 identifies in the pure-arithmetic ARC-107 layer) but not 'learned via dopaminergic RPE.' Held to 0.5: strong on the premise, no traction on the teaching-signal identity.
failure_signatures: The disinhibitory gating solution EMERGED from end-to-end task training; it was not hand-wired. This is a standing prediction against ARC-107's pure-arithmetic arbitration layer: a fixed hand-specified gating rule may be unable to reach the flexible context-routing solution that learning finds, which is ARC-108's core rationale for the F-dominance ceiling.

The paper does not test whether a biologically-local teaching signal (dopaminergic RPE, three-factor plasticity) can discover the same solution -- so it cannot rule out that gradient training reaches a solution unreachable by ARC-108's proposed local rule. ARC-108's dopaminergic-RPE mechanism remains unevidenced by this source.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong, well-designed source (biologically-constrained E/I RNN with a causal in-vivo validation in mouse V1; PLOS Biology; co-first Aquino & Kim, senior Rungratsameetaweemana -- author list per press coverage, not the full byline). It supports MECH-140's COMPUTATIONAL principle almost exactly: a disinhibitory (inhibition-on-inhibition) motif is the load-bearing channel for context-dependent control, it is graded rather than winner-take-all (weakening it degrades task-switching progressively; weakening other connection classes leaves processing intact), and the disinhibitory pathway is specifically the one carrying top-down context. Confidence held to 0.6 by a genuine locus/function mismatch: MECH-140 names a BASAL-GANGLIA indirect-pathway inter-collicular competition for TRI-LOOP CONFLICT ARBITRATION, whereas this paper is CORTICAL disinhibition ROUTING top-down context into sensory processing. The 'disinhibition, graded not WTA' principle transfers; the anatomical locus and the arbitration-vs-routing role do not.
failure_signatures: If REE were to implement cross-loop arbitration as hard winner-take-all suppression, this result predicts loss of context-tracking flexibility: the paper shows it is precisely the inhibition-on-inhibition (graded disinhibitory) connections, not blanket suppression, that carry task context, and that ablating them collapses task-switching.

The disinhibitory channel is shown to be selectively necessary -- weakening non-disinhibitory connection classes left processing intact. A REE arbitration substrate that folds disinhibition into a generic inhibitory pool would not reproduce this selectivity and would mispredict which lesions break flexibility.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality peer-reviewed causal circuit dissection (2-photon imaging + optogenetic perturbation + computational modelling in mouse V1; Neuron; Scanziani/Miller labs). It establishes the concrete cellular disinhibitory circuit -- VIP interneurons inhibit SOM interneurons, relieving excitatory neurons from suppression -- that mediates contextual modulation, and shows it is both NECESSARY and SUFFICIENT. Directly grounds the 'disinhibition is a real, graded, load-bearing control primitive' half of MECH-140 in causal biology. Held to 0.58 by the same locus/function caveat as the Aquino 2026 entry (cortical surround-context modulation, not BG tri-loop conflict arbitration) plus a narrower notion of 'context' (center-surround stimulus congruence, not task-rule switching).
failure_signatures: The circuit works by MODULATING RECURRENT EXCITATION, not by direct feedforward disinhibition -- a REE implementation that models disinhibition as a purely feedforward subtraction on the input would mispredict the dynamics and the sufficiency result.

PV interneurons here are context-INDEPENDENT (they track excitatory activity), so the contextual control is carried specifically by the VIP->SOM limb. Collapsing all interneuron types into one inhibitory pool would erase the very selectivity that makes the circuit a context channel.

This paper's context-routing is implemented in a RECURRENT E/I network whose disinhibitory dynamics settle to context-appropriate states -- consistent with 'context-dependent selection resolves through recurrent inhibitory dynamics, not a one-shot readout.' But the paper does not isolate or test a settling STEP as such, does not compare against a one-shot readout, and the recurrence is cortical sensory-context, not MECH-450's BG thalamocortical settling. Held to 0.48: the paper is congenial to the premise but does not directly evidence the specific settling-vs-argmin substitution.
failure_signatures: The functional solution is carried by recurrent inhibitory dynamics; a one-shot feedforward readout would not reproduce the context-dependent re-routing. This is indirect support for MECH-450's claim that a single-pass argmin is the wrong primitive, but the paper does not run the head-to-head settling-vs-one-shot comparison MECH-450 needs.

Disinhibition modulates RECURRENT excitation (per the Keller 2020 cortical circuit this line builds on); a settling implementation that treats lateral inhibition as a static subtraction rather than a dynamic recurrent term may miss the mechanism, and this paper does not adjudicate the dynamical form.

This is the canonical formalisation of the exact dichotomy Q-078 raises: that action selection is a dedicated architectural FUNCTION (a distinct 'selection' pathway implementing feedforward off-centre on-surround competition, regulated by a separate 'control' pathway) rather than an emergent property of upstream signal strength. Gurney/Prescott/Redgrave recast selection as SIGNAL selection over scalar saliences and show the biological BG is organised as a purpose-built selection circuit -- direct conceptual support for the CONSTITUTIONAL reading (a BG-like selection constitution is a real, dedicated thing beyond parametric salience). Confidence held below 0.8 because the paper does not test REE's specific F-variance-share-vs-constitution contrast; it establishes that the biological reference architecture Q-078 invokes genuinely exists and is functionally load-bearing, which is the load-bearing premise of the constitutional hypothesis but not a direct test of REE's E3 ceiling.
failure_signatures: If REE's E3 conversion ceiling is CONSTITUTIONAL, then no amount of parametric strengthening of upstream saliences will reliably convert committed action -- exactly the pattern Q-078 reports across CRF/OFC/SD-037/dACC/modulatory channels. Gurney 2001 predicts this: in their model, raising a channel's salience without the selection+control architecture in place does not yield clean selection; the off-centre on-surround competition and the control pathway's regulation are what make a strong signal WIN rather than merely be present.

An REE substrate that routes salience directly to action authority without a dedicated selection layer (feedforward inhibitory competition + a separate control/regulation pathway) should exhibit either no selection or distortion-of-selection under strong input -- the signature of a missing selection constitution rather than a weak signal.

entries.confidence_rationale: This embodied follow-up to the Gurney/Redgrave selection model directly probes the parametric axis Q-078 contrasts against constitution: it varies a purely PARAMETRIC modulator (tonic dopamine) inside a FIXED selection architecture and shows that parametric changes alone do not yield graceful selection -- too little DA gives failure-to-initiate, too much gives distorted/leaky selection and behavioural traps, and raising salience (another parametric lever) only PARTIALLY relieves the low-DA deficit. This supports Q-078's suspicion that parametric levers are insufficient and the selection architecture is what carries lawful conversion. Confidence lower (0.62) because the paper's primary aim is modelling DA dysregulation/Parkinsonism, so the parametric-insufficiency point is inferred from its results rather than being the paper's own thesis; and it is a robot-embodied simulation, not an REE test.
failure_signatures: Increasing a parametric drive (salience) to compensate for a selection deficit only PARTIALLY restores selection and can leave the agent in a 'behavioural trap' -- the signature of a parametric fix applied to a constitutional problem. If REE conversion responds only partially, or non-monotonically, to strengthening upstream channels, that argues the ceiling is not merely parametric.

Pushing a parametric modulator too far in the other direction (excess DA) does not improve selection but degrades it -- partially-expressed losing actions leak through, selection integration is lost. A monotone 'more signal is better' assumption is therefore wrong for a genuine selection architecture.

entries.confidence_rationale: Frank 2006 provides direct mechanistic backing for one specific constitutional lever Q-078 enumerates: the hyperdirect-STN conflict-sensitive HOLD and dynamic threshold adjustment. The model shows that a dedicated cortico-subthalamic-pallidal circuit RAISES the response threshold under high cortical response conflict -- a lawful-access rule that is architecturally distinct from, and cannot be reduced to, the strength of any competing action's salience. This is strong support for the claim that commit-timing/threshold machinery is a constitutional component (not parametric). Confidence at 0.7 rather than higher because it evidences one lever (conflict-hold / adaptive threshold) rather than the whole selection constitution, and because it is a computational model validated against Parkinson's/pharmacology data rather than a direct REE test.
failure_signatures: A selection system lacking a conflict-sensitive hold will commit prematurely when multiple candidates are close in value, so the ultimately-committed action is determined by transient noise rather than by lawful competition -- the STN's absence, in Frank's model, changes WHICH response is selected, not just its timing. If REE's E3 has no conflict-gated threshold-widening, strengthening an upstream channel under competition may still fail to convert because the commit fires before the competition resolves.

If REE conversion failures co-occur with high inter-candidate conflict specifically (rather than uniformly), that is the signature of a missing hyperdirect-STN-style hold rather than a globally weak signal.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the single closest paper to Q-080's actual proposal, and it splits the two horns cleanly. It SUPPORTS the 'energy conservation as an evolutionarily-primary drive / least-effort prior' half: the brain is modelled as purposively conserving activity, planning longer-term allocation of a limited metabolic budget (astrocytic glycogen), so a least-effort prior is a first-class control objective, not a derived one. But it WEAKENS the 'effort = harm' framing: conservation is cast as OPTIMAL ALLOCATION of a replenishable buffer, not as damage/irreversible residue -- glycogen depletes AND repletes, with no harm-like special status. So it endorses energy-primacy while explicitly NOT reaching for a harm channel to do it. Confidence 0.6: conceptually on-target and it subsumes both cost/benefit and limited-resource views, but the glycogen-buffer mechanism is a proposal (the authors call the biological basis provisional), and it is a control-theoretic model without direct REE mapping.
failure_signatures: A replenishable energy buffer (glycogen depletes and repletes) supports a least-effort PRIOR without any harm/irreversibility semantics. If REE can get energy-conservation-as-primary-drive from a reversible-budget mechanism, then Q-080's harm-coupling is over-specified: it would wrongly assign irreversible special status to what is actually a reversible resource.

The harm-coupling proposal is only justified where the depletion is genuinely IRREVERSIBLE / damage-like. If, as here, sustained over-use merely draws down a buffer that refills with rest, the correct REE representation is an allostatic-load / opportunity-cost term (already present) plus a least-effort prior -- NOT the harm stream.

entries.confidence_rationale: The EVC theory is the canonical normative account that treats cognitive effort purely as a COST TERM SUBTRACTED from expected payoff -- exactly REE's existing value-subtraction machinery (dACC EVC effort_cost). It is a complete, well-validated framework in which effort is a foregone-value quantity, with no need to route effort through a harm/allostatic/irreversibility channel. Relative to Q-080's harm-coupling proposal this is WEAKENING evidence: the mainstream computational account of how the brain handles effort does its work entirely as value-subtraction, giving a parsimonious alternative that does not require effort-as-harm. Confidence 0.68 because it evidences the sufficiency/parsimony of value-subtraction for NORMAL effort allocation, but it does not directly test the EDGE case Q-080 cares about (over-exertion -> depletion -> a harm-adjacent allostatic state), so it cannot fully close the harm-coupling question.
failure_signatures: If value-subtraction (EVC-style effort_cost) already reproduces the full range of REE's effort-related behaviour -- effort avoidance, effort-reward trade-offs, allocation shifts -- then adding a harm-coupling channel is unfalsifiable surplus unless it predicts something value-subtraction cannot. Q-080's harm-coupling must therefore earn its keep on the over-exertion/depletion regime specifically, where EVC is silent.

A harm-coupled effort account predicts irreversibility-aware, special-status treatment of excess effort (like REE's harm stream); EVC predicts fully reversible, linearly-tradeable cost. If REE's effort behaviour is empirically fully reversible and tradeable, the harm-coupling is wrong; the discriminating test is whether over-exertion leaves a persistent residue that ordinary opportunity-cost cannot.

entries.confidence_rationale: Kurzban et al. is the canonical statement of the OPPORTUNITY-COST account of subjective effort -- which is exactly REE's existing MECH-320/ARC-068 opportunity-cost-of-time machinery. They argue the aversive phenomenology of effort is the felt output of cost/benefit computations over foregone alternative uses of limited executive systems, and they explicitly ARGUE AGAINST the physical-resource-DEPLETION account that is the mechanistic cousin of Q-080's 'over-exertion -> depletion -> harm-adjacent state.' So this both (a) supports the sufficiency of value-subtraction/opportunity-cost and (b) casts specific doubt on the depletion story harm-coupling would rest on -- double-weakening for the harm proposal. Confidence 0.66: strong on the ordinary-effort regime and on the anti-depletion argument, but it is a theoretical target article (much-debated), and it addresses subjective mental effort rather than the metabolic over-exertion REE's harm-coupling most naturally concerns.
failure_signatures: If subjective effort is the felt output of opportunity-cost computation (next-best foregone use of executive systems), then effort is FOREGONE VALUE, not harm -- and REE's existing ARC-068/MECH-320 opportunity-cost machinery already captures it, leaving no gap for a harm channel to fill.

Kurzban et al. marshal evidence AGAINST resource-depletion accounts of effort (e.g. fatigue dissipates on task-switch, is sensitive to incentives). If REE's over-exertion state behaves like opportunity cost (incentive-sensitive, relieved by better alternatives) rather than like damage (persistent, irreversibility-flagged), the harm-coupling is falsified in favour of value-subtraction.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality mechanistic review (Pharmacology & Therapeutics) of the exact bounding dependency the 711 autopsy named as unresolved: the D2 autoreceptor (D2AR) as a tonic NEGATIVE-FEEDBACK homeostat that regulates dopamine neuron firing, DA synthesis, reuptake and release, keeping extracellular DA within a set-point band. This is precisely the 'tonic-DA homeostasis loop that bounds ascending striato-nigro-striatal drive' abstracted by ASG-3. It states dysregulation of this feedback disrupts DA homeostasis and drives substance-use vulnerability -- i.e. removing the bound produces the runaway. Direction 'supports': the biological homeostatic bound the ASG-3 divergence row assumes demonstrably exists and is a negative-feedback loop. Confidence 0.7: strong source + near-exact conceptual mapping (a homeostatic negative-feedback bound on DA drive), discounted because it is a molecular/pharmacological review, not a demonstration that this loop is what bounds the ASCENDING-SPIRAL gain specifically.
failure_signatures: A dopaminergic drive mechanism with NO negative-feedback homeostat on its own output (REE's raw ascending gain, pre-repair) has no biological analogue in the healthy system -- the D2AR loop is always present to clamp firing/synthesis/release toward a set point; its absence is the disease state.

Because the homeostat acts at multiple stages (firing, synthesis, reuptake, release), a single hard clamp at one stage (REE's M_cross box, ASG-4) is a coarser bound than the biology's distributed graded negative feedback -- predicts the hard clamp will be brittle at the edges relative to a soft, multi-stage normalization.

entries.confidence_rationale: Mechanistic transgenic-mouse study that shows the bounding dependency AND its runaway failure mode in one system: normally D2 autoreceptors tonically constrain presynaptic DA (via DAT trafficking + tyrosine-hydroxylase control), but in the DAT Val559 variant tonic D2AR activation flips into a POSITIVE-FEEDBACK loop -- it drives surface expression of efflux-prone transporters, raising extracellular DA and 'overwhelming DAT-mediated DA clearance capacity'. That is a concrete biological instance of a homeostat losing its bound and running away -- the precise dynamical shape of the 711 blow-up (a plastic positive-feedback loop with no saturation). Direction 'mixed': it SUPPORTS the existence of the tonic homeostatic bound, but its headline is the PATHOLOGICAL runaway (a disease variant), so it also functions as the cautionary failure-signature. Confidence 0.62: strong mechanism, but a specific disease-variant model with region/sex specificity, so transfer to REE's abstract controller is via analogy of dynamics, not of substrate.
failure_signatures: A tonic drive coupled to a plastic amplifier with no saturation becomes a positive-feedback runaway that overwhelms the downstream clearance/normalization capacity (Val559: tonic D2AR -> efflux-prone DAT -> DA rises -> more efflux). REE's pre-repair ascending M_cross maturation is the same shape; the anti-windup clamp (ASG-4) is the missing saturation.

Whether a homeostatic loop BOUNDS or RUNS AWAY can depend on region-specific parameters (dorsal vs ventral striatum here) -- predicts REE's parity controller may need loop-specific (limbic vs motor) bounding constants rather than one global ceiling ratio.

entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative Cambridge (Everitt/Robbins) review that names the exact symbol REE imported -- the serial, dopamine-dependent striato-nigro-striatal ascending spiral (Haber 2000 lineage) carrying information ventral(limbic)->dorsal(motor) through segregated cortico-striato-pallido-thalamo-cortical loops. Its highest value here is the FAILURE-MODE mapping: the review's whole thesis is that when this ascending spiral is driven UNCHECKED (by addictive drugs subverting the normal bounding), it produces a pathological runaway -- a compulsive, stimulus-response 'incentive habit' in which the dorsal-motor loop is progressively captured. That is the biological instance of exactly the 711 runaway (limbic drive climbing the spiral without a homeostatic bound and monopolising downstream selection). Direction 'mixed' not 'supports' because the review is a conceptual synthesis (no measured bounding law) and its addiction framing is a divergence-flavoured caveat: the spiral's DEFAULT healthy operation is bounded/graded; runaway is the pathology. Confidence 0.66: high source quality, strong mapping to the symbol + its failure mode, but indirect on the quantitative bound.
failure_signatures: If the ascending limbic->motor spiral is driven without the normal homeostatic constraint (the drug-subversion analogue = REE's unbounded raw scalar gain), the dorsal/motor loop is progressively captured and behaviour collapses onto a single compulsive stimulus-response channel -- the biological form of the 711 limbic-monopoly runaway.

The spiral's benefit is contingent on it staying GRADED and serial (ventral biases dorsal by a bounded increment); a mechanism that lets one loop's ascending drive grow without bound produces maladaptive habit-capture, not adaptive integration.

entries.confidence_rationale: Whole-cell/optogenetic demonstration that striatal spiny projection neurons (SPNs) form a genuine local LATERAL INHIBITION network via axon-collateral GABAergic synapses onto each other (both direct- and indirect-pathway), and that this network is neuromodulator-tunable (5-HT1B scales its strength). This is the concrete substrate ASG-4 abstracts -- the 'soft striatal lateral-inhibition normalization that bounds the biological spiral'. It supports that lateral inhibition is a real, gain-tunable competitive-normalization primitive in the exact circuit REE models, and Wickens' own framing ties it to action selection. Direction 'supports'. Confidence 0.6 (not higher) because the authors are explicit that the FUNCTIONAL role of SPN-SPN lateral inhibition in selection is still 'currently unknown' -- so the substrate exists and is tunable, but its causal selection role is hypothesised, not measured.
failure_signatures: Striatal competition is bounded by a DISTRIBUTED, tunable lateral-inhibition network among the projection neurons themselves, not by a hard per-edge cap; an implementation that omits any mutual-inhibition normalization (REE pre-repair) has no mechanism to keep one channel from dominating.

The lateral-inhibition strength is itself neuromodulator-scaled (5-HT1B here) -- a fixed hard clamp (ASG-4) cannot express the graded, context-dependent bound the biology uses, suggesting a soft normalization with a tunable strength is the more faithful successor.

Directly on SD-063's chosen quantile/pinball form. Supports it as an attractive distribution-free, parametric-assumption-free, model-agnostic way to represent per-input predictive spread (its opening explicitly lists model-based RL as a motivating application). But its central finding is a caveat: optimising the pinball loss alone does NOT guarantee calibrated quantiles -- the calibration/sharpness balance it strikes is arbitrary and depends on model expressivity. Mixed because it both endorses the quantile approach and flags that the raw pinball head SD-063 uses may be miscalibrated without an added calibration step.
failure_signatures: Optimising the pinball loss is not an adequate objective to achieve calibration; the balance between calibration and sharpness implied by pinball loss is arbitrary and depends on the expressivity of the model class, so a highly expressive head can be skewed toward sharpness at the cost of calibration.

Quantile crossing and per-quantile independent optimisation mean a raw multi-quantile pinball head is not guaranteed monotone or calibrated; SD-063 mitigates crossing via monotone rearrangement of [q0.1..q0.9] but rearrangement addresses ordering, not average/adversarial-group calibration.

The paper's calibration metric (ECE over quantile levels) is not what V3-EXQ-712 measured (CRPS + precision_error_corr); a head that wins on CRPS can still be miscalibrated in the Chung sense, so SD-063's diagnostic PASS does not certify calibration.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly on-point and high-fidelity for SD-063's central validity risk. It rigorously documents that the standard Gaussian-NLL heteroscedastic head corrupts the mean estimate (rich-get-richer via 1/sigma^2 gradient scaling), which (a) explains why hetero_gaussian lost to quantile_pinball in V3-EXQ-712 -- supporting SD-063's form choice -- but (b) warns that ANY conditional-uncertainty head coupled to the mean/encoder during joint training can degrade the point prediction, which is exactly SD-063's open, unresolved concern. Mixed because it both corroborates the form decision and raises a concrete failure mode for the wired-in build.
failure_signatures: Minimising a heteroscedastic Gaussian NLL scales the mean gradient by 1/sigma^2(x), biasing learning toward low-variance points and creating a 'rich-get-richer' cycle where poorly-predicted points get high variance to explain away poor mean estimates rather than improving them; the resulting mean can be significantly less accurate than an equally-expressive mean-only (MSE) model.

The pathology arises specifically when mean and variance share ancestral computations (a shared trunk) and are optimised jointly -- the exact configuration a wired-in E2 uncertainty head would create -- so SD-063's joint-training validation gate is precisely where this failure would manifest.

Beta-NLL (Seitzer 2022) and the paper's stop-gradient fix are needed to recover faithful means; a naive joint head does not, meaning SD-063's head must be explicitly shielded or the E2 mean/agency-residual (SD-031) could be corrupted.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational, heavily-cited paper establishing that a per-input (heteroscedastic) aleatoric-uncertainty head predicting input-dependent observation noise outperforms a fixed/global noise assumption -- the exact 'per-input spread vs global EMA' distinction SD-063 rests on. High mapping fidelity on that point. Lowered because the paper's head is a Gaussian log-variance (NLL 'learned attenuation') form, not the distribution-free quantile/pinball form SD-063 selects, and the benefit is demonstrated on vision regression (depth, segmentation), not on a forward-model-feeds-commitment loop.
failure_signatures: The learned-attenuation loss down-weights high-noise points, which is the same 1/sigma^2 gradient scaling later shown (Stirn 2023, Seitzer 2022) to bias mean estimates -- so this head form is exactly the one SD-063's quantile form was chosen to avoid, and using it jointly with E2 could degrade the E2 mean.

Aleatoric uncertainty here is observation noise on a supervised target; SD-063's E2 predicts a latent next-state where part of the 'noise' is agent-caused (SD-031 residual), a component this paper's setup never has to disentangle.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, highly-cited NeurIPS paper establishing that a learned forward/dynamics model should emit input-conditional predictive uncertainty (aleatoric, per-input) and that propagating that uncertainty into action selection materially improves behaviour. High mapping fidelity to SD-063's architecture (E2 forward model emits per-prediction spread -> E3 gates commitment), lowered because PETS represents aleatoric uncertainty with a Gaussian-NLL head + ensemble rather than the distribution-free quantile form SD-063 prefers, and it uses uncertainty for trajectory-sampling planning rather than a single commit/hold gate.
failure_signatures: PETS separates aleatoric from epistemic uncertainty by ensembling; a single-head E2 quantile spread conflates them, so the SD-063 head cannot be assumed to isolate the environment-noise component the way PETS's trajectory sampling does.

PETS obtains its per-input aleatoric variance from a Gaussian-NLL probabilistic network -- exactly the head form that lost to quantile_pinball in V3-EXQ-712 -- so the paper supports 'conditional uncertainty feeds action' without endorsing SD-063's specific distribution-free form.

This is the equation-level synthesis that makes WS-5's core point precise. It shows verbatim that (a) the approximate posterior FACTORISES under a mean-field approximation over hidden-state factors, and (b) expected free energy is a SUM of separable epistemic (salience + novelty) and extrinsic (risk) terms -- i.e. active inference optimises a factorized functional, not an undifferentiated scalar. That directly WEAKENS REE's 'active inference is just one scalar' objection (a strawman as stated). Simultaneously it pins the GENUINE departure: every term of G(pi) is measured in nats and summed, so risk + ambiguity is one commensurable number -- the exact common-currency assumption MECH-069/ARC-021 reject. Confidence moderate: it is a normative-mathematical paper (no empirical test of incommensurability), and the mapping onto REE's three specific channels is interpretive.
failure_signatures: Expected free energy is explicitly assembled as risk + ambiguity (state pathway) or, dually, negative extrinsic value + negative epistemic value -- all in nats and additively combined. This is the concrete existence proof that reward-seeking and information-seeking are COMMENSURABLE and summable, which is the assumption REE's incommensurability claim denies. If a single summed functional over factorized states can reproduce REE's mode/credit behaviour, MECH-069's strong form is unsupported.

The mean-field factorisation Q(s_1:T | pi) = product over tau of Q(s_tau | pi), and the factorisation over distinct hidden-state factors, show active inference already SEPARATES representational dimensions. So REE cannot claim novelty for 'separate channels' -- only for the stronger claim that the separated channels' errors cannot be re-combined into any shared scalar, which this paper does not test and its formalism does not require.

Precision here (including policy precision gamma with its Gamma prior) is a scalar/low-dimensional gain on a common surprise currency. It provides no distinct, non-exchangeable precision axes, so ARC-016's multi-axis precision is an addition NOT licensed by this formalism and must be independently justified.

entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical, comprehensive statement of active inference. Strongly SUPPORTS ARC-016: precision as inverse variance weighting prediction errors, and precision over policies (gamma) as the control variable that sets the behavioural regime, is exactly the precision-to-commitment vocabulary REE re-derived without the calculus. WEAKENS-leaning on the strong form of MECH-069/ARC-021: the textbook shows a single expected-free-energy functional G(pi) can absorb reward-seeking and information-seeking as decomposed terms, so REE's blanket 'active inference is one scalar' objection is partly a strawman -- but the same fact makes the unified functional a live alternative hypothesis to strict incommensurability, which is why the direction is 'mixed' not 'supports'. Confidence is moderate because a textbook is a synthesis, not new empirical evidence, and the mapping onto REE's specific three-channel architecture requires interpretation.
failure_signatures: Active inference derives everything -- perception, learning, action, precision, exploration -- from a SINGLE scalar (variational / expected free energy). This is a standing existence proof that REE's three functionally-distinct control objectives COULD in principle be unified into one functional over a factorized state space, which is precisely the alternative MECH-069 must rule out rather than assume away.

The textbook's precision is a scalar (or low-dimensional) gain on a common prediction-error currency (surprise, measured in nats). REE's ARC-016 asserts multi-axis / heterogeneous precision; active inference does not obviously supply distinct, non-exchangeable precision axes, so the departure REE claims is not free -- it must be shown that a single-currency precision cannot reproduce REE's mode transitions.

Epistemic value in active inference is information gain measured in the same nats as pragmatic value; the two are commensurable and summable by construction. REE's claim that its three error channels are INcommensurable (no common currency at all) is a stronger and different claim than 'distinct terms in one functional', and the textbook offers no support for non-commensurability -- if anything it is the null this claim contradicts.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality synthesis that draws the field's load-bearing distinction -- KNOWLEDGE-based vs COMPETENCE-based intrinsic motivation -- and argues they are functionally distinct drives with distinct mechanisms. Direction is MIXED for REE: it supports the legitimacy of REE's existing knowledge-based stack (MECH-314 family) as one half of IM, but it documents that REE has NO competence-based IM claim at all, which is exactly the missing ingredient WS-1's competence floor implicates. Confidence is high on the conceptual distinction (mapping fidelity strong) but the source is a conceptual/review chapter, not a single decisive experiment.
failure_signatures: Knowledge-based IM (novelty, prediction error, learning progress on the WORLD MODEL) improves the agent's model but does not by itself reward the acquisition of SKILLS/competence -- an agent can be maximally curious and still behaviourally incompetent (the exact WS-1 pattern: curiosity substrate wired, foraging still zero).

Competence-based IM requires a repertoire of self-generated GOALS and a per-goal competence-progress estimator; without an explicit goal representation to measure improvement against, competence-based IM cannot be computed -- a substrate with only a global scalar novelty bonus cannot host it.

Conflating the two IM types (using a single knowledge-based signal to drive skill learning) produces agents that explore richly but never consolidate reusable competences -- the pathology the chapter is written to prevent.

entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical RL-side instantiation of MECH-314a (novelty/count-based bonus): it derives a PSEUDOCOUNT from a density model so that count-based novelty generalises from the tabular case to high-dimensional non-tabular states, and shows a large exploration gain on Montezuma's Revenge. High source quality (NeurIPS, ~1300 citations). Supports MECH-314a's core mechanism (recency/rarity-of-encounter bonus) AND supplies the exact estimator REE needs to make a count-based bonus computable in a learned latent space rather than a tabular grid.
failure_signatures: The pseudocount is only as good as the density model: a poorly-fit or slowly-adapting density model gives mis-calibrated novelty, either over-rewarding already-seen states or failing to flag genuinely novel ones.

Count-based novelty is a LEVEL signal (rarity), not a derivative -- it shares MECH-314a's vulnerability to the noisy-TV / stochastic-trap failure Oudeyer & Kaplan flag: irreducibly random states stay perpetually 'novel' and can sink exploration budget.

The bonus decays as counts accumulate, so it drives COVERAGE (visit-everything) not COMPETENCE (achieve-goals); on Montezuma it helps reach new rooms but does not by itself teach robust goal-directed skill.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational formalisation of learning-progress-as-compression-progress that MECH-314c already cites (Schmidhuber 1991). Very high source quality. Direction is MIXED, not pure support: it corroborates the derivative-of-model-quality signal REE registered, but Schmidhuber's own framing folds curiosity, creativity, and skill acquisition into a SINGLE scalar intrinsic reward on ONE world-model+controller, which is exactly the single-functional framing REE's three-incommensurable-channels design (ARC-021/MECH-069) deliberately rejects. It is therefore simultaneously supporting evidence for MECH-314c and a documented instance of the design REE argues against.
failure_signatures: The intrinsic reward is a single scalar (compression progress) maximised by one RL controller -- a wireheading/self-delusion surface: the agent can be drawn to data it can trivially make more compressible, and the theory needs the environment to supply genuinely novel learnable regularity to avoid degenerate loops.

Compression progress rewards improving the WORLD MODEL (knowledge), not achieving GOALS (competence); Schmidhuber acknowledges skills are acquired only as a side effect of seeking compressible data, so it does not by itself guarantee the agent crosses a behavioural competence floor.

Requires a compressor whose improvement is measurable and attributable to the agent's actions; in high-dimensional stochastic input the compression-progress estimate is noisy and can misattribute environmental change to agent learning.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical source that MECH-314's typology (novelty / info-gain / learning-progress sub-flavours) is organised around, and the direct namesake of MECH-314c (learning_progress_curiosity). Very high source quality (foundational, thousands of citations, defines the field's vocabulary). Mapping fidelity is high because REE's three-way MECH-314/314a/314c split IS Oudeyer & Kaplan's typology re-expressed; the caveat is that Oudeyer & Kaplan derive learning-progress as the reward signal that provably avoids the two failure modes REE's Phase-1 broadcast-scalar instantiation does NOT yet avoid.
failure_signatures: Prediction-error / novelty maximization (MECH-314a-like) drives the agent to unlearnable stochastic regions -- the 'noisy TV' / white-noise trap -- because raw unpredictability is maximal where nothing can be learned.
Predictability-maximization (the dual: seek maximally predictable states) collapses the agent onto trivial, already-mastered regions -- the 'blank wall' trap.

Only the DERIVATIVE (rate of change of predictive error = learning progress), not the level of error or novelty, tracks genuine competence acquisition; a scalar novelty/PE bonus without the derivative is vulnerable to both traps.

Compression progress rewards improving the WORLD MODEL (knowledge), not achieving GOALS (competence); Schmidhuber acknowledges skills are acquired only as a side effect of seeking compressible data, so it does not by itself guarantee the agent crosses a behavioural competence floor.

Requires a compressor whose improvement is measurable and attributable to the agent's actions; in high-dimensional stochastic input the compression-progress estimate is noisy and can misattribute environmental change to agent learning.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical source that MECH-314's typology (novelty / info-gain / learning-progress sub-flavours) is organised around, and the direct namesake of MECH-314c (learning_progress_curiosity). Very high source quality (foundational, thousands of citations, defines the field's vocabulary). Mapping fidelity is high because REE's three-way MECH-314/314a/314c split IS Oudeyer & Kaplan's typology re-expressed; the caveat is that Oudeyer & Kaplan derive learning-progress as the reward signal that provably avoids the two failure modes REE's Phase-1 broadcast-scalar instantiation does NOT yet avoid.

entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical RL-side instantiation of MECH-314a (novelty/count-based bonus): it derives a PSEUDOCOUNT from a density model so that count-based novelty generalises from the tabular case to high-dimensional non-tabular states, and shows a large exploration gain on Montezuma's Revenge. High source quality (NeurIPS, ~1300 citations). Supports MECH-314a's core mechanism (recency/rarity-of-encounter bonus) AND supplies the exact estimator REE needs to make a count-based bonus computable in a learned latent space rather than a tabular grid.

The bonus decays as counts accumulate, so it drives COVERAGE (visit-everything) not COMPETENCE (achieve-goals); on Montezuma it helps reach new rooms but does not by itself teach robust goal-directed skill.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality synthesis that draws the field's load-bearing distinction -- KNOWLEDGE-based vs COMPETENCE-based intrinsic motivation -- and argues they are functionally distinct drives with distinct mechanisms. Direction is MIXED for REE: it supports the legitimacy of REE's existing knowledge-based stack (MECH-314 family) as one half of IM, but it documents that REE has NO competence-based IM claim at all, which is exactly the missing ingredient WS-1's competence floor implicates. Confidence is high on the conceptual distinction (mapping fidelity strong) but the source is a conceptual/review chapter, not a single decisive experiment.

Competence-based IM requires a repertoire of self-generated GOALS and a per-goal competence-progress estimator; without an explicit goal representation to measure improvement against, competence-based IM cannot be computed -- a substrate with only a global scalar novelty bonus cannot host it.

Conflating the two IM types (using a single knowledge-based signal to drive skill learning) produces agents that explore richly but never consolidate reusable competences -- the pathology the chapter is written to prevent.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational, heavily replicated lesion dissociation from the Balleine lab. Provides the single cleanest instance of the 'dissociable lesion signature' Q-019 makes central to the three-gate hypothesis: excitotoxic lesion of the dorsolateral striatum abolishes habit formation (behaviour reverts to outcome-devaluation-sensitive goal-directed control) while lesion of the dorsomedial striatum leaves habit intact -- a double dissociation of two anatomically distinct striatal territories serving distinct control modes. Confidence held below 0.8 because the DMS/DLS axis is goal-directed-vs-habitual, which maps onto the sensorimotor/action-commitment leg of Q-019 (loop 3 and its automaticity gradient) but is not a 1:1 image of the full sensorium/thought/motor triad, and because rodent instrumental habit must transfer to the REE commit-gate construct.
failure_signatures: If commit-gating were implemented by a single convergent gate rather than separable territories, then removing the putative habit/sensorimotor territory should degrade action selection globally rather than selectively abolishing outcome-insensitive (habitual) responding while sparing goal-directed control -- the opposite of what the DLS lesion produces.

If the DLS territory were a generic motor-output stage rather than a distinct gating locus, DLS lesion should impair lever-pressing capability generally; instead it leaves responding intact but restores outcome sensitivity, indicating loss of a specific control mode, not a motor deficit.

entries.confidence_rationale: Landmark Nature paper (Halassa lab) using optogenetic gain- and loss-of-function plus prefrontal electrophysiology in mice to establish that the mediodorsal (MD) thalamus sustains rule-specific PFC representations by amplifying local intracortical connectivity, without itself relaying categorical rule information -- a thalamic control of functional cortical connectivity dissociable from information relay. This directly grounds Q-019's thought-loop substrate claim, which posits the MD thalamus as the thalamic gate that maintains and protects thought-level (associative) representations. Confidence held at 0.68 because Q-019's specific functional attribution to MD is 'prevents bleed-back into sensorium', whereas Schmitt demonstrates a sustaining/amplifying role; the two are compatible but not identical, and mouse PFC-to-REE-E3 transfer is non-trivial.
failure_signatures: If the thalamus were purely a relay (the single-gate-friendly view in which loops share one undifferentiated thalamic pass-through), then enhancing or suppressing MD activity should scale information throughput uniformly; instead MD manipulation selectively changes rule-representation specificity and behavioural performance without relaying categorical content, indicating a dedicated control function.

If maintenance of thought-level representations required no separate thalamic gate, broadly enhancing PFC excitability should preserve or improve rule specificity; instead it diminishes specificity and performance, showing that non-specific cortical drive is not a substitute for targeted MD amplification.

entries.confidence_rationale: Solid Dunnett-lab lesion study that adds a third dissociable striatal territory to the established DMS (goal-directed) / DLS (habit) pair: the ventrolateral striatum (VLS) is shown necessary for using a Pavlovian stimulus-outcome association to guide behaviour, while sparing both instrumental goal-directed action and habit. Taken with the DMS/DLS literature, it evidences a three-way functional parcellation of the striatum -- three territories with dissociable lesion signatures -- which is the parcellation the three-gate reading of Q-019 predicts over a single convergent gate. Confidence held at 0.6 because the striatal axis here (goal-directed / habit / Pavlovian-incentive) is not the same axis as Q-019's sensorium / thought / motor-commitment triad; it supports dissociability-of-territories in principle rather than the specific three loops.
failure_signatures: If the striatum implemented a single convergent selector, an excitotoxic lesion of any one subregion should produce a graded global deficit across instrumental and Pavlovian control; instead the VLS lesion selectively impairs Pavlovian-stimulus-guided responding while leaving instrumental goal-directed action and habit intact -- a selective, not global, signature.

If the three striatal territories were functionally redundant, VLS loss should be compensated by DMS/DLS; the persistence of the specific Pavlovian deficit indicates non-redundant, dissociable functions.

The most decision-relevant ML paper for REE's specific proposed architecture (frozen upstream encoder + separately-trained policy). Stooke et al. show a self-supervised temporal-contrastive encoder (ATC) can be trained separately from the policy and, held FROZEN, match or beat end-to-end RL -- but only because (a) the encoder objective was temporal-contrastive on control-relevant data and (b) a policy is STILL trained by RL on reward on top. Cuts both ways for REE: strongly supports the decoupled 'frozen e2 encoder + trainable policy head' design (V3-EXQ-737 / H1), while documenting the exact failure mode if the frozen features are not control-relevant (residual H2). Confidence 0.71 -- high relevance, but the two-edged verdict lowers directional confidence.
failure_signatures: Frozen-encoder success in ATC was CONDITIONAL on the encoder being trained with a temporal-contrastive objective on control-relevant observation streams. REE's e2 world-forward contrastive is temporally-contrastive in spirit, but if its features do not expose resource/hazard structure at the 5x5 local-view scale, a frozen-encoder + policy-head build can underperform -- the exact H2 residual.

ATC still trains the policy end-to-end by RL on reward. The paper is therefore ALSO evidence against REE's status quo: a decoupled encoder does NOT remove the need for a reward-trained policy; REE's bias-head is not a substitute for the RL-trained actor ATC always keeps.

Benchmarks are pixel-based DMControl/Atari with dense-ish shaping; REE's partially-observed implicit-reward forager is a harder control regime, so 'frozen encoder suffices' does not transfer automatically.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct human fMRI dissociation of the actor-critic decomposition onto the striatum: ventral striatum carries prediction-error signals whether or not an action is required (critic), while dorsal striatum carries them only when an instrumental action must be chosen (actor). This is the single closest biological anchor for the autopsy's 'dorsal-striatal RPE-driven action learning' reference -- it localizes action-learning to a dedicated substrate distinct from value-prediction. Confidence high; below 0.9 only because fMRI is a coarse, correlational readout and the actor/critic identity rests on a model-based regressor analysis rather than causal manipulation.
failure_signatures: fMRI BOLD is coarse and correlational; the actor/critic assignment is inferred from where TD-model regressors fit, not from lesion/causal dissociation. A skeptic could argue the dorsal-striatal signal is action-contingent value rather than a separate actor learner.

The dissociation shows action-learning is *localized to a distinct substrate*, but it does not by itself prove that a prediction-only representation cannot support action -- that negative is REE's H1 to demonstrate empirically (V3-EXQ-737), not something the fMRI establishes.
Human instrumental-conditioning task with explicit rewards; transfer to REE's foraging env (implicit resource reward, partial observability) is a formal import, not a measured equivalence.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong computational grounding for how a dorsal-striatal actor implements credit assignment: OpAL extends the classic actor-critic with a DUAL opponent actor (D1/Go and D2/NoGo populations, the direct/indirect pathways) that separately accumulate positive and negative action values, with dopamine gain-modulating each. It unifies learning and choice-incentive effects the standard actor-critic cannot. Directly grounds the direct/indirect-pathway credit-assignment leg of the pull. Confidence 0.74 (not higher) because the opponent-actor refinement is more architecture than REE needs for the FIRST build -- the load-bearing import is 'a dedicated actor with a value-baseline critic', and OpAL's two-channel detail is a second-order enrichment REE may or may not need.
failure_signatures: OpAL's dual opponent actor is a refinement REE does not need to reach for first: the minimal owed build is a single actor + critic baseline. Importing the D1/D2 opponent split prematurely risks re-instantiating the over-elaboration anti-pattern (governance-mass before capability) the graveyard doc warns against.

OpAL is fit to behavioural/pharmacological data (probabilistic RL, effort-based choice, motor-skill learning); it is a model OF dopamine effects, not a demonstration that an artificial agent needs opponent actors to forage. Transfer to REE competence is indirect.

The interactive learning x incentive effects OpAL captures depend on dopamine as a shared gain term across both actor channels -- a single modulator -- which sits in tension with REE's incommensurable-channel commitment if imported literally.

entries.confidence_rationale: The foundational ML grounding: the policy-gradient theorem establishes that a separately-parameterized policy, optimized directly on expected return, converges to a local optimum -- and that an actor-critic (policy + learned value baseline) is the low-variance form. Crucially, the paper motivates policy gradient by noting the value-function-ONLY approach (derive the policy from an approximated value function) had proven theoretically intractable under function approximation. This is the exact formal reason REE's bias-head-over-prediction-features is impoverished: there is no separately-trained policy object being pushed uphill on return. Confidence 0.8 -- the theorem is canonical and the mapping to REE's gap is tight; slightly reserved because it is a formal guarantee, not evidence that policy gradient clears REE's specific env.
failure_signatures: Policy gradient guarantees convergence to a LOCAL optimum only; a policy head over frozen prediction features could still converge to a poor local optimum if those features do not linearly separate the control-relevant structure -- the residual H2 risk (feature adequacy), not resolved by the theorem.

REINFORCE (which REE's bias-head uses) IS a policy-gradient method -- so the gap is NOT 'REE uses the wrong family'. The gap is that REE applies it to a thin bias head over a frozen prediction encoder with no value baseline (critic), i.e. high-variance, low-capacity, and representation-mismatched. The theorem clarifies the fix (full trainable policy + value baseline), it does not indict the algorithm class.
Formal/theoretical result; sample-efficiency and exploration under partial observability (REE's actual bottleneck regime) are outside its scope.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily-replicated Science paper establishing that midbrain dopamine neurons broadcast a reward-prediction-error (RPE) that functions as a dedicated teaching signal for value/action learning, formalized as TD error. Grounds the translation-gap claim that biological action learning is driven by a distinct reward-error signal, NOT emergent from sensory world-prediction. Confidence high on the biology; slightly below 0.9 because the mapping to REE's specific gap (a reward-RPE-trained policy substrate) is a formal import, and Schultz's RPE is itself a *prediction* error -- the distinction REE must honour is reward-prediction-error-for-action vs sensory-transition-prediction, which the paper supports but does not adjudicate for an artificial substrate.
failure_signatures: The dopamine RPE is a scalar teaching signal; a naive REE import risks collapsing REE's deliberately incommensurable error channels (ARC-021/MECH-069) into one reward scalar. The lesson to import is the *existence of a dedicated reward-error teacher for action*, not a single global objective.

Schultz's RPE is a reward-*prediction* error -- it is still a prediction. This does NOT license the reading that REE already has it because it predicts the world: REE's e2 world-forward contrastive loss predicts sensory transitions, which carries no reward signal and cannot teach action-value. The gap is a reward-error channel wired to a policy, which REE lacks entirely.

Primate/rodent electrophysiology; whether an RPE teaching signal is *sufficient* to recover foraging competence in REE's partially-observed 5x5-local-view env is untested (this is exactly the residual H2 question 738 partially addressed).

entries.confidence_rationale: The strongest CAUSAL grounding for MECH-456's trigger: optogenetic silencing/un-silencing plus two-photon imaging show ACC prediction-error signals are specifically REQUIRED for single-trial switching between two response rules, and the PE signal is LARGER preceding successful transitions -- a graded, causal, single-trial mechanism. This maps onto both DVs in spirit: PE-driven overtake (trigger) and a graded consequence (larger PE -> more successful switch, cf. DV2's graded re-acquisition). Held below 0.8 because task-rule switching in mice is a cognitive-state switch, not an entity/self<->world-config rebinding, and the ACC-circuit specificity does not map onto REE's binder locus.
failure_signatures: Task-switching between two response rules is a cognitive-STATE switch, not a rebinding of an entity/self<->world-configuration; the abstract 'switch when PE says the current model is wrong' transfers, but the bound thing differs.
The causal circuit is ACC + a specific disinhibitory interneuron motif in mouse cortex; REE has no homologous locus, so the mechanism grounds the PRINCIPLE, not REE's implementation.
Larger PE preceding successful transitions is a graded correlate but the single-trial causal test (opto) is on the switch itself, not on a downstream re-acquisition-latency metric like MECH-456 DV2.

entries.confidence_rationale: The normative-inference justification for MECH-456's rebinding rule: online Bayesian inference over an unbounded number of latent causes infers a NEW cause when the current one stops explaining the data, reproducing renewal/latent-inhibition and other context-dependent conditioning results. This is exactly 'drop the currently-bound configuration when a competitor better explains the situation', at the level of principle. Held below 0.75 because the timescale (across-trial conditioning contexts) and domain (associative learning) differ from MECH-456's within-episode perceptual binding, and the paper is a model of behavioural data rather than a neural or architectural test.
failure_signatures: Latent-cause inference here operates over conditioning CONTEXTS across trials (renewal, latent inhibition) -- a slower, associative-learning timescale than MECH-456's within-episode rebinding of a perceptual self<->world-config binding.

It is a normative Bayesian model fit to behavioural phenomena, not a neural or architectural mechanism; the 'switch to a new cause' is inferential, and the paper's own twist is that this capacity is LIMITED (absent in young animals / after hippocampal lesion), which MECH-456 does not model.

'A competitor overtakes' in MECH-456 is a comparison between concurrently-available configurations; latent-cause inference is more naturally 'the current cause stops fitting, infer a (possibly new) one' -- adjacent but not identical framings.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily-replicated demonstration that a perceived object is a persisting FILE that is actively re-linked and updated across time, motion, and occlusion -- not a fixed one-shot binding. This grounds MECH-456's core premise ('binding is maintained-not-intrinsic'). Held below 0.7 because object-file reviewing establishes the UPDATABILITY / maintained-correspondence half of the claim strongly but speaks only obliquely to the SWITCHING half (a competitor world-configuration overtaking and forcing a re-bind); and because it is a 1992 visual-attention psychophysics result whose transfer to a latent self<->world-config binder is analogical, not measured.
failure_signatures: Object-file reviewing shows correspondence is maintained and updated across a gap, but the paradigm does not force a competitor to OVERTAKE the current file -- it is largely evidence for continuity, the opposite pole from rebinding, so it under-tests the switch trigger MECH-456 asserts.

The 'object' is an attended visual token over a brief display (hundreds of ms); MECH-456's bound thing is a self-anchored world-configuration in a trained latent architecture. Equating the two is a formal import, not a measured equivalence.
No prediction-error / competitor-support variable is manipulated; the mechanism that decides WHEN to keep vs re-link the file is not isolated here.

entries.confidence_rationale: A computational + model-based-fMRI account in which endogenous perceptual switches are DRIVEN by prediction errors accruing from residual evidence for the currently-suppressed interpretation, outperforming classic adaptation/noise models and localising the PE signal to frontal cortex. This is the closest mechanistic analogue of MECH-456's asserted trigger: the competitor overtakes when the current configuration accrues prediction error. The predictive-coding framing is also architecturally congenial to REE. Held below 0.8 because bistable perception switches between two fixed interpretations of a CONSTANT ambiguous stimulus with no ground-truth winner, whereas MECH-456 requires an exogenous ground-truth overtake -- the trigger transfers cleanly, the 'which is correct' semantics do not.
failure_signatures: Bistable perception has no ground-truth correct percept -- switching is endogenous and either interpretation is 'right'. MECH-456's rebinding must track a TRUE competitor that genuinely becomes better-supported by the environment; the paper's mechanism explains switching-on-PE but not tracking-the-true-winner (that is DV1 of the functional test, un-addressed here).
The PE signal was localised to inferior frontal gyri / anterior insula via model-based fMRI regressors -- correlational, and in a perceptual-report task, not a self<->world-config binding.
Model comparison favoured predictive coding over adaptation+noise, but bistable dynamics are notoriously fit by multiple models; the win is evidential, not decisive.

entries.confidence_rationale: A rigorous meta-analysis establishing that perception is systematically biased toward the recent past (serial dependence), tuned by time, space, feature-similarity, and attention. For MECH-456 this is genuinely two-directional: it is strong evidence for the STABILITY COUNTERWEIGHT that a rebinding mechanism must overcome, and therefore for the DESIGN choice of a threshold (rebind only when a competitor decisively overtakes, not on every fluctuation) rather than free chatter. But on its own face serial dependence is a persistence/hysteresis phenomenon -- the force OPPOSING rebinding -- so it does not directly support that rebinding occurs, only that if it does it must clear a hysteresis band. Marked mixed for that reason.
failure_signatures: Serial dependence is, at face value, evidence for perceptual STICKINESS -- the opposite of rebinding. A skeptic could read it as showing the system resists switching, i.e. as pressure AGAINST MECH-456's re-bind-on-overtake dynamic rather than for it.

The phenomenon is characterised on low-level continuous features (orientation, numerosity, face identity) in human psychophysics, not on discrete self<->world-configuration bindings; the 'threshold/hysteresis' transfer is a design analogy, not a measured property of any binder.
Meta-analysis of many small-N studies with heterogeneous paradigms; individual differences are large, so the magnitude of the hysteresis a binder should emulate is not pinned down.

Empirical fMRI study (ages 4-10) that directly challenges the strict back-to-front reading INV-088 leans on: it finds pronounced development at BOTH ends of the sensory-association gradient, not sensory-first-then-association. This weakens any claim that the world-representation must fully differentiate before the evaluator begins maturing. However, INV-088's actual assertion is a functional BOUND (evaluator quality bounded by differentiation), which is compatible with concurrent co-development so long as the bound holds -- so the study is a genuine caveat on the ordering premise rather than a refutation of the bound. Logged 'mixed' at moderate confidence because it is a real, well-powered counter-signal on the timing story while not measuring the bound itself.
failure_signatures: Development was pronounced at both the perceptual (visual) and abstract (medial prefrontal) ends of the sensory-association gradient in 4-10 year olds, contradicting the classical view -- which INV-088's ordering premise invokes -- that sensory areas develop first and association areas last.

The study measures functional network segregation/integration, not evaluator readout quality as a function of representational differentiation, so it can neither confirm nor refute the causal bound; it only removes strict temporal precedence as supporting evidence.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-authority multimodal Neuron review establishing the sensorimotor-to-association axis of cortical maturation as a robust, evolutionarily rooted developmental program: lower-order sensory/unimodal cortices mature before higher-order transmodal association cortices, and this ordering exists precisely to enhance feature differentiation between the two. Maps cleanly onto INV-088's premise that world-feature representation (E1/z_world, sensory-like) differentiates before the goal/evaluator (E3, association/PFC-like) can be productively trained. Confidence held below 0.8 because the review evidences the maturational ordering and the differentiation-enhancement, but does not directly test the FUNCTIONAL bound (an evaluator trained on poorly-differentiated input noise-fits) that INV-088 asserts; mapping_fidelity weighted heavily as this is an architectural claim.
failure_signatures: The review documents maturational timing (sensory-before-association) and enhanced feature variation, but does not measure evaluator/value-readout quality as a function of upstream representational differentiation, so it cannot by itself confirm the strict bound (evaluator quality strictly bounded by z_world differentiation) vs merely a temporal correlation.

The same protracted association-cortex plasticity that supports the ordering is shown to confer psychopathology risk, indicating the sensory-first program is not uniformly protective -- a poorly-differentiated-but-still-plastic association stage is a documented failure mode rather than a guaranteed clean sequence.

entries.confidence_rationale: The tethering hypothesis supplies the MECHANISM behind INV-088's ordering premise: sensory hierarchies form under strong molecular-gradient and early-activity constraints, while distributed association networks that fill the gaps are 'untethered' from those constraints and mature late. This explains WHY the evaluator (association-like E3) develops after and is scaffolded by the differentiated sensory representation (E1/z_world), rather than merely asserting that it does. Confidence moderate (0.6) because it is an evolutionary/developmental hypothesis paper, and the untethering story supports the ordering/scaffolding premise but is one inferential step removed from the functional bound INV-088 states.
failure_signatures: The tethering hypothesis is explicitly framed as a hypothesis with acknowledged limitations; it argues association networks are freed from the gradients that build sensory hierarchies, which could equally be read as association representations being LESS constrained by upstream sensory differentiation -- a reading that would tension INV-088's strict bound rather than support it.

The paper is about cross-species evolution and large-scale network topology, not about training dynamics of an evaluator on graded-quality input, so it provides no direct measurement of evaluator degradation under poor upstream differentiation.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the computational formalization of exactly what INV-088 claims: the generalization error of a value function is provably bounded by the quality of the underlying state representation, quantified via 'effective dimension'. In REE terms z_world IS the state representation and the harm/benefit/goal evaluators ARE value-function-like readouts, so the domain match is direct (low transfer risk). Confidence 0.72 rather than higher because the paper's representation-quality construct (effective dimension / generalization-approximation tradeoff) is related to but not identical with INV-088's 'task-relevant differentiation' (decodability of harm-relevant world features), and because a formal bound existing does not itself prove that the REE substrate operates in the regime where the bound is tight.
failure_signatures: The bound characterizes a generalization-vs-approximation TRADEOFF: representations that generalize well can approximate poorly and vice versa, so 'more differentiated' is not monotonically 'better evaluator' in all regimes -- a nuance that could produce non-monotone evaluator-quality-vs-differentiation curves, echoing the high-variance/non-monotone cross-seed coupling already seen in V3-EXQ-744a.

Effective dimension bounds generalization across states; it does not directly certify that a poorly-differentiated representation forces evaluator noise-fitting during TRAINING, which is INV-088's specific developmental-training failure mode.
