Canonical, theoretically-grounded result with a general (task-agnostic) guarantee, so transfer risk is low. Mixed relative to MECH-457: it WEAKENS a naive 'the BC PASS is the answer' reading of 748/749 (pure cloning compounds error quadratically under covariate shift), while SUPPORTING MECH-457's insistence that a dedicated RL/interactive-correction loop -- not imitation alone -- is load-bearing. This is the key interpretive caveat on the whole discrimination portfolio.
failure_signatures: A policy trained by supervised behavior cloning to error rate epsilon under the expert's state distribution can incur cost that grows as O(epsilon * T^2) over a horizon T, because its own mistakes carry it into states the expert never visited and never demonstrated -- covariate shift / compounding error.

The guarantee that removes the quadratic blow-up (DAgger, linear in T) REQUIRES an interactive expert queryable at states the learner actually visits; a fixed demonstration set (as used by REE's BC arms) does not provide that, so the offline-BC ceiling still applies.

High held-out action-match accuracy (REE 748: 0.802, 749: 0.872) does NOT certify closed-loop competence -- per-step accuracy is the exact quantity that compounds; a strong action-match number can still yield a policy that drifts off the expert manifold at deployment.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct, well-replicated precedent for the exact pattern the 748/749 BC arms displayed: a small demonstration set bootstraps a dedicated RL policy through the hard-exploration wall that reward-only RL cannot cross in-budget, and the combined learner then matches or exceeds the demonstrator. High mapping fidelity to REE's discriminated cause (learning-signal/exploration bootstrap, not representation). Discounted for Atari-to-REE transfer and for the fact that DQfD blends imitation WITH continued RL rather than pure BC.
failure_signatures: DQfD's early performance is upper-bounded by demonstration quality and coverage; on games where the human demonstrations were poor, the pretraining advantage was small and pure RL eventually caught up.

It requires the supervised large-margin loss plus continued TD learning to avoid the demonstrations biasing the value function toward unseen actions -- pure supervised cloning without the RL loss would inherit the covariate-shift problem (see the DAgger entry).
The bootstrap accelerates learning but does not by itself prove the substrate can learn WITHOUT a teacher -- it is silent on whether an unsupervised explorer could reach the same competence.

entries.confidence_rationale: Influential, well-replicated demonstration that an intrinsic-curiosity bonus solves sparse-reward tasks vanilla A2C cannot, which supports the viability of the unsupervised-explorer path. Marked mixed rather than supports because the same line of work exposes curiosity's structural fragilities (the noisy-TV problem; dependence on the inverse-dynamics feature space) that make it an unreliable universal fix -- exactly the uncertainty the H-optim leg must resolve. Confidence tempered by Atari/VizDoom-to-REE transfer.
failure_signatures: The forward-model prediction-error bonus is attracted to inherently unpredictable stimuli (the 'noisy-TV' problem): an agent can be trapped maximising curiosity at a stochastic source instead of exploring task-relevant structure.

Curiosity is only useful to the extent the inverse-dynamics feature space captures action-controllable variation; if the learned features miss the task-relevant degrees of freedom, the bonus does not guide exploration toward the goal.
Demonstrated on VizDoom and Super Mario; sparse-reward success is task-structure-dependent and does not guarantee in-budget success on an arbitrary new environment such as REE forage.

entries.confidence_rationale: Biological grounding for the scaffold path: a neuroimaging synthesis arguing observational/imitative action acquisition recruits the same fronto-striatal (and dorsal-frontoparietal, cerebellar) machinery as trial-and-error learning, so a developmental-scaffold/imitation route to REE's actor-critic substrate is biologically faithful rather than an ad-hoc engineering shortcut. Confidence moderate: it is a review (not a single strong causal study), and it flags an inverted ventral-striatal observational prediction-error that complicates naive transfer.
failure_signatures: The ventral striatum shows an INVERTED coding pattern for observational prediction errors relative to individually-experienced reward prediction errors (Burke et al.), so observational and first-person RL are not simply the same computation with a different input -- naive 'imitation reuses the RPE teacher unchanged' is too strong.

The review draws on healthy-adult neuroimaging (correlational BOLD), not lesion/electrophysiology or developmental data, so the causal necessity of the fronto-striatal pathway for observational action acquisition is asserted rather than demonstrated.

It distinguishes imitation (replicating observed actions WITHOUT outcome processing) from observational learning (processing others' action-outcome contingencies) -- REE's behavior-cloning arms are the former, so the review's outcome-processing observational-learning findings map only partially onto the BC result.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong, heavily-replicated result (ICLR, first >human-mean Montezuma without demonstrations) that a dedicated RL policy plus a purely unsupervised exploration bonus can clear hard sparse-reward. Directly bears on the live GOV-FANOUT-1 discrimination (is an expert teacher necessary, or is unsupervised exploration merely too weak). Confidence held below 0.8 by domain transfer: Atari pixel hard-exploration at ~1e9 frames and large parallel actor budgets is a very different regime from REE D3 5x5 forage in-budget.
failure_signatures: RND's SOTA on Montezuma required hundreds of parallel environments and ~1.6-2 billion frames; the exploration bonus is a large-compute solution, not a cheap in-budget one -- so 'unsupervised exploration is sufficient' does not imply 'sufficient in REE's per-arm budget'.
RND is susceptible to the same detachment/derailment failure as other novelty bonuses: the bonus fades as states become familiar, so it can under-explore late-appearing bottleneck states.

Gains were confined to the exploration-hard sparse-reward subset (Montezuma, Gravitar, Venture, Private Eye); on Pitfall! it still scored ~0, i.e. some sparse-reward structures resist even a strong unsupervised explorer.

Supports the separateness + postnatal-refinement premise: nociceptive circuitry functions at birth but undergoes considerable postnatal organization, including the separation of tactile and nociceptive afferent input and maturation of inhibitory control, before full discrimination of noxious from tactile input is possible. Secondary/supporting rather than decisive: the paper's focus is injury-induced plasticity, and the developmental point is scaffolding for that, not its main measured result.
failure_signatures: Evidence is drawn largely from rodent neonatal-injury models; the timetable and even the direction of some plasticity effects may not transfer cleanly to the human harm-representation maturation INV-089 posits.

entries.confidence_rationale: A focused review arguing the nociceptive system develops on its own terms and -- unlike other sensory systems -- cannot rely on prolonged activity-dependent shaping through repeated noxious input. This is close to a direct statement of INV-089's core: harm-evaluation quality is bounded by a maturation trajectory distinct from the exteroceptive (z_world) one. Confidence held below higher because it is a narrative review, not a single decisive measurement, and 'distinct timetable' is asserted across heterogeneous sub-findings.
failure_signatures: The review notes neurophysiological (EEG) and hemodynamic (fMRI/NIRS) measures of infant nociceptive development are 'not always consistent', so the exact ordering and rate of nociceptive-cortex maturation relative to exteroceptive cortex is not pinned to a single agreed curve.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct human intracranial-EEG evidence that nociceptive input reaches sensory and limbic cortex in parallel via anatomically distinct ascending routes (spino-thalamic + spino-parabrachial), supporting a harm stream routed separately from exteroceptive processing. Strong source (iEEG in humans, the exact paper cited in the claim). Confidence held below source_quality because the paper is about adult cortical dynamics, not the developmental-differentiation-bounds-quality mechanism INV-089 actually asserts -- it grounds the separateness premise, not the maturation-order conclusion.
failure_signatures: The paper characterizes the temporal dynamics of an already-mature adult nociceptive network; it provides no developmental time-course, so it cannot by itself establish that z_harm differentiation matures on a schedule distinct from z_world's -- only that the two streams are anatomically separable in the adult.

entries.confidence_rationale: The most direct counter-evidence found: rats behaviorally preferred higher-value goals, yet dorsal CA1/CA3 place-cell activity was NOT modulated by goal value. The authors explicitly argue place cells form a 'value-free map' that links to value 'in other parts of the brain' -- i.e., value is applied downstream, the exact alternative MECH-073 denies. High confidence as a genuine conflict source; this is why the backlog flags MECH-073 active_conflict.
failure_signatures: Place-cell firing showed goal-related out-of-field activity but no value modulation; value affected behavior without a corresponding hippocampal value signal, directly instantiating a 'value-free spatial map + downstream value' architecture.

entries.confidence_rationale: Reward value demonstrably reshapes the hippocampal place map itself -- faster reorganization/stabilization and value-selective replay when a goal carries large reward. This supports MECH-073's core: value/valence is woven into map geometry, not merely read off downstream. Confidence moderate: value modulates map DYNAMICS (rate, field appearance, replay), which is compatible with, but does not uniquely establish, valence being INTRINSIC to the map's geometric code as opposed to an extrinsically-driven reshaping.
failure_signatures: Value modulation of map reorganization could be driven by an extrinsic reward/dopamine signal acting ON the hippocampus, which would be consistent with a 'downstream value applied to a value-free map' account -- the very alternative MECH-073 denies. The study shows value affects the map but not that value is represented within the map's own geometry.

entries.confidence_rationale: Mixed and indirect. On one hand valence is legible in hippocampal CA1 activity patterns (negative vs neutral produce distinct/over-similar CA1 pattern-completion signatures), consistent with valence being carried in the hippocampal representation. On the other, the valence effect is driven by amygdala + mPFC modulation of CA1 at encoding -- i.e., extrinsic affective circuitry shapes the hippocampal valence signature, which cuts toward the downstream/applied view. Low-moderate confidence: human fMRI, developmental/clinical sample, tangential task.
failure_signatures: The hippocampal valence signature is reported as MODULATED BY amygdala and mPFC coupling at encoding, so the study cannot separate valence intrinsic to the hippocampal map from valence imposed on the hippocampus by extrinsic affective structures.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical account of a low-dimensional MODE variable (LC-NE tonic vs phasic gain) that does bidirectional explore/exploit arbitration -- including switching exploration OFF to consolidate exploitation, the half a novelty bonus cannot provide. Biological/modelling, transfer by analogy.
failure_signatures: A per-step novelty bonus can only push exploration UP; it cannot switch exploration off and consolidate into competent exploitation -- the phasic-mode half of adaptive gain.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly on-point: a self-generated goal frontier solves hard procedurally-generated MiniGrid sparse tasks where count-based/RND-style bonuses stay at floor -- the unsupervised analogue of what BC achieved for REE. Moderate build (goal-proposer + goal-conditioned policy). Needs a parameterizable goal space.
failure_signatures: AMIGo/goal-generation assume a parameterizable goal space (e.g. (x,y) target cells); if the useful competence is not expressible as a reachable goal-state the curriculum cannot target it.

entries.confidence_rationale: Human fMRI: exploration is implemented as a separable MODE with its own substrate (frontopolar cortex / IPS) distinct from the value/exploitation system (striatum/vmPFC). Supports mode-as-distinct-mechanism; but the behavioural model fit was a softmax temperature (bonus-like), so it argues substrate separability more than mode>bonus.
failure_signatures: The fitted computational model was a softmax exploration parameter (random exploration), so the paper evidences a mode SUBSTRATE more than it proves a committed-mode latent outperforms a temperature/bonus.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical documentation that pure curiosity is reward-agnostic (noisy-TV) and succeeds only where environment design aligns novelty with reward; directly explains why REE's ICM arm failed and why the whole novelty class plateaus. Weakens 'build more curiosity'.
failure_signatures: A purely curious agent that finds a stochastic/unpredictable source (a noisy TV) parks in front of it forever, because prediction error stays permanently high -- the noisy-TV problem.
Forward-model prediction-error curiosity (ICM) is the most noisy-TV-vulnerable member of the class; REE's ac_zworld_icm arm reproduced this (0.22, sub-floor).

entries.confidence_rationale: Produces a reusable skill library from unsupervised exploration (a capability RND lacks) that accelerates downstream tasks -- but the diversity payoff is largest in high-dim continuous control; on a tiny discrete forage-world few distinct skills exist and RND may already cover them, and DIAYN is the heaviest build of the candidate classes.
failure_signatures: DIAYN's diversity objective and reuse payoff shine in high-dim continuous control; on a small discrete gridworld the number of usefully-distinct skills is small and a novelty bonus may already reach them, so marginal gain over RND may be modest at high build cost.

entries.confidence_rationale: Nature paper; names detachment/derailment as WHY novelty bonuses plateau and shows an archive+return mechanism clears a floor->competent gap novelty cannot (>43k vs ~11k RND on Montezuma). Directly on-point for the class-choice; buildable in a small gridworld.
failure_signatures: Detachment: novelty/intrinsic-reward algorithms forget how to reach previously visited promising states once the local bonus is consumed, so the bonus stops pulling the agent back to the true frontier.
Derailment: stochastic exploratory actions prevent reliable RETURN to a known good state to explore onward from it.

entries.confidence_rationale: Establishes learning-progress as a distinct, competence-directed intrinsic drive (abandons both mastered AND unlearnable regions -- escapes the noisy-TV trap novelty falls into). Lightest build (a goal-selection bookkeeping layer). Framework/robotics evidence, not a MiniGrid floor number.
failure_signatures: A plain novelty/count bonus keeps rewarding irreducible-noise regions (noisy-TV); learning-progress instead tracks reducible error and abandons unlearnable regions -- the property novelty lacks.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational warrant that temporal abstraction is a distinct capability (faster credit assignment, structured exploration over a semi-MDP). But silent on where good options come from; demonstrations use hand-specified options. Supports the framework, not a floor->competent number.
failure_signatures: The options framework is silent on option DISCOVERY; its speedups are shown with hand-specified options, so it does not by itself close a floor->competent gap without a source of good options.

entries.confidence_rationale: Normative theory giving the priority rule (utility = gain x need) for WHICH transitions a credit sweep should update first; reproduces reverse-replay-after-reward. Directly upgrades REE's existing backward_credit_sweep (prioritise by utility/TD-error) -- extend, not duplicate. Theoretical, not a benchmark.
failure_signatures: An undirected per-step novelty bonus spreads learning uniformly; a utility-prioritised backward sweep concentrates updates on exactly the reward-relevant transitions, which is what makes replay efficient.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical biological evidence that the brain propagates reward backward along a just-experienced trajectory via reverse replay -- the exact operation a novelty bonus lacks and the archetype of REE's existing backward_credit_sweep. Grounds the credit-assignment lever; indirect (observational, not an RL benchmark).
failure_signatures: A per-step novelty bonus has no mechanism to propagate a terminal reward backward along the trajectory that earned it; reverse replay is that missing operation.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong source (first method above-average-human on Montezuma without demos); high mapping fidelity to REE's RND arm; but its own framing (bonus rewards coverage, not task success, and vanishes as states become familiar) predicts the plateau REE observed, so it weakens the 'more novelty closes the gap' reading.
failure_signatures: The RND bonus rewards state coverage, not task success; it is non-stationary and vanishes as states become familiar, so it does not convert coverage into competent exploitation once the space is covered.
RND on Montezuma succeeds because progress requires visiting new rooms (novelty aligned with reward by construction); a sparse-pellet forager gives only partial alignment.

entries.confidence_rationale: Biological instantiation of the options-framework primitives (learned start/stop bracketing = initiation/termination of a chunked sequence). Grounds temporal abstraction as a real learned mechanism the brain uses to consolidate practised behaviour; neuroscience, not an RL benchmark.
failure_signatures: Provides mechanistic grounding for chunking/termination but is observational neuroscience -- it grounds the class rather than quantifying a floor->competent delta.

Independent (German) review corroborating the sensory-first / executive-last ordering and hitting INV-064's most specific behavioural prediction head-on: maximum gray-matter density is reached first in primary sensorimotor cortex and last in prefrontal cortex, while subcortical limbic/reward systems mature earlier, producing a mature-subcortical / immature-PFC imbalance that accounts for adolescent risk-taking persisting past sensory-motor competence. Held to 0.66 because it is a general-audience synthesis (not primary data), the imbalance model is one dominant account among competitors, and it documents ordering + behavioural correlate rather than the necessity claim.
failure_signatures: The mature-subcortical / immature-PFC imbalance is the dominant but not the only account of adolescent risk-taking (pure incentive-processing and social-context accounts compete). If risk-taking is driven mainly by incentive salience independent of the maturational lag, INV-064's specific 'risk-taking persists past sensory-motor competence BECAUSE E3 is still integrating' reading loses this support.

entries.confidence_rationale: Large empirical (not review) resting-state fMRI study (n=1033, ages 8-23) showing intrinsic cortical activity refines from synchronized/high-amplitude to sparse/low-amplitude heterochronously ALONG the sensorimotor-association axis, coupled to intracortical myelin maturation, with environmental-disadvantage effects diverging most across the axis in mid-adolescence. Converts the ordering from review-level to primary-data support and directly instantiates INV-064's environment-times-window prediction. Held to 0.74 because intrinsic-activity refinement is a plasticity PROXY (not a competence measure), the environment associations are correlational, and it shares authorship (Sydnor/Satterthwaite lab) with the 2021 review, so the two entries are not fully independent.
failure_signatures: Intrinsic-activity amplitude decline is used as a proxy for declining plasticity; if that proxy dissociates from actual learning capacity along the axis, the mapping to a competence-building curriculum weakens.

The environment-times-axis interaction is correlational (neighborhood disadvantage, not manipulated experience). If the disproportionate-early-experience effect INV-064 predicts is really driven by confounds rather than differential plasticity along the axis, this support softens.

entries.confidence_rationale: Landmark Neuron review synthesising multimodal human neuroimaging into the sensorimotor-to-association (S-A) axis of cortical development: maturation proceeds hierarchically from lower-order primary/unimodal sensorimotor cortices to higher-order transmodal association cortices, tracking an evolutionarily-rooted axis and the hierarchical unfolding of plasticity-related events. This is close to a direct external instantiation of INV-064's E1/E2 (sensory/motor) -> E3 (executive/association) maturational ordering. High source quality; mapping fidelity strong for the ORDERING and its functional/clinical significance, held below 0.85 because the review is observational and does not test the NECESSITY / curriculum-causality that is INV-064's strong claim.
failure_signatures: The S-A axis establishes temporal ordering and its correlates, not curriculum necessity. If a competent transmodal (E3-analogue) system could be built without prior maturation of sensorimotor (E1/E2-analogue) cortices -- e.g. via a training regime that front-loads association-level structure -- INV-064's necessity claim would be weakened while the observed developmental ordering remained true.

entries.confidence_rationale: Classic in-vivo single-unit recording with pharmacological identification (Jacobs lab, independent of the Hobson lineage that dominates the existing MECH-204 entries). Quantitatively pins the depth of the REM serotonergic withdrawal: identified serotonergic neurons fire at 4.49 spikes/s in active waking, 2.14 in SWS, and 0.20 in REM -- an ~95% reduction that grounds the 'zero-point' premise. Held below 0.8 because the recorded nucleus is raphe magnus (a bulbospinal / pain-modulatory nucleus), not the forebrain-projecting dorsal raphe that carries the precision-relevant tone, and because the paper documents the SUBSTRATE FACT of withdrawal, not the active-vs-permissive functional role that is the live MECH-204 conflict.
failure_signatures: If precision-relevant 5-HT tone during REM is carried by dorsal-raphe or median-raphe subpopulations that do NOT go fully silent (the ~12% atypical DR neurons documented by Sakai & Crochet 2001), the near-zero raphe magnus rate would overstate the depth of the forebrain zero-point and the strict tonic_5ht=0 idealisation would need softening.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly informs the active-vs-permissive crux of the MECH-204 conflict but from a different system and in the opposite 5-HT direction, so it is genuinely mixed. It supports the INSTRUCTIVE (non-permissive) half -- serotonergic manipulation does not merely open a plasticity gate, it sculpts a specific synaptic regime (mature GluN2A / GABAA-alpha1 dominance), creating a NOVEL state rather than reverting to a juvenile one. But the DIRECTION conflicts with MECH-204: here elevated 5-HT is the instructive signal that enables plasticity, whereas MECH-204 posits 5-HT WITHDRAWAL as the instructive signal that sets the recalibration zero-point. Confidence is deliberately low (0.48): the transfer is a cross-system conceptual analogy (chronic developmental OD plasticity in rat V1 vs phasic online precision-prior recalibration in REM), not a mechanistic test.
failure_signatures: The instructive reading transfers only at the level of 'serotonergic state shapes the character of the plastic regime, not just its gate'. If MECH-204's zero-point turns out to be purely permissive at the precision-prior level (a threshold that recalibration crosses, with no serotonin-shaped structure to the resulting reference), then this paper's instructive finding in V1 is simply about a different phenomenon and offers no support.

If the relevant sign for online precision recalibration is that HIGH 5-HT stabilises priors and LOW 5-HT destabilises them (consistent with fluoxetine here raising 5-HT to drive plasticity), the directionality of MECH-204 (withdrawal instructs) would be under tension and would need the REM-specific, phasic, forebrain mechanism to be genuinely distinct from the chronic tonic OD-plasticity mechanism.

Causal optogenetic evidence that midbrain dopaminergic input to hippocampus enhances place-cell assembly reactivation and stabilizes spatial memory at newly learned goal locations -- directly supporting the 'stability / durability' sub-component of MECH-232's representational-expansion claim. Held below the Krishnan entry because it targets reactivation/persistence (the stability leg) rather than density/over-representation, and does not address the implicit-vs-explicit-gradient CRUX at all.
failure_signatures: Demonstrates DA-driven stabilization of goal-location representations but says nothing about whether that stability substitutes for, or is distinct from, an explicit positive-valence tag -- the MECH-232 dissociation is untested.

Effect is on offline reactivation during sleep/rest and subsequent recall; MECH-232 as instantiated in REE is an online CEM-scoring / terrain mechanism, so the mapping crosses a consolidation-vs-online-planning boundary.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct, causal, cellular-resolution test of the exact mechanism MECH-232 asserts: a VTA-dopaminergic reward-proximity signal in CA1 that governs the fidelity/stability/over-representation of the reward map rather than writing an explicit positive-valence field. Bidirectional evidence (extinction removes it; optogenetic VTA-DA inhibition reproduces it). Confidence held below 0.9 by rodent-to-REE transfer and because the paper does not directly dissociate 'implicit representational-quality expansion' from an explicit valence gradient the way MECH-232's CRUX demands -- it shows the correlates, not the approach-behaviour dissociation.
failure_signatures: The paper measures encoding-side map quality (over-representation, remapping rate, trial-to-trial reliability) but does not test whether the DA-modulated representation drives approach behaviour in the absence of an explicit positive gradient -- so it supports the representational-expansion premise of MECH-232 without confirming the load-bearing 'this expansion IS the approach mechanism' claim.

Reward-proximity DA signal is a ramping, expectation-dependent scalar; a reader could interpret 'reward proximity' as itself a graded valence-like signal, blurring the very implicit-vs-explicit distinction MECH-232 rests on.

entries.confidence_rationale: Empirical human fMRI evidence that intrinsic curiosity engages the same midbrain-dopaminergic + hippocampal circuit as extrinsic reward and enhances hippocampus-dependent encoding -- grounding SD-025's placement of a curiosity drive ON the hippocampal layer AND its coupling to the SD-024 dopaminergic-expansion substrate (the ARC-057 SD-024 x SD-025 pairing). Held at 0.66 because curiosity here is an epistemic-state manipulation (trivia questions) validated by memory benefit, not a spatial trajectory-scoring bias favoring representational density; the mapping to SD-025's mechanism is by shared circuit and shared functional role, not by measured computation.
failure_signatures: Curiosity is operationalized as anticipatory interest in the answer to a trivia question and read out as a memory-encoding benefit; SD-025 operationalizes curiosity as an online CEM trajectory-scoring bonus proportional to representational density -- the shared construct label ('curiosity') spans two quite different computations.

The paper links curiosity to enhanced ENCODING (a consolidation/memory outcome), not to biased ACTION SELECTION toward information-rich regions -- so it supports the drive's neural substrate more than SD-025's specific behavioural function (approach emergence via density-following).

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational cross-disciplinary (machine-learning + neuroscience) grounding for the design decision that an information-seeking/curiosity drive is a legitimate, uniform bias that guides exploration -- exactly SD-025's move. It licenses the family of mechanisms SD-025 sits in (automatic novelty bias through learning-progress/information-gain search). Held at 0.68 because it is a design_decision grounding, not an empirical validation, and because SD-025's specific operationalization (density-of-RBF-centers as the information proxy, novelty = density * (1 - familiarity)) is only one member of the family the review surveys -- the review does not endorse density-of-representation specifically.
failure_signatures: The review's stronger mechanisms are learning-progress / information-gain based (seek where you can reduce uncertainty fastest); SD-025's density-following proxy is closer to the 'automatic novelty bias' end and does not explicitly compute expected information gain -- so a strict reading pressures SD-025 toward the weaker/simpler member of the family.

Curiosity-as-density can perseverate on high-density-but-fully-learned regions; the review notes pure novelty biases get 'trapped' without a learning-progress term -- SD-025 mitigates this only via the familiarity EMA, an ad hoc discount rather than a learning-progress signal.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical computational demonstration that an intrinsic curiosity signal ALONE -- with no extrinsic reward gradient -- produces directed, goal-approaching navigation (systematic level-traversal in Super Mario, room-to-room navigation in VizDoom). That is the ARC-057 emergence principle in its purest computational form: directed approach as an emergent property of an information-seeking drive rather than a commanded value field. Held at 0.6 because ICM curiosity is forward-model PREDICTION ERROR (seek unpredictable transitions), not SD-025's representational-DENSITY following, and there is no DA-expansion partner shaping the space -- so it evidences the 'intrinsic drive -> directed approach, no explicit gradient' half of ARC-057 but not the SD-024 x SD-025 interaction that makes the approach land on reward.
failure_signatures: The intrinsic reward is prediction error in a learned inverse-dynamics feature space (novelty = surprise), whereas SD-025 defines novelty as representational density x (1 - familiarity). Curiosity here seeks the UNPREDICTABLE; ARC-057's curiosity seeks the representationally DENSE -- the shared word 'curiosity' spans two different computations.

There is no dopaminergic representational-expansion component: the environment's structure is fixed and curiosity explores it uniformly. ARC-057's distinctive claim is that DA ASYMMETRICALLY expands the map so that a uniform drive produces reward-directed approach -- this paper shows the drive-produces-approach half but not the asymmetry-of-the-substrate half.

Prediction-error curiosity is known to be vulnerable to the 'noisy-TV' trap (stochastic transitions look perpetually novel); this failure mode has no analogue in the density-following formulation, so a naive read that 'curiosity always yields adaptive approach' would over-claim.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational, heavily-cited normative model (validated against place- and grid-cell data) showing that goal-directed navigation is read off the STRUCTURE of a hippocampal representation -- a successor representation whose place fields skew and cluster around rewards and barriers -- rather than off an explicit stored value gradient. This is exactly ARC-057's core thesis ('there is no gradient -- there is more map'). Held at 0.62 because the representational scheme is a successor/predictive map (future-occupancy), NOT REE's DA-modulated RBF density expansion, and the paper contains no separate curiosity/information-seeking drive -- it grounds the 'representation-structure produces approach without an explicit gradient' premise but not the specific SD-024 x SD-025 two-component interaction that ARC-057 asserts.
failure_signatures: The map here is a successor representation encoding expected future state occupancy; place fields reshape around reward/goal locations, but the reshaping is driven by the transition/reward structure of the task, not by a dopaminergic representational-DENSITY expansion signal -- so it supports 'structure not gradient' generically while being silent on the DA-expansion (MECH-232/SD-024) leg ARC-057 specifically invokes.

There is no curiosity or information-seeking drive in the model. Approach follows the value/policy read off the SR map, so the paper does not evidence the ARC-057 claim that a UNIFORM curiosity drive (SD-025) operating on the asymmetrically-shaped map is what converts representational structure into approach.

Because the SR map itself encodes reward-weighted expected occupancy, a critic could argue the map is not gradient-free but rather bakes an implicit value gradient into the representation -- the very implicit/explicit boundary ARC-057 rests on is blurred here.

entries.confidence_rationale: Shows that a DENSITY MODEL over the state space, converted into a pseudo-count intrinsic bonus, produces directed navigation toward distant goals in hard sparse-reward tasks (notably Montezuma's Revenge) with no explicit external gradient guiding the agent there. This grounds ARC-057's mechanism-plausibility -- that a density-based intrinsic drive yields emergent directed approach -- and matches SD-025's FAMILIARITY term almost exactly (the bonus is high for rarely-visited states). Held at 0.55 by a real sign-tension: count-based novelty seeks LOW-count / under-explored regions, whereas ARC-057's curiosity is ATTRACTED to HIGH representational density; the two theories agree on the familiarity/visitation term but are opposite on the representational-density term, which is REE's own contribution.
failure_signatures: The pseudo-count bonus is HIGH for LOW-density (rarely visited) states -- novelty-as-rarity. ARC-057's curiosity drive is ATTRACTED to HIGH representational density (more RBF centers = more to distinguish). The word 'density' means opposite things: state-visitation density (Bellemare, seek low) vs representational density (REE, seek high). Support holds only for the visitation/familiarity half of SD-025's novelty = density x (1 - familiarity).

Directedness comes from a value-bootstrapping RL agent propagating the intrinsic bonus via TD backups into a policy, i.e. the approach IS carried by a learned value function -- whereas ARC-057 claims approach without an explicit value/wanting gradient. The mechanism of directedness therefore differs from REE's density-following CEM read-out.

The result is exploration to reach novelty, not approach toward reward per se; the reward-directedness in Montezuma comes from extrinsic reward eventually being found and bootstrapped, not from an asymmetric DA-shaped representation making the drive land on reward.

This is the strongest methodological precedent in the pull for SD-068's core measurement design. SD-068 sidesteps the failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-538a encoding-starvation ceiling by scoring output quality against KNOWN INJECTED content rather than emergent encoding, and applies a spatially-scoped perturbation with a scoped readout. Bar et al. do structurally the same thing in humans: they inject known content (word-location pairs learned with a contextual odor), deliver a hemisphere-scoped perturbation during NREM (unilateral nostril odor cueing, exploiting ipsilateral olfactory processing), and read out both behaviour and local sleep oscillations per hemisphere, with the uncued hemisphere serving as a within-subject control. That the effect was local rather than global is exactly the dissociation a per-phase lesion harness needs to be non-vacuous. Confidence is capped at 0.71 because the scoping axis is anatomical (hemisphere) whereas SD-068's is temporal/functional (pipeline phase), which is a real disanalogy.
failure_signatures: Bar et al. found the local effects only when learning had occurred WITH the contextual odor -- unilateral olfactory stimulation after learning without contextual odor produced no memory or oscillation effect. The analogous harness failure is a per-phase readout that responds to the damage sigma even when no known content was injected; that would indicate the readout is measuring perturbation magnitude rather than content fidelity, and SD-068's non-vacuity argument would fail.

Regional slow-wave power went DOWN in the cued hemisphere relative to uncued, and correlated negatively with memory for cued words. A harness assuming that more activity in a phase means better output quality would invert this sign.

The dissociation depended on the readout being scoped to the same locus as the perturbation. If SD-068's per-phase readouts draw on shared or disjoint state (the claim already notes the three phases operate on DISJOINT state), a perturbation-readout scoping mismatch would produce apparent independence that reflects plumbing rather than functional separability.

entries.confidence_rationale: A well-sourced review in a top primary-neuroscience venue that explicitly revives and argues for the sequential hypothesis -- the position that SWS and REM make distinct, ordered contributions to offline memory processing rather than competing as alternative single-stage accounts. That framing is the conceptual precondition for SD-068's whole design: if consolidation were a single undifferentiated offline process, a per-phase lesion harness with per-phase quality readouts would be instrumenting boxes that do not exist. Confidence is deliberately moderate because this is a narrative review, not new data -- it establishes that the ordered-phases framing is a live and defensible position in the field, and notably that it had been 'largely ignored', which is itself a signal that the field has not settled the question. It cannot adjudicate the specific three-way SWS/NREM/REM split SD-068 instruments.
failure_signatures: Sara notes the role of sleep in memory processing remains 'controversial and elusive' after a century of investigation. If REE's harness produces a crisp, stable staging order across seeds, that cleanliness is itself suspicious relative to the biological literature's noisiness, and should prompt a check that the ordering is not an artefact of the damage model rather than the pipeline.

The review's mechanistic emphasis is on noradrenergic (locus coeruleus) modulation across sleep states. V3 has no noradrenergic plane, so any harness ordering that would biologically be NA-mediated cannot be reproduced -- a structural mismatch that could make the harness's staging order unfaithful for reasons invisible to the harness itself.

If the sequential hypothesis is wrong and SWS/REM contributions are parallel rather than ordered, the harness's staging-order readout would still produce SOME ordering from noise-sensitivity differences alone, which would be vacuous in exactly the way SD-068 claims to avoid.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the closest thing in the human literature to a natural experiment on the SD-068 premise: that the offline-consolidation pipeline is genuinely ordered, so that decomposing it into per-phase, separately-damageable stages is a faithful abstraction rather than an imposed one. Narcoleptic patients who fall asleep in R before N provide the counterfactual (R-N) that physiological sleep never supplies, and the result is a clean order effect -- spindle-linked consolidation appears in N-R naps and not in R-N naps. That is direct evidence that the phases are not interchangeable and that one phase's contribution is contingent on a later phase, which is exactly the dependency structure SD-068's staging-order readout is built to detect. Confidence is held below 0.8 because the population is pathological (central hypersomnolence, incl. narcolepsy) rather than healthy, the task is a single visual perceptual-learning paradigm, and the paper's 'N' collapses the SWS-denoising and NREM-slot-filling phases that SD-068 separates -- so it validates two-stage ordering, not the three-stage decomposition.
failure_signatures: If REE's harness reports a per-phase output-quality degradation for the NREM slot-filling phase that is independent of the state of the downstream REM phase, that is inconsistent with Strauss et al.'s finding that the NREM (spindle) contribution is only realised when a REM phase follows -- and would suggest the harness's phases are more decoupled in the substrate than they are in biology.

Strauss et al. found a NEGATIVE association between rapid-eye-movements during R sleep and perceptual consolidation. A harness that models REM as a monotonically quality-improving phase would mis-predict this sign and could yield a spuriously clean staging order.

The observed order effect is carried by spindles specifically, not by NREM duration. A damage model that scales a single Gaussian sigma over phase state without a spindle-analog may not reproduce the biological dependency even if it reproduces an ordering.

entries.confidence_rationale: The design is well-matched to SD-068's central premise -- the SAME injected cue delivered into DIFFERENT sleep phases produced different downstream signatures (task-related dream reactivation at 1-2 days when cued in REM, 5-6 days when cued in SWS) -- which is phase-dissociation evidence of exactly the kind a per-phase harness needs. But the readout is home dream logs, a subjective and noisy dependent variable, and the authors note their own earlier finding that TMR cueing had NO immediate effect on dream content, so the positive result here rests on a delayed-effect analysis over a 10-day window with multiple comparison opportunities. I mark this MIXED rather than supports: it supports phase-dissociability while simultaneously demonstrating that per-phase effects may only be visible at long latency, which is a genuine problem for a harness that scores output quality immediately after each phase.
failure_signatures: Picard-Deland and Nielsen found NO immediate effect of TMR cueing on dream content, and only a delayed effect days later. If per-phase consolidation effects in biology are latent at the time the phase completes, SD-068's design of scoring per-phase output quality immediately at phase exit may systematically under-detect real phase contributions -- producing a damage-tolerance ordering that reflects readout latency rather than damage tolerance.

The two phases had DIFFERENT latencies (REM 1-2 days, SWS 5-6 days). A harness reading all three phases at a common fixed latency would therefore be sampling each phase at a different point on its own effect curve, systematically biasing the staging order.

Dream-content reactivation is an indirect proxy for consolidation quality. If REE's per-phase readouts (denoising-SNR, transfer-fidelity, precision-calibration-error) are similarly proxy-distant from the functional quantity of interest, apparent phase dissociations may be dissociations in the proxies rather than in the phases.

A genuine NECESSITY result, which is rare and is exactly the evidence-type CDQ-007 asked for: dopamine-deficient mice with intact sensory and motor systems and intact hedonic reactions become aphagic and starve, and targeted regional restoration rescues feeding. This is the strongest available demonstration that a tonic appetitive/approach substrate is REQUIRED for goal-directed action and cannot be substituted by reward learning. Discounted for being a knockout in an adult-developmental context rather than a cold-start bootstrap experiment.
failure_signatures: This is loss-of-function in an animal that already possesses the innate behavioural repertoire, not a cold-start demonstration; it shows the drive is necessary to EXPRESS competence, not that it is sufficient to ACQUIRE it.

Dopamine loss also impairs movement initiation and coordination (not fully rescued by either regional restoration), so aphagia is partly confounded with motoric failure -- the paper itself flags that coordination is not fully restored.

Feeding-for-sustenance and preferring-palatable-substances dissociate anatomically here, which means 'the approach drive' is not one thing; a REE single-scalar drive parameter would be a coarse analog of a circuit biology has already split.

entries.confidence_rationale: A well-controlled experiment with the decisive comparison built in: a 'ghost control' in which objects move with no agent present performed as well as a live conspecific demonstrator. This directly weakens the strong reading of H-bc-prior -- that what a learner needs is an ACTION-LEVEL policy to copy. What the pigs extracted was affordance information about the apparatus, obtainable without any demonstrator. Single species, single manipulative task, moderate n per group.
failure_signatures: Observers of ALL kinds still beat non-observers, so some external information source was required -- the result weakens 'a conspecific demonstrator is needed', not 'external information is needed'.

The task is a two-step manipulation of a fixed apparatus, where affordance information is nearly the whole problem; in a foraging task where the difficulty is action SELECTION over time, action-level copying might carry weight that it does not carry here.
Free-ranging adult pigs already possess a competent exploratory and manipulative repertoire, so this is skill acquisition on top of competence, not a cold-start bootstrap.

entries.confidence_rationale: Optogenetic, cell-type-specific, causal identification of a dedicated circuit whose function is to INITIATE investigatory action toward objects and conspecifics -- i.e. a drive whose output is action, not valuation, and which operates in the absence of any learned reward association. This is close to the cleanest neural evidence available that a demonstrator-free, reward-independent approach drive exists as a distinct substrate. Rodent, and the behaviour is investigation rather than foraging, hence the discount.
failure_signatures: The behaviour measured is object/conspecific investigation, not sustained goal-directed foraging to a food source; an innate investigatory drive is demonstrated, an innate FORAGING policy is not.

The paper does not test extinction under sustained non-reward, so 'non-extinguishing' -- the specific property H-approach-primitive needs -- is inferred from the reward-independence of the circuit, not measured directly.

ZIm activity is modulated by investigatory motivation level, so the drive is state-dependent rather than a fixed constant; a REE analog implemented as a constant action bonus would be a simplification of the biology.

entries.confidence_rationale: Landmark multi-muscle EMG study across four human developmental stages plus four non-human species. Directly measures the question at issue: whether competent locomotion is CONSTRUCTED from scratch by learning or REFINED from a pre-existing innate basis. The answer is unambiguous and cross-phyletic -- the two neonatal primitives are retained into adulthood and augmented, not replaced. Source quality very high; mapping to REE is by analogy (motor primitives vs a foraging policy) so mapping_fidelity is the limiting term.
failure_signatures: The primitives measured are lumbosacral motoneuron activation patterns for stepping, not goal-directed foraging policies; the claim 'action repertoire is refined, not constructed' is demonstrated at the rhythm-generation level, not the decision-making level.

The study says nothing about WHERE the goal-direction comes from -- innate primitives supply the motor alphabet, not the objective. A REE converter given innate action primitives could still forage at floor if the primitives are never sequenced toward food.
Human infants in this study do have caregivers; the design isolates development from learning by age-staging, not by demonstrator deprivation, so it is not a clean demonstrator-free existence proof.

entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative review that makes exactly the claim H-approach-primitive needs -- that exploratory and curiosity-driven behaviour occurs in the absence of a clear goal or reward and is regulated by an INNATE drive with identified substrates -- and reframes phasic dopamine as signalling potentially-important stimuli rather than reward. Its status as a review with an explicit theoretical proposal (environment prediction error) rather than a single decisive experiment caps the confidence.
failure_signatures: This is a review advancing a framework, not a decisive experiment; the 'innate drive' claim is a synthesis position and there are competing accounts that fold information-seeking back into reward learning as an intrinsic bonus.

'Environment prediction error' as the currency means the drive is still error-driven, just against a world-model rather than a reward-model -- so it is not obviously non-extinguishing; a well-modelled environment would quiesce it, which is the opposite of what H-approach-primitive requires for a cold-start.
The review does not address whether such a drive is SUFFICIENT to bootstrap competence absent a demonstrator; it addresses whether it exists and what implements it.

entries.confidence_rationale: Clean causal embryonic experiment with a genetic deprivation manipulation and circuit-level identification. It is mixed rather than supporting because it cuts both ways for CDQ-007: it is a demonstrator-free bootstrap (nothing outside the embryo teaches it), which favours H-approach-primitive; but it also shows the innate circuit is INSUFFICIENT alone and requires self-generated experience to mature, which weakens a naive 'just add an innate drive and competence follows' reading. Invertebrate embryo, so transfer_risk is non-trivial.
failure_signatures: The innate pioneer circuit does NOT produce a mature CPG on its own -- proprioceptive feedback from self-generated movement is REQUIRED. An innate primitive that is never exercised does not mature into competence.

The 'teacher' here is the agent's own body via proprioception, which has no obvious REE analog if the substrate lacks a reafference channel; a REE approach-primitive with no self-generated-experience loop would not reproduce this mechanism.
Drosophila embryonic motor development is several transfer steps from vertebrate goal-directed foraging; the result constrains the general principle, not the specific implementation.

entries.confidence_rationale: The single most informative paper in this pull for the CDQ-007 discrimination, because it disambiguates the two legs within one experiment: neural sequences form WITHOUT a tutor (H-approach-primitive), AND tutor exposure binds those pre-existing sequences to new syllables (H-bc-prior), AND birds whose untutored sequences had already crystallized FAILED to learn from the tutor (the prior is only usable inside a window). Calcium imaging with a clean delayed-tutoring design; songbird-to-REE transfer is the main discount.
failure_signatures: Sequences forming without a tutor does NOT mean competence forms without a tutor -- the untutored birds sing abnormal isolate song. The innate machinery supplies the SCAFFOLD; the demonstrator supplies the CONTENT.

Only half the delayed-tutoring birds learned new syllables, and the failures were exactly those whose pre-tutoring sequences were most crystallized -- an innate/self-organized prior that hardens becomes a BARRIER to later demonstrator-derived learning.

This is a vocal-motor sequence-learning system with a genetically specified critical period; a REE converter has no analogous maturational clock, so the timing result may not transfer even though the mechanism is suggestive.

entries.confidence_rationale: Older, small-sample behavioural study, but it supplies the specific datum the other side of the discrimination needs: untutored zebra finches develop song that is MORE VARIABLE and contains ABNORMAL elements, i.e. the demonstrator-free bootstrap does not reach species-typical competence. It also shows untutored siblings copy each other, so 'demonstrator' is a graded rather than binary condition. Age of the study and the specialised domain cap confidence.
failure_signatures: Untutored birds still produce structured song -- the deficit is degradation toward abnormality, not total failure; this is not a floor-vs-ceiling result of the kind REE observes, so the analogy to a 0-1 foraging floor is loose.

Untutored brothers copied one another as much as tutored birds copied adults, meaning the 'no demonstrator' condition is hard to instantiate cleanly in a social species -- any peer is a partial demonstrator.
1995, small n, acoustic-similarity measures partly by human judgement; would not meet current methodological standards without replication.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the closest thing found to INDEPENDENT support for MECH-459's specific mechanism, and its independence is what gives it value: unlike DreamerV3 it was not the source the claim was authored from, and it targets the exact operator MECH-459 indicts -- per-batch advantage standardisation -- rather than return normalisation one level up. It reports that normalised advantage is harmful DESPITE its near-ubiquity in advantage actor-critic methods, and names two mechanisms, both of which map onto REE: division by a small standard deviation causing gradient spikes when advantages are small early in training, and per-mini-batch variance in the estimation of the normalisation parameters. The first is MECH-459's noise re-amplification form almost verbatim. Confidence is capped at 0.62 by source status and by a residual extraction limitation: this is an unreviewed preprint, and the fetched text confirmed the qualitative claims and mechanisms but did not yield verbatim effect sizes or the benchmark table, so the MAGNITUDE of the reported harm is not independently verified here. The direction is well supported; the size is not.
failure_signatures: Dividing advantages by a per-batch standard deviation produces disproportionately large gradient updates when that standard deviation is small, which is precisely the early-training and low-reward-variance regime.
Normalisation parameters estimated per mini-batch are themselves noisy estimates, so the normaliser injects estimator variance into the policy gradient in addition to whatever it removes.
A widely-adopted default operator can be harmful without being noticed, because it is inherited as boilerplate rather than ablated.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the deliberate counterweight in the pull and the most decision-relevant entry for calibrating what a probe-K result will mean. It is the only paper found that directly tests whether DreamerV3's normalisation machinery TRANSFERS to a different algorithm, which is exactly the inferential step MECH-459 makes when it imports Hafner's prescription into REE's model-free raw-view actor-critic. The finding is explicitly negative on the general question -- the tricks 'do not transfer as general improvements to PPO' across more than 10,000 compute-hours of experiments -- while positive on a narrower one: PPO with the tricks performs comparably to PPO WITH reward clipping and significantly outperforms PPO WITHOUT reward clipping. Peer-reviewed at a top venue with a large compute budget, so source quality is high and the null is well-powered rather than an underpowered miss. Confidence 0.71 reflects solid quality and clear relevance, discounted because the paper tests DreamerV3's normaliser as a BUNDLE on dense-reward Atari, so it cannot isolate the specific sparse-reward, near-zero-return regime in which MECH-459 locates REE's pathology.
failure_signatures: Normalisation machinery that is load-bearing in one algorithm can fail to produce any general improvement when transplanted into another, even at very large compute budgets.
The measured benefit of DreamerV3-style normalisation in PPO was substitutive rather than additive -- it recovered what reward clipping already provided rather than adding gains on top of it.
Evaluating a bundle of tricks jointly cannot attribute effect to any single component, so a bundle-level null does not license a component-level null.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the source MECH-459 explicitly cites, and the three prescriptions the claim attributes to it are confirmed verbatim: the one-sided denominator max(1, Per95 - Per5) that scales large returns down and never scales small returns up; the explicit rejection of running-statistics normalisation as injecting non-stationarity; and discrete/twohot regression for the critic motivated by bimodal return distributions under sparse reward. High source quality (flagship model-based RL result, now peer-reviewed in Nature, very broad domain sweep). Confidence is held below 0.85 for a mapping reason, not a quality one: DreamerV3's normaliser sits on RETURNS inside an imagination-based actor-critic over a learned world model, whereas MECH-459's target is a per-episode ADVANTAGE standardiser in a model-free raw-view actor-critic. The design rationale transfers cleanly; the quantitative claim that removing it moves REE's foraging floor does not follow from this paper and is exactly what the sanctioned knock-out probe must decide. Confirmatory-citation risk is real here (the claim was authored from this paper), so this entry should not be treated as independent corroboration.
failure_signatures: A two-sided normaliser whose denominator has no floor divides out magnitude information by construction, so any experimental axis that acts purely through reward or advantage MAGNITUDE cannot move the resulting policy gradient -- eliminations along such axes are confounded rather than informative.
Under a bimodal sparse-return distribution a scalar MSE critic converges toward the mean of the two modes, a value never actually observed, producing systematically miscalibrated advantages.
Normalising targets by running statistics makes the optimisation non-stationary because the target moves whenever the normaliser moves.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the sharpest and most precisely-targeted counterweight in the pull, and it lands on SD-031's structure rather than on its periphery. The authors draw a distinction REE has not explicitly made: NARROW sense of agency (associated with movements) versus BROAD sense of agency (associated with environmental events). They then argue that the comparator model was developed from, and is evidentially supported by, studies of sensory consequences NARROWLY tied to movements -- while standard experimental paradigms in fact study only BROAD agency. Their conclusion is that the comparator model is not a satisfactory account of sense of agency, that narrow SoA is equally well explained by a simpler motor-signal model, and they report two experiments that failed to induce illusory narrow SoA where the comparator model predicts it should be inducible. This matters for SD-031 specifically because z_world is by definition the BROAD stream -- environmental consequences, 'the door opened because of me' -- and SD-031 proposes to apply a comparator architecture precisely there, which is the extension these authors argue is unwarranted. Confidence 0.69: peer-reviewed, argument is directly on point, and it is the exact structural objection SD-031 must answer; discounted because it is primarily a theoretical/negative-result paper whose empirical component is two null illusion-induction experiments (informative but limited), and because an argument against a comparator as a model of conscious AGENCY EXPERIENCE is not automatically an argument against a comparator as a functional attribution MECHANISM.
failure_signatures: The comparator model's evidential support comes from narrow (movement-tied) sensory consequences, but it is routinely applied to broad (environmental-event) agency, where that support does not extend.
Two experiments designed to induce illusory narrow sense of agency in healthy participants failed to do so, contrary to comparator-model prediction.
For narrow sense of agency a simpler motor-signal model explains the data equally well, so the comparator's extra machinery is not licensed by parsimony.
Conflating narrow and broad agency lets a model validated on one be credited with explaining the other.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly relevant to SD-031's 'single-pass' qualifier, which is the part of the claim most exposed to disconfirmation. Using a bias-free two-alternative forced-choice control-detection task with staircased difficulty (accuracy held at 70%) and signal-detection measures (d', meta-d') across 40 participants, the authors identify TWO distinct processes underlying first-order detection of control: one based on instantaneous sensory predictions for the current movement, and one based on detection of a regular motor-visual relation ACROSS A SERIES of movements. The first is a single-pass comparator of essentially SD-031's form; the second is a temporally-extended regularity detector that a single-pass residual cannot implement. Methodologically strong (bias-free d', staircase control, SEM, n=40, Haggard lab). Confidence 0.66 rather than higher because the paradigm again uses visuomotor object control rather than general world-state consequences, and because the dual-process decomposition is inferred from an individual-differences/SEM analysis rather than from direct manipulation of each process.
failure_signatures: First-order detection of control decomposes into at least two processes -- an instantaneous per-movement sensory prediction and a cross-trial motor-visual regularity detector -- so a purely instantaneous comparator captures only part of the attribution signal.

Metacognitive sensitivity was NEGATIVELY correlated with the predictive-process component, contradicting the hypothesis that detection of control relies on metacognitive monitoring of a predictive circuit and suggesting the predictive comparator operates unconsciously.

Large individual differences in metacognitive sensitivity persisted even when first-order sensitivity was experimentally equated, so aggregate agency measures can mask heterogeneous underlying mechanisms.

entries.confidence_rationale: The strongest available support for SD-031's core architectural bet: that self-versus-other attribution of EXTERNAL consequences is carried by a signal that is separable from the sensorimotor stream that produced the action. Using MVPA on a paradigm where self-agency evolves gradually with sensorimotor experience, the authors decode self-other attribution from sensorimotor, posterior parietal, anterior insular and higher visual cortices, and -- critically for SD-031 -- show a DISSOCIATION of preference: right supramarginal gyrus (inferior parietal lobe) is most sensitive to self-other attribution, while bilateral precentral gyri and left IPL dominantly reflect sensorimotor information. That preference dissociation is the load-bearing finding, because it is the biological analogue of SD-031's decision to give z_world its own comparator rather than reading attribution off the motor/self stream. Peer-reviewed, methodologically strong (MVPA with an explicit preference analysis rather than a single contrast). Confidence held to 0.72 by modality distance -- BOLD decodability establishes that the information is PRESENT in a region, not that the brain computes it as an explicit subtractive residual of a forward-model prediction, which is the specific functional form SD-031 asserts.
failure_signatures: Self-other attribution information is distributed across several regions rather than localised to one comparator, so a single-site or single-stream readout will under-detect it.

Regions carrying attribution information and regions carrying sensorimotor information overlap substantially; only a preference analysis separates them, so a design without such a contrast will confound the two.
Decodability of attribution from a region does not establish that the region computes attribution as an explicit prediction-minus-observation residual.

Large (N=1070) longitudinal cohort with amyloid PET and ~4.3 visits per participant -- strong empirical footing for the ORDERING half of INV-047: metacognitive/confidence change is measurable years before the episodic-memory diagnosis it precedes (anosognosia reached ~3.2 years before dementia onset; heightened awareness up to 1.6 years before MCI). Simultaneously weakens the 'not explained by amyloid' half, since amyloid burden is the variable that predicts the awareness trajectory. Net mixed; confidence reflects the strength of the measurement rather than agreement with the claim as a whole.
failure_signatures: Amyloid burden PREDICTED the rate of awareness decline, and did so across the whole spectrum including cognitively normal participants. INV-047's contrast case is that diffuse amyloid should predict uniform degradation rather than a staged profile -- but here a diffuse pathology marker predicts a specifically-timed, staged change. The dichotomy INV-047 rests on (staged profile vs amyloid) is therefore not clean.

The earliest observed awareness change is HYPERnosognosia -- heightened, not diminished, awareness of memory change before MCI. INV-047 asserts early 'precision/confidence LOSS'. The direction of the earliest metacognitive deviation is opposite to the one the claim states, even though its timing (before episodic failure) matches.

Awareness is operationalised as a self-versus-informant discrepancy score, which conflates metacognitive precision with reporting bias, insight, and informant accuracy. A discrepancy measure cannot isolate the precision term INV-047 needs.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly instruments the object INV-047 asserts -- the fine-grained ORDER in which cognitive deficits appear -- using a data-driven event-based model that requires no a priori clinical staging. Strongly supports the claim's structural half (decline is staged and syndrome-specific, not uniform: PCA is vision-first, typical AD is memory-first). Weakens the claim's specific ordering, because the recovered typical-AD sequence begins with memory, not with the precision/confidence stage INV-047 places first. Confidence reflects a well-matched measurement returning a partially discordant answer.
failure_signatures: The recovered sequence for typical AD is MEMORY-first. INV-047 places precision/confidence loss before episodic memory failure. On the one dataset that models the ordering directly, the claim's first two stages appear in the opposite order.

The neuropsychological battery covers memory, vision, arithmetic and general cognition -- it contains no metacognitive or confidence measure at all. The absence of a confidence-first stage in the recovered sequence is therefore uninformative about whether one exists: the model cannot order an event it never measured.

Two syndromes with the same underlying proteinopathy yield different cognitive orderings (PCA vision-first vs tAD memory-first), which shows the ordering is set by lesion topography rather than by any single canonical dependency sequence -- a challenge to INV-047's derivation of the order from a phase-dependency structure.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly attacks the assumption INV-047 depends on -- that there is ONE staged sequence characterising the disease. Relaxing the single-sequence assumption with a generalised Mallows model shows substantially more cross-subject variation than the classic model estimates, and a Dirichlet process mixture detects three population subgroups following DIFFERENT event sequences. Confidence held at 0.58 because this is a methods paper on imaging events rather than cognitive stages, so it undermines the claim's form rather than its specific content.
failure_signatures: A Dirichlet process mixture recovers THREE distinct subgroups with different event sequences in sporadic AD. INV-047 asserts 'the specific staged cognitive decline profile' in the singular; if the population is a mixture of orderings, no single canonical profile is the thing to be explained.

The classic single-sequence event-based model UNDERSTATES cross-subject variation in ordering. Any prior staging result INV-047 leans on that was produced by the classic model therefore carries an unmodelled false confidence in its ordering.

Heterogeneity of this kind is an alternative explanation for apparent staging: a population mixture of differently-ordered subgroups can produce an averaged profile that looks staged without any subject following the average sequence.

entries.confidence_rationale: A double-blind placebo-controlled causal manipulation (N=52) that raised tonic NE pharmacologically and found NO change in task disengagement or exploratory behaviour, despite confirmed drug action on central and autonomic markers. This is the cleanest available causal test of 'does a global scalar, moved on its own, change behavioural strategy?' and the answer was no -- which is what MECH-463 predicts of a channel that cannot re-rank candidates. Held below 0.7 because it is a null result with the usual power caveats, and because absence of a strategy shift is consistent with several mechanisms besides argmax invariance.
failure_signatures: Raising the global scalar in isolation produced no behavioural differentiation at all -- not a weaker version of the predicted effect, but no effect -- while the drug demonstrably reached the CNS. A scalar channel can therefore be pharmacologically live and behaviourally inert simultaneously, which is the failure mode MECH-463 predicts and MECH-359 also predicts.

The authors note the manipulation may not test exploration that exceeds the current task context; a scalar could still act on task-set switching while being inert within a task. MECH-463's argmax-invariance argument is scoped to within-decision candidate sets and inherits exactly this boundary.

This null cannot discriminate MECH-463 (scalar entrenches the incumbent) from MECH-359 (scalar is too weak to steer) -- both predict the observed absence of differentiation. The discriminating measurement is the commit gate, which this paradigm does not instrument.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily replicated theoretical synthesis (high source quality) whose central construct -- a single scalar gain term that cannot by itself specify WHICH option is chosen, only how sharply the choice is drawn -- is structurally the same object MECH-463 names. Discounted for mapping: AGT's gain is the slope of a sigmoid on unit activation, not a softmax temperature over K candidate scores, and AGT asserts the scalar DOES produce a behavioural regime change (exploration), which is in tension with the argmax-invariance half of MECH-463.
failure_signatures: Adaptive gain theory attributes a genuine behavioural mode switch (exploit -> explore) to a scalar with no per-candidate structure, which -- if true as stated -- would mean a global scalar CAN change realised behaviour and not merely its sharpness. MECH-463 must therefore locate the differentiation in the sampling step, not in the score geometry, or it is under-specified.

The theory is silent on the covariance between the scalar channel and the per-candidate channel, which is exactly the quantity MECH-463's variance decomposition needs; AGT cannot arbitrate F-share vs arousal on its own.

entries.confidence_rationale: Well-executed human pupillometry showing that baseline pupil diameter -- an indirect index of the global arousal scalar -- predicts exploratory vs exploitative choice both within and between individuals. Cuts against MECH-463's strong reading (a scalar that tracks realised behavioural differentiation) while being fully compatible with its weak reading (the scalar changes sampling sharpness, not score ordering). Held at 0.5 because the design is correlational and pupil is a doubly-indirect proxy for the quantity MECH-463 names.
failure_signatures: Baseline arousal predicted WHICH choice class was made (exploratory vs exploitative), not merely how sharply it was made. Taken at face value that is behavioural differentiation attributable to a global scalar, which is what MECH-463 says a uniform scalar cannot deliver -- unless the differentiation is entirely in the sampling draw rather than the score ordering.

The same correlation is produced by the reverse causal arrangement: a control state that changes both the choice and the arousal level, with the scalar as consequence rather than cause. Correlational pupillometry cannot exclude this, so the entry cannot be treated as a causal counterexample.

Directly contradicts the causal null of the same group's reboxetine study (Jepma et al. 2010) in apparent direction; the correlational and causal literatures on this exact question do not agree, which is itself a reason to distrust either as a governance input.
