Speaks to the architectural question underneath SD-024 -- whether reward information enters the spatial map at all, and in what form -- and answers yes, but as a continuum from pure place cells through hybrid cells to dedicated reward cells, with reward cells responding to reward DELIVERY rather than expectation. Moderate confidence: it is a reanalysis of existing recordings in a modest venue, and the coding scheme it finds is a third option that neither SD-024 nor its main competitor predicts.
failure_signatures: Reward cells responded mostly to reward DELIVERY rather than to its expectation, which cuts against SD-024's scaling of the allocation signal by drive_level (an expectation-side quantity) and sits in tension with Krishnan et al. 2022's expectation-dependent ramping signal. The literature is not internally settled on whether the allocating signal is expectation-driven or delivery-driven.

A subpopulation transitioned between place-cell and reward-cell properties within a single 5-task session, so the mapping between 'unit' and 'what it represents' is not stable on the timescale REE's FIFO center lifecycle assumes.
Some cells were typical place cells wholly insensitive to reward location -- reward influence is heterogeneous across the population, not a uniform field-wide modulation.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the paper SD-024's own notes cite as its biological grounding, and it does carry that weight: local D1-receptor blockade in CA1 prevents reward-driven place-cell reorientation and produces perseveration. It earns a solid but not high confidence because it establishes that DA gates reward-relevant REMAPPING, which is a weaker and different statement than DA producing local representational EXPANSION -- the claim's actual mechanism.
failure_signatures: Blocking D1 receptors locally in CA1 prevented place-cell reorientation to the rule-relevant spatial dimension and produced perseveration -- the animal kept using the old reference frame. This is precisely SD-024's declared 'perseveration' failure mode, but note it arises here from DA BLOCKADE, whereas SD-024 predicts perseveration from DA locked HIGH. The claim's failure-mode taxonomy may have the sign inverted, or may be describing a different perseveration.

Learning impairment and representational failure were inseparable in this design: the animals that failed to remap also failed to learn, so the experiment cannot say whether the map change causes the behaviour or vice versa.

entries.confidence_rationale: A well-controlled direct test of the strong form of SD-024 that comes out negative: no general over-representation of goals by place fields in CA1 or CA3, and no modulation of place-cell activity by goal VALUE, in animals whose behaviour demonstrably tracked that value. Confidence is high enough to matter for governance but not higher, because the design dissociates goal location from reward consumption -- which is arguably a manipulation that removes the very DA-delivery event SD-024 says does the allocating.
failure_signatures: Rats reliably preferred the higher-value goal, yet place-cell firing was not modulated by goal value -- behavioural value sensitivity dissociated cleanly from map-level value coding. If REE's benefit terrain shows density scaling with benefit_magnitude, that is a point of divergence from this dataset, not a point of convergence.

No general over-representation of goals was found by place fields in either CA1 or CA3, contradicting the phenomenon SD-024 takes as its starting point. Goal-related activity appeared instead as OUT-OF-FIELD ramping during the waiting period -- a rate/timing code at the goal rather than a reallocation of spatial resource toward it.

The authors' interpretation is that the dorsal hippocampal map is value-FREE and links to value represented elsewhere. Taken at face value this contradicts SD-024's architectural premise that the hippocampal residue field is where reward-scaled representational expansion should live.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly on-target as a computational existence proof that reward-location over-representation and its dynamic shift can be generated by a simple reward-distance-dependent modulation -- SD-024's phenomenon, reproduced in silico. But it is mixed rather than supporting because the mechanism it uses is a dynamic GAIN on existing units in a continuous attractor network, which is exactly the alternative SD-024's weight-independent density discriminator is designed to rule out. It is simultaneously the best available proof-of-concept and the sharpest statement of the confound.
failure_signatures: Over-representation and its shift to a relocated reward were reproduced without any change in the number or placement of representational units -- a distance-dependent gain on a fixed attractor population sufficed. Any REE measurement that reads density off activity or weights will therefore not discriminate SD-024's allocation mechanism from a gain mechanism.

The model is not fit to or validated against recorded data; it reproduces a qualitative phenomenon in 1D tracks and 2D square arenas. Its 5-10 cm over-representation zone is a model output, not a measured constraint, and should not be imported as a scale for da_jitter_radius.

entries.confidence_rationale: The strongest available causal test of the exact dependency SD-024 asserts: a VTA dopaminergic signal in CA1 is what sustains reward-location over-representation, and optogenetically removing it collapses the over-representation. High source quality (Nat Commun, 2-photon calcium imaging plus circuit-specific inhibition, converging manipulations). Confidence is held below 0.9 because the paper measures over-representation as place-field COUNT/reliability in a real CA1 population, whereas SD-024 asserts a specific implementational route (extra RBF centers allocated per DA-scaled reward event) that the paper neither confirms nor excludes.
failure_signatures: When reward expectation is extinguished, over-representation of reward locations vanishes while the animal remains engaged with the environment -- so an implementation that keeps expanded density after reward removal (SD-024's 'craving' failure mode) is biologically off-pattern, not merely suboptimal.

Loss of the dopaminergic reward-proximity signal increases place-field remapping throughout the whole environment and reduces trial-to-trial reliability -- i.e. removing DA does not simply flatten the map locally, it destabilises it globally. An REE ablation that shows only a local density change may be under-modelling the mechanism.

Foundational statement of the exact architectural proposition ARC-112 and INV-091 make -- that a system can be integrated without being synchronised, via coexisting coupling and independence tendencies, with no privileged central controller. Held at 0.52 because it is a conceptual review whose mechanism is broken symmetry in coupled oscillators: the FRAMING transfers, the mechanism does not, and the review predates and is largely superseded on the measurement question by Hancock et al. 2024. Included for the concept, not the method.
failure_signatures: Metastability in this framework arises from symmetry breaking -- the coupling term must be weaker than the components' intrinsic frequency differences. A system whose components are coupled hard enough will lock; one coupled too weakly will be independent. Neither is integration.

The framework's currency is relative phase between oscillators. A system with no oscillatory components has no relative phase, hence no dwells and no escapes in this sense -- the concept does not port to a non-oscillatory substrate without redefinition.

entries.confidence_rationale: The best available external test of MECH-466's premise -- that event boundaries function as shared temporal landmarks across processes running at different characteristic timescales -- and it reports the PARTIAL sharing that MECH-466 and INV-091 jointly predict rather than the total sharing that would be uninteresting or the absence that would refute. 85% of searchlight pairs share boundaries above chance while nesting is explicitly imperfect, which is the band shape INV-091 asserts. Held at 0.58 because the transfer is brain-to-REE (GOV-ANALOGY-1), because it never compares event-locked against clock-locked alignment -- MECH-466's actual falsifier -- and because the boundaries are detected by the analyst's algorithm rather than broadcast by the system, which is the reverse of REE's situation.
failure_signatures: Nesting was imperfect: relative boundary overlap between regions fell short of its theoretical maximum of 1.0. Regions at different timescales genuinely disagree about where boundaries are -- so a REE analysis that requires all streams to agree on a boundary set would fail on a system behaving exactly like this one.

State durations spanned 4.5 s in sensory cortex to 27.2 s in prefrontal cortex -- roughly a factor of six, comparable to REE's 1:10 E1:E3 ratio. Boundary sharing therefore has to be assessed across unequal timescales, and a fixed tolerance window would bias toward the fast streams.

The authors state it is 'not yet clear what a distinct neural state might represent' in transmodal regions -- the states are statistically robust but semantically opaque, so recurrence of states is not by itself evidence that anything functional is being shared.

entries.confidence_rationale: Highest-quality available source on the exact measurement question Q-081 faces, and the single most useful literature item for constraining the prospective recording run. Scored MIXED and held below 0.7 deliberately: it SUPPORTS the integration/segregation band that INV-091 asserts (the review's explicit 'sweet spot'), but it WEAKENS the implicit assumption that a cross-stream statistic can settle Outcome A vs Outcome B at all -- its Box 2 states that observed state-switching is a necessary but NOT sufficient condition, that the standard signatures 'do not disambiguate metastable or multi-stable dynamics', and that metastability is a property of a dynamical system 'and not of data'. mapping_fidelity is mid-range because every signature discussed is defined over oscillatory phase (Kuramoto order parameter, Hilbert phase, time-varying FC), which REE's streams do not have.
failure_signatures: A cross-stream statistic that merely shows REE's streams switching between distinct, long-dwelling configurations does NOT establish shared organisation -- the review states this is 'a necessary but not sufficient condition', shared by both metastable and multi-stable systems.

A high variance in a global coordination index 'could reflect either metastable or multi-stable dynamics, or it could even reflect mere random fluctuations within the system' -- so a raw variance-of-coordination readout cannot by itself exclude Outcome B.
No normative values exist for any metastability signature; the field's standard practice is to contrast conditions against a reference. A single-arm absolute REE number would be uninterpretable.

The signatures are heuristics adopted BECAUSE full attractor-landscape reconstruction is infeasible at realistic data volumes -- so choosing one is accepting a known-incomplete test, not deferring a rigorous one.

entries.confidence_rationale: Included primarily as a CONTROL-DESIGN template rather than for its neuroscience: it is the cleanest worked example in this pull of discriminating genuine cross-timescale organisation from structure trivially implied by the components' own rates. The lag gradient across networks appeared consistently across eight distinct stories and was ABSENT both at rest and under a scrambled-story stimulus -- a control that preserves low-level input statistics and destroys only the nested event structure. That is structurally the discriminator Q-081's Outcome A vs B needs and the alignment statistic MECH-466 needs. Held at 0.61 by GOV-ANALOGY-1, by the haemodynamic confound on any lag measure in fMRI, and because cross-stream lag is a weaker notion of shared organisation than homologous transition motifs.
failure_signatures: The lag gradient was absent for scrambled stories and at rest. A cross-stream statistic that survives destruction of the system's event structure was measuring the input or the wiring, not the organisation -- so REE's run must include the analogous structure-destroying arm, not only a shuffle surrogate.

Inter-subject cross-correlation isolates stimulus-driven coupling by correlating ACROSS subjects, removing within-subject noise-driven correlation. REE has no across-subject axis; the nearest analogue is across-seed, and using it changes what is being estimated (shared across seeds is not the same as shared within a run).

Lags were on the scale of several seconds in a haemodynamically filtered signal; regional HRF differences alone can produce apparent lags. Any lag-based cross-stream statistic needs a control for rate-induced apparent lag -- in REE, the fact that E3 updates every 10 steps guarantees an apparent lag relative to E1 with no shared organisation whatever.

entries.confidence_rationale: The single most directly usable item in this pull for Q-081's measurement problem, and the only one whose substrate is the same kind of object as REE (artificial recurrent networks, not brains). It gives an operational definition of 'homologous dynamics across heterogeneous state spaces' -- the literal subject of search 6 -- and demonstrates that dynamical similarity is detectable where geometric similarity measures (CKA, plain Procrustes) fail. Highest confidence here because transfer_risk is genuinely low: it compares latent trajectories of artificial networks, which is what REE streams are. Held below 0.8 because it is a conference method paper, is contested by later work on whether orthogonal alignment is sufficient for topological conjugacy, and -- decisively -- supplies NO null model, which is the thing Q-081 most needs.
failure_signatures: DSA compares dynamics via finite-dimensional Koopman/DMD approximations aligned by an orthogonal transformation. Later work (Beyond DSA, arXiv:2607.04493) questions whether orthogonal alignment is necessary and sufficient for topological comparison -- so a DSA similarity score is not by itself a conjugacy certificate.

The method supplies a similarity SCORE with no accompanying null distribution. A DSA score between two REE streams is uninterpretable on its own; it needs a surrogate distribution built for it, which the paper does not provide.

Delay embedding and DMD rank are free parameters. Two streams sampled at different rates (E1 every step vs E3 every ten) will have different effective embedding requirements, and a naive shared choice could manufacture or destroy apparent similarity.

entries.confidence_rationale: The closest available METHOD template for what Q-081's prospective run must compute: infer a discrete state sequence over multivariate signals, build the state-to-state transition matrix, and test whether its structure is non-random and hierarchically organised. Also an existence proof that the analysis has power to find real structure (states are heritable and predict cognitive traits). Held at 0.63 because the substrate mapping is loose -- brain regions are not REE streams -- and because the paper's own null is 'transitions are non-random', which is precisely the null REE cannot use, since a configured multi-rate clock makes non-random transitions inevitable.
failure_signatures: The paper's discriminating test is that transitions are non-random. For REE that test is vacuous: E1/E2/E3 at periods 1/3/10 produce non-random transition structure by construction. Adopting this null unmodified would return a guaranteed PASS that means nothing -- Outcome B recorded as Outcome A.
HMM state inference is sensitive to the chosen number of states K; an inappropriate K can manufacture or destroy apparent hierarchical structure, and the method does not select K for you.

The strongest evidence that the states are real is external validation (heritability, subject-consistency, correlation with cognitive traits), not any property of the state sequence itself. A REE analogue therefore needs an external anchor -- e.g. the statistic must move under ablation -- and cannot be validated from within the trace.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly answers the live methodological question the telemetry audit exposed -- how to build the rate-matched null that separates Q-081's Outcome A from Outcome B. It is the canonical reference for surrogate construction, is substrate-neutral (a review of statistical methodology for time series, not a claim about brains or agents), and specifically covers surrogates for testing COUPLING between systems, which is the cross-stream case. Highest source_quality x lowest transfer_risk combination in this pull. Held below 0.8 only because it does not treat the unequal-sampling-rate case REE has, so the rate-matched surrogate still has to be designed rather than looked up.
failure_signatures: The whole method stands or falls on the discriminating statistic being sensitive to the tested property and INSENSITIVE to everything the surrogates preserve. Choose a statistic that responds to update rate and the test is void regardless of how good the surrogates are.

Fourier-transform surrogates preserve the power spectrum and hence the autocorrelation -- so a structure that is fully explained by each stream's own autocorrelation will survive into the surrogates and correctly fail to reach significance. A test that lacks this property is testing a weaker null than it claims.

Constrained-realisation surrogates must replicate ALL characteristics of the original except the property under test. A surrogate that also destroys something incidental produces significance for the wrong reason -- a false positive that looks exactly like a real finding.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the entry that makes search 10 non-decorative. It converts ARC-112's framing assertion -- that REE is one system rather than a collection of modules -- into a quantity with a scalable estimator (Psi, Delta, Gamma; pairwise mutual information only; linear in system size) and public code. Scored 0.68 rather than higher because the criteria are explicitly ONE-SIDED: Psi>0 is sufficient for causal emergence but not necessary, and the authors state plainly that they 'are unable to rule out emergence'. Combined with their own warning that redundancy makes emergence HARDER to detect, and REE's streams being heavily redundant by construction, a negative result in REE would be uninterpretable. So the paper enables a positive test of ARC-112 and forbids a negative one -- hence mixed rather than supports.
failure_signatures: Psi, Delta and Gamma are sufficient but not necessary conditions. A REE run returning Psi <= 0 across all candidate macro features licenses NO conclusion about ARC-112; reporting it as evidence that the federation framing is wrong would be a direct misuse of the criterion.

The criteria double-count redundancy up to n times, so systems with high redundancy yield false negatives. REE's streams share environmental input and are causally wired to each other (E2 consumes E1, the beta gate reads across), which is exactly the high-redundancy regime where the estimator is least sensitive.

Emergence is defined only relative to a chosen microscopic partition, and the authors state no principled method for choosing it. In REE the partition is a design decision (per-stream? per-latent-block? per-module?) that can manufacture or destroy the result, and nothing in the theory constrains it.

The framework assumes fully observable systems with Markovian dynamics, which the authors say 'often do not hold when dealing with experimental data'. REE's per-step telemetry is a partial view of a non-Markovian system with hidden recurrent state.

entries.confidence_rationale: The only paper found in search 10 whose substrate is REE's own kind of object -- causal emergence computed on the latent representations of neural-network RL agents across six Gymnasium-family environments, two architectures (MLP, GRU) and two algorithm families -- so it establishes that the Rosas/Mediano estimator can actually be run on a trained agent, which is a real precondition for using it on REE. Held to 0.45 by three things the paper itself reports. It is an unrefereed preprint. The macro variable was not chosen on principled grounds but produced by a minimum-information bipartition via the Fiedler vector, because PhiID cannot handle many parts -- so what was measured is emergence across an algorithmically chosen half-split of the latent layer, not across functionally meaningful streams, which is the case REE needs. And the authors' own control found causal emergence 'did not capture a quantitatively different direction' from standard representation metrics -- it summarised information already scattered across weaker signals. Add a sign flip on CrafterReward (global alignment -0.95 against +0.35 to +1.00 elsewhere) and the quantity looks task-dependent rather than invariant.
failure_signatures: The macro variable was obtained by bisecting the latent graph with the Fiedler vector and averaging within each half, adopted explicitly because the decomposition cannot handle systems with many parts. REE's question is about emergence across NAMED heterogeneous streams with different dimensionalities and update rates; an algorithmic bipartition of a single latent layer is a different measurement and the paper offers no evidence the two behave alike.

Causal emergence scores were significantly above random projections but NOT significantly different from standard representation metrics (entropy, mutual information, autocorrelation, effective dimension, latent magnitude). The authors conclude it 'did not capture a quantitatively different direction'. A REE result showing high causal emergence may therefore be re-describable by a much cheaper statistic, which is a discriminant-validity failure, not merely a redundancy.

Global reward alignment was strongly POSITIVE in five environments and strongly NEGATIVE in CrafterReward (-0.95), which the authors attribute post hoc to exploration. A quantity whose sign depends on the task cannot be read as a substrate-independent organisational invariant, which is what search 10 was looking for.

Local (step-by-step) alignment was approximately zero in every environment. The quantity tracks slow representational drift over training, not moment-to-moment coordination -- so it does not speak to Q-081's per-step cross-stream organisation question at all.

Gaussian information theory was assumed after a copula rank-normal transform, and 28.53% of units still rejected normality. The estimator is a linear-Gaussian approximation applied to non-Gaussian neural activations.

entries.confidence_rationale: The brief asked whether constraint closure yields anything measurable or only a definition. The answer is split, and the split is the finding. The STRUCTURAL criterion is real and computable on a dependency graph: a set of constraints realises overall closure iff every constraint is both dependent and generative, and realises STRICT closure iff it additionally cannot be split into two closed sets. That third condition is ARC-112's assertion almost word for word -- one system rather than two independent ones -- and it can be evaluated on REE's constraint graph today without any experiment. The QUANTITATIVE part does not transfer at all: the tendency-to-closure measure dK(V,l) is defined over an increasing volume of physical SPACE, which REE does not have, and the authors themselves call the treatment 'still preliminary' and footnote that their notion of organised complexity is adopted for the discussion rather than in general. Scored 0.50 as the average of a genuinely useful structural criterion and a non-transferable measure, not as uniform mediocrity.
failure_signatures: The closure conditions are evaluated on a graph of constraints that someone must first construct. For REE that graph is an act of interpretation, not a measurement -- which mechanisms count as constraints, and which dependencies are direct, are analyst choices that determine the verdict before any computation runs.

Strict closure is a Boolean property of a chosen constraint set. It cannot distinguish a federation whose integration is functionally meaningful from one whose only cross-dependency is a single trivial wire, because both are unsplittable. The criterion therefore cannot speak to INV-091's band at all -- it has no notion of degree in the dimension that matters.

The quantitative tendency-to-closure measure dK(V,l) is defined by growing a volume of physical space and counting dependencies inside it. REE has no spatial embedding, so there is no non-arbitrary analogue of the volume-growth procedure and no analogue of the boundary-collapse signature the measure detects.

Garson's liberality objection applies to the framework generally: closure of constraints is satisfiable by simple systems that are intuitively not unified organisms. A REE constraint graph passing strict closure therefore does not by itself establish that REE is a federation in any interesting sense.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the entry that makes search 10 non-decorative. It converts ARC-112's framing assertion -- that REE is one system rather than a collection of modules -- into a quantity with a scalable estimator (Psi, Delta, Gamma; pairwise mutual information only; linear in system size) and public code. Scored 0.68 rather than higher because the criteria are explicitly ONE-SIDED: Psi>0 is sufficient for causal emergence but not necessary, and the authors state plainly that they 'are unable to rule out emergence'. Combined with their own warning that redundancy makes emergence HARDER to detect, and REE's streams being heavily redundant by construction, a negative result in REE would be uninterpretable. So the paper enables a positive test of ARC-112 and forbids a negative one -- hence mixed rather than supports.
failure_signatures: Psi, Delta and Gamma are sufficient but not necessary conditions. A REE run returning Psi <= 0 across all candidate macro features licenses NO conclusion about ARC-112; reporting it as evidence that the federation framing is wrong would be a direct misuse of the criterion.

The criteria double-count redundancy up to n times, so systems with high redundancy yield false negatives. REE's streams share environmental input and are causally wired to each other (E2 consumes E1, the beta gate reads across), which is exactly the high-redundancy regime where the estimator is least sensitive.

Emergence is defined only relative to a chosen microscopic partition, and the authors state no principled method for choosing it. In REE the partition is a design decision (per-stream? per-latent-block? per-module?) that can manufacture or destroy the result, and nothing in the theory constrains it.

The framework assumes fully observable systems with Markovian dynamics, which the authors say 'often do not hold when dealing with experimental data'. REE's per-step telemetry is a partial view of a non-Markovian system with hidden recurrent state.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly methodological and directly load-bearing for the shape this cluster's prospective run has to take. The paper establishes that raw PID atoms are not comparable across systems or conditions with different total mutual information -- systems with identical structure but different noise flip from synergy-dominated to redundancy-dominated -- and supplies a TMI-matched null-model normalisation (NuMIT) with released code. INV-091's falsifier is explicitly an ABLATION SERIES comparing cross-stream statistics across arms; ablations change noise and change total mutual information, so this failure mode is not hypothetical for us, it is structural. Scored 0.72 rather than higher because the validation is on Gaussian and VAR(1) models plus one neuroimaging dataset, the authors state the linear-dynamics assumption is a real limit, and they concede that 'biologically meaningful null models remain unknown' -- the null-construction problem is improved here, not solved.
failure_signatures: Systems with identical source-target structure but different noise levels show PID atoms flipping from synergy-dominated to redundancy-dominated. An INV-091 ablation that changes a stream's effective noise -- which most ablations do -- can therefore reverse the apparent synergy/redundancy verdict with no change in organisation whatever, and be written up as evidence for the band.

Normalising by total mutual information (the obvious fix) assumes linear scaling, which is false: synergy, redundancy and unique information each scale differently with noise. A REE analysis that divides by TMI to make arms comparable has introduced a distortion rather than removed one.

Different PID definitions (MMI, CCS, DEP) agreed with each other at only about rho 0.4 on raw or naively normalised atoms. The choice of redundancy function is therefore a free parameter capable of changing the answer, and a REE result reported under a single unnamed PID definition is not reproducible.

The null ensembles preserve total mutual information ONLY, randomising everything else. The authors state that whether such nulls resemble real systems is an open question and that biologically meaningful nulls remain unknown -- so a NuMIT-normalised REE result is calibrated against a generic ensemble, not against a REE-plausible one.
Validation covers VAR(1) and linear-Gaussian dynamics; the authors state non-linear relationships are essential but not addressed. REE's streams are nonlinear by construction.

entries.confidence_rationale: Undercuts the measurement validity of the distractor positivity, the principal neural marker cited as evidence for a dedicated proactive suppression process, by showing it is attenuated when target features vary even though target selection itself is unaffected. Modest confidence: a single-study measurement critique in a contested literature, not a demonstration that suppression is absent.
failure_signatures: The distractor positivity was reliably attenuated when target features varied randomly across trials while the N2pc target-selection marker and manual response times were unaffected -- so the marker tracks something other than suppression alone.

Because the PD partly reflects target-feature upweighting, published evidence citing PD amplitude as an index of a dedicated suppression substrate is confounded with selection-history-driven target facilitation, and cannot be used to argue that REE lacks a mechanism its priority competition already supplies.

entries.confidence_rationale: Causal microstimulation plus recording, in primate, showing suppression is a graded competitive process WITHIN the selection map whose residue leaks into behaviour -- which cuts against the 'separate suppression module' reading of Q-082 while confirming suppression is genuinely pre-behavioural. Mixed because it supports the pre-selection timing but weakens the separable-substrate framing.
failure_signatures: Suppression is INCOMPLETE and time-varying at the moment of commitment, and the residual distractor activity biases the executed action continuously rather than being cleanly gated out -- a binary pre-selection filter does not reproduce curved trajectories.

Distractor-coding activity and target-coding activity live in the SAME map; suppression is expressed as relative activity within the selection substrate, so an architecture that adds a separate suppression module may double-count a function the priority competition already performs.
Selection can be committed BEFORE competition resolves -- the bottleneck does not wait, which means a top-k boundary can emit a contaminated selection rather than failing visibly.

entries.confidence_rationale: The strongest available evidence that biology implements a DEDICATED, anatomically separable pre-selection suppression substrate rather than folding suppression into the priority map -- causal inactivation, single-unit recording, and both exogenous and endogenous routes through one circuit. Discounted for the avian midbrain preparation and for the gap between a spatial space-map and REE's non-spatial cue routing.
failure_signatures: Inactivating Imc ABOLISHED competitive selection entirely -- selection did not degrade gracefully to a facilitation-only mode, so a priority map without a dedicated inhibitory partner may not select at all under competition rather than selecting worse.

The same circuit carried BOTH exogenous and endogenous suppression; an architecture that implements bottom-up salience competition and top-down goal biasing through separate mechanisms diverges from this organisation.
Suppression was global across the entire tectal space map from a spatially precise input -- a local or pairwise inhibition scheme does not reproduce this.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly tests and fails to find the central prediction of the signal suppression hypothesis using two independent converging measures with an appropriate task-irrelevant filler baseline. Weakens the premise that a proactive PRE-selection suppression signal is required, which is the premise Q-082 interrogates. Held below 0.75 because it is a null result in a deliberately minimal two-item display, where competition may be too weak to require suppression.
failure_signatures: No early proactive suppression of highly salient distractors was detectable below the task-irrelevant filler baseline -- the pattern was initial capture by ALL colour-change items followed by later focusing on the target, i.e. facilitation, not suppression.

A null result in a two-item display may not generalise to higher set sizes where competition is stronger; an architecture that reads this as 'no suppression substrate needed' may fail as the number of competing candidates grows -- directly relevant to whether MECH-254's top-k bottleneck scales.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, high-venue, neurally-grounded demonstration of exactly the asymmetry SD-076 posits (desirable errors incorporated, undesirable errors under-coded). Confidence held below 0.8 because the domain is self-referential beliefs about future life events, not a running estimate of one's own predictive accuracy, and because the paradigm's statistical basis was subsequently contested (see the Ni 2023 and Garrett 2018 entries in this directory).
failure_signatures: The asymmetry is carried by a FAILURE TO CODE undesirable errors, not by a symmetric rate difference -- if REE implements SD-076 as a pure two-rate EMA it reproduces the outcome but not the mechanism, and will not show the selective error-tracking dropout this paper measures.

Optimistic individuals showed reduced error tracking in right inferior prefrontal gyrus specifically for negative updates -- a between-subject trait axis SD-076's single global asymmetry parameter cannot express.

entries.confidence_rationale: Highest mapping fidelity of any entry in this directory: the asymmetry is driven BY a confidence/precision variable and acts ON subsequent evidence integration, which is structurally the self-reinforcing precision loop SD-076 encodes. MEG plus computational modelling, strong venue. Held below 0.85 because it is a within-trial post-decisional effect on perceptual evidence, not a slow across-episode drift in a variance estimate.
failure_signatures: Disconfirmatory evidence processing was ABOLISHED rather than merely attenuated at high confidence -- a linear two-rate EMA cannot produce a hard gate, so SD-076's functional form may understate the effect at the high-precision end where runaway inflation is most dangerous.

The effect is driven by confidence in a JUST-MADE choice; if REE's rv update is not conditioned on the agent's own commitment, the analogous gating has no trigger and SD-076 reduces to an unmotivated constant asymmetry.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly attacks the measurability of the parameter SD-076 posits, with model recovery analyses rather than assertion. Rated weakens rather than mixed because its consequence for REE is a concrete methodological hazard in SD-076's own validation design. Held at 0.7 because it concerns first-order reinforcement learning rates, and SD-076's quantity is a second-order variance estimate whose initialisation REE actually controls.
failure_signatures: Learning-rate asymmetry and initial value expectation are partially non-identifiable: fitting an asymmetry parameter without simultaneously fitting the initial expectation recovers the WRONG SIGN of asymmetry.

The direction of positive-vs-negative learning asymmetry in elementary reinforcement learning remains contested across studies -- so SD-076 cannot cite 'the RL literature' as settled support for a downward drift.
An ablation arm that changes the rv initialisation while intending to change only the asymmetry would produce a confounded MECH-204 Phase 7 result that looks like a precision-drift effect.

entries.confidence_rationale: Replicates the baseline asymmetry (supporting SD-076's existence) while showing it is state-dependent and vanishes under threat (weakening SD-076's implementation as a fixed global constant). Randomised laboratory manipulation plus an on-duty firefighter field sample is unusually strong converging design. Held at 0.68 by the same first-order/second-order mapping gap that limits the Sharot 2011 entry.
failure_signatures: The asymmetry EVAPORATES under perceived threat, tracked by galvanic skin response and self-reported anxiety -- a constant asymmetry parameter predicts drift in threatening contexts where humans show none.
If REE ever couples arousal or a threat signal to E3, an SD-076 with a fixed asymmetry will diverge from the biology precisely in the high-stakes regime where precision miscalibration is most costly.

entries.confidence_rationale: Neuron-tier human fMRI with an explicit computational arbitrator fit to behaviour and localised to inferior lateral PFC / frontopolar cortex. This is the empirical complement MECH-477 was missing: it establishes that a dedicated arbitration ELEMENT exists as a distinct neural signal, not merely that two pathways coexist -- exactly the architecture/dynamics distinction MECH-477 was minted to separate. Mapping fidelity is held below source quality because REE's goal-directed pathway is hippocampally-planned whereas the paper's model-based system is a tree-search over a task graph; the arbitration logic transfers more cleanly than the pathway identities.
failure_signatures: Arbitration is driven by RELIABILITY (inverse dispersion of prediction error), not by uncertainty in state-action VALUE as Daw 2005 proposed -- an arbitrator reading value-uncertainty is implementing a different quantity from the one the empirical work localises.

The two reliabilities are computed by DIFFERENT machinery and are not symmetric: model-based reliability from a Bayesian estimate over state prediction error, model-free reliability from a Pearce-Hall-style running average of |RPE|. A build that computes both arms' reliability with one shared estimator departs from the fitted model.

Arbitration acts by SUPPRESSING the model-free valuation pathway, with no reciprocal effect detected on the model-based pathway. A symmetric gain-sharing arbitrator is not what the connectivity data support.
A bias term favouring habit (lower cognitive effort) is required in the fitted transition dynamics; an unbiased arbitrator over-recruits the model-based arm.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the fMRI test of the Daw 2005 proposal already on file, and it cuts both ways for MECH-477. It SUPPORTS the graded-weighting half: choices reflected both influences, and the ventral striatal signal reflected model-free and model-based predictions in proportions MATCHING those that best explained each subject's behaviour -- a per-subject correspondence that is hard to get from anything other than a common weighting term. It WEAKENS the clean two-pathway architecture MECH-477 inherits from MECH-163: the authors' own conclusion is that the result challenges the notion of a separate model-free learner and suggests a more integrated computational architecture. Confidence is held at 0.62 because the paper is methodologically strong (source_quality 0.90) but its bearing on MECH-477 is genuinely ambiguous in direction, which is a mapping problem, not a quality problem.
failure_signatures: The ventral striatal BOLD signal is NOT a pure model-free report; it carries model-based prediction error too. A REE design that reads 'habit pathway activity' as a clean model-free proxy, and infers arbitration state from it, will mis-attribute planned influence to the habit arm.

Because the mixing proportions in the neural signal matched the proportions in behaviour, an integrated single-value architecture can reproduce graded recruitment WITHOUT a separable arbitration element -- so a graded novel-minus-familiar recruitment delta is NOT by itself sufficient evidence for MECH-477's arbitrator.

The two-step task dissociates model-based from model-free influence at the level of choice statistics, not at the level of anatomically separate pathways; evidence for arbitration DYNAMICS does not license the inference to two separable substrates.

entries.confidence_rationale: Causal, not correlational: pharmacological inactivation of a specific nucleus during behaviour, with single-unit recording in the target. Directly answers the question the pull was owed on -- biological selection variability is injected by a DEDICATED ANATOMICAL CHANNEL (LMAN, a basal-ganglia-forebrain output) onto a specific downstream motor population (RA), and it self-anneals over learning. Filed as MIXED rather than supports because it cuts in opposite directions on MECH-440's two halves: it strongly SUPPORTS the anti-global-temperature half (variability injection is channel-specific and separable) while UNDERCUTTING the sufficiency of the NoisyNet weight-noise form, which is still noise on the selection head's own parameters rather than a separate proposing pathway.
failure_signatures: LMAN inactivation made RA firing patterns adultlike in stereotypy WITHOUT dramatically affecting spike statistics or overall firing patterns -- so the variability source is anatomically SEPARABLE from the pathway that carries the action content. A single global scalar (temperature) applied to the selection distribution cannot reproduce this dissociation, because it necessarily perturbs the content pathway itself.

The variability is injected by a channel that ALSO carries a corrective bias, i.e. it is a structured exploratory signal, not zero-mean noise. A zero-mean isotropic perturbation is the wrong functional form.

Removing HVC (the premotor content input) destroyed song stereotypy entirely, whereas removing LMAN did not. Variability injection and action specification are doubly dissociable -- a design in which the exploration knob and the policy share one parameter set conflates them.

The relative contribution of the variability channel DECLINES as circuits mature, with the annealing implemented as a shift in the balance between two anatomically distinct inputs -- not as a decaying scalar on one input.

entries.confidence_rationale: Exceptionally broad and robust empirical base -- 14 datasets, seven cortical areas across four lobes, two species, replicated in membrane potential, single-unit spiking and array-measured correlated variability, awake and anaesthetised. Source quality is very high. It is filed as mixed for MECH-440 because it establishes the existence and modulation of a pre-commitment variability regime (supporting the premise that there IS a spread to modulate) while simultaneously identifying a mechanism -- input-driven stabilisation of network state -- that predicts injected variability will be QUENCHED at exactly the point MECH-440 needs it to propagate. That second reading is a candidate explanation for the V3-EXQ-708a null and is the reason this entry is decision-relevant rather than merely contextual.
failure_signatures: Variability declines at stimulus onset even when the stimulus produces little change in MEAN firing rate. So a manipulation can be demonstrably live in the mean while its variance contribution is independently suppressed -- an instrument that verifies a lever is 'reaching' the pathway by checking mean-level effects does NOT thereby show the variance survives to commitment.

The decline was observed for every stimulus tested, in every one of seven cortical areas, awake or anaesthetised -- suggesting a general property of cortex that its state is STABILISED by input. Injected noise upstream of a strongly input-driven stage should be expected to be attenuated by default, not to propagate by default.
The quenching appears in correlated variability measured across populations, not only in single units, so it is not a spike-count artefact that a population-level readout would average away.

A quantitative coordinate-based meta-analysis over 27 experiments is a strong aggregate source, and its central contrast -- semantic versus visuospatial analogy -- is a genuine cross-domain comparison of the kind Q-083 needs. Confidence is held below 0.8 because co-activation of a common region is architectural evidence of a weaker kind than behavioural transfer: shared BOLD activation does not establish a shared computation, and Q-083 is asked in terms of transfer, not localisation.
failure_signatures: Two relational-reasoning tasks that a domain-general account would treat as the same computation (visuospatial analogy and matrix problems) recruit at least partly distinct left/right networks and separate subregions within left rostrolateral PFC, so a single apprehender does not fall out of the imaging data even within one domain.

Domain-oriented regions in inferior and middle frontal gyri are recruited alongside the domain-general region, so any REE architecture claiming a single apprehender must still explain what the domain-specific machinery is doing.

entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative review arguing explicitly that map-like coding observed in spatial tasks is an instance of a general knowledge-organising mechanism that applies across domains -- the domain-general arm of Q-083's fork, stated as the paper's thesis. Confidence is held in the moderate band because it is a review advancing a position rather than a decisive test, and because the non-spatial domains it draws on (conceptual, social, task-space) are a narrower and more structurally homogeneous set than Q-083's six.
failure_signatures: The evidence for cross-domain map-like coding is strongest where the non-spatial domain has an obvious low-dimensional metric structure (continuous concept spaces, social hierarchies); domains without such structure are not shown to be organised this way, so the generality claim is untested exactly where Q-083 is least confident.

Demonstrating that the same REPRESENTATIONAL FORMAT appears in several domains does not demonstrate that one apprehension PROCESS built all of them -- shared format is compatible with parallel domain-specific learners converging on the same code.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality synthesis in a leading review venue, and it addresses Q-083's fork head-on rather than by analogy -- the paper exists precisely because the domain-general assumption failed empirically. It is downgraded from the top band because it is a review of behavioural statistical-learning studies in humans, not a direct test of a cross-domain transfer prediction under matched structure, which is the design Q-083's what_would_answer specifies.
failure_signatures: Learners' statistical-learning performance in one modality correlates poorly or not at all with their performance in another, so a single latent 'apprehender' capacity does not account for individual differences across domains.

Regularities of identical formal structure are learned at different rates and to different asymptotes depending on the modality and stimulus type carrying them, so apprehension rate is not a pure function of rule structure.

A cross-domain transfer test can therefore return a null not because the apprehender is domain-specific but because the two domains impose different input constraints on a shared computation -- the null is ambiguous between the two arms of Q-083.

entries.confidence_rationale: Rat hippocampal pyramidal-cell recordings analysed with an explicitly higher-order method (cliques are simplices; Betti curves are homology of the clique complex), finding structure that eigenvalue-based pairwise analysis misses. That is close to a direct demonstration that higher-order relational structure is present and informative in hippocampal population activity. Held below 0.8 because the higher-order object here is an ANALYST'S projection over a pairwise correlation matrix, not a demonstration that the circuit represents or uses hyperedges -- which is exactly Q-084's organisational-versus-representational distinction.
failure_signatures: Standard eigenvalue/PCA analyses of the same correlation matrices fail to distinguish geometric from random structure in the presence of unknown monotone nonlinearities, so a pairwise-summary readout can be actively misleading rather than merely incomplete.

Geometric organisation of correlations persists during wheel running and REM sleep, i.e. when there is no spatial position to code, so the structure cannot be explained as a downstream consequence of position coding -- an REE analogue would be topological structure in anchor correlations that survives removal of the spatial payload.

The clique-topology signal is computed from a PAIRWISE correlation matrix; a positive result therefore does not establish that anything above a pairwise relation is stored, only that the pairwise relations have higher-order geometric consequences.

entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative review directly addressing the source thought's candidate biological prediction 4 (longitudinal differences correspond to different levels of granularity) and bearing on prediction 1 (subregions preferentially encode different relation types). It supports the weaker organisational reading -- multiple functional domains plus superimposed gradients -- but says nothing about higher-order or multistep relational structure, which is Q-084's actual proposition. Filed at 0.60 because the mapping is to the thought's background hypothesis rather than to the registered claim.
failure_signatures: The long axis shows BOTH sharply demarcated gene-expression domains AND continuous anatomical/electrophysiological gradients, so a clean 'one subregion, one relation type' partition is not what the biology offers -- an REE design that assigns distinct relation types to distinct discrete modules would be over-committing.

Multiple functional organisations along the axis are established at the level of granularity and affective-versus-spatial function, not at the level of RELATION TYPE, so the review does not deliver the differentiated-relational-organisation evidence the source thought hoped for.

entries.confidence_rationale: A model built entirely on pairwise transition structure reproduces the diversity of entorhinal and hippocampal cell types, matches non-spatial relational task recordings, and yields a confirmed novel prediction (structure preserved across remapping) -- all without any representation above a pairwise relation. That is a substantive existence proof against Q-084's necessity claim. Held at 0.68 because absence of a need in one model family is not absence of a need in general, and TEM was never tested against the multistep typed-path readouts Q-084 specifies.
failure_signatures: A purely pairwise-transition model accounts for grid, band, border, object-vector, place and landmark cells plus non-spatial relational task representations, so the observed richness of hippocampal-entorhinal coding is not by itself evidence that higher-order structure is represented.

TEM's generalisation comes from factorising structure from sensory content, not from higher-order relations -- so an REE metapath readout that beats a pairwise baseline might be recovering factorisation the pairwise baseline failed to learn, rather than genuinely higher-order information.
The model was never compared against a metapath-aware or hyperedge readout, so its success bounds the necessity claim without testing the sufficiency claim Q-084 poses.

entries.confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed review in a respectable venue by authors with primary hippocampal expertise, and it is the closest thing in the literature to a direct statement of MECH-321's central architectural bet -- that one boundary-marker class serves both externally-driven and internally-generated sequences. But it is a hypothesis paper, not new data, and it argues for shared MARKERS, not for the specific operation MECH-321 needs (a boundary detected within an imagined trajectory causing that trajectory to be re-segmented at finer grain). Mapping fidelity is therefore the binding constraint and confidence is held below 0.6 despite good source quality.
failure_signatures: Sharp-wave ripples are described as occurring following the CESSATION of a unit of behaviour -- a post-hoc boundary marker. If REE's rollout-side segmenter inherits this timing, boundaries would be available only after a chunk has finished being imagined, which cannot support MECH-321's mid-execution decomposition phase.

The review treats consolidation, preplay and boundary-marking as competing interpretations of the same SWR signal. If one physiological event is genuinely doing all three jobs, a REE substrate that reads BoundaryEvents filtered by input_stream may be discarding the very multiplexing that makes the biological signal work.
No evidence is offered that boundary markers on internally generated sequences are RECURSIVE. The depth-cap-3-4 commitment MECH-321 inherits from Badre & D'Esposito has no support in this paper.

entries.confidence_rationale: Confirms that subgoal-grain prediction-error signals are real, striatally instantiated, and behaviourally consequential -- which supports the machinery MECH-321 presupposes. But the headline result is a cost, not a benefit: subgoal-grain signals biased choice toward pseudo-rewarding options that carried no actual reward advantage. Directionally mixed for that reason. Held at 0.60 because the samples are small (n=20 fMRI, n=19 behavioural) and the striatal individual-differences correlation is the statistically fragile part of the paper, while the mapping requires a mediating assumption REE has not yet committed to.
failure_signatures: Participants developed a preference for the most pseudo-rewarding option even though it did not yield more monetary reward -- subgoal-grain credit signals bias policy toward subgoal-rich trajectories with no terminal-objective advantage.

The strength of that bias tracked individual differences in relative striatal sensitivity to pseudo-reward PEs versus real reward PEs, so the distortion scales with how strongly the decomposition machinery is weighted rather than being a fixed offset that could be calibrated away once.

A decomposition operator that fires more readily (lower V_s threshold) produces more subgoals and therefore more pseudo-reward signal, giving a positive feedback path from decomposition depth to subgoal-seeking bias that MECH-321's depth cap does not obviously bound.

entries.confidence_rationale: The most direct available support for MECH-323's output contract: an empirical test, with formal Bayesian model comparison over model families, finding that humans build action sequences and that a goal-directed controller selecting over a mixed inventory of primitives and chunked sequences beats a flat architecture with an external arbitrator. Converging choice and reaction-time evidence. High mapping fidelity because what transfers is an architectural relation rather than a parameter. Held below 0.8 because the task is a single two-stage decision paradigm and the authors are careful that their result does not rule out all model-free accounts.
failure_signatures: The authors conclude that model-free RL is UNNECESSARY to explain habitual action -- chunked action sequences alone suffice. This bears directly on MECH-163 dual_goal_directed_systems, which MECH-323 cross-links to: if chunking is sufficient, the habit system may be the chunk inventory rather than a separate value-caching controller, and MECH-323 would be the whole habit story rather than the formation half of a dual system.

If habits are action sequences selected by a goal-directed process, then apparent outcome-insensitivity is a consequence of sequence GRAIN (the controller cannot intervene mid-sequence) rather than of a separate insensitive controller. A REE substrate that models habit as cached values will reproduce the phenomenon by the wrong mechanism and will mispredict where intervention is possible.

Chunk boundaries become the only points at which goal-directed control can act. A chunk-size budget set too high therefore silently reduces controllability, and the failure presents as outcome-insensitivity rather than as anything the accumulator itself reports.

entries.confidence_rationale: Primate single-unit recordings during untutored sequence acquisition, in a strong venue, hitting three separate MECH-323 commitments at once: an integrated cost-benefit (not repetition-only) formation signal, a gradual rather than step-like crystallisation profile, and a trial-end phasic response that sharpens with learning and reads naturally as a termination-condition marker. Discounted for being correlational -- the sharpening parallels learning with no causal manipulation -- and for a saccadic-motor notion of sequence that is well below REE's policy-primitive grain.
failure_signatures: The learning-correlated signal is an INTEGRATED cost-benefit quantity, not outcome alone. A REE accumulator gated on outcome consistency while ignoring accumulated action cost would form chunks the biology would not form, and would be blind to the case where a reliably-rewarded sequence is nevertheless too expensive to crystallise.

Sequence acquisition was untutored and repetitive scanning emerged without instruction, so the accumulator can crystallise chunks that no planner ever proposed as a unit. MECH-323's default MECH-094-strict write path assumes real executions are the trustworthy source; this shows real executions can be self-generated repetition rather than deliberate policy, which the replay_origin flag does not distinguish.

The trial-end response SHARPENS progressively rather than switching on. A substrate implementing chunk formation as a threshold crossing on F_low will produce a step-like commitment profile with no biological counterpart, and will lose the graded window in which a partly-formed chunk is still cheap to abandon.

This is Badre's own nine-years-later re-appraisal of the review that MECH-321's title cites for the depth cap, and it withdraws the premise the citation rests on: 'Our review of the evidence supports neither a unitary model of lateral frontal function nor a unidimensional abstraction gradient.' If there is no single ordered abstraction axis, there is no well-defined 'number of levels along it' to cap at 3-4. The replacement picture -- separate frontal networks interacting via local AND global hierarchical structure -- is not depth-indexed at all. Source quality 0.88 (TiCS review, first author is the author of the cited 2009 review, so this is self-correction rather than an outside critique); mapping fidelity 0.70 (it speaks directly to the construct the citation depends on); transfer risk 0.35.
failure_signatures: The 2009 rostro-caudal review is cited in MECH-321's title as licensing a depth cap of 3-4. Its own first author concluded in 2018 that a unidimensional abstraction gradient is not supported by the evidence -- so the citation is grounding a numeric cap on a construct its source now disputes.

If frontal control is multiple interacting networks with local and global hierarchical structure rather than one ordered axis, then 'decomposition depth' may not be the right control parameter at all -- the substrate analog would be several decomposition operators at different scales, not one operator recursing N times.

MECH-321's implementation currently mirrors ARC-071's chunk_max_depth for inverse-operator symmetry. Nothing in the updated hierarchical-control literature requires the composition and decomposition operators to share a depth budget; that symmetry is an REE design assumption with no biological warrant so far.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the primary empirical source behind the '3-4 levels' number that MECH-321's title attributes to Koechlin & Summerfield 2007, and it does license a small integer: the 2003 fMRI study resolves THREE nested control levels (sensory -> contextual -> episodic, mapped onto premotor -> caudal LPFC -> rostral LPFC), and the 2007 TiCS successor adds branching control at frontopolar cortex for a fourth. So the MAGNITUDE 3-4 is real and empirically anchored. What it does NOT license is the CONSTRUCT: this is a fixed anatomical cascade of qualitatively DIFFERENT control signals, each level adding a distinct kind of context-conditional information, measured during overt task performance. MECH-321's depth cap governs RECURSIVE self-similar re-application of one decomposition operator on the rollout stream. Those are different quantities that happen to share a number. Source quality 0.90 (Science, canonical, heavily replicated cascade design); mapping fidelity 0.45 -- the number transfers, the construct does not; transfer risk 0.50.
failure_signatures: The Koechlin cascade levels are QUALITATIVELY heterogeneous (sensory, contextual, episodic, branching) -- each level processes a different information type. MECH-321's recursion is HOMOGENEOUS (the same tiling operator re-applied). A cap derived from the heterogeneous cascade does not automatically bound the homogeneous recursion, and MECH-321 should not cite this paper as if it did.

The cascade is measured during OVERT task execution under external cueing, not during rollout / imagination. MECH-321 operates on the imagined trajectory, where nothing constrains the number of nested re-segmentations by an anatomical terminus.

If MECH-321's depth cap is defended on Koechlin grounds, the falsifier is that raising the cap above 4 should produce NO further behavioural differentiation. If deeper recursion keeps paying, the anatomical-cascade justification is the wrong justification even if the cap is a good engineering choice.

entries.confidence_rationale: Recorded deliberately as an explicit NULL rather than omitted. This is the strongest available normative account of what makes one action hierarchy better than another at exactly REE's grain (subtasks over primitive actions, not finger movements), backed by four human behavioural experiments -- so if a principled depth cap or subtask-size budget existed at policy grain, this is where it would be. It is not there. The authors restrict their analysis to one-level hierarchies purely 'to assure computational tractability in the present application' and state the framework 'generalizes without any alteration to deeper hierarchies'. They partition on bottleneck states, and impose no constraint on how many primitive actions a subtask may contain. Source quality 0.85; mapping fidelity 0.65 (right grain, right question, no answer); transfer risk 0.30. Direction 'unknown' because the paper neither supports nor weakens the numbers -- it establishes that the normative literature is silent on both.
failure_signatures: The leading normative account of hierarchy quality imposes no depth limit and no subtask-size budget. Both of MECH-321's depth cap and MECH-323's 2-5 chunk-size budget are therefore engineering choices at policy grain, not literature-derived defaults, and should be labelled as such wherever they are stated.

Solway et al. restrict to one-level hierarchies for tractability -- the same reason MECH-321 caps depth. That is an honest parallel and arguably the correct justification for MECH-321's cap, but it is a computational-cost argument, not a biological one, and it predicts the cap should MOVE as compute allows rather than sit at a fixed biological constant.

Their optimal hierarchies are defined by WHERE the partition falls (bottleneck states), not by how large or how deep the pieces are. This is a direct argument that MECH-321's R5 bottleneck trigger mode is better motivated than its depth cap -- the literature constrains the partition location and leaves the budget free.

entries.confidence_rationale: Supplies the missing MECHANISM behind the 2-5 range while undercutting its status as a constant. Chunk length correlates with visuospatial working-memory capacity within both young and older adults, and older adults show a joint reduction in BOTH capacity and chunk length. So the small-integer chunk size is downstream of a capacity bottleneck rather than being a primitive of the chunking system -- which is a satisfying explanation for why the number lands near the classic short-term capacity range, and simultaneously a warning that it is agent-specific and can shift. Source quality 0.72 (J Neurophysiol, correlational, moderate n); mapping fidelity 0.60; transfer risk 0.42.
failure_signatures: Chunk length tracks working-memory capacity across individuals and declines with age alongside it. A chunk-size budget hard-coded at 2-5 for every REE agent asserts a uniformity the human data specifically contradicts -- the budget should be derived from whatever plays the capacity role in REE, not set by fiat.

The correlation between capacity and LEARNING RATE held in young adults but NOT in older adults, while the capacity-to-chunk-length correlation held in both. Chunk size and formation rate are therefore dissociable, so MECH-323's R_min (repetition count) and its size budget should not be calibrated as if they were governed by one underlying quantity.

This is explicit sequence learning with a declarative component. If REE's accumulator is meant to be the DLS-analog procedural path (Graybiel repetition-and-consistency, value-flat), a capacity-derived size bound imported from an explicit task may be importing the wrong system's constraint.

entries.confidence_rationale: Weakens the FIXED-CONSTANT form of MECH-323's chunk-size budget while supporting its small-at-first spirit. Monkeys learning a 10-element reaching sequence over months start with many short chunks and progressively merge them: 'the length of individual chunks increases. As chunks become longer over the course of learning, movements are optimized over increasingly longer horizons.' Chunk size is therefore a MOVING quantity set by a compute-versus-efficiency trade-off, not a species constant in 2-5. The authors propose no fixed upper bound; the observed ceiling is a diminishing-returns effect (chunk structures stay at roughly 50-60% of the complexity of executing the sequence as a single chunk). Source quality 0.85 (Nature Communications, longitudinal non-human primate, explicit generative model); mapping fidelity 0.60 (reaching kinematics, not policy primitives); transfer risk 0.40.
failure_signatures: Chunk size GROWS with practice. A hard chunk-size budget fixed at 2-5 for the agent's lifetime forbids the single most robust longitudinal signature in this literature, and would make MECH-323 unable to reproduce the observed learning trajectory even if every other trigger condition were right.

The ceiling on chunk size is set by a compute-versus-efficiency trade-off, not by a capacity constant. Two REE agents with different rollout budgets should therefore settle at different chunk sizes -- so a single global max chunk length is the wrong shape of parameter; it should be derived from the deliberation budget.

The monkeys never chunk the whole sequence as one unit, staying near 50-60% of single-chunk complexity. An REE accumulator that grows chunks monotonically without a returns-based brake would eventually collapse an episode into one chunk, which is the failure mode this paper's trade-off explicitly rules out.

entries.confidence_rationale: The most direct available evidence for the DIRECTION of MECH-323/MECH-324's hysteresis, from the same lab and preparation as the ARC-071 substrate anchors already in the corpus. Long-term multi-unit recording in sensorimotor striatum across acquisition, extinction and reacquisition: task-related ensemble patterns 'successively formed, reversed and then re-emerged', and the paper opens by noting that learning not to perform an ingrained habit is notoriously difficult while regaining one can occur with a few exposures. That is an explicit acquisition-versus-dissolution asymmetry with a neural correlate, which is exactly the relation F_low < F_high is meant to encode. Source quality 0.92 (Nature, chronic ensemble recording, behaviour-correlated); mapping fidelity 0.55 (it is a timescale and reversibility asymmetry, not a variance-threshold measurement); transfer risk 0.40.
failure_signatures: The asymmetry Barnes et al. demonstrate is one of TIMESCALE and RETRIEVABILITY -- the pattern reverses under extinction but re-emerges almost immediately on reacquisition -- not one of a higher evidence THRESHOLD for dissolution. MECH-324's T_dissolve (slower dissolution timescale) is directly supported; F_high > F_low as a variance-gate asymmetry is supported only by analogy.

Because the trace survives dissolution, an REE implementation that DELETES a chunk on crossing F_high diverges from the biology: the biological chunk is suppressed and rapidly re-instatable, not erased. A dissolved chunk should be retained in a dormant state with a lowered re-formation threshold, which the current MECH-323/324 pair does not specify.

Task-irrelevant firing was suppressed, rebounded, then suppressed again across the three phases. If REE's accumulator has no analog of that rebound, dissolution will look cleaner in REE than in biology and the re-formation dynamics will be wrong even if the thresholds are right.

entries.confidence_rationale: The behavioural half of the dissolution-asymmetry case, and specifically the INSTRUMENTAL (action) half rather than the Pavlovian one -- which matters because MECH-323 chunks actions, not cues. Bouton et al. review three converging relapse effects after instrumental extinction (renewal in a changed context, resurgence when an alternative response is itself extinguished, and rapid reacquisition on re-reinforcement), all showing extinction 'weakens behavior without erasing the original learning'. Extinction is new, context-dependent learning stored alongside the old. This is the mechanistic account of why dissolution is asymmetric with formation. Source quality 0.78 (review of the authors' own programme, rat operant, well-replicated effects); mapping fidelity 0.65; transfer risk 0.35.
failure_signatures: Extinction does not erase; it installs a competing, context-gated memory. An REE dissolution operator that removes the chunk from the library implements erasure, which the instrumental-extinction literature says is the wrong operation -- and predicts REE will not show renewal, resurgence, or rapid reacquisition, all of which are robust in the biology.

Extinction learning is 'relatively dependent on the context for expression'. MECH-323's chunks carry an initiation_set of contexts. If dissolution is context-blind while formation is context-conditioned, an REE chunk dissolved in one context stays dissolved in all -- diverging from renewal, where the behaviour returns simply by changing context.

Resurgence means a chunk can return not because its own evidence improved but because a COMPETING chunk was extinguished. Nothing in MECH-323/324 as registered produces that coupling, so a chunk library that competes for selection would need dissolution state shared across candidates to reproduce it.

entries.confidence_rationale: The most direct available evidence for the DIRECTION of MECH-323/MECH-324's hysteresis, from the same lab and preparation as the ARC-071 substrate anchors already in the corpus. Long-term multi-unit recording in sensorimotor striatum across acquisition, extinction and reacquisition: task-related ensemble patterns 'successively formed, reversed and then re-emerged', and the paper opens by noting that learning not to perform an ingrained habit is notoriously difficult while regaining one can occur with a few exposures. That is an explicit acquisition-versus-dissolution asymmetry with a neural correlate, which is exactly the relation F_low < F_high is meant to encode. Source quality 0.92 (Nature, chronic ensemble recording, behaviour-correlated); mapping fidelity 0.55 (it is a timescale and reversibility asymmetry, not a variance-threshold measurement); transfer risk 0.40.
failure_signatures: The asymmetry Barnes et al. demonstrate is one of TIMESCALE and RETRIEVABILITY -- the pattern reverses under extinction but re-emerges almost immediately on reacquisition -- not one of a higher evidence THRESHOLD for dissolution. MECH-324's T_dissolve (slower dissolution timescale) is directly supported; F_high > F_low as a variance-gate asymmetry is supported only by analogy.

Because the trace survives dissolution, an REE implementation that DELETES a chunk on crossing F_high diverges from the biology: the biological chunk is suppressed and rapidly re-instatable, not erased. A dissolved chunk should be retained in a dormant state with a lowered re-formation threshold, which the current MECH-323/324 pair does not specify.

Task-irrelevant firing was suppressed, rebounded, then suppressed again across the three phases. If REE's accumulator has no analog of that rebound, dissolution will look cleaner in REE than in biology and the re-formation dynamics will be wrong even if the thresholds are right.
