entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical prior-art paper for the operation SD-078 performs: it establishes that a learned representation carries a large common mean vector that is not content, that removing it improves downstream discrimination, and that the improvement is consistent across tasks, datasets, hyperparameters and languages. That breadth is what makes SD-078's centering a well-precedented move rather than an ad-hoc patch. Confidence is capped at 0.70 because REE implements only HALF the prescribed operation -- the common mean vector, not the top dominating directions -- and the paper's evaluation is of the combined procedure, so its headline gains cannot be attributed to mean-removal alone.
failure_signatures: The paper's prescribed operation is mean removal PLUS elimination of the top ~d/100 principal directions; its reported gains are for the combination. SD-078 implements only the mean-removal half, so the evidence transfers only partially and the residual dominating directions are left in place.

The number of directions removed is a hyperparameter, and Timkey & van Schijndel (2021) report all-but-the-top to be highly sensitive to it -- ineffective at the final layer of GPT-2 for any choice of D. A REE extension to PC removal would therefore introduce a tuning surface that the current mean-only fix does not have.

The method assumes a corpus-level static mean estimated over the whole vocabulary. It says nothing about an online estimate over a non-stationary stream, which is what SD-078's EMA baseline actually is.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong, carefully-ablated empirical support for the DIAGNOSIS half of SD-078 -- that a cosine over a learned latent can be dominated by a common mode to the point of carrying no usable ordering information, at anisotropy levels quantitatively comparable to REE's measured z_world cone. Weakened on the PRESCRIPTION half: the paper's own comparison found mean-subtraction alone insufficient exactly where the dominant dimension has high variance rather than merely a high mean, with per-dimension standardization the more reliable correction. SD-078 implements mean-subtraction only. Source quality high (EMNLP main, 4 models x all layers, 500k token pairs, public code, prior result replicated); mapping fidelity good but not identity (transformer token embeddings vs an RL world-model latent), so held below 0.8.
failure_signatures: Subtracting only the mean vector can leave the cosine still dominated by the same 1-3 dimensions when those dimensions have high variance and not merely a large mean: the paper reports that mean-subtraction yielded substantial gains in most models but failed in the final layers of GPT-2 and XLNet, where 1-3 dimensions still drove the variability of cosine similarity after the mean was removed.

Rank-based readouts are not automatically safe. Spearman correlation is robust to outlier dimensions, but the paper notes rogue dimensions tend to occupy the top or bottom ranks, so a rank statistic can still be systematically shaped by the common mode.

The dimensions that dominate cosine similarity are not the dimensions that drive downstream behaviour: ablating the cosine-dominating dimensions in GPT-2 and XLNet produced only vanishingly small changes to the model's output distribution. A representation can therefore look degenerate under cosine while its consumers are unaffected, and vice versa -- so a cosine-level repair does not by itself predict a consumer-level effect.

entries.confidence_rationale: The strongest and most decision-relevant literature finding for SD-079, and it cuts both ways. It confirms that removing a shared common mode from a set of signals is a decisive, non-cosmetic operation that transforms an inflated all-positive similarity distribution into a differentiated one -- SD-079's central mechanism. But it also establishes ANALYTICALLY, not merely empirically, that after such a removal the similarity values must sum to a negative value and are distributed approximately centred on zero. That makes the specific downstream evidence SD-079 cites for success -- that the MECH-292 goal_match_floor now excludes 9 of 24 anchors and the MECH-339 outshining gate is now nonzero on 9 of 24 -- partly a mathematical consequence of centering rather than a demonstration that those absolute gates now select on motivational relevance. Confidence held at 0.62: source quality is high and the analytic component transfers exactly, but the empirical apparatus (BOLD, seed-voxel correlation, breath-holding) is far from a hippocampal anchor pool, so transfer risk is substantial.
failure_signatures: After subtraction of a common mode, the similarity values to a given reference must sum to a negative value, and the empirical distribution of those values becomes bell-shaped and centred on zero. Any ABSOLUTE threshold applied downstream of centering therefore partitions the pool at a location largely determined by the centering operation itself, not by the content of the cue -- so 'the gate is now live' and 'the gate is now meaningful' are different claims, and only the first is demonstrated by an exclusion count.

Negative similarity values produced by centering can be spurious: the paper shows in simulation that small phase differences between signals are sufficient to produce negative correlations after global regression, and concludes that global signal regression is most likely the cause of the anti-correlated networks previously interpreted as intrinsic brain organisation. The analogous REE risk is that centered goal_match values below zero are read as active dissimilarity between a goal and an anchor when they encode nothing of the sort.

The interpretation of any structure discovered only after common-mode removal is called into question by this paper's central argument. A REE result of the form 'the centered arm shows differentiation that the raw arm does not' is necessary but not sufficient; it needs a check that the differentiation tracks something independently identifiable, not merely that it exists.

entries.confidence_rationale: Supports SD-079's premise on strong empirical footing -- across three independent datasets plus 47 task contrasts from the Human Connectome Project, removing a shared widespread component demonstrably improves anatomical specificity and reduces spurious structure. But the paper's central result is that a SINGLE global mean estimate captures only one kind of widespread coherent structure, and that an iterative cluster-based estimator (DiCER) removes more of it and better preserves genuine task-related structure. SD-079 uses a single scalar-alpha EMA mean vector, which is the class of estimator this paper finds incomplete. Confidence 0.55 because mapping fidelity is the weakest of the four entries in this pull: the evidence is about the sufficiency of an estimator in a spatiotemporal imaging pipeline, and the argument that it generalises to an online latent baseline is structural rather than demonstrated.
failure_signatures: A single global-mean estimate is only effective against specific kinds of widespread coherent structure. The paper reordered carpet plots to expose cluster structure and found a greater diversity of widespread signal deflections than previously recognised, varying across time and across participants, of which global signal regression removes only some -- so 'the common mode has been subtracted' does not entail 'the common mode has been removed'.

Removal of a shared component can distort between-group comparisons of the resulting connectivity measures. The REE analogue is arm-vs-arm comparison: an ON arm and an OFF arm differing in whether centering is applied are not merely differing in one term, since centering alters the distribution of every downstream match, and a between-arm delta can therefore reflect the estimator rather than the mechanism under test.

The common mode is not necessarily stationary in form. The paper reports that the precise form of widespread deflections varies across time and participants, so an estimator tuned on one regime can under-remove in another -- the direct analogue of SD-079's own finding that alpha 0.02 lags a drifting z_goal (spread 0.0942 / 0.1508 / 0.3319 across seeds 101/202/303) while 0.05 tracks it.

entries.confidence_rationale: Scoped weakening, not a refutation. The paper's Bayesian model comparison over model FAMILIES favours a hierarchical architecture in which habits are chunked action sequences selected by a single goal-directed process, and concludes model-free RL is UNNECESSARY to explain habitual action. That bears directly on MECH-163's characterisation of its habit pathway as `model-free`, and on nothing else in the claim: it does not touch the existence of two selectable grains, and it says nothing whatever about novel-context recruitment (which is V3-EXQ-786b's business). Held below the companion MECH-323 entry's 0.78 because the load-bearing content HERE is the paper's NEGATIVE claim, which the authors themselves hedge as not ruling out all possible model-free accounts -- a negative from a single two-stage paradigm is weaker evidence than the positive architectural relation the MECH-323 entry borrows. Held at 0.72 rather than lower because the weakening is independently corroborated at source: REE's substrate contains no model-free machinery to defend.
failure_signatures: MECH-163's habit pathway is described as `model-free` (SNc/dorsal-striatum, cached S-R associations). ree-v3/ree_core/ contains NO model-free machinery: zero hits for model_free / q_value / q_table / td_error / sarsa. SD-081 implements the habit read as _score_depth_limit truncation of the SAME model-based E3 scorer. The descriptor was never true of the build, so the paper's model comparison and the substrate agree against the claim's wording.

If the habit pathway is a depth-limited read of one model rather than a second controller, then V3-EXQ-811a's PASS is evidence that DEPTH-arbitration produces the recruitment signature -- not evidence for a cached-value second system. Citing 811a as support for a model-free/model-based dual system would over-read it.

The hierarchical account relocates outcome-insensitivity from a separate insensitive controller to sequence GRAIN. In REE that relocation is already realised: a committed ARC-071 chunk is released by five mechanisms (MECH-091, MECH-342, rung-6 duration + SD-033e, MECH-321/ARC-070, SD-034) and NONE reads whether the committed outcome is still valuable. A substrate that models habit as cached values will mispredict where intervention is possible.

Independent causal confirmation, by a different method (muscimol inactivation) in a different task (instrumental lever-press with specific-satiety devaluation) from a different laboratory, that infralimbic cortex is required for habitual rather than goal-directed control, and that removing it restores the goal-directed alternative INTACT. This is the convergent-evidence pillar under MECH-324's maintenance-operator framing, and it independently supports retention: the action-outcome representation survived extended overtraining unimpaired and was immediately usable. Held at 0.76 rather than higher because the paper's own conclusion -- that habit reflects ACTIVE INHIBITION of goal-directed responding -- describes a mechanism MECH-324 does not implement, so the entry supports the claim's phenomenon while flagging a real architectural divergence.
failure_signatures: The authors conclude that 'the development of habitual responding reflects the active inhibition of goal-directed responses that are mediated by action-outcome associations'. MECH-324's maintenance operator gates whether a CHUNK is selectable; it does not implement an inhibitory projection onto the decomposed goal-directed alternative. These are functionally similar and mechanistically different, and the difference predicts divergence wherever the two alternatives must compete rather than merely be enabled or disabled.

Goal-directed control returned in full after extended overtraining, meaning the action-outcome representation was never degraded by habitisation. Any REE implementation in which chunk crystallisation weakens, overwrites, or reduces the accessibility of the constituent primitives would diverge from this result. MECH-321 decomposition interacts here: the claim's own notes flag the open question of whether decomposition should trigger DISSOLVING, and this paper argues the primitives stay fully available regardless of chunk state.

Control-infused overtrained animals were insensitive to devaluation while muscimol animals were sensitive. A validation experiment that measures only chunk selection frequency, without an outcome-sensitivity probe, cannot distinguish 'the chunk was dissolved' from 'the chunk was never selected on these trials'. Devaluation-sensitivity is the discriminating measure and REE has no analog of it registered.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the causal-necessity paper MECH-324's implementation_note cites in spirit but which was not on file, and it is the direct biological warrant for the 2026-07-27 structural correction from erasure/tombstone to suppression-with-retention. Two findings map almost one-to-one: (1) disrupting infralimbic cortex BLOCKS an established habit online, within an average of three trials and as early as the first trial, so maintenance is a continuously-required gate rather than a one-shot crystallisation event; (2) after weeks of new-habit training, re-imposing the same perturbation caused rats to REGAIN the previously suppressed original habit while the newer one was blocked -- the suppressed chunk was retained, dormant and recoverable, which is exactly what MECH-324's corrected DISSOLVED state now asserts and what the as-first-built absorbing tombstone forbade. Held at 0.82 rather than higher because the mapping runs from an IL population-activity disruption to a software maintenance switch, and because rodent T-maze habit is a much narrower behavioural object than a policy chunk.
failure_signatures: The original habit was regained on re-perturbation, meaning it survived weeks of a competing habit being trained over it. Any implementation in which DISSOLVED is terminal, or in which a dissolved sequence is blocked from re-forming, is inconsistent with this result -- which is precisely the defect corrected in ree-v3 6c3e67e, where a retained tombstone permanently blocked its own sequence from re-forming at any number of repetitions.

Blockade occurred within about 9 seconds of inhibition and as soon as the first trial (<3 s). Maintenance is therefore fast-acting and continuously required. An REE maintenance operator whose dissolution is slow-by-construction (the DISSOLVING hysteresis window) will not reproduce this latency; if a validation experiment measures time-to-suppression it should expect a discrepancy attributable to REE design choice, not to a substrate bug.

Perturbation toggled BOTH ways -- suppressing the new habit while restoring the old one in the same intervention. This implies a competitive selection among retained chunks rather than independent per-chunk gates. MECH-324 implements per-chunk lifecycle states with no cross-chunk competition, so this is an unmodelled degree of freedom and a candidate explanation if a validation experiment finds dissolution behaving independently across chunks when biology predicts trade-off.

Generalised performance ability and motivation to consume reward were unaffected. A REE dissolution mechanism that degrades general policy performance alongside chunk suppression would be diverging from the biology, and a validation experiment should carry that as an explicit control rather than reading a global performance drop as successful dissolution.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly on point for the ISOLABILITY of the action-side deficit: the paper ablates state embeddings and action embeddings separately and reports that 'action embeddings alone improve the sample efficiency and peak performance of model-free RL on control from low-dimensional states'. That is the precise counterfactual SD-080 needs, because the spike's control showed z_world DOES vary and world_forward DOES become state-dependent -- i.e. the REE deficit is action-side-only, exactly the arm this paper isolates. Held below 0.8 because the learning objective is forward prediction over action SEQUENCES in continuous control, whereas REE's O is a per-step, 5-discrete-action space, and the paper's downstream consumer is model-free RL rather than a CEM planner.
failure_signatures: The paper's action embedding is trained by forward prediction -- predicting the resulting state from (state embedding, action-sequence embedding). A representation trained this way is state-conditioned by construction. REE's action_object_head takes z_world as input but, being frozen at initialisation, produces output that is 99.5% a function of the action label alone, so it fails the defining property of a dynamics-aware embedding while retaining its input signature.

The benefit here is measured as sample efficiency and peak performance on continuous control, not as planning quality inside the embedding. If REE reproduces this experiment it must not assume the two transfer: a CEM planner that refits a sampling distribution inside O could in principle be helped or hurt by a learned geometry in ways a policy-gradient learner is not.

The paper's action embeddings are of action SEQUENCES, deliberately, because the informative dynamics structure lives at the multi-step level. REE's action objects are single-step. If the consequence structure that matters is multi-step, then even a fully-trained single-step REE action_object_head would not recover what this paper shows to be useful -- SD-080's fix as currently framed may be necessary but not sufficient.

entries.confidence_rationale: Included deliberately as the counterweight to the two supporting entries: it is the strongest available demonstration that a randomly initialised, never-trained encoder can be not merely adequate but PREFERABLE for a downstream geometric computation, outperforming ICM and RND on DeepMind Control Suite. It therefore weakens the inference 'frozen and random, therefore useless'. But it does NOT weaken SD-080's actual finding, because RE3's random encoder is a random encoder OF THE INPUT and its output varies with the input, which is what makes the k-NN entropy estimate meaningful -- whereas REE's frozen head has measured r2_explained_by_action_alone = 0.9947, i.e. it discards its state input almost entirely. Confidence is moderate because the entry's value is analytic (it sharpens what SD-080's defect IS) rather than directly evidential about REE.
failure_signatures: RE3 shows that random-projection geometry is preserved well enough for k-NN distance computations, which sharpens SD-080 into a stronger claim than 'the head is random': a random projection of (z_world, a) should have INHERITED some of z_world's variation, yet the spike measured between-state variance of about 6e-05 against a z_world total variance of 0.0031. The collapse is therefore attributable to initialisation scale or architecture, not to randomness as such -- and a fix that only 'connects the gradient' without diagnosing why the state input is being annihilated may not resolve it.

If a frozen random encoder is sufficient for the downstream consumer's purpose, adding a learned one can be pure cost. RE3's authors explicitly motivate the random encoder on compute grounds -- no gradient updates through it. Any REE experiment repairing SD-080 must therefore measure the cost side as well, and must include a frozen-but-non-collapsed control arm, not only frozen-vs-learned.

The property RE3 needs from its encoder is only that distances be approximately preserved. The property SD-004 needs from O is far stronger: that distance MEAN similarity of world-effect, so that actions with the same consequence embed alike. Random projection gives the first and cannot give the second. An REE experiment that validates only distance-preservation in O would pass while leaving the SD-004 specification unmet.

entries.confidence_rationale: High mapping fidelity: the paper's learned action-representation space is the same object SD-004 specifies for O -- a low-dimensional action space whose geometry is induced by observed consequences (inverse dynamics over state transitions), with the policy searching IN that space. The paper's central empirical result is precisely the counterfactual SD-080 asserts: agents whose action space carries no learned consequence structure degrade as the action set grows, while the learned-representation agent does not. Confidence is held below 0.85 because the demonstrated gains are for LARGE finite action sets (2^4 to 2^12; thousands of actions in the recommender domains), whereas REE's action_dim is 5 -- the paper does not establish that the deficit bites at that scale, and the SD-080 spike measured the representation, not a performance decrement.
failure_signatures: An action space with no learned consequence structure cannot support inference about the outcome of an untried action from the outcomes of similar tried actions -- the paper's stated mechanism for generalisation. A frozen random action-object head therefore gives the CEM no basis for generalising across the action-object neighbourhood it searches.

The paper's baselines (actor-critic, DPG) degrade monotonically as the action set grows from 2^4 to 2^12 while the learned-representation agent holds performance. This predicts that the SD-080 defect is scale-dependent and may be near-invisible at REE's action_dim = 5, so a null result in a small-action-space REE experiment would NOT license concluding the frozen head is harmless.

The representation is learned by supervised inverse dynamics, NOT by the policy-gradient signal. This means the deficit cannot be repaired merely by letting the existing REE training paths reach the head: the training paths that currently miss it are reward/prediction paths, and the paper's own argument is that a supervised-transition objective is what makes the representation low-variance and learnable.

The most direct empirical evidence available for Q-085's central premise -- that the grain of the represented action unit sets the grain at which outcome-value information can act -- established by a clean double dissociation (sham rats reorganised at sequence level, dmPFC-lesioned rats at element level). Direction is mixed rather than supports because the same result cuts against the naive reading of Q-085's RESOLVED-YES criterion: the chunked animals were fully devaluation-SENSITIVE at the sequence boundary. Capped at 0.72 because sequences were two presses, so the study contributes nothing to the monotonic dose-response over chunk length that Q-085 actually tests.
failure_signatures: Chunking did not abolish outcome sensitivity -- it relocated it to the sequence boundary. Sham rats withheld the entire sequence whose outcome had been devalued. A design that makes the devaluation fully knowable BEFORE chunk onset can therefore find flat persistence across chunk lengths while the grain-as-controllability hypothesis is true, because the animal (or agent) simply declines to commit.

The lesion manipulates the CAPACITY to chunk, not chunk SIZE. A chunk-versus-no-chunk contrast cannot distinguish a monotonic dose-response in realised length from a threshold effect at any length greater than one.

When sequence-level representation was disrupted, control did not disappear but shifted to the terminal response specifically -- the element closest to the outcome -- rather than distributing across elements. Element-wise credit assignment is not the null case for losing a chunk.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong, causally-supported evidence (recording plus genetic disruption) that a learned action sequence acquires explicitly signalled boundaries, which is the structural premise Q-085 rests on: if boundaries are what the circuit represents, boundaries are where control can be applied. The specific result that start/stop activity did NOT reflect action value is an independent echo of the V3 substrate finding that none of the five release mechanisms reads whether the committed outcome is still valuable. Held at 0.64 because the study never tests devaluation or mid-sequence intervention, so it evidences the boundary structure and not the controllability consequence.
failure_signatures: Start/stop activity emerged only WITH sequence learning -- boundaries are a learned property of a consolidated sequence, not a fixed property of the task. An agent whose chunks have not yet crystallised has no boundary structure to measure, which is the readiness failure V3-EXQ-810 hit on two of three seeds.

The bracketing signals did not reflect interval timing, movement speed, or action value. A sequence-boundary signal being value-blind means the representation that governs commitment carries no information about whether the committed outcome is still worth having.

Disrupting striatal circuit function abolished the development of start/stop activity AND selectively impaired sequence learning, so boundary signalling and sequence acquisition are not separable -- one cannot ablate the boundary structure while leaving chunk formation intact as a control.

entries.confidence_rationale: High source quality (eLife, four independent single-unit datasets spanning rat and macaque, prefrontal and orbitofrontal), and the specific finding SD-082 needs -- that a condition-independent component absorbs a large share of population variance and swamps the task-relevant components unless it is explicitly removed -- is exactly the failure SD-082 diagnoses in the SD-033a bias head. Held below 0.8 because dPCA is an analyst's decomposition, not a circuit mechanism: the paper establishes that the common mode exists and dominates, not that any downstream neural read-out subtracts it.
failure_signatures: A task variable can be robustly and differentially encoded in a population while being invisible in any read-out taken from the raw population response, because a condition-independent component of much larger magnitude dominates the signal. Measuring the differentiation upstream (as V3-EXQ-822 did with on_rule_state_diff 0.644) therefore does not license the inference that the differentiation is available downstream.

Standard PCA -- and, by the same logic, any variance-ranked or magnitude-ranked summary of candidate states -- returns components that mix the common mode with the task-relevant signal, so the leading components are not the informative ones.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily replicated result from a top venue, and it speaks to both halves of SD-082 -- but in opposite directions, which is why the direction is mixed rather than supports. It corroborates the premise (a context/rule signal is a small displacement riding on a much larger shared representation, and is not gated out at the input) while undercutting the sufficiency of the remedy (in cortex, context is converted into differential action by recurrent dynamics over time, not by a static affine read-out). Held at 0.66 because the task -- two-modality perceptual discrimination in macaque -- is a long way from a learned pool of sixteen live rules biasing action candidates.
failure_signatures: Irrelevant evidence is not suppressed at the input: both the relevant and the irrelevant sensory signals remain robustly represented in the prefrontal population, and selection occurs downstream in the recurrent dynamics. An architecture that assumes the rule signal arrives pre-separated, or that a single read-out layer can do the separating, is assuming away the part cortex actually solves dynamically.

The context signal itself is a comparatively small displacement of the population state relative to the dominant condition-shared and time-varying structure, so its behavioural leverage is not proportional to its magnitude in the raw response.

entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative review establishing that removing a pooled common drive is a canonical cortical operation, present across areas, modalities and species -- which is real biological warrant for SD-082's design instinct on BOTH of its changes (strip the common mode; bound the output without a hard rail). Scored below 0.6 because of a specific and non-trivial operator mismatch: the canonical computation is DIVISIVE and SD-082 implements SUBTRACTIVE mean removal, and a review cannot be evidence for a form it does not describe.
failure_signatures: Without normalisation, a strong shared drive saturates responses and destroys the differential pattern across a population -- the same end state as SD-082's hard clamp railing every candidate to a common value.
Divisive gain control bounds responses while preserving relative differences; a bound implemented instead as a hard rail discards both the differences and the local gradient in its flat region.

entries.confidence_rationale: Provides the specific empirical prediction MECH-476's third arm is built on: a weak training episode that would only yield short-term memory is consolidated into long-term memory when a novelty exposure occurs close in time. That is the exact discriminator between a consolidation PROCESS and a mere regulariser, because a regulariser has no reason to respond to an unrelated novelty exposure. Confidence held below the design-source paper because the mechanism (dopaminergic PRP capture, protein synthesis) is biologically specific and REE's RND novelty drive is only a functional analog.
failure_signatures: The novelty effect required activation of dopamine D1/D5 receptors and newly synthesised proteins in dorsal hippocampus, and depended on temporal proximity between the weak trace and the novelty exposure. REE's RND novelty drive is a reward-shaping signal, not a protein-synthesis-gated capture process, so a null result in the REE novelty-paired arm may reflect an absent capture MECHANISM rather than an absent tag -- it cannot by itself falsify behavioural tagging as a target.

Behavioural tagging depends on the WEAK trace actually setting a tag; if the sub-threshold BC install sets no learnable trace at all (the install-did-not-take case), the arm is uninformative and must self-route substrate_not_ready_requeue rather than return a novelty-paired null.

entries.confidence_rationale: Supports the abstract dissociation MECH-476 asserts (acquisition, consolidation, and reconsolidation are separable stages with distinct substrate requirements) and independently corroborates the interference-resistance definition. But it simultaneously localises biological consolidation to SLEEP and shows reactivation returns a memory to a labile state -- both of which REE lacks. It is therefore the clearest single marker of the known AWAKE/ONLINE/UNDIFFERENTIATED-vs-sleep/replay divergence, which is why it is filed as mixed rather than supports.
failure_signatures: The consolidation that matters here is time-in-SLEEP, not merely elapsed clock time -- overnight sleep produced consolidation that equivalent waking time did not. REE's demonstrated protection pathways (distributional critic, KL anchor) are awake/online and have no sleep or replay analog, so a REE interval effect driven purely by offline STEPS is not the same object Walker measured, and a null REE interval effect does not falsify the biological process.

Waking reactivation turned a previously consolidated memory back into a labile, interference-susceptible state (reconsolidation). REE has no reactivation-gated labile window, so its retention dynamics may be strictly monotone where biology's are cyclic -- a structural mismatch the claim should not paper over.

entries.confidence_rationale: The ML instantiation that closes the loop from the biology to REE's actual substrate. EWC is a per-PARAMETER, Fisher-importance-weighted quadratic penalty toward a previous optimum -- a computationally realised, trace-selective analog of exactly the global KL anchor REE currently uses. It demonstrates, in neural networks, that selective (importance-weighted) protection retains prior competence markedly better than an undifferentiated constraint, and that the retention lever is the UPDATE CONSTRAINT, not continued demonstration -- both central to MECH-476. Confidence held at 0.72 by the supervised-sequential-task setting and EWC's own known limitations.
failure_signatures: EWC's importance weights are computed at task boundaries from the diagonal Fisher information; it presupposes identifiable tasks and a stationary previous optimum. REE's BC->RL erosion is a single continuing task with a shifting objective, so a naive port of EWC may have no well-defined 'previous task' to anchor per-parameter importance to -- the selectivity mechanism is not free to REE even though the concept transfers.

The diagonal-Fisher approximation ignores parameter interactions and is known to degrade over long task sequences; so even the ML trace-selective solution is imperfect, and adopting it in REE would trade a global-KL crudeness for a different, approximation-bound one rather than reproducing STC's synapse-exact selectivity.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct empirical instantiation of the exact A->B->A assay MECH-476's falsifier proposes, in humans, showing resistance-to-interference grows with BOTH elapsed interval (24 h vs 5 min) AND doubled initial training (dose). This validates the assay and the two levers the falsifier varies; it does not test REE's substrate, so mapping fidelity to REE is design-level not mechanism-level, and it carries a methodological warning (anterograde interference / washout) the REE experiment must honour.
failure_signatures: Without washout blocks removing anterograde interference, a counter-rotation interfered even at a 24 h interval -- i.e. apparent 'no consolidation' can be a retrieval-competition artefact rather than a true absence of a consolidation process. The REE A->B->A design must remove analogous anterograde effects (measure retained A cleanly) or a null result is uninterpretable.

Visuomotor rotation, unlike force-field or sequence learning, did NOT consolidate over time under the naive design -- consolidation is task/representation-specific, so a null in one REE competence-band does not generalise across substrates.

entries.confidence_rationale: The current authoritative review of synaptic tagging and capture, which grounds MECH-476's TRACE-SELECTIVITY content: consolidation in biology is synapse-specific -- a tag is set at particular synapses and captures plasticity-related products locally -- and tag-setting and PRP-synthesis are separable operations. This is exactly the property a single GLOBAL KL coefficient cannot express (which traces are protected). Supports the claim's distinctive assertion while defining the target REE lacks. Held to 0.64 because it is a conceptual review, not a direct test, and the mapping is to the GAP the claim names rather than to a REE result.
failure_signatures: Biological protection is synapse- and trace-SPECIFIC: the tag localises capture to the potentiated synapses, so unrelated memories are not indiscriminately shielded. REE's KL anchor is a global divergence penalty over the whole policy/value parameterisation and cannot select WHICH competence traces to protect -- so even a SUPPORTED interval/dose result would leave REE with a structurally cruder consolidation than the biology, and trace-selectivity remains an unbuilt target.

Tag-setting and plasticity-related-product synthesis are separable, and either can fail independently. A REE mechanism that conflates 'mark this trace' with 'supply the resource to stabilise it' (as a single global coefficient does) cannot reproduce the dissociations STC documents, so mapping any single REE lever onto 'consolidation' overstates the correspondence.

entries.confidence_rationale: Single-unit rat evidence that RPE-like teaching signals in posterior dorsomedial striatum (pDMS) are ACTION-SPECIFIC -- unlike midbrain dopamine RPEs, which are not. This localises the INFORMATIVE action-critic teaching signal that REE's actor-critic pathway would need, and shows it is a distinct, action-addressed channel whose absence would specifically impair action-value updating. Confidence 0.58: the population is small (10% of pDMS fast-firing neurons), the species is rodent, and the link to active competence LOSS is inferential -- the paper shows the signal's existence and specificity, not the consequence of removing it.
failure_signatures: The action-specific RPE population was only ~10% of pDMS fast-firing neurons (19/196) -- a thin substrate, so arguments that its uninformativeness dominates behaviour must be careful about how much of the action-value teaching signal it actually carries.

Midbrain dopamine RPEs are explicitly NOT action-specific; if REE's critic teaching signal is modelled on a global DA-like RPE rather than this pDMS action-addressed signal, the biological analog for an informative action-critic is mis-specified -- a design caveat, not support.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly demonstrates the claim's causal STRUCTURE in the same domain (deep actor-critic RL): critic function-approximation error propagates into the actor, producing a WORSE policy, and correcting the critic (twin clipped critics + delayed policy updates + target smoothing) reverses it, outperforming the prior state of the art in every environment tested. This is the computational analog of REE's V3-EXQ-788 result (a distributional critic RETAINS 1.839 competence where the scalar critic degrades) -- fix-the-critic-flips-the-sign. Confidence 0.66, not higher, because TD3's specific failure mode is OVERESTIMATION BIAS (a directional error), whereas MECH-475's is UNINFORMATIVENESS/FLATNESS (a variance error); the two are cousins, not identical.
failure_signatures: TD3's diagnosed pathology is critic OVERESTIMATION (biased-high value), not the FLAT/low-variance critic MECH-475 measured (std(V)/std(G)=0.041); an intervention that fixes overestimation need not fix uninformativeness, so the corrective mechanism does not transfer part-for-part -- only the structural claim 'bad critic actively degrades actor, fixing critic reverses it' transfers.

The reversal was shown on continuous-control gym benchmarks with dense reward; REE's regime is sparse-ish foraging with a critic that is flat on the policy's own state distribution, so the magnitude of achievable reversal is not licensed by this paper.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational single-unit primate result: >1/3 of striatal projection neurons were tuned to the value of ONE of the two actions during the pre-choice delay, with fewer tuned to relative value or to the choice itself. This is the direct evidence that ACTION-value (an actor-critic-style action-value signal) is explicitly represented in the striatum, which is what resolves the Rothenhoefer divergence: action-value learning survives a VS lesion because it lives in a different (dorsal/caudate-putamen) striatal population. Confidence 0.66 -- high locus-mapping fidelity for the 'REE's DV is action-like' question, moderated by the correlational (recording, not causal) design and the species/task gap.
failure_signatures: The signal is an ACTION-value code, not an advantage or a baseline per se -- so the paper establishes WHERE an informative action-critic lives but does not itself demonstrate that removing/flattening it produces active degradation; that causal step is imported from lesion (Rothenhoefer) and computational (Fujimoto, Tucker) entries.

Fewer neurons coded relative value or the choice; a substrate that represents absolute action-values without a strong relative/advantage code is consistent with REE's measured pathology (an advantage dominated by variance) but the paper does not measure variance of the value estimate.

entries.confidence_rationale: Decomposes the variance of the policy-gradient estimator and shows empirically that the STATE-DEPENDENT VALUE BASELINE is the load-bearing variance reducer -- fancier action-dependent baselines add ~nothing beyond it in standard benchmarks, and reported gains traced to implementation artifacts. This extends Sutton 2000 (already on file) from 'a baseline reduces variance' to 'the state-value baseline is WHERE the reduction comes from', which is the formal counterpart of MECH-475: if that state-value baseline is uninformative/flat, the variance it should have removed stays in the advantage. Confidence 0.6 -- the paper is ABOUT action-dependent baselines being a mirage, so it evidences the primacy of the state-value baseline indirectly rather than testing an uninformative baseline head-on.
failure_signatures: The paper's positive result is a NEGATIVE one about action-dependent baselines; it does not directly manipulate baseline INFORMATIVENESS and measure competence, so it grounds the variance mechanism theoretically rather than demonstrating the degradation empirically.

Its benchmarks are dense-reward continuous control where a well-fit state-value baseline is achievable; it says nothing about regimes (like REE's) where the critic is flat ON THE POLICY'S OWN STATE DISTRIBUTION, which is a harder failure than a merely imperfect fit.

entries.confidence_rationale: High source quality (primate excitotoxic lesion + RL/Bayesian modelling on an interleaved stimulus/action bandit) but the mapping cuts both ways. SUPPORTS the claim's degradation SIGNATURE -- VS-lesioned monkeys were more influenced by negative feedback and had LOWER choice consistency, an unbaselined/noisy-value signature, not a plateau. DIVERGES on LOCUS -- the deficit was specific to STIMULUS-value learning and left ACTION-value learning intact, so this paper alone does not license 'silence the critic -> action learning degrades'. Confidence held at 0.62 because the locus divergence is exactly what the next two entries (Samejima 2005, Stalnaker 2012) resolve, not what this paper settles.
failure_signatures: The VS deficit was specific to learning the value of STIMULI; discrimination between ACTIONS of different value remained intact -- so a ventral-striatal critic lesion is the WRONG biological analog for REE's action-selection foraging DV, and citing VS lesions as 'silent critic degrades action competence' would be a locus error.

VS-lesion monkeys defaulted to an action-based choice strategy under a stimulus-value deficit -- i.e. a compromised value channel produced a STRATEGY SHIFT, not uniform degradation, a confound REE's terminal-competence readouts would not distinguish from a floor.

This is the closest available engineering precedent for SD-082(i), and the match is close enough to be structural rather than analogical. The dueling architecture computes a per-action head output and then subtracts the mean of that head across the action set -- 'Q(s,a) = V(s) + (A(s,a) - (1/|A|) sum_{a'} A(s,a'))' -- for two stated reasons that map one-to-one onto SD-082's two problems. First, IDENTIFIABILITY: the naive sum is 'unidentifiable in the sense that given Q we cannot recover V and A uniquely', because a constant can be added to one stream and subtracted from the other with no change in output. That is precisely the SD-082 pathology in reverse -- a shared additive component across the candidate set that the output cannot distinguish from zero, so gradient never resolves it. Second, OPTIMISATION STABILITY: the mean form is preferred over the max form because 'the advantages only need to change as fast as the mean, instead of having to compensate any change to the optimal action's advantage'. So mean-subtraction across a candidate/action set is not a REE invention or a hack around SD-008; it is an established, empirically validated primitive whose adoption was justified by the same reasoning SD-082 gives. Confidence high on source quality (ICML 2016 Best Paper, large-scale empirical validation across the Atari suite, and the mean-aggregation choice is specifically credited in the paper's own ablation reasoning) and high on mapping fidelity for component (i). Held below 0.85 because the paper says nothing about component (ii) -- it has no bounded output and no saturation problem -- and because dueling's shared component is an unidentifiable degree of freedom in the OUTPUT parameterisation, whereas SD-082's is a dominant structure in the INPUT.
failure_signatures: The dueling mean-subtraction is applied to the head's OUTPUT (the advantage stream), whereas SD-082(i) applies it to the head's INPUT (the candidate world summaries, before rule_bias_head). These are not equivalent. Subtracting the input mean is a linear reparameterisation only for the linear part of the head; the SD-033a head is a nonlinear MLP, so centering the input changes which region of the nonlinearity each candidate lands in -- a change dueling's argument does not cover and cannot underwrite. If the head's first-layer nonlinearity is where the differentiation is actually being lost, input-centering may shift rather than solve the problem.

Dueling networks subtract the mean to fix an identifiability problem that exists REGARDLESS of the input geometry -- it is a property of the V + A parameterisation. SD-082's common mode is a contingent property of a specific broken encoder (SD-008). The dueling precedent therefore does NOT license SD-082 as a permanent architectural commitment; it licenses it as a read-out-stage mitigation. If SD-008 / SD-070 are ever repaired at the encoder, the dueling analogy gives no reason to keep the centering, and it should be re-ablated rather than inherited.

The paper's stability argument is about the relative rate at which advantages must change, in a value-based off-policy setting with a replay buffer and target network. SD-082's head trains under on-policy REINFORCE in a short P1 window (70 episodes was already shown insufficient at the clamp). Neither the stability claim nor the sample-efficiency gains transfer to that regime, so nothing here predicts that centering alone makes the head trainable in the budget available -- it predicts only that the shared-component degeneracy is removed.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the only source found that empirically compares the three bounding strategies SD-082 is choosing among, and it splits cleanly: it CONFIRMS SD-082's diagnosis and CONTRADICTS SD-082's chosen remedy. Confirms: their 'zeroing gradients' condition -- zero the gradient for any parameter already at its limit -- is functionally the clamp's flat region, and it failed, with 'Unstable learning ... in one of the two zeroing gradient agents' and the remaining stable agent showing 'clear results of not learning'. That is an independent replication of the V3-EXQ-822 null (70 episodes of REINFORCE moving nothing at the clamp), from a different algorithm, task and codebase. Contradicts: their 'squashing gradients' condition IS SD-082(ii) -- 'A squashing function such as the hyperbolic tangent (tanh) is used to bound the activation of each parameter' -- and it ALSO failed: 'parameters stayed within their bounds, but squashing functions quickly became saturated', and 'The resulting agents take the same discrete action with the same maximum/minimum parameters each timestep.' That end-state -- every output pinned at the same rail, no differentiation -- is the exact pathology SD-082 exists to remove, recurring under SD-082's own fix. Only their third option, inverting gradients (downscale approaching the bound, invert on exceeding it), worked. Confidence 0.74: high source quality and unusually high mapping fidelity for the specific mechanism, discounted because the pressure regime differs in a way that may be decisive (see caveat) and because n=2 agents per condition in a RoboCup domain is thin.
failure_signatures: PRIMARY RISK TO SD-082(ii). Tanh squashing was tried and failed by saturation: 'Given the observed proclivity of the critic's gradients to push parameters towards ever larger/small values, it is no surprise that squashing function quickly become saturated and never recover.' 'Never recover' is the operative phrase -- tanh's gradient is non-zero everywhere but decays exponentially, so sustained one-directional pressure produces a soft-saturated state that is practically as dead as a clamp and, unlike a clamp, gives no diagnostic signal that it has happened. SD-082's readout_init_scale (0.25) addresses only the INITIAL operating point; it does nothing to prevent drift into saturation over a training window. V3-EXQ-822a could therefore reproduce the 822 null with a non-zero-but-collapsing prop_delta and be misread as a partial success.

The acceptance criterion for V3-EXQ-822a (on_prop_delta_mean >= 0.001 with an ON>OFF contrast) is a WINDOW-MEAN and is blind to this failure mode. A run that starts in tanh's responsive band (as readout_init_scale intends) and saturates partway through P1 will have a healthy early prop_delta and a dead late one, and can clear 0.001 on the mean while ending in exactly the state SD-082 was built to prevent. Recommended instrumentation before or alongside 822a: log the per-tick saturation fraction (share of candidates with |bias_raw| > bias_scale) and the head grad-norm as TIME SERIES over P1, not just window means, and check the trend rather than the average.

Zeroing gradients also failed by OVERFLOW, not only by non-learning: 'parameters still overflow their bounds', hypothesised to arise from 'gradients applied to other parameters pi != p which inadvertently allow parameter p to overflow' (observed a dash power of 120 against a maximum of 100). This is a warning about coupled multi-output heads: bounding one output per-element does not keep the others in range when the head is shared. The SD-033a bias head emits a per-candidate vector from shared parameters, so per-candidate bounding does not guarantee per-candidate control of where each candidate sits relative to the bound.

Only inverting gradients succeeded in this comparison, and SD-082 did not consider it. If 822a shows saturation drift, the literature's actually-successful option is an untried DESIGN ALTERNATIVE for SD-082 (downscale the gradient as bias_raw approaches +/- bias_scale, invert if it exceeds), not a novel invention. Recording it here so that a 822a failure routes to a known alternative rather than to a fresh substrate-design cycle.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the strongest available biological grounding for SD-082's premise -- not for the fix, but for the structure the fix assumes. Kaufman et al. decompose M1/PMd population responses and find robust 'condition-invariant' components whose magnitude and time course are nearly identical regardless of which reach was made, and critically that the largest such component is much larger than any tuned component, i.e. it explains more of the structure in individual-neuron responses than the movement-identity signal does. That is a measured biological instance of exactly the geometry SD-008 describes in z_world and SD-082 must defeat at the read-out: a single large shared vector dominating the population, with the discriminative (condition-dependent) content relegated to a much smaller subspace. The paper further reports the condition-invariant components occupy dimensions ORTHOGONAL to the tuned components, which is the load-bearing detail for SD-082(i): if the common mode is orthogonal to the differentiated residual, subtracting it removes the dominant variance without destroying the discriminative signal -- the precondition for centering being a repair rather than a lossy projection. Confidence is high on source quality (Shenoy/Churchland population-geometry programme, dPCA-based decomposition, primate electrophysiology) and moderate on mapping: the paper is descriptive about a population geometry, not prescriptive about a read-out, and it never tests whether a downstream decoder saturates.
failure_signatures: The orthogonality result is a property of the M1/PMd population under a reaching task, established by dPCA on trial-averaged data. SD-082 assumes the SD-008 z_world common mode is likewise near-orthogonal to the differentiated candidate residual. That has NOT been measured in REE. If the common mode in z_world is instead partially aligned with the candidate-discriminative direction, mean-subtraction removes real signal along with the offset, and prop_delta could come up non-zero while carrying less rule information than the raw path -- a failure invisible to the V3-EXQ-822a acceptance criterion (on_prop_delta_mean >= 0.001), which tests only that propagation is non-vacuous, not that it is faithful.

The paper's condition-invariant signal is functional, not nuisance: its timing predicts most of the trial-by-trial reaction-time variance. So in the biology, the large shared component CARRIES INFORMATION (when to move) rather than being an artefact to discard. SD-082 subtracts the analogous component unconditionally. If any REE quantity of interest is encoded in the across-candidate mean summary -- an overall urgency, salience or commitment level -- centering at the read-out destroys it, and the loss would show up not in prop_delta but in some other downstream behaviour.

Kaufman et al. subtract nothing in a working control loop; the decomposition is an offline analysis of recorded data. The paper therefore provides no evidence that a nervous system implements common-mode subtraction as an online operation at a read-out stage, which is the specific mechanistic assertion SD-082 makes about lateral PFC.

entries.confidence_rationale: This entry supports SD-082's PRINCIPLE and undercuts its FORM. Support: Louie et al. show that neurons in monkey lateral intraparietal cortex do not encode the absolute value of an option but a relative value 'explicitly dependent on the values of the other available alternatives', including alternatives outside the response field, and that this context-dependence is 'precisely described by divisive normalization'. So the general architectural commitment SD-082 makes -- that a per-candidate quantity feeding choice should be computed relative to the rest of the candidate set rather than absolutely -- is how a real decision circuit works, not a convenience. This matters because SD-082's centering is otherwise open to the objection that it discards information the agent might need. Undercut: the measured cortical operation is DIVISIVE gain control (scale by a denominator summing the alternatives' values), not SUBTRACTIVE mean removal. These have different consequences under exactly the regime SD-082 operates in. Divisive normalization rescales a near-collinear set without changing its poor angular separation, whereas subtraction removes the shared offset and amplifies the residual -- so the paper's mechanism would NOT have repaired the V3-EXQ-822 structural zero, and the paper is therefore evidence for context-relative coding in general and against the claim that SD-082's specific arithmetic is the biologically attested one. Confidence 0.61: strong primate electrophysiology, but the form mismatch is central rather than peripheral to what SD-082 asserts, and the area is LIP rather than lateral PFC.
failure_signatures: FORM MISMATCH, and it is not cosmetic. Divisive normalization scales a set of values by a common denominator; subtractive centering removes a common addend. Under the SD-008 regime these come apart decisively: dividing a set of near-collinear vectors (min cosine 0.963) by a scalar leaves them just as collinear, so a divisive read-out would have reproduced the V3-EXQ-822 structural zero, while subtraction is what rescues it. SD-082 therefore cannot claim divisive normalization as its biological warrant. If SD-082's architecture doc or claims.yaml entry is ever read as 'normalization is canonical in cortex, therefore SD-082 is biologically grounded', that inference is invalid -- the canonical cortical operation is the one that would NOT have worked here.

Louie et al.'s normalization is over the values of concurrently available ALTERNATIVES and is reported in baseline firing rates as well as stimulus-driven activity, i.e. it is a persistent property of the circuit. SD-082's centering is gated on K >= 2 candidates and computed per tick with no memory. A single-candidate tick therefore receives no centering at all, so the read-out's input statistics change discontinuously with candidate-set size. Nothing in this paper (or in SD-082's validation plan) tests whether that discontinuity matters, and a mixed-K episode could show tick-to-tick bias instability that the window-mean prop_delta would average away.

OPEN DISAGREEMENT WITH A SIBLING ENTRY IN THIS SAME DIRECTORY, recorded rather than resolved. The earlier entry 2026-07-29_sd_082_divisive_normalization_canonical_carandini2012 (landed REE_assembly e41e28d6f3) reads normalization as supporting BOTH SD-082 components at once, on the ground that normalization 'discounts the pooled common drive AND bounds the response smoothly'. This entry argues the discounting half does not transfer, because divisive scaling of a near-collinear set does not improve its angular separation. Both are partly right and the reconciliation is a real refinement: divisive normalization DOES fix the SATURATION half (dividing by a denominator that pools the alternatives pulls an over-driven set back into dynamic range, which is exactly the clamp-rail problem) but does NOT improve the SIGNAL-TO-COMMON-MODE RATIO (for summaries x_i = c + delta_i with c >> delta, division returns (c + delta_i)/(sigma + Kc), preserving the small relative differences instead of exposing them). Subtraction addresses both halves; division addresses one. So SD-082(i)'s subtractive choice is better-motivated than the Carandini entry implies and better-motivated than pure form-mismatch would suggest -- but the biological attestation covers only the weaker operation. Governance should not treat either sibling entry as settling this; the discriminating measurement is REE-side (the angle between the common mode and the candidate-discriminative direction), not literature-side.

The paper's headline behavioural consequence of normalization is IRRATIONALITY -- context-dependent violations of rational choice, where the presence of a third option changes the preference between two others. If SD-082's centering imports the same context-dependence into the candidate bias, then the bias becomes a function of which other candidates happen to be in the set on that tick. That is arguably correct as biology and is a hazard for any REE claim that treats the bias as a stable per-candidate property. It should be checked before SD-082's centering is inherited by consumers beyond the SD-078 path.

entries.confidence_rationale: Included for the subject-level grounding SD-082's architecture doc explicitly rests on -- 'corticostriatal rule-to-action mapping: a selected rule/context representation must gate a motor bias for the selection to have behavioural consequence; selection without a trained read-out to action is inert.' Muhammad et al. recorded across four connected areas while monkeys applied abstract 'same'/'different' rules to a hold-or-release response, and found rule information and response information co-represented in lateral PFC, premotor cortex and dorsal striatum, with negligible rule coding in inferior temporal cortex. That is direct primate evidence that abstract rule signals reach the structures that select actions rather than remaining confined to a rule-representing area -- the premise that makes SD-082's read-out a necessary component rather than an optional one, and that makes V3-EXQ-822's structural zero a genuine architectural defect rather than an acceptable design. But the paper also complicates SD-082's assumed direction of flow, and that is why the direction is mixed rather than supports: rules and behavioural responses 'were reflected most strongly and, on average, tended to be earlier in the PMC followed by the PFC and then the STR'. Premotor cortex leading prefrontal cortex is the opposite of the serial PFC-computes-rule-then-biases-action architecture that SD-082's data flow diagram encodes. Confidence 0.58: solid primate electrophysiology at the level of area-wise information content, but it evidences the EXISTENCE and DISTRIBUTION of a rule-to-action pathway, not the FORM of any read-out, and it says nothing at all about common-mode geometry or output bounds -- the two things SD-082 actually changes.
failure_signatures: DIRECTIONALITY. Rule and response signals appeared earliest and most strongly in PREMOTOR cortex, then PFC, then striatum. SD-082's data-flow diagram is strictly serial and prefrontal-first: CandidateRuleField -> rule_state -> LateralPFCAnalog.compute_bias -> E3 per-candidate score_bias. If the biology is closer to concurrent or premotor-led rule/action coding, then SD-082 correctly identifies that a read-out must exist while getting its architectural placement wrong, and no amount of tuning at the LateralPFCAnalog read-out would reproduce the biological computation. This is not a defect that V3-EXQ-822a can detect -- 822a tests whether propagation is non-vacuous, which a wrongly-placed-but-functional read-out would pass.

The paper resolves rule and response coding at the level of area-wise information content and latency, with no measurement of the geometry of the population code and no test of how a downstream area reads it. It therefore cannot discriminate between ANY of the candidate read-out mechanisms SD-082 chose among -- raw versus centered input, hard clamp versus scaled tanh are all equally consistent with these data. Citing it as support for SD-082's mechanism (as opposed to SD-082's necessity) would be an overreach.

The task uses two abstract rules ('same'/'different') and a binary hold-or-release response, so the candidate set has cardinality two and there is no meaningful 'across-candidate mean' to speak of. SD-082's centering is gated on K >= 2 and its benefit is expected to grow with candidate-set size (V3-EXQ-822 had max_live 16 rules). This paradigm is at the extreme low end of that range and provides no evidence about the many-similar-alternatives regime that is precisely where the common-mode pathology bites.

Rule coding was negligible in inferior temporal cortex while perceptual identity information was strongest and earliest there -- a clean dissociation showing the rule pathway is selective, not a broadcast. If REE's rule_state is read by consumers that should NOT see it, this paper is a reason to check that selectivity; SD-082 adds a consumer without any stated gating on which downstream structures may read the rule signal.

This is the canonical human mechanistic precedent for MECH-204's general architecture -- REM sleep physiology, driven by suppression of an aminergic neuromodulator, recalibrating a next-day reactivity set-point -- and is the closest thing the biology-first triage in the autopsy asked for: a dedicated, well-cited, quantitative demonstration that a REM-specific (not just sleep-general) process resets a waking measure. Held at 0.6 rather than higher because the neuromodulator (noradrenergic/adrenergic, not serotonergic) and the target variable (amygdala reactivity to emotional stimuli, not a metacognitive confidence/precision estimate) both diverge from MECH-204's specific claim.
failure_signatures: The proposed mechanism is suppression of central ADRENERGIC (noradrenergic) neurotransmitters during REM, not serotonergic withdrawal -- MECH-204 states the zero-point is set by SEROTONERGIC withdrawal specifically (title: serotonergic_rem_gate_zero_point), so this paper supports the general REM-aminergic-withdrawal-as-recalibration architecture but not the specific neurotransmitter system MECH-204 names.

The recalibrated variable here is amygdala BOLD reactivity and subjective emotional intensity to previously-viewed images, not a metacognitive precision/confidence estimate -- the paper offers no evidence, one way or the other, about whether the same REM physiology recalibrates a confidence-in-self-accuracy variable rather than an affective-reactivity variable.

The design contrasts a night of sleep (with REM) against a day of equivalent wakefulness, not REM sleep against non-REM sleep directly -- so the causal attribution to REM specifically (rather than sleep in general) rests on secondary EEG correlations (high-frequency activity) within the sleep condition, a weaker design than a REM-deprivation manipulation would provide.

entries.confidence_rationale: Commissioned specifically to establish the expected MAGNITUDE of waking metacognitive drift (GOV-FANOUT-1 H3). This is the closest paradigm match in the literature to SD-076's actual construct -- confidence in one's OWN response accuracy, not a world-belief -- and the direct answer is a null: calibration, resolution, and over/underconfidence indices were all statistically unaffected across 3 days of sustained cognitive work and sleep deprivation. Held at 0.68 rather than lower because a well-instrumented null on the exact right construct is informative, not merely unhelpful; held below 0.8 because N=16 males in one lab, 1994, and no direct manipulation of REM sleep specifically (this is a deprivation, not a recalibration-mechanism, test).
failure_signatures: The correlation between confidence and performance (calibration), the ability to differentiate correct from incorrect judgments (resolution), and validity of subjective certainty were ALL unaffected by extensive sleep deprivation -- the paper's own conclusion is that people retain fairly reliable internal feedback about their own performance during sustained vigilant work, which is the opposite of SD-076's premise of an accumulating waking overconfidence drift.

If REE's asymmetric-EMA drift source is calibrated to reproduce a LARGE, easily-measurable calibration shift under extended wakefulness, it is calibrated against an effect this study could not detect at N=16 over 3 days -- the small, sub-threshold log-ratio swing observed in V3-EXQ-794a (~0.02 between LO and HI asymmetry) is, if anything, MORE consistent with this human calibration literature than a large threshold-clearing effect would have been.

entries.confidence_rationale: The only paper in this pull that documents a genuine overconfidence effect emerging under extended wakefulness, with a rough timescale anchor (self-rated impairment onset ~19h into continuous wakefulness, tracking a PVT-measured decrement equivalent to 0.05% BAC). Confidence held at only 0.55 because the effect is COMPARATIVE (self vs. a hypothetical other), not calibration-based (confidence vs. own accuracy) -- a materially different construct from SD-076's running self-accuracy estimate, and from the null findings in the two Baranski entries above.
failure_signatures: Participants consistently rated a hypothetical OTHER person's driving ability as worse than their own under the same conditions of extended wakefulness -- the overconfidence here is a self-other comparative bias, not a drift in the accuracy of self-assessment per se; self-ratings of one's OWN driving ability DID decline roughly in step with objective PVT performance, which is the opposite of what a pure calibration-drift account would predict.

The authors' own concluding concern is about the GAP between self-rating and other-rating, not a demonstrated failure of self-calibration -- so this paper should not be read as establishing that waking self-accuracy confidence becomes miscalibrated; it establishes something narrower and different, a social-comparison optimism bias that happens to co-occur with fatigue.

entries.confidence_rationale: Larger, better-powered replication of the same author's 1994 finding (also in this directory), across three tasks spanning different cognitive abilities. Same conclusion: traditional confidence-accuracy indices (calibration, resolution, over/underconfidence) remain stable across 28h of sleep deprivation. Held at 0.72, slightly above the 1994 entry, for the larger N, the broader task battery, and the higher-tier venue (APA journal) -- but capped short of 0.8 because it is still one research group's paradigm, not an independent replication.
failure_signatures: Across THREE different tasks (perceptual comparison, general knowledge, mental addition) spanning a range of cognitive demands and SD-susceptibility, over- and underconfidence indices and the accuracy of pre/post-task performance estimates all remained stable across 28 hours of sleep deprivation -- a within-study replication of the null found in the author's own 1994 study, now across a wider construct space.

The paper's own stated implication is that people can accurately assess their cognitive performance after one night without sleep, and that this self-assessment ability does not depend on subjective sleepiness ratings -- directly at odds with a picture in which waking confidence reliably and substantially inflates over a single wake episode.

entries.confidence_rationale: The single most load-bearing timescale finding in this pull: it directly dissociates acute total sleep deprivation (TSD, ~one wake episode) from chronic partial sleep restriction (SR, across multiple nights), and finds metacognitive error-awareness drift ONLY in the chronic condition. V3-EXQ-794a's design (30 training episodes, K=1 single-fire sleep) is structurally closer to the acute TSD arm than the chronic SR arm. Confidence held at 0.65: recent, well-designed (combined EEG + behavior, two separate cohorts), but error awareness on a per-trial task is a narrower construct than a continuously-updated precision estimate.
failure_signatures: Acute total sleep deprivation did NOT influence behavioral error awareness, ERN amplitude, or Pe amplitude -- the acute-deprivation regime structurally closest to V3-EXQ-794a's single-episode design showed NO measurable metacognitive drift on this task.

Chronic sleep RESTRICTION (repeated nights of partial sleep loss) DID reduce behavioral error awareness, increase detection latency, and reduce Pe amplitude -- so the drift SD-076 posits is empirically real, but appears to require accumulated exposure across multiple sleep-wake cycles, not a single wake episode, which bears directly on GOV-FANOUT-1's H2 (insufficient training exposure).

If REE's asymmetric-EMA is meant to model the ACUTE, within-episode regime, this paper predicts it should show little to no drift; if it is meant to model the CHRONIC, across-cycles regime, the driver's K=1 single-fire, 30-episode design may simply not accumulate enough exposure to express it -- directly informing whether the fanout's H2 (exposure) or H3 (wrong mechanism) is the better explanation for V3-EXQ-794a's small effect.
