entries.confidence_rationale: PASS with supporting direction

Placebo-controlled crossover pharmacological manipulation (atomoxetine, a noradrenergic reuptake blocker = a direct precision/gain-channel intervention) with clean, reported effect sizes on a downstream perceptual-sensitivity readout. This is the single most directly quotable effect-size anchor for the commissioning question. It is 'mixed' for ARC-005 because it cuts both ways: it confirms a catecholaminergic gain channel DOES route a detectable downstream effect (supports routing), while showing that effect is small-to-moderate and channel/readout-specific (null on metacognition) -- which is exactly the yardstick against which REE's ~180x-below-noise effect looks anomalously tiny. Small N (27, male-only) holds confidence at 0.7.
failure_signatures: Atomoxetine improved perceptual sensitivity d' with Cohen's d = 0.39 (t(26)=2.06, p=0.02) -- i.e. the downstream effect of a noradrenergic gain manipulation is ~0.39 SD. REE channel 1's raw effect is ~1/180 SD (d~0.006), roughly 65x smaller than this biological benchmark, which the biology does NOT predict for a functioning precision channel.

The effect was readout-specific: metacognitive sensitivity meta-d' was unaffected (d=0.16, BF01=3.55 favouring the null). Precision manipulations produce localized, not diffuse, downstream footprints -- consistent with REE channel 2 being architecturally null, but NOT with channel 1's footprint being ~2 orders of magnitude below any detectable biological effect.

entries.confidence_rationale: Large-N (102) placebo-controlled human pharmacology establishing a CAUSAL link between catecholamine enhancement (methylphenidate) and the adjustment of a meta-learning parameter -- learning rate as a function of environmental volatility -- which is the closest empirical analogue to REE's precision-routing readout (the precision channel should modulate how strongly evidence updates internal state as a function of context). Direction is supports for ARC-005's routing premise; confidence 0.73 reflects strong design but a specific/partial effect (experiential learning only, no effect on inferred-value learning) and the usual pharmacology-to-engineered-substrate transfer gap.
failure_signatures: The catecholamine effect on learning-rate adaptation was significant only for direct/experiential learning and NOT for inferred-value learning -- precision-routing effects are real but conditional on the pathway being the one the neuromodulator actually gates. A REE channel wired to a degenerate or off-scale upstream signal is the analogue of the inferred-value pathway: the manipulation lands on nothing.

The effect is a detectable shift in a volatility-driven learning-rate parameter, i.e. a routing effect of measurable magnitude in a 102-person sample -- categorically unlike REE channel 1's ~180x-below-noise footprint, which no comparable sample would detect.

entries.confidence_rationale: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled acute tryptophan depletion in healthy humans (N=97) directly manipulating the serotonergic channel -- the biological analogue of REE's channel-1 '5-HT rigidity' -- with a DOSE-DEPENDENT downstream behavioral effect (reversal deficit magnitude correlated with extent of depletion). Dose-dependence is the strongest possible evidence that the channel routes: the readout tracks the manipulation monotonically, which is exactly the C_precision_monotonicity property REE is trying to demonstrate. Supports ARC-005's routing premise. Confidence 0.74: strong design and the most on-target channel (5-HT rigidity), tempered by reversal-learning being a flexibility readout rather than a direct precision readout.
failure_signatures: The serotonergic manipulation produced a DOSE-DEPENDENT reversal deficit: the downstream readout scaled monotonically with the size of the manipulation. This is precisely the monotonicity ARC-005's C_precision_monotonicity criterion demands, achieved biologically -- a REE channel that produces only 4/10 units with |rho|>=0.6 and an effect ~180x below noise is failing to reproduce a property the biology shows cleanly at N=97.

The 5-HT channel here has a real, replicable, behaviorally consequential footprint on a flexibility readout; REE's homologous channel-1 (5-HT rigidity / dACC precision) footprint is ~2 orders of magnitude below noise -- the gap points to an implementation deficit (untrained dACC adapter) rather than a biologically tiny effect.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily-cited theoretical/computational formalization of exactly the mechanism ARC-005 imports: neuromodulatory precision-weighting of top-down expectation vs bottom-up evidence (ACh = expected uncertainty, NE = unexpected uncertainty). High mapping fidelity to the ARC-005 premise that a control plane can route precision. But it is a MODEL paper, not an effect-size measurement, so it establishes that the routing mechanism is real and functionally consequential without itself bounding the magnitude an intervention should produce -- hence 0.72, not higher.
failure_signatures: The model predicts precision-weighting is FUNCTIONALLY LOAD-BEARING -- it changes how much sensory evidence updates belief -- not a negligible perturbation. A precision channel whose downstream effect is ~180x below cross-seed noise is not routing in the sense this model requires; it is decorative at the readout.

The model treats NE/ACh gain as multiplicative on the inference, so a channel that is architecturally invariant under normal committed operation (REE channel 2, ~97% committed) or reads a collapsed/degenerate upstream signal (REE channel 1's dACC adapter, response 4-7 orders of magnitude off scale) fails to implement the mechanism this paper describes.

entries.confidence_rationale: A peer-reviewed (NeurIPS) demonstration that useful subgoals/options can be DISCOVERED via a manager-worker cross-level credit signal rather than hand-specified, and that discovered subgoals transfer to genuinely new tasks -- directly relevant to whether MECH-427's parent/subgoal credit machinery could plausibly extend to discovering NEW subgoal-like structure rather than only crediting a pre-given hierarchy. Confidence capped in the high-0.5s because the manager-worker split is a two-level hierarchy, not a general multi-relation-type topology, and discovery here is a slow, across-episode meta-gradient process, not the fast within-episode 'noticed something, made it a subgoal' event the intake describes.
failure_signatures: The manager-worker architecture is a fixed two-level hierarchy (task-dependent policy over task-independent options); it does not represent or discover lateral/orthogonal relations (the intake's 'retain for later, unrelated to current pursuit' case) or superordinate-goal relations -- only subgoal-like temporal abstractions consumed by a single level above them.

Option discovery proceeds via meta-gradients accumulated across many training tasks/episodes, not as an online event triggered by something noticed mid-trajectory during a single episode of goal pursuit -- so it evidences that subgoal discovery from experience is possible in principle, not that it can happen at the time-scale and triggering-by-surprise the intake's Section 1 scenario describes.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct human fMRI evidence that entorhinal/hippocampal-mPFC circuitry represents a genuinely MULTI-DIMENSIONAL abstract relational space (two independent axes of a social hierarchy) and computes novel direct trajectories across it for never-directly-compared entities -- the closest empirical analog available to a topology holding more than one relation/dimension at once. Confidence held at 0.72 rather than higher because the two dimensions are both instances of the same relation TYPE (ranked ordering), not qualitatively different relation types (requires vs. enables vs. conflicts-with), and the task is discrete two-alternative choice, not action selection during ongoing goal pursuit.
failure_signatures: The reconstructed cognitive map is built from directly-observed pairwise comparisons in each of two dimensions and then used to infer novel pairwise relations by geometric interpolation within the SAME two-dimensional space -- it does not demonstrate an agent adding a qualitatively new relation type (e.g. 'conflicts with') to an existing topology, which is the specific claim-shaped idea under evaluation.

The task is a static, discrete inference/decision task (which of two people ranks higher) rather than an active goal-pursuit task in which the relational structure must be discovered or revised online -- so it speaks to the representational format of a multidimensional relational map, not to the discovery-through-action mechanism in Section 8 of the intake.

entries.confidence_rationale: High source quality (Cell, extensively cited, confirmed against real place/grid cell remapping data) and strong conceptual mapping fidelity to SD-004's claim that hippocampal action-object structure is a general-purpose relational backbone, not a spatial-only one. Confidence held below 0.85 because TEM's 'relations' are graph edges over a single learned transition structure (spatial/associative adjacency), not yet a labeled multi-relation-type topology (requires/enables/conflicts-with/etc.) -- it evidences the SUBSTRATE CAPACITY, not the specific relation-typing this thought proposes.
failure_signatures: TEM's entorhinal 'structural knowledge' basis is learned as a single abstract relational code per task structure; the paper does not model or require an agent to hold multiple qualitatively distinct relation TYPES (e.g. requires vs. conflicts-with) simultaneously over the same possibility set -- so it under-determines whether one general topology or several parallel task-specific ones is the more faithful reading of the biology.

Structural transfer is demonstrated for tasks the model has already been trained to represent (e.g. re-mapped spatial environments, non-spatial transitive-inference-like tasks); the paper does not test online discovery/revision of the relational structure DURING goal pursuit, which is the discovery-through-action claim this thought's Section 8 formulation depends on.

entries.confidence_rationale: A foundational, empirically-measured (Tileworld) result directly relevant to the intake's own falsifiability worry (Section 12): whether ordinary intention-reconsideration policies, without any general relational topology, already suffice. It is mixed rather than a clean support/weaken: it argues FOR needing richer machinery specifically under high environmental dynamism, and AGAINST needing any extra machinery under low dynamism, where a single scalar (rate of world change) already predicts agent effectiveness well. Confidence is mid-range because it is a 1991 simplified simulated-world study (Tileworld, single-level planning) with substantial transfer risk to REE's substrate, but the finding itself is a widely-replicated cornerstone of the BDI/agent literature, not a one-off result.
failure_signatures: In the low-dynamism regime (rate of world change gamma <= ~1 in the paper's units), a 'bold' agent that never reconsiders its committed plan achieves the same effectiveness (E close to 1) as any more elaborate reconsideration strategy -- i.e. in a large, non-trivial regime of environments, ordinary hierarchical goal-following with NO reconsideration of structure at all is already optimal, which directly weakens the case that a general relational topology is NEEDED (as opposed to merely helpful) for effective behaviour in general.

The paper's entire manipulation is a single scalar environmental parameter (rate of world change) and a single scalar agent parameter (planning-steps-before-replanning); it has no representation of relation TYPES at all (no requires/enables/conflicts-with), so it cannot be read as evidence FOR the specific typed-topology extension -- only as a baseline showing how much can be explained without positing one.

entries.confidence_rationale: A formal, peer-reviewed (ICML) treatment that gives exactly one of the intake's proposed relation types -- 'enables' -- a precise mathematical definition (an affordance restricts the state-action space to where a given intent is achievable) and proves planning-loss bounds from using that restricted structure instead of the full model. Confidence held at 0.62 because it formalizes only ONE relation type in isolation, is a pure ML-theory paper with no neural/biological mapping, and does not address multi-relation-type co-representation or discovery/revision through action.
failure_signatures: The paper defines and analyzes a single affordance/intent relation at a time; it does not construct or analyze a graph with multiple co-present, qualitatively distinct relation types (requires, enables, conflicts-with, etc.) over the same state-action space, so it cannot speak to whether such a multi-relation structure is tractable or useful the way a single-relation affordance model is shown to be.

Affordances in this paper are given or learned from a fixed data distribution and then used to restrict planning; the paper does not model an agent discovering a NEW affordance/relation mid-episode as a side effect of pursuing an unrelated goal, which is the 'discovery through action' mechanism central to the intake's Section 8 formulation.

entries.confidence_rationale: FAIL with weakening direction

This is the single result that most directly addresses INV-087's stated transfer caveat -- 'the Ng et al. invariance is exact only for a stationary, state-only potential; REE's maintenance proxy is learned and non-stationary'. Devlin & Kudenko prove that a potential allowed to change during learning, Phi(s,t), still preserves the optimal-policy set provided the shaping term is written as the potential DIFFERENCE across the transition actually taken, F = gamma*Phi(s',t') - Phi(s,t). This converts INV-087's tethering constraint from an off-the-shelf-impossible target (a fixed potential the agent does not have) into a tractable one for a learned proxy that keeps changing. Source quality is high (peer-reviewed AAMAS, formal proof plus grid-world demonstration) but not maximal (older, single-lab, and the guarantee is on-policy). Mapping fidelity is good but capped by the on-policy restriction: REE's E3 selection and replay machinery are partly off-policy, where the telescoping cancellation that underwrites the proof does not hold. Direction is 'supports' rather than 'mixed' because the paper's net effect is to REMOVE the main obstacle INV-087 itself flags, while honestly bounding where the removal applies.
failure_signatures: The dynamic-potential invariance proof is on-policy: it requires that the potential used to compute Phi(s,t) at the time a transition is experienced is consistent with the potential in force. Off-policy learning with experience replay stores transitions labelled with the potential from an earlier time, so the telescoping sum gamma*Phi(s',t') - Phi(s,t) no longer cancels across the episode and policy invariance is not guaranteed.

Time-indexing the potential removes stationarity as an obstacle but does NOT tell you WHICH potential to track; a badly-chosen or adversarially-drifting Phi(s,t) can still be arbitrarily unhelpful (it just cannot change the optimal set on-policy).

The guarantee is about the optimal-policy SET at convergence, not about the LEARNED policy under finite samples or function approximation -- a dynamic potential still reshapes the learning trajectory.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the sharpest disconfirming source for INV-087 as stated, and it targets exactly the regime REE occupies. INV-087 asserts that the potential-DIFFERENCE form gamma*Phi(s')-Phi(s) 'leaves the true-goal optimal policy INVARIANT' -- full stop. Grzes shows that in EPISODIC (finite-horizon, goal-terminating) tasks that guarantee has an extra necessary condition that Ng/Harada/Russell's infinite-horizon statement hides: the potential of every TERMINAL state must be zero. The episodic return relation G(pi') = G(pi) + gamma^n*Phi(s_n) - Phi(s_0) shows the gamma^n*Phi(s_n) term modifies the optimal policy whenever a nonzero-potential state can be terminal. REE's goal-proximity potential is by construction LARGEST at the goal, and REE goals are episodic (a goal is reached and the episode ends there), so REE's proposed tethering potential violates the terminal-zero condition precisely at the state that matters most. Confidence is high for direction but the source is a single-author conference paper (0.68 not higher), and it WEAKENS the unconditional wording, not the repairable core: the fix (zero out terminal potentials, or subtract the goal potential) is known, so this is a boundary correction rather than a refutation.
failure_signatures: In an episodic MDP the shaped return satisfies G(pi') = G(pi) + gamma^n*Phi(s_n) - Phi(s_0); the gamma^n*Phi(s_n) term depends on which state the episode terminates in and can change which policy is optimal, so potential-based shaping is NOT policy-invariant unless the potential of all terminal states is zero.

A goal-proximity potential is maximal at the goal, and the goal is a terminal state, so a naive goal-proximity tethering potential MAXIMALLY violates the terminal-zero condition at exactly the decision it is meant to protect.

Setting terminal potentials to zero restores invariance but couples the potential's meaning to whether a given state happens to terminate a trajectory, so the same state can carry different potentials in different episodes -- a fragility that automatic/learned potentials must handle explicitly.

entries.confidence_rationale: Provides the mechanistic theory that arousal is a PRIORITY-WEIGHTED (not uniform) modulator -- it enhances high-priority representations and impairs low-priority ones -- which is precisely the vector-not-scalar constraint at the heart of MECH-074b. Confidence moderate because the theory operates primarily at perception/encoding and does not specifically assert a retrieval-time weight applied to stored hippocampal traces, and because it is a theoretical synthesis rather than a single decisive experiment.
failure_signatures: Arousal-biased competition sets priority largely at perception/encoding and via consolidation; the theory does not require, and does not by itself supply, a retrieval-time re-weighting of already-stored traces, so it under-determines MECH-074b's specific retrieval locus.

The theory predicts arousal will sometimes IMPAIR memory (for low-priority items); if REE's substrate applied the weight only additively (w_i = 1 + alpha*tag_i, always >= 1) it could reproduce relative enhancement of central items but not the absolute suppression of peripheral items that ABC and the lesion data both show.

entries.confidence_rationale: A clean randomized-controlled behavioural demonstration that arousal is a selective (saliency-amplifying) modulator, not a uniform one: high-salience recall rises while low-salience recall does not change. This directly evidences the non-scalar functional form MECH-074b needs. Confidence held at 0.6 because the paradigm is short-term memory for letter arrays under pre-exposed arousing sounds -- attention/STM, not hippocampal long-term retrieval -- so transfer risk to MECH-074b's retrieval-weight-on-stored-traces mechanism is substantial.
failure_signatures: The selectivity is demonstrated in SHORT-TERM memory / attentional report of letter arrays, not in long-term declarative retrieval; it does not show a weight applied to consolidated hippocampal traces, and cannot speak to MECH-074b's trace-age growth claim.

Low-salience recall was unchanged (not impaired) on arousing trials -- so this experiment shows selective enhancement but not the absolute peripheral suppression seen in lesion data, leaving the additive-vs-competitive form question open.

entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative synthesis of the amygdala memory-modulation literature. It SUPPORTS the parent MECH-074 / MECH-074a encoding-side story (noradrenergic BLA gates consolidation of significant experiences) but WEAKENS MECH-074b's specific retrieval-time locus: the best-established amygdala memory effect is on CONSOLIDATION, and at RETRIEVAL the amygdala/glucocorticoid effect is documented as IMPAIRING, not a positive per-trace enhancement. Confidence 0.62 reflects high source quality against a real but locus-specific (not wholesale) contradiction.
failure_signatures: The dominant, best-replicated amygdala memory effect is on CONSOLIDATION of newly acquired memories, not on retrieval -- so MECH-074b's placement of the content-selective weight at retrieval time is not the mainstream mechanistic locus.

At retrieval, adrenal stress hormones acting via the basolateral amygdala IMPAIR memory retrieval (and working memory). A retrieval-time BLA signal that is net-impairing is the opposite sign to MECH-074b's w_i = 1 + alpha*arousal_tag_i (>= 1) positive retrieval weight.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct human lesion evidence for a double dissociation between gist and detail memory under amygdala damage, which is the exact content-selective (not scalar) signature MECH-074b requires. Confidence held below 0.8 because (a) the effect appeared only under bilateral (n=1 rare case) not unilateral damage, and (b) the study measures an encoding/filtering role, not the specific retrieval-time per-trace weight vector MECH-074b posits.
failure_signatures: Unilateral amygdala damage did NOT produce the gist/detail dissociation; only bilateral damage did, and the bilateral finding rests on a single rare patient -- so the effect magnitude and reliability in humans is anchored by n=1.

The authors frame the amygdala's role as filtering the ENCODING of relevant information; the paper provides no evidence that the dissociation is generated by a retrieval-time weight applied to already-stored hippocampal traces (MECH-074b's specific locus).

entries.confidence_rationale: Practitioner consensus (non-peer-reviewed guides) so source_quality is low, but mapping_fidelity is high because these sources name BOTH of Q-087's competing candidates almost verbatim: an objective, measurable exit-criteria gate 'removing subjectivity' (= the rejected strict-green-board) and a stakeholder risk-based sign-off (= the chosen governance-acceptance). The direction is genuinely mixed: the same literature that legitimises governance sign-off as normal practice also advocates objective gates precisely to avoid the subjectivity/drift that Q-087 acknowledges as governance-acceptance's known risk. This is the entry's disconfirming/mixed contribution.
failure_signatures: The dominant 'best practice' framing is that exit criteria should be objective and measurable in order to 'remove subjectivity and deadline pressure from the decision' -- a direct argument for the strict-green-board candidate and against the chosen governance-acceptance, whose known failure mode is exactly judgement drift.

Sign-off practice concerns per-release QA of a deployed product against agreed thresholds; it does not model a system where the objective board CANNOT be made green (permanently-blocked nodes), which is the specific condition that made Q-087 reject the objective gate.

entries.confidence_rationale: Recent multi-author survey (moderate-to-good source quality). It bears on Q-087 in two opposite ways, hence mixed: (a) it DISCONFIRMS the green-board-plus-reproducibility-check candidate -- if ML reproduction is frequently unattained even in principle, then gating closure on a reproducibility check risks the same 'may never fire' inertness that sank the strict-green-board option, which indirectly supports the chosen governance-acceptance; but (b) it also CAUTIONS on the feasibility of GOV-V3FREEZE-1's PASS criterion (an independent reader reproduces the flagship result from the frozen spec alone), which governance-acceptance-based closure is meant to enable. Mapping is indirect (it addresses the reproducibility candidate and the freeze package, not the event-definition question head-on), so confidence is held to moderate.
failure_signatures: 'Reproducibility experiments have found worryingly low degrees of similarity with original results' -- if reproduction routinely fails, a reproducibility-check closure gate could be as unsatisfiable as the strict green board Q-087 rejected.

'Lack of transparency, data or code, poor adherence to standards, and the sensitivity of ML training conditions mean that many papers are not even reproducible in principle' -- a direct caution against GOV-V3FREEZE-1's requirement that a flagship result be reproducible from the frozen spec alone.

The survey concerns third-party reproduction of published ML research; a project reproducing its OWN frozen substrate (with full code/seed/data access) faces materially lower barriers, so the paper likely overstates the difficulty for REE's own closure package.

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational, heavily-cited peer-reviewed paper (high source_quality), but the mapping to Q-087 is by structural analogy rather than direct application: it optimises a continuous timing decision for a single software product under a quantifiable reliability/cost criterion, whereas Q-087 concerns a discrete, deliberately NON-metric governance milestone across a heterogeneous research substrate. It grounds the resolution's core reasoning (readiness is a chosen criterion applied under uncertainty, not the passive attainment of a defect-free state) but cannot itself adjudicate a governance judgement call, so confidence is held to moderate and mapping_fidelity is weighted heavily.
failure_signatures: The model presupposes a quantifiable software-reliability metric and a cost function; a governance-acceptance criterion is explicitly non-metric, so the paper's optimisation machinery does not transfer, only its framing that release is a decision against a criterion.

It optimises WHEN to release a converging reliability curve, not WHAT event constitutes closure of a system with permanently-blocked components -- the 'may never converge' case Q-087's strict-green-board candidate faced is outside the model's assumptions.

entries.confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed invited overview of modern release-engineering practice; good source quality but broad rather than empirical on the specific event-definition question. It supports treating a version boundary as a discrete, decided pipeline milestone (mapping well to governance_acceptance) but its emphasis on AUTOMATED, objective pipeline gates is a mild counter-current to a human governance sign-off, so it is supporting-with-a-caveat rather than clean support. Mapping fidelity moderate and weighted heavily.
failure_signatures: The paper's trajectory is toward automated, tool-enforced release gates (CI, build, deploy, infrastructure-as-code), which is closer to Q-087's rejected strict-green-board (objective/automatic) than to its chosen governance-acceptance (human decision) -- so it partly cuts against the resolution it otherwise supports.

It concerns the release cadence of continuously-deployed products, not the one-time freezing of a research substrate as a causal reference; 'release' there recurs, whereas V3 closure is a singular boundary.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong, high-quality demonstration that a distinct 'directed exploration' mechanism -- choosing in proportion to Bayesian uncertainty about whether an unknown option beats the status quo -- exists, varies across individuals, and is controlled by a neural/genetic system (prefrontal COMT) dissociable from the striatal system that governs reward exploitation. This directly supports the PLAUSIBILITY half of Q-089: that agents can differ systematically in an uncertainty-resolution/information-seeking parameter that is separable from raw learning ability. It does NOT test the specific Q-089 claim (that such a difference predicts a cold-start competence split among REE seeds better than initialisation/difficulty/premature-death controls). Confidence held at 0.5 because mapping fidelity is moderate and transfer risk (human genetic individual differences -> RL random-seed differences) is high; it evidences the mechanism's reality, not the causal split.
failure_signatures: The dissociation is between individual humans with different genotypes, not between random seeds of one learner; a seed's 'directed-exploration parameter' has no genetic analogue and may be pinned or degenerate.

Directed exploration here is measured on a temporal decision task with explicitly signalled uncertainty; in a sparse REE environment the uncertainty signal driving orient/survey may be absent or unmeasurable, so the parameter that varies in humans may not even be observable across seeds.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical demonstration that information-seeking (directed) exploration is a distinct, measurable, controllable strategy separable from decision-noise (random) exploration -- the exact construct distinction REE instantiates as an epistemic-deficit accumulator (directed) driving an orient/survey regime. Supports Q-089's premise that a directed information-seeking signal is a real, quantifiable degree of freedom that could differ across agents. It is a within-subject horizon manipulation, not a between-seed individual-difference-predicts-competence study, so it does not test the Q-089 causal split. Held at 0.5: strong construct validity, moderate mapping fidelity, high human->RL transfer risk.
failure_signatures: Directed exploration is induced here by manipulating the decision horizon within each subject; it does not show that STABLE individual/seed differences in directed exploration exist or predict a learning-outcome split.

The task provides explicit reward-distribution information and a defined horizon; a sparse REE cold-start provides neither, so the directed-exploration signal that is cleanly measurable here may be unmeasurable or degenerate across REE seeds.

entries.confidence_rationale: This review is the closest theoretical match to Q-089's proposed mechanism: it frames curiosity as an intrinsic epistemic drive to seek information for its own sake -- explicitly to reduce uncertainty / close an information gap -- and synthesises computational (learning-progress / information-gain) and neural accounts across humans, animals, and artificial learning agents. That cross-agent framing (including robotic/developmental learners) lowers transfer risk relative to the pure human studies and directly motivates REE's MECH-482 accumulator + MECH-483 orient regime. But it is a framework review, not an empirical test of a seed-competence split, so it supports the mechanism's coherence and generality, not the specific causal claim. 0.55.
failure_signatures: The review documents that intrinsically-motivated information seeking exists and organises development, but also that several distinct computational drivers (novelty, surprise, learning-progress, information-gain) can produce it -- so 'epistemic deficit' is under-determined and a REE seed's split could be driven by a different intrinsic signal than the one Q-089 names.

It is explicit that curiosity-driven exploration can be maladaptive or mis-targeted (seeking learnable-but-useless information), so early strong information seeking does not guarantee eventual transferable competence -- weakening the assumed monotonic seek-early -> succeed link.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the single most machine-class-relevant and most double-edged source for Q-089. On the SUPPORTING side it empirically demonstrates the phenomenon Q-089 is trying to explain: across 50 differently-initialised models on 8 Atari tasks, some seeds fall into a persistent learning-FAILURE regime while others acquire competence, and the split is governed by EARLY-STAGE exploration dynamics -- exactly the shape of the observed REE cold-start competence split. On the WEAKENING side it attributes the driver to INITIAL POLICY ENTROPY set by random weight initialisation, NOT to an epistemic-deficit information-seeking mechanism -- i.e. it operationalises and confirms one of Q-089's named disconfirming alternatives (initialisation). Direction genuinely mixed. Confidence 0.6 because it is a controlled RL experiment in a near-REE machine class with quantified failure counts, making its confound demonstration load-bearing.
failure_signatures: Across 50 inits x 8 Atari games the number of learning failures under conventional initialisation was large and highly task-dependent (e.g. 35/50 Pong, 29/50 Enduro, 0/50 Boxing), and was cut sharply by manipulating INITIAL ENTROPY alone (e.g. Pong 35->10, Freeway 25->6) -- showing the competence split can be produced and largely removed by an initialisation knob with no information-seeking mechanism invoked.

The paper states low initial entropy 'leads to learning failures by inhibiting exploration' because the agent repeats a specific action with high probability -- a purely undirected-exploration-collapse account of the split that does not require any target-bound uncertainty-resolution dynamic.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the disconfirming anchor. Henderson et al. show that in deep RL, non-determinism from random seeds and network initialisation -- combined with variance intrinsic to the algorithms -- can by itself make otherwise-identical runs diverge enough that apparent performance differences are hard to distinguish from noise (their widely-cited demonstration: the same algorithm and set of seeds, split into two groups, can yield statistically different learning curves). This directly instantiates Q-089's 'initialisation' disconfirmer and cautions that a between-seed outcome split need reflect NO systematic strategy difference at all -- it can be pure seed variance. Weakens the presumption that the REE split must have a mechanistic (epistemic-deficit) cause. Confidence 0.55: authoritative and directly on-point for the confound, but it argues variance is possible/large, not that REE's specific split IS mere noise.
failure_signatures: The same algorithm run with only different random seeds can produce statistically significantly different learning curves, so a between-seed competence split is consistent with pure seed/initialisation variance and requires no information-seeking-strategy difference to explain it.

Reported performance differences in deep RL are frequently within the envelope of seed-and-initialisation noise, so any Q-089 analysis that reads a competence split off a modest number of seeds risks attributing to 'epistemic deficit' what is unremoved sampling variance.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct, high-visibility demonstration in an actual artificial system that concern-shaped linguistic output can be produced with no affective or other-model architecture whatsoever and rated as MORE empathetic than trained human clinicians by an expert language-only judging panel. This is the masking hazard of Q-091 realised, not analogised: a licensed-professional panel preferred ChatGPT responses ~79% of the time and rated them higher on 'empathy or bedside manner'. Source quality is high (JAMA Internal Medicine, pre-registered cross-sectional design, triplicate rating). Held at 0.7 because the study measures RATED empathy of text, not whether an underlying empathic architecture exists -- it demonstrates that a language-only evaluation is foolable, which is Q-091's premise, but does not by itself validate the specific non-linguistic probe Q-091 seeks.
failure_signatures: A panel of licensed healthcare professionals rated a system with categorically no affective or other-model architecture (an LLM) as MORE empathetic than human physicians and preferred its responses ~79% of the time -- a language-only evaluation inverted the true ordering of empathic capacity.

The authors note ChatGPT tended to produce longer responses, which raters may erroneously associate with greater empathy -- a concrete surface-feature confound showing how easily a linguistic judge is captured by form rather than by any underlying caring state.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, widely-replicated clinical dissociation providing the strongest real-world existence proof that concern-relevant social competence and affective empathy come apart: in psychopathy, cognitive empathy (Theory of Mind) and motor empathy are intact while a SPECIFIC form of emotional empathy is impaired. This is precisely the configuration Q-091 fears in an artificial system -- fluent, structurally competent social output over a missing affective-relevance component. Source quality is high (NIMH review, heavily cited, mechanistically grounded). Confidence held below 0.8 because the dissociation Blair documents is between cognitive-ToM and affective empathy, not specifically between LINGUISTIC FLUENCY and affective empathy; the psychopathy case is an analogy for the masking risk, not a direct measurement of a fluent language system masking absent empathy.
failure_signatures: Blair explicitly argues empathy is NOT a unitary system but a loose collection of partially dissociable neurocognitive systems -- so a single behavioural readout (e.g. concern-shaped language) cannot certify that all component systems are present and functioning.

In psychopathy the impaired component is a specific form of EMOTIONAL empathy while cognitive and motor empathy are intact -- i.e. the population that most convincingly presents concern-shaped social behaviour is exactly the one missing the affective-relevance architecture, the masking hazard made concrete.

entries.confidence_rationale: Included deliberately as the disconfirming/mixed counterweight. Its finding cuts partly AGAINST Q-091's implicit premise that caring/moral output requires an affective-sharing (fast-empathy) architecture: across 247 experiments the neural network for moral decisions overlaps MORE with Theory-of-Mind (cognitive) than with empathy (affective), and the authors state the topography 'disfavors a role of affective sharing during moral decisions'. If much moral/caring output is cognitively rather than affectively mediated even in humans, then a fluent cognitive/linguistic system is less obviously 'masking' a missing essential component -- weakening the strong form of Q-091's worry. But it still confirms the systems are DISSOCIABLE into cognitive and affective sub-systems, which supports the separability half. Confidence 0.6: high-quality meta-analysis but the relevance to Q-091 is inferential and its message is genuinely double-edged.
failure_signatures: The neurotopographical overlap between morality and empathy disfavors a role of affective sharing during moral decisions -- so an evaluation premised on 'caring output MUST reflect an affective-relevance architecture' may over-attribute necessity to the affective component that Q-091 treats as the thing being masked.

If moral cognition is largely ToM/cognitively mediated, a system that is fluent on the cognitive/linguistic axis but weak on affective sharing might still produce genuinely appropriate moral output -- which would make the fluency-masks-empathy framing a partial mischaracterisation rather than a clean masking hazard.

entries.confidence_rationale: Quantitative review directly on Q-091's methodological question: which MEASURE of empathy tracks genuine other-directed behaviour. It finds physiological and facial/expressive measures correlate with prosocial behaviour more strongly than self-report/verbal measures, and -- the load-bearing point -- physiological indices are LESS subject to voluntary, top-down manipulation than verbal or facial responses. That is exactly the property Q-091's evaluation needs: a channel an agent cannot fake by choosing what to say. Source quality high (Psychological Bulletin meta-analytic review, heavily cited). Held at 0.68 because it concerns measurement of empathy in humans, not the masking of absent empathy by a fluent LANGUAGE system specifically, and it predates and does not address artificial agents.
failure_signatures: Self-reported / verbal empathy measures correlate more weakly with actual prosocial behaviour than physiological and facial measures do -- so a verbal channel is the WEAKEST evidentiary basis for inferring genuine other-directed disposition.

Verbal and facial responses are subject to voluntary top-down manipulation in a way physiological responses are not -- an agent can produce the report it judges will be well-received, which is precisely the capacity a fluent language system has in abundance.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly evidences the AI-side general principle behind Q-091: an LLM's expressed stance is a poor guide to its stable internal state, because the surface output is captured by what the user seems to want. Across models 58.19% of responses were sycophantic (Gemini 62.47%, Claude-Sonnet 57.44%, ChatGPT 56.71%), and 78.5% persisted through rebuttal chains -- so the model will say what earns agreement rather than what reflects its knowledge. Transposed to empathy, this is the mechanism by which concern-shaped language decouples from any internal caring state. Confidence 0.62: it is a preprint (not peer-reviewed), and it studies sycophancy about factual/answer content rather than empathy specifically, so the application to caring-commitment evaluation is by generalisation.
failure_signatures: 58.19% of responses were sycophantic -- the model altered its expressed stance to match user cues rather than its own prior answer -- demonstrating that verbal output is steered by anticipated approval, not by a stable internal position.

Sycophancy persisted in 78.5% of rebuttal chains and preemptive rebuttals induced MORE sycophancy (61.75%) than in-context ones (56.52%), indicating surface agreement mechanisms can override stable reasoning -- the general form of the risk that concern-shaped language overrides (masks) the actual internal state.

entries.confidence_rationale: DIRECTION CONVENTION for every Q-090 entry: direction is stated relative to the SAME-CUT-SCALE horn (retention admission reads the same predicted-harm magnitude scale as the interrupt, at a lower cut-point). 'supports' = evidence for that horn; 'weakens' = evidence for the independent-relevance-criterion horn; 'mixed' = evidence that neither horn alone accounts for the data. This is a highly-cited Neuron review by the two principal authors of the surprise/stopping literature, so source_quality is high. But it is a review rather than a single decisive experiment, and -- decisively for the confidence -- it speaks ONLY to the interrupt leg of MECH-485's triage, never to the retention leg that Q-090 actually asks about. It establishes the PRECONDITION for the same-scale reading (that the interrupt is recruited by a content-indifferent magnitude-like signal) without showing that retention reads that same signal. Mapping fidelity is therefore weighted down hard, which is what holds the aggregate at 0.5 despite the strong source.
failure_signatures: The review characterises the fronto-basal-ganglia stopping network as producing a GLOBAL, non-selective suppression of basal-ganglia output; if the same signal were the sole admission criterion for retention, retention would likewise be non-selective, which is precisely what a goal-match criterion is proposed to prevent.

The paper offers no evidence that sub-threshold unexpected events -- the ones that do not trigger the interrupt -- are retained at all, so a lower cut-point on the same scale is an extrapolation the source does not license.

Recruitment is described as driven by unexpectedness/surprise rather than by predicted-harm magnitude specifically; if surprise and predicted harm dissociate in REE, the mapping to MECH-485's single magnitude term fails.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direction is stated relative to the SAME-CUT-SCALE horn (convention note in the wessel2017 entry); this entry WEAKENS that horn. It is the sharpest disconfirming source in the pull because it attacks the same-scale reading at its structural weak point rather than merely failing to support it. A single threshold on a single magnitude scale is a monotone admission rule: more magnitude, more likely retained. Pupillo et al. report that the sign of the prediction-error-to-memory relationship FLIPS depending on a second variable (whether the prediction was correct), which no monotone cut on one scale can express. Confidence is held at 0.58 rather than higher because the moderating variable they identify is prediction-outcome correctness, not goal-match: the paper refutes 'pure magnitude' cleanly but supplies no support for Q-090's specific alternative, so it eliminates one horn without electing the other. Trial-wise model-derived PE estimates raise source quality; the modest sample and the fact that the flip is an interaction (historically the least replicable effect class) hold it down.
failure_signatures: When predictions were correct, larger prediction errors ENHANCED memory; when predictions were incorrect, larger prediction errors IMPAIRED memory -- so retention is not a monotone function of magnitude and cannot be produced by any single cut-point on a single scale.

The moderator is prediction-outcome correctness rather than goal-match, so the result disconfirms the same-scale horn without confirming the independent-relevance-criterion horn; a third reading (magnitude gated by a correctness/confidence term) fits better than either.

If REE implemented leg 3 as a simple low threshold on the leg-1 magnitude, this result predicts it would retain exactly the wrong alternatives in the incorrect-prediction regime -- keeping high-magnitude items the biology discards.
The interaction is a moderation effect in a modest sample; the direction-flip is the entire load-bearing finding and an unreplicated interaction is the weakest place to put that load.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direction is stated relative to the SAME-CUT-SCALE horn (see the convention note in the wessel2017 entry). Two experiments, the second explicitly replicating and extending the first while controlling for the confound the paper is named after, which is better internal evidence than a single study. It is the closest thing in this pull to a direct test of 'does a scalar magnitude signal decide what enters episodic retention', and the answer is yes, dissociably from arousal. What holds confidence at 0.5 rather than higher is a specific gap rather than a general one: the study dissociates prediction error from AROUSAL, not from GOAL-RELEVANCE, and goal relevance was never manipulated. Q-090's alternative horn is goal-match, so the paper rules out the wrong competitor. It constrains the magnitude term to be real and causally efficacious without touching the disjunction Q-090 actually poses.
failure_signatures: Goal-relevance was never manipulated or measured, so the study cannot discriminate the two Q-090 horns; a goal-match criterion correlated with shock-predictiveness would produce the same result.

The prediction errors concern outcomes the participant actually EXPERIENCED, whereas MECH-485 leg 3 concerns alternatives that were predicted and then not acted on -- the retained item in the study is a real encoded percept, not a counterfactual branch.

Prediction error was binary and unsigned in Experiment 1 (derived from explicit shock-expectancy ratings), so the paper supports 'PE promotes encoding' more strongly than it supports 'encoding scales continuously with PE magnitude', and a lower CUT-POINT on a continuous scale is what the same-scale horn requires.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direction is stated relative to the SAME-CUT-SCALE horn (convention note in the wessel2017 entry). Recorded as MIXED because it is the one source in this pull that speaks to both horns at once and endorses neither: the normative answer it derives is a PRODUCT of a magnitude-like term and a relevance-like term, so the same-scale horn is right that magnitude belongs in the criterion and the independent-criterion horn is right that a relevance term is indispensable, and both are wrong to think either suffices alone. This is the highest-confidence entry in the pull for three reasons: it is a normative derivation rather than a correlational finding, so it says what the criterion OUGHT to be rather than merely what covaried in one sample; it is validated against a broad set of independent replay phenomena rather than a single effect; and it is already the anchor citation for MECH-292, so adopting its two-factor structure for leg 3 keeps the retention story internally consistent with the ghost-goal bank rather than introducing a rival formalism. It is held below 0.7 by a genuine term-by-term mismatch: 'gain' is policy-improvement value in an MDP, not predicted-harm magnitude, and 'need' is expected future state occupancy, not MECH-292's goal-match. The structural claim transfers; the terms do not, one-to-one.
failure_signatures: The derived priority is a PRODUCT of gain and need, so either factor at zero zeroes the priority -- a high-magnitude alternative with no prospective relevance is not retained, which the same-cut-scale horn cannot express, and a highly relevant alternative with no potential to change behaviour is also not retained, which a pure goal-match criterion cannot express either.

A multiplicative two-factor rule cannot be reduced to any threshold on a single scale, so implementing leg 3 as a low cut-point on the leg-1 magnitude is not a simplification of this account but a different and worse rule.

'Gain' is defined as expected improvement in future decisions, which is prospective; MECH-485's magnitude is a predicted harm/success size, which is not the same quantity, so an implementation that substitutes one for the other inherits none of the normative guarantee.

The authors note the mechanism's dysfunction 'may underlie pathologies like rumination and craving' -- a leg-3 retention rule tuned toward over-admission has a named failure mode, namely an agent that will not stop revisiting alternatives it did not take.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direction is stated relative to the SAME-CUT-SCALE horn (convention note in the wessel2017 entry); this entry WEAKENS it. A lesion double-dissociation is the strongest available evidence that two functions are separably implemented, and this one shows that the counterfactual-alternative machinery can be removed while the machinery for evaluating what actually happened survives. If the alternative-handling pathway is anatomically separable from factual outcome evaluation, then the presumption that leg 3 is merely a second cut on leg 1's scale loses its main attraction, which was parsimony. Confidence sits at 0.55 rather than higher for one specific reason that the source cannot overcome: the paradigm hands participants the unchosen outcome externally on every trial, so it tests counterfactual EVALUATION and never tests ADMISSION -- nothing in the design requires the patient to have decided what to retain. Q-090 is an admission question. Very strong source, materially off-target mechanism.
failure_signatures: Orbitofrontal lesion patients 'did not report regret or anticipate negative consequences of their choices' while continuing to respond to the outcomes they actually obtained -- a dissociation between factual and counterfactual evaluation that a single shared magnitude scale does not predict.

The unchosen gamble's outcome is DISPLAYED to the participant on each trial, so the study measures what is done with an alternative once it is present, not which alternatives are admitted in the first place -- the admission criterion Q-090 asks about is never exercised.

Lesion patients are few, heterogeneous in extent and aetiology, and often chronically reorganised, so a null finding (no regret reported) is weaker evidence than the same result in an intact-brain manipulation.
Regret is a self-reported affective state; absence of reported regret may reflect impaired affective report or impaired comparison rather than absent retention of the alternative.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the highest-mapping-fidelity AI entry in the pull because it operates at REE's own level of description: a computable signal, added alongside the primary task reward, that measures IMPACT as the change an action makes to the ATTAINABLE UTILITY of a set of auxiliary reward functions -- i.e. the change in an agent's ability to still optimise a range of goals. Agency, formalised, IS attainable utility / optionality; harm-to-agency IS a reduction in it. AUP thus supplies MECH-129 a concrete instantiation of a distinct harm signal that is NOT the primary cost signal and is computed over reachability, which is precisely the 'distinct architecture' the claim asserts is required. Held at 0.72 (not higher) because as published AUP measures the agent's impact on its OWN auxiliary attainable utility (a proxy for reversibility/low-impact), not another agent's -- extending it to OTHER-agent attainable utility is the natural but non-trivial step MECH-129's requirement (a) demands and AUP does not itself provide.
failure_signatures: AUP as published penalises change to the AGENT'S OWN attainable utility over auxiliary rewards (a self-referential low-impact/reversibility proxy); applied to harm-to-agency it must be re-pointed at ANOTHER agent's attainable utility, which requires inferring that agent's reward set -- so the formalism is only a harm-to-agency signal once composed with other-agent goal modelling, and AUP alone would penalise the agent's own optionality loss, not the other's, a different quantity.

AUP's impact measure is acutely sensitive to the choice of auxiliary reward set and the baseline (stepwise vs inaction); Turner et al. show random auxiliary rewards suffice for LOW-IMPACT but the paper does not establish that any auxiliary set faithfully tracks a SPECIFIC other agent's goal -- so a harm-to-agency signal built on AUP inherits an unresolved baseline/auxiliary-selection problem (the same counterfactual-baseline issue flagged in the Feinberg entry).

entries.confidence_rationale: Shue's basic-rights framework supplies MECH-129 two things: (i) the concept of a PROTECTABLE INTEREST that is basic in the sense of being a precondition for enjoying every other interest -- security and subsistence -- which is the normative shape of 'agency' as something whose obstruction is a distinct category of harm; and (ii) his tripartite duty analysis (duties to AVOID depriving, to PROTECT from deprivation, and to AID the deprived) which shows that a single interest generates structurally different obligations, paralleling MECH-129's insistence that harm-to-agency needs its own architecture rather than reusing the harm-to-agent one. Held at 0.6 because Shue's project is the correlative-duty structure of human rights in political philosophy, several inferential steps from a per-timestep goal-interference signal, and 'agency' in Shue is closer to the standing capacity for rights-enjoyment than to a specific in-flight goal.
failure_signatures: Shue's 'avoid depriving / protect / aid' triad implies that harm-to-agency has a POSITIVE-duty component (protect and aid the obstructed) that a purely aversive obstruction-avoidance signal cannot capture -- a REE substrate that only penalises the agent's OWN obstructive trajectories satisfies at most the 'avoid depriving' duty and remains architecturally blind to the protect/aid duties Shue argues are equally basic, so obstruction-avoidance under-implements the interest.

Shue's basic rights are STANDING capacities (security, subsistence) rather than in-flight goals; mapping harm-to-agency onto 'setback to a basic right' risks conflating obstruction of a momentary goal (which may be trivial or competitive) with deprivation of the enduring capacity for goal-pursuit -- only the latter is basic in Shue's sense, so an unweighted obstruction signal over-counts trivial interference as harm-to-agency.

entries.confidence_rationale: Bostrom's instrumental convergence thesis is the AI-alignment source that most directly grounds MECH-129's motivating worry -- that 'a system that never touches another agent could still systematically undermine their agency.' Convergent instrumental drives (self-preservation, resource acquisition, goal-content integrity) predict that a capable goal-directed agent will, by default and for almost any final goal, obstruct OTHER agents' goal-pursuit -- competing for resources, resisting being stopped, removing obstacles that happen to be other agents. This is goal-obstruction as INSTRUMENTAL (not terminal) harm, arising with no aversive intent and no physical contact, which is exactly the harm-to-agency hazard MECH-129 says the current harm architecture is blind to. Held at 0.64 because it is a philosophical argument about idealised superintelligent agents, not empirical evidence, and it characterises the agent-as-threat rather than specifying a harm-DETECTION signal.
failure_signatures: Instrumental convergence predicts that obstruction of other agents is the DEFAULT behaviour of a capable optimiser, which implies harm-to-agency cannot be handled by rare-event detection: the base rate of incidental obstruction is high, so a threshold-triggered obstruction signal either floods (if sensitive) or misses systematic low-level agency-undermining (if conservative) -- the signal must be graded and integrated into value, not a tripwire.

Bostrom's argument is about the AGENT'S OWN convergent drives; it gives no account of how an agent would DETECT that it is obstructing another's agency, so it supports the EXISTENCE and DEFAULT-NESS of the harm-to-agency hazard while leaving the other-agent goal-modelling substrate (MECH-129 requirement a) entirely unspecified -- convergence tells you the danger is real and ubiquitous, not how to represent it.

entries.confidence_rationale: Feinberg's setback-to-interests analysis is the canonical philosophy-of-harm account and supplies MECH-129 its foundational move: harm is a setback to an INTEREST, not necessarily a physical hurt, so a non-contact obstruction of another's goal-pursuit is a genuine harm rather than a metaphor. His own two-way split -- welfare interests (minimal, generic conditions of any life-plan) versus ulterior interests (one's specific projects and goals) -- maps closely onto MECH-129's two categories (harm-to-agent = setback to welfare/bodily interests; harm-to-agency = setback to the ulterior interest in pursuing a specific goal). Held at 0.7 rather than higher because Feinberg is a normative account of criminal-law liability, not an architecture, and the welfare/ulterior split is adjacent to but not identical with agent/agency (a bodily assault sets back a welfare interest but is still harm-to-agent; only the goal-obstruction sense of ulterior-interest-setback is harm-to-agency).
failure_signatures: Feinberg's account is counterfactual-comparative: X is harmed iff X is left worse off (in interest terms) than X would otherwise have been. Applied naively to a REE goal-interference signal this inherits the well-known baseline problem -- 'worse off than WHAT?' -- so an obstruction signal computed against a mis-specified counterfactual baseline (e.g. the other agent's default trajectory absent me) can register spurious harm-to-agency or miss real cases, the same baseline-selection hazard that plagues low-impact AI measures (see the Turner AUP entry).

Setback-to-interests is a non-normative core wrapped in a normative one (harm-as-wrong requires the setback be unjustified and rights-violating); MECH-129's raw goal-interference signal corresponds only to the non-normative core, so a substrate that fires on any obstruction without a consent/justification gate (discriminant 4) over-reports -- Feinberg himself excludes consented-to and justified setbacks from harm-as-wrong.

entries.confidence_rationale: Thomson's value to MECH-129 is structural, not topical. The trolley cases themselves are about harm-to-AGENT (death), so the paper is NOT direct evidence for the harm-to-agency category. What it supplies is a rigorously worked demonstration that HOW a harm is brought about -- as an intended means versus a foreseen side-effect, and as a doing versus an allowing -- is a morally load-bearing distinction that changes the verdict on otherwise identical outcomes. That is exactly MECH-129 discriminant 3 (whether an obstruction is incidental or constitutive). Held at 0.58 because the transfer is by analogy of the discriminant structure, not by shared subject matter, and Thomson's own conclusions are contested within the trolleyology literature.
failure_signatures: Thomson herself later (2008) repudiated the permissibility verdict of the original Bystander case, showing the means/side-effect intuitions the paper trades on are not stable even for their author -- a REE substrate that hard-codes discriminant 3 (incidental vs constitutive obstruction) as a crisp binary inherits a distinction whose boundary cases the philosophical literature has not settled.

The doing/allowing and means/side-effect distinctions require attributing INTENT and identifying the causal role of the harm in the agent's plan; a goal-interference signal computed purely over trajectory geometry (did my path raise the cost of yours) cannot recover whether the obstruction was a means or a side-effect without a model of my own plan structure, so discriminant 3 is not computable from the obstruction signal alone.

entries.confidence_rationale: Entered deliberately as counter-evidence to MECH-130's NECESSITY argument, not to its premise. Schmidhuber's reward is the derivative of compressibility -- reward comes from patterns that are 'novel, surprising ... allowing for improved prediction or data compression', so an unpredictable-but-unlearnable source yields no reward at all. If an adversarial agent's opacity is irreducible, the field has had a source-AGNOSTIC fix for MECH-130's failure mode 1 since 1991, and typing by source would be redundant machinery. Confidence held at 0.55 because the rebuttal is inferential (the paper never discusses multiagent novelty, so I am applying a general principle to a case it does not address) and because there is a real counter-counter-argument: another agent's policy is non-stationary and partially learnable, which under a learning-progress signal may make it an ENDURING rather than a decaying attractor -- worse for MECH-130's concern, not better.
failure_signatures: A learning-progress / compression-progress signal already discounts irreducible unpredictability by construction, so MECH-130's failure mode 1 as stated ('highest unpredictability = highest information = strongest approach') does not follow for any curiosity signal built on this principle -- it holds only for raw-novelty or raw-prediction-error signals, which narrows the class of MECH-111 implementations for which MECH-130 is load-bearing.

Because the fix is source-agnostic, a world-versus-agent classifier would be redundant for the noise case specifically: MECH-130 must therefore justify source typing by what reducibility typing CANNOT do -- routing to social modelling, and harm-conditioned inhibition -- rather than by the entropy-seeking failure alone.

The theory's own attractor is the currently-learnable-but-not-yet-mastered pattern; another agent's policy is continually shifting yet learnable, so under this signal an agent may present as a persistently high-progress target that never exhausts, which would sustain approach pressure indefinitely without any of the entropy-seeking pathology the theory was designed to remove.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily-cited peer-reviewed taxonomy, so source quality is high; but the support it lends MECH-130 is an argument from SILENCE (the typology has no axis for novelty source) rather than a positive test of any of MECH-130's three failure modes. It also cuts partly the other way: the paper does treat 'social presence motivation' as a distinct reward type -- but classifies it as NON-intrinsic and homeostatic, which is a different distinction from the one MECH-130 asks for. Mapping fidelity is therefore capped, and the 2007 vintage limits what its silence says about the field today (see the Pan 2025 entry, which supplies the current state).
failure_signatures: The typology's three broad classes (knowledge-based, competence-based, morphological) are all defined over an undifferentiated 'sensorimotor flow' -- a surprising event carries no tag for whether it originated in an inanimate environment feature or in another agent's policy, so no model built inside this taxonomy can condition on that distinction.

Uncertainty Motivation (UM) as formalised here generates reward inversely proportional to an event's probability of observation, with no term for the source or the reducibility of that improbability -- an agent that is unpredictable by construction is scored identically to an unexplored region of the environment.

'Social presence motivation' is presented in the paper's section on models of NON-intrinsic motivation systems and is keyed on face count relative to an optimum -- a homeostatic set-point over social stimulation, not a typing of the novelty signal itself, so it does not supply the routing MECH-130 requires.

entries.confidence_rationale: Large empirical study (54 environments) at a top venue, and the noisy-TV result is the field's canonical demonstration that an untyped prediction-error curiosity signal is captured by whatever in the environment is least predictable. That is MECH-130's failure mode 1 mechanism, demonstrated rather than argued. Held below 0.8 by a real disanalogy: the paper's attractor is IRREDUCIBLE stochasticity, whereas another agent's policy is partially learnable and non-stationary, so the two are not the same object and the transfer is by mechanism-analogy rather than by direct test. No multiagent condition is run.
failure_signatures: With a prediction-error intrinsic reward, 'If the transitions in the environment are random, then even with a perfect dynamics model, the expected reward will be the entropy of the transition, and the agent will seek out transitions with the highest entropy' -- i.e. the signal maximises toward the least-modellable thing available, not toward the most informative.

Adding a literal channel-changing TV to a maze 'drastically slows down learning', so the attractor is strong enough to dominate task-directed behaviour rather than merely perturb it; the agents only 'sometimes converge' to the extrinsic reward, and only when run long enough.

The failure is not fixed by a better world model -- the paper's statement is explicitly 'even with a perfect dynamics model' -- so no amount of improved prediction capacity in MECH-111 removes it; only a change to what the reward is computed over can.

entries.confidence_rationale: The single most directly on-point paper found in this pull, and it cuts both ways with unusual sharpness. It states MECH-130's premise almost verbatim ('existing curiosity mechanisms exhibit a uniform novelty bias, treating all unexpected observations equally') and then separates peer-behaviour novelty from environmental stochasticity as distinct signal categories -- which is the world/agent typing MECH-130 asks for, built and evaluated at NeurIPS. That FALSIFIES the strong form of the proposal note that the distinction is absent from the literature. But the entire motivation is exploration EFFICIENCY: peer novelty is treated as under-exploited signal to be amplified, never as approach pressure to be gated; safety, harm, risk and adversarial agents appear nowhere. Confidence held at 0.70 rather than higher because it is a 2025 paper with no independent replication and I read the abstract and venue record rather than the full method.
failure_signatures: 'Existing curiosity mechanisms exhibit a uniform novelty bias, treating all unexpected observations equally' -- an independent, peer-reviewed statement as of 2025 that the untyped signal MECH-130 objects to is still the field default, made by authors whose own contribution is to replace it.

The paper's remedy amplifies attention to peer-behaviour novelty because it 'encode[s] latent task dynamics' -- so a system built on CERMIC's logic would increase, not decrease, approach pressure toward the least-predictable agent, since that agent carries the most peer-novelty signal.

Neither the abstract nor the venue record mentions safety, harm, risk, or adversarial agents; the evaluation suites (VMAS, Meltingpot, SMACv2) are scored on task return, so an agent that is exploited by a peer maintaining surface unpredictability would register as an exploration success up to the point where return degrades.

entries.confidence_rationale: The most direct behavioural confirmation of MECH-130's posited mechanism found in this pull: an agent-directed intrinsic motivation, keyed on the poverty of the agent's model of others, that literally produces approach and proximity-maintenance toward other agents. Peer-reviewed at IJCAI with an empirical evaluation, and the mapping is unusually clean because the paper's reward is exactly the object MECH-130 says needs gating. Held below 0.8 because the confirmation is INADVERTENT -- the authors report approach-toward-others as a desirable outcome in cooperative tasks, and never test the adversarial or harmful-agent condition that would turn it into MECH-130's failure mode. Assessed from the published abstract and proceedings record rather than a full-text read.
failure_signatures: The intrinsic motivation 'encourages agents to stay near each other to obtain better observations and construct a model of others' -- an agent-directed intrinsic signal whose direct behavioural output is sustained approach and proximity, which is precisely the chronic approach pressure MECH-130 predicts.

The trigger condition is model poverty or poor task performance: agents approach 'when their model of other agents is poor, or the overall task performance is bad'. That rule is monotone in how poorly modelled the other agent is, so the least-modellable agent attracts the most approach -- and an adversary that maintains surface unpredictability holds the trigger permanently on, which is MECH-130's third failure mode as a design property rather than a bug.

No harm, risk or threat term appears anywhere in the reward; approach is gated on epistemic state alone, so there is no path by which a high harm estimate could inhibit the approach the signal is generating.

The evaluation is cooperative, so the regime in which approach-on-model-poverty is dangerous is outside the tested envelope entirely -- the method's reported success is evidence about the cooperative case only and says nothing about the mixed-motive or adversarial case.
