A clean computational demonstration that goals held at the agent's current level of attainability expand the set of achievable goals bottom-up under sparse reward, with no prior knowledge of the environment -- the zone-of-proximal-development principle made mechanical. Held down because the goal SPACE is given a priori and the architecture is flat goal-conditioned RL with no superordinate goal at all, so it evidences the reachability-expansion half of MECH-428 and not the parent-formation half.
failure_signatures: An agent trained with ordinary RL is capable of achieving only the single task specified by its reward function -- the failure mode that makes direct superordinate seeding brittle when that one goal is rarely contacted.

Goals that are too hard yield no learning signal and goals that are too easy yield no learning pressure; the generator must be adversarially held at INTERMEDIATE difficulty, meaning the bootstrapping window is narrow and must be actively tracked as competence changes.
The method presupposes a parametrized goal space (subsets of the state space) supplied by the designer -- it discovers WHICH goals are currently attainable, not what the space of goals is.

There is no goal hierarchy: nothing in the architecture corresponds to a superordinate goal that subgoal attainment could seed, so the mechanism cannot in principle exhibit MECH-428's formation-direction effect.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly matches the regime MECH-428 names -- a terminal benefit so sparsely reached that a flat agent scores zero -- and shows that attainable subgoals with their own intrinsic progress signal produce learning where direct pursuit produces none. Discounted because the subgoals are hand-specified from an object detector rather than discovered, and because the superordinate value function is architecturally PRE-PROVIDED rather than formed bottom-up, which is precisely the step MECH-428 claims.
failure_signatures: Flat DQN scores zero on Montezuma's Revenge -- with terminal reward this sparse, direct top-down pursuit of the superordinate goal yields no learning signal at all, which is the seeding-failure regime MECH-428 is written for.

The paper's own stated diagnosis of the failure is INSUFFICIENT EXPLORATION resulting in an agent unable to learn robust value functions -- i.e. the goal representation never gets the contact it needs to become well-formed.

The subgoal set is supplied externally (entities from a custom object detector), so the demonstration is that ATTAINABLE SUBGOALS RESCUE learning, not that an agent can generate its own subgoal structure -- a limitation later hierarchical-RL work has repeatedly had to confront.

The meta-controller's value function over intrinsic goals exists from initialisation; nothing here shows a superordinate goal being CREATED by repeated subgoal attainment where it did not previously exist.

entries.confidence_rationale: The canonical source for scaffolding and the developmental anchor MECH-428's own notes flagged as the next lit-pull, so it fills a named gap in the claim's grounding. Confidence is deliberately modest: it is a 1976 observational study of tutor-child interaction whose abstract is not retrievable through PubMed, its evidential standards predate modern developmental methodology, and -- most importantly -- the scaffold it documents is EXTERNALLY PROVIDED, which is the sibling mechanism (scaffolded_sd054_onboarding) rather than MECH-428's internal complement.
failure_signatures: A task beyond the learner's current unaided capacity yields no productive engagement at all until it is decomposed -- the developmental counterpart of a superordinate goal that cannot be seeded because its terminal benefit is never contacted.
The decomposition in this paper is performed by a TUTOR, not by the learner; the study documents scaffolded acquisition and does not show a learner generating its own subgoal structure.

Effectiveness of tutoring varied systematically with the child's age and developmental level, indicating the subgoal grading must match current competence -- a mis-graded scaffold is not merely less helpful but can fail to engage the learner.
Non-retrievable abstract and 1976-era observational methodology mean effect sizes, sample and analysis cannot be independently verified from the record obtained here.

entries.confidence_rationale: Nature-tier in vivo two-photon imaging with a CAUSAL manipulation that removes the bounding mechanism and produces exactly the failure MECH-471 predicts: prior motor competence is disrupted by learning a second task. Discounted for mapping -- the two tasks are both forelimb motor tasks in the same cortical region, so 'unrelated' here is weaker than MECH-471's 'unrelated previously-acquired competences', and the bounding is biophysical (dendritic compartmentalisation) with no direct REE analogue.
failure_signatures: When somatostatin-expressing interneurons are inactivated, different motor tasks stop being routed to different apical tuft branches and instead frequently induce Ca2+ spikes on the SAME branches -- i.e. the scope bound on the competence update is removed.

On those shared branches, spines potentiated during one task are DEPOTENTIATED when active seconds before Ca2+ spikes induced by another task: a later update silently overwrites the substrate of an earlier competence.
The overwrite is behaviourally consequential, not merely synaptic -- increased neuronal activity and the performance improvement after learning one task are disrupted when another task is learned.
The protective mechanism is inhibitory and therefore FAILABLE: competence isolation is not a static property of the substrate but an actively maintained gate that can be switched off.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily replicated demonstration in ARTIFICIAL learners -- the correct machine class for REE -- that an ungated competence update destroys unrelated prior competence, and that a per-parameter importance gate largely prevents it. Held below 0.8 by two things: the method's quadratic-penalty derivation was formally critiqued in a PNAS comment, and EWC delivers only ONE of MECH-471's three registered properties.
failure_signatures: Sequential training on a new task degrades performance on previously learned, unrelated tasks to near-chance in ordinary gradient-trained networks -- the paper's baseline condition IS the failure MECH-471's falsifier is designed to detect.

Catastrophic forgetting had been 'widely thought to be an inevitable feature of connectionist models', i.e. the default assumption was that no discipline was available -- an assumption this paper falsifies but which explains why competence-path discipline goes unregistered by default.

The remedy is explicitly a GATE: learning is selectively slowed on the weights important for prior tasks. Without such a gate, a single successful update propagates across the whole parameter set -- MECH-471's named failure mode, stated in machine terms.

EWC provides bounding WITHOUT provenance or rollback: the Fisher-weighted penalty records only that a parameter matters, not which experience made it matter, and offers no operation to revert a specific update. A system can therefore satisfy the bounding property and still fail the other two.

The formulation's quadratic-penalty derivation was subsequently challenged in a PNAS comment (Huszar, 10.1073/pnas.1717042115) arguing the multiple-penalty scheme is not the correct Bayesian recursion -- the discipline is real but this particular instantiation is not settled.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong Nature-tier causal work that is unusually well-shaped for this claim -- it demonstrates all three MECH-471 properties (a provenance-like label over which synapses a given competence episode wrote, a rollback operation, and demonstrated specificity of that rollback) in one preparation. Discounted substantially because the labelling and the erasure are EXPERIMENTER-IMPOSED tooling, not endogenous mechanisms the organism runs; the paper shows the substrate ADMITS provenance-and-rollback, not that biology implements it.
failure_signatures: A newly acquired motor skill depends on a task-specific dense synaptic ensemble -- so a competence is not diffusely stored, and an update that reaches that ensemble can destroy it wholesale.

Optical shrinkage of the potentiated spines DISRUPTED the acquired motor learning, establishing that the competence is causally carried by an identifiable, addressable subset of the substrate rather than being merely correlated with it.

The disruption is SPECIFIC: the identical manipulation applied to spines evoked by a distinct motor task in the same cortical region did NOT affect the first learning. Absent that specificity, any rollback operation would itself be a catastrophic-interference event.
Synaptic remodelling was confined to a small subset of neurons, i.e. a single learning episode's write is naturally narrow -- which is the property an ungated competence-update rule would forfeit.

Directly supports the non-collapsibility half of MECH-141: a single model containing BOTH the hyperdirect (fronto-subthalamic) and indirect (fronto-striatal) pathways best explained brain activation on stop trials, and combined connection strength was highest on successfully inhibited trials -- i.e. successful inhibition needs both pathways engaged, not one. Fast vs slow inhibitors dissociated on which fronto-caudate connection dominated. Held at 0.74 because the paper frames the second route as the INDIRECT (fronto-striatal-pallidal) pathway rather than a seconds-scale PROACTIVE one; the 'both are needed' and 'fast/slow dissociation' evidence maps well, but the specific proactive-vs-reactive timescale labels are the anchor paper's, not this one's.
failure_signatures: The complementary pathway here is the classic INDIRECT (fronto-striatal-pallidal) route, characterised within reactive stopping, not an explicitly anticipatory seconds-scale proactive route; the mapping to MECH-141's 'slow proactive' pathway is therefore by analogy (both are the longer, caudate-routed pathway) rather than a direct measurement of proactive control.

All connectivity is measured on stop-signal trials within a single reactive task; a model where one pathway sufficed on some trials would not obviously be excluded by the group-level 'both pathways' winning model.

entries.confidence_rationale: Provides the direct temporal evidence the DCM anchor cannot: intracranial field-potential recordings from IFG and STN in 21 humans show short-latency (monosynaptic-indicative) IFG->ventral-STN connectivity, and during stopping the cortical stopping-related potential PRECEDES STN activity, with IFG-STN synchronization predicting stop-signal reaction time. This nails the 'fast reactive milliseconds-scale hyperdirect' half of MECH-141 with real latencies rather than inferred ones. Held at 0.80 (not higher) because it characterises only the fast reactive pathway -- it does not itself test the slow proactive pathway or the non-collapsibility of the two, so it corroborates one half of the dual-timescale claim.
failure_signatures: The study characterises only the reactive/hyperdirect route; it offers no measurement of a slow proactive prefrontal-caudate pathway, so it cannot by itself establish that the two timescales are segregated -- it establishes only that the fast one exists and is genuinely fast.
Recordings are from Parkinson's disease patients undergoing DBS surgery; disease-related basal-ganglia pathology is a transfer confound for a claim about the healthy arbitration architecture.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct anchor for the claim: whole-brain fMRI plus Bayesian model selection over 70+13 DCMs isolates a 'longer' DLPFC->caudate->IFG->SMA->STN->M1 pathway whose caudate->IFG link is modulated ONLY under proactive inhibition, versus a 'shorter' IFG->SMA->STN->M1 hyperdirect pathway carrying reactive inhibition. This is exactly the two-pathway dissociation MECH-141 asserts. Confidence held below 0.85 because the paper's own framing is a COMMON network (shared IFG-SMA-STN-M1 core), so it evidences dissociation at the modulatory-connectivity level rather than fully segregated anatomy, and DCM is a model-comparison inference, not a direct latency measurement of the two timescales.
failure_signatures: The two pathways share the IFG-SMA-STN-M1 core; the dissociation is in which effective connections are modulated, not in fully non-overlapping anatomy. A substrate that collapsed the shared core while preserving the distinct front-end modulation would still satisfy this paper's evidence, so the paper does not on its own falsify a partially-collapsed arbitration signal.
Timescale segregation (seconds vs milliseconds) is inferred from the pathway lengths and task structure, not measured directly here; DCM reports connection strengths, not conduction latencies.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical foundation for the reactive/STN half: right IFC and STN are specifically activated by stopping (not going), and stopping-related activation is greater for FAST inhibitors than slow ones in both regions, with IFC and STN activity correlated -- convergent, independent support that the fast reactive route runs through the STN and that its engagement tracks stopping speed. Lower confidence (0.62) because it is a 2006 activation/correlation study that only hypothesises the hyperdirect projection (its closing sentence calls for future work to establish a direct IFC-STN pathway), speaks only to the reactive half, and says nothing about proactive control or non-collapsibility.
failure_signatures: The paper itself does not demonstrate the hyperdirect pathway -- it explicitly leaves establishing a direct IFC->STN projection to future research; it shows co-activation and correlation, not connectivity.

It addresses only reactive stopping; it provides no evidence for a separate proactive pathway or for the two operating at segregated, non-collapsible timescales, so it cannot on its own distinguish MECH-141 from a single-pathway account.

Recent, well-scoped mini-review by a group whose primary work is in this exact area, synthesising the dorsoventral literature MECH-143 and MECH-144 jointly partition. Source quality 0.70 -- a review, so secondary, and Frontiers rather than a top-tier venue. Mapping fidelity 0.60: it surveys the dorsal valence literature broadly rather than isolating the value-at-fixed-location manipulation MECH-143 actually asserts. Net 0.58. NOTE: the same source is assessed separately against MECH-144, where its direction is 'mixed' -- see the paired entry in targeted_review_connectome_mech_144.
failure_signatures: The review's own summary position is that dorsal hippocampal place cells remap in response to aversive and rewarding stimuli and thereby embed valence-related information within a spatially anchored framework -- the direct contrary of a value-free dorsal map.
Aversive events such as footshock or predator odour induce dorsal remapping with NO physical change to the environment, so dorsal map stability cannot be attributed to environmental constancy.
Place fields concentrate around emotionally salient regions (both appetitive and aversive), described in the review as goal-directed remapping.

A subset of dorsal neurons is selectively activated at reward sites regardless of spatial position ('reward cells'), encoding positive valence independently of spatial context within the dorsal compartment itself.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong source (PLoS Biology; tetrode recording combined with optogenetic VTA manipulation, so causal rather than merely correlational). Discounted on mapping_fidelity (0.55) because the manipulation is reward-driven PREFERENCE learning over locations, not value change at a fixed goal -- adjacent to MECH-143's design rather than identical to it. Net 0.60.
failure_signatures: CA1 place fields cluster toward rewarded locations, and the degree of clustering correlates with the animal's behavioural navigation preference -- the dorsal map's geometry is not independent of experienced value.

The redistribution is causally driven by ventral tegmental dopaminergic activity, established by optogenetic manipulation, so this is a mechanism for writing value into the dorsal map rather than an incidental correlation.
The authors conclude explicitly that hippocampal neurons store concurrent context reward value, which is the direct negation of a value-free dorsal map.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong source (PNAS, rat tetrode recording, well-controlled dissociation of reward from navigation history). Mapping fidelity is the limiting term (0.50): the value signal is found in REPLAY CONTENT, a different variable from the place-field geometry MECH-143 asserts, so the paper neither confirms nor refutes the claim on its own terms -- it relocates where value lives. Net 0.52, deliberately below the 0.5-0.79 band's midpoint.
failure_signatures: Reward selectively increases the fidelity of forward replays for high-value trajectories, so value information demonstrably enters dorsal hippocampal sequence content even where place-field geometry is unchanged.

The authors propose explicitly that hippocampal replay constructs a map of potential trajectories AND their associated values -- a 'value map' -- which is incompatible with reading the dorsal hippocampus as a wholly value-free structure.
MECH-143's no-new-value-computation constraint is therefore only defensible if stated at the level of place-field geometry; stated at the level of dorsal hippocampal output it is false.

entries.confidence_rationale: Closest design match in the corpus to the manipulation MECH-143 actually asserts -- reward VALUE changed while goal LOCATION is held constant -- so mapping_fidelity is weighted heavily (0.85). Discounted for preprint status (not yet peer reviewed) rather than for method, which is strong (longitudinal calcium imaging of CA1 across a reward downshift). Net 0.62: high evidential relevance, provisional source standing.
failure_signatures: A dedicated subpopulation of dorsal CA1 place cells -- 'reward-tethered place cells' -- binds spatial context to reward magnitude and remaps selectively when reward value is reduced at an unchanged location, so the blanket statement that dorsal CA1 place cells are insensitive to goal value is false at the subpopulation level.

CA1 population event rates are elevated at high-value locations and equalize when reward is downshifted, which is a value-dependent change in the dorsal representation with no accompanying change in the physical environment.
The value-driven remapping PRECEDES the behavioural adjustment to the downshift, so it cannot be dismissed as a downstream read-out of changed behaviour or changed occupancy.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong primary source (Science Advances; converging anatomy, electrophysiology, transcriptomics and chemogenetics, with a pharmacological rescue). Confidence is nonetheless held below 0.5 because mapping_fidelity is genuinely poor (0.35): the paper demonstrates a dorsoventral valence dissociation in cholinergic INPUT and measures no spatial coding at all, so it cannot bear on whether valence is intrinsic to ventral map geometry. Included as corroboration of the dorsoventral functional split that MECH-143/MECH-144 jointly presuppose, not as evidence for MECH-144's geometric content.
failure_signatures: The dorsoventral valence dissociation demonstrated here is carried by differential cholinergic INPUT to the two poles, not by any intrinsic property of hippocampal map geometry -- so this evidence is equally compatible with valence being externally tagged onto the ventral map, which is the reading MECH-144 rejects.
No spatial coding is measured anywhere in the study, so it cannot discriminate 'spatially organized valence encoding' from valence encoding that is merely located in a spatial structure.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly on-topic recent synthesis of exactly the ventral valence literature MECH-144 cites. Mapping fidelity raised to 0.70 (higher than the paired MECH-143 entry) because the review addresses ventral valence coding head-on. Direction is 'mixed' rather than 'supports' on a specific structural point: the review reports that ventral anxiety cells show MINIMAL OVERLAP with classical place cells, which supports the claim's first half (ventral valence encoding exists) while cutting against its second half (valence intrinsic to MAP GEOMETRY rather than externally tagged). Net 0.62. Paired entry assessing the same source against MECH-143 is in targeted_review_connectome_mech_143, direction 'weakens'.
failure_signatures: Ventral anxiety-related neurons show minimal overlap with classical place cells, and the review reads this as the ventral hippocampus generalising across anxiogenic situations INDEPENDENTLY of their specific locations -- which is valence carried by a separate population, not valence embedded in map geometry.

The review cites recent work showing ventral populations maintain stable representations of a stimulus even when its associated valence is REVERSED, explicitly described as challenging the valence-centric view of ventral coding in favour of identity-and-salience coding.

Ventral valence effects are substantially carried by projection-defined pathways (lateral hypothalamus, medial prefrontal cortex, nucleus accumbens shell, basolateral amygdala) rather than by intrinsic map structure, so the locus of valence may be the output routing rather than the map.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the paper the SD-009/MECH-100 prose has been leaning on for its biological grounding, registered here for the first time against SD-009 and with a VERIFIED citation (the prose cited a non-existent 'Murray et al. 2004, TICS 8:56-61'; the MECH-100 record.json that did exist carried the right authors/year/venue but a wrong title, a wrong DOI and a PMID pointing at an unrelated hepatology paper -- see metadata_correction in that record and evidence/planning/sd009_murray_citation_and_mech100_currency_review_2026-08-09.md). On the substance: Murray, Bussey and Saksida argue that perirhinal cortex -- the apex of the ventral visual stream for object knowledge -- represents feature CONJUNCTIONS that support discrimination between objects sharing many features, and that this representational structure is shaped by discrimination demands rather than falling out of passive exposure to input statistics. That supports the general half of SD-009 (a world-state encoder needs a discriminative training pressure, not reconstruction alone) but NOT the specific half that SD-009 actually asserts -- that the pressure must be a DEDICATED event-type CE head. Confidence is set at 0.50, below the 0.62 the same paper carries against MECH-100, for two reasons that are specific to SD-009 rather than to the source: (1) SD-009 is a design decision naming one particular head, and this review speaks to the necessity of categorical discrimination pressure in general, which SD-070's own grounding heads already supply; (2) V3-EXQ-897 (2026-08-08) measured the marginal contribution of the dedicated event-CE head over SD-070's other grounding heads at null-to-negative on 3/3 seeds, so the literature and the experiment now bear on different granularities of the same claim and the literature should not be read as covering the gap.
failure_signatures: The review's argument is that perirhinal representations are shaped by DISCRIMINATION DEMANDS in general, not by a dedicated category-classification head in particular. If any discriminative training pressure suffices -- which is what SD-070's hazard/resource-presence and distance-bucket grounding heads already supply -- then this paper supports SD-070's recipe and says nothing in favour of SD-009's additional event-CE head.

The biological mechanism is experience-dependent plasticity across development and long-run task training in intact animals; SD-009 is an auxiliary cross-entropy head trained inside a short P0 phase. Alignment is conceptual, not mechanistic.

Perirhinal cortex sits at the ventral-stream/MTL boundary and carries mnemonic as well as perceptual function. If the correct biological analog of z_world is earlier ventral stream (V4/posterior IT), the mapping is mislocated -- the same caveat the MECH-100 entry records.

If z_world's event-type decodability under SD-070 turns out to be inherited from the static scene-structure targets rather than from any event-level pressure at all, the object-discrimination framing of this review would be the wrong biological frame for SD-009 specifically.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality primate single-unit recording (Cell 2021) and MECH-144's second founding citation. It is the strongest existing demonstration that hippocampal cognitive maps extend to value geometry: value place fields share four diagnostic properties with spatial place cells, so value is map-structured rather than tagged. Confidence set at 0.70, BELOW the Q-020 sibling's 0.78, because MECH-144 is specifically a claim about the VENTRAL compartment and this recording is primate hippocampus without a dorsal/ventral localisation -- the compartment specificity that makes this evidence fit MECH-144 is exactly what the paper does not establish. NOTE ON DIRECTION: this record is 'supports' while the sibling Q-020 record on the same paper is 'weakens'. Both are correct -- the paper weakens Q-020's ARC-007 'hippocampus is value-free' framing precisely BY supporting MECH-144. See the direction-sign note in evidence/planning/literature_claim_tag_audit.md.

Calcium imaging plus causal optogenetics in freely moving mice, top-tier venue. MECH-144 asserts that ventral CA1 contains spatially organized valence encoding; this paper is that claim's founding citation and demonstrates it directly -- vCA1 'anxiety cells' fire in proportion to proximity to anxiogenic space, the tuning is stable across sessions, and it is causally required for avoidance. Confidence carried over from the Q-020 sibling entry (0.72) rather than raised: the mouse-anxiety-to-agent-harm transfer risk that capped that estimate applies identically here. NOTE ON DIRECTION: this record is 'supports' while the sibling Q-020 record on the same paper is 'weakens'. That is not an inconsistency -- the paper weakens Q-020's ARC-007 'hippocampus is value-free' framing precisely BY supporting MECH-144's ventral-valence-encoding claim. See the direction-sign note in evidence/planning/literature_claim_tag_audit.md.

This is the strongest available empirical demonstration that separation and completion are performed by DIFFERENT STAGES on the SAME input, and it is the key entry for the SD-016 H2 (structured retrieval unit) leg rather than for H3. Its methodological strength is the simultaneity: recording DG and CA3 at once during a local-global cue conflict removes the usual confound of comparing separately-recorded populations under nominally-matched conditions, and it lets the authors show DG input to CA3 was severely disrupted WHILE CA3's own output stayed coherent. That is a within-animal, within-session dissociation, which is a much harder result to explain away than the region-by-region comparisons that preceded it. Confidence is held below the Espinoza entry for two reasons: the mapping to SD-016 is architectural-by-analogy (REE has no DG/CA3 stage separation to map onto, so the paper motivates BUILDING one rather than validating an existing design), and the double-rotation cue-conflict paradigm is a specific spatial-navigation manipulation whose relationship to REE's safe-vs-dangerous context distinction requires an inferential step the paper does not license directly.
failure_signatures: Separation and completion are ANTAGONISTIC operations, and the paper's framing is that CA3 arbitrates between them. A single-stage selection mechanism (SD-016's current design) has no place to put that arbitration and may be structurally incapable of achieving both -- pushing toward separation degrades retrieval of a stored association from a partial cue, and pushing toward completion collapses distinct contexts together. The uniform-selection saddle may be what 'maximum completion / zero separation' looks like from the outside.

CA3's behaviour depends on the RELATIVE STRENGTH of its internal attractor dynamics against its external inputs (Knierim & Neunuebel 2016 make this explicit). A retrieval unit with no recurrent/attractor component has no internal dynamics to weigh against input, so the separation-completion balance is not a parameter it possesses -- it is fixed implicitly by the architecture.

DG's pattern separation in this study is expressed via changes in FIRING RATE of place-modulated granule cells rather than by recruiting non-overlapping cell populations; Leutgeb et al. 2007 found the population-recruitment mechanism in CA3 but not DG. A REE design that assumes 'separation == disjoint slot selection' imports only one of the two biological mechanisms and may miss rate-coded separation entirely.

The result is obtained in a cue-CONFLICT paradigm (local and global reference frames placed in opposition), which is an unusually strong perturbation. It does not establish that the same separation/completion division operates under ordinary, non-conflicting input.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the single strongest biological reference for the SD-016 H3 (hard/competitive selection) leg, and it is unusually direct: it does not merely assert that the dentate gyrus performs winner-take-all selection, it measures the connectivity statistics that would be REQUIRED for a WTA circuit and shows the dentate gyrus has them while neocortex does not. 9098 tested connections across 270 slices via up to octuple simultaneous patch-clamp is exceptional methodological quality for a connectivity study. Mapping fidelity is high but not maximal: the paper establishes that the ARCHITECTURE affords WTA, not that WTA selection is observed in behaving animals, so the REE translation ('build the competitive operator into the circuit rather than hoping a downstream loss induces it') is licensed structurally rather than functionally. Transfer risk moderate-low: the finding is an architectural/statistical property of a microcircuit, which is the level REE is actually importing from, so the usual rodent-to-artificial-agent worry bites less than it would for a behavioural result. Weighted toward mapping_fidelity per the skill's guidance for architectural claims.
failure_signatures: Lateral inhibition dominance is a property of the DENTATE GYRUS specifically -- in neocortex, entorhinal cortex and presubiculum, recurrent inhibition is equally or more abundant than lateral inhibition, which the authors state 'would seem incompatible with efficient pattern separation'. So competitive selection is not a generic property of cortical circuits that REE can assume; it is a specialisation that must be deliberately built.

Recurrent inhibition (a unit inhibiting itself) is argued to be actively COUNTER-PRODUCTIVE for WTA because it suppresses potential winners. A naive REE implementation that applies an undifferentiated inhibition/normalisation term across all slots (including self-inhibition) may reproduce the failure mode rather than the fix.

Unitary GC->PV EPSPs (mean 1.79 mV) were measured in vivo to be insufficient to trigger a spike alone against a 10.3 mV threshold gap -- the competitive mechanism depends on SPATIAL SUMMATION across many converging units, so a competitive operator over too few slots (or with too weak convergence) may not engage at all.

Reciprocal GC-PV motifs were NOT significantly enriched, contrary to the neocortical prior the authors tested against. An REE design that imports 'the standard cortical E-I motif' would import the wrong statistics.
The recordings are in vitro slice at ~22 C in juvenile mice (P20-44); connection probabilities may differ in adult, awake, behaving conditions.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the most directly IMPLEMENTABLE reference in the pull: it is a spiking-network model that states the winner-take-all selection rule as an explicit, reproducible mechanism (per-cluster feedback inhibition, with survival determined by whether a unit's time-averaged excitatory:inhibitory conductance ratio exceeds a threshold), rather than describing WTA qualitatively. That makes it useful as a specification for the H3 operator in a way the electrophysiology papers are not. Confidence is held at 0.66 rather than higher for two independent reasons. First, source quality: Physical Review E is a solid physics venue but this is a modelling paper with no new empirical data, and it inherits rather than tests the WTA premise -- it explains HOW WTA arises given an assumed circuit, it does not establish THAT the dentate gyrus does WTA. Second, mapping fidelity: the model's competition is organised into lamellar clusters each with one basket cell, and the mechanism depends on conductance-based spiking dynamics with a meaningful time axis, none of which has a counterpart in SD-016's single-tick feedforward tagger over 16 slots. The value here is the ALGORITHMIC SKELETON (relative-drive competition against a shared inhibitory pool, thresholded, yielding sparse survival), which transfers; the biophysics does not.
failure_signatures: The WTA outcome in this model depends on a THRESHOLD on the E-I conductance ratio: units above R_th survive, all others go silent. A selection mechanism implemented with a soft/graded competition term but no effective thresholding non-linearity may reproduce the uniform-mixing outcome rather than sparse selection -- which is precisely the SD-016 418d/e/i failure signature (an auxiliary diversification loss on a plain softmax achieved population-level diversity without breaking the entropy ceiling).

Competition is LOCAL to a lamellar cluster (one basket cell per cluster), not global across the whole granule-cell population. A single global inhibition/normalisation term over all 16 SD-016 slots is a different architecture from the modelled one, and the paper gives no reason to expect it behaves equivalently.

The model reports that mossy-cell death and adult-born immature granule cells both perturb the WTA competition -- i.e. the sparse-selection regime is sensitive to the composition of the competing population, not robust to it. An REE slot array whose slots have heterogeneous or drifting effective gain may not sit in the WTA regime at all.
Sparsity in the model is ~5% activation of granule cells. Scaled to 16 slots this is below one slot, so the modelled operating regime does not straightforwardly instantiate at SD-016's slot count.

entries.confidence_rationale: Included deliberately as the entry that constrains how far the other four can be pushed, and it earns its place by changing a design recommendation rather than merely adding caution. It supports the pull's central thesis -- that pattern separation is produced by STRUCTURAL circuit properties rather than by a downstream objective -- while reassigning which structural property matters: the authors argue the primary mechanism is expansion into a higher-dimensional space with SPARSE CONNECTIVITY, and that sparse ACTIVITY and lateral inhibition are secondary contributors rather than the core. That directly qualifies the Espinoza/Kim reading and it bears on the SD-016 design, because SD-016's retrieval layer is dimensionality-REDUCING (z_world dim 32 -> 16 slots) whereas every biological circuit reviewed here is strongly expansive. Direction is 'mixed' rather than 'supports' because the paper simultaneously strengthens the H2 leg and undercuts a naive H3-only reading. Confidence 0.74 reflects a high-quality synthesis review in a top venue by authors with the relevant modelling expertise, discounted because it is argument and synthesis rather than new measurement, and because its cross-circuit comparative frame (cerebellum, mushroom body, DG) means not every conclusion is hippocampus-specific.
failure_signatures: The paper's central structural claim is EXPANSION with sparse connectivity: cerebellar granule layer, insect mushroom body and dentate gyrus all map inputs into a much LARGER population than the input layer. SD-016 does the opposite -- it maps a 32-dim z_world onto 16 slots, a contraction. If expansion is the primary mechanism, then no choice of selection operator over 16 slots recovers it, and both H3 and H2 as currently scoped may be attacking a secondary variable. This is the single most consequential finding in this pull for the portfolio's design.

The authors explicitly state that recent findings 'have questioned long-held ideas' about how these circuits perform pattern separation -- so the Marr-lineage framing that the V3-EXQ-898 autopsy used as its biological reference is itself contested, and should not be treated as settled ground truth.

Decorrelation and sparse activity are argued to be neither necessary nor sufficient for pattern separation in general; a design that optimises a decorrelation/divergence metric (which is close to what SD-016's C1b context-divergence instrument measures) may improve the metric without improving the downstream associative-learning function the separation is FOR.

The relevant benefit of pattern separation in the authors' framing is facilitating associative learning IN THE PRESENCE OF TRIAL-TO-TRIAL VARIABILITY. SD-016's acceptance criteria (C1 entropy, C1b context-divergence) measure representational properties, not learning facilitation under noise, so a pass on both could still leave the functional benefit undemonstrated.

entries.confidence_rationale: This entry exists to prevent the pull from being a one-sided case for the mechanism the V3-EXQ-898 autopsy already favoured, and it is the strongest available statement of the dissenting position: that the theoretical support and empirical evidence for the DG-as-pattern-separator theory 'are not strong', and that 'binding' of different types of incoming sensory information better captures the DG's contribution to memory encoding. Its direct relevance to SD-016 is sharp, because BINDING is arguably a better description of what SD-016's ContextMemory is actually for -- associating a context cue with hazard-relevant content -- than separation is. Confidence 0.61 rather than higher because this is a minority position argued in a review rather than demonstrated with new data, it predates the strongest connectivity evidence in this pull (Espinoza 2018) which materially strengthens the case it argues against, and the authors' positive alternative (binding) is specified far less precisely than the theory they criticise -- which limits how much design guidance it can actually supply. It is weighted here as a genuine and well-argued caution, not as a refutation.
failure_signatures: The core critique is that 'pattern separation' as used in the behavioural literature (discriminating similar contexts) and as defined computationally (orthogonalising overlapping input patterns) are DIFFERENT claims routinely conflated. SD-016's C1b context-divergence instrument measures the computational sense; the claim's actual functional motivation (vmPFC-like anticipatory hazard response) is behavioural. A pass on the computational instrument does not establish the behavioural function, and the two must not be reported as if they were one result.

If the DG's primary role is BINDING rather than separation, then engineering competitive/sparsifying dynamics into SD-016's retrieval could be actively counterproductive -- sparsification discards the conjunctive combination of inputs that binding requires. The H3 leg would then be expected to produce low entropy AND degraded downstream terrain/action performance, which is a specific, falsifiable prediction worth instrumenting for rather than a vague caution.

The authors conclude the empirical evidence for pattern separation is 'not strong', which means the biological-reference triage in the V3-EXQ-898 autopsy rests on a contested rather than settled literature. The autopsy's framing of the REE tagger as a 'formal-definition import' of pattern separation may therefore be importing a definition whose biological reality is itself disputed.

Much of the behavioural evidence for DG pattern separation comes from adult-neurogenesis manipulations, which have effects on excitability, network sparsity and mood-related behaviour beyond any separation-specific role -- so the causal attribution to separation specifically is weaker than the literature's confident vocabulary suggests.

Canonical, highly-cited (Nature, single-unit hippocampal recording) direct demonstration that hippocampal place-cell sequences encode prospective trajectories toward remembered goals -- the foundational empirical result the 2026 theta-sweep papers extend. Moderate transfer risk: rat, physical-space navigation, not abstract goal-directed cognition (REE's actual claim domain).
failure_signatures: The paper's own framing is limited to 'replay'-class sequence events in an open arena with learned reward locations -- it does not test whether the same mechanism operates for non-spatial or abstract goal structures, which is the generalisation MECH-236/MECH-289 (and the 2026-08-08 REE thought that prompted this pull) actually need.

entries.confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed Nature Neuroscience paper with a dissociation-design task (Honeycomb maze) that specifically rules out the confound of movement/heading direction, directly targeting whether goal-direction coding is a genuinely relational signal rather than a motor correlate -- exactly the property MECH-236's z_goal-conditioning premise needs to be true. Confidence held below 0.8 because full text (statistics, effect sizes) was not accessible (Nature paywalled, bioRxiv blocked WebFetch with HTTP 403); assessment is based on the verified verbatim abstract only, not the complete methods/results.
failure_signatures: This is the medicalxpress-reported prompting evidence's primary source, and its own abstract is explicit that the goal-directedness of theta sweeps was, prior to this paper, 'unresolved' -- i.e. the field itself did not consider this settled until this and the companion Tang et al. paper. See also the skeptical commentary entry (schmidt2026) in this same directory, which frames the two 2026 papers as first steps toward resolving an active controversy, not a closed question.

failure_signatures: Full text inaccessible (Nature paywall; no PMC/bioRxiv mirror found for a commentary/News & Views piece, which typically are not deposited as preprints). Cannot rule out that this commentary's skepticism is narrowly scoped to a specific claim in Yu et al./Tang et al. entries.confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed Nature Neuroscience paper, large-scale recordings, with a stated circuit mechanism (CA1 egocentric-goal-direction subpopulation + reduced feedback inhibition) and an explicit link between the online (theta) and offline (SWR) generative modes MECH-289 already distinguishes -- directly on-target for MECH-289's claim that the same generative hippocampal substrate operates in both modes. Full text accessed via PMC mirror (preprint), giving more confidence than an abstract-only read; the peer-reviewed Nature Neuroscience version was not independently checked for changes from the preprint.
failure_signatures: This is a preprint-derived summary (PMC12407861 mirrors the bioRxiv version, DOI 10.1101/2025.08.26.672489); the published Nature Neuroscience version (DOI 10.1038/s41593-026-02364-3) may differ in details not captured here.

Learning-dependence is explicitly part of the finding (goal-directed sweeps are described as learning-dependent, distinct from a stereotypic left-right alternating sweep type) -- this paper does not claim ALL theta sweeps are goal-directed, only a learned subpopulation, a distinction REE's claims should not flatten.

entries.confidence_rationale: High mapping fidelity on the anatomical/functional gate claim (this is IL specifically, not a PFC subregion analog, with a clean causal manipulation and a directly comparable freeze-suppression readout) -- but the paper's central learning-trajectory finding directly contradicts the piece of MECH-357 that carries its falsifiability (suppression must scale with LEARNED efficacy, not an early, non-scaling signal). Confidence reflects strong evidence on a genuinely mixed verdict, not weak evidence.
failure_signatures: IL PV movement-related activity during avoidance emerged tens of trials before animals had learned the avoidance response, immediately after a single shock exposure.

IL PV activity during the avoidance movement was not attenuated (or otherwise changed) by further learning (p=0.8886, one-way ANOVA) -- i.e. it did not scale with an accruing avoidance-efficacy signal.

Optogenetic suppression of IL PV neurons delayed avoidance latency and increased freezing duration during the tone -- freeze suppression is genuinely causal, not merely correlational, going the other direction from the failure signature above.

entries.confidence_rationale: Supports the general architectural principle MECH-357 depends on (an inhibitory prefrontal signal, not excitatory drive, gates avoidance) with a large, well-controlled rat dataset -- but the effect is localized to PRELIMBIC cortex, not infralimbic, which is the specific region MECH-357 names its analog after. Confidence held at moderate: strong internal evidence, weaker claim-specific mapping.
failure_signatures: Rats with pharmacological inactivation spreading into infralimbic cortex were explicitly excluded from the dataset (n=3) rather than analyzed as a separate infralimbic condition -- this study cannot itself confirm or rule out an IL-specific effect distinct from the PL effect it reports.

Optogenetic silencing of PL glutamatergic (excitatory) neurons did NOT impair avoidance, only silencing tied to the inhibitory tone-responsive subpopulation and its artificial reactivation did -- so a naive 'more PL activity = more suppression' framing is wrong even within PL itself.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly supports the claim's central architectural bet (a ventromedial-PFC-sourced projection suppresses freezing specifically as a consequence of avoidance being learned, not tonically) with three convergent chemogenetic/pharmacological experiments. Confidence held below 0.7 because the projection target (nucleus reuniens, a thalamic relay) has no REE analogue and the paper does not directly measure the suppression signal's magnitude growing WITH training -- it infers training-dependence from a post-training-only test design plus cited prior work, rather than from a within-subject trajectory.

This is a causal double dissociation (not merely correlational): selective erasure of plasticity in an ACC-to-retrosplenial-cortex pathway altered whether behaviour transitioned to habit without changing execution level, while selective erasure of plasticity in a lateral-OFC-to-central-striatum pathway altered execution level without changing the decision-strategy transition. That is close to a direct biological analogue of MECH-480's central claim -- that 'whether a policy retains behavioural-adjustment authority' and 'how strongly a persisting policy is expressed' are separably implemented. Confidence is capped below the source-quality/mapping-fidelity average because full-text Methods/Results (exact plasticity-erasure technique, sample sizes, effect sizes, statistical tests) were not accessible -- nature.com redirected to an authentication gate and the bioRxiv HTML returned 403 Forbidden. This entry is built from the verified bioRxiv API abstract plus three independent institutional/press accounts (Kyoto University research news, EurekAlert, Neuroscience News), all of which agree on the circuit-level claim and the mouse two-stage-training paradigm but none of which report inferential statistics. A future session with journal access should re-verify against the primary Methods/Results before this entry is used to argue for anything beyond the qualitative dissociation.
failure_signatures: The abstract itself flags a puzzle this paper exists to resolve, not a limitation of its answer: habit execution level (frequency/duration) is described as 'superficially maintained despite a decline in motivational drive' during the strategy shift -- i.e. before this paper's manipulations, execution and strategy looked coupled on the surface, and the dissociation only becomes visible once each pathway's plasticity is erased independently. A reader taking only the surface behavioural trajectory (without the causal manipulation) would see execution and strategy change together and could wrongly conclude they are not separable -- this is exactly the confound MECH-480's own falsifier warns against (see what_would_answer's NON-DEGENERACY guard on floor/ceiling artifacts).

The secondary sources (Kyoto University press release, EurekAlert) explicitly decline to name the plasticity-erasure technique (optogenetic vs. chemogenetic vs. pharmacological) or report sample sizes/statistics -- this record cannot independently confirm the manipulation was single-cell-type-specific, reversible, or free of off-target circuit effects, all of which bear on how directly the paper's causal claim should be trusted.

The paper title and framing ('global remapping', 'network reset') sound directly on-topic for a decision-time attractor claim, and this is exactly why it is important: on close reading, the remapping is inferred entirely from immediate-early-gene expression compared across two 5-minute exposures separated by 20 minutes, not from any within-exploration/real-time readout. The authors themselves state their method cannot detect whether a population-code switch happens within seconds during ongoing exploration. This directly weakens the assumption that 'global remapping' literature licenses a decision-time attractor-width metric.
failure_signatures: Remapping is detected via catFISH immediate-early-gene (Arc/Zif268) compartmentalization comparing TWO separated 5-minute exposures 20 minutes apart, not via real-time recording during a single exploration bout

Authors explicitly state: 'rate remapping, place field rotation, or place field splitting occurring with novelty would not be detected as a loss of network overlap' -- their own technique cannot resolve within-session dynamics

The manipulation is pharmacological (glutamate microinfusion into LC) delivered over a 30-second infusion period, itself far longer than a single decision, with a further 60-second dwell before behavior begins
No optogenetic or electrophysiological demonstration exists in this paper of a remapping event occurring within seconds of phasic LC firing during ongoing behavior

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong optogenetic causal evidence that LC input to CA3 is functionally important -- but the readout is explicitly encoding-then-next-day-retention, not a within-trial/decision-time attractor measure. Directly weakens the decision-time operationalization of MECH-075's dorsal leg by demonstrating that the field's own gold-standard LC-CA3 causal study measures its effect via delayed behavioral retention, not immediate representational geometry.
failure_signatures: Optogenetic silencing of LC input to CA3 during the day-1 novel-context exposure impairs day-2 recognition memory -- the causal window is at encoding, but the READOUT requires a 24-hour retention interval
Silencing LC input to CA3 during the day-2 recall test itself has no effect -- the LC-CA3 pathway is not needed for retrieval/decision-time performance, only for what gets encoded

The mechanism is explicitly framed as 'plastic changes in the CA3 microcircuit' (i.e. synaptic plasticity), with place-field similarity across days as the geometric readout, not basin width within a single exploration bout
No measurement anywhere in the paper of attractor basin width, convergence speed, or any within-session/within-decision geometric quantity

entries.confidence_rationale: Foundational, extremely well-replicated review establishing that phasic LC firing IS decision-locked (~90-150ms latency around a discrimination/target-detection decision, brief 3-4-spike bursts) and is proposed to modulate downstream target-neuron gain at that same short timescale -- this licenses 'decision-time LC effects' as a real phenomenon in principle. Confidence held at moderate rather than high because the entire empirical base for the theory is cortical/decision-network gain modulation (LIP, cingulate, sensory cortex target-detection), not hippocampal attractor dynamics -- it establishes plausibility, not applicability to MECH-075's specific dorsal-HPC operationalization.
failure_signatures: Phasic LC excitatory responses to target cues occur at short latency (~90-150ms) and consist of only 3-4 action potentials followed by a long refractory period -- the effect window per burst is brief, not sustained
The theory's evidentiary base is cortical target-detection and decision-network gain (LIP, ACC, OFC afferents to LC), not hippocampal attractor geometry
Tonic vs phasic LC modes map onto exploration vs exploitation over a task, not onto within-single-decision attractor width

entries.confidence_rationale: The single most directly on-target paper found in this review: it explicitly frames real-time CA1 population dynamics under measured NE release in attractor language ('NE perturbed neural activity away from the stored attractor'). This is genuine, current, within-session evidence that NE tracks hippocampal representational dynamics during ongoing behavior -- but the reported timescale is minutes (exponential decay of both NE signal and representational drift over ~10 minutes), one to two orders of magnitude slower than a single CEM decision step. Confidence held at moderate because it is a reviewed preprint (not yet a final version-of-record) and because the direct attractor-basin-width vs. decision-time question is still not tested at the sub-minute scale.
failure_signatures: NE signal (GRAB-NE fiber photometry) rises sharply at a context-transition event boundary and then exponentially DECAYS TO BASELINE OVER MINUTES, not seconds

CA1 population representational drift away from the steady-state code tracks the same minutes-scale decay as the NE signal -- 'the patterns recorded in the first minute were less correlated than those observed 10 minutes into the session'

The authors did not find enhanced replay of post-transition moments -- the expected plasticity/consolidation signature was absent, leaving the mechanism as an online attractor perturbation rather than a memory-consolidation effect, but still on a multi-minute timescale
No claim or measurement anywhere in the paper of a sub-second or single-decision-step attractor transition

entries.confidence_rationale: A computational modeling paper, grounded in prior electrophysiology, that explicitly and deliberately codes noradrenaline's action on CA3 ensemble formation as a plasticity-ENABLING (STDP-gating) factor only -- with no online/moment-to-moment modulation of cellular excitability or recurrent synaptic weight, in direct contrast to how the same model treats acetylcholine. This is current computational-modeling consensus that directly supports reading a null within-decision noradrenergic basin_width effect as consistent with, rather than contradicting, how the field currently models NE's action on CA3 attractor circuits.
failure_signatures: The model explicitly states noradrenaline 'was assumed to enable synaptic plasticity between CA3 pyramidal cells and therefore ensemble formation but did not otherwise affect CA3 network properties' -- no online effect on excitability, recurrent weight, or inhibition beyond a fixed ~30% IPSC reduction

Acetylcholine, by contrast, is modeled with an immediate ~5mV depolarization and instantaneous reduction of recurrent CA3-CA3 synaptic weight -- i.e. the SAME modeling framework gives ACh a fast/online channel and gives NE none

Noradrenaline narrows (not widens) the burst-frequency window in which ensembles can stably form (ensembles form at 30Hz but are 'almost completely abolished' at 20Hz under NA alone) -- a plasticity-permissiveness effect, not a basin-widening gain effect

No receptor-kinetics or phasic/tonic timescale distinction is modeled for noradrenaline at all -- the paper's own silence on NE timescale reflects that the modeling literature has not yet needed to resolve it

This is the strongest available direct precedent for MECH-490's specific mechanistic distinction (execution FLUENCY of an already-formed sequence, not chunk formation itself) and for its REM-vs-SWS question. It reports a formation/concatenation dissociation -- chunks form during acquisition in both age groups, but only young adults show sleep-dependent SPEEDING of the slowest (between-chunk) transitions, i.e. more persistent, less-interrupted execution of the already-learned sequence -- and ties that concatenation gain specifically to nREM2 sigma power (spindles), not REM. Held below 0.8 because the measured construct is transition SPEED at fixed accuracy, not a direct read of decision/re-evaluation frequency, and the design is correlational (EEG-behavior correlation within a sleep-vs-wake groups design), not a causal REM/SWS deprivation manipulation.
failure_signatures: The paper measures movement-transition SPEED (relative Element Movement Time) at chunk boundaries, not an explicit per-tick re-decision or re-planning rate -- mapping this onto E3Selector's commit-variance/re-scoring frequency is an inference, not a direct read-out of the same variable.

Older adults showing 'no significant sleep-dependent improvement' in concatenation is explained post hoc as reduced nREM2 sigma power with age -- an association, not a manipulation, so the sigma-power-drives-concatenation causal claim rests on correlation within a small sample stratified by age.

This is a human finger/arm-sequence paradigm with a fixed, externally-imposed action sequence (a keypress or pegboard order) learned via massed practice -- structurally different from Fishtank's continuously re-planned, environment-conditioned action sequence, where 'the sequence' is generated online by CEM/softmax rather than rote-learned once.

entries.confidence_rationale: Independent corroboration (different sequence type -- gross arm movements on a 15-element pegboard, not finger keypresses) of the same formation-vs-fluency dissociation as the Bottary companion entry, with sleep specifically implicated (gains present after a night of sleep, absent after equivalent waking retention) -- but this paper does not report sleep-stage EEG data at all, so it cannot independently speak to the REM-vs-SWS question. Confidence set lower than the Bottary entry for that reason and for a smaller, non-age-stratified sample.
failure_signatures: No polysomnography or sleep-stage breakdown is reported in this paper -- the sleep-vs-wake comparison establishes that sleep (of unspecified composition) matters, but says nothing about which stage, so it cannot independently discriminate the REM-vs-SWS question MECH-490's depends_on (MECH-204) raises.

The reanalysis is of Malangre et al. (2014)'s original dataset restricted to element-level movement times -- a secondary, exploratory analysis on an already-collected small sample (n=24, two groups of 12), not a study purpose-designed to test the concatenation hypothesis with adequate power.

As with the Bottary entry, this is a rote, once-learned, externally-specified motor sequence (a fixed pegboard order practiced to criterion), not an online-replanned action sequence in a changing task environment -- the same structural transfer risk to Fishtank applies.

entries.confidence_rationale: Included as evidence for a PRECONDITION of MECH-490, not for the sleep-link claim itself: it establishes that a variance/threshold-gated commitment architecture -- evidence accumulates, is smoothed, and only releases motor execution once a gate threshold is crossed, after which the motor system commits and stops re-accumulating fresh evidence for that action -- is an empirically supported human decision-motor mechanism, closely analogous in structure to E3Selector's commit_variance/threshold gate. Marked evidence_direction 'unknown' rather than 'supports' because the paper contains no sleep, consolidation, or offline-processing content whatsoever and therefore cannot speak to whether sleep modulates gate persistence -- it only speaks to whether the gate architecture itself is neurally real.
failure_signatures: Zero sleep, consolidation, or time-of-day content in this paper -- it is a same-session, single-timepoint decision-making study (motion perception, numerical cognition, recognition memory, lexical knowledge tasks with EMG), so it provides NO evidence, direction, or otherwise, about whether sleep changes the gate threshold or the persistence of a committed state. Citing it as support for the sleep-link half of MECH-490 would overstate what it shows.

The four tasks tested are single discrete perceptual/cognitive decisions with one motor response each, not a multi-step action SEQUENCE with an open-loop execution period -- the paper's 'gate' releases one motor act, not a run of several ticks executed without re-scoring, so the analogy to E3Selector's sequence-level commitment is structural, not a direct empirical match.

The paper does not identify what determines gate-threshold PERSISTENCE or how it might change over time (practice, fatigue, or otherwise) -- it characterises the gate's existence and its role in RT/EMG dynamics within a session, not what modulates its stability across sessions, which is exactly the open question MECH-490 poses for sleep specifically.

entries.confidence_rationale: The foundational, most-cited paper establishing that sleep -- specifically the amount of stage-2 NREM late in the night -- drives overnight motor sequence gains that equivalent wake time does not. Included as the canonical anchor the later chunk-concatenation work refines, and as independent, large-effect, well-replicated confirmation of the NREM2-not-REM stage attribution. Held at moderate rather than high confidence because it measures whole-sequence speed and accuracy (a coarser index than the later chunk-transition-specific work) and does not itself distinguish chunk formation from execution fluency -- that refinement came from the later papers, not this one.
failure_signatures: The outcome measure is overall sequence typing speed and accuracy, not a transition-level or chunk-level breakdown -- this paper alone cannot distinguish 'sleep formed better chunks' from 'sleep made execution of the same chunks more fluent,' the exact distinction MECH-490 needs; that separation is only available from the later Bottary/Blischke work.

A finger-keypress sequence task, learned to criterion via massed practice in a single session, then retested after one night -- a much shorter and simpler learning/consolidation window than a Fishtank agent's ongoing, environment-conditioned replanning.

Some later studies (e.g. Rickard et al. 2008, cited widely as a partial non-replication for probabilistic sequence learning) found sleep benefits were smaller or absent for less deterministic sequence structures -- this paper's finding is robust for a fixed, deterministic sequence but should not be over-generalised to all motor-sequence learning without qualification.

Directly and rigorously supports the source thought's 'variability must not automatically be classified as noise' section: mice in a task with a fully deterministic reward structure nonetheless actively generated increasing choice variability, converging on a randomness LEVEL that maximized reward under uncertainty about the true rule, rather than following a fixed-sequence strategy that a naive optimality analysis would predict. The study additionally provides a worked example of GOV-BEHADJ-1's 'Perturb' step done well: a discriminating behavioral-switch test distinguishes the randomness-strategy explanation from a memorized-sequence explanation. High confidence given the rigor of the design, though mapping fidelity to REE's richer spatial/naturalistic Fishtank environment is only moderate.

This is the strongest modern, peer-reviewed, controlled replication of the Clever Hans effect in a working-animal paradigm, and it is directly on-point for the source thought's 'Blind' workflow step: it shows human belief about a condition contaminates the interpretation of animal behavioral output even when the animal's actual behavior is unaffected by the (absent) target stimulus. It both supports the thought's instinct that blinding matters AND complicates the specific proposed implementation, because the contamination here occurred in a live, in-the-loop human-animal interaction, not in after-the-fact scoring of pre-recorded trajectories -- a distinction the source thought's 'Blind' step (hide condition labels during scoring) does not fully address. Confidence held at 0.55 because REE's Fishtank trajectories are generated by a fixed environment/policy with no live human 'handler' present during generation, so the closest REE analogue is the human researcher's own visual impression-formation, a narrower target than the paper's live-interaction paradigm.
failure_signatures: Handlers were falsely told scent-target markers were present at certain search locations. Across 164 search trials with NO drug or explosive scent actually present anywhere, handlers reported 225 dog alerts, disproportionately at the falsely marked locations -- human belief manufactured the appearance of correct animal behavioral output where none of the eliciting stimulus existed.

Human influence on alert location outweighed dog-directed decoy influence (food/toy placed to independently attract the dog) in the same design, showing the contamination pathway ran primarily through the human interpreter/handler, not through the animal's own behavior -- i.e. blinding the SCORER after the fact would not have caught this, because the bias entered during data GENERATION via the handler's real-time interpretation and cuing, not during a separate post-hoc analysis step.

entries.confidence_rationale: Comprehensive, authoritative review by leading movement-ecology statisticians of hidden Markov models (HMMs) as the field's standard rigorous tool for inferring latent behavioral states from tracking/movement data -- directly on-point for the source thought's informal state-transition language (refuge/explore/food-seeking states) and its request for 'validated measures of sequence structure.' Rated mixed rather than purely supports because the paper is equally explicit about documented failure modes in exactly this class of method, which speak directly to the anti-Goodharting risk GOV-BEHADJ-1 raises for hand-picked metrics -- the same risk recurs, in a different form, in model-based state discovery. High confidence given the source's authority and very close conceptual match to the claim's subject matter.
failure_signatures: 'The decision of the appropriate number of states can be challenging; there is again no foolproof or automatic way to determine this' -- state-count selection in HMM-based behavioral segmentation is a documented open problem, not a solved one, directly analogous to the metric-choice Goodharting risk the source thought raises.

When the transition matrix is fully free-parameterized, 'the characteristics of the model states as represented by the state-dependent distributions are fully data driven, and hence may not correspond exactly to biologically meaningful entities' -- i.e. an unsupervised or semi-supervised discovery pass can output statistically coherent 'states' that are model artifacts rather than real behavioral categories, a known failure mode in behavioural classification directly requested by the source thought's literature-mining instructions.

'Coarse-graining could result in masking or misclassification of meaningfully distinct states' when approximating a continuous behavioral space with too few discrete states -- and conditional-independence violations (observation at time t depending on the observation at t-1, not just the hidden state at t) can further confound behavioral inference if unaddressed.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is a landmark, rigorously designed multi-site replication (identical apparatus/protocol/environmental controls, 3 labs, several inbred strains + 1 null mutant, 6 behaviors tested simultaneously) that directly supplies the exact historical precedent the source thought's own 'literature mining' section asked for: an apparently genuine, well-measured behavioral effect (strain-driven genotype differences) that turned out to be idiosyncratic to testing context despite maximal standardization. Held to 0.65 rather than higher because the mapping from a physical wet-lab confound to REE's computational substrate is real but indirect (see mapping_caveat) -- it establishes the CLASS of failure (protocol standardization is necessary but not sufficient to rule out context-dependence), not a REE-specific instance.
failure_signatures: Despite apparatus, protocols, and 'many environmental variables' being rigorously equated across 3 laboratories, strain-by-lab interactions were still detected: 'for some tests, the magnitude of genetic differences depended upon the specific testing lab' -- i.e. a behavioral effect that looked like a clean genotype effect was in fact partly an artifact of unmeasured context.

The authors' own conclusion is a direct caution against the source thought's implicit assumption that sufficiently rigorous perturbation/replication protocols will fully discriminate genuine organisation from artifact: 'experiments characterizing mutants may yield results that are idiosyncratic to a particular laboratory' even when the experimenters believed they had controlled for context.

entries.confidence_rationale: A widely-cited open-science methods paper that formalizes, within an established psychometric construct-validity framework, precisely the anti-Goodharting concern GOV-BEHADJ-1's source thought raises informally about behavioral metrics ('a behavioural metric should generally remain an indicator, not an ontology'). It names 'questionable measurement practices' (QMPs) as a distinct category alongside the better-known questionable RESEARCH practices, and supplies a structured set of transparency questions about construct definition and operationalization that a REE behavioural-adjudication skill's Measure step could adopt close to as-is. Confidence held moderate (0.55) because the paper's full text sits behind a publisher paywall and could not be directly verified beyond abstract-level and secondary-source description, and because its own domain (self-report psychometric instruments) maps only loosely onto REE's computational behavioral metrics.

A highly-cited, formal statistical methodology directly answering the source thought's 'statistical methods for multi-metric adjudication' request: rather than picking one analysis pipeline and reporting its result, multiverse analysis runs the SAME question through every reasonable combination of data-processing/analytic choices and reports how conclusions vary across that space. This gives GOV-BEHADJ-1's 'Adjudicate' step ('judge the pattern of evidence across measures... rather than allowing one metric to define the phenomenon') a concrete, established, off-the-shelf statistical instantiation rather than leaving it as a qualitative aspiration. Confidence held at 0.65 because the paper's own domain (survey/questionnaire data processing choices) differs from REE's (trajectory-metric definitional choices), though the underlying logic transfers cleanly.

The highest-fidelity mapping among all entries in this pull: both this paper and REE's Fishtank work are deep RL agents whose apparent behavioral competence needs to be checked against held-out, procedurally varied environments to distinguish a general strategy from memorization of training-distribution specifics. The paper both SUPPORTS the source thought's 'Generalise' step (it is a rigorous, quantitative, established precedent for exactly that kind of test) and DIRECTLY COMPLICATES the specific Fishtank observations that motivated GOV-BEHADJ-1 (post-sleep trajectories 'looking smoother' within the same small set of training-distribution runs is exactly the observational signature this paper shows can be pure memorization, undetectable without a generalization test). High confidence given the very close structural match.
failure_signatures: Deep RL agents evaluated only within their training distribution (the same small set of levels/seeds used during training) can show high, apparently competent performance while dramatically failing to generalize to held-out, structurally similar but previously unseen levels -- the CoinRun benchmark quantifies substantial train-test performance gaps that are invisible unless a genuinely novel, procedurally varied test set is used.

Standard RL evaluation practice (reporting performance on the training distribution, or on a small fixed set of episodes/seeds) 'masks substantial overfitting' -- an agent can appear to have learned a general strategy when it has in fact memorized specifics of the limited environment set it was trained and evaluated on.

entries.confidence_rationale: A methods tutorial proposing parametric survival models (hazard/frailty models) as a more flexible, statistically validated alternative to simple Markov-chain transition-probability analysis for behavioral sequence data -- directly answering the source thought's request for 'validated measures of sequence structure' and 'experimental designs more rigorous than those suggested here.' Rated mixed because the paper's own motivation is an implicit critique of the informal transition-counting approach the source thought's language (refuge->explore->refuge->explore) most naturally suggests: first-order Markov transition-probability description assumes memorylessness, an assumption the tutorial's own framing treats as often unrealistic for real behavioral sequences. Confidence moderate given the source is a specialist-journal tutorial rather than a widely-cited landmark, and full text could not be directly verified (paywalled; based on abstract/secondary sources).
failure_signatures: The tutorial's own motivating critique is that standard sequential analysis of behavior has been underused in part because simple Markov-chain description assumes the transition probability from the current state depends only on the current state (memorylessness) -- an assumption that is frequently unrealistic for behavior organized in longer chains or context-dependent sequences, meaning naive transition-probability counting (the implicit default suggested by the source thought's refuge/explore/food-seeking transition language) can misrepresent real sequential structure that has longer-range dependence.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the foundational paper for Motion Sequencing (MoSeq), a formal, rigorous, widely-adopted generative-model approach to exactly the 'discovery-oriented analysis' the source thought gestures at informally. It demonstrates that a real, established, statistically principled method exists for decomposing continuous behavior into a reusable vocabulary of stereotyped modules with defined transition probabilities -- direct confirmation that the thought's aspiration (motifs/states/transitions rather than aggregate totals) is not merely plausible but already has a mature methodological answer in computational ethology. Confidence held at 0.7 rather than higher because REE's environment (2D/discrete grid navigation) differs substantially from MoSeq's domain (3D depth-video pose dynamics in an open field), so the specific modeling machinery would need substantial adaptation, not direct reuse.
failure_signatures: MoSeq's own methodology requires selecting a model-order hyperparameter (the number of distinct behavioral syllables/states), which has no single objectively correct value -- illustrating that even a rigorous, formal, unsupervised discovery method does not eliminate researcher degrees of freedom, it relocates them from ad hoc metric choice to model-order/hyperparameter choice, a caution directly relevant to how GOV-BEHADJ-1's 'Discover' step would need its own explicit anti-Goodharting safeguards if implemented with an analogous generative model.
