Human psychophysiology with two convergent and mechanistically distinct indices (startle potentiation for defensive activation, fear bradycardia for attentive orienting), which were positively correlated with one another -- that convergence is what makes the 'immobility is an ATTENTIVE state' reading solid rather than inferential. Supports MECH-489's claim structure directly: the claim asserts freeze-arrest coupled to an orient/identify step, and this is evidence that biological defensive immobility is exactly such a coupled state rather than pure motor arrest. Mapping fidelity is good because the claim-level assertion (freeze co-occurs with active monitoring) is what was measured. Held at 0.72 rather than higher because the paradigm is conditioned distal threat in a laboratory, and because the study indexes attention physiologically rather than demonstrating that information is actually acquired and used.
failure_signatures: An implementation in which the arrest state performs no sensory-sampling change, no active localisation and no belief update is not modelling attentive immobility -- it is modelling the motor-arrest half of a state whose defining property in the biology is that motor arrest and heightened sensory intake occur TOGETHER.

If the arrest is genuinely attentive, the organism's defensive sensitivity should be ELEVATED during immobility rather than merely held constant; a substrate whose arrest is a pure no-op predicts no such elevation.

entries.confidence_rationale: Authoritative synthesis in a top venue proposing that the central amygdala uses mutually inhibitory, winner-takes-all circuits to switch between discrete defensive modes organised along threat imminence. Supports two structural commitments MECH-489 makes: that post-arrest action selection is a selection among mutually exclusive defensive modes (approach / withdraw / resume) rather than a continuous adjustment, and that phasic and chronic defensive states are architecturally distinct (the MECH-489 vs MECH-279 boundary). Confidence is 0.70 rather than higher because this is a review/perspective rather than a single decisive experiment, and because the organising variable it proposes -- threat imminence, learned through association -- is not the variable MECH-489 gates on.
failure_signatures: If defensive modes are selected by mutually inhibitory winner-takes-all competition, a decision layer that resolves to the same mode on every single override event is not exhibiting selection at all -- a winner-takes-all circuit with a structurally biased input produces exactly that degenerate signature.

Defensive mode is organised by threat imminence and prior association; a mechanism that gates only on instantaneous onset magnitude has no representation of imminence and so cannot reproduce the mode ordering the biology shows.

entries.confidence_rationale: Very strong source (Neuron, circuit dissection with identified parallel superior colliculus to basolateral amygdala routes, plus a behavioural-phenotype split). Direction is mixed and the reasoning matters: it SUPPORTS MECH-489's assertion that defensive-response termination is a governed process rather than a fixed schedule -- habituation here is an active, circuit-mediated, arousal-modulated computation with stable individual differences, not stimulus-response fatigue -- while simultaneously indicating that the governing variable is AROUSAL STATE rather than epistemic resolution, which is not what MECH-489's 'epistemic-sufficiency override' asserts. Confidence held to 0.58 by the binding mapping problem: this is habituation ACROSS repeated stimulus presentations, whereas MECH-489's release is WITHIN a single arrest episode. Those are different timescales and the paper does not bridge them.
failure_signatures: Response decrement that is governed by arousal state and shows stable individual differences cannot be reproduced by a fixed decay constant applied uniformly -- a substrate whose release is a pure signal-decay timer predicts no between-individual variation in habituation rate and no arousal dependence, both of which are observed.
Two animals receiving identical stimulus sequences diverge into persistent-escape and rapid-habituation phenotypes, so the decrement cannot be a function of the stimulus history alone.

entries.confidence_rationale: Review of human motor defensive reactions to violence-related threat using stabilometry, distinguishing three distinct immobility types within a defensive cascade, of which attentive immobility is one and peritraumatic tonic immobility -- strongly associated with PTSD severity -- is another. Supports MECH-489's registered boundary against MECH-279 with human data, which is a different and complementary line of support from the rodent circuit work in this directory. Confidence 0.68: the taxonomic distinction is well established and the human-clinical grounding is genuinely valuable for a claim about a PAG-subject mechanism, but the paper is a review, the stabilometry evidence base is comparatively small, and the immobility types are distinguished largely descriptively rather than by dissociating mechanism.
failure_signatures: Collapsing distinct immobility types into a single freeze mechanism loses the clinically load-bearing distinction between an attentive, reversible, orienting immobility and a tonic, unresponsive peritraumatic immobility that predicts PTSD severity -- these have different triggers, different durations and different outcomes.
A phasic arrest whose duration is governed only by decay of the eliciting signal has no way to represent the transition into tonic immobility, which is not a longer version of the same state.

entries.confidence_rationale: High source quality -- Current Biology, cell-type-specific (Kcnip2+) ablation AND selective optogenetic activation, i.e. both necessity and sufficiency for the behaviour, with recordings showing the cells encode looming size. The direction is genuinely mixed rather than a clean weakens because MECH-489's trigger is stated as a DISJUNCTION: unsigned prediction-error surprise OR sensory-discriminative harm. This paper weakens the first disjunct and supports the second. Confidence is held at 0.62 rather than higher because mapping fidelity is the binding constraint: REE has no retina and no visual looming feature, so the transfer is at the level of channel ARCHITECTURE (dedicated feature-specific line vs generic magnitude signal), not of the specific detector.
failure_signatures: A defensive-orienting trigger built on a generic, modality-agnostic surprise magnitude will under-fire on ethologically specific threat events, because the biological system does not route those events through a generic salience channel at all -- it routes them through a dedicated feature-tuned line that is separable from novelty.

Ablating the dedicated channel abolishes the defensive response even though generic visual novelty and stimulus change remain intact, showing the two signals are dissociable and that novelty alone is not sufficient to elicit the response.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly evidences the PREMISE MECH-151 inherits from MECH-150 -- that a frontal region computes a compact label for the current task state, including unobservable components held in working memory, and that this label is consumed by learning and decision machinery ELSEWHERE in the brain. That 'consumed elsewhere' clause is the projection premise MECH-151 builds on. It is not evidence for the action_bias projection specifically, so mapping fidelity for MECH-151 proper is moderate and the confidence reflects that rather than any weakness in the paper.
failure_signatures: If the frontal state abstraction were consumed only locally -- used within OFC for valuation and never exported -- then MECH-151's premise that a cue-indexed context vector is broadcast to downstream action machinery would lose its biological warrant, and the E1 -> action_bias projection would be an engineering choice with no analogue rather than a modelled one.

Wilson et al. require the state label to include UNOBSERVABLE task components (working-memory contents), not just current sensory input. A cue_context vector computed purely from present sensory features would be a strictly weaker object than the one this theory describes, and would fail on exactly the partially-observable tasks the theory was built to explain.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily-replicated architectural proposal whose insertion point for top-down influence is close to one-to-one with MECH-151's. Cisek argues that several potential actions are specified in PARALLEL in fronto-parietal cortex and then compete, with prefrontal regions and the basal ganglia supplying biasing influences into that competition before a single response is selected. MECH-151 asserts exactly this ordering: E2.action_object() specifies the affordance manifold, E1's cue-indexed context adds an action_bias to it, and only then does HippocampalModule search and E3 select. Held back from higher confidence because this is a hypothesis-plus-simulation paper rather than new data, and because Cisek's action space is parameterised motor directions whereas REE's is a learned compressed world-effect embedding.
failure_signatures: If action selection were strictly serial -- construct a full world representation first, then compute a single action plan -- there would be no pre-selection manifold of candidate actions for a bias to act on, and MECH-151's insertion point (bias added to E2.action_object outputs BEFORE HippocampalModule search) would be architecturally misplaced rather than merely mistuned.

Cisek locates biasing influences in prefrontal cortex AND the basal ganglia jointly. MECH-151 routes the entire bias through a single E1 cue-context projection with no basal-ganglia-analogue gate, so if the biological arrangement requires a gating stage downstream of the cortical bias, a purely additive cortical projection may under-express the effect.

entries.confidence_rationale: Causal, not merely correlational: asymmetric unilateral lesions surgically DISCONNECT orbitofrontal cortex from ventrolateral striatum and abolish sensitivity to outcome-predictive relationships, with symmetric-lesion animals sparing one intact network as controls. That is direct evidence the frontal-to-striatal projection MECH-151 cites as its biological analogue carries action-outcome information into action selection rather than only valuation. Confidence is nonetheless modest: the readout is instrumental contingency sensitivity in mice, several inferential steps away from a graded bias applied to an affordance manifold, and a disconnection cannot distinguish a graded bias from an all-or-none gate.
failure_signatures: Disconnection abolishes outcome sensitivity outright rather than flattening a graded preference, so this design cannot discriminate MECH-151's additive-bias account from an all-or-none gating account of the frontal-to-striatal contribution. Both predict the same lesion result, which means a positive finding here does not favour MECH-151 over its nearest architectural rival.

The pathway that carries the effect is orbitofrontal, and the compartment is VENTROlateral striatum, with the authors explicitly contrasting it against a dorsolateral compartment subserving stimulus-response habit. If REE's action_bias is functionally a stimulus-response shortcut rather than an outcome-model-dependent reweighting, it is the wrong compartment's analogue and the anatomical warrant in MECH-151's notes does not transfer.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong single-unit evidence that a biasing signal really is applied to premotor representations of candidate actions before selection -- which supports MECH-151's architecture -- but the measured form of that bias contradicts MECH-151's stated functional form. In the one-target task, directionally tuned PMd delay activity showed NO value modulation; modulation appeared only in the two-target task and was always RELATIVE to the competing option's value. MECH-151 posits an unconditional additive bias (o_t_biased = o_t + action_bias), which predicts modulation in the single-option case too. Direction is therefore mixed rather than supports. Confidence is held at 0.66 by good source quality against a real content mismatch: the biasing variable here is reward value, not cue-indexed context.
failure_signatures: MECH-151's additive form predicts a non-zero action_bias contribution even when only one action-object is viable. PMd showed no value modulation of directionally tuned delay activity in the one-target task, so the biological analogue implements a relative, competition-conditioned bias rather than an absolute additive one. If REE's instrumented mean_cue_action_bias_norm is non-zero in single-affordance situations, that is a divergence from the primate data -- and if it is measured only in single-affordance situations, the primate data predict it will read at floor for reasons that have nothing to do with the projection being broken.

Relative-value modulation appeared MUCH LATER than directional tuning. A bias that is applied simultaneously with affordance specification, rather than as a later second wave, would not reproduce this timing -- so an implementation that folds the bias into E2.action_object's own forward pass, rather than adding it to the output, would diverge.

entries.confidence_rationale: Goal neglect is defined as ignoring a task requirement while remaining able to describe it -- which is MECH-467's leg 3 (behavioural capture with the rule intact) as an established, replicated human phenomenon with a fifty-year literature and a tight relationship to psychometric g. That makes the dissociability the claim asserts a documented fact rather than a conjecture, which is the strongest thing literature can do for a claim of this shape. Held below 0.8 because Duncan's own mechanistic account complicates rather than confirms MECH-467's three-way carve-up: he attributes neglect to task-model components being LOST under representational competition, which is closer to rule corruption than to the rule-survives-but-action-is-captured reading MECH-467 gives leg 3.
failure_signatures: MECH-467's PASS criterion is rule drift at floor while wrong-target selection is elevated. Duncan's account predicts this exact pattern can arise from plain rule corruption whenever the drift measure reads a STORED or reportable rule rather than the representation actually driving selection -- neglect is defined by the gap between describable and operative. So a battery that instruments rule state at a storage site rather than at the point of action selection cannot distinguish leg 2 from leg 3, and a PASS would be uninterpretable.

Neglect is driven by the complexity of the task model, and increasing the real-time demands of one component does NOT promote neglect of another. A distractor battery that manipulates moment-to-moment perceptual load while holding the rule set small may therefore fail to elicit behavioural capture at all, and return a floor result that is a property of the design rather than of the substrate.

entries.confidence_rationale: About as close as the human literature gets to a direct measurement of MECH-467's leg 3. Participants hold an intact, reportable task set -- find the target shape, ignore the salient distractor -- and their FIRST EYE MOVEMENT still goes to the distractor on a substantial fraction of trials. Overt action selection is captured while the rule is intact, which is the failure rule-state protection cannot catch. The awareness manipulation strengthens it: participants can often report that they were just captured, and reporting it does not prevent the next capture, so the failure is not a rule-knowledge failure at any level. Held at 0.66 because task-set integrity is assumed from instruction rather than measured trial-by-trial.
failure_signatures: If overt capture occurred only on trials where the task set had also degraded, legs 2 and 3 would be one failure mode and MECH-467's three-way dissociation would reduce to two. The paradigm does not observe that -- capture occurs while the task set is intact and even introspectively monitored -- but it never independently measures task-set integrity per trial, so it constrains the alternative rather than eliminating it.

Awareness of having been captured did not prevent subsequent capture. Any REE mechanism that proposes to close leg 3 by DETECTING wrong-target selection and feeding that back into rule maintenance is predicted by this result to be insufficient: the detection signal exists in humans and does not fix the behaviour.

entries.confidence_rationale: Supports MECH-467's separation of sensory capture from downstream failure modes -- capture is not obligatory, and a salient distractor can be suppressed BEFORE it captures -- with converging psychophysics, eye-tracking and ERP evidence. But the same finding undermines MECH-467's non-degeneracy guard, which infers 'the distractor was never registered' from a floor sensory-capture rate. Registered-then-suppressed and never-encoded yield the same floor at the behavioural level and are separable only with an encoding-side index. Direction is therefore mixed. Confidence 0.64: a strong review whose bearing on the claim is half supportive and half corrective.
failure_signatures: MECH-467's non-degeneracy guard requires a non-zero sensory-capture rate in at least one arm and self-routes substrate_not_ready otherwise, on the reasoning that a distractor the agent never encodes tests nothing. The suppression literature shows a distractor can be fully encoded and then actively suppressed below baseline, producing the same floor capture rate. The guard can therefore discard a battery in which the distractor WAS registered and the substrate handled it correctly -- a false substrate_not_ready, and the most expensive kind of error because it looks like a clean self-route.

Suppression efficacy varies with task demands and with lapses of cognitive control. A battery reporting a single aggregate sensory-capture rate across a block will average over trials where the distractor was suppressed and trials where it captured, and may report a mid-range value that describes no trial that actually occurred.

entries.confidence_rationale: The single most on-point result in this pull for MECH-053's commitment-suppression function: habenula responses to dynamically updated shock-cue values PREDICT behavioural suppression of responding, and the reward-side response predicts invigoration. Human data removes species transfer risk entirely. Confidence held below 0.85 by the resolution problem -- the habenula is a very small structure for fMRI, the paper cannot cleanly separate lateral from medial habenula, and BOLD cannot deliver the 'fast' in MECH-053's fast gate.
failure_signatures: fMRI at habenula scale cannot dissociate lateral from medial habenula, so the anatomical specificity MECH-053 inherits from the LHb literature is not established by this study.
BOLD timing cannot evidence the FAST, pre-consolidation interrupt that MECH-053 requires; the result is compatible with a slow value-tracking signal that biases responding over trials.

entries.confidence_rationale: MECH-053 has been disambiguated (2026-08-18, claims.yaml notes) to the FUNCTIONAL reading -- one signed channel, asymmetric dynamics and downstream consequences, not folded into a symmetric scalar -- rather than an architectural reading requiring two anatomically disjoint channels. Under that reading this paper is straightforward support on two counts: the acquisition asymmetry (aversive-cue responses within a few trials vs. prolonged conditioning plus high reward probability for reward-cue inhibition) is direct evidence for the FAST half of MECH-053's fast aversive gate and for aversive signals being privileged for speed; and the bidirectional signing within one population -- excited by aversive events, inhibited by reward -- is exactly the signature of a single signed channel whose limbs are not collapsed into a symmetric scalar, which is what the disambiguated claim now asserts.
failure_signatures: LHb neurons here are bidirectional -- excited by aversive events and inhibited by reward -- in the SAME population, so this paper cannot be read as evidence for an anatomically distinct population carrying only harm-PE. A REE implementation that instantiates two disjoint channels (rather than one signed channel with asymmetric limbs) would diverge from this substrate.

The reward-side response requires prolonged conditioning and high reward probability to appear, so a REE gate assuming symmetric acquisition rates for appetitive and aversive learning would mispredict the biology.

entries.confidence_rationale: On-point for MECH-053's action-suppression function -- LHb is described as suppressing less-rewarding saccades by inhibiting dopamine neurons, which is the closest the primate literature comes to a motor-commitment veto. But it is a short conference-proceedings review (4 pages) rather than a primary report, and the suppression it describes is of LESS-REWARDING actions rather than aversively-gated ones. Confidence deliberately low.
failure_signatures: The suppression described is of less-rewarding saccades -- an appetitive-value comparison -- not suppression triggered by an aversive prediction-error spike. Reading it as direct evidence for a harm-PE veto conflates reward-magnitude gating with aversive gating, which is exactly the collapse MECH-053 exists to prevent.
Four-page review in a proceedings volume; primary data are reported elsewhere and this entry should not be weighted as an independent empirical source.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical primate single-unit study establishing that LHb encodes negative motivational value as a context-relative signal, not merely reward omission. Source quality is high (Nat Neurosci, monkey electrophysiology, replicated repeatedly since). Mapping fidelity is good for the 'aversive channel is distinct and asymmetric' half of MECH-053 but only indirect for the 'suppresses commitment' half -- this is a Pavlovian recording study, not an action-veto manipulation.
failure_signatures: The LHb signal here is context-relative (excited by the most unpleasant event WITHIN each context), so a REE gate keying on an absolute harm-PE magnitude would not reproduce the primate signal.
The paper is correlational: it shows LHb represents negative value, not that LHb activity vetoes an already-forming commitment.

entries.confidence_rationale: The causal complement to the recording studies: LHb lesions AND selective ablation of the LHb->RMTg projection both abolish the ability of a negative predictor to bias choice AWAY from an action, while leaving positive predictors intact. That asymmetry -- critical for negative predictors, not positive ones -- is precisely the channel separation MECH-053 asserts, and it is demonstrated causally rather than inferred. Held at 0.80 by rodent-to-REE transfer and by the fact that the DV is instrumental choice bias, not commitment interruption.
failure_signatures: The demonstrated function is OUTCOME-SPECIFIC inhibition learned over training, not a fast general-purpose interrupt; a REE gate that suppresses commitment indiscriminately on any harm-PE spike would be a different mechanism from the one shown here.
Lesion/ablation methods show necessity for the behavioural effect but cannot establish the timing or the pre-consolidation position MECH-053 asserts.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly validates the single most important design choice in Q-092's confirming signature -- that held-out accuracy must be tested against an EMPIRICAL PERMUTATION NULL rather than a theoretical 50% chance level. The demonstration is quantitative and adversarial (random Gaussian signals reaching 70%+ two-class accuracy at small n), so it constrains Q-092's episode budget as well as its statistics. High confidence: the result is methodological and machine-independent, so domain transfer risk is nearly nil.
failure_signatures: If Q-092 is run with a small number of held-out episodes, an accuracy well above 50% is expected under the null and reporting it against theoretical chance would manufacture a false PASS.

The permutation null controls for small-sample inflation but NOT for a genuine confound shared by the two conditions -- clearing this null is necessary and explicitly insufficient for Q-092's verdict.

entries.confidence_rationale: Supplies the formal framework Q-092's design is an instance of, and adds a distinction Q-092 does not currently make: a label permutation tests whether ANY class structure was found, whereas a restricted within-class FEATURE permutation tests whether the classifier is exploiting feature DEPENDENCY. Q-092's multivariate trajectory-segment signature makes that second test directly applicable and currently unspecified. Foundational, widely-cited, domain-general.
failure_signatures: A label-permutation p-value alone cannot distinguish a classifier exploiting the multivariate DEPENDENCY structure of the trajectory signature from one riding a single dominant marginal feature (e.g. refuge occupancy alone) -- Q-092's Stage-1 claim to a 'multivariate signature' is not established by the test it currently specifies.
Under the label-permutation null the class marginals are preserved, so a strongly imbalanced or degenerate feature set can still yield a misleadingly interpretable result that the null does not flag.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the methodological principle behind Q-092's matched untrained-policy control and its orthogonal-perturbation check, stated in general form: run the SAME analysis pipeline on simulated confounds, null data and control data, because a novel pipeline's failure modes are not predictable from the design alone. Q-092 independently arrived at two instances of this. High confidence; the demonstrated error classes (counterbalancing/cross-validation mismatch, linear decoding of a variance difference) are directly reachable by Q-092's design.
failure_signatures: A trajectory classifier can separate conditions on a DIFFERENCE IN VARIANCE rather than in mean structure -- Görgen et al. show a linear decoder doing exactly this for a nonlinear effect. Reef-OFF episodes plausibly have higher trajectory variance than reef-ON, which would yield real, replicable, permutation-clearing discriminability that means only 'one condition is more variable'.

Mismatch between how episodes are counterbalanced/blocked and how cross-validation folds are cut can produce systematically BELOW-chance accuracy, which a one-sided reading of Q-092's falsifying signature would misclassify as a clean null result rather than as a broken pipeline.

Two-sided by construction, which is why the direction is mixed rather than supports. It is the strongest available methodological warrant for Q-093's insistence on MATCHED-budget comparison -- Chinchilla's whole result exists only because Gopher, GPT-3 and Megatron-Turing NLG were re-compared at equal compute rather than at equal parameter count, and the ranking inverted. But its central empirical finding cuts the other way for the baseline class: for monolithic transformers, capacity and experience must scale EQUALLY, so the comparison class Q-093 must beat is strictly proportional, with no sublinear dividend of its own. Confidence reflects an exceptionally solid result (400+ trained models) applied to a question it was not designed to answer.
failure_signatures: For monolithic transformers the compute-optimal frontier requires model size and training tokens to scale 1:1, so any efficiency dividend REE claims must come from the architectural seam between control and representation -- it cannot come from sitting on a better-tuned scaling curve, because the baseline class already occupies its own optimum.

Chinchilla's parameter count N is undecomposed: a monolithic transformer has no control-machinery-versus-representational-store seam, so this paper cannot supply a baseline MEASUREMENT of the specific ratio Q-093 asks about, only of total capacity against total experience.

The paper's cost variable is pre-training FLOPs alone. Comparing REE against a Chinchilla-optimal baseline on that variable would silently drop most of Q-093's stated cost terms and could produce a verdict that reverses once inference, memory and adaptation are counted.

entries.confidence_rationale: Supports the MEASUREMENT-PROTOCOL half of Q-093 rather than its architectural half, and the support is concrete: it shows that changing the denominator from pre-training compute to training-plus-inference lifetime compute MOVES THE OPTIMUM -- systems facing substantial inference demand should be trained smaller and longer than Chinchilla-optimal. That is empirical vindication of Q-093's decision to define efficiency over total lifetime cost rather than per-step cost or parameter count, and it comes with 47 trained models rather than an argument. Confidence held below source quality because the paper's lifetime accounting is still narrower than Q-093's.
failure_signatures: The optimal configuration under lifetime accounting depends on an ASSUMED inference demand (their headline case is roughly 1 billion requests). Q-093 specifies no comparable deployment-volume parameter, so a REE-versus-baseline lifetime-cost verdict could be flipped by an unstated choice of assumed demand -- the protocol must fix and declare this before any comparison is run.

This paper's lifetime cost counts pre-training and inference only. It excludes memory storage and retrieval, offline replay and consolidation, and post-deployment adaptation -- precisely the terms Q-093 requires and precisely the terms where REE's replay, residue and consolidation machinery ADD cost. Adopting this accounting wholesale would bias the comparison in REE's favour.

Scaling laws fitted at typical token/parameter ratios overestimate the benefit of additional tokens at extreme ratios; by the same logic, any REE scaling curve extrapolated from a narrow band of configurations should be treated as unreliable outside that band.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the adversarial reading of the single best supporting result in this pull, and it lands where it hurts: the RETRO offload dividend largely tracks TOKEN OVERLAP between the retrieval database and the test data rather than non-trivial generalisation from the combination of weights and retrieval. If the mechanism is substantially lookup, then the RAG literature's apparent demonstration of sublinear control-machinery scaling is a weaker warrant for Q-093 than it first appears. Confidence is moderate rather than high because the reproduction is at smaller scale than the original and the paper reports a contribution analysis rather than a clean causal decomposition -- it establishes that overlap explains much of the gain, not exactly how much survives without it.
failure_signatures: If REE's efficiency dividend is measured on a task family whose content overlaps what z_world, semantic memory and episodic structures already encode, the measured dividend may be retrieval-lookup rather than the structural reuse Q-093 is actually asking about -- so the protocol needs an explicit, PRE-REGISTERED overlap control between the evaluation family and the contents of the persistent stores.

Even limited token overlap significantly decreased test-time loss, so an overlap control cannot be a binary contamination check; it has to be graded, and a REE result reported without a graded overlap measure is uninterpretable in this respect.

The paper generalises to a measurement problem, not just a RETRO problem: evaluating any retrieval- or memory-augmented system's generalisation is intrinsically hard because the store and the test set are drawn from overlapping distributions. Q-093 inherits this difficulty in full.

entries.confidence_rationale: The closest existing empirical analogue of Q-093's confirming direction: a FIXED-SIZE processing component (a 7.5B-parameter transformer) reaches parity with monolithic models 25x larger by conditioning on a 2-trillion-token external store, and performance keeps improving as the STORE grows with the model held constant. That is the sublinear-control-machinery shape Q-093 asks about, demonstrated at scale in a peer-reviewed venue. Confidence is held well below source quality because the mapping is loose in two load-bearing ways: RETRO's fixed component is a next-token predictor, not a control/organising system, and the headline is a PARAMETER count rather than the lifetime-cost denominator Q-093 explicitly requires.
failure_signatures: The 25x reduction is a PARAMETER count, not a lifetime-cost count: the storage footprint of the 2-trillion-token database and the per-query approximate-nearest-neighbour cost sit outside the headline, so reading this result as a 25x efficiency dividend would systematically overstate what Q-093 would measure.

RETRO's fixed-size component is a predictor over token chunks, not a controller that must commit, replay, maintain goals and carry residue; evidence that a predictor stays small as its knowledge store grows does not entail that E1/E2/E3, commitment and replay stay small as z_world richness grows.

Retrieval is over a STATIC corpus indexed once. REE's representational spaces are learned and continually rewritten, so the analogue of 'growing the database' in REE also grows the cost of maintaining and consolidating it -- a term with no counterpart here.

entries.confidence_rationale: The strongest entry in this pull for Q-093's confirming direction, and the only one that satisfies the non-degeneracy precondition head-on: EMPA is compared against humans AT MATCHED COMPETENCE across 90 games, not at unmatched competence, and it is the experiential-cost axis -- 'does the system need less environmental experience per acquired capability' -- that the comparison measures. It is a genuine existence proof that structured, persistent, causal world-modelling plus planning can reach a competence level that model-free deep RL reaches only with vastly more experience. Confidence sits at 0.72 rather than higher because EMPA is not REE and, critically, the paper reports matched SAMPLE efficiency without reporting matched COMPUTE.
failure_signatures: EMPA matches human SAMPLE efficiency but the paper does not establish matched COMPUTE: theory-based exploration and planning are expensive per decision, so experiential efficiency can be bought with inference cost. Under Q-093's total-lifetime-cost denominator that trade could cancel the dividend outright -- this is the single most important unresolved term.

The task family is 90 simple 2D video games built around objects, agents and their interactions, which is exactly the structure intuitive theories are well matched to. An efficiency dividend demonstrated where the right abstractions are effectively given a priori may not survive in domains where those abstractions must themselves be discovered.

EMPA's structured priors are hand-specified rather than learned. REE's confirming direction requires that ACQUIRED structure persists and pays off; a demonstration resting on built-in structure evidences the value of having the right structure, not the value of having learned it.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct primate electrophysiology showing that midbrain dopamine neurons split into two functionally and anatomically distinct populations during a Pavlovian task with both appetitive (reward) and aversive (airpuff) outcomes: a minority 'value-coding' group excited by reward-predicting cues and inhibited by airpuff-predicting cues (a signed channel), and a majority 'salience-coding' group excited by both (an unsigned/motivational-salience channel). The two groups are anatomically segregated (dorsolateral vs ventromedial SNc/VTA). This is the most direct primate evidence this corpus holds that a signed valence channel and a non-signed salience channel are computed by separable dopaminergic populations rather than one blended signal -- the specific structural claim MECH-054 makes about signed harm/benefit precision channels remaining distinct. Confidence is not higher because (a) the paper's 'signed' population is the minority, not the majority, of recorded neurons, complicating a direct 'this IS the MECH-054 channel' identification, and (b) the task uses simple Pavlovian cue-outcome pairs (liquid reward vs airpuff), not the graded, harm-vs-benefit residue-field valence structure REE models.
failure_signatures: The anatomically-segregated 'value-coding' dopamine population is a minority of recorded neurons; most dopamine neurons in this dataset are salience-coding (excited by both reward- and aversive-predicting cues), so a strict 'dopamine = signed valence' reading is not what the paper shows -- it shows a mixture, with signed coding as one identifiable component

Anatomical segregation (dorsolateral vs ventromedial SNc/VTA) is correlational with response type in this dataset; the paper does not causally manipulate one population to show it alone carries signed information

The aversive stimulus (airpuff) is a low-level noxious/startle stimulus, not the graded, contextual harm signal REE's harm stream represents -- transfer from 'airpuff' to 'harm residue field' is an inferential step

Not a defensive-behavior or orienting study -- included as a deliberate CONTRAST anchor for what a genuinely sub-theta-cycle (Option C) persistence window looks like in real decision-making data, so its own commitment-reversal window (a few hundred ms) can be checked against the multi-second defensive-freezing entries elsewhere in this directory. Direction coded mixed because it neither directly supports nor weakens SD-099 -- it calibrates what fast-decision-commitment timescales actually look like, and the answer sharpens the contrast rather than closing it.
failure_signatures: This paradigm shows that when a biological decision-making system genuinely operates on a sub-second commitment window, that window is reported in the low hundreds of milliseconds (a few hundred ms), not the 60-125ms range Option C proposes -- so even the fastest well-characterized human decision-commitment literature does not land inside Option C's own range, a further data point against reading Option C's magnitude as biologically typical.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly quantitative, well-powered (n=58 mice, 44+14 by response type) primary measurement of exactly the transition this claim's persistence window concerns -- the fast defensive-orienting/escape response and the duration of the ensuing defensive state before the animal is free to resume normal behavior. Held below 0.8 because the paradigm measures freezing-state duration, not a specifically DECISIONAL (approach vs withdraw) bias, and is rodent/innate-defense rather than a graded valence-gated choice.
failure_signatures: A design that assumes the post-orienting defensive bias clears within ~100ms (Option C, less than one theta cycle) is contradicted by two orders of magnitude by this paradigm's measured freezing-state duration (21-28s).

Escape ITSELF is fast (154ms latency, <1s duration) -- if SD-099's window were meant to model the ballistic motor act rather than the ensuing defensive STATE, sub-100ms would be defensible; conflating the two is the likely source of an under-estimate.

entries.confidence_rationale: Standard, well-cited review of the Sokolov-lineage human psychophysiological orienting response literature, giving the classical multi-second time course of the ORIENTING EPISODE itself (Q1b's cross-check quantity) rather than the post-decision persistence question (Q1) directly. Confidence held at moderate because it is a review synthesizing others' data rather than a primary quantitative source, and because it characterizes autonomic/attentional orienting components, not a behavioral action-selection bias.
failure_signatures: If SD-099's post-orienting bias window were meant to be much SHORTER than the orienting episode it follows, that would be a novel and unsupported claim -- every human psychophysiological component of the orienting response reviewed here (cardiac deceleration, electrodermal response, late positive potential) unfolds and resolves on a multi-second timescale, not a sub-200ms one.

entries.confidence_rationale: Triangulates the Shang 2018 seconds-scale finding with a second, independent, graded-threat paradigm (freezing duration scales with looming urgency, 630ms to 7.9s) and adds a distinct spatial-persistence measure (4.6s), but the direction is coded mixed because the paper's central finding -- that defensive behavior is state-dependent/re-entrant on shelter availability, updating within 1-2 trials -- argues against 'fixed duration' as the right primitive at all (bears on Q2, not just Q1).
failure_signatures: The fastest measured freezing-state duration in this paper (629.9 +/- 100.0 ms, rapid-looming/shelter-closed condition) still lands almost exactly at Option A's own lower bound (625ms), not inside Option C's 60-125ms range -- a second independent triangulation point against the sub-theta-cycle reading.

Defensive strategy (freeze vs. flee) reversed COMPLETELY within a single subsequent trial once the shelter route was reopened -- a fixed-duration bias window is a worse model of this system than an evidence/state-gated one; a rigid tick-count may be the wrong primitive regardless of which magnitude is chosen.

The canonical direct measurement that primate cortex is not organised around a single flat clock: intrinsic spiking-fluctuation timescales are hierarchically ordered across seven areas, short in sensory and long in prefrontal. That is the biological warrant for INV-013's MULTI-TIMESCALE limb, which requires at least two coexisting and interacting update rates. Confidence 0.74 rather than higher because of a specific and instructive mismatch that INV-013's own what_would_answer already anticipates: the timescales measured here are INTRINSIC (autocorrelation of fluctuation), which establishes graded time constants but not that the areas interact ACROSS rates -- and interaction is explicitly part of what the limb requires. The paper is also silent on offline or consolidation-cadence timescales, which is where half of REE's multi-timescale property actually lives.
failure_signatures: The measured quantity is the intrinsic autocorrelation timescale of spiking fluctuation, not a task-update rate. A hierarchy of intrinsic time constants does not by itself establish that the areas INTERACT across those rates, and INV-013's MULTI-TIMESCALE limb explicitly requires that at least two rates 'coexist and interact'. This entry supports coexistence more strongly than interaction.

Seven cortical areas, with data aggregated across laboratories, species-matched but task-heterogeneous. The hierarchical ordering is a group-level trend with substantial within-area heterogeneity, so a single area does not have a single clean clock rate.

The paper says nothing about offline or consolidation-cadence processing. REE's MULTI-TIMESCALE property is carried jointly by the within-episode fast/slow split (E2 versus E1) AND the cross-episode sleep cadence in ree_core/sleep/; this evidence bears only on the first kind of split.

Read against ARC-004's own audit finding -- that LatentStack.encode currently smooths z_beta/z_theta/z_delta with a single shared EMA constant (alpha_shared=0.3) -- the biology here is GRADED per area in a way REE's L-space presently is not. The paper therefore highlights the exact place REE's implementation of this limb is thinnest rather than validating it.

entries.confidence_rationale: High-quality perspective in Neuron by two leading circuit neuroscientists, and the canonical modern statement that prediction is not an optional add-on to cortical processing but its default motif. That bears directly on INV-013's PREDICTIVE limb: the architectural commitment REE makes is the one cortex is argued to make. Confidence held to 0.72 rather than higher for two reasons. First, INV-013 is explicitly an audit of REE's own live code paths (E1's LSTM slow world model, E2's world_forward/predict_next_state, both wired into Agent.step()) -- no literature can certify that those paths are exercised, so the paper can only establish that the commitment is well-founded, never that REE realises it. Second, the paper is scrupulous that predictive processing's circuit-level implementation remains under-determined and devotes a section to how it could be falsified, which is the same labelled-versus-genuine distinction INV-013 delegates to ARC-002.
failure_signatures: The paper states that the circuit-level implementation of predictive processing is not settled -- observing a prediction-error-like response does not by itself establish an underlying generative forward model. A substrate could show error-shaped signals without being predictive in INV-013's sense.

The treatment is centred on sensory cortex and sensorimotor prediction. Prediction of AFFORDANCES conditioned on action -- which is what ARC-002 asks of REE's E2 -- is not the paper's evidential target, so the strongest form of REE's predictive commitment is not directly supported here.

The proposed distinction between positive- and negative-prediction-error neuron populations is presented as a testable implementation hypothesis, not an established finding; a substrate organised differently would not thereby be non-predictive.

entries.confidence_rationale: Strong, well-controlled primate electrophysiology with a behaviourally-anchored design: the authors first isolate 'challenge' images behaviourally, then show that behaviourally-sufficient identity solutions arrive ~30 ms LATER in IT for exactly those images, and that the late-phase population patterns are poorly predicted by feedforward CNNs. That is direct evidence that a single forward pass is insufficient for a real class of inputs -- the necessity form of INV-013's ITERATIVE limb, not merely its availability. Confidence held at 0.70 for two reasons: the paper's own finding of functional equivalence between recurrence and additional feedforward depth shows iteration is a parameter-efficient route to depth rather than a strictly necessary architecture, and the level of the mapping differs (perceptual categorisation recurrence in the ventral stream versus REE's CEM-style proposal loop over ACTIONS in the planning path).
failure_signatures: The authors report a functional equivalence between additional nonlinear transformations and recurrence -- very-deep feedforward CNNs predicted the late IT responses about as well as shallower recurrent CNNs. So iteration is shown to be how the primate brain buys the extra computation, not that iterative refinement is the only architecture that could deliver it. Any REE argument that iteration is architecturally NECESSARY overreaches this evidence.

The recurrence demonstrated is within perceptual categorisation in the ventral stream. REE's ITERATIVE mechanism is a proposal-score-revise loop over candidate ACTIONS in agent.py with stuck-state-gated widening. Both are more-than-one-pass-per-decision, but they sit at different levels of the loop, and evidence for one does not transfer automatically to the other.

The ~30 ms late-solution signature is established for a curated subset of challenge images; the majority of images are solved in the feedforward sweep, so the result bounds how much of ordinary processing is genuinely iterative.

entries.confidence_rationale: The most directly Q-094-shaped paper found in this pull, and the only one that speaks to the BODILY/INTEROCEPTIVE variable rather than the goal variable. The same hippocampal population was recorded while rats performed identical tasks under food versus water deprivation, so the internal state is manipulated with the scene held constant. Three findings map onto Q-094 almost line for line, and the third is the valuable one: motivational state influenced coding strongly during contextual memory retrieval, when the internal cue was needed to select among remembered actions in the SAME PLACES, and left the same populations relatively unaffected during random foraging, when hunger and thirst were incidental -- deprivation signals 'informed, but did not determine' hippocampal coding. That is a demand-gated inclusion, which is an architectural answer Q-094's what_would_answer does not currently list as an option. Confidence 0.79, capped mainly because hunger and thirst are sustained discrete states rather than the continuously-fluctuating interoceptive signal Q-094's destabilisation worry is actually about.
failure_signatures: Hunger and thirst are discrete, sustained deprivation states, not the continuously-varying interoceptive signal Q-094 worries would destabilise the context variable. The paper therefore does NOT test the worst case for inclusion, and cannot be cited as having retired the destabilisation risk.

The gating is inferred from a between-task contrast (contextual retrieval versus random foraging) rather than from a manipulation of relevance within a single task. The mechanism that produces the gate is not identified, so 'include internal state only when task-relevant' is a description of the observed pattern rather than a validated control policy REE could copy.
Rodent hippocampus recorded during behaviour; REE's ContextMemory is an engineered bank with no claim to be a hippocampal model. The mapping is functional-analogical throughout.

The finding that deprivation-derived signals 'informed but did not determine' hippocampal coding is a qualitative characterisation of an effect-size difference between conditions, not a demonstration of an explicit gating mechanism; a competing reading is simply that internal state has a weaker but constant influence which becomes detectable only when task demand amplifies its behavioural consequences.

entries.confidence_rationale: Genuinely mixed for Q-094 rather than diplomatically hedged. It supports the premise strongly: task states that are UNOBSERVABLE from sensory input can be decoded from human OFC, decoding accuracy tracks task performance and predicts individual behavioural errors, and representational similarity between consecutive states correlates with transition accuracy -- so non-sensory state is represented AND is behaviourally load-bearing, which is the functional half Wood et al. cannot supply. But it cuts against the specific INCLUSION reading of Q-094 by locating that representation in OFC, a structure separate from the hippocampal place/context system. Read as architecture that is an argument for keeping MECH-150's z_world-only ContextMemory and adding a distinct task-state module, not for augmenting the context query -- a third design option that governance should have in front of it. Confidence 0.66 reflects fMRI decoding's coarse spatial and temporal resolution and the fact that the mixed reading rests on an anatomical-separation inference the paper does not itself draw.
failure_signatures: The representation is localised to OFC, not to hippocampus or any structure REE's ContextMemory is analogised to. Taken at face value this argues for a SEPARATE task-state module rather than for augmenting the context retrieval query, which is a design option distinct from both of Q-094's stated poles and which would leave MECH-150's decision standing.

fMRI multivariate decoding has coarse spatial and temporal resolution; successful decoding of a state variable from a region establishes that information is present in the measured signal, not that a downstream circuit reads it out in that form or uses it as a retrieval key.

The task states here are abstract, discrete and externally defined by the experimental structure (16 states). Q-094's candidate internal variables -- bodily state, confidence, inferred social situation -- are continuous, self-generated and not externally enumerable, so the demonstrated decodability does not transfer straightforwardly.

The anatomical-separation argument that grounds the mixed direction is an inference this paper does not itself make; the authors' claim is about OFC's function, not about what hippocampal context representation should or should not contain.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the canonical matched-scene manipulation and it is almost exactly the experimental shape Q-094's what_would_answer asks for: hold the sensory scene and the overt behaviour constant, vary only the episode/goal identity, and ask whether the representation differentiates. It does -- two-thirds of hippocampal complex-spike cells fired differentially on the common stem by left- versus right-turn trial type, with running speed, heading and position on the stem explicitly controlled. So the biological system provably does not key context on scene identity alone. Supports the ADDS-CAPABILITY horn in the currency Q-095's what_would_answer actually specifies -- downstream competence rather than internal representational statistics. The review's core argument is that endowing an RL system with episodic memory buys three things a parametric/semantic value representation does not deliver: efficient value approximation over high-dimensional partially-observable state spaces, learning from very little data, and bridging long-term action-reward dependencies. If REE's trajectory-generation account already provides instance-based retrieval of individual past experiences, then this paper's capability argument is ALREADY discharged by the existing architecture and cannot be counted as evidence for the additional coordinated principle -- the two must be scored separately.

Scoring a Q-095 arm on asymptotic performance alone will miss the effect this literature predicts, which is concentrated in sample efficiency and early learning; the discriminating measurement is the learning curve, not its endpoint.

entries.confidence_rationale: This is the most direct empirical evidence available for the one capability Q-095's own notes flag as having no clean existing owner: BINDING heterogeneous elements into a single coherent event representation. The design is the load-bearing part -- participants learn events from multiple overlapping pairs and are tested on all pairwise associations, so a pairwise-associative or trajectory-linked account makes a specific prediction (retrieval reinstates the tested partner) that differs from the holistic account's prediction (retrieval reinstates ALL elements, including ones incidental to the tested pair). The incidental reinstatement is observed, is neocortically specific to element type, and its degree correlates with hippocampal activity. Confidence 0.73 rather than higher because the hippocampal link is correlational fMRI rather than causal, and because 'event' here is a laboratory construction of arbitrary element pairs rather than a naturally segmented episode.
failure_signatures: An REE memory that retrieves only the queried association and its immediate trajectory neighbours, without reinstating task-incidental co-bound elements, is NOT implementing episodic binding in the sense this literature means -- it is implementing pairwise association, and should not be described as episodic.

If REE's ContextMemory shows all-or-none (dependent) retrieval across an event's elements, that is a positive signature of holistic completion; graded independent retrieval per element is the signature of the pairwise alternative.

entries.confidence_rationale: Direct primate electrophysiology showing that the RELATIVE PHASE relationship between two synchronized oscillatory populations (not just synchrony magnitude) has a measurable downstream behavioral consequence (reaction time). entries.confidence_rationale: Directly documents the specific failure shape ARC-130 warns about: within the option-critic framework (see companion 2017 entry in this directory), options that formally exist, are represented, and are locally operable nonetheless collapse into degenerate solutions absent an explicit regularizer -- either terminating on almost every step (never accumulating committed, multi-step behaviour) or running for an entire episode regardless of state (never exhibiting state-sensitive competitive authority). This is an external, non-REE, empirically-documented instance of ARC-130's central claim that 'authority at one internal selection boundary does not by itself establish that authority reaches committed behaviour' -- here, the option is selected and begins executing (an internal selection event) but the architecture-as-trained does not reliably carry that selection through to a stable, temporally-extended, ecologically meaningful commitment without an additional cost term designed specifically to make that gap visible and correctable.
failure_signatures: Options frameworks trained by the base option-critic objective alone run into degenerate solutions in the absence of proper regularization, where a sub-policy either terminates after each step (collapsing temporal abstraction entirely -- the option never demonstrates committed, extended behaviour) or runs for the entire episode regardless of state (never demonstrating state-sensitive, competitive selection) -- both are failures of exactly the middle-to-late rungs of ARC-130's ladder (competitive authority, committed throughput) despite the option's existence, representation, and local operability being intact.

entries.confidence_rationale: Canonical, extremely highly-cited foundational paper that formally decomposes a hierarchical RL 'option' into three independently-learnable components -- an intra-option policy, an initiation condition, and a termination condition -- learned jointly by policy gradient with no external subgoal supervision. This formal separation is direct external-domain evidence that ARC-130's core methodological move (treating 'does the mechanism exist/is it represented' as separable from 'does it operate locally' as separable from 'does it terminate/commit appropriately') is not an REE-specific invention but corresponds to an established, load-bearing decomposition in a mature literature outside REE. Held at moderate confidence because this paper by itself only establishes that the stages ARE separable and jointly learnable -- it does not itself document a case where one stage is achieved and a later stage fails (that gap is the companion entry, Harb et al. 2018, in this same directory).
failure_signatures: Not directly documented in this paper -- see the companion 2018 deliberation-cost entry in this directory for the external instance of options that exist and operate locally but fail to reach stable, ecologically meaningful committed behaviour without additional regularization.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly instantiates the NON-ORACLE / SILKY quadrant of GOV-INTERVENE-1's taxonomy in a rigorous, widely-adopted methodology: the paper's activation-patching interventions perturb one suspected variable (a professions term's implied gender) in a minimally disruptive, distribution-preserving way, without supplying the model any privileged target-correct answer -- it establishes causal SENSITIVITY of specific components to the manipulated variable, not a ceiling on achievable performance. The paper's explicit decomposition of total effect into direct and indirect (mediator-routed) effects is independent methodological support for GOV-INTERVENE-1's requirement that provenance (which stage/variable/relation was altered) be recorded and that the effect be attributed to the intervention condition rather than silently treated as endogenous competence.
failure_signatures: The paper explicitly frames its method as attributing bias effects to specific mediating components via intervention, not as establishing that the network 'naturally' or 'endogenously' expresses that pathway during ordinary operation -- exactly the attribution discipline GOV-INTERVENE-1 requires and which the source thought warns is otherwise easy to silently drop.

Gender-bias effects are found to be sparse (concentrated in a small part of the network) and synergistic (amplified or repressed by different components in combination), meaning a single-mediator intervention alone can systematically under- or mis-attribute causal responsibility -- a concrete illustration of why GOV-INTERVENE-1 insists interventions be classified and their provenance recorded rather than treated as a single undifferentiated 'positive control' device.

entries.confidence_rationale: Directly instantiates the ORACLE quadrant of GOV-INTERVENE-1's taxonomy: an interchange intervention sets a neural representation to the value it would take under a DIFFERENT, causal-model-specified input -- i.e. it imports privileged, target-correct information about what a hypothesised causal variable should contain -- and is used specifically as a verification/ceiling test of whether the representation has the causal properties of its hypothesised role, not as a naturalistic probe of ordinary behaviour. The paper's own explicit distinction between 'this representation CAN be made to behave like variable V under intervention' and 'the model NATURALLY implements the causal structure containing V' is close to a formal statement of GOV-INTERVENE-1's warning that an oracle result does not become evidence of natural/endogenous competence.
failure_signatures: The paper finds that a simpler baseline model fails to realize the hypothesised causal structure even under interchange-intervention testing, while a stronger BERT-based model succeeds on parts of it -- demonstrating that oracle-style verification is genuinely informative (it can and does fail), not merely a rubber-stamp of whatever structure is proposed; a positive interchange-intervention result is real information about achievable ceiling structure, but the paper is explicit that this establishes the network CAN be aligned to a causal model, not that it ordinarily exercises that structure unprompted.

entries.confidence_rationale: Jardri & Deneve build a hierarchical Bayesian message-passing model in which subtle excitatory/inhibitory imbalance lets bottom-up sensory evidence and top-down predictions reverberate rather than being correctly discounted for their shared history -- a pathological loop they name 'circular belief propagation'. This is a structural analogue of the self-reinforcing loop ARC-132/MECH-514's notes describe (attractor -> biased perception/retrieval -> attractor-consistent derived material -> selective replay -> apparent confirmation -> stronger attractor): in both cases, failing to keep evidence and its own downstream reinterpretation separately tagged lets non-independent signal be double-counted as fresh confirmation, producing pathological over-confidence, spurious causal learning, and (in the model) resistance to perceptual illusions that lower-confidence percepts would normally show. That structural parallel is real corroboration for why ARC-132 requires an attractor's carried quantities to stay separable rather than collapsing into one strength scalar, and for why MECH-514's anti-circularity requirement (repeated replay of one episode must not be miscounted as independent samples) is a load-bearing design constraint rather than an optional nicety. Confidence is kept low and the direction is read narrowly: the raw thought's own evidential-boundary section and both claims' notes are explicit that this paper is cited as failure-mode inspiration only, not as demonstrated evidence that REE's attractor architecture works this way or that axis-conflation is schizophrenia's actual mechanism -- Jardri & Deneve's model is a specific message-passing algorithm error in a clinical human population, not an architectural commitment about carried-quantity separability in an artificial cognitive system. This entry should not be read as hardening either claim past 'candidate' / substrate_conditional.
failure_signatures: The paper's mechanism is a computational-psychiatry model of excitatory/inhibitory imbalance in cortical hierarchical inference, not a claim about multi-axis attractor properties (reliability, confidence, familiarity, valence, salience, urgency, self-relevance, source) -- ARC-132's axis list has no counterpart in the model.

Jardri & Deneve's circular belief propagation is a failure of discounting shared history between bottom-up and top-down signal in one inference pass; REE's self-reinforcing loop (per the raw thought) operates across perception, retrieval, and replay over time -- same qualitative shape (double-counting non-independent evidence), different granularity and timescale.

The model is validated against schizophrenia symptom clusters (hallucinations, delusions, illusion resistance) in a clinical population; there is no direct test of an artificial multi-axis attractor representation or of an offline counterfactual-replay protocol.

entries.confidence_rationale: Pellegrini et al. give direct, empirical continual-learning evidence for the failure mode MECH-513 is designed to prevent: when a network's intermediate representation keeps changing (as lower layers keep training), previously stored activations of that representation drift out of alignment with what the current network would produce, degrading recognition performance across non-uniform, real-time data streams (CORe50 NICv2, OpenLORIS). This directly corroborates the raw thought's framing that a change in representational primitives can silently invalidate previously stored, indexed content unless something explicit is done about it -- exactly the failure MECH-513 names for episodic memory. The paper's own fix, however, is a different strategy from MECH-513's: rather than reindexing/versioning stored content after the representation changes, it prevents most of the drift from occurring in the first place by slowing (near-freezing) learning in the layers below the replay point while letting only the layers above it train freely. MECH-513 explicitly declines to freeze representational structure and instead proposes an additive, versioned reindexing layer that lets episodes remain interpretable under both the old and new scheme -- so this paper evidences the problem MECH-513 responds to and the empirical cost of not solving it, without evidencing MECH-513's specific proposed solution.
failure_signatures: Pellegrini et al.'s primary mitigation is architectural rate-limiting (freeze/slow lower layers), not the additive versioned reindexing MECH-513 proposes -- the paper does not test or validate an explicit multi-version indexing scheme against a frozen-lower-layers baseline.

The paper's representation is a CNN's intermediate feature layer under supervised image/video classification; MECH-513's target is episodic memory indexed by structures like ContextMemory slots or an E1 associative manifold (MECH-154), which are not evaluated here.

MECH-513's change drivers include bucket split/merge and dimensionality crystallisation (MECH-496) as discrete structural events; the paper's drift is continuous and gradual (ongoing SGD on lower layers), a different temporal profile than a discrete re-indexing event.
